Biskopen efterlyste 1963 en kyrktomt mit: In 1963 the bishop called for a church site in the middle of the new housing, and in 1966 the Ihre family at Ekebyhov Palace offered land on the estate. The church wasn't consecrated until the fourth Sunday of Advent, 21 December 1980.
Biskopsgårdens kyrka ritades i brutalist: Biskopsgården Church was designed in the Brutalist style by Johannes Olivegren. A triangular, white-painted concrete roof reaches up towards a free-form concrete tower. The bell frame is shaped like a mainsail with three free-hanging bells, and a weathercock sits at the very top.
Biskopsgårdens kyrka vid Vårväderstorget: Biskopsgården Church on Vårväderstorget was completed in 1961 to designs by the architect Johannes Olivegren.
Bjurslättskyrkan är en så kallad vandrin: Bjurslätt Church is a 'travelling church', built to be moved. It went up in 1966 as Länsmansgården's church and was moved here when Länsmansgården got a permanent church in 1972. It was consecrated on its new site in 1973.
Bjärköarätten slog fast att brott som be: The medieval town law known as Bjärköarätten laid down that crimes committed between Stockholm and 'Konungshamn' were to be 'fined according to Stockholm law'. Later, during the late medieval struggles over the Kalmar Union, Danish kings anchored here with their fleets.
Björkekärrs kyrka i mörkrött tegel ritad: Björkekärr church, in dark red brick, was designed by Johannes Olivegren and consecrated by Bishop Bo Giertz on Whit Sunday, 25 May 1958. The great mosaic window in the chancel, by Ralph Bergholtz, runs from floor to ceiling and serves as both façade decoration and altarpiece.
Björkekärrs kyrka ritades av Johannes Ol: Björkekärr Church was designed by Johannes Olivegren and consecrated by Bishop Bo Giertz on Whit Sunday 1958. The large mosaic window in the chancel, by Ralph Bergholtz, serves as both facade decoration and altarpiece.
Björkekärrs vattentorn söder om Träringe: Björkekärr water tower, south of Träringen, was designed by Jan Wallinder and completed in 1969. It looks a lot like a mushroom.
Björkhagen hörde under två korta år, 199: For just two years, 1997 and 1998, Björkhagen was part of the Hammarby district, which was abolished when the number of city districts was cut from 24 to 18. A stone's throw away rises Duggregnet 5, Stockholm's tallest residential building when it went up in 1957. And from the metro station starts Sörmlandsleden, a hiking trail that's part of the European long-distance path E6.
Björkhagens skola invigdes 1949, ritad a: Björkhagen School opened in 1949, designed by the architect Åke Lindqvist, and on its eastern side the school grounds run right up to Nackareservatet, the Nacka nature reserve. The nearby Taklampan block also backs straight onto the reserve, and it was one of ten projects nominated for Stockholm Building of the Year 2018. So here, deep forest is practically on your doorstep.
Björkhagens station öppnade den 19 novem: Björkhagen station opened on the green line on 19 November 1958. This is where the first stage of the Sörmlandsleden hiking trail begins.
Björknäs centrum var en gång Boo kommuns: Björknäs centrum was once the commercial heart of Boo municipality. The 1940 fire station now houses a kiosk, a hairdresser and a dry cleaner, while the old cinema and the Konsum co-op shop from 1938 have become a sweet shop and offices.
Björknäs nämns i skrift redan 1436 och h: Björknäs is mentioned in writing as early as 1436 and takes its name from the farm Stora Björknäs gård. It sits at the eastern end of the Skuru bridges, where the Skurusundet strait marks a provincial border: west of the water is Södermanland, east of it Uppland. The bridges have been built in three stages – in 1915, 1957 and 2023. When the newest opened it took over the name Skurubron, and the older ones became Gamla Skurubron, the Old Skuru Bridge.
Björkängens IP har två ishallar. B-halle: Björkängen sports ground has two ice rinks. Rink B used to be known as Nickehallen, after Bengt "Nicke" Nilsson, one of the stalwarts of the Huddinge IK club.
Björkö kyrka byggdes helt på frivillig v: Björkö Church was built entirely on voluntary contributions, without a penny of tax money, and is owned by the Björkö Church Association. Designed by Olov Geggen in yellow brick, it was consecrated in 1957.
Björkö kyrka byggdes på frivillig väg ut: Björkö kyrka was built by volunteers without any tax money and is owned by the Björkö Church Association. Designed by Olov Geggen in yellow facing brick, it was consecrated in 1957 and also houses a parish hall.
Björkö, eller Bohus-Björkö som postorten: Björkö – or Bohus-Björkö, as its postal address has it – has just over 1,500 permanent residents. Out on Björkö Huvud, near Bovik, the Gothenburg Outdoor Association owns a stretch of land used as a naturist area, with swimming and camping. Also near Bovik is Pjonken, famous for the masses of hepaticas – little blue anemones – that flower there every spring.

Björkö – or Bohus-Björkö, as its postal address has it – has a few more secrets than you might expect. Out on Björkö Huvud, near Bovik, the Gothenburg outdoor association owns a stretch of land that's used as a naturist area, with swimming and camping. The island has about 1,500 year-round residents and covers just under five and a half square kilometres.
Björlanda kyrka, en bit härifrån, står p: Björlanda Church, a short way from here, stands on north-western Hisingen and has belonged to Torslanda-Björlanda parish since 2010. The old parish of Björlanda counted as part of Bohuslän and merged into the City of Gothenburg in 1967. It's a big parish, almost 44 square kilometres, and in 2000 it was home to just over 5,000 people.

Björlanda Church, a little way from here, stands on north-western Hisingen and has been part of Torslanda-Björlanda parish since 2010. The old parish of Björlanda belonged to the province of Bohuslän and became part of the City of Gothenburg in 1967. In 2000, just over 10,000 people lived in the parish. It covers a large area, almost 44 square kilometres, and in 2000 it had just over 5,000 inhabitants.
Björlanda, kyrkbyn i Björlanda socken, h: Björlanda, the church village of Björlanda parish, has had trouble deciding what it is. Until 2015 it was a locality in its own right, then it became part of Torslanda, in 2018 it was a locality of its own again, and since 2023 it's been counted as part of Gothenburg. Its houses cluster around the church and were mostly built in the 1990s.
Björn och Fulluge högg stenen: Björn and Fulluge carved the stone
Björnberget, som tidigare hette August S: Björnberget, formerly known as August Strindberg's Park, is a stretch of hilly, rocky terrain right in the middle of the villa district. On it is a stone setting that's probably a Bronze Age grave.
Blackebergs tunnelbanestation från 1952: Blackeberg metro station, from 1952, was designed by Peter Celsing in raw concrete. Two-thirds of the platform is outdoors and the rest lies in a rock tunnel. The station building has a thin concrete roof over the ticket hall.
Blackeberg metro station from 1952 was designed in raw concrete by Peter Celsing. Two-thirds of the platform is outdoors and the rest sits in a rock tunnel. The artwork is by Ruben Heleander.
Bland Birkas invånare fanns snickaren Ar: Among Birka's residents was the carpenter Arvid Samsiö, who helped build Villa Birka – the house that gave the area its name – as well as his own house, Villa Samsiö. The first villas were large multi-family houses, often with glazed verandas.
Bland de begravda på kyrkogården finns k: Among those buried in the cemetery are camera pioneer Victor Hasselblad, author Henning Mankell and Per-Olof Ahl, founder of the Kapp-Ahl clothing chain. Gothenburg's first city architect, Carl Wilhelm Carlberg, is also laid to rest here.
Bland de ett 60-tal träd som planeras på: Among the 60 or so trees planned for the square are sequoias and tulip trees, as well as robinia, or black locust. The two parts of the square cover 9,000 square metres between them.
Bland de första Wallenbergarna här var A: Among the first Wallenbergs here were André Oscar Wallenberg and his wife Anna von Sydow; his bronze bust stands behind the mausoleum. Back in the 1600s and 1700s the site was already used as a burial ground for the Malmvik manor.
Bland de första med kyrkklockor: Among the first with church bells
Bland de nyare husen finns Villa Öhman,: Among the newer houses is Villa Öhman, designed by Sven Markelius in 1929, which has been the residence of Kenya's ambassador since 1970. Ralph Erskine designed Villa Nilsson on Duvnäsvägen in 1948.
Bland de sista barnrikehusen: Among the last homes for large families
Bland de stora loppen på Åby finns Åby S: The big races at Åby include Åby Stora Pris and the two trophy races, King Gustaf V's Cup and Queen Silvia's Cup. The track draws around 100,000 visitors a year over some 60 race days.
Bland de största loppen finns Åby Stora: The biggest races include Åby Stora Pris and the two trophy races, Konung Gustaf V:s Pokal and Drottning Silvias Pokal – King Gustaf V's Cup and Queen Silvia's Cup. Since 2024 the Åby World Grand Prix has also been held every four years.
Bland de största loppen på Åbytravet fin: The biggest races at Åby trotting track include Åby Stora Pris, Paralympiatravet and the two trophy races, Konung Gustaf V:s Pokal and Drottning Silvias Pokal. Since 2024, the Åby World Grand Prix has also been held every four years.
Bland dem som bott i Pixbo finns musiker: Former Pixbo residents include the musicians Karin and Olof Dreijer, singer Hanna Ferm, radio personality Erik Blix and chef Frida Ronge. Pixbo is also where the floorball club Pixbo Wallenstam IBK was founded.
Bland dem som bott i Pixbo finns sångers: Former Pixbo residents include the singers Hanna Ferm and Evelyn Jons, the musicians Karin and Olof Dreijer, the radio presenter Erik Blix and the chef Frida Ronge.
Bland dem som deltog i inrättandet av KI: Among those who helped found the Karolinska Institute was the chemist Jöns Jacob Berzelius. His research laid the foundations of the university's scientific profile, and he was counted as a professor at the new institute as early as 1811.
Bland dem som gått på Bromma gymnasium f: Former pupils of Bromma gymnasium, the upper secondary school, include Tomas Lindahl, winner of the 2015 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, the astronaut Christer Fuglesang, the singer Martin "E-type" Eriksson and the Swedish international footballer Viktor Gyökeres.
Bland dem som gått på Farsta gymnasium f: Former pupils of Farsta upper secondary school include the writer Alex Schulman, the world wrestling champion Martin Lidberg and the stand-up comedian Janne Westerlund.
Bland dem som gått på Hulebäcksgymnasiet: Former pupils of Hulebäcksgymnasiet include the metal band Avatar, radio personality Navid Modiri and Hanna Ferm, runner-up in Idol 2017.
Bland dem som vuxit upp i Kåhög finns ar: Among those who grew up in Kåhög are the musician Timo Räisänen, Lars Beckung and Conny Ray. The footballer Gunnar Zacharoff lived here too.
People who grew up in Kåhög include the musician Timo Räisänen, Lars Beckung and Conny Ray. The footballer Gunnar Zacharoff lived here too.
Bland dem som vuxit upp i Kåhög finns mu: People who grew up in Kåhög include the musicians Timo Räisänen, Lars Beckung and Conny Ray. The footballer Gunnar Zacharoff lived here too.
Bland dem som är födda i Lindome finns s: Lindome’s famous sons and daughters include cartoonist Rune Andréasson, actor Jessica Liedberg, director Björn Runge and actor and singer Tage Severin.
Bland eleverna på Farsta gymnasium finns: Former pupils of Farsta gymnasium include the writer Alex Schulman, wrestling world champion Martin Lidberg, stand-up comedian Janne Westerlund and editorial writer Karin Pettersson.
Bland fartygen varvet arbetat med finns: Among the vessels the yard has worked on are M/S Härön from 2015 and the cable ferry Malin, which was rebuilt in 2004–2005.
Bland gästerna fanns Karl XII, Carl von: Guests included Karl XII, Carl Linnaeus and Carl Michael Bellman, who wrote about life at the inn. In 1741 Linnaeus noted that they reached Fittja, "where we waited a long time for horses". Gustav III arrived by boat from Drottningholm.
Bland gästerna på Fittja värdshus finns: Guests at Fittja inn have included Charles XII, Carl Linnaeus and Bellman, who wrote about life here. In 1741 Linnaeus noted: “…we came to Fittja, where we waited long for horses.” The coaching logbooks are full of complaints about worn-out horses.
Bland gårdens ekonomibyggnader finns sta: Among the farm's outbuildings are the stable and the storehouse from the late 1800s. The storehouse is now home to a summer café.
Bland konstnärerna som målat på väggarna: Among the artists who have painted the walls of Snösätra is Daniel Blomqvist, better known as Puppet. The area was originally farmland belonging to Snösätra croft.
Bland museets föremål finns pilspetsar o: Among the museum's finds are arrowheads and stone tools, plus a Stone Age axe discovered at the bus depot in Handen. The smithy turns out hand-forged nails, fittings and Viking-style weapons, among other things.
Bland skolans kända elever finns Louis H: Famous former pupils include Louis Herrey, Petter Ljunggren and Karl Corneliusson.
Bland skolans tidigare elever finns fotb: The school's former pupils include the footballers Pierre Bengtsson and Alexander Milosevic, both of whom have played for AIK, and Brwa Nouri of Östersunds IK.
Bland skulpturerna i Västertorp står Hen: Among Västertorp's many sculptures is Henry Moore's "Internal and External Forms" from 1952–53, standing by the square. You'll also find Allan Runefelt's "The Old Man with the Goat" and Ivar Johnsson's "The Man in the Icelandic Sweater".
Bland Åva gymnasiums tidigare elever fin: Former students at Åva gymnasium include Prime Minister Fredrik Reinfeldt, the literature professor Sara Danius and the TV personality Kristian Luuk. Andreas Hoffer, who played Sune in the Sune films, went to school here too.
Blocket byggdes vid Lidingöbanans då nya: The block was built by what was then the new terminus of the Lidingöbanan railway. It has pale yellow rendered facades, a mansard roof and bay windows topped with little turret-like roofs. In 1919 AGA bought the building and offered the flats to its office staff.
Blocket har drag av jugend och nationalr: The building blends Art Nouveau and National Romantic features, with pale yellow rendered facades and a tall mansard roof. Two bay windows rise from the ground and are topped with little turret-like roofs. In 1919 AGA bought the building for its salaried staff.
Blockhusudden är Djurgårdens östligaste: Blockhusudden is the easternmost tip of Djurgården. This is where Stora Sjötullen, the great maritime customs house, once stood – it's mentioned as early as 1623. Every boat coming in from the archipelago had to stop here and pay a toll before it could reach the city. Along Blockhusringen there are several fine villas, among them Johannisberg, whose summer salon has been listed since 1935. And a little further on, the art treasures of Thielska galleriet, the Thiel Gallery, await.
Blockmakaren Gustaf Andersson tillverkad: The blockmaker Gustaf Andersson made pulley blocks for the navy, and his lathe still stands in the main room, which doubled as his workshop. On the ground floor the widow Emilia Gustafsson rented a room with her five children and worked as a cleaner, washerwoman and newspaper deliverer.
Blockmakarens hus har återställts till h: The blockmaker's house has been restored to how it looked in 1917–1923. So there's no electricity or running water, and the privy stands in the little courtyard. People lived here right up until 1975.
Blommensbergsviadukten invigdes 21 augus: The Blommensberg viaduct opened on 21 August 1966 and is 300 metres long. At its highest it runs 30 metres above the Vinterviken valley, carried by thirteen pairs of round concrete pillars.
Blommensbergsviadukten är 300 meter lång: The Blommensberg viaduct is 300 metres long and stands up to 30 metres above the valley floor. Its 29.5-metre-wide roadway rests on thirteen pairs of round concrete pillars, each 1.5 metres thick.
Blommor och grönsaker till stan: Flowers and vegetables for the city
Bläckfabriken som flyttade till Skansen: The ink factory that moved to Skansen
Blå Stjärnan började den 23 januari 1933: Blå Stjärnan opened on 23 January 1933 as a stable for sick animals in Gamlestaden, run by Svenska Röda Stjärnan. In its first year it treated 645 animals, mostly for simple wound care. By the mid-1960s the figure was around 25,000 a year.
Blå Stället invigdes den 22 april 1979 o: Blå Stället, "the Blue Place", opened on 22 April 1979 and is the oldest cultural centre in Gothenburg's suburbs. In the 1980s the Gothenburg City Theatre opened a branch here, and after two years of renovation the building reopened on 30 August 2014.
Blå gången och Take the A-train: Blå gången and Take the A-train
Blå linjen nås via Blå gången, en drygt: You reach the blue line via Blå gången, the Blue Passage – a tunnel of just over 100 metres with moving walkways. It's home to Carl Fredrik Reuterswärd's Take the A-train from 1984. While the City Line rail tunnel was being built in 2011–2017, the walls were covered with information boards, but the artwork has since been restored.
Blå linjen växer fyra kilometer: The Blue Line grows by four kilometres
Blåsippor och sällsynt sandviol: Hepaticas and the rare sand violet
Blåsut är en utomhusstation som öppnade: Blåsut is an open-air station that opened on 1 October 1950. Alongside the speed stripes, Ann Edholm's 2008 artwork includes an abstract composition that might just make you think of a face.
Blått biotak och mosaikridå: A blue ceiling and a mosaic curtain
Bo Jonsson Grip köpte ön: Bo Jonsson Grip bought the island
Bo Möller gav Lidingö Arena en tydlig ho: Bo Möller gave Lidingö Arena a strong horizontal look, with long ribbons of windows and sun shades in red-painted metal. The red is echoed in the reddish-brown brick and the sheet-metal details. Since 1996 the building has also housed a 31-room hotel.
Bo gård hette från början Vikby, byn i v: Bo farm was originally called Vikby, the village in the bay – the bay being Kyrkviken. Burial grounds nearby show it was already an important farm in prehistoric times. In the Middle Ages it owned most of the farms and crofts on Lidingö.
Bo gård saknar huvudbyggnad, och någon s: Bo gård has no main house, and as far as anyone knows one was never planned. Instead, two yellow L-shaped buildings and two red pavilions enclose a courtyard. The wings were built in 1777.
Bo kvarn, gårdens husbehovskvarn, byggde: Bo kvarn, the farm's own mill, was built in 1816 just east of the farmhouse. It's one of the oldest windmills around Stockholm still standing where it was first built.
Boberg gav Villa Sjöstigen formen av en: Boberg designed Villa Sjöstigen as a larger version of a Norwegian mountain cabin, with tarred shingles on the walls. It’s the only known example of his low-cost villa.
Bocken stor som en tiokrona: A goat the size of a ten-krona coin
Bodal finns på en karta från 1661 som Bo: Bodal appears on a map from 1661 as Boodaal. In the late 18th century the tenant farmer Israel Hansson lived here in a long, single-storey log house, and in 1796 he became churchwarden at Lidingö Church.
Bodal nämns redan 1379 som Bothadall och: Bodal is mentioned as early as 1379, as Bothadall, and began life as a farm. The blocks of flats along Bodalsvägen were built in 1952–1955 and have been classed as historically valuable and worth preserving.
Bodals gård byggdes om 1934–1935 till bo: In 1934–1935 the main house of the old Bodal farm was converted into a home for Supreme Court justice Birger Wedberg. It was later renovated and became part of the school, which was completed in 2009 with a new building designed by Gillberg Arkitekter.
Bodals gård byggdes om 1934–35 för justi: Bodal manor was remodelled in 1934–35 for Supreme Court justice Birger Wedberg in the 1920s Classicism known as Swedish Grace – the same style as Carl Malmsten's furniture. The rusticated corners, on the other hand, were the height of fashion in the 17th and 18th centuries.
Bodals kyrka började som ett kapell 1972: Bodal Church began as a chapel in 1972 and became a church in 1983. In the 2010s damp damage was discovered; the church closed in 2017 and was demolished in October 2018.
Bodde här bara tre år: They lived here only three years
Boden vid nyodlingen: The hut by the new clearing
Bogserbåten Sven byggdes 1897 av Götebor: The tugboat Sven was built in 1897 by Göteborgs mekaniska verkstad as the icebreaker Björn, with Åhus as her home port. She served there until 1963, apart from a spell in the navy during the Second World War.
Boholmen är Kyrkvikens enda ö och blir s: Boholmen is the only island in Kyrkviken bay and grows a little larger every year thanks to post-glacial land rise. Locally it's known as Kärleksön, Love Island. You reach it by a small bridge, and there's a picnic and barbecue spot on the east side.
Boholmen är Kyrkvikens enda ö och kallad: Boholmen is the only island in Kyrkviken bay and was known locally as Kärleksön – the Island of Love. Thanks to land rise it keeps getting bigger: maps from the early 19th century show only a shallow patch here.
Boktornet i kupolen: The book tower in the dome
Bolindermuseet grundades av Kåre Anderss: The Bolinder Museum was founded by Kåre Andersson, who began collecting objects from Bolinders in the mid-1980s. Today the museum owns about 1,000 items, including Trim outboard motors.
Bolinders startade 1844 på Kungsholmen o: Bolinders was founded in 1844 on Kungsholmen and became known for steam engines and wood-burning stoves. The foundry also turned out kitchenware such as frying pans, pots, waffle irons and mincers. In the 1950s it made fridges and electric cookers.

Bollmora centrum invigdes 1965 med gågat: Bollmora centrum opened in 1965 with pedestrian streets and was converted into an indoor mall in the early 1990s. Just before it reopened in 1992, several of the buildings were hit by a major fire, and the opening was delayed.
Bollmora centrum invigdes 1965 som ett l: Bollmora centrum opened in 1965 as a small suburban centre with pedestrian streets. In the early 1990s it was converted into a mall, but just before the reopening in 1992 a major fire swept through several buildings and delayed the opening.
Bollmora centrum invigdes den 12 septemb: Bollmora centrum opened on 12 September 1965 as a modest suburban centre with pedestrian streets. In 1992 the new centre opened as a shopping mall under the name Tyresö Centrum. The old Bollmora farm stood roughly where Willys supermarket is today.
Bollmora centrum opened on 12 September 1965 as a small suburban centre with pedestrian streets. In 1992 the new centre opened as an indoor shopping mall and was named Tyresö Centrum.
Bollmora centrum opened on 12 September 1965 as a modest suburban centre with pedestrian streets. In 1992 the new centre opened as a shopping mall, and the name changed to Tyresö Centrum.
Bollmora gård låg ungefär där det först: Bollmora farm stood roughly where a Shell petrol station was later built and, since 2014, a Willys supermarket, at the junction of Njupkärrsvägen and Industrivägen. Until the 1950s Bollmora was a village.

Bollmora farm stood roughly where a Shell petrol station was first built and where, since 2014, there's been a Willys supermarket. Until the 1950s Bollmora was a village. The town centre opened in 1965 and became a shopping mall in 1992.
Bollmora gård låg ungefär i korsningen N: Bollmora farm stood roughly where Njupkärrsvägen meets Industrivägen. A Shell petrol station took its place, and since 2014 there's been a Willys supermarket on the spot. Bollmora was still a village until the 1950s.

Bollmora farm stood roughly where Njupkärrsvägen meets Industrivägen. A Shell petrol station later occupied the site until it was demolished in 2012, and since 2014 there has been a Willys supermarket here.
Bollmora was a village until the 1950s. A change in the law in 1959, known as Lex Bollmora, allowed municipal housing companies to build in other municipalities, and Stockholm's companies started building here straight away, since land was in short supply in the capital.
Bollmora var faktiskt en egen tätort åre: From 1965 to 1974, Bollmora was actually a town in its own right, but these days most people call the area Tyresö centrum. There's a glass-roofed shopping centre with 74 shops and a library with its own exhibition hall. Towering over it all is Tyresö View, 82 metres and 23 storeys high – in 2016, the fourth-tallest residential building in the whole of Stockholm County.
Bollmora var åren 1965–1974 en egen täto: From 1965 to 1974, Bollmora was a town in its own right, but these days most people call the area Tyresö centrum. This is where you'll find the glass-roofed shopping centre with 74 shops, the municipal offices and a library with its own exhibition hall. A little further off is Tyresövallen – formerly Bollmoravallen – the home ground of both Tyresö FF and the Tyresö Royal Crowns, with room for about 2,700 spectators.
Bollmora, som Tyresö centrum egentligen: Bollmora, the real name of Tyresö centrum, was a locality in its own right from 1965 to 1974, and it had 16,566 inhabitants in 2010. A few minutes away is Bollmoradalen Church, the parish church of Tyresö parish, which covers the whole municipality. Bollmora grew fast in the 1960s thanks to Lex Bollmora, a law that allowed Stockholm's housing companies to build here.

Bollmora – the real name of Tyresö centrum – was a town in its own right from 1965 to 1974 and had 16,566 residents in 2010. A few minutes away is Bollmoradalen church, the parish church of Tyresö parish, which covers the whole municipality. And a little further on, Tyresö View rises 82 metres – one of the tallest residential buildings in the county.
Bollmoradalens kyrka i gult tegel ritade: The yellow-brick Bollmoradalen Church was designed by Bo Sahlin and completed in 1973. Its 31-stop organ was destroyed in a fire in 1988. In 1993 a new 32-stop mechanical organ, built in Torshälla, was inaugurated.
Bollmoras snabba utbyggnad möjliggjordes: Bollmora's rapid growth was made possible by Lex Bollmora, a 1959 change in the law that allowed municipal housing companies to build in other municipalities. Stockholm's companies started building here straight away, since the capital was short of land to build on.

Boo breder ut sig på västra delen av ön: Boo spreads across the western part of the island of Värmdö, east of the Skurusundet strait. It was a town in its own right until 2015, but since then it has merged with the Stockholm urban area – so in practice, the big city has made it across the water. Not far from here is the glittering Kocktorpssjön, a small lake in the district.

Bostadshusen är byggda i liggande timmer: The houses are built of horizontal timber with vertical panelling in neoclassical style, and the large main house has more than ten rooms. An inventory in 1899 also listed three privies, a brewhouse and two summerhouses.
Bostadshuset 79&Park, alldeles intill, ä: The residential building right next door, 79&Park, was designed by the Danish firm Bjarke Ingels Group and was nominated for Stockholm's Building of the Year in 2019. A little way off, in a 1920s warehouse in Frihamnen, the free port, the financier Robert Weil and museum director David Neuman founded what became the Magasin III art museum in 1987. Since May 2024, however, the museum no longer runs public activities in Stockholm.
Bostadshuset från cirka 1821 har faluröd: The farmhouse, dating from around 1821, has Falu red wooden panelling and white windows. Inside, the joinery, tiled stoves and local country furniture are beautifully preserved, and the kitchen still has its big iron range and bread oven.
Bostadshuset på Bäckebols gård byggdes 1: The farmhouse at Bäckebol was built in 1764 and gained another storey in the 1830s. South of the farm lies the Friedländer Cemetery, which has been a private burial ground since the 1770s.
The farmhouse at Bäckebol was built in 1764 and gained an extra storey in the 1830s. Just south of the farm lies the Friedländer Cemetery, a private burial ground since the 1770s.
Bostadslängan är cirka 135 meter lång, o: The residential range is about 135 metres long, and a passage with star vaulting in bare brick runs right through the middle. The architect, Erik Hahr, gave the building the same heavy stone architecture as Dalén's Villa Ekbacken.
Bostadsområdet Agnesberg började byggas: Building began on the Agnesberg housing area in 1987. As Järvastaden took shape, new homes went up in 2010 at Fridensborgsvägen 9–17, designed by Mats Carlsson of Lindberg Stenberg Arkitekter.
Bostadsområdet Alphyddan byggdes 1960 ti: The Alphyddan housing area was built between 1960 and 1965 to designs by the architects Backström and Reinius, with the Svindersberg nature area as its green neighbour to the east. A little further on is Dieselverkstaden, the Diesel Workshop, where Atlas Diesel made diesel engines until 1951. Today it's a cultural centre with a library and cinema. Next door, Sickla Köpkvarter has around 160 shops and restaurants.
Bostadsområdet Annedal vid Bällstaån har: The Annedal housing area by the Bällstaån stream is named after a plot of land owned in the 1880s by Anna Augusta Wickman-Olsson. Around 2,000 flats went up here between 2008 and 2013, and at its north-western end the area is rounded off by the Mattisborgen block and its tower. Across Ulvsundavägen lies Solvalla, the trotting track.
Bostadsområdet Krusboda, i området här o: The Krusboda housing estate, all around us, went up in the first half of the 1970s, between 1970 and 1975, and has a school of its own, Krusboda skola. A longer walk away is Barnsjön, a small forest lake just under nine metres deep, with a public swimming spot. It's part of the Tyresån catchment, so the water here eventually finds its way into the Tyresån river.
Bostadsområdet Myrängen-Högmora ligger i: The Myrängen-Högmora neighbourhood nestles into Kynäsberget hill, between the western end of Magelungen and lake Trehörningen. Högmora is mostly holiday cottages with a few year-round homes, and it became a district in its own right in 2018. Myrängen has terraced houses and a school for the youngest children. Beyond them, forest and hills take over – an area of national importance for outdoor recreation.
Bostadsområdet Västra Smedshagen invigde: The Västra Smedshagen housing area opened in 1987. It was designed by the architect Johan Nyrén, with four-storey buildings grouped around enclosed courtyards.
Bostadsområdet byggdes 1982–1988 på en p: The housing estate was built in 1982–1988 on a plateau around Rissne torg. With no through road it’s quiet, and some sixty sculptures by well-known Swedish artists are dotted between the buildings.
Bostadsområdet byggdes mellan 1969 och 1: The housing estate went up between 1969 and 1974, spreading south of the Alebäcken stream, which had previously marked Rävekärr's boundary. The first tenants moved in in 1973, and the school and nursery were finished in December 1974.
Bostadsrättsföreningen fick namnet Atlan: The housing cooperative got the name Atlantis by mistake. It was started by four architects who were looking for somewhere to live in 1951. They were working on the Vällingby project at the City Planning Office, and each of them moved into a terraced house here.
Bostadsrättsföreningen kallades av misst: The housing co-operative was named Atlantis by mistake. It was founded by four architects who were themselves looking for homes, worked on the Vällingby project and then each moved into a terraced house on the block.
Bostäder ovanpå gallerian: Homes on top of the mall
Bostäderna på Söderlingska ängen byggdes: The homes on Söderlingska ängen were built in 1936–1939 to Uno Åhrén's town plan, with rows of landshövdingehus – Gothenburg's typical stone-and-wood tenements – around a central park. One newspaper debate piece called it ‘an open, socialist town plan’.
Bostäderna speglade Gustaf Daléns social: The homes reflected Gustaf Dalén's social ideals, with plenty of light and air. The flats had electricity and flush toilets from the start, and on the ground floor were one of Lidingö's first co-op shops, a cinema and a reading room.
Botkyrka folkhögskola har särskilt locka: Botkyrka folk high school – an adult education college – has proved especially popular with women who have been some way outside the job market. Its textile course and women's course have been a springboard into further study and working life.
Botkyrka-Salem Hemslöjdsförening har öpp: The Botkyrka-Salem Handicraft Society holds open days at Nedre Söderby, with crafts for sale and coffee served. In summer, cows and sheep graze the meadows below the farm.
Botkyrkahallen tar omkring 1 500 åskådar: Botkyrkahallen holds about 1,500 spectators, and the adjoining halls are used for table tennis, strength sports and gymnastics, among other things. Since it opened it has also been the sports hall for Brunnaskolan, whose own hall burnt down in 1996.
Botkyrkahallen, några minuter härifrån,: A few minutes from here is Botkyrkahallen, opened by King Carl XVI Gustaf in summer 2000 and home to Balrog IK's men's team. Not far off is S:t Botvids gymnasium, a sixth-form school best known for its contemporary circus programme run together with Cirkus Cirkör. Former pupils include the artist Dogge Doggelito and the politician Ibrahim Baylan.
Botkyrkamonumentet är ett block av rödak: The Botkyrka monument is a 172-centimetre block of reddish sandstone, shaped like a Romanesque church or a reliquary. Among other things, the relief shows Björn rising from the grave while an angel sounds a trumpet. It's probably the first time this kind of leaf ornament appears in Scandinavia.
Botten som aldrig hittades: The bottom no one ever found
Bottenfaunan i tjärnen anses ha höga nat: The pond's bottom-dwelling wildlife is considered highly valuable. Rare species live here, including the water bee, the flat valve snail and a water boatman called Sigara scotti.
Bottenvåningen ritades för ett postkonto: The ground floor was designed for a post office, now closed. At one end of the building there was a konditori, a café-bakery, and a restaurant occupies the spot today.
Bragevägens hållplats öppnade 1924 och s: The Bragevägen stop opened in 1924 and closed in 1976, when SL shut the line to Eddavägen. The old embankment survives as a footpath, but right by Bragevägen it has become a car park for the parish hall, known as Änglagaraget – the Angel Garage.

Brandmännen på Vällingby brandstation är: The firefighters at Vällingby fire station are specially trained in roof ventilation and abseiling, in other words high-altitude climbing. The station covers an area stretching from Abrahamsberg in the south to Lövsta in the north.
Brandstation där gården brann: A fire station where the manor burned
Brandstation med frisör: A fire station with a hairdresser

Brandstationen ritades av Gunnar Lené oc: The fire station was designed by Gunnar Lené and opened in 1956 as Enskede fire station, but was renamed after Farsta parish was formed in 1957. It also has a crew that can be flown out by helicopter to carry out rescues and fight fires at sea.
Brann två gånger, prisades tredje: Burned twice, celebrated the third time
Branting blev 1920 Sveriges första socia: In 1920 Branting became Sweden's first Social Democratic prime minister. The following year, 1921, he shared the Nobel Peace Prize with Christian Lange for his work in the League of Nations.
Branting står i övernaturlig storlek och: A larger-than-life Branting stands delivering a May Day speech, flanked by August Palm and Axel Danielsson. At his left foot sits a little fairy with flowers – in the sculptor Carl Eldh's words, 'spring awakening among the flowers'.
Bred gata för ett tåg: A street wide enough for a train
Bredvid anläggningen ligger gula femvåni: Next to the complex are yellow five-storey blocks and green two-storey houses. Many people assume the housing area is called Högsätra too, not least because of Högsätravägen – but it isn't: it all belongs to the larger area of Gångsätra.
Bredvid kvarnen finns en dansbana och en: Beside the mill is an open-air dance floor and a hut selling coffee whenever there's an event on.
Bredvid ligger U 81, som aldrig blev kla: Next to it is U 81, which was never finished. The serpent band is uneven and the lines so shallow they're hard to see. The only legible word is the man's name Ärnmund, and the carver was hardly as experienced as the master behind U 80.
Bredvid ligger ytterligare en hall som f: Next door is a second rink, funded by Högsätra Ishall AB, a company owned by Lidingö Vikings Hockey Club. The City of Lidingö runs it, and the company rents it out to both the city and local clubs.
Bredäng är ordentligt kuperat: Bredängss: Bredäng is seriously hilly: Bredängsskolan, the school, sits 62 metres above sea level, and Bredängshemmet, the care home, a full 67 metres. Bredängsparken, next to the centre, is one of the biggest parks in the district, and drinking alcohol has been banned there because things used to get rowdy. Bredäng Church doesn't have a building of its own – it's in a parish hall at one end of the shopping centre.
Bredängs centrum invigdes 1965 och har e: Bredäng's centre opened in 1965 and holds an important place in Stockholm's planning history. It was the first fully realised example of an all-in-one centre, with shops, a school, a library and a church grouped around the metro station.
Bredängshallen och Bredängsskolan ritade: Bredängshallen and Bredängsskolan were designed by the same firm, Höjer & Ljungqvist, and completed in 1966. The hall was meant to serve both the public and the school as its gym and swimming pool, with a 25-metre pool and a sauna. The baths are sometimes called Bredängsbadet.
Bremerska villan byggdes 1912 för sillha: The Bremer Villa was built in 1912 for the herring merchant Börjesson, reportedly with timber salvaged from the wrecked ship Svolder. It served as both a bank and a guesthouse before the smuggling king Ernst Bremer bought it in 1927. At its height, his fleet numbered 16 vessels.
Bremnäs är en liten by med ett lite förv: Bremnäs is a little village with a slightly confusing life in the statistics. Statistics Sweden counted it as a small locality for fifteen years – until it had grown together with its neighbour Stora Lycke, and the two suddenly became a single urban area with the double name Lycke och Bremnäs. The area belongs to Lycke parish, on the coast south-east of Marstrand, and the parish church, Lycke Church, stands not far from here.
Brevik betyder \"breda viken\" och skrev: Brevik means 'the broad bay' and was written Bredewijk in Jöns Ulfsson's land register of 1498. On Lidingö's oldest known map, from 1661, the main house is marked with a tower and a flag – the symbol of a manor.
Breviks gård, som gav området sitt namn,: Brevik farm, which gave the area its name, dated back to the 1300s. Its last main house was pulled down in 1987, and Brevik's shopping centre now stands in its place. Next to it is Blocket, built in the 1910s and one of Lidingö's oldest blocks of flats. In 1905 the farm's owner offered to pay for a small elementary school, today number 7 Banvägen. A little way off is the Abenius villa, designed by Ferdinand Boberg.

Breviks gård, the manor that gave the area its name, went back to the 14th century. Its last main building was pulled down in 1987, and Brevik centre stands there now. Next to it is Blocket, built in 1914–1915 and one of Lidingö's oldest apartment buildings. In 1905 the estate's owner offered to fund a small primary school – today Banvägen 7. Not far away is Abeniuska villan, the Abenius Villa, designed by Ferdinand Boberg.
Bristol var från början bara biograf. 19: Bristol started out as just a cinema. In 1977 it was rebuilt so it could double as a theatre, and in 2018 it became a cultural venue. The auditorium seats 144 and is run by two volunteer associations offering film, dance, music and theatre.
Bristol ägdes från början av Algot Myrgr: Bristol was originally owned by Algot Myrgren and was purely a cinema. In 1977 it was converted for theatre, and since 2018 it has been run by two non-profit associations, offering film, dance, music and theatre. The auditorium has 144 seats.
Bristol ägdes från början av en Algot My: Bristol was originally owned by one Algot Myrgren. In 1977 it was rebuilt so that it could double as a theatre, and since 2018 it has been run by voluntary associations offering film, dance, music and theatre. The auditorium has 144 seats.
Broar var en specialitet för Bergsunds M: Bridges were a speciality of Bergsunds Mekaniska Verkstad, which supplied some 800 railway and road bridges. One of the last was the new Liljeholmsbron in 1928. In 1860 the works had more than 500 workers, and by 1902 it employed 1,075 people.
Bromma flygplats invigdes den 13 maj 193: Bromma Airport was opened by King Gustaf V on 13 May 1936 and was the first airport in Europe with asphalt runways. Its old hangars were the largest in Northern Europe in their day, and today they house the Bromma Blocks shopping centre – where the first hypermarket moved in as early as 1972.
Bromma flygplats invigdes i maj 1936 av: Bromma Airport was opened by King Gustaf V in May 1936 and was the first airport in Europe with asphalt runways. Its old hangars were the largest in northern Europe in their day, and today they house the Bromma Blocks shopping centre. The first hypermarket moved in as early as 1972.
Bromma kyrkas runda mittdel byggdes 1168: The round central section of Bromma church was built in 1168 as a defensive tower along Lake Mälaren, together with the round churches in Solna and Munsö. Women and children were to shelter in the Maiden's Chamber above the nave while the men defended from a parapet at the very top.
Bromma kyrkskola används än i dag för år: Bromma's old church school is still used today for years 1 and 2. The old stoves that once heated it are still there. The Lucia celebrations are held in Bromma Church.
Brommadepån ritades av ingenjör Sven Ves: The Bromma depot was designed by the engineer Sven Vestergren and the architect Erik Vestergren. Until 2010 buses were kept here too. Since the Tvärbanan light rail cars moved to the Ulvsunda depot in 2016, it has served the trams of the Nockebybanan line.
Brommadepån, som stod klar 1944, byggdes: Brommadepån, the tram depot completed in 1944, stands where there was emergency housing from 1917, and trams from the Ängbybanan, Nockebybanan and Tvärbanan lines have all been parked here. Not far away, in the summer of 1927, no fewer than 29 brand-new villas along Ekorrvägen were put on show at the Bygge och Bo housing exhibition in Äppelviken. The garden suburb of Ulvsunda next door was originally called Kungsholms villastad.
Brommahöjden har bara tre lägenheter per: Brommahöjden has just three flats per floor to keep its silhouette slim. The white band framing the gable balconies carries on over the roof, so from a distance the building can look like an upside-down U. Some of the balcony glass is pastel-tinted to give the façade a playful touch.
Bromsten hade en egen station på järnväg: Bromsten had its own station on the Stockholm–Västerås railway, with a small centre that boasted a post office, an ironmonger’s and a milliner’s. The station closed in February 1968, just before the commuter trains to Kungsängen started running.
Bromstens gårds huvudbyggnad revs sommar: The main building of Bromsten farm was demolished in summer 1964 to make room for more traffic on Duvbovägen. The plan was to move the house to Åsögatan in Södermalm, but it turned out to be in far too poor a condition.
Bron 30 meter över dalen: The bridge 30 metres above the valley
Bron från 1915 var Nordeuropas största b: When it was built in 1915, the bridge was the largest concrete bridge in northern Europe, with a 72-metre arch. The mould was supported by scaffolding on an artificial island in the middle of the shipping lane. When the scaffolding came down, the central arch sank by just four millimetres.
Bron i inskriften förde resenärerna på G: The bridge mentioned in the inscription carried travellers on Göta landsväg, the great road south, over a stream in the marshy Glömsta valley – an important link between Stockholm and southern Sweden. The carving was once painted, probably in black, red and white, and stood out clearly to everyone who passed.
Bron på vägen till Drottningholm: The bridge on the way to Drottningholm
Bron saknade först officiellt namn. P4 S: At first the bridge had no official name. In 2015 the radio station P4 Stockholm held a naming competition that drew over 1,500 suggestions, among them Ryggraden (the Backbone) and Årstafrun (the Lady of Årsta). Älvsjöbågen won with 1,479 of the 3,201 votes.

Bron som väntade på plank: The bridge that waited for planks
Bron vilar på cirka 800 pålar, mellan 20: The bridge rests on some 800 piles, each between 20 and 50 metres long, and around 20,000 cubic metres of concrete went into it. The slabs were so big that they had to be cooled with water coils after casting.
Bron är svetsad av upp till 25 millimete: The bridge is welded from stainless-steel plates up to 25 millimetres thick, which were then glass-blasted. It was made in Trollhättan and transported to Stockholm in three sections, and silver sand has been mixed into the asphalt on the deck.
Bron är två parallella broar, 255 meter: The bridge is actually two parallel bridges, 255 metres long, with five ">"-shaped concrete brackets supporting the steel girders. The piers were designed by the architect Jonas Björkman to give a sense of lightness.
Brons många liv: A bridge rebuilt again and again
Bronsportföljen Attachéväska R.W. finns: The bronze briefcase Attachéväska R.W. stands in several places, including the UN headquarters in New York, Budapest and outside the Arvfurstens palats in Stockholm. It depicts a briefcase of the kind Raoul Wallenberg carried in Budapest in 1944–1945.
Bronsstatyn Ung man skapades av Astrid N: Astrid Noack made the bronze statue Young Man back in 1948, but it only arrived in Kungsladugård in 1968, on the corner of Ståthållaregatan and Fågelfängaregatan. The beach ball by the paddling pool is much younger – it was put in place in 2007.
Bronsyxan på museet: The bronze axe in the museum
Bropelare i hangartaket: Bridge girders in the hangar roof
Broströmska stiftelsens hus byggdes efte: The Broström Foundation's buildings were funded by a donation from the heirs of Axel and Mathilda Broström. The hundred-odd flats were meant for employees – or their widows – in shipping, the port, customs, the railways and the post office. Tenants with links to the sea still live here today.
Brostugan byggdes som bostad åt brovakte: Brostugan was built as a home for the bridge-keeper when Gustav III had the first bridge to Drottningholm built in 1787. His job was to open the bridge and collect tolls from those crossing, and the bridge-keeper lived here right up to 1931.
Brostugan på Kärsön har anor från 1700-t: Brostugan, the Bridge Cottage, on Kärsön dates from the 18th century and stands beside Nockebybron, a swing bridge across Lake Mälaren. The bridge has recently been given a new lease of life: the Swedish Transport Administration has moved the footpath and cycle path to the other side and added a reversible lane that switches direction with the flow of traffic. The work is part of building the Stockholm Bypass, Förbifart Stockholm.
Brostugan var från början värdshus med g: Brostugan, the bridge house, was originally an inn with guest rooms, and the bridge toll was collected in a shed by the bridgehead. Lars Fresk later also built Lidingöbro värdshus on the Djurgården side, which opened in 1823 when his son Olof celebrated his wedding there.
Brotorp became part of Sundbyberg in 1949. The first residents moved in in 2007, and terraced houses, semi-detached houses and blocks of flats are still going up.
Brotorp nämns första gången 1677 och het: Brotorp is first mentioned in 1677, when it was called Brostugan. It was one of around twenty crofts for estate labourers under Skarpnäck manor, and it still stands inside the Nacka nature reserve, near the Ältaån stream.
Brotorp är Sundbybergs ytmässigt minsta: Brotorp is Sundbyberg's smallest district by area, just three per cent of the municipality. For a long time the land was used by the military, and not far from here was Järva skjutfält, an army training ground on Järvafältet. Today Brotorp is Sundbyberg's share of Järvastaden, a large new urban development it shares with Solna.
Brottet blev naturminne 1972 och var nat: The quarry was declared a natural monument in 1972 and was a 1.2-hectare nature reserve from 2011 to 2016. Since 2016 it has been part of the larger Änggårdsbergen nature reserve.
Browallshof är den enda av områdets malm: Browallshof is the only one of the area’s old suburban manor houses still standing. The Clas på Hörnet inn had been closed since the 1860s, but in 1984 it reopened in the old main building.
Brukets arbetarbostäder fick namn efter: The mill workers' housing was named after letters of the alphabet, such as Littera A, though locals had their own names for the buildings, like Smålänningegården. Young women who moved here for work lived in Flickhemmet, the girls' hostel.
Brunnaskolans egen idrottshall brann ned: Brunnaskolan's own sports hall burned down in 1996. Since Botkyrkahallen opened, the school has held its PE lessons there. The neighbouring rooms are also used for table tennis, strength sports and gymnastics.
Brunnen är en attrapp: The well is just for show
Brunnsbokyrkan från 1972 ritades av Rolf: Designed by Rolf Bergh, Brunnsbo Church from 1972 is meant to recall a tent – a nod to the tabernacle the Israelites carried through the wilderness. Seen from above it forms an eight-pointed star, held up by two crossed glulam beams.
Brunnsparken är stadens hjärta för kolle: Brunnsparken is the beating heart of the city's public transport – almost every tram line passes through here. Right next to it is Gustaf Adolfs torg, with a statue of the king who founded Gothenburg in 1621. The city was built by Dutch engineers, and that's why Gothenburg has canals: the Dutch knew how to build on clay.
Brunnstorpsnäs är en liten ort vid Nordr: Brunnstorpsnäs is a little village on the banks of the Nordre älv river on Hisingen, with just 87 residents in 2023. Small but important – this is where the Kornhall ferry crosses the river to Kornhall in Kungälv municipality. The village is in the former parish of Säve, around two kilometres north-west of Säve itself.
Bruno Wendel, Hennigs svärson, ledde fab: Bruno Wendel, Hennig's son-in-law, ran the factories for many years and built himself a white wooden villa, almost a castle, to the north of them. Since 1908 the villa has housed Wendelsberg folk high school, which even has its own theatre where the students put on shows.
Bruno Wendels trähus ritades av arkitekt: Bruno Wendel’s wooden house was designed by the architect Adrian C. Peterson. It needed renovating as early as the beginning of the 1900s, and a major rebuild in the 1930s added 30 rooms that are still used as boarding accommodation.
Brunt tegel och glas mot torget: Brown brick and glass facing the square
Bryggan som lyftes på plats: The jetty that was lifted into place
Bryggaren Anders Berg köpte en gård i En: The brewer Anders Berg bought a farm in Eneby village in 1769. Tradition has it that he combined Eneby with his surname to make Enebyberg, but that's never been confirmed. Others think the berg was a hill that was later blasted away.
Bryggaren som döpte gården: The brewer who named the farm
Bryggaren som kanske gav namnet: The brewer who may have given the name
Bryggaren som köpte godset: The brewer who bought the estate
Bryggaren som köpte grannen: The brewer who bought the neighbour

Bryggeri och ishus i Skarvik: Brewery and ice house in Skarvik
Bryggeriet lades ner 1945, men varumärke: The brewery closed in 1945, but the Club Soda brand lived on with Apotekarnes, Pripps and Carlsberg before disappearing in 2006. The spring was restored in 2009, and today you can pump up salty water with a hand pump.
Bräcke by ligger i Torsby socken, fyra k: The village of Bräcke lies in Torsby parish, four kilometres from the Kattegat coast and seven kilometres north of where the Nordre älv river meets the sea. At the Råckeröd pass, about 700 metres east of the village, stands Bräcke soldattorp, a soldier's croft from the 1830s. It's now a local heritage museum – and it was actually moved there from a spot north of the village.
Bräcke cemetery has a grim history. Cholera hit Sweden hard in the 19th century, and the disease entered the country through Gothenburg. This cemetery was opened during the epidemic of 1834 and stayed in use until 1886, when Lundby church was completed with its own churchyard. It's now a protected ancient monument, and since 2017 it has been a memorial garden for scattering ashes.
Bräcke småstugeområde från 1934 var Göte: Built in 1934, the Bräcke småstuge estate of small self-build homes was Gothenburg's first. The houses were strictly functionalist and standardised, and the two-storey ones looked so much like boxes stood on end that they earned nicknames like 'sugar box' and 'matchbox'.
Bräckelinjens banvall har legat nästan o: The old embankment of the Bräcke line has been left almost untouched since the tracks were removed. Gothenburg’s current comprehensive plan includes proposals to rebuild the line.
Brännö kyrkogård är från 1850 och ägdes: Brännö churchyard dates from 1850 and was owned by the village's landholders' association until 1975. It lies on the northern part of the island and holds 122 graves.
Brännöborna har använt Källö som fårbete: The people of Brännö have used Källö to graze their sheep. Just to the west lies privately owned Lilla Källö, which today has just two summer cottages.
Bråk med militären om bullret: Clashing with the army over noise
Bråket om Tre Kronor: The row over the Three Crowns
Bråvallavägens station planeras att lägg: Bråvallavägen station is due to close when the Roslagsbanan line is extended to T-Centralen. It has few passengers and sits on a slope where it's hard for trains to start and stop – skipping it saves a minute.
Bråvallavägens station, en bit härifrån,: Bråvallavägen station, not far from here, opened in 1909. It's a small station, with about 150 people getting on there on an ordinary winter weekday. In 2013 two trains collided there while carriages were being coupled. In the other direction is Altorp station, in use since 1910, a passing point on the single-track stretch towards Näsbypark.
Bröderna Börje och Folke Claeson fick id: The brothers Börje and Folke Claeson came up with the idea after visiting trade fairs on the Continent. They rented the Royal Tennis Hall, and the first fair opened in 1942. The exhibition halls in Älvsjö were built on a field that was once Lake Brännkyrkasjön.

The brothers Börje and Folke Claeson got the idea after visiting trade fairs in Europe. The first fair opened in 1942 in the Royal Tennis Hall and was named S:t Eriks-Mässan after Stockholm's patron saint, St Erik.
Bröderna Gert och Göran Bjerendahl var i: For several decades the brothers Gert and Göran Bjerendahl were among Sweden's top archers. Göran competed at four Olympic Games, finishing sixth at best. Gert went to two Olympics and came eighth with the Swedish team in 1988.

Bröllopsmiddag under eken: A wedding feast under the oak
Bullegummans hus ägdes en tid av Götebor: For a time, the Bun Lady's house was owned by the City of Gothenburg and used as a reception centre for refugees. The street got its present name in 1965.
Bullegummans hus är i ursprungligt skick: The Bun Lady's house survives in its original state, and the hatch in the wall where she sold her buns was still there in 2011. For a time the house was owned by the City of Gothenburg and served as a reception centre for refugees.
Bulleluckan finns kvar: The bun hatch is still there
Bullhuset blev flyktingsluss: The bun house became a refugee centre
Burås kvarn är en hättekvarn, eller kjor: Burås kvarn is a smock mill (also known as a 'skirt mill'), the most common type of windmill in Bohuslän. Its octagonal body tapers towards the top. The sails are fixed to the revolving cap, which looks like an upturned boat, and is turned into the wind with long poles.
Burås kvarn är en hättekvarn, eller ”kjo: Burås mill is a cap mill, or 'skirt mill', the most common type of windmill in Bohuslän. The sails are mounted on a rotating cap shaped rather like an upturned boat, and tarred poles are used to turn it into the wind.
Burås kvarn är en hättekvarn, även kalla: Burås mill is a cap mill – also known as a 'skirt mill' – the most common type of windmill in Bohuslän. The octagonal body tapers towards the top, and the sails are fixed to a rotating cap shaped rather like an upturned boat. Long poles were used to turn the cap into the wind.
Buss längs Söder och ut till Mälarhöjden: A bus ride across Södermalm and out to Mälarhöjden, where Jakobs stege (Jacob's Ladder) leads down to Lake Mälaren and the Bellmanskällan spring bubbles. On the way back, hop off on Södermalm for the highest natural viewpoint in the inner city.
Buss och båt till stugan: By bus and boat to the cabin
Buss till Ropsten, Lidingöbanan till AGA: Bus to Ropsten, the Lidingö line to AGA's yellow optics tower, and then a long boat trip along the shores of Lidingö, Nacka and Djurgården back to Nybroplan.
Bussarna mot Marstrand, Orust, Stenungsu: Buses to Marstrand, Orust, Stenungsund and Tjörn leave from the travel centre, and right next door is Kongahälla Center, with around a hundred shops and restaurants, opened in 2019. The E6 motorway roars past alongside. A little further away is Oasen, a swimming pool and ice rink built after the old public baths burned down. It has a 25-metre pool and a rehab pool with warmer water.
Bussdepån som blev villor: The bus depot that became villas
Bussen går via Sickla och Nacka kvarn, d: The bus runs via Sickla and Nacka kvarn, where the Nacka ström stream drops 18 metres in 500 metres.
Bussen går över Kungsholmen förbi Kungsh: The bus crosses Kungsholmen, passing Kungsholmstorg, where Otto Strandman's fountain sculpture Vesslan (the Weasel) has stood since 1912.
Bussenhus var Nälstas dragontorp och näm: Bussenhus was the dragoon croft of Nälsta, first mentioned in 1725. According to the Spånga local history society, it was built by the farming family of Hässelby, who were obliged to supply a mounted soldier for the Swedish army.
Busshallen blev funkisvillor: From bus depot to functionalist villas
Busslinjen som började 1922: The bus route that began in 1922
Busstation under bron: A bus station under the bridge
Bussterminal ovanpå spåren: A bus terminal above the tracks
Bussterminalen ritades av den norske ark: The bus terminal was designed by the Norwegian architect Niels Torp and opened in 1996. The walls and roof are all glass and steel, forming a bright waiting hall 150 metres long. The same year it won the Kasper Salin Prize, Sweden's top architecture award.
Bussterminalen vid tunnelbanan togs i br: The bus terminal by the metro opened in 1968, mainly for buses to Ekerö. It replaced the old terminus for the Mälaröbussarna buses at Kronobergsparken near Fridhemsplan in the city centre.
Butiksbiträdet som gifte in sig: The shop assistant who married in
Bybrunnen framför stugan är bara en attr: The village well in front of the cottage is only a replica. The park also has a farm bell from 1963, rung at New Year, and a bronze bust of Emric Öhman, one of the founders of the villa community.
Bygden här på sydöstra Färingsö har gaml: The countryside here in south-eastern Färingsö has a long history. Mörby village can be traced back to the mid-1400s, and neighbouring Ekeby is mentioned as early as 1342, when Eskil Petersson and his wife Cecilia exchanged land with Vårfruberga convent. At Troxhammar stands a Viking Age granite runestone a full 2.2 metres tall.
Bygg själv i stället för kontantinsats: Build it yourself instead of a deposit
Byggd av stenen på platsen: Built from the stone on site
Byggd för jättar i luften: Built for giants of the sky
Byggd med OS i sikte: Built with the Olympics in mind
Byggd mot atombomben: Built to withstand the atom bomb
Byggd på stadens sankaste plats: Built on the city's lowest ground
Byggdes muren av krigsfångar?: Was the wall built by prisoners of war?
Byggelementen som lyftes bort från husen: The building sections lifted off the blocks on Stjärnbildsgatan were reused elsewhere, including on the Båtsmansgatorna streets in Backatorp and on Vegagatan in Linnéstaden. The idea came from Helmut Junkers, head of development at the housing company Göteborgshem.
Bygget av Huvudstaleden stannade av bris: Work on the Huvudsta road stalled for lack of money and after calls for a 1,000-metre tunnel under Huvudsta. A roughly 200-metre stub of motorway was left behind and is now known as the 'ruin motorway'. Student barracks used to stand there.
Bygget av Partille Arena startade den 5: Construction of Partille Arena began on 5 December 2013 and took three years. Once finished, it replaced the old Partillebohallen sports hall, which was finally demolished in April 2017.
Bygget började 1939, och med sina 75 mm: Construction began in 1939, and with its 75 mm anti-aircraft guns, Käppala was among the most heavily armed batteries around Stockholm. Its position on Lidingö made it strategically important as the last outpost to the east.
Bygget kom igång senast 1773 och det mes: Building was under way by 1773 at the latest, and most of it was finished by 1777. Then Carlberg set off on a journey abroad lasting almost five years, which held up the final stages. The manor wasn't ready to move into until 1780.
Bygget omfattade 27 300 kvadratmeter nya: The project included 27,300 square metres of new premises, and an old 9,000-square-metre warehouse was converted into offices. The property company Klövern expected to invest around 660 million kronor.
Bygget slukade 55 000 kubikmeter betong: The construction swallowed 55,000 cubic metres of concrete and 2,225,000 bricks. The three factory units were 1,100 metres long in total, and the four-million-square-metre site was then the largest industrial site in Sweden.
Bygget slukade 55 000 kubikmeter betong,: Construction swallowed 55,000 cubic metres of concrete, 3,380 tonnes of reinforcing steel and 2,225,000 bricks. The three factory units were 1,100 metres long altogether, and the site was then the largest industrial plot in Sweden.

Construction swallowed 55,000 cubic metres of concrete, 3,380 tonnes of reinforcing steel and 2,225,000 bricks. The three factory units were 1,100 metres long in total, and the 4-million-square-metre site was then the largest industrial plot in Sweden.
Bygget startade 1960 och centrumet invig: Construction began in 1960, and the centre opened in 1965 as one of the most modern in the region. The architect Sture Frölén designed both the layout and every single building, commercial and public alike.
Bygget startade i mars 1938, och redan d: Construction began in March 1938, and by 18 November that year a topping-out party for 500 guests was held in the Blue Hall of Stockholm City Hall. Before building started, study visits were made to modern factories in France, Holland and England.
Bygget startade i september 2004, och vi: Construction began in September 2004, and 75,000 people turned up for the opening on 9 April 2006. Today Allum welcomes around 5.6 million shoppers a year.
Bygget tog 15 år och huset invigdes 23 j: Construction took 15 years, and the building was inaugurated on 23 June 1923 – four hundred years to the day after Gustav Vasa's entry into Stockholm. Since 2025 Stockholm City Hall has been part of Sweden's cultural canon.
Byggföretaget SIAB levererade sina hus i: The construction firm SIAB delivered its houses in large prefabricated sections assembled on site, while Skånska Cementgjuteriet built its houses on the spot. Skånska's areas turned out more varied and better suited to the terrain. As the houses were built with state loans, the footprint could not exceed 140 square metres.
Byggherrarna längs Odengatan 3–13 kom öv: The developers along Odengatan 3–13 agreed on a uniform streetscape, a reaction against the motley villas of Lärkstaden. They all used dark-red Helsingborg brick but varied the details. In 1912 Svenska Dagbladet wrote of a uniformity "previously unknown in Stockholm's architectural history".
Byggmästaren Andreas Gustaf Sällström ro: The master builder Andreas Gustaf Sällström bought the estate at auction in 1889 for 55,000 kronor. At the same time he was building the new Royal Opera, and when King Gustav III's old opera house was demolished he moved valuable interior details here.
Byggmästaren som byggde villan på Florag: The builder who put up the villa at Floragatan 4 in 1881 obeyed the rule requiring villas along the street. But tucked well out of sight on the plot, he also built a three-storey block of flats, a stable and a coach house.
Byggnaden fick allvarliga mögelskador oc: Serious mould damage forced the congregation out of the building, and it now meets in temporary huts next door. The plan is to demolish the church and build a care home with a church under the same roof, due for completion in 2029.
Byggnaden från 1974 ritades av Tore Fors: The 1974 building was designed by Tore Forsman and Ulf Snellman. It has outer walls of brown brick, a glass wall facing Fisksätra square and a roof partly clad in red-painted aluminium sheeting.
Byggnaden hette först Gamlestadens kapel: The building started out as Gamlestaden Chapel and became a parish church in 1951, when it was renamed Nylöse Church. The Church of Sweden has now begun the process of taking it out of use.
Byggnaden ritades av Erik Ahnborg, och g: The building was designed by Erik Ahnborg, and its glass facades in various shades of blue became a familiar Sollentuna landmark. Hall II opened in 1987, adding another 6,000 square metres of exhibition space.
Byggnaden ritades av Sigge Cronstedt i j: The building was designed by Sigge Cronstedt in art nouveau-inspired brick, and he also designed the railway's station buildings. The power station's two tall chimneys became a new feature of the townscape and gave their name to the Skorstenen (Chimney) block, even though both were later demolished.
Byggnaden ritades av tyske arkitekten Fr: The building was designed by the German architect Friedrich August Stüler. The collections number some 700,000 objects, and you can even see works that once belonged to Gustav Vasa.
Byggnaden vid Eneby torg uppfördes 1977: The building on Eneby torg went up in 1977 to house both the Mission Church and Enebyberg library. The architect Janne Feldt also designed the light fittings, altar table and altarpiece, and the wooden ceiling rests on glulam beams.

Byggt på gammal sjöbotten: Built on an old lake bed

Byn Krokslätt nämns redan på 1300-talet,: The village of Krokslätt is mentioned as early as the 14th century, but nobody knows for sure what the name means. It may come from the many taverns (krogar) here – in the 18th century it was spelled Krogslätt. It could also refer to the bends (krokar) of the Mölndalsån river, or to a medieval personal name, Krok.
Byn bjuder på ett litet vikingatida gall: The village has its own little gallery of Viking Age stones. One runestone, U 44, signed by the carver Snare, vanished some time between around 1795 and 1850 and only resurfaced in 1981, in pieces that were then fitted back together – it's more than two metres tall. Another, U 43, has stood at the entrance to a farm since 1937, and on a boulder set into the ground, a man called Saxe had runes carved in memory of his mother.
Byn har rötter i sena järnåldern, vid en: The village dates back to the late Iron Age, on a sea inlet that post-glacial land rise slowly turned into Edsviken bay. The inlet may have given it the name ‘Myr-byn’, the bog village. In 1952 the county council bought 8.7 hectares of the farm’s land, and Danderyd Hospital grew up there.
Byn låg vid korsningen mellan Danderydsv: The village lay where Danderydsvägen and Norrtäljevägen crossed, and the post road between Stockholm and Turku (Åbo) passed through here. Rinkeby also had a large burial ground, which was cleared in the mid-1800s to make more room for fields.
Byn som dök upp i ett jordbyte: A village that turned up in a land swap
Byn som gav kyrkan dess namn nämns 1474: The village that gave the church its name is mentioned in 1474 as Herlandæ by. In 1925 the ruin was excavated and restored at the city's expense, and the memorial stone calls it Gothenburg's oldest Christian monument.
Byn som låg här före torget: The village that came before the square
Byn såldes till helgeandshuset: The village sold to the Holy Spirit hospital
Bynamnet Skintebo finns redan 1567, som: The village name Skintebo is recorded as early as 1567, as Skinteboda or simply Skintan. One theory is that skinta means good soil – the word crops up in several places around Askim. Other suggestions are a furrow, a hollow, a ditch or a sunken lane.
Bynamnet Sörred finns belagt redan 1388: The village name Sörred is recorded as early as 1388, as Surfua rudi. The first part is thought to come from the nickname Surv, meaning something like a careless fellow or sloven, and the second from the Old Swedish ryd, cleared land.
Bynamnet finns belagt redan 1567, då som: The village name is recorded as early as 1567, as Skinteboda or simply Skintan. It has several possible meanings, including good soil, furrow, pit, ditch or sunken lane. The word skinta in the sense of good soil crops up in several places around Askim.
Bysten av Carl Michael Bellman avtäcktes: The bust of the poet and songwriter Carl Michael Bellman was unveiled in 1829. The year before, the court confectioner Carlmark had opened a café here, and it was named Bellmansro – 'Bellman's Rest' – after the bust. The restaurant burned down in 1955, but the spot has kept the name. Next door is the Oakhill mansion, which Ferdinand Boberg designed for Prince Wilhelm in 1910. It has been the Italian Embassy since 1926.
