Byt vid Slussen. Vid Mariatorget passera: Change at Slussen. At Mariatorget you pass the fountain Tor's Fishing, from 1903.
Bäckahagens skola byggdes i etapper mell: Bäckahagen school was built in stages between 1953 and 1968 to designs by the architect David Dahl, and it came with its own caretaker's flat and even its own dental clinic. Bandhagen as a whole is a fine example of folkhem architecture – the style of Sweden's post-war welfare state – with low blocks arranged around leafy courtyards and the odd taller tower block to break things up and add variety.
Bäckebol Center har bara ett tjugotal bu: Bäckebol Center has only about twenty shops, but they cover a full 95,000 square metres. In 2008 Media Markt opened its second Gothenburg store here, in Coop Bygg's old premises.
Bäckebol Center är ett av Hisingens stor: Bäckebol Center is one of Hisingen's big retail parks, with around twenty shops spread over no less than 95,000 square metres. Shops come and go – one left in 2010, only to return three years later. A short way off flows the Lärjeån river, which rises north of Gråbo and joins the Göta älv river at Lärjeholm.
Bäckebols församling bröts ut ur Backa f: Bäckebol parish was only split off from Backa parish in 1995, and it merged back into it as early as 2010. The district created in 2016 has the same boundaries the parish had around the turn of the millennium.
Bäckebols gård började byggas i sten 176: Bäckebol manor was begun in stone in 1764 by Johan Oliveholm, the town's weighmaster. Its limestone front steps and the half-moon lunette windows in the gables give the house its character. It has been a listed building since 1969.
Bäckebols gård, en bit härifrån, är en h: Bäckebol Manor, a short way from here, is a manor house and former noble estate beside a stream. Work on the stone house was begun in 1764 by Johan Oliveholm, a weighmaster and ironworks owner, and the manor was restored in 1943–1944. It has been a listed building since the 1960s, and Gothenburg's smallest cemetery belongs to the estate too.

Not far from here is Bäckebols gård, a manor house and former estate beside a stream. The weighmaster and ironworks owner Johan Oliveholm began building it in stone in 1764, and the house was restored in 1943–1944. It has been a listed building since 9 January 1969 – and the estate even includes Gothenburg's smallest churchyard.
Bäckebols herrgård började byggas i sten: Work on the stone manor house at Bäckebol began in 1764, commissioned by Johan Oliveholm, a weighmaster and ironworks owner. A limestone staircase leads up to the front door, half-moon lunette windows sit high in the gables, and a plaque in the hall records how the house came to be built.
Bäckebols kyrksal invigdes på trettonded: Bäckebol's church hall opened on Twelfth Day 1971, and its last services were held on 30 May 2021. The end wall was decorated with a metal sculpture showing scenes from the life of Jesus. The congregation moved to Brunnsbo Church and Backa Church.

Bäckebol's church hall opened on Twelfth Day, 6 January 1971. The last services were held on 30 May 2021, when it closed for the redevelopment of the square. The congregation moved to Brunnsbo church and Backa church.
Bäckravinen i parken från 1940 är en rek: The stream ravine in the park, from 1940, recreates a small watercourse that once drained the ponds and fountains of Kristineberg. Even the paddling pool has a predecessor – a little lake that appears on a map from 1805.
Bällsta är en trädgårdsstad av små trähu: Bällsta is a garden suburb of small wooden houses from the 1940s. Around 200 of these cottages were built by their owners themselves, using materials and instructions supplied by the City of Stockholm's small-house office. A little further on is Solvalla, Sweden's national trotting stadium, with room for 35,000 spectators and home to Elitloppet, one of the biggest harness races in the world. On a hill nearby stands the radar tower that locals call Golfbollen, the Golf Ball.
Bällsta är en trädgårdsstad med mest enp: Bällsta is a garden suburb made up mostly of single-storey wood-panelled cottages that originally had red tiled roofs. Since the plots are under 1,000 square metres they've never been subdivided, and the area is classed as a valuable heritage environment.
Bällstas hus ligger regelbundet med lång: Bällsta's houses stand in neat rows, long side to the street, along long straight roads. The façades are timber-clad and the roofs were originally red clay tiles. Because the plots are under 1,000 square metres they've never been subdivided, so the area has kept its character.
Bällstavägen drogs omkring 1675 rakt öve: Around 1675 Bällstavägen was driven straight across the grave field. Today Björklunds hage is a meeting place for children and parents, with a preschool, an adventure playground with animals, a café and a 4-H farm. The name Ängby comes from Engiaby, ‘the village by the meadows’.
Bällstavägen följer en gammal väg från B: Bällstavägen follows an old road from Bällsta bro to a ferry landing at Tyska Botten. It was laid out around 1675 and driven straight across the burial ground, probably destroying a few graves. Today there's a supervised play park here with animals, a café and a 4-H farm.
Bällstavägen follows an old road from Bällsta bridge to a ferry landing at Tyska botten. It was laid out around 1675 and cut right across the burial ground, probably destroying some of the graves.
Bällstaån är 10,5 kilometer lång men fal: Bällstaån is 10.5 kilometres long but drops only about ten metres, so it has no fast-flowing stretches. Almost all of it has been straightened, and only a short section near Hjulsta and Tensta still follows its original course.
Bänk vid vattnet med utsikt mot Långholm: A waterside bench looking out to Långholmen
Bärby Korsväg är bara cirka 650 meter lå: Bärby Korsväg is only about 650 metres long, running between Kongahällavägen and Svensbyvägen in the little village of Bärby. But the village has a grander past than the road suggests: from 1824 to 1887 Bärby was the court seat for the Västra and Östra Hising districts, where cases from much of Hisingen were tried.
Båda älvstränderna vid färjeleden är nat: Both riverbanks at the ferry crossing are nature reserves and part of the EU's Natura 2000 network. The boundary between Kungälv and Gothenburg runs right down the middle of Nordre älv.
Båda älvstränderna vid färjeläget är nat: Both riverbanks at the ferry landing are nature reserves and part of the EU's Natura 2000 network. The boundary between Kungälv and Gothenburg runs down the middle of the Nordre älv, so you change municipality halfway across.
Både Solbacken och Hammardal var små stu: Solbacken and Hammardal were both small cottages belonging to Ågesta farm, but neither survives. In the 1950s and 60s Solbacken was divided into plots for holiday homes. The turning off Ågestavägen is called Hammardalsslingan.
Både Sparreholms bilmuseum och Skokloste: Both the Sparreholm car museum and the Skokloster motor museum have claimed that their Cadillac was the one in the accident. The royal court had three identical cars, and according to one motoring historian there’s no way of telling which it was. The press photos show no number plates, just a royal crown on the boot.
Både Sten Sture den äldre och Gustav Vas: Both Sten Sture the Elder and Gustav Vasa owned Järla gård, but neither lived there – they leased the estate out. In 1560 it became a tenant farm under Danvik's hospital.
Både Valåsen och Källeberget, bergsknall: Valåsen and Källeberget, the rocky knolls on either side of Fräntorpsgatan, each have a small cave formation. The name Fräntorp probably goes back to Old Norse.
Båten Rescue Mignon Wallenius, en gåva f: The rescue boat Rescue Mignon Wallenius, donated by the Wallenius shipping companies in 2005, was stationed at Malevik in summer for call-outs off Särö. Today the station's boats include Rescue Josephine, an 11.8-metre enclosed vessel built in 2021.
Båten lägger till vid Allmänna gränd och: The boat calls at Allmänna gränd and passes Saltsjöqvarn, Finnboda and Kvarnholmen on its way out towards the harbour entrance.
Båten lägger till vid Dalénum, Nacka str: The boat calls at Dalénum, Nacka strand with Milles' water arch, Kvarnholmen and Finnboda before reaching Nybroplan.
Båtsmannen som dog i Kanton: The sailor who died in Canton
Båtsmanstorpet Myrstugan låg nära Albysj: Myrstugan, a croft once allotted to a naval rating, stood near Lake Albysjön. When the housing estate was built, it was moved to Slottsparken, where the Vårby estate once stood.
Båtsmanstorpet byggdes i början av 1700-: The sailor’s croft was built in the early 1700s for a seaman in the navy. Between 1892 and 1907 it was the schoolhouse for local children. A photo from the early 1900s shows two schoolmistresses and 20 children.
Båtsmännen hette alltid Myrman: The boatmen were always called Myrman
Båtsmännen här fick soldatnamnet Tupp, s: The navy boatmen here were given the soldier's name Tupp (Cockerel), which passed on to each new boatman. Other names in the same company included Lax, Örn, Mild and Släthår. A boatman was entitled to a cottage, a small barn and a byre for two cows.
Båtturen tillbaka går via Skeppsholmen,: The boat trip back goes via Skeppsholmen, the navy's old island.
Bö herrgård omnämns redan 1485, och 1746: Bö manor is first mentioned in 1485, and in 1746 none other than Carl Linnaeus came to visit and wrote about the house and its garden. He's said to have planted a pear tree there. Closer by is Örgryte New Church, built in the Gothic Revival style with a tower almost 60 metres tall. It got electric lighting in 1908 – the same year as its neighbour, Bö School.
Bö var från början ett skattehemman med: Bö began as a tax-paying farmstead with a mill by a stream. A certain Sven Böker donated the font that stands in Örgryte's old church. Today the manor house is home to Casa, a Montessori school.
Börja bland växthus och dammar i Botanis: Start among the glasshouses and ponds of the Botanical Garden and finish out among the islands. The tram carries you from the city's green lungs to the marina and the archipelago.
Började i Malmstens egen skola: It began in Malmsten's own school
Började i en tennishall: It started in a tennis hall
Började som sjukstall 1933: Started as an animal hospital in 1933
Café och Milles dödsängel: A café and Milles's Angel of Death
Calder ville att verket skulle omges av: Calder wanted the work to have space around it so it could be seen from a distance. His wish was only granted in 2013, when it was moved to the lawn in the town park. Before that it stood outside the Blå stället arts centre.
Campus Albano har 70 000 kvadratmeter un: Campus Albano has 70,000 square metres of university space. Together with Karolinska Institutet's campus in Solna and the Stockholm School of Economics' campus on Sveavägen, it makes up what's known as the Science City. Plans allow for 2,000 bicycle spaces.
Canadahusen byggdes 1907–1908 efter enge: The Canada houses were built in 1907–1908 on an English model, originally meant for the craftsmen who were building the garden suburb. They are just 5.75 metres wide. Two similar blocks, Chile and Peru, were planned but never built.

The Canada houses were built in 1907–1908 on an English model, originally meant to house the craftsmen who would build the garden suburb. Two similar blocks, Chile and Peru, were also planned but never built.
Canon blev kvar här till 2001 och flytta: Canon stayed here until 2001, when it moved to Frösunda in Solna. The new building was the right size but had the wrong character, so Tengboms were brought back to “Canonify” it just as they had in Sätra.
Canon flyttade, stilen följde med: Canon moved, and the style went too
Canonhuset, några minuter härifrån, bygg: Canonhuset, a few minutes from here, was built for the electronics company Canon and houses offices, a warehouse and a workshop. It's one of the few examples of Swedish high-tech architecture and has the City Museum's highest heritage rating. A little further on is Sätra pistol range, which – despite its name – is in Bredäng, and is the only range of its kind in the whole of Söderort, Stockholm's southern suburbs.
Capitol öppnade 31 juli 1926. Över entré: Capitol opened on 31 July 1926. Over the entrance was a canopy on columns with capitals shaped like lotus flowers. The oval auditorium was pink, the curtain blue and brown, and there were 639 seats.
Capitol öppnade den 21 november 1941 med: Capitol opened on 21 November 1941 with the film Cobra Woman, starring Dorothy Lamour. The auditorium had 458 seats – birch armchairs upholstered in English-red velvet – and a neon canopy over the entrance.
Carl Bergsten tänkte sig en obelisk fram: Carl Bergsten had pictured an obelisk in front of the building – in fact a decorated chimney. It was dropped for lack of money. Instead, in 1919, Carl Milles's sculpture Bågskytten, the Archer, was raised on a 12-metre granite column.
Carl Gustaf Wrangel hade sex stora bygge: Carl Gustaf Wrangel had six major building projects on the go at the same time, among them Skokloster. When he died in 1676 work here ground to a halt, and it was only completed by the next owner, Baron Erik Lovisin.
Carl Gustaf von Platen slog 1905 ihop tv: In 1905 Carl Gustaf von Platen knocked two flats together into one apartment of nine rooms and a kitchen, with a library, a gentleman's drawing room, a lady's room and a room for the valet. The entrance has a marble staircase and a frieze of cherubs below the ceiling.
Carl Johan Bernadotte var vice vd för An: Carl Johan Bernadotte was deputy CEO of Anglo-Nordic Traktor, which built workshops here in 1953. He also helped persuade the American firm Sundstrand to move production here. At its peak the factory employed about 500 people and was Huddinge's largest employer, but it closed in 1974.
Carl Julius Ahlgren var befälhavare på I: Carl Julius Ahlgren was master of the Isolda from 1909 to 1960. Under his command the schooner sailed to the West Indies, Mexico, the east coast of South America and West Africa. In 1928 she was fitted with a 110-horsepower diesel engine.
Carl Malmsten tillbringade barndomens so: Furniture designer Carl Malmsten spent his childhood summers here, as his grandfather Cadier had bought Övre Karlsro. He began renting the house from his aunt in 1920 and bought it five years later. He built studios, made much of the fitted interior himself and, in 1930, stripped off the fretwork gingerbread trim in favour of a more classical look.
Carl Michael Bellman besökte gärna Fågel: The poet and songwriter Carl Michael Bellman liked to visit Fågelsången farm by the lake Trekanten. His younger sister Fredrika Eleonora lived there with her husband, the palace treasurer Georg Stiernhoff.
Carl Michael Bellman ledde en sommarsäso: Carl Michael Bellman ran a summer season of opera, ballet and concerts at the theatre. He was also fond of the inn, and mentions Ulriksdal in one of his songs.
Carl Milles Flöjtspelande ängel, ett av: Flöjtspelande ängel, the Flute-Playing Angel, is one of Carl Milles's late works, originally meant for the Saint Martin Fountain, and you'll find it in several places, including by Lidingöbron, the Lidingö Bridge. At the landing of the old Lidingö Bridge stands a small building by Ivar Tengbom, opened in 1925 and used as a waiting shelter until 1967. It's such a windy spot that people nicknamed it Vindarnas tempel, the Temple of the Winds.
Carl Milles studerade elefanter i djurpa: Carl Milles studied elephants at the Jardin des Plantes zoo in Paris in 1898. They were clearly one of his favourite animals, giving him the chance to work with volume and mass.
Carl Robert Lamm byggde upp en stor kons: Carl Robert Lamm built up a large art collection of Italian sculpture and paintings. Some of it has been sold, but works by Bruno Liljefors, Anders Zorn and Carl Milles can still be found at the castle today.
Carl och Olga Milles köpte tomten på Her: Carl and Olga Milles bought the plot on the Herserud cliff in 1906, and the house was inaugurated in 1908. The fine marble portal at the old entrance comes from Hotel Rydberg, demolished in 1914. In 1936 Millesgården was turned into a foundation and gifted to the Swedish people.
Carl och Olga Milles vilar i Skogskapell: Carl and Olga Milles are buried in the Woodland Chapel, in the part known as Little Austria. The chapel was inspired by the wayside chapels of southern Germany and Austria, modelled on Moritz von Schwind's painting Die Waldkapelle.
Carl-Erik Lindell var den siste på Fulle: Carl-Erik Lindell was the last person to farm at Fullersta. He gave it up and from 1902 sold 'Lovely plots for villas and homes of your own'. The brochure stressed that the trip from Stockholm Central took just half an hour.
Carlanderska sjukhuset intill uppfördes: Carlanderska sjukhuset, the hospital next door, was built in 1927 to designs by Arvid Bjerke and was originally called Carlanderska sjukhemmet, the Carlander nursing home. A little way off, in Renströmsparken park, stands Solringen, the Sun Ring, a 4.4-metre ring by Claes Hake. It has a twin: a version in patinated bronze went up that same year, 1993, in Hjørring in Denmark.
Cellfängelset hade 107 celler och byggde: The cell prison had 107 cells and was built on the rock where the St Erik bastion had once stood. The last prisoners were moved to Härlanda prison in 1907, after which the building became Rosenborg, a Salvation Army hostel. Once it was demolished in 1972, the rock was blasted away to make room for the Oscarsleden road.
Centralpalatset är ett typexempel på sve: Centralpalatset is a textbook example of Swedish National Romanticism, with a dark brick facade, bay windows and a steep mansard roof. On the west side rises a corner tower bearing the year 1913. The municipality has given the building its blue rating, the highest heritage grade.
Centrum efter amerikanskt mönster: A centre on the American model
Centrum och bostäderna byggdes i etapper: The centre and the homes were built in stages between 1983 and 1991. The culture centre houses a library, a gallery and Erskinesalen, a hall for theatre, concerts, talks and films.
Centrum pryds av 22 konstverk av bland a: The centre is decorated with 22 works of art by artists including Peter Dahl, Petter Hellsing and Asmund Arle. Huddinge centrum is twinned with Jokkmokk in Swedish Lapland, and every year it hosts the Jokkmokk Days – complete with an ice sculpture competition.
Centrumateljéerna började 1940 i en hyrd: Centrumateljéerna started out in 1940 in a rented tennis hall by Djurgårdsbrunnsviken. From 1948 Sandrews shot around 140 films here, including Folket i fält and Taxi 13, before moving to Filmstaden in Solna in 1961.
Centrumbyggnaden, med sin snäckform, rit: The shell-shaped centre building was designed by Kell Åström and Lars Bryde. The City Museum has given the centre and square its green listing for heritage value, and the row of point blocks along Askersundsgatan is described as a Rågsved landmark.
Centrumet byggdes i etapper och många ty: The centre was built in stages, and many felt it was taking far too long. In April 1948 the monthly Årstabladet dubbed the square Skandaltorget – Scandal Square – because the community and leisure facilities never seemed to materialise.
Centrumet byggdes mitt i järnåldersbyn T: The shopping centre was built right in the middle of the Iron Age village of Tibble gård, one of the densest archaeological sites in Sweden. Many burial grounds were excavated, and by 2000 only a few remained.
Centrumet hette egentligen Forum Nacka,: The centre was officially called Forum Nacka, but most people called it Nacka Forum – and on 13 September 2010 it changed its name to match. Today its four floors hold 123 shops and 18 restaurants and cafés.
Centrumet invigdes 1965 som Bollmora cen: The centre opened in 1965 as Bollmora Centrum, a small suburban centre with pedestrian streets. In the early 1990s it was rebuilt as a shopping mall and renamed Tyresö Centrum in 1992. A major fire in several of the buildings delayed the reopening.
Centrumet invigdes 1965 under namnet Bol: The centre opened in 1965 as Bollmora centrum, a small suburban centre with pedestrian streets. In the early 1990s it was rebuilt as a glazed shopping mall and reopened in 1992 as Tyresö Centrum.
The centre opened in 1965 as Bollmora centrum, then a small suburban centre with pedestrian streets. It was rebuilt as a shopping mall and reopened as Tyresö Centrum in 1992.
The centre opened in 1965 as Bollmora centrum, a small suburban centre with pedestrian streets. It was rebuilt as a shopping mall and reopened in 1992 under the name Tyresö Centrum.
Centrumet ritades av den danskfödde arki: The centre was designed by the Danish-born architect Hack Kampmann, who was given a free hand. The result was low façades of glass, render and sheet metal around a square with a pond in the middle. Kampmann also designed the nearby slab blocks.
Centrumet vid Tallkrogsplan invigdes 194: The shopping centre on Tallkrogsplan opened in 1943. For many years it was home to small shops – a home bakery, a fishmonger, a greengrocer, a haberdasher and a cobbler. Most of them are gone today.
Centrumets emblem är en kyrktupp, en lit: The centre's emblem is a weathercock, a slightly altered version of the award-winning gilded cockerel on Vantör Church. The point block east of the metro is called Tupphuset – the Cockerel House. Many of the facades and pillars are clad in Älvdalen quartzite.
Centrumkyrkans byggnad i kvarteret Röker: Centrumkyrkan's building in the Rökeriet block was designed by the architect David Jansson and built in 1906 as a Baptist church.
Chalmers började som Chalmersska slöjdsk: Chalmers started life as the Chalmersska slöjdskolan, a craft school. Under William Chalmers' will it was to be an industrial school for poor children who had learned to read and write. It wasn't called a university of technology until 1937.
Chalmers köpte fastigheten 1 november 19: Chalmers bought the property on 1 November 1945 for 4,420 kronor, planning to knock the house down to make way for a new library. That never happened – instead the house was fitted out as an architects' office.
Chalmers tekniska högskola grundades 182: Chalmers University of Technology was founded in 1829 with money left by William Chalmers, who had worked for the Swedish East India Company. All around you is the Johanneberg campus, where thousands of engineers are trained every year.
Chalmerstunneln är egentligen två parall: The Chalmers tunnel is actually two parallel single-track tunnels, linked by six cross passages for evacuation. It cost 188 million kronor to build and opened to traffic on 10 February 2002.
Chapmans torg fick sitt namn 1939 efter: Chapmans torg was named in 1939 after the legendary sea captain Charles Chapman, who worked here in Majorna in the 18th century. Many of the people who lived in Majorna once earned their living in the shipyards and the harbour.
Charabang på nya vägen: A charabanc on the new road
Charlottenburg var från början Frösunda: Charlottenburg started out as Frösunda croft, which appears on a map from the 1670s. Adolf Fredrik Wijnbladh rebuilt it as a house with nine rooms in a row and named the place after his wife, Charlotte Arbin.
Charlottenburg var från början ett torp: Charlottenburg started out as a croft belonging to Stora Frösunda. In 1801 Adolf Fredrik Wijnbladh rebuilt it as a house with nine rooms in an enfilade and named it after his wife, Charlotte Arbin. By the entrance is a stone labyrinth – a 'jungfrudans', or maiden's dance – from 1990.
Chefsvilla med tennisbana: A manager's villa with a tennis court
Choklad, konst och plask! Marabouparken: Chocolate, art and splashing about! Marabouparken is open to everyone. By the 1970s its sculpture collection had grown to sixteen works, and the paddling pool is a big draw for families. The art gallery opened in 2010 and is built underground, next to the old cocoa laboratory. Nearby, Sundbyberg Museum tells the story of Sweden's first suburb and has burnt bones from a Viking Age grave on display.

Chocolate, art and splashing about! Marabouparken is open to everyone, with a sculpture collection that had grown to sixteen works by the 1970s and a paddling pool that draws families with children. The art gallery opened in 2010 and is built underground, next to the old cocoa laboratory building. The park was laid out from 1937 by Sven Hermelin and Inger Wedborn on the site of Sundbyberg's old manor farm from 1785.
Chokladfabriken Marabou kom till Sundbyb: The Marabou chocolate factory came to Sundbyberg in 1916 and shaped the town for decades. Marabou is now in Upplands Väsby, but Marabouparken remains and is known for its art gallery. The metro station, from 1985, lies 26 metres down in the rock, with a connection to the commuter trains.
Christinedals gård drev ett tegelbruk. L: Christinedal farm ran a brickworks. The clay was dug locally, and you can still see the pits left behind on the slope west of the houses. Towards the end they even took clay from the bottom of Stensjön lake, at what is now the bathing spot.
Christinedals gård drev tegelbruk och st: Christinedal farm ran a brickworks and a large timber business, and sold ice and sand on the side. You can still see the clay pits on the slope west of the buildings, and towards the end, clay was dug from the bottom of Stensjön lake by the bathing spot.
Christinedals gård hade tegelbruk och st: Christinedal farm had a brickworks and a large timber business. The clay was dug locally, and you can still see the old clay pits on the slope west of the buildings. In the final years, clay was taken from the bottom of Stensjön lake, where the bathing spot is today.
Cino4 öppnades 2007 av kulturminister Le: Cino4 was opened in 2007 by the culture minister Lena Adelsohn Liljeroth, and more than 12,000 tickets were sold in the first month. The effects were so realistic that children under four weren't allowed in. The cinema closed in 2016, when the technology could no longer be kept up to date.
Cirka 100 meter öster om Bällstavägen fi: About 100 metres east of Bällstavägen is a fairly recent carving on a rock slab, with a circular pattern, an unfinished human figure and the letters IOGT. It's linked to Björklundstorpet, which was for a time the meeting hall of a temperance organisation.
Cisternen rymde 400 kubikmeter vatten fr: The tank held 400 cubic metres of water drawn from the ridge at Ulriksdal. But the wells were pumped so hard that brackish water from Brunnsviken seeped in. As early as 1926 Sundbyberg switched to water from Lake Mälaren, and the tower was left with no purpose.
City ritades av Curt Strehlenert på HSB:: The City cinema was designed by Curt Strehlenert at the HSB architects’ office. The auditorium was styled as an open-air theatre, with dark blue walls and ceiling and lighting that looked like a starry sky. It had 500 red armchair seats, and the name shone out over the square in big red neon letters.
City var en av flera förortsbiografer fr: City was one of several suburban cinemas of its day. Forum in Årsta centrum opened in 1951, Fontänen in Vällingby in 1956, and in 1961 both Fanfaren in Farsta and Reflexen in Kärrtorp opened their doors.
Clarebergs gård hette först Berg. När ko: Clarebergs gård was originally called Berg. When Magnus Lagerström, a councillor of commerce and director of the Swedish East India Company, took it over in 1735, he renamed it after his wife, Clara.
Clarebergs gård i Kärra hette först Berg: Clarebergs gård in Kärra was originally called Berg. When Magnus Lagerström, a director of the Swedish East India Company, took it over in 1735, he renamed it after his wife, Clara.
Coldinuorden 3 är ett av 32 skivhus som: Coldinuorden 3 is one of the 32 slab blocks that define Bredäng. The City Museum describes the development as a large-scale example of the modernist idea of houses set in a park, one that 'has no equivalent in Sweden'.
Coldinuorden fick fästningen Nya Chartag: In 1786 the Coldinu Order, a convivial society, was given the 'fortress' Nya Chartago by the wine steward of the Pelikan tavern. It was a round tower with a saluting battery, where members sailed out to play at sieges and battles. In 1797 the fortress was ceded, and the commandant was granted free passage out with his men and ten cannon.
Coldinuorden har länge satt upp gröna el: The Coldinu Order has long put up green or white crosses in the archipelago, a tradition dating back to the age of exploration, when a cross showed that a place had been charted. In 1928 a cast-iron cross was raised on Korseberget on Hönö in memory of seafarers. At its centre is a five-pointed star with an eye.
Colour by Numbers skapades av arkitekten: Colour by Numbers was created by the architect Milo Lavén, the interaction designer Loove Broms and the artist Erik Krikortz. In winter 2008–2009 the work was shown in a tower in Seville during the city's third biennial, and in 2011 it became a permanent fixture here.
Containerslottet med vindbrygga: The container castle with a drawbridge
Coop Konsum i Vinsta hette tidigare Björ: The Coop Konsum supermarket in Vinsta used to be called Björnbodahallen. The national vehicle-inspection company Bilprovningen had its head office here until spring 2012, and one of the local petrol stations was pulled down in 2017 to make way for the Stockholm Bypass.
Cyrillus Johansson hämtade inspiration f: Cyrillus Johansson drew inspiration from southern Europe, most obviously in the free-standing bell tower, a 48-metre campanile. Its three bells are called “Faith”, “Hope” and “Love”. The church was his last commission, and he didn't live to see it finished.
Dag Ribbings tio radhus i rött tegel ble: Dag Ribbing's ten red-brick terraced houses were ready to move into in 1950 and quickly became popular with staff at the nearby Karolinska Hospital. As a result, most of the households in the housing association were doctors' families.
Dagens Jacobsdal byggdes 1798 i timmer o: Today's Jacobsdal was built of timber in 1798 and still has its 18th- and 19th-century joinery and tiled stoves. The house is let as a home through the Royal Court's own housing queue. Since the 1960s Bergshamravägen has separated it from the neighbouring house, Karlshäll.
Dagens Lundby nya kyrka invigdes 1996. F: Today's Lundby New Church was consecrated in 1996. Its model was a simple medieval Italian country church, a basilica. It's built of red brick in various shades on a granite base, with floors of limestone and oak. The winning competition entry was called "A Journey Through Time and Space".
Dagens bro byggdes av Bergsunds mekanisk: Today's bridge was built by the Bergsund engineering works and finished in time for the Stockholm Exhibition of 1897. It was made wide enough for the Strandvägen trams, and its cast-iron railing is decorated with stylised plants.
Dagens bro i betong från 1996 är 907 met: Today's concrete bridge, from 1996, is 907 metres long but has a clearance of just 5.9 metres, so it has to open for most ships. It's operated remotely from the control tower on the Göta älvbron bridge.
Dagens kyrka ritades av Arvid Bjerke och: Today's church was designed by Arvid Bjerke and consecrated on Palm Sunday 1923. It's built of rough-hewn augen gneiss quarried right here, and a weathercock tops the copper cap of the tower.
Dagsverkstorpet från 1715 byggdes ut til: This croft from 1715, whose tenants paid their rent in labour, was enlarged into a double cottage in 1915. The land around it has been used, among other things, as a market garden.
Dagtid går färjan var 20:e minut och i r: During the day the ferry runs every 20 minutes, and every 15 minutes at rush hour. Some late-night and early-morning crossings, however, have to be booked by phone. The ferry landings have moved twice, in 1928 and 1964.
Dagvattenanläggningen vid Dammträsket bl: The stormwater facility at Dammträsket was completed in 2019 with a new cleansing pre-pond, an upper pond and wetland in between. The water is channelled along a winding ditch, and the bends slow it down so that it has time to be cleaned.
Dalen mitt i Hagsätraskogen var åkermark: The valley in the middle of Hagsätra forest was farmland belonging to the Ormkärr croft, first mentioned in 1617 and part of the Älvsjö estate. Stone foundations, a clearance cairn and old field ditches can still be seen.
Dalen ner mot havet: The valley down to the sea
Dalens sjukhus från 1977 är ett välbevar: Dalen Hospital, completed in 1977, is a well-preserved example of the late modernist architecture of its day and an important piece of urban planning history. A little way off, on the Nytorp field, stood the croft of Nytorp, which belonged to the Hammarby estate. It disappeared in the early 1960s to make way for the Nytorpsbadet pool. The Dalen residential area is made up of 14 courtyard blocks, and the City Museum has classed the whole of it as culturally valuable.

Dammen som blev en gångbro: The weir that became a footbridge
Dammen som skulle vara fisktom: The pond meant to have no fish
Dammen var en myr: The pond was once a bog
Danderyds gymnasium: Danderyds gymnasium, the upper secondary school
Danderyds kyrka ligger ett par minuter b: Danderyd church is a couple of minutes away, right next to the busy E18 towards Norrtälje. By the gate stands the runestone U 127, one of the Jarlabanke stones. South of the churchyard is Berga gård, a farm that probably goes back to the Viking Age, with an 18th-century manor house. And beside the church is Klockare Malm's Chapel, used for smaller christenings, weddings and funerals.
Danderyds kyrka var länge släkten Banérs: Danderyd Church was for a long time the burial and parish church of the Banér family, and there are two burial vaults beneath the chancel. Ebba Grip donated the pulpit in memory of her husband, Svante Banér, who died in 1628.
Danderyds kyrka, en bit härifrån, gömmer: Danderyd Church, a little way from here, hides several Viking Age runestone fragments. One of them, the top of a sandstone runestone, was discovered as recently as 1938 in the Banér family vault during restoration work, and it's now mounted on the inside of the church's west wall. Just west of the church stands another runestone, U 131, between the old Klockargården, the parish clerk's house, and the former parish hall.
Danderyds kyrkklockor nämns av Carl Mich: Danderyd's church bells get a mention from Carl Michael Bellman in Fredman's Epistle No. 80: '…and Dandryd's bells kept on tinkling…'. The weathervane on the bell tower bears the year 1728.

Carl Michael Bellman mentions Danderyd's church bells in Fredman's Epistle No. 80: "and Dandryd's bells kept jingling". The weather vane on the bell tower bears the year 1728, and the largest bell dates from 1953.
Danderyds sjukhus var det första sjukhus: Danderyd Hospital was the first hospital on the metro network to have a station of its own bearing its name, opened in 1978. The hospital management had convinced the transport planners that it was needed.
Daniel Asplund kom till Stockholm som ni: Daniel Asplund arrived in Stockholm at nineteen with nothing to his name and became a wholesale merchant in 1781. At Bergsund he founded a starch works, a bleachery and a dye works. He built homes for his workers and in 1793 started a school for their children.
Daniel Ek, som grundade Spotify, är född: Daniel Ek, the founder of Spotify, was born and raised in Rågsved. The musicians Jireel, Thomas Rusiak and Lokal come from here too.
Dans och folkpark på Kikås: Dancing and a people's park at Kikås
Dans och kaffe vid kvarnen: Dancing and coffee by the mill
Dansbana och folkpark på Kikås: Dance floor and folkpark at Kikås
Dansbåt från Stadshuset: A dance boat from City Hall
Danskar och svenskar på Rya Nabbe: Danes and Swedes at Rya Nabbe
Danskarna erövrade Älvsborg 1612 efter a: The Danes captured Älvsborg fortress in 1612 after bombarding it from Sannabacken. Under the peace of 1613 the ransom was set at one million riksdaler in silver, paid in four instalments over six years. The Danes didn't leave the fortress until 1619.
Danske kungen Fredrik II blev så glad öv: The Danish king Frederick II was so delighted that Bohus had been saved that he wanted the event immortalised. His sarcophagus in Roskilde Cathedral carries a marble relief of the Bohus Blast. The descendants of the soldier Hans Sund were granted the farm of Röset on Hisingen in perpetuity.
Dansrotundan från 1940 var en av Europas: The dance rotunda from 1940 was one of Europe's largest dance halls, with room for 1,200 dancers. Upstairs was the Uggleklubben (Owl Club) bar, an almost legendary haunt in the 1950s.
Dansös och skådespelare ägde gården: Owned by a dancer and actors
Danvikens begravningsplats invigdes 1834: Danviken Cemetery opened in 1834 as a burial ground for the poor and for cholera victims, and many people from Sicklaön and eastern Södermalm were buried here too. The last burial took place in 1956, but a number of gravestones and crosses survive.
Danviks gamla kvarn slogs ut: Danvik's old mill was put out of business
Danvikshem byggdes 1912–1915 av Kreuger: Danvikshem was built in 1912–1915 by Kreuger & Toll in the National Romantic style, with Aron Johansson as architect. The monumental building at the sea approach to Stockholm was designed for more than 400 residents.
Datacentralen och koppartak: A data centre and a copper canopy
De 160 försäljningsplatserna i de gamla: The 160 market pitches in the former horse stables are known as spiltor, or stalls. You'll find everything here from glassware, china and books to toys, fabrics, tools and work equipment.
De 39 radhusen vid Rastvägen byggdes 194: The 39 terraced houses on Rastvägen were built in 1948–1950 as something between terraced houses and blocks of flats. Each home has four rooms and a kitchen and its own front door, but instead of a private patch of garden there's a recessed terrace and a shared courtyard.
De 75 atriumhusen från 1960 kallades i f: Locals nicknamed the 75 atrium houses from 1960 'the rabbit hutches'. The street names all have a coin theme – Växelmyntsgatan, Pennygången and Fyrktorget – and when new link houses went up in 2012, their street became Kastmyntsgatan.
De eleganta villorna i Lärkstaden byggde: The elegant villas of Lärkstaden were built around 1912. Prime Minister Karl Staaff lived at Tofslärkan 3 from 1912 to 1915, and the villa next door, Tofslärkan 6, has been the Latvian Embassy since 1995. The plots were tiny: Tofslärkan 3 measured just 292 square metres, including a nine-metre strip for the garden.
De engelska radhusen byggdes som ett spa: The English-style terraced houses were built as a cost-cutting experiment in a time of crisis, using hollow bricks, lean concrete and reused moulds. The facades were finished in sack-rubbed brick: a thin layer of mortar was scrubbed on with a jute sack, so the brick still partly shows through.
De fem rödmålade stugorna längs Kvastmak: The interiors of the five red-painted cottages along Kvastmakartrappan, the Broom-Maker’s Steps, weren’t renovated until the early 2000s – and running water and indoor toilets were deliberately left out. Instead, new outdoor privies and water pumps were put in the yards, and the walls were given freshly printed wallpaper in 1920s patterns. The cottages may only be used as studios.
De femton husen är grupperade kring en g: The fifteen buildings are grouped around a shared courtyard, six facing Kärrtorpsvägen and nine facing the new Sophie Sagers gata. The courtyard doubles as a public park, and the rendered façades come in warm, muted colours.
De flesta AGA-anställda bodde på Söderma: Most AGA employees lived on Södermalm and had to take a steamer to Lidingö. The journey was so long that they demanded shorter working hours. The tram only reached here in 1919.
De flesta av Manhems hyreshus ritades av: Most of Manhem's apartment blocks were designed by the architect Albin Brag in a simple Art Nouveau style, with decorative gables, bay windows and steep roofs. In 1997 the City Planning Office declared central Aspudden unique in Stockholm as a uniform area of 1910s apartment buildings.
De flesta gatorna här har namn efter tid: Most of the streets here are named after ways of measuring time – Tideräkningsgatan (Calendar Reckoning Street), Kalendervägen, Halvsekelsgatan (Half-Century Street). The squares follow the theme too: Årstidstorget, Citytorget, Kortedala torg and Kalendertorget.
De flesta gatorna i Höglandet fick namn: Most of the streets in Höglandet were named between 1924 and 1930 on two themes: 'the art of writing' and place names from Dalarna. That's why you'll find Thespisvägen, Rimmargatan (Rhymer Street) and Journalistgränd alongside Sollerövägen, Orevägen and Våmhusvägen.
De flesta gatorna i Kortedala har namn e: Most of the streets in Kortedala are named after ways of measuring time, such as Tideräkningsgatan (Calendar Reckoning Street), Kalendervägen and Halvsekelsgatan (Half-Century Street). The squares are Årstidstorget, Citytorget, Kortedala torg and Kalendertorget. Kortedala itself means 'the short valley', as opposed to Djupedalen, 'the deep valley'.
De flesta gatunamn i Hagsätra kommer frå: Most of the street names in Hagsätra come from places in the province of Närke. Olshammarsgatan, for instance, is named after Olshammar in Askersund municipality.
De flesta gatunamnen i Hagsätra kommer f: Most of the street names in Hagsätra come from places in the province of Närke. Olshammarsgatan is named after Olshammar in Askersund municipality, and its neighbours include Glanshammarsgatan, Fjugestagränd and Vintrosagatan.
De flesta gårdar ligger längs Tuve kyrkv: Most of the farms lie along Tuve kyrkväg, which was once the main road between central Hisingen and Säve. When the traffic got too heavy, Tuvevägen was built a few hundred metres to the east, right out on the Skändla plain.
De flesta industribyggnaderna revs i bör: Most of the industrial buildings were torn down in the early 2000s. One of the few left was built in 1889–1890 as a paint factory for Fernissaktiebolaget, the varnish company, and later housed the Albano Smide metalworks. The area's mortar factory ran from 1903 to 1963.
De flesta villorna hade små kök med serv: Most of the villas had small kitchens with a serving room, a dining room, a maid's room and often a gentleman's study. The architecture assumed a housewife with a domestic help. The façades were painted in light pastel shades.
De flesta villorna längs Segeltorpsvägen: Most of the houses along Segeltorpsvägen went up in the 1940s and 1950s. The owners built them with their own hands, using instructions and materials from the City of Stockholm.
De fyra höga ekarna framför huvudbyggnad: The four tall oaks in front of the main house have been shaped with one crown at the top and another lower down, to make the view all the more magnificent. The mill owner, Werner Rhedin, planted many exotic and rare trees in the park.
De första Vasakungarna använde holmen fö: The first Vasa kings used the island for recreation. Gustav Vasa laid out a garden, Erik XIV often threw parties here and Johan III built a pavilion. The naval shipyard moved here in the 1630s, probably because Queen Kristina didn't want to see building sites from the palace.
De första affärerna som öppnade var varu: The first shops to open were the Domus and EPA department stores, on 3 September 1964. The shopping arcade was opened by the King and Queen on 24 October 1993 and named Shopping Centre of the Year that same year.
De första arbetarhusen i Tallbacken var: The first workers' houses in Tallbacken were red wooden buildings resembling farm labourers' row houses. They were built of rough planks insulated with wood shavings and heated with firewood. The privies were in a separate building, the laundry was down by the lake, and electricity didn't arrive until 1922.
De första eleverna gick vidare till yrke: The first students went on to become organ builders, sailmakers, goldsmiths, mirror makers, lithographers and sugar refiners. Teaching was meant to be practical rather than strictly academic – and free of charge.
De första fullskaliga båtarna var livbåt: The first full-size boats built here were lifeboats, in 1931. From 1935 the yard turned to leisure craft – first prize boats for raffles, such as Långedrag dinghies, and 22s for the GKSS sailing club.
De första färjorna var roddfärjor. År 18: The first ferries were rowing boats. In 1874 Eriksbergs Mekaniska Verkstad delivered a 12-horsepower steam launch, nicknamed Bonnafröjda. The ferry that replaced it in 1927 came from Stockholm, where it had carried trams across to Lidingö.
De första företagen här, Billman-Regulat: The first companies here – Billman-Regulator, LM Ericsson and ASEA – all worked with electricity. So the blocks were given names like Anoden, Katoden, Batteriet and Ackumulatorn (Anode, Cathode, Battery and Accumulator), and the streets are called Jonvägen, Elektronvägen and Regulatorvägen.
De första hallarna var långa industrihal: The first halls were long industrial sheds in corrugated metal, orange with blue details. The cladding has since been replaced with aluminium-coloured panels. The fair's landmark is the 19-storey hotel from 2006.
De första hyresgästerna flyttade in 1969: The first tenants moved in in 1969. From 1984, for about ten years, the estate underwent a major renewal: the courtyards were redesigned and some buildings were given colourful façades.
De första kikåsborna kom i slutet av 180: The first people settled in Kikås in the late 19th century, and the first new house went up in 1916. Self-build housing took off in the early 1920s, and after the Second World War the villa district grew rapidly between 1945 and 1949.

The first residents arrived in Kikås in the late 1800s, and the first new house was built in 1916. Self-build homes took off in the early 1920s, and after the Second World War there was a lot of building around Solvändan and Berghällsgatan.

The first people settled in Kikås in the late 1800s. The first new house went up in 1916, and in the early 1920s self-build home ownership really took off. The Hålsten area could only be built once Hålsten bog had been drained.
De första kolonisterna kom i maj 1936, o: The first allotment holders arrived in May 1936, and by the end of the year around 200 plots were already in use. By the early 1950s, every single plot had a cottage on it.
De första kolonistugorna växte upp 1916: The first allotment cabins went up in 1916, and most were built from scrap timber from car crates – the packaging Ford's car parts were shipped in from the USA. Today there are 192 plots, down from 250 at the start.
De första kända ägarna till Hammarby var: The first known owners of Hammarby were Sven and Bänkfrid, who lived in the 11th century. They were pagans, and their son was Saint Botvid. In 1129 a stave church was built on the farm's land – the forerunner of Botkyrka Church.
De första mässhallarna liknade långa ind: The first exhibition halls looked like long industrial sheds, with façades of corrugated orange metal and blue details. Over the years the orange cladding has been replaced by aluminium-coloured panels.
De första patienterna flyttades in den 1: The first patients moved in on 14 May 1924, but the official opening didn't take place until 3 September. The first chief physician was Dr Torild Lundén.
De första rödakorssystrarna utbildades f: The first Red Cross nurses were trained mainly to care for the wounded in war. As early as 1897 two Swedish Red Cross nurses were sent to the war in Greece, and in 1912 the first Red Cross ambulance was sent there.
De första skolorna i området byggdes som: The area's first schools were single-storey pavilions. Tomtebergsskolan opened in spring 1963 in eight pavilions, and Slottsbergsskolan on Munspelsgatan was put together from prefabricated pavilions in time for autumn 1965.
De första villorna i Birka byggdes kring: The first villas in Birka were built around 1900 as large two-and-a-half-storey houses for several families, most of them clad in wooden panelling and many with glazed verandas. The carpenter Arvid Samsiö helped build Villa Birka, which gave the area its name.
De första villorna var egnahemshus som b: The first villas were self-build homes put up by the Graham brothers. By 1907, 14 identical houses stood finished in the blocks now called Apelsinen, Ananasen, Bananen and Blåbäret – the Orange, the Pineapple, the Banana and the Blueberry.
De första åtta paviljongerna har slammat: The first eight pavilions have limewashed brick, steep tiled roofs and small-paned windows in the National Romantic style. G-huset turned out a little larger, with two wings, and is known as “the castle”. The last three buildings, from the 1950s, stand out with their red brick facades.
De gamla husen längs gatan hade folkliga: The old houses along the street went by folksy names such as 'Kalle Kypps', 'Klickens' and 'Fylle-Petterssons'. In the yard at Ånäsvägen 7 lived the rock blasters 'Pajen' and 'Borrar-Johan', while number 11 was home to lads like 'Ville Klämma' and 'Karve-Albin'.
De gamla trähusen runt berget: The old wooden houses on the hill
De gröna fönsterluckorna, och troligen y: The green window shutters, and probably the front door too, came from Hagalund inn, which was pulled down in 1954; they were put up after 1965. The shutter hooks came from Linvävaretorpet, the weaver's croft, demolished in 1967 when Uppsalavägen was widened.
De japanska körsbärsträden planterades i: The avenue of Japanese cherry trees was planted during the 1997–98 makeover, when Stockholm was European Capital of Culture, and the large pond was added at the same time. The ice rink has been here since November 1962.
De många små ventilskorstenarna på taket: The many small vent chimneys on the roof are there because of the chamber-pot cabinets in the cells, which were used right up until the prison closed. A vent ran from each cabinet up through the roof.
De nya husen ritades av Brunnberg & Fors: The new buildings were designed by Brunnberg & Forshed, with facades of rust-red Corten steel that match the 1940s brick. City architect Karolina Keyzer said they show that architecture doesn’t have to shout or be expensive to make its mark.
De pyramidformade taken inspirerades tro: The pyramid-shaped roofs were probably inspired by 18th-century architects such as Ledoux and Boullée. The pointed forms and the green roofs and façades may also have been a way of letting the building blend into the pine forest.
De röda neonglasögonen satt först ovanfö: The red neon glasses originally hung above the entrance and were made by Morneon, one of Sweden's biggest illuminated-sign makers. When the lettered sign arrived in the 1960s, the glasses moved to the right-hand side of the facade.
De röda tegelhusen byggdes 1944–1949 som: The red-brick buildings went up in 1944–1949 as barnrikehus – subsidised housing for large families – designed by Ernst Hawerman and Nils G:son Friberg for Stockholmshem. They're among the last of their kind built in Sweden.
De som bor vid bäcken: Those who live by the stream
De som fick lotterna i den andra etappen: Those who got plots in the second phase often came from allotment areas in Stockholm's southern suburbs that had been cleared, and many brought their old cottages with them. Unlike the functionalist cabins, these were often in a rustic folk style and looked like little crofts.
De stora stenarna på Sveriges holme tolk: Early in the 20th century, the large stones on Sveriges holme were taken to be an ancient monument, perhaps a judgement ring. A later survey showed they were just a moraine formation. The islet is also home to one of the Order of Neptune's tridents.
De tre korfönstren visar 'det stora fisk: The three chancel windows show the miraculous draught of fishes, when Jesus calls the apostles to become fishers of men. In 1945 the church was also given two votive ships – a schooner and a fishing boat – by men from Hyppeln and Knippla.
De tre vingarna: De tre vingarna, the Three Wings
De två funkisvillorna från 1932 planerad: The two functionalist villas from 1932 were designed for families with several children and domestic help. They had flower rooms, a maid's room in the attic and, in the basement, a garage for the master of the house's car. Today both are private homes.
De två hemmanen i Sandbäck hette Prästgå: Sandbäck's two farmsteads were called Prästgården and Kullen. From 1677 the curate of Fässberg, Per Hermenius, lived at Prästgården. In 1777 Kullen belonged to Martin Holterman, and after his death his widow gave the farm's income to the parish school.

Sandbäck's two farmsteads were called Prästgården and Kullen. In 1673 Prästgården came under Johan Gabriel Stenbock, and from 1677 the Fässberg chaplain lived there. When Kullen's owner Martin Holterman died, his widow donated the farm's income to the parish school.
De två röda trävillorna vid Valsvägen by: The two red wooden villas on Valsvägen were built in 1919–1920 for workers at the superphosphate factory and are Kvarnholmen's oldest surviving buildings. Right up to the 1970s they had no central heating or hot water.
De två små likadana husen norr om fontän: The two small matching buildings north of the fountain were built in 1924–1925 in the Nordic classicism of the 1920s, to designs by Hugo Jahnke. One was a kiosk, the other a taxi stand.
De ursprungliga radhusen hade tre rum oc: The original terraced houses had three rooms and a kitchen and were only 5.75 metres wide. By the mid-20th century they were hard to fill, so in some of them the kitchen was moved down to the basement, which had originally been just for storage.
De väggmålningar som fortfarande syns på: The murals you can still see on the façades around the square were painted by the architects and their staff themselves. The regular painters had refused, on the grounds that 'surely a house can't look like that'.
De yngsta mynten i Vallaskatten präglade: The youngest coins in the Valla hoard were minted under Charles IX, so the treasure was probably hidden shortly after 1611. It had been buried in a rock crevice in the woods on Valla's land.
De yttersta skären sköljs ständigt över: The outermost skerries are constantly washed by salt water and support little more than lichens and salt-tolerant grasses. On the larger Amundö islands people even farmed, and in sheltered spots sessile oak, silver birch and black alder grow.
De äldsta bevarade husen ritades av slot: The oldest surviving buildings were designed by the royal architect Nicodemus Tessin the Younger around 1700. The newest is Moderna Museet, the Museum of Modern Art, designed by the Spanish architect Rafael Moneo and opened in 1998. The old naval storehouse, Intendenturförrådet, is the only surviving monumental building by the city architect Johan Eberhard Carlberg.
De äldsta delarna av Danderyds kyrka är: The oldest parts of Danderyd Church date from around 1400, and there was probably a chapel on the site even earlier. Farm names and rune carvings show that people have lived in the area since at least the Iron Age.
De åtta studenthusen på Bosön står i sol: The eight student houses on Bosön island fan out around a small hill, and each has a sporting name: Bollen, Bågen, Båten, Hjälmen, Kubban, Kulan, Skidan and Värjan – the Ball, the Bow, the Boat, the Helmet, the Kubb, the Shot, the Ski and the Foil. The laundry on the hill is called Kompassen, the Compass.
Delar av Tyresta nationalpark präglas av: Parts of Tyresta National Park still bear the marks of the 1999 forest fire. In the burnt area a new species of fly has been discovered: the Tyresta fly.
Delfinkar och 3,6 km staket: Dolphin basins and 3.6 km of railings
Delsjövägen fick sitt namn 1923 efter De: Delsjövägen was named in 1923 after Delsjön, a lake about 1.5 kilometres south-east of here. In 1312 the lake was written Dilsiö, and in 1650 Delesiön.
Delvis under Södertäljevägen, en bit här: Partly beneath the main road, Södertäljevägen, a little way from here, lies Svarta Löt – one of the best-known medieval assembly sites in the area, where local courts, or “things”, were already being held when Stockholm was founded. It's thought to have been near the croft of Eriksberg, once called Tingsta, on the Kumla estate. Older still is Albykistan, a reconstructed stone burial chamber from the late Stone Age, dated to around 1800 BC. Only seven graves of this kind are known in the whole of Stockholm County.
Den 1 april 1949 fotograferade trafikins: On 1 April 1949 the traffic inspector Einar Lundh photographed the first train to switch onto the new double track between Baggeby and AGA. The picture shows the station name on the ridge of the roof and a Linderoths station clock on top. Both are gone today.
Den 1 december 2018 invigdes folkbibliot: On 1 December 2018 the public library Världslitteraturhuset, the House of World Literature, opened in one of the tower blocks in the middle of the square. It replaced Gamlestaden's old library in the community centre, which closed that autumn.
Den 1 januari 1914 förbjöds försäljning: On 1 January 1914 the sale of fresh meat on the square was banned for reasons of hygiene. Soon fish, butter, cheese, bread and cooked food were banned too, and many traders moved into the market halls. That left the market gardeners and the fruit, vegetable and flower sellers.
Den 1 maj 1957 flyttade de allra första: On 1 May 1957, the very first residents of Farsta moved into the tower block at Filipstadsbacken 36. That was no accident: while the bus routes and metro were still being built, only here could you catch a train into town, from the station then called Södertörns villastad – today's Farsta Strand.
Den 1 oktober 1930 började spårvagnslinj: On 1 October 1930 tram line 19 began serving the area. It ran on the same embankment that the metro line of the same number uses today. On 9 September 1951 the trams were replaced by the metro.
Den 12 mars 1992 skenade ett strömlöst s: On 12 March 1992 a tram that had lost power ran away backwards down Guldhedsgatan and Aschebergsgatan at an estimated 100 km/h. At Vasaplatsen it derailed and ploughed across the stop. Thirteen people were killed and 29 injured.
Den 13 september 1971 låg hällen mitt i: On 13 September 1971, the rock lay right in the path of the new Botkyrkaleden road, completely overgrown. The archaeologist Rudolf Hansson got curious and peeled back some moss – revealing a carving of a ship. The road authorities altered the route at the last minute so the rock could stay where it was.
Den 14 april 1993 rasade marken vid Agne: On 14 April 1993, the ground gave way at the Agnesberg industrial estate on the eastern bank of the Göta älv river, not far from here. A ship's pilot spotted the landslide at nine o'clock – by which time a patch of land about 20 by 50 metres had already slid into the river. The slide reached right up to an industrial building, and several smaller slips followed later that day.
Den 15 juli 2008 rånades Casino Cosmopol: On 15 July 2008 Casino Cosmopol was robbed – the first time a casino had ever been held up in Sweden. Its four floors held around thirty gaming tables and some 350 slot machines.
Den 15 juni 1950 startade det första Mid: On 15 June 1950 the first Midnight Sun Rally – later the Swedish Rally – set off from Götaplatsen with 30 entrants. Other competitors started at the same time from Stockholm and Falsterbo.
Den 15 september 1940 förstördes Hersby: On 15 September 1940 the farm buildings at Hersby gård were destroyed in a huge fire. Only the log-built granary from the early 1800s could be saved, and terraced houses were later built where the burned buildings had stood.
Den 17 juni 1911 klockan 19.30 startade: At 7.30 pm on 17 June 1911, Skansen's open-air theatre opened with the play Värmlänningarna.
Den 18 juli 1994 firade herrlandslaget i: On 18 July 1994 the Swedish men's football team celebrated their World Cup bronze medals in Rålambshovsparken, known locally as Rålis. More than 70,000 people sang När vi gräver guld i USA along with the band GES.
Den 18 mars 1923 kom närmare 4 000 perso: On 18 March 1923 almost 4,000 people turned up at IFK's old home ground to watch them beat Göteborgs BIS 7–0. Around New Year 2001–2002 the pitch was covered in crushed stone and turned into a car park.
Den 19 oktober 1979 inledde Abba här den: On 19 October 1979 Abba kicked off the European leg of their final world tour here. In 1985 the arena hosted the Eurovision Song Contest, presented by Lill Lindfors and won by Bobbysocks from Norway. Kiss have played here eight times.
Den 20 oktober 1953 grävde man efter fyl: On 20 October 1953, workers digging for fill for a house at Nyodlingsvägen 4 found the runestone. It was lying on what had once been the farmyard of old Kummelby.
Den 22 februari 1944 fällde ett sovjetis: On 22 February 1944 a Soviet bomber dropped three bombs here. Two landed in Eriksdalslunden park and the third destroyed the new Eriksdal Theatre. Nobody was hurt, but a few seconds later and Södersjukhuset hospital could have been hit. It was the only time bombs fell on Stockholm during the war.
Den 22 september 2022 nådde tornet 193 m: On 22 September 2022 the tower reached 193 metres, overtaking Turning Torso in Malmö as the tallest building in the Nordic countries. The first residents moved in on 22 August 2023.
Den 23 juli 1901 exploderade lasten på b: On 23 July 1901 the cargo of the barque Louise Adelaide, which had come from Philadelphia with crude oil and paraffin, exploded by the superphosphate factory. Ten people were killed. The wreck was identified during surveys in 2008–2009.
Den 23 mars 1836 såldes Kungsporten för: On 23 March 1836 Kungsporten, the King's Gate, was sold for 345 riksdaler banko to the master coppersmith Carl Erik Lilja, but the purchase passed to the city. Despite several attempts to save it, the gate was demolished in 1836–1838.
Den 25 april 1973 köpte Mölndals kommun: On 25 April 1973, Mölndal municipality bought the farm and the surrounding land – just over 412,000 square metres in all – for 1.2 million kronor.
Den 26 april 1937, på sin 45-årsdag, fly: On 26 April 1937, his 45th birthday, Harry Hjörne moved with his family into a third-floor flat in the GP building, home of the Göteborgs-Posten newspaper.
Den 26 december 1961 öppnade biografen F: On 26 December 1961 the Fanfaren cinema opened, with 535 seats and a CinemaScope screen. After various ups and downs it closed in May 1992.
On 26 December 1961, the Fanfaren cinema opened with 535 seats and a CinemaScope screen. After various ups and downs, it closed in May 1992.
Den 26 november 1867 gled drygt två tunn: On 26 November 1867, more than two acres of land slid into Ulvsundasjön lake. Cobblestones ordered for Stockholm's streets, two stone jetties and an expensive crane all vanished – and none of it was insured. The flat ground the landslide left behind later became a festival ground.
Den 26 september 1986 spelade Cliff Burt: On 26 September 1986, Cliff Burton played his last concert with Metallica here at Solnahallen. Shortly afterwards he was killed when the tour bus crashed outside Ljungby in Småland.
Den 27 november 2020 stängde Skansen för: On 27 November 2020 Skansen closed for the first time in its 129-year history, because of its poor finances during the coronavirus pandemic. In its first fifty years, by contrast, the open-air museum made such healthy profits that it funded the Nordic Museum.
Den 27 september 1912 testade Ericssons: On 27 September 1912 Ericsson's friend Gustaf Dalén was testing acetylene cylinders in a quarry at Alby. One that had failed to explode went off as he walked up to it. Dalén barely survived and lost his sight.
Den 28 juni 2024 flyttades herrgården om: On 28 June 2024 the manor house was moved about 500 metres in one piece. It travelled on a special trailer at a speed of 0.1 kilometres an hour.
Den 29 maj 1958 invigdes arenan med en m: The stadium opened on 29 May 1958 with a match between the Swedish national team and a Gothenburg city side, watched by 49,493 spectators. It ended 2–2, and the very first goal was scored by Gunnar Gren. That evening a 'Miss Ullevi' was crowned as well.
Den 3 april 1973 öppnade OBS i Bäckebol,: On 3 April 1973, OBS opened in Bäckebol: 30,000 square metres, and at the time the biggest hypermarket in the country. Long before that, this was Bäckebol farm. Work on its stone manor house began in 1764 under the weighmaster Johan Oliveholm, and it has been a listed building since 1969. The estate's owners even have a private burial ground of their own, in use since the mid-1700s.
Den 3 mars 1957 beslöt magistraten i Göt: On 3 March 1957 Gothenburg's city authorities decided to split Arendal into two districts, Arendal and Syrhåla. Arendal became a purely industrial area – only 90 people lived there in 2012 – and it's home to the headquarters of Volvo Buses, among others. Syrhåla kept its old name, first recorded in 1550, which means a swampy place or sour ground.
Den 30-åriga drottning Elizabeth bad om: The 30-year-old Queen Elizabeth asked to see a Swedish housing area. In June 1956, accompanied by King Gustaf VI Adolf, she visited the villa at Anundsvägen 49, owned by the Larsson family.
Den 4 september 1923 landade fransmannen: On 4 September 1923 the Frenchman J. Dagnaux landed at Barkarby after flying from Paris in twelve hours. Until 1936 Barkarby and Bulltofta were the only Swedish airports with scheduled international flights.
Den 5 augusti 1776 sålde Arren von Kapel: On 5 August 1776 Arren von Kapelman – brother-in-law of the poet Carl Michael Bellman and owner of Hägersten farm – sold Hökmossens gård for 600 daler. The buyer was Johan Rydgren, a kitchen steward at the Royal Palace. The farm was also known as Kristineberg.
Den 5 december 1846 blev Göteborg först: On 5 December 1846 Gothenburg became the first town in Sweden with a gas supply, piped from the gasworks by the Rosenlund Canal. The gasworks at Gullbergsvass was, in its day, the second largest in the country.

On 5 December 1846 Gothenburg became the first city in Sweden to have town gas, supplied by the gasworks on the Rosenlund Canal. In its day, the gasworks at Gullbergsvass was the second largest in the country.
Den 5 december 1963 öppnade KF sin först: On 5 December 1963 the Swedish co-op KF opened its first hypermarket in Sweden here, modelled on American supermarkets. Many doubted people would travel so far to shop, but in its very first year it turned over 36 million kronor – far above budget.
Den 5 september 1970 brann huset efter e: On 5 September 1970 the store burned down after an electrical fault in an advertising sign. The management hadn't been able to decide between 'Möbel-IKEA' and 'IKEA', so both signs had gone up. Some 8,000 people queued for the fire sale – some had slept in tents – and the store reopened in March 1971.
Den 5 september 1970 brann varuhuset eft: On 5 September 1970 the department store burned down after an electrical fault in an advertising sign. Around 8,000 people queued for the fire sale, some of them having slept in tents. The insurance payout of 23 million kronor was the biggest in Sweden up to that time.
Den 6 november 1810 gick Sveriges första: On 6 November 1810, Heden hosted Sweden's first horse race run the English way. There were three races, each over an English mile. George Hebden won two of them and Emanuel Norling the third.
Den 7 maj 1977 blev Göte Kärnsby Ullevis: On 7 May 1977 Göte Kärnsby became Ullevi's ten-millionth visitor.
Den 8 februari 1812 stal Lasse-Maja till: On 8 February 1812 the notorious thief Lasse-Maja and two accomplices stole the church silver from Järfälla church. After the thefts he was caught, convicted and locked up in Carlsten fortress in Marstrand.
Den 8 september 1966 klippte statsrådet: On 8 September 1966, after seven years of construction, government minister Olof Palme cut the ribbon. Frölunda Torg was then the largest shopping centre under one roof in the Nordic countries, and it had its own tram stop from day one. In the first four days alone, 50,000 people came through the doors.
Den 8 september 1968 invigde prins Berti: On 8 September 1968 Prince Bertil opened Skärholmen and its shopping centre. Back then it was entirely open-air, with streets and walkways, and had its own cinema, Vågen. In 1984 the streets were glazed over.
Den T-formade parkens södra del är i nut: The southern part of the T-shaped park is laid out in a modern take on the Baroque, with straight gravel paths and a fountain. The northern part is more modern, with a paddling pool and Egon Möller-Nielsen's play sculpture Ägget – the Egg – from 1952. Husmorssemester is by Olof Thorwald Ohlsson.
Den allra första operan som sattes upp h: The very first opera staged here was Aniara, followed by The Marriage of Figaro and Madama Butterfly. The house has also hosted Melodifestivalen 2000 – Sweden's Eurovision selection – and the Guldbagge Awards, the Swedish film awards.
Den andra förbränningsanläggningen invig: The second incineration plant opened in 1938. It was designed by Holger Blom in the functionalist style, with yellow-brick façades, and its chimney stood almost 58 metres tall. The building was demolished in 2006.
Den andra gasklockan togs i bruk år 1900: The second gasholder came into use in 1900 and was then considered the largest in the world, with a capacity of 65,000 cubic metres. It was needed: gas production had more than doubled during the 1890s.
Den branta kyrktomten krävde mycket arbe: The steep church site took a lot of work. The terrace walls and church park weren't built until the 1940s, and were finished in 1943.
Den bro du ser i dag blev klar 1980, bre: The bridge you see today was finished in 1980, next to the 1929 bridge. It's a steel girder bridge resting on nine concrete pillars, with a clearance of just 1.6 metres.
Den danskfödde arkitekten Hack Kampmann: The Danish-born architect Hack Kampmann was given a free hand and designed low façades of glass, render and sheet metal around a square with a pond. City commissioner Walfrid Frank praised the architects for abandoning 'the sky-storming' in favour of a human scale.

The Danish-born architect Hack Kampmann designed the whole complex, metro buildings included, in a distinctly international Modernism rarely seen in Sweden. The combination of a tall residential block, a low-rise centre and a metro station has no equal in Stockholm.

The Danish-born architect Hack Kampmann designed the whole complex of slab block, shopping centre and metro station – a combination unmatched in Stockholm. The slab block is 170 metres long and just 13 metres deep, with access balconies facing north and private balconies facing south.

The Danish-born architect Hack Kampmann changed the town plan and built a single 170-metre slab block above the centre's low-rise buildings instead of two smaller blocks. His reasons were both aesthetic and economic: it meant not having to put a large building on top of the metro.
Den del av Hagsätra som ligger sydväst o: The part of Hagsätra south-west of Huddingevägen has a name of its own: Ormkärr. A little further away is Hagsätra Centre, which opened in 1960 after just a year of building – the same year the metro reached Hagsätra. The centre's trademark is Barnet med käpphästen, 'The Child with the Hobby Horse', a copper sculpture designed by Marie Stenqvist.
Den del av Ånäsvägen som går mellan Redb: The stretch of Ånäsvägen between Redbergsplatsen and Ejdergatan once had a delightful name: Nyfikeliden, or simply Nyfiken and Nyfika – 'nyfiken' means curious. 'Liden' means a slope, and the name probably comes from a house called Nyfika on a map from 1790. Ånäsvägen itself was named in 1883 after the Ånäs country estate and is just over a kilometre long.
Den ena igensatt, den andra i bruk: One sealed, the other in use
Den enda byggnaden vid Husarvikens norra: The only building on the northern shore of Husarviken is Fisksjöängsladan, a barn that held winter feed for the deer of the Royal Djurgården. Every log is numbered, because the barn was moved here in the mid-1800s.
Den enda synliga ledtråden till Elefante: The only visible clue to Elefanten is the radio mast on the hill above. Inside the rock, three buildings stand on shock-absorbing springs, clear of the rock walls, and they're clad in fully welded steel plates to protect against electromagnetic pulses.
Den engelske metodistpastorn George Scot: The English Methodist minister George Scott built the first church here, the English Chapel. He was unpopular, and on Palm Sunday 1842 a mob stormed the building. Scott was forced to flee, and the chapel stayed closed until 1851.
Den faluröda Sätra friidrottshall invigd: The Falu red Sätra athletics hall opened in April 1998. The idea was that it would also host badminton if Stockholm won the 2004 Summer Olympics.
Den faluröda nödbostadslängan på klippan: The Falu-red row of emergency housing on the rock by Ulvsundavägen was designed by Gustaf Larson. The bottom floors are stone and the upper ones wood – a type known in Gothenburg as a landshövdingehus. It was meant to be temporary, but thanks to its handsome facade it became permanent in the 1960s.
Den fristående klockbocken är formad som: The free-standing bell frame is shaped like a mainsail and holds three freely hanging bells with inscriptions. Inside the church, the font, pulpit and altar base are cast in bare concrete, and the floor is laid with handmade brick.
Den fristående klockstapeln tros vara li: The free-standing bell tower is thought to be as old as the churchyard, which dates from the 1830s and began as a cholera cemetery. The original bell from 1835 was moved to the church, and the tower now holds a bell cast at the Götaverken shipyard in 1933.
Den fula ankungen blev svan: The ugly duckling became a swan
Den första Kummelby kyrka från 1957 hade: The first Kummelby Church, from 1957, seated only 50 people and was sometimes called Kummelby's 'little church'. Problems with its foundations led to its demolition, which caused quite a stir. A new church in Danish brick was consecrated just before Christmas 2000.
Den första Marieholmsbron togs i bruk i: The first Marieholm Bridge opened in March 1909 and was then the longest railway bridge in Sweden. The engineers chose a bridge rather than an embankment across Marieholm because solid ground lay so far down – and a bridge is lighter.
Den första Nybodatunneln, 276 meter lång: The first Nyboda tunnel, 276 metres long, was blasted out in 1858–1859 by convicts from Långholmen prison using black powder. The rock was hauled up with hand-driven cranes, under the watch of armed guards.
Den första bastun var en prototyp. Somma: The first sauna was a prototype. In the summer of 2024 it was replaced by a permanent building that looks exactly the same from outside. Everything was renewed except the metal facade panels, which were kept.
Den första bilen från Torslandaverken va: The first car off the line at the Torslanda plant was a Volvo Amazon, presented to King Gustaf VI Adolf. At the opening in 1964 the King rode through the factory in the back seat of a Volvo ÖV4. Two days later, more than 20,000 employees and their families were invited.
Den första bron byggdes av Svea ingenjör: The first bridge was built by the Svea Engineer Regiment to supply the Södra Fronten defence line. Work began in 1913, but a shortage of planks for the roadway meant it wasn't finished until the following year. After the First World War it lost its strategic importance.
Den första bron över Lullehovssundet var: The first bridge across the Lullehovssundet strait was a pontoon bridge from around 1830, just west of today's bridge. The old road embankment and a milestone reading "1 MIL" survive. The stone bears the initials of the county governor, Gustaf Fredrik Liljencrantz.
Den första bron över Skurusundet var en: The first bridge over Skurusundet strait was a pontoon bridge from around 1830, built at the old ferry crossing. The engineer in charge was Immanuel Nobel, father of Alfred Nobel. There was a toll to cross.
Den första bron över sundet, en flottbro: The first bridge across the strait, a pontoon bridge, was laid around 1830 just west of today's bridge. The old road embankment and a milestone reading "1 MIL" survive. The stone bears the initials of the county governor, Gustaf Fredrik Liljencrantz.
Den första filmen här spelades in redan: The first film shot here was made as early as summer 1920: Victor Sjöström's The Phantom Carriage. But it was so complicated, with all its double exposures, that Mauritz Stiller's Erotikon reached cinemas first. The first Swedish sound film was also recorded here, in 1929.
Den första färjan på leden rymde 12 pers: The first ferry on the route carried 12 cars, and the one that replaced it takes 16. Short as the crossing is, the Björkö ferry is the sixth busiest route run by Färjerederiet, with just over 540,000 vehicles in 2009.
Den första gården på platsen byggdes i t: The first farmhouse on the site was built of wood around 1630, and Gustav II Adolf granted permission for an inn next door. That inn is still here and since 2021 has been run as Edsbacka Krog. Queen Christina stayed at the farm in 1645.
Den första klaffbron över Tappström bygg: The first bascule bridge over Tappström was built in 1828. In the 1880s it was replaced by an opening wooden bridge paid for by the bank director André Oscar Wallenberg. New bridges then followed in 1930 and 1973.
Den första kullen studenter utexaminerad: The first students graduated in 1911. Among them was Assar Gabrielsson, who came up with the idea for Volvo and was its CEO from 1927 to 1956. Dag Hammarskjöld also worked at the school.
Den första kvarnen vid Jakobsbergs gård: The first mill at Jakobsberg farm was probably built in the 1780s. By 1926, when milling stopped, 25 millers had worked there. Most of them stayed only a year or two.
Den första kyrkan byggdes i romansk stil: The first church was built in Romanesque style in the 12th century. After a fire in the late 13th century it was rebuilt in Gothic style, and by around 1500 it had reached its present size.

The first church was built in the Romanesque style in the 1100s. In the late 1200s it was ravaged by fire and rebuilt in the Gothic style, and by around 1500 it had reached its present size. The small church bell dates from 1653.
Den första kyrkan i Tynnered, från 1967,: Tynnered's first church, from 1967, was a portable church made by Oresjö Sektionshus. It was later moved and became Grevegården's church. Today's church was consecrated in 1973 by Bishop Bertil Gärtner.
Den första kyrkan med namnet ritades av: The first church of that name was designed by Adrian C. Peterson and consecrated in 1886. The driving force was the vicar Uddo Lechard Ullman, a champion of Gothic Revival in Swedish church architecture. The altar group, with a large crucifix, came from Munich.
Den första kyrkan, i nygotik: The first church, in Gothic Revival style
Den första kända bosättningen på Fotö är: The first known settlement on Fotö dates from the 1600s, and by 1880 the island had 98 residents. The new fishing harbour on the Söö islet and the ferry arrived in the 1960s, and since 1993 the Fotö Bridge has linked the island with Hönö.
Den första kända ägaren av Partille herr: The first known owner of Partille Manor was Oluff Nilsson. In 1583 he bought the estate from the Crown for 18½ daler in silver coin and two oxen.
