Det var arkitekten Sven Wedenmark som by: In 1939 the architect Sven Wedenmark rebuilt and extended the building in the functionalist style. The Rex cinema was owned by Hugo Hansson.
Det var bolaget Lidingö villastad, under: From 1906, the company Lidingö villastad, led by Hjalmar Arwin, turned Lidingö from farmland and a summer retreat for well-off Stockholmers into a modern suburb. Its very first purchase, and its first office, was Vattängen farm on Stockholmsvägen. In the middle of the villa town you'll also find Centralpalatset, built in 1912–1913, and Vasaborgen, which was planned as early as 1913 but not built until 1923.
Det var diakonissorna på Ersta diakoniss: It was the deaconesses at the Ersta deaconess institute on Södermalm who objected to the name Ersta Villastad. The naming committee then went looking for historical events and settled on the Battle of Brännkyrka, where Sten Sture the Younger drove out Christian II. And so the area became Stureby.
Det var drottning Victoria som drev på,: It was Queen Victoria who pushed for the clinic, after hearing from her mother about good results with X-rays and radium in Germany. It deliberately opened in an ordinary eight-room flat to make patients feel more at ease. The equipment: one X-ray machine and 120 mg of radium.
Det var elever från Enskedefältets skola: In 2016 pupils from Enskedefältet school wrote to the district council suggesting the spot be smartened up. The proposal was approved, and the following year the last wooden structure was pulled down and steps were built up the hill.
Det var elever på Enskedefältets skola s: It was pupils at Enskedefältet school who wrote to the district council suggesting the spot be smartened up. Now there's a viewpoint with a roof and benches on the old concrete foundations, and the slopes below have become popular sledging hills.
Det var en nykterhetsklubb som byggde hu: The building was put up by a temperance club and opened in 1903 as a Folkets hus, a community hall. In the 1940s it became a sweet factory, from 1954 a warehouse, and by the mid-1980s it was almost ready to be pulled down before it was restored.
Det var fiskebåten GG 195 Normy från Häl: It was the Hälsö fishing boat GG 195 Normy that, after almost three weeks of searching, found the submarine Ulven on 5 May 1943. The submarine had struck a mine south-west of Stora Pölsan.

It was the Hälsö fishing boat GG 195 Normy that found the submarine Ulven on 5 May 1943, after almost three weeks of searching. The submarine had struck a mine south-west of Stora Pölsan and gone down with all hands.
Det var grosshandlarna Fredric Althainz: In 1887 the wholesale merchants Fredric Althainz and Carl Bengtsson bought Farsta farm – around 1,000 hectares. Althainz’s firm owned Eldkvarn mill on Kungsholmen, where Stockholm City Hall stands today. They divided the land into almost 600 plots.
Det var i juni 1956 som 30-åriga drottni: In June 1956 the 30-year-old Queen Elizabeth asked to see a Swedish housing area. Accompanied by King Gustaf VI Adolf, she visited the house at Anundsvägen 49, then owned by the Larsson family.
Det var kronprins Gustaf Adolf som invig: It was Crown Prince Gustaf Adolf who opened Kvarnbyvallen on 15 July 1934. Fässbergs IF had asked for a sports ground as early as 1919, but a first attempt was halted by a strike, and a second try in 1926 also came to nothing.
Det var kyrkoherde Bengt Thure Molander: In the early 1970s the vicar Bengt Thure Molander came up with the idea of the heritage trail, to make the island's many ancient monuments better known. The Lovö local history society laid it out, and in 2015 it was reopened with new signs. The route is marked with slanted blue metal plates.
Det var mycket bråk på krogen, och 1853: There was plenty of trouble at the inn, and in 1853 it was banned from serving spirits. In 1872 it closed altogether for lack of customers, and the building became a primary school. It wasn't until Walpurgis Eve 1983, 111 years later, that Christer Lingström opened a restaurant here again.
Det var några vandringsentusiaster ledda: It was a group of hiking enthusiasts led by Kurt Kjellgren from Gnesta who began preparing the Sörmlandsleden trail in 1966. By 1975 you could walk some 500 kilometres from Björkhagen to Nyköping, and in 1988 the loop around Sörmland was complete.
Det var på Grand som Olof och Lisbeth Pa: It was at the Grand that Olof and Lisbeth Palme watched the film The Mozart Brothers on 28 February 1986, before the Prime Minister was murdered on his way home. The cinema visit became hugely important in the investigation.
Det var tänkt som Centrala Bromma: It was meant to be Central Bromma
Det var ägaren till två Esso-macker vid: It was Tore Jakobson, owner of two Esso petrol stations by the main road, who gave the spot the name Kungens kurva – 'the King's Bend'. The name later became official for the whole area. A planned square is to be called Gustav V:s torg.
Det var översten Albert Amundson som eft: It was Colonel Albert Amundson who gave the house its castle-like look after 1889, adding a towered extension, tall Renaissance gables, bay windows and turrets. Upstairs he fitted out a knights' hall with 17th-century furniture.
Det vita huset med grön kopparkupol på h: The white building with a green copper dome on the corner of Basargatan was designed by city architect Heinrich Kaufmann and built in 1850. The dome was added in 1891, when the savings bank bought the building. Since 2004 it has housed the Chinese Consulate General.
Det välvda trätaket målades av John Sten: The vaulted wooden ceiling was painted by John Sten in a style that echoes 17th- and 18th-century church painting, with naive scenes from Bible history. The church is well preserved and a popular choice for weddings.
Det välvda trätaket och väggarna målades: The vaulted wooden ceiling and the walls were painted by John Sten in a style recalling 17th- and 18th-century church painting, with naive scenes from the Bible. The church is well preserved from when it was built and is popular for weddings.
Det äldsta belägget för namnet Ekerö, ”a: The earliest record of the name Ekerö, "akru", is on a runestone found on 22 April 2013 at Bogesundslandet.
Det äldsta i Backa kyrka är dopfunten i: The oldest thing in Backa church is the soapstone font from the medieval church, probably made after 1250. It has no drain hole, and its original base was replaced with a new one in 1934.
Det äldsta skriftliga belägget för Ågest: The oldest written record of Ågesta dates from the 1330s, when Canon Brynolf of Strängnäs left his cloak to Christine in Agastum in his will. Archaeological finds show there was a farm here as early as the 4th–5th centuries.
Det äldsta torpet i Alvik, Ahlwijken, nä: Alvik's oldest croft, Ahlwijken, is mentioned in the land register of 1720 and stood between today's metro station and Sankt Ansgars kyrka. In 1787 it was turned into an inn, Krogen Alvik.
Det är inte klarlagt vem som ritade Vill: Nobody knows for sure who designed Villa Strandvik. It's often attributed to Ferdinand Boberg, but the client's British-born wife, Maud Jane Beavis, was also involved – and the drawings are signed by the master builder G. A. Bengtsson.
Det är inte varje dag man ser en soffgru: It's not every day you see a three-piece suite on a rooftop – but you will here. The furniture store founded by Skinngruppen in 1975 has become a local landmark thanks to the giant sofa perched on top. Krokslätt used to be an industrial area, home to the Krokslätt factories, and it's also where the very first self-built family homes in the Gothenburg area went up.
Det öppningsbara taket är 107 gånger 80: The retractable roof measures 107 by 80 metres – slightly larger than the pitch – and sits 33 metres up. It was supplied by the Dutch company Hollandia and rolls across eight roof beams on wheels fitted with SKF bearings. The arena is ready for grass, gravel and ice.

Dieselverkstaden används i dag av Nacka: Today Dieselverkstaden, the old Diesel Workshop, is used by Nacka's culture department, with a library, a cinema and several stages.
Dieselverkstaden hette ursprungligen Sam: Dieselverkstaden, the Diesel Workshop, was originally known as the Assembly Hall, and Atlas Diesel built diesel engines here right up until 1951. Since 2002 the old factory hall has been full of culture instead, with an arts centre, a library, a climbing centre and a five-screen cinema. And deep beneath the shopping streets of Sickla Köpkvarter is a test mine where rock drills and mining machines are put through their paces.
Direkt väster om gården ligger ett gravr: Just west of the farm is a Bronze Age burial cairn, 35 metres across and 5–6 metres high. It's the second-largest known cairn in the province of Södermanland.
Disponentvillan har tio rum och fasader: The managing director's villa has ten rooms and façades of dark red Helsingborg brick, chosen to signal exclusivity. The house came with a large garden and a tennis court. The first to move in was the mill's technical manager, Emil Hamring.
Ditzingers två hus är inte bara identisk: Ditzinger's two houses aren't just identical – they're mirror images of each other. Their style comes from the ornate board-clad architecture of the day, typical of wealthy Stockholmers' summer villas. The farm's old earth cellar is still there.
Ditzingers två hus är inte bara lika, de: The two Ditzinger houses aren't just alike – they're mirror images of each other. Their style was inspired by the timber-panelled architecture of well-to-do Stockholmers' summer villas. The brothers didn't keep them long: they sold the property as early as 1890.
Djupt inne i berget under bostadsområdet: Deep in the rock beneath the Eriksberg housing area, the red line's metro trains sleep. Norsborg depot lies 18 to 37 metres down inside Aspberget and the Eriksbergsåsen ridge, connected to the metro at Norsborg. Norsborg station itself, a couple of minutes from here, opened in 1975 and is the westernmost station on the whole network.
Djupt inne i ett bergrum i Edsberg finns: Deep inside a rock cavern in Edsberg lies Elefanten, 'the Elephant' – a command centre built in 1972–77 to withstand a nuclear bomb, with room for 200 people. It was meant to protect the leaders of Stockholm and Sollentuna municipalities in the event of war. After standing empty for 19 years, it was bought in 2017 by the Swedish Armed Forces, who modernised it and put it back into service. Above ground, life is more peaceful, with Edsberg church, a red wooden church.
Djupt under campus forskade man en gång: Deep under the campus, scientists once carried out research in accelerator physics. Since 2019 the old laboratory has been the Accelerator art gallery, opened by the artist Tino Sehgal. The lab is named after Manne Siegbahn, winner of the 1924 Nobel Prize in Physics. Ralph Erskine designed the Law Building as a semicircle wrapped around an old oak – and the same idea of sparing the oaks shaped Aula Magna too.
Djupt under fötterna, 27 till 36 meter n: Deep below your feet, 27 to 36 metres down in the bedrock, is the metro station, opened in 1975. Above it is one of the biggest shopping centres in the Stockholm region, with more than 95 shops and 22 restaurants. Across Centralvägen is Eric Grate's Park, named after the sculptor, who spent the last fifteen years of his life in Solna. Two of his bronzes stand there: Oberon and Sparvguden, the Sparrow God.

Djursholm är villornas rike, och i närhe: Djursholm is a world of grand villas, and nearby is Villa Snellman, one of the early works of the architect Gunnar Asplund. Djursholm's own Strandvägen, along the waters of Lilla and Stora Värtan, is often counted among the most exclusive addresses in Sweden. The Djursholm railway, Djursholmsbanan, used to run past here, and for many years there was a little kiosk selling sweets and newspapers on the narrow platform at the Bragevägen stop.
Djursholms första vattentorn tog vattnet: Djursholm's first water tower drew its water from Ösbysjön lake, but that wasn't enough once the garden suburb grew. Ekeby water tower was instead supplied from Lake Norrviken through a ten-kilometre pipeline, and according to one newspaper the water was crystal clear and tasted good.
Djursholms slott ägdes av ätten Banér i: Djursholm Castle belonged to the Banér family for over 300 years, from 1508 to 1813, and parts of it date from the late Middle Ages. Today it's the municipal hall – and you can hire its banqueting rooms for a wedding. On the hill next door is the water tower from 1890. It was built beside a little Dutch-style windmill, which was pulled down shortly afterwards. And Djursholm's co-educational school, founded in 1891, stood just nearby.

Djursjukhuset tar emot mer än 42 000 bes: The animal hospital receives more than 42,000 visits a year. Its expertise in exotic small animals and rodents is unique, and because it is owned by a foundation, every krona of profit goes back into the hospital.

Donsö kyrka byggdes 1932 som begravnings: Donsö church was built in 1932 as a funeral chapel and converted into a church in 1954–1955. Donsö kyrkogård invigdes 1834 och var fr: Donsö cemetery was consecrated in 1834 and began life as a cholera burial ground. Beside the church is a memorial to fishermen lost at sea.
Donsö är en levande skärgårdsö med Donsö: Donsö is a lively archipelago island with its own church and more than 1,500 year-round residents. A little to the south is tiny Kårholmen, which has a lovely story. On 7 May 1933, twenty people hired a motorboat, founded a club called Arbetarna till havet – “Workers to the Sea” – and were allowed to take over the island. They were all poor working people, and today the island is almost entirely covered with just over 80 summer cottages.

Dopfunten i glimmergnejs från förra hälf: The mica-gneiss font, from the first half of the 1100s, is carved with scenes including the baptism of Christ and Adam and Eve. Dopfunten är ett huggit granitblock som: The font is a carved block of granite set into the south wall. Water runs out of an opening in the wall, down into the font and on its way. The church also has a terracotta angel by Hertha Hillfon.
Dopfunten är gjord av Sven Palmqvist på: The font was made by Sven Palmqvist of Orrefors from loose glass blocks arranged in a square. The ceiling of the nave consists of folded concrete screens that let daylight in between them.

Drottningtorget ligger mitt framför Cent: Drottningtorget is the square right in front of the Central Station, which opened in 1858 and is one of the oldest station buildings in Sweden still in use. Drygt hälften av de 29 villorna såldes u: Just over half of the 29 villas were sold during the exhibition. The first residents were allowed to live rent-free for their first summer, provided they showed their homes to visitors.

The floors are staggered by half a level, giving flats on several levels with windows facing two ways. It was the light that Varhelyi was proudest of.

When it went up in 1957 it was Stockholm's tallest residential building, and today the City Museum has marked it blue, its highest grade. Down in the metro station are artworks by Lenka Jonesson, unveiled in 1991.

Duvbo kyrka invigdes första advent, den: Duvbo Church was consecrated on Advent Sunday, 27 November 1904, by Archbishop Johan August Ekman. The guests included Prince Carl and Princess Ingeborg. The idea came from Carl Alm, a local district officer who lived in the garden suburb of Duvbo himself.
Duvnäs nämns i skrift redan 1436, men vi: Duvnäs is mentioned in writing as early as 1436, but the villas only came once the Saltsjöbanan railway station opened in 1893. By Ringparken stands Herrgårdsvillan, built in 1910–1911 as a show home to tempt buyers to the new building plots, and in the park is Ringparksstugan, the cottage where neighbours celebrate the year's festivities. A little further on is Duvnäs Lower Manor, built by the industrialist Robert Finlay in the late 1740s.

Duvnäs is mentioned in records as early as 1436, but the villas didn't arrive until the Saltsjöbanan railway opened its station here in 1893. In Ringparken stands Herrgårdsvillan, the Manor Villa, built in 1910–11 as a show home to tempt buyers to the new building plots. The park is also home to Ringparksstugan, a cottage where neighbours get together for their yearly celebrations. A little further on, Kvarngården – the miller's house from the mid-1700s – is a reminder of the old watermill that once stood by Duvnäsviken bay.
Dvärgahuset beskrevs i skrift redan på 1: Dvärgahuset, "the dwarf's house", was described in writing as early as the 1600s, and local people probably knew of it long before that. In 1899 the archaeologist Oscar Montelius excavated the grave.
Där Alviks gamla industriområde en gång: Alvik's old industrial area by Lake Mälaren is now mostly offices and a handful of restaurants. Gamla Tryckeriet, the Old Printworks, is an events venue nearby where the TV competition show Floor Filler was recorded. The Tvärbanan light rail plunges into the rock through the Alvik tunnel, about 250 metres long, and then crosses the Oxhålssundet strait on the 400-metre Alvik bridge, completed in 2000.
Där Arendalsvarvet låg finns i dag ett s: Where the Arendal shipyard once stood there's now a large logistics and industrial area, home to Volvo Buses' head office and the Volvo Museum, among others. The property company Platzer bought most of the site from Volvo in 2016.
Där Bergslagsvägen går i dag låg under f: In prehistoric times a lake called Ängbysjön lay where Bergslagsvägen runs today. All that's left of it now is Råcksta träsk.
Där Bråviksvägen går i dag gjorde landsv: Where Bråviksvägen runs today, the old highway made a sharp 90-degree turn. Locals called it Snurrom or Snörom, and a stone-faced road embankment still survives.
Där Ekebyhovsbacken ligger fanns på 1950: In the 1950s the site of today's Ekebyhovsbacken ski slope was a gravel pit with a 55-metre summit. It was built up with demolition rubble to 82 metres above sea level – the highest artificial point on the ridge. The longest run is 510 metres.
Där Eriksbergsskolan ligger fanns förr e: Where Eriksbergsskolan school now stands there was once a marsh where people went skating in winter. Parts of the bottom were black, and rumour had it that a wagon full of tar had come off the rails. It later emerged that the state railway SJ had once treated railway sleepers with creosote here.
Där Flatenbanan ligger fanns torpet Ekst: Where the Flaten track is now, there used to be the croft of Ekstubben, belonging to Skarpnäck farm. In 1972 the Stockholm raggare – Sweden's American-car enthusiasts – opened a motor clubhouse here. The clubhouse survives and is now used as an indoor track for radio-controlled model cars, and the outdoor tracks are 330 and 340 metres long.
Där Fågelbergskyrkan står låg förr Rävek: Fågelberg Church stands where Rävekärr vicarage used to be. The last priest moved out in 1978, and the vicarage was demolished on 19 January 1984. On 1 December that same year, Bishop Bertil Gärtner consecrated the new church.
Där Hallonbergen ligger i dag fanns tidi: Where Hallonbergen stands today there was once a farm called Freden, where tobacco was grown. The area belonged to Spånga rural municipality before becoming part of Sundbyberg in 1949.
Där Husby står i dag övade militären änd: Where Husby stands today, soldiers were still training right up until 1965, as Järvafältet was a military training ground. The district was built in 1971 and was first called Husby gård. Today it has Husbybadet, a swimming centre with an adventure pool, a 25-metre pool and a diving tower with 1- and 3-metre boards.
Där Kattegatt möter Skagerrak: Where the Kattegat meets the Skagerrak
Där Linnégatan går rann förr Djupedalsbä: Where Linnégatan runs today, Djupedalsbäcken stream once flowed – its oldest known name, from 1624, was Ryssbäcken. It came down from Slottsskogen and dropped 12 metres towards Järntorget. In 1878 it was decided to fill it in and channel it through a culvert to the Göta älv river.
Där Masmobäcken skurit en djup ravin lig: Where the Masmobäcken stream has carved out a deep ravine lies the Stone Age settlement of Masmo. Those who lived there fetched their drinking water from the stream, because Albysjön was then a salty inlet of the Baltic. Evergreen plants such as rough horsetail grow in the ravine.
Där Obs! Stormarknad slog upp portarna 1: Where the Obs! Stormarknad hypermarket opened its doors in 1963, there was once Haga gård, an outlying farm of the Vårby estate that was pulled down in the early 20th century. The store building is still here, but Obs! closed in 1998 and furniture shops moved in. Right next door is Fittjanäset, and across the narrow strait to Fittja ran Fittja bro, the Fittja bridge – the main road south out of Stockholm until the end of the 1950s.
Där Rösjö centrum ligger i dag fanns Sve: Where Rösjö centrum stands today was once Svensk Talfilm's studio. From 1950 and for almost 20 years, the Åsa-Nisse films – much-loved Swedish rural comedies – were shot here, and many outdoor scenes were filmed in Skarpäng. John Elfström, who played Åsa-Nisse, lived in Skarpäng until his death in 1981.
Där Segeltorps gård låg står i dag en na: Where Segeltorp farm once stood, there's now an oak protected as a natural monument. It was protected in 1961, and by 2005 its trunk measured a full 464 centimetres round.
Där Skogskyrkogården ligger fanns tre gr: There were once three gravel pits where Skogskyrkogården, the Woodland Cemetery, now lies. One of them was shaped into an artificial valley with a reflecting pond, and selling the gravel was expected to cover the construction costs. Much of the digging was done as relief work during the First World War and the Depression of the 1930s.
Där Skärholmens centrum ligger i dag fan: Where Skärholmen centrum stands today there was once a farm, Smista gård, dating back to at least the 800s, and people were living nearby as early as the 200s, in the Roman Iron Age. In the 1700s and 1800s Smista was an outlying farm belonging to Vårby gård. Today you'll find, among other things, the Red Cross folk high school, some of whose courses even travel abroad, and Skärisbiografen, a cinema that opened in 2017.
Där Spånga IP ligger i dag fanns Spånga: Where Spånga sports ground is today, the Spånga radio broadcasting station stood from 1930 to 1954.
Där Spånga IP ligger i dag fanns mellan: Where Spånga sports ground is today, the Spånga radio transmitter stood from 1930 to 1954. Solhem had a volunteer fire brigade from 1925, whose firefighters built their own fire engines.
Där Spånga IP ligger i dag låg Spånga ru: From 1930 to 1954, the Spånga broadcasting station stood where Spånga IP sports ground is today.
Där Spånga IP ligger i dag låg mellan 19: Where Spånga IP sports ground is today, the Spånga broadcasting station stood from 1930 to 1954. At the local trade school, engines were built that were used in races at Solvalla.
Där Stockholmsmässan står i dag låg en g: Where Stockholmsmässan, the Stockholm exhibition centre, stands today, there used to be a lake. Brännkyrkasjön, also called Kyrksjön, lay just south of Brännkyrka Church and was drained bit by bit, from the 1870s right through to the 1950s. Since 1971 the exhibition halls and car parks have occupied the western side of the old lake bed, while the eastern side is still mostly open land.
Där Stora Tissan stod, i hörnet Dalagata: Where the Stora Tissan windmill once stood, on the corner of Dalagatan and Rådmansgatan, Adolf Fredrik's School was later built, opening in 1910. The mill itself was given new walls in Märsta, lost its sails in the 1920s and burned down in the early 1960s.
Där Strandska huset står låg förr staden: Where Strandska huset stands today was once the town's poorhouse and hospital, which burned down in 1796. In the new building, Göteborgs Handelsbank opened a branch in 1902, followed by the city's post office in 1906.
Där Ulriksdals Golfklubb ligger i dag gi: Where Ulriksdal Golf Club is today, the pace used to be much faster – this was once the site of the Ulriksdal racecourse. The commuter rail station is 7.1 kilometres from Stockholm Central, on the line towards Märsta, and took on its present look in 1990, with the ticket hall on the platform and the entrance through a pedestrian tunnel.
Där bostadsområdet Minneberg ligger låg: The Minneberg housing area stands on the site of the old Stockholm Bonemeal Factory, which turned out glue, bone oil, chicken feed and even a washing powder called Pärlglans. The smelly business moved away in 1968, and Minneberg was built in the 1980s. Next door is Tranebergs gård, a farm that goes back to a ferryman's croft from the 1670s. The croft was named Traneberg after its owner, Bengt Trana.
Där bostadsområdet Rissne ligger i dag h: The Rissne housing estate stands on old military ground. The Svea Artillery Regiment had its barracks here until 1963, and the Ordnance Administration School took over the site until 1977. The blocks of flats only went up between 1982 and 1988. Fittingly, the square was called Dragonplan, Dragoon Square, before it was renamed Rissne torg.
Där det nya bostadsområdet vid Farsta st: Where the new housing at Farsta strand is going up, there used to be a gravel pitch that was flooded for ice in winter. On the hockey rink next to it, Djurgården and national team player Mats Waltin, among others, took his first strides on skates.
Där egendomarna Hammarby, Enskede och Sk: Where the estates of Hammarby, Enskede and Skarpnäck met, the boundary was marked by a big white-painted stone called Vita sten. It's still there, by the bus stop south of Sockenvägen below Gränsberget hill.
Där gården står låg 1791–1822 Ulfsunda F: Where the farmhouse now stands, Ulfsunda Fabrique operated from 1791 to 1822, making art porcelain, tiled stoves and sugarloaf moulds. The stove-maker Anders Westman later bought the land to dig clay for his own production.
Där gårdens ladugård låg lät Gunnar och: On the site of the old farm's barn, opposite Bromma gymnasium, Gunnar and Alva Myrdal had Sven Markelius design their famous functionalist villa. Two-thirds of the district's villas were designed by a single architect, Edvin Engström, which is why the area looks so uniform.
Där gårdens park låg vid Drevvikens stra: Where the farm's park once ran down to the shore of Drevviken, you'll now find Gårdens bad, one of the municipality's public swimming spots.
Där idrottsplatsen ligger stod tidigare: Sweden's first broadcasting station once stood where the sports ground is now. It was demolished when construction began. The bandy rink opened in December 1977 with an international between Sweden and the Soviet Union.
Där kvarteret Barnmorskan ligger fanns t: Where the Barnmorskan block now stands there used to be a narrow strip of park, about 25 metres wide and 200 metres long. Of all the allotment gardens that surrounded the villa area in the 1920s, only Dalen's allotments remain.
Där kvarteret norr om Älvsjövägen ligger: The block north of Älvsjövägen was once the site of the Brotäppan homestead. According to the place-name scholar Carl Ivar Ståhle, the name marks the eastern end of Longabro, the log causeway that gave Långbro its name.
Där kyrkan står vände förr spårvagnarna: Where the church stands, trams used to turn in a loop with two stops: Källviken for getting off and Nockeby for getting on. The loop was removed in 1960, and Källviken was renamed Nockeby. King Gustav VI Adolf attended the consecration.
Där luftvärnet en gång siktade mot himle: Where the anti-aircraft guns once took aim at the sky, the two chimneys of the Käppala sewage works now stand right in the middle of the old firing range.
Där modellbilsbanan ligger fanns torpet: Where the model car track is now, there was once a croft called Ekstubben. In 1972 the Stockholmsraggarna, Stockholm's raggare car enthusiasts, opened their own motor club here. The clubhouse is still standing and is now used as an indoor track for radio-controlled cars.
Där mordet på kungen planerades: Where the king's murder was plotted
When the sun shines on Hisingen, there's electricity to be harvested. The Nya Solevi solar park, in Säve north-west of Gothenburg, is designed to produce around 5.5 gigawatt hours a year. It went up in record time: the first spade went into the ground in September 2018 and it opened in December the same year. While it was being planned, it was called Säve Solcellspark.
Där torget ligger i dag fanns tidigare s: Where the square is today there was once a lake called Fatburen. The square was laid out in the late 1850s, when the railway and Södra station arrived, as a market for farm produce coming in by train.
Där torget ligger i dag stod från 1630-t: From the 1630s until 1825, the Baroque palace Makalös – “Matchless” – stood where the square is today.
Där villorna står i dag låg förr åkrar s: The villas you see today stand on what were once fields belonging to Viksjö gård, a farm that goes back to prehistoric times. In 1921 the farm was sold to Viksjö AB, which went on farming the land, but in 1963 a group of builders began developing the area. The result is a mix of villas and terraced houses from the 1960s, 70s and 80s, with patches of nature in between.
Där ån lämnar Aspen har stranden grävts: Where the stream leaves Lake Aspen, the bank has been dug out into a narrow canal about 140 metres long that leads into the park. It then widens into several small ponds before carrying on eastwards.

Dösen byggdes omkring 3500 före Kristus: The dolmen was built on a seashore around 3500 BC, when the sea stood 15 metres higher than it does today.
EFS-föreningen i Furulund fanns i tjugo: The EFS congregation in Furulund – part of a Lutheran revival movement – existed for twenty years before its church was built in 2001. As early as 2007 it was extended, almost doubling the size of the worship space.
EPAs torg i Nationalteaterns låt: The 'EPA square' of a Nationalteatern song
Eddavägen var under många år slutstation: From 1901 to 1976 Eddavägen was the terminus of a branch of the Djursholmsbanan railway. The embankment of the closed Eddavägen line is now a footpath.
Edsbacka krog grundades 1626 vid landsvä: Edsbacka krog was founded in 1626 on the road between Stockholm and Uppsala. Gustav II Adolf granted the inn a charter, the first of its kind, and a copy hangs in the entrance today.
Edsbacka krog grundades redan 1626 av pr: Edsbacka krog was founded as early as 1626 by the quartermaster Henrik Olofsson, who received a royal charter from Gustav II Adolf to run an inn on the road between Stockholm and Uppsala. It was the first charter of its kind, and a copy hangs in the inn's entrance today.
Edsbacka krog vid Edsviken blev den förs: Edsbacka krog, by the Edsviken bay, became the first restaurant in Sweden to hold two Michelin stars, under the restaurateur Christer Lingström. The stars went when it changed hands in 2010, but since spring 2021 the restaurant has once again been called Edsbacka krog. Back in the 17th century, a fallen runestone lay just north of the restaurant; its base now stands just south of the avenue up to Edsberg Palace.
Edsbergs centrum invigdes 1964 och fick: Edsbergs centrum opened in 1964 and was given a makeover around 2004, including a new multi-storey car park. Here you'll find a library, a pharmacy, an Ica supermarket and two grill restaurants, Oscar and Ló Mero Kök och Bar. Right next door is Edsbergskyrkan, a red wooden church belonging to Sollentuna parish. The district is also home to Edsberg Palace, Rudbecksskolan school and the Edsbacka krog restaurant.
Edsbergs centrum invigdes 1964 och har b: Edsbergs centrum opened in 1964 and has a library, shops and a couple of grill bars. Right beside it stands Edsbergskyrkan, a red wooden church. And somewhere in the rock not far away lies Elefanten, 'the Elephant' – a command centre built in the 1970s to withstand a nuclear bomb, and now back in use by the Swedish Armed Forces.
Edsbergs slott stod färdigt 1760 vid Eds: Edsberg Palace, on the northern shore of Edsviken bay, was completed in 1760 at the initiative of Thure Gustaf Rudbeck, and the Rudbeck family owned it for almost 200 years. Today part of the Royal College of Music's chamber music programme is based here, and the palace has its own wedding room. Close by is Edsbacka krog, the first restaurant in Sweden to win two Michelin stars.
Edsbergskyrkan byggdes 1972 efter ritnin: Edsbergskyrkan was built in 1972 to designs by Lars Olof Torstensson. He created the 2004 altarpiece together with his son Jonas: a painted steel cross surrounded by glass in different colours. Before the church, a grey wooden hut called Edsbergsgården stood here.
Edsbergskyrkan ritades av Lars Olof Tors: Edsberg Church was designed by Lars Olof Torstensson and completed in 1972. He designed the 2004 altarpiece together with his son Jonas: a painted steel cross surrounded by glass in different colours.
Edsvikens bräckta vatten ger en unik mil: The brackish water of Edsviken creates a unique environment. Sea club-rush grows here, along with the tufted forget-me-not, rare in Sweden, and in autumn barnacle geese stop over in the bay.
Edsvikens villastad planerades som tjäns: The Edsviken garden suburb was planned as a white-collar suburb with 350 plots, and sales began in 1923. Many of the first villas were built in the functionalist style, with a footprint of 70–90 square metres.
Edsvikens villastad var tänkt som en tjä: The Edsviken garden suburb was intended for white-collar workers, and Arvid Stille drew up the town plan for 350 plots. Sales began in 1923. Many of the original villas are 70–90 square metres and built in the functionalist 'funkis' style.
Edsängens gravfält, ett par hundra meter: A couple of hundred metres away is the Edsängen burial ground, with around 125 Viking Age mounds – one of the largest in Sollentuna. Not far from there is something completely different: Elefanten, the Elephant, a command centre blasted into the rock and built to withstand a nuclear bomb. Closest of all is Rudbecksskolan, one of Sweden's biggest sixth-form schools, with around 2,400 students and a national athletics programme.
Edvard Wavrinsky var bland annat ordföra: Among other roles, Edvard Wavrinsky chaired the Gothenburg shooting society, whose range lay on and just south of today's square. When the name was confirmed in 1954, the city council also highlighted his work for temperance and popular movements.
Efter 1861 blev den gamla sjukhusbyggnad: After 1861 the old hospital building became workers' housing for the Sommelii oil mill. Today it's ordinary owner-occupied flats, and it's listed, so the exterior mustn't be altered.
Efter Gustav III:s död glömdes teatern b: After Gustav III's death the theatre was forgotten. Its stage machinery was dismantled in the 1860s and the auditorium became a hunting hall for King Karl XV. Since 2003–2004, the scenery can once again be changed in a matter of seconds in full view of the audience.
Efter Gustav III:s italienska resa 1783–: After Gustav III's Italian journey of 1783–1784, several places around Brunnsviken were named after Italian models. Albano is one of them, along with its neighbours Frescati, Montebello and Tivoli.
Efter Karl XV:s död 1872 tog kocken Jean: After King Karl XV died in 1872, the chef Jean-François Régis Cadier, founder of the Grand Hôtel, took over the lease. He laid out kitchen gardens at Tivoliudden to supply his hotel with vegetables, and traces of them remain in Tivoliparken.
Efter Philips flyttade energibolag in. 1: After Philips left, energy companies moved in. In 1996 the low-rise section was rebuilt for the TV4 channel, and the facades were painted red at the same time. The old Philips building on Gävlegatan, which the company had outgrown, was designed in 1930 by Sigurd Lewerentz.
Efter Postens omvandling år 2000 krympte: After the Swedish postal service was restructured in 2000, operations shrank, and by 2009 just over 300 people worked here. In April 2015 the last mail trains rolled out of Tomteboda.
Efter andra världskriget etablerade sig: After the Second World War several car companies set up here, among them Volvo, General Motors and Hallgrens Bil. Volvo was one of the first, building a site for offices, sales and servicing in 1955.
Efter andra världskriget fick Albert Bon: After the Second World War, Albert Bonnier wasn't allowed to buy printing presses, so he proposed making a small offset press, the 'Chief 22', under licence. More than 30,000 'Solna Chiefs' were made and sold all over the world. An early one from 1946 is on show in the museum.
Efter andra världskriget rådde svår bost: After the Second World War there was a severe housing shortage, and the building was planned as a youth hotel with lots of small flats for young people moving to Stockholm. The idea was housing 'from the cradle to the grave', with care homes, family flats, studios, a restaurant – and even a garage with a petrol station in the basement.
Efter andra världskriget växte nya föror: After the Second World War, new suburbs sprang up in western Stockholm. This route takes you to Vällingby, planned as an "ABC town" combining work, housing and a centre, and on to Tensta, built during the Million Programme, Sweden's great 1960s–70s housing drive.
Efter att Rondo stängde 1983 byggdes lok: After the Rondo cinema closed in 1983, the premises were converted in 1984. A pharmacy moved into the part facing the square, and the auditorium was given an extra floor with shops and flats.
Efter att Wallenbergs tagit över lät de: After the Wallenbergs took over, in 1895 they had photographer Caroline Gaudard record the interiors – she was much in demand in Gothenburg's wealthy homes. Several of her photographs turned up in 2021 in the archives of AB Papyrus, showing how the villa looked around 1900.
Efter att anläggningen tagits ur bruk 19: After it was taken out of use in 1998, the facility stood completely intact, with all its original fittings, until 2017. In 2010 the idea of giving it listed-building status was raised.
Efter att driften lagts ned blev tornet: Once the mill had closed, the tower became a storehouse, and in the 1950s the Kvarnen pharmacy had a laboratory here. Artists' studios followed, and in 1992–1994 eight owner-occupied flats were built on eight floors.
Efter att floden tog träbron 1724 byggde: After the flood swept away the wooden bridge in 1724, Carlberg built a new one of a different design. It needed strengthening as early as 1731, and a stone arch bridge was completed in 1822.
Efter att kommunen bildades 1971 använde: After the municipality was formed in 1971, it used the Härryda Cross, made up of the initials HK. When it tried to register this as a coat of arms in 1977, the application was rejected because the symbol couldn't be described in heraldic terms. A logo featuring an aeroplane followed instead.
Efter att skulpturen satts upp 1958 förs: After the sculpture was put up in 1958, a professor of medicine tried through an intermediary to get Grate to give it arms and legs. The row prompted Axel Hirsch to donate Nils Möllerberg's calmer sculpture Mor och barn – Mother and Child – as consolation for the protesting teachers.
Efter att tornet tagits ur bruk i slutet: After it was taken out of use in the late 1960s, the tower served as a radio mast for the city's communications radio and the National Police Board. Since 2008 it has held 74 fan-shaped student flats, with a shared roof terrace on the eleventh floor.

Efter branden 1893 fick bryggeriet en mo: After the fire of 1893, the brewery was rebuilt as a modern plant, and around 1900 it was Sweden's largest, with 350 employees and a quarter of the capital's beer. The façade facing Riddarfjärden contains 1.2 million bricks.
Efter branden 2008 krävde många kulturar: After the fire in 2008, many cultural figures signed a petition demanding permanent planning permission for the building, among them the writer Kristina Lugn, the singer Joakim Thåström and the musician Dror Feiler. The new Cyklopen opened in 2013.
Efter branden lät Oscar Ekman 1872–73 by: After the fire, in 1872–73, Oscar Ekman had a new summer house built in stone to a design by Axel Kumlien. Above the estate, on Korpberget, a two-storey lookout tower known as Blå Tornet, the Blue Tower, was built in the late 19th century.
Efter den första flottbron kom en ny bro: After the first pontoon bridge came a new bridge, opened on 5 June 1929 after a difficult build. Today's bridge was built alongside it to the east – a steel girder bridge on nine concrete piers, with a clearance of just 1.6 metres.
Efter dieseltiden tillverkades bergborra: After the diesel era, rock drills and compressors were made here, and in the early 1960s Atlas Copco employed about 2,100 people in Sickla. In 1992 production moved to Örebro.
Efter en brand 1819 byggdes de tre Sörgå: After a fire in 1819, the three Sörgårdar farms were rebuilt. When the land was redistributed in 1824, the surveyor managed to draw the plots so that none of the newly built farms had to move, and in 1826 the village was judged too new to be broken up.
Efter en domstolsprövning sänktes höjden: After a court ruling, Gasklockan was scaled down to 90 metres and around 300 flats. The city terminated the land agreement in 2019, and the dispute concerns, among other things, who should pay for cleaning up tar and oil left from the gasworks era.
Efter en stor ombyggnad 1922 rymde Resta: After a major rebuild in 1922, the Restauranten had several dining rooms, a banqueting hall, a wedding room, a 200-seat cinema and its own bowling alley. The cinema also hosted theatre, dances and concerts.
Efter ett medborgarförslag 2011 flyttade: Following a suggestion from a resident in 2011, a millstone was moved to Gymnasievägen below Kvarnberget, where it has been on display since 2013. It's made of sandstone, about 1.25 metres across, with grooves that carried the flour out towards the edge.
Efter ett medborgarförslag 2011 rengjord: Following a suggestion from a local resident in 2011, one of the millstones was cleaned up and, in the summer of 2013, moved to Gymnasievägen below Kvarnberget hill. The sandstone millstone is about 1.25 metres across, with grooves that channelled the flour out towards the edge.

Following a suggestion from a resident in 2011, a millstone was cleaned up and moved in summer 2013 to Gymnasievägen below Kvarnberget. It's sandstone, about 1.25 metres across, with grooves that channelled the flour out to the edge. Two more stones are set into the pavement by Kvarnbergsgården.
Efter flera bränder är dagens kyrka den: After a series of fires, today's church is the fourth to stand here. Designed by Carl Wilhelm Carlberg in a Neoclassical style, it has been a cathedral since 1665, when Gothenburg became the seat of a bishop.
Efter folkparkstiden revs alla anläggnin: Once its days as a people's park were over, all the attractions were torn down, and Krokäng has been an ordinary park for strolling ever since, covering about 7.5 hectares. It has an unusually rich stand of hazel and old oaks.
Efter folkskolan kunde Spångaelever gå v: After elementary school, Spånga pupils could move on to the trade school, which trained engine fitters and mechanics. Places were limited, and the engines built there were used in races at Solvalla.
Efter föräldrarnas död ärvde Branting en: When his parents died, Hjalmar Branting inherited a considerable fortune – and ran through it in a few years on parties and generous loans. He was also sentenced several times to prison and fines, for offences including blasphemy and breaching press laws.
Efter häktestiden har Bysis varit epidem: After its years as a jail, Bysis has served as an isolation hospital, a disinfection station, a printing works and a handicrafts venue. From the late 1960s the Stockholm Chess Federation was based here, and in 1970 the Museum of the Painting Trade moved in.
Efter hökarna bodde Karin Christoffersdo: After the grocers, Karin Christoffersdotter lived here until her death, and in her day the place was called Krögareholmen, 'Innkeeper's Island'. Perhaps she ran an inn – or it may simply be a slip of the district judge's clerk's pen.
Efter istiden låg hela Järfälla under et: After the Ice Age, the whole of Järfälla lay beneath a sea about 100 metres deep. Around 5200 BC the first hilltop broke the surface – and that was Hummelmoraberget.
After the Ice Age, the whole of Järfälla lay beneath a sea about 100 metres deep. Around 5200 BC the first hilltop broke the surface – what is now Hummelmoraberget.
After the Ice Age, the whole of Järfälla lay beneath a sea about 100 metres deep. Around 5200 BC the first hilltop poked up out of the water – today's Hummelmoraberget.

Efter konkursen revs alla nöjesanläggnin: After the bankruptcy all the amusements were torn down, and ever since, Krokäng has been an ordinary park for strolling. It's notable for an unusually rich stand of hazel and old oaks.
Efter landstinget blev huset vanligt kon: After the county council moved out, the building became an ordinary office block. Following a sale and renovation in 2017–2018, it’s now a hotel, Hotel Gio, with the restaurant Mama Gio on the ground floor. Both names pay tribute to Gio Ponti.
Efter lång strid beslutades 2015 att väg: After a long battle, it was decided in 2015 that the wall should be protected and become the centrepiece of a new park. But in 2020 it was found to be in such poor condition that it risked collapsing, and it was demolished in December 2021.
Efter mordet på Gustav III stannade bygg: After Gustav III was assassinated, building work in the park stopped – except on this very tower. One theory is that Duke Karl, Grand Master of the Swedish Order of Freemasons, wanted to use it for Masonic rites. The King's brother-in-law had already built a similar brick tower on his Louisenlund estate in 1784.
Efter många år med ungdomsverksamhet sto: After many years as a youth centre, the building stood empty in 2008 and was renovated. Today it’s privately owned, and the plot, once 10,100 square metres, has been divided into four.
Efter nedläggningen 1983 fanns idéer om: After the cinema closed in 1983, there were ideas about saving the premises for public use, but nothing came of them. In the 1984 conversion, the pharmacy moved into the entrance section facing the square, and the auditorium became shops and flats.
Efter nedläggningen sålde man möbler i s: After the cinema closed, furniture was sold in the auditorium, and later it housed a Systembolaget, the state off-licence. Today it's a corner shop. Only the doorway surround and the copper-clad canopy recall the cinema, once one of three in Aspudden.
Efter några ekonomiskt tuffa år utsågs L: After a few tough years financially, Lingström was named Chef of the Year in 1985. The first Michelin star came in 1992 and the second in 2000. In 2002 the restaurant opened a classic casual offshoot across Sollentunavägen: Edsbacka Bistro.
Efter raset flyttades 100 000 kubikmeter: After the landslide, 100,000 cubic metres of clay were moved and a 108-metre-long berm of blasted rock was anchored to the bedrock. The Tuve landslide made Sweden far more aware of the risk of landslides, and today municipalities can't grant planning permission until the ground has been judged safe.
Efter sedimenteringsdammen rinner vattne: After the sedimentation pond, the water flows over a stretch of grass that takes up some of the nitrogen in summer. Last comes a biological pond. Measurements from 2000–2003 showed that the ponds remove a very large share of the pollutants before the water reaches Albysjön lake.
Efter sitt fälttåg 1790 ville Gustav III: After his campaign of 1790, Gustav III wanted to raise a monument to himself at the top of the hill, roughly where Storkyrkan, Stockholm Cathedral, stands – and the church could happily be torn down. A new theatre was planned by the water. The only part that happened was the King's statue at Skeppsbron.
Efter slutet av 1800-talet har husen i s: Since the late 1800s the buildings have stayed much as they were. The farm is still private land owned by the Wedberg family, so visitors can't go beyond the gate. By the entrance, a modern single-storey timber house has been built that blends into its surroundings.
Eftersom Långsjön är övergödd pumpar Sto: Because Långsjön suffers from over-fertilisation, Stockholm Vatten pumps 30 litres of clean drinking water into the lake every second. Motorboats have been banned since 1993.
Eftersom ingen bor i kontorsområdet stan: Since nobody lives in the office district, trains used to stop calling here after about half past ten at night, and at weekends only in the middle of the day. Since August 2011 every train stops here.
Egen bio i förorten: A suburb with its own cinema
Egen kraftstation och bigård: Its own power station and apiary
Egendomen Älvsborgs Kungsladugård omfatt: The Älvsborgs Kungsladugård estate, a royal farm, covered what are now the districts of Majorna and Kungsladugård. The street was named in 1918 and runs for about 1,350 metres from Mariaplan to Högsboleden.
Egentligen syftar namnet Tibble kyrka ba: Strictly speaking, the name Tibble kyrka refers only to the big worship space on the building's fourth floor. The same cube-shaped building also houses a restaurant, a preschool, a youth centre and a chapel. It was designed by Göran Kjessler and Gudrun Steenberg.

Strictly speaking, the name Tibble Church refers only to the large church hall on the building's fourth floor. The rest of the building houses a restaurant, a preschool, a youth centre, a chapel and hobby rooms, among other things.
Eget samhälle i nästan 40 år: Its own town for almost 40 years
Egnahemsföreningen tvekade mellan Stocks: The home-ownership association couldn't decide between Stocksund and Storängen. Interest in both was so great that the association split in two, and Stocksund became, in a sense, Storängen's sister suburb.
Einar Forseths glasmålningar blandar kri: Einar Forseth's stained glass mixes Christian symbols with scenes from everyday life, including skiers, nurses and building workers – the images were even criticised for being too 'ordinary'. The four windows are called Foundation, Sowing, Growth and Harvest.
Ekebyhovs slott användes som inspelnings: Ekebyhov Castle was a filming location for Mirakel, SVT's 2020 Christmas advent series. On weekdays the castle hosts courses and conferences, and at weekends weddings and parties.
Ekebyhovseken har störst volym, ca 84 ku: The Ekebyhov oak has the greatest volume, about 84 cubic metres, while the Rumskulla oak is the thickest, with a girth of about 13 metres. Prince Eugen's oak is the largest broadleaf tree in the City of Stockholm.
Ekebyhovseken, även kallad Ekeröjätten,: The Ekebyhov Oak, also known as the Ekerö Giant, has a volume of about 84 cubic metres, a girth of 10.5 metres and a height of 17 metres. Its crown is damaged, so it was probably much taller once. Standing alone in a field, it has been able to grow without competition.
Ekebyhovskyrkan, en bit härifrån, är mer: Ekebyhovskyrkan, Ekebyhov Church, a little way from here, is more than just a church. It's part of a church centre that houses the parish office for every parish in the Ekerö pastorate, and it even has its own full-time preschool. A little further on is Tappström, a narrow strait about one and a half kilometres long and only just over three metres deep, which separates the islands of Lovön and Ekerön.
Ekebysjön är tre meter djup och ligger b: Ekebysjön is three metres deep and lies only six metres above sea level. The nature reserve around the lake covers some 42 hectares and has been protected since 2008.
Eken fick sitt namn efter småbruket Hags: The oak took its name from the smallholding Hagsta, which was here from 1923. It was Huddinge's only named oak, and there was also a bus stop here called Eken, the Oak. It was removed in 2012.
The oak took its name from the smallholding Hagsta, which was here from 1923. The bus stop beside it was named after the tree and was simply called Eken, the Oak, until it was removed in 2012.
Eken fick sitt namn för att kungliga eki: The oak got its name because royal carriages turned round here on their outings on Djurgården – and the well-to-do townsfolk did the same. The oak was also the turning point for the very first May Day march, at the end of the 19th century.
Eken som fick en hållplats: The oak that got its own bus stop
Eken som minns gården: The oak that remembers the farm
EkenCenter byggdes 1990 och hade ett 25-: EkenCenter was built in 1990 and had some 25 shops. In its final years, competition made the units hard to let. After it was demolished in 2013, a new retail building went up in its place.
Ekensberg har fått sitt namn efter värds: Ekensberg takes its name from the Ekensberg inn, built in the early 1700s and still standing at Gröndalsvägen 184. Between 1926 and 1934, Ekensberg was the name for most of what's now called Gröndal. The headland lies between Mörtviken bay and the Essingesundet channel.
Ekensbergs värdshus är en gammal sjökrog: Ekensbergs värdshus is an old waterside inn from the mid-18th century that later became the office of the Ekensberg shipyard. The yard closed in 1972, and the building has since been converted into homes and is listed.
Ekerö centrum byggdes i etapper 1983–199: Ekerö centrum was built in stages between 1983 and 1991 and houses everything from a cobbler to the police and a church. The municipal council meets in Mälarökyrkan.
Ekerö's town centre was built in stages between 1983 and 1991. The municipal council holds its meetings in Mälarö Church.
Ekerö centrum, en bit härifrån vid Tapps: Ekerö centrum, a little way from here at Tappström, is easy to spot thanks to its navigation marker, more than twenty metres tall. The area was designed by Ralph Erskine, who lived on the island of Lovön himself, and his vision was to create a little town on Lake Mälaren. Of all his projects, Erskine was proudest of this one, saying it worked as a complete community. From Tappström, commuter boat 89 runs all the way to Stadshuskajen, the City Hall quay in Stockholm.
Ekerö är främst en bostadsort, och den s: Ekerö is mainly a place to live, and most commuters head into Stockholm. Until 1990, the village of Träkvista, not far from here, was the centre of the municipality. That year Ekerö centrum, designed by the architect Ralph Erskine, opened and took over the role. Träkvista torg still has a supermarket, a pizzeria and a restaurant, though.
Ekerö, inte att förväxla med åländska Ec: Ekerö – not to be confused with Eckerö in Åland – lies on the island of Ekerön in eastern Lake Mälaren and is the main town of Ekerö municipality. Ekerö centrum was designed by the renowned architect Ralph Erskine and opened in 1990; before that, Träkvista was the heart of the town. The biggest employer here is the municipality itself.

Ekerö – not to be confused with Eckerö in Åland – is the main town of Ekerö municipality. It's mainly a place to live, and most people commute into Stockholm. Ekerö centrum at Tappström was designed by Ralph Erskine, and its hallmark is a dot more than twenty metres up, standing over the shops like a navigation marker. In the past, though, the heart of the town was Träkvista.
Ekhagens lägenheter från 1930-talet hade: The 1930s flats at Ekhagen had small kitchens but did have fridges, which was unusual back then. Many had a maid's room, and a numbered board in the kitchen showed the maid which room her employers were ringing from.
Ekhagens strandbad har en cirka 50 meter: Ekhagen's beach has about 50 metres of sand with no jetty, a lawn for sunbathing, and woods and rocks all around. There are no toilets, changing rooms or kiosk. Families come during the day, students in the evening.
Ekholmshöjden ligger 30 meter högre än S: Ekholmshöjden sits 30 metres higher than the centre of Skärholmen. After many breakdowns, the decision was taken to build a new inclined lift that will be more reliable and better able to cope with severe weather. It's due to be finished in 2026.
Ekholmshöjden ligger 30 meter högre än c: Ekholmshöjden sits 30 metres higher than the town centre, and people used to get up through a pedestrian tunnel and a lift inside the rock. Residents found it unpleasant and proposed a funicular themselves. The 63-metre line opened in 2001 and carries around 30 people in about a minute.
Eklanda har ett rikt näringsliv inriktat: Eklanda has a thriving business community focused on motor vehicles, mainly cars, with many well-known brands.
Eklanda har ett rikt näringsliv med inri: Eklanda has a thriving business community built around vehicles, mainly cars, with plenty of well-known brands. It's also home to the football club Solängens BK, with 800 members and 20 teams.
Eklanda är en ung stadsdel med gamla röt: Eklanda is a young district with old roots. For a long time there was just a small cluster of older buildings here, but from 1993 houses began springing up, and now there are about 700. The Änggårdsbergen nature reserve is right next door, making the area a playground for the many families with children who live here.
Eklanda är stadsdelen där barnfamiljerna: Eklanda is a district that families with children have made their own. Since building started in 1993, around 700 homes have sprung up, with about 3,100 residents, right next to the Änggårdsbergen nature reserve. A short way from here, in Åby, is Åbytravet, Sweden's second-largest trotting track.
Eklandagatan, en cirka 1 400 meter lång: Eklandagatan, a street some 1,400 metres long with a long climb up towards Johanneberg, has been given its own song. Hästpojken sing its praises in the track Eklandagatan on their 2008 album Caligula.
Eklidens skola består av nio hus. Sex av: Ekliden school is made up of nine buildings. Six of them are joined by a glass corridor running through the school, while the music rooms and the conference centre are reached from outside.
Ektorpet i parken var fiskarstuga i slut: Ektorpet, in the park, was a fisherman's cottage in the late 18th century and is now a summer café. In the shop you can buy the Waldemarsudde pot, designed by Prince Eugen in 1915.
Eldstad vid ytterväggen: A hearth by the outer wall
Elefanterna föddes i Paris: The elephants were born in Paris
Elektraparken har fått sitt namn efter E: Elektraparken takes its name from Elektraverken, which made electrical measuring instruments nearby from 1917. Between 1915 and 1944 the site was home to Södra folkparken, a 'people's park' for open-air entertainment. In 1939 the building magnate Olle Engkvist built a lavish villa for himself and his wife Signhild on Västberga allé, but Villa Engkvist was knocked down as early as 1967–68 to make room for an industrial building.
Elektricitet fanns inte förrän på 1920-t: There was no electricity until the 1920s – the residents' association lit the roads with paraffin-powered lamps. The developer promised good spring water, but the wells ran dry in hot, dry summers.
Elektriska plogar och gödselakvedukt: Electric ploughs and a manure aqueduct
Elementens kamp: Elementens kamp – “The Battle of the Elements”
Elementens kamp invigdes på svenska flag: Elementens kamp ('The Battle of the Elements') was unveiled on Swedish Flag Day in 1930. At the handover, the speaker assured the audience that the people of Olskroken shouldn't see the figures as any kind of depiction of life in their neighbourhood.
Eleverna på Åby Travgymnasium går Naturb: Students at Åby Travgymnasium take the natural resources programme, specialising in animals with a focus on trotting or riding. As well as a B trainer's licence, they can also get licences to drive and to ride in races.
Eleverna på Öckerö seglande gymnasieskol: Students at Öckerö's sailing upper secondary school spend around two months of the school year aboard the training ship T/S Gunilla. Voyages take them to the North Sea, the Atlantic, the Mediterranean and the Caribbean, and every year they cross the Atlantic in both directions.
Elfvinggården har fått sitt namn efter s: Elfvinggården is named after the sisters Ingeborg and Gunborg Elfving, two unmarried working women in Stockholm. The housing foundation is first mentioned in Gunborg's will of December 1918.
Ellesbo Nordgård var under 1700-talet bo: In the 18th century Ellesbo Nordgård was home to the commandant of Bohus Fortress. Carl Wilhelm Carlberg, the architect behind Ellesbo, had designed Gunnebo House a few years earlier.
Elva bergsprängare på gården: Eleven rock blasters on the farm
Elva invånare på fel sida: Eleven residents on the wrong side
Elvira Kjellberg stod på torget i alla v: Elvira Kjellberg stood on the square in all weathers from 1888 to 1928. When she was interviewed on her retirement, she was selling pears for 75 öre a litre. Down in the Vallgraven moat, potatoes were sold straight from moored boats, and fishermen landed salted herring and dried ling.
En \"stabbe\" är en virkesstapel i en br: A 'stabbe' is a stack of timber in a lumber yard. The square was finished in 1954 and named in honour of the Säfveåns AB sawmill. Other squares nearby are Trätorget (Timber Square) from 1953 and Spåntorget (Shingle Square).
En 150 meter lång trädallé leder fram ti: A 150-metre avenue of trees leads up to Bäckebol farm. To the north-west of the house is a terraced park, and to the east a large orchard.

A 150-metre tree-lined avenue leads up to the house. To the north-west lies a terraced park, and to the east a large orchard. South of the garden, on land that once belonged to the estate, you'll now find allotments.
En Bernadotte i industriområdet: A Bernadotte on the industrial estate
En Picasso mitt i parken: A Picasso in the middle of the park
En alldeles egen laxstam: A salmon strain all its own
En allé leder från landeriet upp till Kv: An avenue of trees leads from the old country estate up to Kvibergsvägen. The garden is bounded by the Säveån river to the south and the Kvibergsbäcken stream to the east.
En annan tolkning är att Svingeln var et: Another theory is that Svingeln was an outwork of Gullberg fortress, the forerunner of Skansen Lejonet. But this outwork appears only on a map from 1682 and is missing from every other map of the time, so the idea is considered doubtful.
En ark strandad på berget: An ark stranded on the hill
En arkitekttävling 1960 vanns av Michael: Michael Granit won an architectural competition in 1960, but his design was rejected and the commission went to Hans Borgström and Bengt Lindroos instead. The buildings were meant to have brick façades but were partly built from concrete panels, since industrial production brought better loan terms at the time.
En arkitekttävling 1967 gav ett storskal: A 1967 architecture competition produced a large-scale design that would have meant major demolition along Stockholmsvägen. Only the town hall was built. In 1994 architect Lolle Lundqvist said a shopping centre on the island ought to be 'small-scale and include housing'.
En av Lilla Stampans ägare var kommissar: One of Lilla Stampan's owners was Lyder Bartels Adlersköld, a commissioner at the Board of Trade. He is said to have given his name to the Adlern block, where the mill stood.
En av Stockholms äldsta trästugor: One of Stockholm's oldest timber houses
En av Sveriges första golfbanor: One of Sweden’s first golf courses
En av Sveriges nordligaste bokskogar: One of Sweden's northernmost beech woods
En av Sveriges största samfälligheter: One of Sweden's largest joint properties
En av Sveriges äldsta musikskolor: One of Sweden’s oldest music schools
En av de första delarna som blev klara v: One of the first parts to be finished was the “Hvalmuseet”, the whale museum with its whale skeletons on display, which opened in 1908 – eight years before the whole museum was inaugurated. In 1993 it gained Cosmonova, Sweden's only dome-shaped IMAX cinema.
En av de första funkisparkerna: One of the first functionalist parks
En av de mindre runstenarna, U 50 i röd: One of the smaller rune stones, U 50 in red sandstone, bears an inscription that may continue the one on its neighbour, U 49. It reads: Johan the warlike and Ragnvor, in memory of her husband Holmsten.
En av de sista banmästarna i Bergfana va: One of the last track masters at Bergfana was Hilding Hafström. The family had greenhouses north of the railway and bred grey partridges and ducks south of it. The Hafströms are said to have been the first in Sweden to breed mountain hares.
En av gårdens byggnader, en gammal arbet: One of the farm buildings, an old workers' house, is known as Grytan – the Pot. The name comes from its three chimneys, which together look like an upturned cooking pot.
En av sjöns tre badplatser kallas Täbysi: One of the lake's three bathing spots is called Täbysidan, the Täby side, and can only be reached from Skarpäng in Täby – yet officially it's in Sollentuna. Eleven Sollentuna residents also live here who can only reach the rest of their municipality by travelling through Danderyd and Täby.
En av tre stadsvassar: One of three city reed beds
En avdelning i AGA:s bergfabrik kallades: One department in AGA's underground factory was nicknamed ‘finbageriet’ – the fine bakery – because the staff wore white coats and caps. Delicate optical instruments were made there in an ultra-clean environment, including gyroscopes known as ‘pigs’.
En avdelning i berget kallades finbageri: One department inside the rock was known as the 'fine bakery', because the staff wore white coats and caps. Delicate optical instruments were made there in an extremely clean environment, including gyros nicknamed 'pigs'.
En avdelning inne i berget kallades \"fi: One department deep inside the rock was nicknamed the ‘fine bakery’ because the staff wore white coats and caps. Delicate instruments were made there in extremely clean conditions – gyroscopes nicknamed ‘pigs’, for example, and instruments for the S-tank.
En avdelning kallades ”finbageriet”, eft: One department was nicknamed 'the fine bakery' because its staff wore white coats and caps. Sensitive instruments were built there in an ultra-clean environment – gyroscopes, for example, which were known as 'pigs'.
En backe byggd av rivningsmassor: A slope built from demolition rubble
En barockorgel från USA: A baroque organ from the USA
En biograf blev början på en hel butiksk: A cinema was the start of an entire chain of shops. Saga, on Sofiagatan, showed films from 1942 to 1964. When Bengt Johansson bought the closed cinema, he opened a grocery there – Saga hemköp, the first of the Sagabutikerna shops. Right next door was Härlanda prison, in use from 1907 to 1997. Its walls are still standing as a listed building, and since 2011 the area has been called Härlanda park.
En biograf som liknar en kyrka: A cinema that looks like a church
En bit Lundby mitt på Hisingen: A slice of Lundby in the middle of Hisingen
En bit Mölndal mitt i skogen: A piece of Mölndal in the middle of the forest
En bit av nationalparken: A piece of the national park
En bit bort breder Ryssbergen ut sig, en: A little way off are the Ryssbergen hills, around 30 hectares of pine forest on bare rock, rising to 60 metres above sea level. Down below, in Ryssviken, is Marinstaden, a neighbourhood in an old harbour where people live right on the water. In the other direction is Birka, one of Nacka's oldest residential areas, where the first houses were built for factory workers in the 1880s.
En bit bort går Kongahällavägen, Hisinge: Not far off runs Kongahällavägen, the oldest country road on Hisingen, stretching about 23 kilometres from Torslanda to Eriksdal, south of Kungälv's fortress. Until 1970 it was called Kungälvsvägen. The new name uses the old spelling of the royal estate of Kungahälla, which lay roughly where Ragnhildsholmen is, by the Nordre älv river.
En bit bort ligger Angereds Centrum, knu: Not far away is Angereds Centrum, the local hub, with around sixty shops and restaurants and the end of the line for three tram routes. The decision to build it was taken unanimously by the municipal executive board in 1975. On Angereds torg stands Blå Stället, an arts centre with a library, cinema, theatre and restaurant, and by the terminus is Angered Local Hospital, opened in 2015.
En bit bort ligger Glose, sydväst om Kär: Not far away is Glose, south-west of Kärna in Kungälv municipality. The shore meadows along the Ryskärsfjorden inlet are so rich in birds and plants that Swedish Radio has broadcast its nature programme Naturmorgon live from there. The area is both a nature reserve and a protected Natura 2000 site, and the county authorities rank it among the most valuable natural areas in the region.
En bit bort ligger Kästadalsparken, en l: A little further on is Kästadalsparken, a playground in the Kästa villa area where everything is inspired by fairy tales. Flemingsberg Church was built in 1975–1976 to designs by Gunnar Cedervall and consecrated by Bishop Ingmar Ström in August 1976. Nearby also stood Hagstaeken, the Hagsta oak – Huddinge's largest oak and a protected natural monument – until it was felled in December 2025.
En bit bort ligger Preemraff Göteborg, e: A little way off is Preemraff Göteborg, a refinery that can process around six million tonnes of crude oil a year. Most of the oil comes from the North Sea and is stored in huge caverns in the rock. Even ULCC-class ships, the biggest tankers in the world at 333 metres long and 60 metres wide, have docked at the crude oil harbour on Hjärtholmen.
En bit bort ligger pingstkyrkan Aspnäsky: A little further on is Aspnäskyrkan, a Pentecostal church whose motto is “Discover faith, share hope, grow deeper in love”. In the same area is Aspnässkolan, which in 1846 became the first school in Järfälla parish to have its own building. It started out in an old roadside inn, and the original schoolhouse is now used as a shelter at the Ängsjö outdoor centre.
En bit bort svävar Angeredsbron, cirka 5: A little further on, Angeredsbron soars about 50 metres above the ground. This 930-metre bridge spans the E6 motorway, the Göta älv river, the E45 and the railway. Ships have 47 metres of clearance beneath it, and the spans between its piers are around 130 metres long. At one end the road runs straight into the Gårdsten tunnel, built in 1978 – 235 metres long, with three traffic lanes and a path for walkers and cyclists.

A little way off, the Angered Bridge soars over the E6, the Göta älv river, the E45 and the railway, about 50 metres high and 930 metres long. Ships have 47 metres of clearance beneath it, and the spans between its piers are about 130 metres long. The bridge leads straight into the Gårdsten Tunnel, built in 1978 and a couple of hundred metres long, with three traffic lanes and a footpath and cycle path.
En bit bort, på Göta älvs östra strand,: Not far off, on the eastern bank of the Göta älv river, lies Agnesberg. Travellers have been stopping there for centuries – it was a coaching inn long before the railway station arrived in 1880. After that, industry moved in, including a paint maker and a flour-milling company. Across the river is Kärra, which goes by Hisings Kärra in postal addresses.
En bit från annexet står Grytan, en gamm: Not far from the annexe stands Grytan, an old workers' house. It takes its name, 'the pot', from its three chimneys, which are said to look like an upturned cooking pot.
En bit härifrån breder Gunnestorps mosse: Not far from here lies Gunnestorps mosse, a bog where bulrushes, water lilies, cranberries and sundews grow. East of the bog, down towards Tuvevägen, runs a strip of meadow and broadleaf woodland. And on the northern edge of the bog are the ruins of Mosstorpet, now part of the Fruktträdgården playground.
En bit härifrån breder Kvibergs kyrkogår: Not far from here is Kviberg cemetery. At 130 hectares, it's the largest cemetery in Sweden and the second largest in northern Europe by area. It has over 24,000 graves, with room for 30,000 coffins and 50,000 urns. Gamlestadsvägen, which runs right past, has had its name since 1883.
En bit härifrån breder Trångsundsskogens: Not far from here, the Trångsundsskogen nature reserve stretches along the western shore of Lake Drevviken, from the swimming spot at Mörtviken to just north of Trångsund manor. The reserve was created in 2006 and covers 53 hectares, ten of them water – though the manor and its immediate grounds aren't part of it. Mörtviks gård, a farm, also stands at Mörtviken.
En bit härifrån breder naturreservatet V: Nearby lies the Välen nature reserve, a wetland at the far end of Askimsviken bay. Shaggy Highland cattle have grazed its shore meadows since 1992, and the reserve contains two ancient sites from the Bronze Age. In the other direction is Opaltorget, the end of the line for the Tynnered tram.
En bit härifrån breder villaområdet Nora: Not far from here lies the villa neighbourhood of Nora, about ten kilometres north of Stockholm. This used to be farmland, but in 1926 the fields of Nora gård began to be divided up into villa plots. In the same area is the lake Nora träsk, which drains into the Åkerström-Norrström coastal catchment.
En bit härifrån byggs tunnelbanestatione: Not far from here, the new Barkarbystaden metro station is under construction, right in the middle of the urban development of the same name. In the other direction is Järfälla Church, where in 1728 Olof Celsius wrote about a runestone outside the porch door. He described it as lost and worn away – and sure enough, nobody has seen it since. Further off is Kyrkbyn, the church village, which used to be called Järfälla gård.
En bit härifrån börjar Eklanda, en stads: A short way from here is Eklanda, a district in western Mölndal on the edge of the Änggårdsbergen nature reserve. Apart from a small core of older buildings, it wasn't developed until 1993, and today around 3,100 people live here, many of them families with children. The plan is for new housing on the farmland to the east to join Eklanda up with the village of Fässberg.
En bit härifrån börjar Görvälns naturres: A little way from here is the start of the Görväln nature reserve, which runs for almost eight kilometres along the unspoilt shore of Lake Mälaren, from Hässelby to Kallhäll. Inside it is Baset, an old croft that has been privately owned since 2021. But a legal right of way means the path down to the swimming spot has to stay open to everyone – so a dip in Mälaren is still free for all.
En bit härifrån börjar Pixbo, ett bostad: A short way from here begins Pixbo, a residential area on the southern side of Lake Rådasjön. Pixbo is very hilly, because it's built on and around a height called Björnåsen. It lies in Härryda municipality – apart from a handful of properties that belong to Mölndal – and has its own postal town.
En bit härifrån börjar Rågsveds friområd: Not far from here begins the Rågsved open space, also known as Kräppladalen: just over 100 hectares of countryside with some dramatic terrain – hills, valleys and steep slopes. In the middle of it lies the Snösätra storage area, which since 2014 has become a hub for graffiti and street art, with façades and walls painted with the owners' blessing. Nature and spray cans, side by side.
En bit härifrån börjar naturreservatet J: Not far from here the Jonsereds strömmar nature reserve begins, following the Säveån river valley from the bridge at Kåhög to Lake Aspen. It's mixed broadleaf woodland with a rich variety of fungi, including the red-listed smoky finger fungus. Keep an eye out for grey wagtails, kingfishers and dippers – birds that love running water.
En bit härifrån börjar naturreservatet Ä: Just along from here begins the Älta mosse–Strålsjön nature reserve, set up in 1995 and covering 52 hectares. Together with the Strålsjön–Erstavik reserve it forms a large green area for walks and outdoor life, with little Lake Strålsjön at its heart. The lake's water is dark because it drains in from Älta mosse, a peaty bog, and it's home to pike, perch and roach.
En bit härifrån finns ett unikt minne fr: Not far from here is a unique relic of the Second World War. Käppalaställningen is an anti-aircraft position with several foxholes and three gun emplacements. It was restored and reopened in 1994 as a protected monument to Stockholm's air defences – the only one of its kind in Sweden.
En bit härifrån gick förr den numera ned: The now-closed Djursholm railway ran a short way from here, and from 1924 Valevägen had its own stop, Bragevägen, with a kiosk selling sweets and newspapers on its narrow platform. It closed in 1976. Until the 1920s, the train ran through open fields here. Not far away, at Hildingavägen 26, is the Laurin Villa, designed in 1910 by the architect Karl Güettler.
En bit härifrån går Bullegummans gata, m: Not far from here runs Bullegummans gata, the Bun Lady's Street, and it comes with a sweet story. In the 1930s, a Mrs Liljegren lived here who baked such good buns that the children on their way to Påvelundsskolan school just couldn't resist them. So she cut a hatch in the wall of her house and sold buns through it, and the locals came to know her as Bullegumman, the Bun Lady. The house still stands in its original state, and the hatch was still there as recently as 2011.
En bit härifrån går Marieholmsbron, en b: Not far from here is Marieholmsbron, a bridge carrying trains, pedestrians and cyclists from Gamlestaden over the Säveån and Göta älv rivers to Tingstad on Hisingen. The section over the Göta älv is a swing bridge that pivots to let boats through. It's part of the Bohusbanan railway and links Gothenburg's harbour railway to the rest of the rail network.
En bit härifrån gömmer sig något unikt:: A short way from here is something unique: Hammarkullen, the only fully underground tram stop in Sweden. It lies 25 metres below ground and was modelled on Stockholm's metro stations, because in the 1970s there were plans to run a metro out to Angered. The platforms are built for 120-metre trains, but only 70 metres of them are used today.
En bit härifrån höll Sollentunamässan ti: Not far from here stood Sollentunamässan, the Sollentuna exhibition centre, which opened in 1973. With just over 17,000 square metres of exhibition space, it was Sweden's third-largest trade fair venue until it closed in 2008 and Kistamässan took over. Demolition began on 24 May 2017, and homes are now going up where the exhibition halls once stood.
En bit härifrån korsar Gamlestadsbron Sä: Not far from here, Gamlestadsbron, the Gamlestaden bridge, crosses the Säveån river – and there's been a bridge on this spot for more than 500 years. When Nya Lödöse was founded in 1473, traffic was heavy, as the main road to Norway passed this way. In the summer of 1723 the city architect Johan Eberhard Carlberg was given permission to build a brand-new wooden bridge, but by January 1724 it had been swept away by a fierce flood carrying timber.
En bit härifrån ligger Akalla, en stadsd: Not far from here is Akalla, a district on the Järvafältet plain, built between 1972 and 1977 at the same time as its neighbours Husby and Kista. Running through it is Sibeliusgången, a 900-metre walkway named after the Finnish composer Jean Sibelius. Along the way you'll pass bubbling fountains by the artist Bertil Johnson, put up in 1976 – among them the Akalla fountain in a little square.
En bit härifrån ligger Angereds sporthal: A short way from here, by Angered Centrum, is the Angered sports hall, with room for 400 people.
