Enligt Botvidslegenden hette den äldsta: According to the legend of St Botvid, the oldest church in Salem was called Säby Church. It stood on the shore of Lake Bornsjön, where Salem Church stands today.
Enligt Daniel Höglander valdes namnet de: According to Daniel Höglander, the name was chosen partly so it wouldn't give away anything about the cooking. The cuisine is described as a reaction against the New Nordic trend for seasonal, locally sourced ingredients.
Enligt Erikskrönikan stod en stor sjödra: According to the Chronicle of Erik, a great sea battle was fought here in 1309. King Håkon of Norway had been driven into Kalvsund by a storm, and Duke Erik, son of King Magnus Ladulås, attacked in haste with whatever ships he could muster. Seven enemy vessels were captured.
Enligt Erikskrönikan utkämpades 1309 ett: According to the Chronicle of Erik, a great sea battle was fought in Kalvsund in 1309. King Håkan of Norway had been forced to shelter from a storm, and Duke Erik launched a hasty attack, capturing seven of the enemy's ships.
Enligt Jan Wallander bodde Per Albin Han: According to Jan Wallander, Per Albin Hansson and Sigfrid Hansson lived with their families off the same stairwell in the 1920s. The artist Einar Jolin painted in a top-floor flat, and a cousin became tutor to Egypt's Crown Prince Farouk.
Enligt Mitt i har fem av sju svenska USA: According to the local paper Mitt i, five of the seven Swedish US number ones were recorded here, including Blue Swede's Hooked on a Feeling. Ulf Lundell made his debut album, Vargmåne, here too. The studio is still going: in 2025, strings were recorded here for Taylor Swift's The Life of a Showgirl.
Enligt Trafikverket ska ytterligare ett: According to the Swedish Transport Administration, another tunnel tube is to be built through the cliff at Lindö, as part of the improvements around the Förbifart Stockholm bypass.
Enligt arkitekterna på C.F. Møller har t: According to the architects at C.F. Møller, the tower's shape was inspired by the sharp cliffs that rise out of Lake Mälaren. The facades are clad in terrazzo, an artificial stone made from crushed stone and white cement.
Enligt en gammal skröna skulle Gustav II: An old story has it that Gustav III gave Annelund to his favourite, Elis Schröderheim, but it isn’t true. The name most likely comes from the wholesale merchant Eric Giers, who named the farm after his wife, Anna Maria.
Enligt en gammal teori lät Sankt Sigfrid: An old theory holds that St Sigfrid had the first Christian church built here in the 11th century. The legend may contain a grain of truth: during a later restoration, remains of a wooden church were found and dated to exactly that century.
Enligt en gravyr i hallen skrev Esaias T: An engraving in the hall claims that Esaias Tegnér wrote parts of his epic Frithiof's Saga here. It's not true – he wrote nothing at Råda. The estate did, however, receive a visit in 1795 from the English writer Mary Wollstonecraft.
Enligt en legend tappade drottning Krist: Legend has it that Queen Christina’s horse lost a silver shoe here as her coronation procession passed by in 1650. The story is highly unlikely, since Silverdal isn’t on the road between Ulriksdal and Stockholm. What’s more, the croft was originally called Skogsdal.
Enligt en muntlig tradition ska smedjan: Local lore has it that the smithy belonged to Älvsborg Castle, but that has never been proven. What is certain is that it's marked as Smedia on a map from 1783.
Enligt en sägen byggdes stenmuren runt S: Legend has it that the stone wall around Stengärdet was built by Russian prisoners of war in the 1700s. No one knows for sure when it went up, and some of the stones even bear the marks of modern rock drills.
Enligt en teori lät Sankt Sigfrid bygga: One theory has it that Saint Sigfrid had Örgryte's first Christian church built here in the 11th century. The legend may hold a grain of truth: during a restoration, the remains of a wooden church dated to the 1000s were found. The stone church from the 1200s probably doubled as a stronghold.
Enligt en tradition kan Slaget vid Bränn: According to one tradition, the Battle of Brännkyrka in 1518 may have been fought here. Legend has it that a Danish cannon was dug up from one of the marshes around the Magelungsdiket or Kräppladiket ditches.
Enligt en tradition kan slaget vid Bränn: According to one tradition, the Battle of Brännkyrka in 1518 may have been fought here. Legend has it that a Danish cannon was once dug up from the marshes around the Magelungsdiket or Kräppladiket ditches.
Enligt en tradition planerades mordet på: According to tradition, the assassination of King Gustav III was planned at the manor over a Christmas dinner in 1791. Carl Fredrik Ehrensvärd, whose father owned Hallunda, admitted his involvement and was sentenced to exile for life.
Enligt en tradition väntade en ung kvinn: According to one tradition, a young woman stood here one evening waiting for her betrothed, but during a storm she vanished into the lake along with the rock, the trees and the ground beneath her. Another theory is that the name refers to an ancient stone labyrinth known as a jungfrudans, or "maiden's dance". A map from as early as 1754 records the spot as Jungfru Salen.
Enligt ett förslag från 2017 skulle tvil: Under a 2017 proposal, the twin towers would have been 243 and 183 metres tall, with a sky bar, restaurant and visitor centre at the top. Of the nearly 1,200 planned homes, more than 95 per cent would have been one- or two-room flats.
Enligt folkräkningen 1910 bodde lagerbit: According to the 1910 census, stockroom assistant Karl Fritiof Leonard Hagman Svensson lived here with his wife Gerda and their two children. The family were probably the first to live at Valdorshem.
Enligt gamla beskrivningar var tullen in: According to old descriptions, the toll gate was no pleasant spot: muddy roads, shabby wooden shacks and trading booths. To make matters worse, the gallows hill and the cholera cemetery were nearby.
Enligt idén om självförsörjande förorter: In line with the idea of self-sufficient suburbs, Gubbängen was to have every service – a cinema included. The City cinema on Gubbängstorget opened in April 1953.
Enligt legenden bröt en källa fram 1129,: Legend has it that a spring burst forth in 1129, as St Botvid's remains were carried in procession from Salem Church to the forerunner of Botkyrka Church. Botvid's spring is artesian: the water wells up under its own pressure, at 5–10 litres a second.
Enligt legenden satte bärarna ner Botvid: Legend has it that in 1129, as the bearers set down St Botvid's remains for a rest on the way to Botkyrka, a spring burst forth. The spring here today, however, can't be the same one as in the legend.
Enligt legenden skulle Sankt Botvids kva: Legend has it that in 1129 the remains of Saint Botvid were to be carried in procession to a new church. When the bearers stopped to rest, a spring welled up. This particular spring, though, can't be the one from the legend.
Enligt legenden tappade drottning Kristi: Legend has it that Queen Christina's horse lost a silver shoe here as her coronation procession passed in 1650. The story is highly unlikely, though, since Silverdal doesn't lie on the road between Ulriksdal and Stockholm – and the croft was originally called Skogsdal anyway.

Enligt legenden tvingades fiskaren Jakob: Legend has it that a fisherman called Jakob was forced to pilot a warship but escaped, swimming via Fotö and Hönö to Öckerö, where he hid under a rocky ledge. He threw his cap into the water, and his pursuers assumed he had drowned. The spot is still called Jakobs bratt, "Jakob's cliff".
Enligt legenden växte helgonet Sankt Bot: Legend has it that Saint Botvid grew up at Hammarby gård, a short way from here by Prästviken bay on Lake Aspen – and Botkyrka is named after him. In the Middle Ages the farm became a rectory, and the present main house from 1804 was the church's rectory right up until 1997. The farm is even mentioned in the runic inscription on the famous Botkyrka monument by the church.

Legend has it that St Botvid grew up at Hammarby farm, a short way from here on Prästviken bay in Lake Aspen – and it's after him that Botkyrka is named. In the Middle Ages the farm became a rectory, and the present main house, from 1804, served as the church's rectory right up until 1997. The farm is even mentioned in the runic inscription on the famous Botkyrka monument; the original is in the Swedish History Museum, while a copy stands by the church.
Enligt planerna skulle utbyggnaden ta 12: The development was supposed to take 12 years but ended up taking 18. Along the way it was built more densely, so instead of the planned 12,000 residents there were 16,300.
Enligt runorna blev Olev sviken på Finnv: According to the runes, Olev was betrayed in Finnveden. The Swedish National Heritage Board takes this to mean he was killed in an ambush or a trap rather than in a fair fight. His brothers inherited Nora but lived at Älgesta, further north in Uppland.
Enligt stadsplanen skulle villorna i Lär: Under the town plan, the villas in Lärkan were to be single-family homes, but the rule was often dodged. Staaff's house had rooms to let, with their own WC and shower, on the upper floors. Only 21 of the 51 plots were built with true villas for a single household.
Enligt svenska källor misslyckades det f: According to Swedish sources, the first attack at dawn failed because the Danes had been warned by a sentry at Långbro. As they fled, the heavy cavalry got stuck in the marshes. The claim that Gustav Vasa carried the main banner in the battle is now disputed.
Enligt sägnen flydde sagokungen Erik Väd: Legend has it that the mythical King Erik Weatherhat fled on horseback down the steep cliffs of Kungshatt. His horse could swim and he escaped, but his hat was left behind on the rock. Erik was said to control the winds by turning his hat.
Enligt tidskriften Studio sjöng Joey Tem: According to the magazine Studio, Joey Tempest recorded the vocals for Europe’s ‘The Final Countdown’ at Soundtrade. At the time the studio was working with the record label Alpha Records.
Enligt traditionen fick krogen Pungpinan: Tradition has it that the Pungpinan inn got its name from guests squeezing (pina) their purses (pung) to pay for their brännvin, Swedish aquavit. It was also known as Skarpnecks krog or Krogen i kröken, 'the inn on the bend'. The inn is first mentioned in 1670, and the building was demolished in 1876.
Enligt traditionen ska Förö ha skänkts t: Tradition has it that Förö was given to Donsö, but there's no evidence to back that up. Lilla Förö has several tomtningar, the remains of simple seasonal huts, and together the two islands cover 54 hectares.
Enligt traditionen var det en man från L: Tradition has it that a man from Livonia called Mickel lived in the hillside cottage Mickelsberg. The cottage stood right up against a rock face. It's gone now, but the name lives on in Mickelsbergsvägen.
Enligt traditionen var det här som greve: Tradition has it that this is where Count Claes Horn, Jacob Anckarström, Carl Fredrik Pechlin and Adolph Ribbing plotted the murder of Gustav III in 1792. That's why the house is also called Mördarslottet, the Murderers' Castle.
Enligt traditionen visade Gustav Vasa pr: Tradition has it that Gustav Vasa proved his courage at the Battle of Vädla in 1517, right where the bridge’s northern abutment stands today.
Enskede kyrka ritades av Carl Bergsten o: Enskede church was designed by Carl Bergsten and consecrated on 21 November 1915 by Archbishop Nathan Söderblom. Instead of an altarpiece it has a tall window with a stained-glass Ascension of Christ from 1929.
Enskede skolas huvudbyggnad kallades \"V: The main building of Enskede School was known as 'the White School' for its pale colour. When it opened in 1915 it had a swimming pool in the basement and an open-air classroom on the top floor for pupils with lung disease.
Enskedefältets skola kallades även \"Vit: Enskedefältet School was also known as 'the White School' because of its pale façade. Hedqvist's competition entry was lightly modernist, but the finished building leaned more towards the heavy architecture of the 1920s. The ground floor originally had both a swimming pool and bathtubs.
Enskedestationen gjorde om växelström ti: The Enskede substation converted alternating current to direct current. It was to supply not just the new suburb but also the newly built Enskede slaughterhouse. Above the entrance is Stockholm's coat of arms, showing Saint Erik.
Eric Grate fick idén redan på 1920-talet: Eric Grate got the idea back in the 1920s in Paris, where Miss Violetta, the woman without arms or legs, put herself on show for money at funfairs. He worked on the subject from 1930, first as a terracotta relief.
Eric Grate skapade skulpturen Våren 1944: Eric Grate made the sculpture Våren (Spring) in 1944. Charles Felix Lindberg's donation fund bought it together with his statue Sommaren (Summer) and had it placed on the square.
Eric Grates park fick sitt namn 1993. Fö: Eric Grate's park got its name in 1993. Besides Oberon and Sparvguden, the Sparrow God, there's a third bronze by Grate here: Nike de Sant Andria from 1968.
Erik Dahlbergh tecknade Rissne gård på 1: Erik Dahlbergh drew Rissne farm in the 1660s: a four-storey manor house with stepped gables. In 1811 the top two floors were removed because of rot. Since 1983 the farm has been a listed building.
Erik Josephson återanvände gamla delar i: Erik Josephson reused old salvaged parts in his villa. The entrance door on Valhallavägen was carved in the 1700s, and the carriage gate on Baldersgatan comes from the Piehl house on Drottninggatan, with carved helmets and double axes in the Empire style.
Eriksberg var ett av Göteborgs stora var: Eriksberg was one of Gothenburg's great shipyards. The huge gantry crane that still towers over the site is a reminder of those days, and it has become a landmark for the whole riverside.
Eriksbergs Mekaniska Verkstad bildades 1: Eriksbergs Mekaniska Verkstad was founded in 1850 and became a limited company in 1876. During the shipyard crisis the state took it over, and the last ship left the yard in 1979.
Eriksbergskranen kunde lyfta 450 ton och: The Eriksberg crane could lift 450 tonnes and was used to build ships of up to 500,000 tonnes. It's the only crane of its kind left in Sweden: the Uddevalla crane was scrapped in 1986, and the Kockums crane in Malmö was sold to Hyundai in 2002 for one dollar.
Eriksbo byggdes 1968–1971 med omkring 1: Eriksbo was built in 1968–1971, with around 1,100 flats in three-storey slab blocks, on land taken over from Angered municipality in 1967. There are older detached houses here too. The area is made up of three parts: Hjällbogärdet, Västergärdet and Östergärdet.
Eriksbo ligger i Lärjeåns dalgång, med b: Eriksbo sits in the Lärjeån valley, with steep hills north of Gråbovägen. The Västgöta railway once ran through the valley, and its old trackbed is now a cycle path.
Eriksbo ligger i Lärjeåns dalgång, och h: Eriksbo sits in the valley of the Lärjeån river, its houses climbing a slope towards Gråbovägen, with steep hills rising on the north side. The Västgötabanan railway once ran through the valley, and its old embankment is now a cycle path.
Erikskrönikan berättar att stormannen Jo: Erik's Chronicle tells how the nobleman Jon Jarl was killed by Estonians in the 13th century. His wife fled to Hundhammar, gathered men and drove the Estonians up onto the hill Estaskär. There they lost their lives, and she had their ships hauled ashore and burnt.
Ernst Bremer stod modell för huvudperson: Ernst Bremer was the model for the main character in the Swedish feature film Smugglarkungen (The Smuggler King). In summer you can see an exhibition about him on the ground floor of the Bremer villa.
Ernst Bremer, som bodde på ön under spri: Ernst Bremer, who lived on the island during the bootlegging days of the 1920s and 30s, inspired the Swedish feature film Smugglarkungen (The Smuggler King). In summer there's an exhibition about him on the ground floor of the villa.
Erstas byggnader stod kvar ända till 197: Ersta's buildings stood until the 1970s, when they were demolished to make way for the new roads to Östberga. Today only fragments of brick and stone remain, and garden plants gone wild grow on the site.
Eskil Sundahl fyllde sin villa med moder: Eskil Sundahl filled his villa with modern conveniences such as underfloor heating and triple glazing. "To reduce the bother of shovelling snow", he had the area in front of the garage heated with electric cables – effective but expensive, as he himself pointed out. A lift ran between the entrance and the living floor.
Eskil Sundahl gav sin villa golvvärme, t: Eskil Sundahl gave his villa underfloor heating, triple glazing and a lift between the entrance and the living floor. To avoid shovelling snow, he had the forecourt by the garage heated with electric cables – effective but expensive to run, as he himself pointed out.
Essingeleden och brons östra körbana inv: Essingeleden and the bridge's eastern carriageway opened on 21 August 1966, while Sweden still drove on the left. The western half came into use on the very day the country switched to driving on the right: 3 September 1967.
Essingeleden svävar förbi här på Blommen: The Essingeleden motorway sweeps past on the Blommensberg viaduct, spanning the Vinterviken valley and almost skimming the roofs of Blommensberg school. The bridge opened on 21 August 1966. Just a stone's throw away is Stora Fågelsången, an 18th-century farm by the little lake Trekanten, whose garden is now allotments – without the usual cabins. A bit further on stands Sankt Sigfrid's church, a red wooden church moved here from Vasastaden in 1904.
Etoile öppnade 2018 i kvarteret Sländan,: Etoile opened in 2018 in the Sländan block, founded by the chefs Jonas Lagerström, Rakel Wennemo and Danny Falkeman. The cooking is described as experimental, with flavours from all over the world.

Before the metro came, trams on the Ängby line ran past here from 1944, and the station's abstract murals in glazed tiles, made by Rigmor Roxner in 1999, are a nod to the tiled stations of the tram era. Close by is the white-rendered Abrahamsberg church, consecrated on All Saints' Day 1955.

The buildings are well preserved and considered of very high cultural and historical value. The nearby Huvudstaleden road was planned as part of an urban motorway, but only part of it was ever built.

Ett par hundra meter bort ligger Kvarnto: A couple of hundred metres away is Kvarntorpshällen, a rune-carved rock slab discovered in 1943 by the author Jan Fridegård. Its inscription includes the word 'stepsons', which is rare in runic texts. Nearby is the egg-shaped Näsbydal housing estate, with 900 flats ranging from a single room to seven rooms over two floors. Next door, the Grindtorp area sits beside what used to be Täby's racecourse.
Ett par hundra meter bort ligger Tacksäg: A couple of hundred metres away is Tacksägelsekyrkan, the Church of Thanksgiving, also known as Trångsund Church. It was designed by the architect Sture Frölén and consecrated in 1957, as Trångsund was growing into a town. It served as the parish church until 1987, when Mariakyrkan in Skogås took over. Beside the church there's a memorial grove and a small burial ground.
Ett par hundra meter bort står Tibble ky: A couple of hundred metres away stands Tibble Church, which has been called the Cathedral of Roslagen and is both church and administrative centre for Täby parish. The Tibble district is also home to Täby Centrum, and its library holds a Viking Age runestone fragment from Lissby measuring just 47 by 46 centimetres. It was found in 1930 together with a piece that turned out to belong to a different stone.

A couple of hundred metres away is Tibble Church, sometimes called the cathedral of Roslagen, which serves as both a church and the administrative centre of Täby parish. The Tibble district is also home to Täby centrum, and its library holds two fragments of Viking Age runestones found at Lissby in 1930. One of them measures just 47 by 46 centimetres.
Ett par hundra meter härifrån ligger Hög: A couple of hundred metres from here is the Högsbo pegmatite quarry, where feldspar, quartz, mica and beryl were mined from 1945 until the late 1950s. The rock also held rare minerals such as monazite and columbite. Today the quarries are part of the Änggårdsbergen nature reserve, which is also home to the small lake Axlemossen.
Ett par hundra meter härifrån låg Hörnin: A couple of hundred metres from here, by what is now Parkhemsvägen, stood Hörningsnäs gård, a manor and large estate in Huddinge parish. The farm buildings burned down in the 1950s, but the name lives on in the Hörningsnäs housing area. A little further on is Lake Trehörningen, where you may spot bats and protected frogs and toads.

A couple of hundred metres from here, where Parkhemsvägen runs today, stood Hörningsnäs, a manor and sizeable estate in Huddinge parish. In the late 1950s the rural municipality of Huddinge bought the estate and had the house burned down, but the name lives on in the Hörningsnäs housing area. A little further away is Lake Trehörningen, where you might spot bats and protected frogs and toads.
Ett par hundra meter härifrån stod Hagst: A couple of hundred metres from here stood Hagstaeken, a mighty oak in Glömsta. Measured round the trunk, it was the biggest of the ten oaks protected as natural monuments in Huddinge. On the night of 3 December 2025 it was cut down for safety reasons, following a government decision and despite protests. A little further on, the valley of Glömstadalen opens up, an area the municipality values for its cultural heritage.
Ett par hundra meter härifrån står Stens: A couple of hundred metres from here is Stensjökyrkan, one of the two churches in Stensjön parish. A little further on, at the very top of the steep hill on Kvarnbygatan known as Mölndals kråka, the Mölndal Crow, is Mölndal's city museum. Its café serves lunch on weekdays and coffee and cakes at weekends – a well-earned reward after that climb.
Ett par hundra meter sydväst om gamla Ve: A couple of hundred metres south-west of old Veddesta farm is Fruns backe, a burial ground with more than 70 visible graves. The village probably dates back to the early Viking Age. On Kvarnbacken hill are the remains of the farm's windmill.
Ett par kvarter bort ligger Atlantisområ: A couple of blocks away is Atlantis, a 1950s terraced-house village that drew international attention – Olof Palme lived here with his family from 1968 to 1983. Further off, in Beckomberga, stood Beckomberga sjukhus, a psychiatric hospital built in 1930–1932 that stayed open until 1995. Since the mid-2000s its old buildings have been turned into homes.
Ett par minuter bort ligger Filmstaden H: A couple of minutes away is Filmstaden Heron City, Sweden's biggest cinema, with eighteen screens and 4,166 seats in all. It's part of Kungens kurva, which together with Skärholmen Centre draws 30 million visitors a year. Long before the popcorn arrived, this was the site of Sadelmakartorp, the saddler's croft, which dates back to the late 17th century and became a schoolhouse after 1860.
Ett par minuter bort ligger Högdalens sk: A couple of minutes away is Högdalen skatepark, also known as Highvalley Skateworld – a whole concrete world for skaters, with a freestyle area, a children's area, the Mega Ditch and a bowl. At around 5,500 square metres, it's the biggest in Stockholm. Next door is Cyklopen, a cultural centre run entirely by volunteers, and a little further on is Högdalen's town centre, which was modelled on the centre in Vällingby.
Ett par minuter bort ligger Skärisbiogra: A couple of minutes away is Skärisbiografen, a non-profit municipal cinema that opened in 2017 and is run by Kulturhuset Stadsteatern, Stockholm's culture house and city theatre. Its neighbours are the Red Cross folk high school, offering courses with an international and humanitarian focus, and the old Skärholmen upper secondary school from 1974. Underneath it all lie traces of Smista gård, a farm that goes back to the 800s, in the Viking Age.
Ett par minuter bort snurrar Vridande mo: A couple of minutes away, Vridande moment, ‘Torque’, slowly turns. Also known as Skruven, the Screw, Aston Forsberg's steel sculpture has become the emblem of Skärholmen centrum. It won first prize in an ideas competition in 1968. Skärholmen centrum had 15 million visitors in 2013, and together with nearby Kungens kurva, home to the world's second-largest IKEA store, it forms the biggest out-of-town shopping area in the Nordic countries.
Ett par minuter härifrån börjar Ulriksda: A couple of minutes from here, the Ulriksdal nature reserve begins – about 32 hectares between the Brunnsviken and Edsviken bays, protected since 1988. It also includes the ancient graves of the Mellanjärva burial ground. In the palace park stands Villa Beylon, a pink-rendered brick villa from 1803, next to Ulriksdal Palace Theatre, which has been a state-listed building since 1935.
Ett par minuter härifrån ligger Björkäng: A couple of minutes from here is the Björkängen sports ground, with a football pitch and two ice rinks where Huddinge IK play their home hockey games. One of the rinks used to be called Nickehallen, after the club stalwart Bengt 'Nicke' Nilsson. Until 2018 the area belonged to the Stuvsta-Snättringe municipal district, which was then split in two, so that Stuvsta and Snättringe each became a district of their own.
Ett par minuter härifrån står runstenarn: A couple of minutes from here are the Häradsvägen runestones, a pair from the Viking Age. One of them has had quite an adventure: in the 1800s it served as a doorstep in Lindal, then went missing for a while before turning up again in 1938, lying on a burial mound at Skälby gård. The other was given a rather fanciful interpretation by Olof Rudbeck the Elder in his work Atlantica.
Ett par minuter härifrån, längs Hallunda: A couple of minutes away, on the Hallunda heritage trail opposite Slagsta motel, is a rock carving that wasn't discovered until 1971. Nearby is Slagsta gård, a historic manor, and down by Lake Mälaren is Slagstabadet, an EU-designated bathing spot with excellent water quality. One of Slagsta's two brickworks once stood there, and in the woods you can still make out terraces and old house foundations.
Ett par minuters promenad bort ligger Lå: A couple of minutes' walk away is Långsjö farm, on the northern shore of Lake Långsjön. It has two identical main houses, and the reason is a touching one: the businessman Robert Ditzinger built them in 1882, one for each of his two sons. The farm goes back to the 17th century and gave its name to the whole district of Långsjö.
Ett par minuters promenad bort ligger Ty: A couple of minutes' walk away is Tyresövallen, formerly known as Bollmoravallen. It's the home ground of Tyresö FF and the Tyresö Royal Crowns, with room for about 2,700 spectators. Tyresö's ice rink is in the same area, and a little further on is the glass-roofed Tyresö centrum, with the municipal offices and library.
Ett par stenkast bort, i Sundby, ligger: Just a short way off, in Sundby, two rune-carved rock slabs lie side by side: U 80, large and richly decorated, and U 81, which was never finished. Sundby is counted as part of Old Spånga. The name has been known since 1312, although the district itself wasn't created until 1953, on land the City of Stockholm had bought from Spånga in 1949.

Ett stenkast bort ligger Hagsätra centru: A stone's throw away is Hagsätra centrum, the local town centre, which opened in 1960 – the same year the metro arrived. Look out for Barnet med käpphästen, the Child with the Hobby Horse, a copper sculpture by Marie Stenqvist that has become the centre's emblem. A little further on there's an outdoor pool with a funny name: Älvsjöbadet. Despite what it says, it isn't in Älvsjö at all, but right here in Hagsätra. It was built in 1937–1938.
Ett stenkast bort ligger Älta kyrka, int: A stone's throw away is Älta Church, beside Ältavägen. The road was built in 1934 and winds for just over eight kilometres through the open countryside between Älta and Nackanäs. The neighbouring area of Stensö carries a memory of the water: the peninsula was once an island in Lake Ältasjön, and at its tip the Stensö beach invites you in for a swim.
Ett stenkast bort står Vårby gårds kyrka: Close by is Vårby gård church, colourful and full of imagination, and considered one of the first postmodern buildings in Sweden. It was consecrated on 25 May 1975 and sits on a slope looking out over Lake Mälaren, next to a Viking Age burial ground. And just south-west of the church, at Duvberget, the Vårby hoard – a cache of silver treasure – was discovered in 1871.
Ett stenkast härifrån breder Rålambshovs: Just nearby is Rålambshovsparken – Rålis to the locals – named after the old Rålambshov estate. The park was laid out in the 1930s, at around the same time as Västerbron, the Western Bridge, and Lilla Västerbron, the Little Western Bridge, runs straight across it. By the square you'll also find Riksarkivet, the National Archives. Its main building was completed in 1968, when the archives moved here from Gamla Riksarkivet, the Old National Archives, on Riddarholmen.
Ett stenkast härifrån ligger Albykistan,: A stone's throw from here is Albykistan, a reconstructed stone cist – a type of late Stone Age grave that is very rare around Lake Mälaren. Only seven are known in the whole of Stockholm County, and this one has been dated to around 1800 BC. From the Stone Age to the big top: Alby is also home to Subtopia, the base of the contemporary circus company Cirkus Cirkör.
Ett stenkast härifrån ligger Bullegumman: Close by is Bullegummans gata, the Bun Lady's Street, named after Mrs Liljegren, who in the 1930s sold home-baked buns through a hatch in the wall of her house to children on their way to Påvelundsskolan. The house was later used for a while as a reception centre for refugees. It still stands in its original state, and the hatch was still there in 2011.
Ett stenkast härifrån ligger Kristineber: A stone's throw away is Kristineberg Castle, a manor that looks like a castle. It was once a malmgård – a country house on the edge of the city – and still has much of its 18th-century character. The main house has been a private home since the 1930s, while the wings are used by Kristinebergsskolan school. Over by Fredhällsparken park was the Tranan cinema, which showed films from 1933 to 1961.
Ett stenkast härifrån ligger en teater s: A stone's throw from here is a theatre that used to be a barn. Teaterhuset Mölndal has 150 seats and is home to six amateur theatre societies, all under one shared umbrella organisation. These days it's mostly revues and comedies created by young people, and the building even has an English-language theatre group.
Ett stenkast härifrån ligger Ågestaverke: Just a stone's throw away is Ågestaverket, the Ågesta plant – also known as R3 or Adam – which was Sweden's first nuclear power station to supply energy to consumers. Most of its output was district heating for Farsta, which earned it the name ‘the nuclear heating plant’. The reactor ran on heavy water and natural uranium. It closed in 1974, but most of it is still standing and has found a new role as a training ground for Stockholm's fire service.

A stone's throw from here lies the Ågesta plant, also known as R3 or Adam, Sweden's first nuclear power station to supply energy to consumers. It mainly provided district heating for Farsta, which earned it the name 'the atomic heating plant'. The reactor ran on heavy water and natural uranium. Ett stenkast härifrån låg Råsunda fotbol: A stone's throw from here stood Råsunda football stadium. The 1958 World Cup final was played there on 29 June, when Brazil beat Sweden 5–2 in front of almost 50,000 spectators. The stadium closed in 2012, once the new national arena in Arenastaden was finished, and the site has since been turned into homes and offices.
Ett stenkast härifrån står Ängbystenen,: A stone's throw from here, on a small knoll in the middle of the houses, stands Ängbystenen, runestone U 60. It gave its name to Runstensvägen, Runestone Road, and the streets around it also have names linked to runes and the Viking Age. A little further on is Björklunds hage, Bromma's best-preserved burial ground from the early Viking Age, and the Stora Ängby manor, whose main house dates from the very end of the 1600s.
Ett stycke härifrån slingrar sig Bällsta: Not far from here winds the Bällstaån stream, also called Spångaån in its upper reaches. It rises on a hill in Viksjö and goes on quite an adventure: under Spånga it runs through a tunnel about 1.4 kilometres long, and further on it crosses the Solvalla trotting track end to end, right through the green infield.

Europa-rondellen, som fick ge plats åt d: The Europa roundabout, which made way for today's interchange, wasn't particularly old itself. The unusually large roundabout was built in the 1970s – so it was demolished after just a couple of decades.
Exakt 50 år senare publicerade DN en ann: Exactly 50 years later the newspaper DN published another version. According to one of the court chauffeurs, Prince Gustaf Adolf's car tried to overtake the king's, and chauffeur Gösta Ledin said "We'll take him" and put his foot down. Instead of getting past, they ended up in the ditch.

Exactly 50 years later the newspaper DN published another version: the King's car had supposedly been racing Prince Gustaf Adolf's. The King loved speed and was annoyed at being overtaken. “We'll have him,” said the chauffeur, and put his foot down.
Exploateringen började 1910, när auditör: Development began in 1910, when the auditor Clas Östberg bought 30 hectares between the railway station and Edsviken bay. The land was divided into 61 villa plots, and about twenty had been sold by the end of the first year. Roads, water and drains were all put in before the plots went on sale.
FFA gick 2001 upp i Totalförsvarets fors: In 2001 the aeronautical research institute FFA was merged into the Swedish Defence Research Agency, FOI. The wind tunnel work carried on for a while, and in 2008 it was taken over by the consultancy Sjöland & Thyselius, which set up a new company, STARCS, to keep it going.
Fabriken består av tre delar: TA där kar: The plant has three parts: TA, where the bodies are assembled; TB, the paint shop; and TC, where the car gets its final assembly. The first two are largely automated, while most of the work in final assembly is done by hand.
Fabriken brann ner i februari 1858 men b: The factory burned down in February 1858 but was rebuilt, this time with eleven buildings, most of them stone. It had its own gasworks supplying 250 flames, replaced by electricity in 1889.
Fabriken byggde bostäder åt sina arbetar: The factory built homes for its workers from the 1880s, but the earliest houses have since been demolished or burnt down. In the 1940s four narrow apartment blocks went up to designs by Wejke & Ödéen, and they're still standing today.

Fabriken lades ned 1931, och lokalerna h: The factory closed in 1931, after which the premises were let to small businesses. It was demolished in 2001–2002. The area is now called Kvarteret Tändstickan, the Matchstick block, where the ÅF building opened in 2014.

Fabriken stod klar 1932 och bakade först: The factory was finished in 1932 and at first baked nothing but crispbread. Raw ingredients came in at one end of the great hall, and the finished bread was packed at the other. In the early 1970s it was converted into a bakery for ordinary bread.
Fabriken var som störst under första vär: The factory was at its largest during the First World War, with 400 employees. It closed in 1931, and in 1936–1937 the premises were converted and let to small businesses.

Fabriken vid Barnhusviken växte snabbt:: The factory at Barnhusviken grew fast: in 1895 it made some 16,000 cream separators, and around the turn of the century the workforce rose from 345 to 1,300. The site eventually covered three hectares. Today only the office building remains.
Fabriksbyggnaden med sin svängda fasad m: The factory building with its curved street façade is still here. The tall chimney was taken down, and in 1985–1990 the building was converted into the Henriksborg serviced offices.

Fackföreningarna sålde ön eftersom allt: The trade unions sold the island because fewer and fewer members wanted to rent a cabin there. After the sale in 2014 the island changed character, and 52 newly built houses sold for up to eight million kronor each.
Fagersjö började som en del av Södertörn: Fagersjö started life as part of Södertörns villastad, a planned garden suburb. Nearby is Villa Edvardshäll, the very first villa in the Fagersjö area, built in 1903 just north of what was then the brand-new Nynäs railway. Its builder, the machinist Axel Edvard Samuelsson, named the house after himself – and naming your villa after yourself became something of a tradition among Fagersjö's pioneers.
Fagersjö hade en gång en egen station på: Fagersjö once had its own station on the Nynäs line, but it closed in May 1963. Commuter trains started running ten years later and still pass straight through without stopping.
Fagersjö hade en gång en station på Nynä: Fagersjö once had a station on the Nynäs line, but it closed in May 1963. The commuter trains still run past today – they just don’t stop.
Fagersjö ligger utmed sjön Magelungens n: Fagersjö stretches along the northern shore of Lake Magelungen, and it's home to Högdalstoppen – two of Stockholm's highest points, with sweeping views over the south of the city. The street has its own little story too: Villa Lundin, nicknamed ‘the Castle’, was once at Vildandsvägen 14. In the 1930s the Lundin family are said to have owned one of the only two cars in Fagersjö.
Fagersjö var en del av Södertörns villas: Fagersjö was part of Södertörns villastad, a garden suburb laid out by two businessmen in the early 1900s. Business went badly, and in 1912 the City of Stockholm bought up the company's land. Another house named after its owner is Villa Lindhov, built in 1910 for Harald Lind.

Fagersjös landmärke är Högdalsreservoare: Fagersjö's landmark is the Högdalen reservoir, a water tower from 1958 designed by the architect Nils Sterner. The Stockholm City Museum rates it as highly important to the cityscape.

Fagersjöskogen has unusually large trees. The spruces measure over three metres round the trunk, and there are aspens of around two metres – considered rare. Goshawks and black woodpeckers nest in the woods.
Faggens krog är en nästan musealt bevara: Faggens krog is an 18th-century townhouse preserved almost like a museum. Carl Michael Bellman sang about it, and over the years it has been both a tavern and a cloth factory. Just below the music pavilion on Vita bergen stood Ceders Café, where the Ceder family served summer fika – coffee and cake – from the 1910s onwards. The building was later used by the youth club Vitabergsklubben, led by the author Per Anders Fogelström, until arsonists destroyed it in 1969 and 1970.
Falkeneraren Lucas Boogers kom från Holl: The falconer Lucas Boogers came from Holland and rose to become master falconer. He died in 1779, aged 77, and is buried in a burial chapel at Solna church. The chapel is decorated with his initials, LB, around a falcon.

Familjehotellet har fyra höghus och fler: The family hotel has four tower blocks and several low-rise buildings, with 340 flats in all. A 750-metre corridor links everything together, so you can walk to the dining hall without getting your feet wet, whatever the weather.
Familjehotellets hus binds ihop av ett 7: The family hotel's buildings are linked by a 750-metre corridor system. The idea was that residents could reach the dining room and the building's other facilities in any weather without getting their feet wet.
Familjen Hansson drev Lilla Torps trädgå: The Hansson family ran the Lilla Torp market garden for three generations, from 1918 to 2010. The big garden had 220 fruit trees and 300 berry bushes, among other things. Today it's home to the Gothenburg Lawn Tennis Club.
Familjen Jansson bodde i Storgården och: The Jansson family lived at Storgården and farmed the land from the 1790s right up to 1974, when the last harvest was brought in. By then, building work on the new district had already started the year before.

Familjen Larsson flyttade redan 1910 til: As early as 1910 the Larsson family moved to Villa Mullberget on Djurgården, next to Elin's parents' home, Nedre Manilla. Those villas were designed by Östberg too. In 1979 the villa in Storängen was judged to be of irreplaceable cultural and historical value.
Familjen Palmes första radhus låg på Tor: The Palme family's first terraced house was at Tornedalsgatan 18, where they lived from 1956 to 1968. It was here in 1967 that the director Vilgot Sjöman filmed his much-discussed interview with Olof Palme about class society for the film I Am Curious (Yellow).
Familjen Widstrand kallade sitt hem ”Vil: The Widstrand family called their home ‘Villa Skoga’. In the 1960s the Saltsjöbaden road cut off the villa’s path down to the lake.
Familjen använde huvudtrappan i ek med d: The family used the oak main staircase with its double flights, while the servants had to make do with a well-hidden spiral staircase in the west of the house. The English-style open fireplaces have Art Nouveau tiles, probably made at the porcelain factory.
Far och son i samma kyrka: Father and son in the same church
Farsta Centrum var den första platsen i: Farsta Centrum was the first place in Stockholm where you could use a parking disc, launched on 1 December 1993. The building with Martin Olsson's grocery still has its oiled teak façade, crowned with globe lights.
Farsta Centrum was the first place in Stockholm where you could use a parking disc. It made its debut on 1 December 1993.
Farsta brandstation har en särskild styr: Farsta fire station has a special sea rescue unit that carries out rescues and fights fires at sea, flown out by helicopter. The station was renamed from Enskede fire station when Farsta parish was formed in 1957.
Farsta centrum invigdes den 23 oktober 1: Farsta Centre opened on 23 October 1960 and was big for its day, escalators and all. Its car park, with space for 4,000 cars, was one of the largest in Europe, and moving walkways were installed to carry shoppers from their cars to the shops. Farsta was hailed as the southern suburbs' answer to Vällingby.

Farsta gård nämns i ett pergamentsbrev f: Farsta gård is mentioned in a parchment letter from 1384, when it was owned by the powerful nobleman Bo Jonsson Grip. Its lands covered what are now Fagersjö, Hökarängen, Larsboda, Farsta, Farstanäset, Farsta Strand and parts of Sköndal.
Farsta gård och Farstastenen: Farsta gård and the Farsta runestone
Farsta gård vid Magelungen har rötter än: Farsta gård, on the shores of Lake Magelungen, has roots that go all the way back to the 14th century. Today the farm is run by the Farsta association council, an umbrella group of around 70 local clubs and societies. Here you'll also find Farstastenen, the only surviving runestone in Söderort, Stockholm's southern suburbs. It was put back up in 1875 and stands beside the footpath from the farm down to Farstabadet.
Farsta torg är 180 gånger 100 meter och: Farsta torg, the main square, measures 180 by 100 metres, and its convex shape may have been inspired by the Piazza delle Erbe in Verona. In the middle stands the Farsta fountain, sculpted by Per-Erik Willö in 1960.
Farsta torg, ett par minuter härifrån, a: A couple of minutes from here is Farsta torg, laid out like an Italian piazza and opened on 23 October 1960. The long square measures 180 by 100 metres, and its gently curving shape may have been inspired by Piazza delle Erbe in Verona. Most days there's a market selling fruit and flowers. Next door is the former Farsta gymnasium, a secondary school that's now home to the Adolf Fredrik music classes.
Farstastenen minns en bror: The Farsta stone remembers a brother
Farstastenen pryds av en runorm lagd i e: The Farsta Stone is decorated with a rune serpent coiled in a figure of eight, with a braided ring cross in the upper loop. Tore and Sven raised it in memory of their brother Vinut, Helga’s son. In the 19th century the stone lay flat between the farm buildings, and it was raised again in 1875.
Farstastenen är från 1000-talet. Ornamen: The Farsta Stone dates from the 11th century. It’s decorated with a rune serpent coiled in a figure of eight, with a braided ring cross in the upper loop. In the 19th century the stone lay flat between the farm buildings, and it was raised again in 1875.
Farstaviken sträcker sig från Baggensfjä: Farstaviken bay reaches in from Baggensfjärden towards Gustavsberg, the main town of Värmdö municipality, about 20 kilometres east of Stockholm. Here nature itself has redrawn the map: as the land has slowly risen since the Ice Age, the islands of Farstalandet and Ormingelandet have joined together.
