Around 1970 every one of the fifteen houses and farms was torn down except one, which still stands just east of Frölunda Kulturhus, the cultural centre.

Frölunda torg stands on the old lands of Ekebäck village, with farms nicknamed "Nilses", "Sme'ns" and "Kalles" – and even a fox farm. The village was broken up in the land reform of the 1800s. Of its fifteen houses, all but one were pulled down around 1970; the survivor stands east of the cultural centre.
Frölundaborg invigdes 12 september 1967: Frölundaborg opened on 12 September 1967 with a sensation: Västra Frölunda IF beat the Swedish national ice hockey team 4–3. The arena holds just over 6,000 spectators and is still home to Frölunda HC. Next to it runs Friidrottens väg, the Athletics Way. It used to be called Viljo Nousiainens Gångväg, after the coach who led Patrik Sjöberg, Stefan Holm and Christian Olsson to great things at Slottsskogsvallen stadium.
Frölundaborg rymmer 6 044 åskådare, och: Frölundaborg holds 6,044 spectators, 3,614 of them standing. It’s Frölunda HC’s training arena, but the ice hockey team also plays here when Scandinavium is booked and in the Champions Hockey League. The name comes from the neighbouring residential area of Frölundaborg.
Frölundaborg tar 6 044 åskådare, varav 3: Frölundaborg holds 6,044 spectators, 3,614 of them standing. Besides ice hockey and figure skating, the arena also hosts trade fairs and concerts.
Frösundatoppen var ett stort grustag som: Frösundatoppen was a large gravel pit that was filled in with excavated earth and demolition rubble – including from the Klara district, torn down in the 1960s and 70s. A memorial stone inscribed 'In memory of Klara 1600–1960' was put up here in 2005.
Fullersta bio byggdes 1932–1933 i funkti: Fullersta cinema was built in 1932–1933 in the functionalist style, with the municipality's first co-op shops on the ground floor and the cinema one flight up. The projectionist lived at the very top. The building cost 156,260 kronor.
Fullersta bio byggdes 1932–1933 och är e: Fullersta cinema was built in 1932–1933 and is one of Huddinge's purest functionalist buildings. The ground floor housed the municipality's first co-op shops, with the cinema upstairs and the projectionist living at the very top.
Fullersta gård, några minuter härifrån,: A few minutes from here is Fullersta gård, a former manor that since 2009 has been an art gallery, with a permanent exhibition that includes works by Peter Dahl and Ewert Karlsson – and a café. Even closer is Fullersta bio, where an old cinema and former Konsum co-op shops have been turned into an art gallery and theatre.
Fullt utbyggd ska Arken kombiterminal ku: Once fully built, the Arken intermodal terminal will be able to load and unload 70,000 semi-trailers a year, with ten trains a day. It will have seven tracks – 3,360 metres of rail in all – on a site covering 65,000 square metres.

Furulund är omgivet av skog, som i väste: Furulund is surrounded by forest that stretches about eight kilometres west, all the way to the eastern edge of Gothenburg. You can go angling at Prästtjärnen, and the lake Maderna–Haketjärn is popular with long-distance skaters. Kåsjön has a well-loved beach.
Furulundskyrkan är lite ovanlig: den är: Furulundskyrkan is a bit out of the ordinary: it's shared between EFS, a revival movement within the Church of Sweden, and the parish of Furulund-Öjersjö. Tucked away not far from here is Prästtjärnen, a little lake that, small as it is, is a full 14 metres deep. It sits just over 108 metres above sea level and drains into the Göta älv river basin.
Furåsens kyrka ligger alldeles intill, m: Furåsen Church is right next door, and not far from here is a street with a sweet story behind it. In the 1930s, a Mrs Liljegren lived around here and baked buns that the children walking to Påvelundsskolan school just couldn't resist. She opened a hatch in the wall of her house and sold them through it, and so she became Bullegumman, the Bun Lady. Today the street carries her nickname.
Furåsens kyrka är en vandringskyrka som: Furåsen church is a portable church that first stood in Brunnsbo on Hisingen from 1965. It was moved here and reconsecrated in 1972. It's the first portable church of its kind in Sweden from the Oresjö factories.

Fyra arkitekter som jobbade med att plan: In 1951, four architects working on the plans for Vällingby were looking for somewhere to live. The neighbours down by Lake Mälaren didn't want them, so they built here instead and each moved into a terraced house of their own.

Around the junction you'll find kiosks, hairdressers and restaurants, and at Bellevue market people hunt for bargains among the second-hand stalls. From 1910 to 1914 the ball-bearing giant SKF had its offices at Mariedal, a landeri – one of Gothenburg's old country estates – nearby.
Fyren som bytte ljus: The lighthouse that changed its light
Fyren som flyttade in i sjön: The lighthouse that moved to the lake
Fyrtornets fasader är klädda med skiffer: The façades of the Fyrtornet building are clad in a slate called Otta rust, quarried in Otta in Norway, which gets its sheen from magnetite and sulphur in mica. Gert Wingårdh wanted the façade to echo the colours of autumn leaves and 'the green island of Lidingö in autumn'.

Fältmarskalk Lennart Torstenson fick omr: Field Marshal Lennart Torstenson was given the area by Queen Kristina after the Thirty Years' War. The estate was named after his daughter-in-law Christina Stenbock – not after the queen, as many people think.
Fältsjukhuset skulle först ha byggts vid: The field hospital was originally going to be built at Uppsala-Ärna airfield. The beds were screened off with partitions of building board about two metres high, topped with thick black fabric. The hospital was never used and was dismantled in June 2020.
Fängelset byggdes efter en 1800-talsmode: The prison followed a 19th-century model familiar from San Quentin and Alcatraz, with open galleries between the floors that made it easy to keep watch. The ground plan is cross-shaped, and with 175 cells it was one of the larger prisons in the country.

Färdiga produkter lastas ut i Skarviksha: Finished products are shipped out from Skarvikshamnen, also known as the energy port, by train, lorry and ship. From here they also go to other oil companies – OKQ8's products, for example, are made by Preem.

Still, its pattern resembles another stone, so perhaps the same man carved both. In Törnby there's a runic inscription on a reddish granite boulder set in the ground. A man named Saxe had it carved in memory of his mother – sadly, her name has been lost.

Färjan tar dig rakt över älven tillbaka: The ferry takes you straight across the river back to Stenpiren, where the route ends.

Färjeläget låg först vid Lindholmsgymnas: The ferry terminal was first by Lindholmsgymnasiet school, but in 2003 it moved to a harbour basin a little further east and was renamed Lindholmspiren. From 2015, Gothenburg's first zero-emission electric buses ran from here to Johanneberg Science Park.
Fässberg skrevs 1312 Fästbiärrg. Förlede: Fässberg was written Fästbiärrg in 1312. The first part means a rope or hawser for making a ship fast, and probably refers to a mooring place from the days when the fjord was navigable all the way up here.
Fässbergs Bio på Fiskargatan 4 öppnade i: Fässbergs Bio, at Fiskargatan 4, opened in January 2013. It's run by the municipality and screens films digitally.
Fässbergs Bio öppnade i januari 2013 i d: Fässbergs Bio opened in January 2013 in Fässbergssalen, the converted assembly hall of Fässberg upper secondary school at Fiskargatan 4. It's run by the municipality and screens films digitally.
Fässbergs kyrka ligger strax intill, och: Fässberg Church is right beside us – and between 1922 and 1976 it was actually called Mölndal Church. Fässberg has the largest population of any parish district in both the province and the county. Close by is Fässbergs Bio, a 400-seat cinema in the old secondary school's assembly hall, now converted into an events venue.
Fässbergs kyrka är byggd i nygotisk stil: Fässberg church is built of red brick in the Gothic Revival style, designed by Adrian C. Peterson. The tower and spire rise 52 metres. The church stands on Baazs berg, a hill whose summit was blasted away and replaced with a landscaped park.
Få byggnader har bytt skepnad som Hammar: Few buildings have changed roles quite like Hammarkullen church. It was a parish church in Angered parish until it was deconsecrated in 2011 and became a preschool. Then the building was transformed once again, and today it's Hammarkullen mosque.
Fåfängan, kafé med utsikt: Fåfängan, a café with a view
Fågel Grön och blå framtid: Green Bird and a blue future
Fågelbergskyrkan är byggd av rödbrunt te: Fågelbergskyrkan is built of reddish-brown brick inside and out, with a single-pitched roof. Behind the free-standing altar rises a brick pillar, and the rest of the wall is glazed from floor to ceiling. The church hall seats about ninety people.
Fågelbergskyrkan är byggd i rödbrunt teg: Fågelbergskyrkan is red-brown brick inside and out. It stands on the site of the old vicarage in Rävekärr and was consecrated on 1 December 1984. Behind the altar the wall is glazed from floor to ceiling. By then the parishioners had been campaigning for a parish hall for thirty years.
Fågeldammen fick flytta: The duck pond had to move
Fågellivet i Gallhålan är rikt, med lövs: Gallhålan is rich in birdlife, with woodland species such as the lesser spotted woodpecker, tawny owl, hawfinch and spotted flycatcher. Hazel, guelder rose and alder buckthorn are common among the shrubs.
Fågellivet längs Igelbäcken och i Råstas: Birdlife along the Igelbäcken stream and on Lake Råstasjön is wonderfully rich. Near Hästa farm there’s a man-made frog pond, deer are often spotted, and in the wetlands around Igelbäcken you can see trees that beavers have gnawed and felled.
Fållan var sommarnöje för stadsaktuarien: Fållan was the summer retreat of the city actuary Magnus Zetterman, whose first wife was related to Bellman. The houses stood empty for a few years before being demolished around 1840. Today's villas in Fållan date from the early 1900s.
Fåret är Järfällas symbol och finns i ko: The sheep is Järfälla's symbol and appears on the municipal coat of arms. In the car-free Jakobsberg centre, concrete sheep have been placed to keep traffic out. Next door is Riddarparken, whose designer won the Siena Prize in 1996.
För 2000 år sedan låg Brunnsvikens stran: Two thousand years ago the shoreline of Brunnsviken bay was about ten metres higher than today, and the Fröfjärden inlet linked the Saltsjön bay with Lake Mälaren. Where Järva krog stands today was open water. The burial grounds at Stora Frösunda farm date from the 400s BC.
För 500–600 år sedan var Hustegaholm ski: 500–600 years ago Hustegaholm was separated from the rest of Lidingö, but post-glacial land rise joined it to the island – hence holme, “islet”, in the name. Along the northern shore of Kyrkviken stand two giant oaks, protected as natural monuments since 1969, with trunk girths of 684 and 463 centimetres.
För Abrahamsberg föreskrevs gult tegel o: Abrahamsberg was to be built in yellow brick with extra-thick walls, while its sister district Åkeslund got red brick. According to the City Museum, this is Stockholm's best-preserved area of smalhus – the narrow, three-storey blocks of the 1930s and 40s. The school was designed by Paul Hedqvist, who also designed Bromma gymnasium.
För Västlänkens skull monterades delar a: To make room for the West Link rail tunnel, parts of the terminal's northern end were dismantled in 2020. They'll be put back once the new main entrance to Station Centralen is built. In the meantime, the Åkareplatsen travel centre opened south of the Central Station in 2018.
För att dryga ut inkomsten drev Clara Ka: To make ends meet, Clara Karlsson ran a small laundry at Nytorp. She washed for neighbours, a few families in Stockholm and a hotel, in a ramshackle wash house beside a pond fed by Lake Gömmaren.
För att få en tomt skulle du ha jobbat v: To get a plot you had to have worked for the state railways, SJ, for at least five years and have at least nine years left before retirement. The land was let on a 60-year leasehold, and the houses had to be two storeys with a cellar.
För att inga stödben skulle skymma sikte: So that no supports would block the view, the roof over the main stand was hung on steel cables from two hollow pylons 53 metres high. The design was advanced for its day and drew attention abroad.
För att ta dig ner till perrongen i Hamm: To get down to the platform at Hammarkullen you ride Gothenburg's longest escalators, 24 metres high and 58 metres long. There's also an inclined lift, a kind of funicular.
För att understryka idén om ett energice: To underline the idea of an energy centre, the blocks were named Vattenkraften, Solkraften and Vindkraften – Hydropower, Solar Power and Wind Power – and the streets were given matching names. The vision of energy-efficient buildings was only partly realised, and today it's mostly an ordinary office and industrial area.
För cirka 8 000 år sedan började trakten: Around 8,000 years ago the land around Handen began rising out of the Littorina Sea, the forerunner of the Baltic. The ice sheet left its mark in the form of giant's kettles – deep potholes in the rock – for example in the Kolartorp nature reserve and by Övre Rudasjön.
För omkring 4000 år sedan låg Stora moss: Around 4,000 years ago Stora mossen lay under the sea, and Bromma looked like an archipelago. The bog was then a lake on an island where Nockeby and Äppelviken are today. Along the old shoreline are boulders with cup marks, probably from the Bronze Age.
Förbi Axel Dahlströms Torg med höghuset: Past Axel Dahlströms Torg with its 1956 tower block, and through 1960s Västra Frölunda with its musical street names. Frölunda Torg opened in 1966 as one of Sweden's first big suburban shopping centres.
Förbi Gamlestaden och Kviberg ut till Ko: Past Gamlestaden and Kviberg out to Kortedala, Gothenburg's first suburb, built in the 1950s.
Förbi Järntorget med fontänen som förest: Past Järntorget and its fountain depicting the world's five continents.
Förbi Linnéplatsen och Olivedalsgatan ne: Past Linnéplatsen and down Olivedalsgatan to Järntorget.
Förbi Riddarhuset från 1600-talet vid Ri: Past the 17th-century House of Nobility on Riddarhustorget, where the nobility once gathered.
Förbi Råsta gick en forntida färdväg som: An ancient route ran past Råsta, marked by two runestones. The inscription on the one still standing reads: 'Holmsten and Hosve had the stone raised in memory of Jobjörn, their father, and Gyrid in memory of (him).'
Past City Hall and across Kungsholmen.
Förbi Wieselgrensplatsen med landshövdin: Past Wieselgrensplatsen, a square ringed by landshövdingehus – Gothenburg's distinctive tenements with a stone ground floor and wooden upper storeys.

Före 1860 kallades Ekudden för Lilla Lis: Before 1860, Ekudden was known as Lilla Listudden. Its current name, 'Oak Point', comes from the oak-covered headland on Lake Flaten. From 1748 the croft was rented by the merchant Christian Hebbe, whose trading house stood on Skeppsbron.
Före 1972 stod här en vandringskyrka frå: Before 1972 a travelling church from 1966 stood here. It moved on and became Bjurslättskyrkan. Ingrid Danielsson's three-part tapestry has now moved to Lundby parish hall.
Före Nacka Forum fanns Skvaltan, ett pro: Before Nacka Forum there was Skvaltan, a temporary shopping centre in prefab huts from the late 1960s that lasted twenty years. Work on the new centre began with blasting into the rock in 1986.
Före Stefanskyrkan fanns ett litet träka: Before Stefanskyrkan was built, a small wooden chapel stood on the corner of Frejgatan and Tulegatan, serving the poor of a neighbourhood known as Siberia. When the church was completed in 1904, the chapel was taken apart and moved to Aspudden, where it became Sankt Sigfrid's church. It was declared a listed building in 1993.
Före USA i strålskydd: Ahead of the US on radiation shielding
Före dagens bro fanns en smal träbro frå: Before today's bridge there was a narrow wooden one from 1924, where cars had to take turns in one direction at no more than 20 km/h. It was blown up with dynamite and still lies on the lake bed east of the current bridge. Today's 200-metre concrete bridge opened in 1974.
Före dagens kyrka fanns en så kallad stu: Before today's church there was a 'studio church' made of prefabricated wooden sections, designed by Rolf Bergh. It first stood in Barkarby while Järfälla Church was being restored, then came to Viksjö in 1971. It remained in use right up until the Sunday before the new church was consecrated.
Före dagens kyrka fanns en vandringskyrk: Before today's church there was a portable wooden church built from prefabricated sections. It first stood in Barkarby from 1969 while Järfälla Church was being restored, then in 1971 moved to the stable yard at Viksjö farm, where it was used until June 2005.
Före dagens kyrka fanns här en vandrings: Before today's church there was a travelling church here – a prefabricated building that could be taken apart, moved here from the Tynnered church site in 1975. The wooden bell tower has a carillon you can see from outside.
Före mitten av 1200-talet hörde Tuve soc: Until the mid-1200s Tuve parish belonged to the Hising ship district in Älvsyssel, then part of Norway. In 1462 the name was written Twfua, and it probably refers to a tuva – a tussock – in the shape of a rocky knoll.
Före mitten av 1200-talet ingick Tuve so: Until the mid-13th century, Tuve parish was part of Hising's naval district in Älvsyssel, which then belonged to Norway. In 1462 the name was written Twfua, and it probably refers to a tuva – a hillock or rocky knoll.
Före nuvarande kyrka fanns en vandringsk: Before today's church there was a portable wooden church, assembled from prefabricated sections. It first stood in Barkarby from 1969 while Järfälla church was being restored, then moved in 1971 to the old stable yard at Viksjö gård. It remained in use until 12 June 2005.
Förebilden var Centralbygningen i Köpenh: The model was Centralbygningen in Copenhagen from 1903, Europe's first collective housing block with a shared kitchen. Hemgården ran into financial trouble: the central kitchen closed in 1914 and the building went bankrupt, but it then became one of Sweden's first housing cooperatives.
Föregångaren Nackabro krog hade tidvis d: Its predecessor, Nackabro krog, at times had a bad name as a haunt for rowdies on day trips from Södermalm. In 1837 the inn was banned. The new one ended up on the north side of the strait, on land where the ban on serving drink didn't apply.
Föreningen Stockholm Sub Surfers började: The association Stockholm Sub Surfers started campaigning for a skatepark in 1985. Rålis Skatepark, under Lilla Västerbron bridge, finally opened on 3 November 2010, with several bowls and a large street section.
Föreningen bildades den 13 juni 1918 på: The association was founded on 13 June 1918, out of food shortages and an ‘innate love of the soil’. In spring 1919, 104 plots of 240 square metres were allotted by lottery, and the annual fee was one krona.
Föreståndaren som köpte gården: The matron who bought the estate
Företaget Globe Sömfabrik grundades 1875: Globe Sömfabrik was founded in 1875 as a branch of the English firm United Shoe and Nail. In 1912 the Norwegian company AB O Mustad & Son took over and moved nail-making to Dalsland. After that, Mustad made soap and cosmetics here until the 1960s.
Företaget Tacton knoppades av från SICS: The company Tacton was spun off from SICS, the Swedish Institute of Computer Science, in 1998 after an AI project on expert systems. In summer 2023 an American company bought a majority stake for around 2.7 billion kronor.
Företaget köpte Rudolf Diesels svenska p: The company bought Rudolf Diesel's Swedish patent and built its first workshop here in 1898. A branch line linked the factory to the entire European rail network, and engines could be loaded onto wagons right inside the factory.
Företaget startade 1915 under namnet Ske: The company was founded in 1915 as Skeppsmodeller (Ship Models) at Kyrkogatan 3 in central Gothenburg, with Olof Traung among its founders. Only after buying Kärra farm, along with the small Nyebro barge yard, did it move out here to the river and take the name AB Sverre.
Författaren Agnes von Krusenstjerna vård: The writer Agnes von Krusenstjerna was treated here for nine months in 1918. In her 1926 novel Tonys sista läroår, the heroine ends up at Solna nursing home, called the Emperor's Hotel in the book after its chief physician, Henry Marcus.
Författaren August Blanche var informato: The writer August Blanche worked as a private tutor at Nora gård in the summer of 1827. The stories he heard here found their way into, among other works, Berättelser efter klockaren i Danderyd – Tales from the Danderyd Parish Clerk. The farm's old 18th-century main house is now known as Blanchegården.
Författaren Gösta Langenfelt kallade nam: In 1944 the writer Gösta Langenfelt called the name Alléparken, 'the Avenue Park', a monstrosity – there was neither a park nor an avenue here. It later turned out, though, that an avenue really had led to the croft of Asplund, and a few of its trees are still standing. Next door are the 'English terraced houses', 43 of them, built in 1919–1920. And up on Alviksberget, Elfvinggården went up in 1939–1940: a collective housing block for single, educated women.
Författaren Nelly Sachs lades in på Beck: The writer Nelly Sachs was admitted to Beckomberga psychiatric hospital in 1960. She liked it there, and her stay didn't stop her writing. In 1966 she was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.
Författaren Sigfrid Siwertz var sommargä: The writer Sigfrid Siwertz spent his summers in Huvudsta, and some read his novel Selambs as a roman à clef about the district.
The writer Sigfrid Siwertz spent his summers in Huvudsta. Some read his novel Selambs as a thinly veiled portrait of the area.
Förgården har en oregelbunden form efter: The forecourt has an irregular shape based on the Capitoline Hill in Rome, and the towered wings angle slightly inwards. Above the entrance are the coats of arms of Gustaf Bonde and his wife, Christina Natt och Dag.
Förleden i Sörred tros komma från öknamn: The first part of the name Sörred is thought to come from the nickname Surv, meaning "a negligent fellow, a sloven, a good-for-nothing". The second part comes from the Old Swedish ryd, cleared land. In 1476 the name was written Sorwerith.
Förleden ”sand-” kommer av sanden och gr: The 'Sand-' at the start of the name comes from the sand and gravel of the Stockholm esker as it runs on southwards. There were several gravel pits here, including one on the northern part of what is now Skogskyrkogården cemetery.
Förr bedrevs fattigvård, sjukvård och ma: The building once housed poor relief, healthcare and a canteen, and weddings were held in the Committee Room, decorated with turtle doves. Nordiska Musikgymnasiet, a music school that moved in in 2003, was founded by the pianist Monika Kowalska and takes students from all over Europe.
Förr fanns här en lustträdgård, en kökst: There was once a pleasure garden here, along with a kitchen garden and a melon garden with an orangery. The gardener Anders Lundström ran a market garden from 1834, and in the park north of the farm part of his historic orchard has been restored.
Förr fanns två väntsalar, en för tredje: There used to be two waiting rooms, one for third class and one for first and second, with the staff flat up in the attic. The building was originally clad in red-painted boards, with white decorative surrounds framing the doors and windows.
Förr gick Göta landsväg förbi här. I dag: The old Göta highway once ran past here. Today the former assembly site, where the local court met, lies partly beneath Södertäljevägen (E4/E20), near the Hallunda interchange. The council has marked the spot with a small green space and a granite wall inscribed ‘Svartlösa Tingsplats | Alby Centrum’.
Förr gick Göta landsväg förbi tingsplats: The old Göta landsväg highway used to pass the thing site, where the local assembly met. Today the council has marked the spot with a small green space and a granite wall bearing the words "Svartlösa Tingsplats | Alby Centrum".
Förr gick man mellan Höjden och centrum: People used to get between Höjden and the centre via a 60-metre pedestrian tunnel and a lift inside the rock. In 1996 residents formed a working group and proposed an open-air funicular instead. It opened on 20 June 2001.
Förr gick trafiken på krokiga vägar förb: Traffic once wound along twisting roads past Tuve Church and through the village of Skändla. Once new housing estates were built, that was no longer workable, so Tuvevägen was laid out running more or less straight north. By the Skändla cairn you can still see traces of the old church road.
Förr gick vägen efter kurvorna vidare lä: After the bends, the road used to carry on along the edge of the woods in a narrow avenue to Malmvik. When the tunnel was built, that stretch was moved out onto the field, where there was room for a wider road.
Förr hanterades kol och koks i hamnbassä: The harbour basin once handled coal and coke, and later served as a container yard and salt harbour. Today it's full of private boats. Sannegårdsbron bridge crosses the harbour, with a small bascule section that opens to let sailing boats in and out.
Förr låg Ugglums by här. När järnvägssta: The village of Ugglum once stood here. When the railway station was built in 1917 it was named Sävedalen instead, so it wouldn't be mixed up with Ucklum in Bohuslän. Before then, you had to go to Fräntorp to catch the train to Gothenburg.
Förr rann en öppen bäck från Ekebysjön f: An open stream once ran from Lake Ekebysjön past Danderyd Church and Nora farm out towards Edsviken bay. Today it's mostly piped underground, but an old 18th-century mill building still stands in Kvarnparken, the Mill Park.
Förr reste sig Tyskbagarbergen på platse: This is where the Tyskbagarbergen hills once rose, named after Martin Kammecker, a baker from Mecklenburg who built windmills on his land in the 1600s. One of them stood at the far end of Jungfrugatan. The hills were in the way of traffic, so a passage, Karl XV:s port, was blasted through to let Nybrogatan continue up to Valhallavägen. That's where you'll now find the monumental red-brick home of the Swedish Patent and Registration Office, designed by Ragnar Östberg.
Förr slingrade sig Ekerövägen genom skar: Ekerövägen used to snake through tight, narrow bends right here, between Tillflykten and Lindö lada. In 1994 they blasted straight through the rock instead, creating the 178-metre Lindö tunnel. The result? Fewer accidents and shorter rush-hour queues.
Förr släpptes orenat avloppsvatten ut i: Untreated sewage used to be pumped straight into Riddarfjärden and Lake Mälaren. In 1930 a major report, nicknamed the 'sewage bible', was completed. The city's first treatment plant, Ålstensverket, was finished in 1934 and treated the waste water of about 5,000 people.
Förr tog man sig upp till vallen från Mö: People used to climb up to the ridge from central Mölndal on Lillbörje's long, steep flights of steps. Plans for the new housing area included a 40-metre lift that shortens the walk to Mölndalsbro and the town centre.
Förr var Fridhemsplan en stor spårvägskn: Fridhemsplan was once a major tram hub, serving lines such as the Ängby line. Until 1968 it also had a bus terminal for the buses out to the Lake Mälaren islands. In 2017–2018 the central island was removed and a new square was laid out on the north side of Drottningholmsvägen.
Förr var Hönö en utpräglad jordbruksbygd: Hönö was once a farming island through and through, and until the mid-1800s its houses were clustered in four villages: Hult, Heden, Röd and Gårda. Fishing mattered too – in 1945, 123 fishing boats had Hönö as their home port.
Församlingen bildades 1473 och hette för: The parish was founded in 1473 and was first known as Götaholm parish. From 1474 it was called Nya Lödöse, from 1543 Älvsborg parish, and from 1571 Nylöse once more. War and people moving away brought it to an end around 1624.
Församlingen har en fritidsgård, Koviken: The parish has a holiday centre, Koviken on Lovön, where confirmation and sailing camps are held every summer. The sailing camp is run by Vindens vänner, a sailing club for people with disabilities.
Församlingen köpte 1968 en flyttbar vand: In 1968 the parish bought a portable church, which was set up in Lindalen. In 1973 it was replaced by Bollmora's parish centre in yellow brick, designed by Bo Sahlin. After a fire in 1988 the church interior was restored to its original state.
Församlingen växte ur grupper av troende: The congregation grew out of groups of devout women in Ulvsunda and Nockebyhov in the early 1900s. From 1909 to 1955 they met at Grönvik mission house in Nockeby, until the new church was finished.
Församlingen ägde också mark norr om Als: The parish also owned land north of Alströmergatan, which the housing cooperative HSB bought in the 1920s. In 1928–1929 Scandinavia's largest apartment block went up there, designed by Sven Wallander.
Församlingshuset med kyrksal ritades av: The parish hall with its church hall was designed by Carl Alfred Danielsson-Bååk and opened in 1925. But it wasn't until 1972 that the hall was consecrated as a church, by Bishop Ingmar Ström.
Församlingshuset ritades av Hakon Ahlber: The parish hall was designed by Hakon Ahlberg in 1920s Classicism. Beneath the archway is a fresco by Jurgen Wrangel, "The Battle of Brännkyrka 1519". In the Committee Room, where weddings were held, a frieze of urns, flowers and turtle doves runs round the walls.
Förslaget hette Polstjärnan: The entry called the Pole Star
Först 1937 gjorde bilfabriken skäl för s: It wasn't until 1937, when Gunnar Philipson took over, that the car factory lived up to its name. As AB Svenska Bilfabriken it assembled cars from makers including DKW, Dodge and, later, Mercedes.
Först fanns bara tåget från Älvsjö. År 1: At first there was only the train from Älvsjö. In 1922 the bus operator Olof Strand and the cab owner K. I. Jansson were given permission to run a bus between Midsommarkransen and Långsjö. In 1930 Stockholm Tramways took over the route, which became line 64.
Först försökte man elda upp soporna dire: At first they tried burning the rubbish right in the chute, but when the clouds were low the smoke settled over the streets. The first chutes were square, and rubbish got stuck. The fix – round chutes with small, tight hatches – became Wallander's patent, which he handed over to HSB.
Först hette stationen bara Centralen. Re: At first the station was simply called Centralen. As early as 27 January 1958 a T was added – for tunnelbana, the metro – so that no one would confuse it with Central Station itself.
Först i Sverige med dagvård: Sweden's first day care for patients
Först i Sverige med stadsgas: First in Sweden with town gas
Först i landet med stadsgas: First in Sweden with town gas
Först i världen med saltkilen: A world first with the salt wedge
Först när den ombyggda trafikplatsen inv: It wasn't until the rebuilt interchange opened in 1935 that the name Slussen began to be used for the whole area on Stockholm's official maps. Before that, Slussen – “the Lock” – referred only to the lock itself in Söderström.
Först på 1700-talet, särskilt under Gust: Only in the 18th century, especially under Gustav III, was the public let in. The park became a pleasure ground of the merriest kind, as several of Bellman's songs describe. The Orangery opened in 1772 as the Vauxhall entertainment palace, with concerts and balls.
Först renades vattnet med kemisk fällnin: At first the water was treated by chemical precipitation and rapid filtration. But it smelled and tasted bad, so in 1938 the works was expanded with slow sand filtration. A large main was later laid to the new suburbs of Hässelby, Vällingby, Grimsta and Blackeberg.
Först var den ljusgrön: At first it was light green
Första bygget var tankfartyget Talmud 18: The first ship built here was the tanker Talmud in 1882, and the last was the 6,500-tonne Nordic Link, launched on 11 June 1981 – 75 new vessels in all. The yard also made sluice gates and the spans for the new Lidingö Bridge.
Första fartyget hette Kare: The first ship was called Kare
Första huset på vassen: The first house on the reclaimed marsh
Första hästbytet söderut: The first change of horses heading south
Första konserten på Slottsskogsvallen va: The very first concert at Slottsskogsvallen stadium was given by Per Gessle on 6 August 2003, in front of 22,000 people. In 2008, Kent and Lars Winnerbäck both played here.
Första ljudet och första färgen: The first sound and the first colour
Första motionen om en anläggning i Lundb: The first motion for a pool in Lundby was tabled in 1954. It didn’t open until 1973, cost 15.5 million kronor and replaced the Renström bathhouse. Outside there’s a 50-metre pool.
Första ordern från Västerås: The first order came from Västerås
Första spadtaget för tunnelbanan till Ba: Ground was broken for the metro extension to Barkarby in August 2018, and the line is being extended by around 4 kilometres from Akalla. At Barkarbystaden, 2,800 passengers are expected to get on or off during the busiest morning hour in 2030.

Ground was broken for the metro extension to Barkarby in August 2018. The line is being extended by around four kilometres from Akalla, and the work is expected to be finished in the fourth quarter of 2028.
Första spadtaget togs 1917, under första: The first sod was turned in 1917, during the First World War, to grow potatoes and vegetables. The allotments were first at Åkeshov but had to move when Drottningholmsvägen and the tramway were built, and in 1939–40 they ended up here. Some of the cabins are still the very ones that were moved back then.
Första spadtaget togs 1965, och fram til: Ground was broken in 1965, and by 1970 some 2,600 flats had gone up on what had been rocky hills and farmland. By the time the area was finished in 1969, it already had schools, a church, a library, a youth centre and a shopping centre.
Första spadtaget togs 26 juni 1908. Tank: Ground was broken on 26 June 1908. The idea was that ordinary people should be able to get a house with a garden for the same price as a two-room flat in the inner city, with the city lending 80 per cent.
Första spadtaget togs den 2 februari 197: Ground was broken on 2 February 1976. The square was opened on 26 October 1978 by King Carl XVI Gustaf, who first rode the tram out from central Gothenburg. Back then there were some 40 shops; today there are around 60.
Första spadtaget togs i november 1966, o: Ground was broken in November 1966, and the first residents moved in the following year. They had to shop in temporary huts and walk along muddy paths. A brochure from 1969 warned: "You are moving to a district in the making." At Kämpingebacken 13 there's now a museum flat from that era.
Första storbanken ut ur city: The first big bank to leave the city centre
Första toppen över havet: The first peak above the sea
Första tåget på dubbelspår: The first train on double track
Första uppropsdagen var den 22 augusti 1: The first day of term was 22 August 1929, with 300 to 400 'disciples', as the pupils were called. At the start of the Second World War the military took over more and more of the school, and in 1942 the whole building became barracks.
Första villan hette Stensjöklint: The first villa was called Stensjöklint
Första vågen låg i Brunnsparken: The first weigh house was in Brunnsparken
Första året fanns renar, lapphundar, hön: In the first year there were reindeer, Lapphund dogs, hens, geese, ducks and two goats. Soon exotic animals arrived too, such as a walrus, a rhinoceros and chital deer. In 1901 the brown bear Maja and the polar bear Prinsen came from the Tivoli menagerie.
Första ön ur havet: The first island out of the sea
Försvarslinjen med ett 30-tal befästning: The defensive line of some 30 fortifications between the lakes around Stockholm was nicknamed Korvlinjen, "the Sausage Line", because of its shape on the map. It was paid for by private individuals in the Society for the Fixed Defence of Stockholm, and the fortifications were then donated to the military.
Försvarsunderrättelsedomstolen inrättade: The Defence Intelligence Court was set up on 1 December 2009, replacing the Signals Intelligence Board. The board had been criticised by the Council on Legislation, among others, for not being independent enough from the armed forces.
Förtrollad skog och flygande matta: An enchanted forest and a flying carpet
Förut fick kungligheterna åka omvägen vi: Before, the royals had to take the long way round via Solna and Bällsta to the ferry at Tyska botten. The new road cut the journey from 17 arduous kilometres to 11 comfortable ones. Gustav III dreamed of a perfectly straight sightline to the palace, but the terrain put a stop to that.
Förutom container- och bilfartyg går äve: As well as container ships and car carriers, freight ferries for lorries leave from here too. DFDS Seaways’ passenger ships used to sail from Skandiahamnen, but in the early 2000s they moved closer in, to Norra Frihamnspiren.
Förutom en fast utställning om Lindomemö: Alongside its permanent exhibition on Lindome furniture, the museum has staged plenty of quirky temporary shows – on graffiti, on cleaning and on Barbie dolls, to name a few.
Förutom husets stengrund finns också gru: Besides the house's stone foundation, the footings of a cowshed survive too. The site borders the Igelboda plots, with untouched woodland and wetlands, parts of which are of real conservation value. Ludvig Nordgren, the first of the family here, was born in Norunga in 1858.
Förvaltarbostaden som blev kårhus åt Cha: The steward's house that became the Chalmers students' union building was nicknamed "the flea house" – because the pest-control firm Anticimex had used it before them.
Föräldrarna slog sig ihop med hockeyklub: Local parents joined forces with the hockey clubs IF Demonerna, HK Kometerna and Hisingens VIK, who all dreamed of an indoor rink on Hisingen. Together they formed the Tuve rink association, and in the 1980/1981 season Tuve ishall opened beside the Tuvevallen sports ground. It's still going today.
Föräldrarna som fick en ishall: The parents who got an ice rink built
Föräldrarna som lagade isrinken: Parents who fixed the ice rink
GP-huset byggdes på gammal mark i Gullbe: The GP building, home of the Göteborgs-Posten newspaper, stands on reclaimed land in Gullbergsvassviken bay. For its metre-thick concrete foundations to carry the heavy printing presses, 2,362 piles had to be driven into the bottomless clay. The site was chosen partly because it was close to the railway and the newsprint.
Galenskaparna & After Shave sjunger om W: The comedy troupe Galenskaparna & After Shave sing about Wavrinskys plats in the song Adjö, from their TV series En himla många program.
The gallows appear on a map as early as 1689. The condemned were led here along Götha vägen, now Götgatan, and are said to have been given one last drink at the Källaren Hamburg tavern on the corner of Götgatan and Folkungagatan. From the hill there's a sweeping view over the city.
Galjonen hade 397 platser under den stor: Galjonen had 397 seats beneath the large terrace. The ceiling was deep blue, and the mosaic-patterned curtain was made by the artist K-G Andersson. The auditorium later became a recording studio, and today it's home to Vår Teater.
Galleri Kusten flyttade in 1973 och höll: Galleri Kusten moved in in 1973 and stayed until 2000, when the restaurant Sjömagasinet took over. Since April 2021 the building has been home to the restaurant Ankarsmedjan Social.
Gallhålans naturreservat bildades 1988 o: The Gallhålan nature reserve was created in 1988 and enlarged in 2013 to 96 hectares. As well as oak woodland, it has alder swamps, pine forest on bare rock and a hay meadow, with hazel, guelder rose and alder buckthorn among the shrubs. The reserve lies on the eastern slope of the Tahult drumlin, a long glacial ridge that drops steeply to the little lake Agntjärnen, and it's rich in birdlife.
Galoppbanan gav namn åt Roslagsbanans st: The racecourse gave its name to Galoppfältet station on the Roslagsbanan line, previously called Åkerby. A city park of around 10 hectares is planned in the middle of the new Täby Park, with meadows and natural hillocks from the old racecourse.
Gamla Boråsvägen en bit härifrån var en: Gamla Boråsvägen, the old Borås road just along from here, was once Gothenburg's main route in and out of the city, part of national road 5 from 1945 into the 1950s. Its narrow, steep and winding stretch, known as Kallebäcks lider, was dreaded by motorists and carters alike. Just south of the road, Örgryte IS trains at ÖIS-gården, where one of the pitches has been called Hammarviken Arena since 2013.
Gamla Boråsvägen har mycket gamla anor s: Gamla Boråsvägen has been a road for a very long time, but it wasn't cobbled until the 1930s. Older Gothenburgers sometimes call today's Kallebäcksbacke hill on Route 40 Kallebäcks lider. It was rebuilt as a four-lane motorway in the late 1970s.
Gamla Brommabor uttalade namnet Kasvik,: Old-time Bromma residents pronounced the name 'Kasvik', just like the earliest spelling, Kaswik, from 1409. According to the place-name scholar Jöran Sahlgren, the first part is the word 'kas(e)', a pile of brushwood.
Gamla Danderyds socken var en gång rätt: The old parish of Danderyd was once fairly sparsely populated. In 1905 it had 3,605 inhabitants, spread over an area that now takes in Djursholm, Stocksund, Enebyberg, Mörby and Nora. The parish church, Danderyd Church, is a little way from here beside the E18. And in nearby Rinkeby there was once a fragment of a runestone, U 132, which went missing in the latter half of the 1800s.
Gamla Filmstaden: Gamla Filmstaden, the old film studios
Gamla Huddingevägen kantades från början: Gamla Huddingevägen was originally lined mostly with villas from the early 1900s. Only a few remain today, and the street is dominated by blocks of flats with restaurants and services on the ground floor. Along the street you'll also find the architecturally interesting Leipzighuset.
Gamla Huddingevägen var en gång en del a: Gamla Huddingevägen was once part of the main Huddinge road. But so much through traffic was cutting right through the villa suburb of Örby that in 1971 the road was diverted north of the district. Not far from here is Stockholmsmässan, Sweden's largest exhibition and congress centre, along with the Scandic Talk Hotel, seen as the exhibition centre's signature building.
Gamla Klara vilar i kullen: Old Klara rests in the hill
Gamla Kungälv i trä omger hållplatsen. R: The stop is surrounded by the wooden houses of old Kungälv. The town hall on Gamla torget, the Old Square, has become a symbol of the old town, and several of Kungälv's oldest houses line Västra gatan. The Zetterlöf House was built in 1762, and the Strand House, with its archways, double staircase and cobbled courtyard, was built for a merchant in the early 1800s. Its neighbour is the Thorild House.

All around the stop is old wooden Kungälv. The town hall on Gamla torget, the Old Square, has become a symbol of the old town, and some of its oldest houses line Västra gatan. Zetterlöfska huset dates from 1762, while Strandska huset, with its gateways, double staircase and cobbled courtyard, was built by the merchant David Werming. Thorildska huset has served as both a school and a telegraph station.
Gamla Kvibergs regemente har fått nya li: The old Kviberg regiment has found new lives. The former horse stables now house Kvibergs marknad, a market with 160 stalls full of antiques, curiosities, books and toys. And just north of the barracks rises Prioritet Serneke Arena, the biggest multi-sport complex in the Nordic region, with an indoor ski slope and a 1.2-kilometre ski track.
Gamla Lundbybadet stängde den 26 maj 197: The old Lundbybadet baths closed on 26 May 1973, and the new Lundbybadet – now at Lantmannagatan 5 – opened as early as 14 September that same year. Since 1987 the old building has been part of the city's conservation programme.
Gamla Lundenskolan har källare av granit: The old Lunden school has a granite basement, façades of dark red-brown brick and small-paned windows, with sturdy canopies over the corner entrances. It cost 264,000 kronor and had 34 rooms when it opened.
Gamla Skogsinstitutets byggnad var urspr: The old Forestry Institute building was originally the official residence of the Master of the Royal Hunt, built in 1773. The Forestry Institute, which planted the park's trees, was based here from 1828 to 1916, and since 2011 the building has housed the Israeli embassy.
Gamla Stockholmsvägen, alldeles i närhet: Gamla Stockholmsvägen, the old Stockholm road nearby, links Snättringe and Glömsta. Further along the same road is Nytorp, a former croft from the mid-1600s that now serves coffee – an old crofter's cottage turned café.
Gamla Vanadisbadet från 1938 ritades av: The old Vanadisbadet pool from 1938 was designed by architect Paul Hedqvist in a strict functionalist style, all white-painted concrete, large expanses of glass and blue steel details. The outdoor pool was set into an old quarry, sheltered and facing south-west, and from the sun terrace you look out over Stockholm.
Gamla barnbadet blev nakenbad: The old children's beach became a nudist beach
Gamla bron blev gångbro: The old bridge, now for walkers
Gamla flygfältet kallas det också, Torsl: A short way from here, on the west side of Hisingen and about 15 kilometres from central Gothenburg, is Torslanda airfield, also known as the old airfield. It was laid out in 1923 and served as the city's airport for more than fifty years, until Landvetter took over in 1977. Today Torslanda is best known for Volvo's car plant, the Torslanda Works.
Gamla landsvägen och kapellet: The old highway and the chapel
Gamla riksgränsen genom fabriken: The old national border runs through the factory
Gamla riksgränsen går genom fabriken: The old border runs through the factory
Gamla skolan ritades av Georg A. Nilsson: The old school was designed by Georg A. Nilsson, one of the leading school architects of his day, in austere 1920s classicism with lion-yellow render and a black slate roof. Above the two entrances are limestone medallions showing a star and Aladdin's lamp.
Gamla stans gränder: The narrow lanes of Gamla stan, the Old Town
Gamla stationshuset från 1905 ritades av: The old station building from 1905 was designed by Sigge Cronstedt in a blend of National Romanticism and Swedish Art Nouveau. Today it's a protected building and a private home. The spot is officially called Järnvägsdalen, "Railway Valley".
Gamla trähus i backen: Old wooden houses on the slope
Gamlestaden är just det, den gamla stade: Gamlestaden means just what it says: the old town. Nya Lödöse was founded here in 1473, long before present-day Gothenburg was laid out in 1621. The area later became industrial, and it's where the ball-bearing company SKF grew up.
Gamlestadens fabriker, mat och design: Gamlestadens fabriker – food and design in the old factories
Gamlestads torg ska inte förväxlas med G: Gamlestads torg shouldn’t be confused with Gamlestadstorget, a square from the 1890s that has since been built over. To stop emergency crews being sent to the wrong place by their GPS, the city’s cultural department decided in 2013 that the new square would be called Gamlestads torg.
Gamlestadsvägen, en bit härifrån, är en: Gamlestadsvägen, a little way from here, is a major road running alongside the E45 through Bagaregården, Gamlestaden and Olskroken. It was named in 1883, after the Gamlestaden district. It crosses the Säveån river on the Gamlestaden bridge, passes Nylöse Church and carries on towards the Lärje junction. The Fredrikshamn redoubt, a fortification from 1645, is nearby too.
Gamlestadsvägen, som löper alldeles inti: Gamlestadsvägen, the road running right beside us, was named back in 1883 after the district of Gamlestaden. A little further on is Hospitalskyrkogården, also called Nylöse hospitalskyrkogård, which served as the graveyard for the hospital parish from the late 1500s. Hardly any of the gravestones are left, but a Franciscan friary once stood on the same spot.
Gammal gård i nya skolan: An old farmhouse in the new school
Gammal gård, ny krog: An old farm, a new restaurant
Gammal krog i skogen: An old tavern in the woods
Gammal sluss blev fiskväg: An old lock turned fish pass
Gammelbyn, klar 1930, byggdes till minne: Gammelbyn, completed in 1930, was built to mark the opening of Stockholm City Hall and represented a new way of thinking about care for the elderly: instead of big barrack-like blocks, there were ten two-storey houses set among greenery. Since 1990 they've been owner-occupied flats.
Garnisonskapellet från 1923 ritades av E: The Garrison Chapel, from 1923, was designed by Erik Josephson in the National Romantic style, with echoes of a medieval church. There is still space in the military section, where burials can be requested by the commander of the Life Guards. Today it holds just over 140 graves.

The 1923 garrison chapel was designed by Erik Josephson in the National Romantic style, with echoes of a medieval church. The military section of the cemetery has just over 140 graves, and to this day the commander of the Life Guards can request burial there for anyone with close enough ties to the garrison.
Garvaren Melchior Eichhorn köpte marken: The tanner Melchior Eichhorn bought the land in 1781–1782 and built a summer house that he named after his wife, Maria Westerberg. And so Maria gave her name to the whole district of Mariehäll.
Garvaren Melchior Eichhorn köpte torpet: The tanner Melchior Eichhorn bought the Brostugan croft in 1781 and built a summer house he named after his wife, Maria Elisabeth. The name Mariehäll first appears on a map in 1782. The seller thought the spot was 'almost the most beautiful on the whole Bällsta estate'.
Gasklockan hade formen av en 20-hörning: The gasholder was a 20-sided structure supplied by Maschinenfabrik Augsburg-Nürnberg, with Götaverken as subcontractor. It held 100,000 cubic metres of gas, and you reached the roof by stairs or an external lift.
Gasten huserar i Jakobsdal, en garnfabri: Gasten, Liseberg's haunted house, occupies Jakobsdal, a yarn mill from 1911 that the amusement park bought in 1988. The original idea was an entertainment venue with a 3D cinema, but the plans were reworked into a haunted house themed on Gothenburg's harbour history.
Gastrologik öppnade 2011 i Jacobs krogs: Gastrologik opened in 2011 in the old premises of Jacobs krog and had room for just 25 guests. The restaurant won a Michelin star in 2013 and a second in 2019, and closed in December 2022.
Gasverket gjorde gas av stenkol, och kok: The gasworks made gas from coal, and coke and coal tar turned out to be profitable by-products. Some 250,000 tonnes of tar were produced here, used among other things for asphalt.
Gatan byggdes för spårvagnen: A street built for the tram
Gatan bär en gårdsägares namn: A street named after a farm owner
Gatan fick grundarens namn: A street named after the founder
Gatan fick sitt namn 1888 efter Albert L: The street was named in 1888 after Albert Lindhagen, the man behind Stockholm's grand street plans. Nearby was Gamla Stadshagen, sometimes called Guldgrävarlägret, the Gold Diggers' Camp, where some 350 emergency homes housed working-class families from 1917 to 1965. And Thorildsplan is named after the writer Thomas Thorild, who wrote in his letters about seeking out the parks of Kungsholmen to take in the view.
Gatan fick sitt namn 1890 efter kemisten: The street was named in 1890 after the chemist Jöns Jacob Berzelius. It was extended to its present route, all the way to Götaplatsen, ahead of the 1923 Jubilee Exhibition.
Gatan fick sitt namn 1937 och kantas av: The street was named in 1937 and is lined with the slim apartment blocks typical of the 1930s and 1940s. Many of the buildings around the square are 'green-classified' by Stockholm City Museum, meaning they're of particular cultural and historical value.
Gatan fick sitt namn vid namnrevisionen: The street got its name in the great renaming of 1885, chosen to suit the location and landscape. ‘Lid’ means a slope or hillside, and Högalidsgatan is about a kilometre long.
Gatan fick sitt nuvarande namn 1885. Tid: The street got its present name in 1885. Before that it went by names such as Sörmannelandsgattunn, recorded in 1668, and Södermanlandz Gatan in 1674.
Gatan gick från början ända nerifrån Söd: The street originally ran all the way up from Söder Mälarstrand and was meant as an approach road for traffic. Since 1977 that stretch has been called Münchensbacken and is part of Skinnarviksparken, where motor vehicles aren't allowed.
Gatan har fått namn efter Ersta malmgård: The street is named after Ersta malmgård, a country house probably built in the 1670s by the distiller Oluf Håkansson. In 1862 the property was handed over to the Deaconess Society, which built Ersta chapel and Ersta hospital, among other things.
Gatan har fått sitt namn efter Johannisd: This street is named after Johannisdalsgården, a croft first recorded in the 1770s and pulled down in the 1940s. Much of today's Mälarhöjden grew up on the farm's land, and the Johannisgården block is another reminder of the old property. Just up the road is Fruängen's town centre, which opened in 1962 and has a green listing from the City Museum.
Gatan har fått sitt namn efter markland,: This street is named after the markland, an old unit used to value land. Right next door is the Frölundaborg ice rink, which opened in 1967 with a friendly in which Västra Frölunda IF beat the Swedish national ice hockey team 4–3. And winding past Slottsskogsvallen, the athletics stadium where high jumpers like Patrik Sjöberg and Stefan Holm trained, is Friidrottens väg – the Athletics Way.
Gatan hette Allmänna Gatan 1806 och Allm: The street was called Allmänna Gatan in 1806 and Allmänna Gränd in 1844. 'Allmän' means public, signalling that it was open to everyone. In the 1860s it was widened and lined with lime trees.
Gatan ledde fram till Djurgårdens inhägn: The street led up to the fence around Djurgården. At Djurgårdsvägen there was a gate, Rundstyckesgrinden, where you had to pay to get into the Royal Djurgården park.
Gatan med en egen låt: The street with its own song
Gatan minns adelsätten Eketrä, som från: This street remembers the noble Eketrä family, who from the 18th century until 1875 owned the Västra Pilegården estate, right where the tarmac is today. It's also where the Bräcke tram line branched off to the south. The line closed in 1968 and was taken up in the 1980s, but its embankment is still here, almost untouched – a trace of another age.
Gatan skulle egentligen fortsätta cirka: The street was supposed to continue about 500 metres down to Riddarfjärden bay and Rålambstorget. That stretch was never built, but the lower house numbers had been set aside for it – which is why 45 is the lowest number on Lindhagensgatan.
Gatan som bytte namn: The street that changed its name
Gatan som kallas Hängmattan: The street known as the Hammock
Gatan som minns vargarna: The street that remembers the wolves
Gatan är en bit av en riktig kungsväg. G: This street is part of a genuine royal road. On 19 August 1787 Gustav III opened his own road to Drottningholm Palace, running from the Royal Palace across Bromma, roughly along today's Gustav III:s väg. The surroundings, though, are pure 20th century: Abrahamsberg is one of Stockholm's larger areas of narrow slab blocks, sometimes called 'the yellow town' because of all the yellow brick.
Gatan är uppkallad efter Knut Tengdahl,: The street is named after Knut Tengdahl, born in 1867 in Katarina parish here on Södermalm, and got its name in 1937. The neighbouring Tengdahlsparken was designed by the city's head gardener, Holger Blom.
Gator efter författare och dalabyar: Streets named after writing and Dalarna villages
Gator som löparbanor: Streets laid out like a running track
Gatorna här har väder i blodet. Väderils: The streets round here have weather in their blood. Väderilsgatan, just up the road, was named in 1958 as part of a group of street names on the theme of weather and meteorology – and it's where tram line 2 turns round in a loop. Near the stop is Länsmanstorget, an indoor square built in 1966. Länsmansgården Church held its last service in April 2024 and is set to become an activity centre open to everyone.
Gatorna i Bifrost är uppkallade efter la: The streets of Bifrost are named after farming: Pinnharvsgatan, Rullharvsgatan and Släpharvsgatan (all types of harrow), plus Havrekornsgatan and Vetekornsgatan (oat grain and wheat grain). Fittingly, the whole area is encircled by Lantbruksgatan – Agriculture Street.
Gatorna i Grindtorp heter Grindtorpsväge: Grindtorp's streets are called Grindtorpsvägen, Kometvägen and Meteorvägen – Comet Road and Meteor Road. In the late 1960s around 5,000 people lived in the area.
Gatorna i Hagsätra har fått namn efter o: Hagsätra's streets are named after towns and villages, mostly in the province of Närke – Glanshammarsgatan, Fjugestagränd and Vintrosagatan, for example.
Gatorna och kvarteren här har namn efter: The streets and blocks here are named after footwear, a theme that goes back to the 1940s. In Apelsinlunden, for example, you'll find Sandalmakarbacken (Sandal-maker's Hill), Mockasinvägen (Moccasin Road) and Toffelbacken (Slipper Hill), and blocks called Skohornet (the Shoehorn), Kilklacken (the Wedge Heel) and Klacklappen (the Heel Tip).
Gatorna och kvarteren här har namn från: The streets and blocks here are named after shoemaking. You can walk along Mockasinvägen (Moccasin Road) and Toffelbacken (Slipper Hill), and the blocks include Skohornet (the Shoehorn), Kilklacken (the Wedge Heel) and Klacklappen (the Heel Tip).
Gatorna på Södra Guldheden är uppkallade: The streets of Södra Guldheden are named after doctors. Doktor Liborius gata honours Johan August Liborius, chief surgeon at Sahlgrenska Hospital from 1845 to 1870, who is seen as the hospital's first modern surgeon. Doktor Bex gata is named after Abraham Bex, Gothenburg's town physician around 1685. At the very top of that street are some unusual shop buildings from 1951, where the Konsum co-op was the first tenant.
Gatorna skulle först få namn efter afrik: The streets were first going to be named after African animals, but the city council voted that down as far too exotic. As a compromise the blocks got the animal names – Tapiren (the Tapir), Puman, Krokodilen and Giraffen – while the streets were named after places in Dalarna, such as Moravägen and Rättviksvägen.

The streets were first going to be named after African animals, but the city council found that too exotic. As a compromise, the blocks got the animal names instead – Puman, Tapiren and Giraffen (the Puma, the Tapir and the Giraffe) – while the streets were named after places in Dalarna and figures from the saga of Sigurd.
Gatstumpen som ingen äger: The scrap of street no one owns
Gatu- och kvartersnamnen minns industrin: The names of streets and blocks are a nod to local industry: there's Optikvägen, Radiovägen, Prismavägen and Ackumulatorvägen, plus blocks such as Solventilen, Agaspisen and Geodimetern – all inventions made famous by Swedish firms.
Gatu- och kvartersnamnen påminner om ind: The street and block names are a nod to local industry: there’s Optikvägen, Radiovägen, Prismavägen and Ackumulatorvägen (optics, radio, prism and accumulator roads), and blocks called Agaspisen, Solventilen and Geodimetern – the AGA cooker, the sun valve and the geodimeter.
Gatukök och pizza på torget: Street food and pizza on the square
Gatunamn med kanoner och valkyrior: Street names with cannons and Valkyries
Gatunamnen berättar historia. Lavettväge: The street names tell a story. Lavettvägen (Gun Carriage Road), Kavallerivägen (Cavalry Road) and Pjäsbacken (Cannon Hill) recall the military years, while Mjölnerbacken, Odalvägen and Valkyriavägen allude to the many ancient remains in the area.
Gatunamnen bär på historia. Signalistgat: The street names are full of history. Signalistgatan, Ballonggatan, Telegrafgatan and Brevduvegatan – Signaller, Balloon, Telegraph and Carrier Pigeon Streets – nod to the old signals regiment. Signe Tillischgatan and Pomonagatan are named after apple varieties, and there's an apple orchard at Lilla Frösunda.
Gatunamnen här doftar häst, och det är i: The street names around here smell of horses – and that's no coincidence. A few hundred metres away is Åbytravet, Sweden's second-largest trotting track, run by the Åby Travsällskap association. Its neighbour, the Åbybadet swimming centre, opened in 2023, so both people and horses can get their hearts racing here.
Gatunamnen här doftar sågspån. Sågmästar: The street names around here smell of fresh sawdust. Nils Georg Sörensen ran the Säfveåns AB sawmill, and it inspired several of Björkekärr's street names, all taken from sawmill terms: Hyvelsågsgatan, Klyvsågsgatan and Stabbetorget, this square. Sörensen even got a street named after him. On a hill by the square stands Björkekärr Church, and the area borders the Delsjö nature reserve.
Gatunamnen här är ingen slump, Biskopsgå: The street names round here are no accident – Biskopsgården is full of names with a weather theme. A short walk away, on Vårväderstorget, 'Spring Weather Square', is Biskopsgården library. It opened in 1964 and is now one of the most popular libraries in the city, with 700 to 800 visitors on an ordinary day. In 2020 the Swedish Arts Council named it a Romani reading embassy.
Gatunamnen i Bifrost är som en lektion i: The street names in Bifrost read like a lesson in farming. Lantbruksgatan (‘Agriculture Street’) wraps around the whole area, and the blocks of flats stand on streets such as Pinnharvsgatan, Rullharvsgatan and Släpharvsgatan – named after different kinds of harrow – as well as Havrekornsgatan and Vetekornsgatan (oat grain and wheat grain). You’ll find the houses on Axgatan and Rågkornsgatan (ear of corn and rye grain).
Gatunamnet Krysshammarvägen syftar på et: The street name Krysshammarvägen refers to a technique for dressing the surface of granite. The big open quarry can be seen from the street Jungfrudansen and from the waterside promenade by Ulvsundasjön. Two wooden villas from around 1880 are the only workers' homes left from the quarries.
Gatunamnet ljuger inte: ett par hundra m: The street name tells no lies: a couple of hundred metres away, Kållered Church stands on a rise in the village. As well as being the parish church of Kållered, it's the oldest building in the whole of Mölndal municipality. Kållered was farming country for centuries, until the superstores moved into the western part of town.
Gatunamnet passar bra, för en kort prome: The street name is well chosen: a short walk away is Skansberget, one of eight ancient hillforts in Huddinge municipality. Closer still, the Smista bridge spans the E4/E20 motorway. This steel bridge for pedestrians and cyclists opened in 2008 and crosses in a single span between Segeltorp and Sätra, making it easier to get from one to the other.
Gatunamnet passar perfekt. På Tullinge g: The street name couldn't be more fitting. At Tullinge gymnasium, the upper secondary school a couple of hundred metres away, there's a tradition of a Nobel laureate visiting every year – usually a scientist. In 2014 the chemistry laureates Eric Betzig and William Moerner came, and in 2017 Michael W. Young. Not many schools can boast guest speakers like that.
Gatunamnet påminner om Svenska Ostindisk: The street name recalls the Swedish East India Company, based in Gothenburg from 1731 to 1813. Its ships sailed to China and came home laden with tea, porcelain and silk.
Gatunamnet är ingen slump. Strax intill: The street name is no coincidence. Right next to us is Stora Sköndal, which started life as a Lutheran deacons' institution. It was founded in Gävle in 1898 to train deacons, and moved here in 1905, when the Stora Sköndal estate was bought. Fittingly enough, Terrasshuset, the Terrace House, designed by Axel Kandell and marked in blue by the City Museum, stands on a steep south-facing plot in a block called Predikanten – the Preacher.
Gatunamnet är inte taget ur luften. Inge: The street name didn't come out of nowhere. In 1885 the engineer Gerhard Arehn opened a factory here on Kungsholmen making matchboxes – and the machines that made matchboxes. The business eventually became part of Svenska Tändsticksaktiebolaget, the Swedish Match Company. Nearby you'd also have found Tullmuseum, the Customs Museum, which from 1927 displayed objects collected by Swedish Customs, and the old Jewish cemetery, Aronsberg.
Gav namn åt ett härad: It gave its name to a hundred
Gebers byggdes tack vare bankiren Martin: Gebers was built thanks to the banker Martin Geber, who left 800,000 kronor in his will so that convalescents without means could recover in the countryside. Karl Güettler's functionalist building had 136 beds, large sun verandas and a reflecting pool between its wings.
Gebers konvalescenthem invigdes 1936 eft: Gebers convalescent home opened in 1936, funded by a bequest in the will of the banker Martin Geber. Since 1997 it has been a housing cooperative for ecological communal living, and it's one of just two small rural settlements within the City of Stockholm. The name Orhem first appears in 1409.
Genealogiska Föreningen började tidigt k: Early on, the Genealogical Society began clipping family announcements from Svenska Dagbladet and later Dagens Nyheter. Since 2011 it has been indexing old internal passports, and in 2024 it passed 600,000 records, most from 1812–1860.
Genom Angered slingrar Lärjeån i en ravi: The Lärjeån river winds through Angered in a ravine, and to the north lies the forest of Vättlefjäll. The last bear here was shot in 1750, and wolves and lynx still roamed the area as late as the end of the 19th century.
Genom Angered slingrar sig Lärjeån i en: The Lärje river winds through Angered in a ravine cut through an old rural landscape, and to the north lies Vättlefjäll, with canoe routes and hiking trails. The last bear was shot in 1750, and wolves and lynx still roamed here in the late 1800s.
Genom Annedal gick förr en järnväg som f: A railway once ran through Annedal, used mainly by industry; it has since been torn up. Around 2,000 flats were built here between 2008 and 2013, and in August 2012 the area hosted the Annedal 2012 housing expo under the slogan “Sustainable homes – for tomorrow's demands”.
Genom Barkarby villastad går markerade k: Marked heritage trails run through Barkarby villastad. They lead to places such as Järfälla Church, the old courthouse and the coaching inn on Barkarby torg, as well as to ancient burial grounds.
Genom Djurgården, som i flera hundra år: Through Djurgården, for centuries the king's hunting park, past Bellmansro and Djurgårdsskolan.
Genom Henriksdalsberget går Saltsjöbanan: The Saltsjöbanan railway runs through the Henriksdal hill in a 337-metre tunnel, and trains have rumbled through it since 1893. The area around Henriksborg used to be industrial, and from 1882 until the late 1950s the Rylander and Rudolph factory made, among other things, batteries for crank telephones and carbon rods for arc lamps. In 1987 the Danvikcenter office building won a European award for its steelwork.
Genom Majorna och ut mot kusten, förbi K: Through Majorna and out towards the coast, past Kungssten and the Älvsborg Bridge.
Genom Majorna, Haga och Vasastaden. Lyss: Through Majorna, Haga and Vasastaden. Listen out for the Palladium cinema at Kungsportsplatsen.
Genom Masthugget och Majorna mot älvmynn: Through Masthugget and Majorna towards the mouth of the river.
Genom Vasastaden med sina pampiga stenhu: Through Vasastaden and its grand late 19th-century stone buildings.
Genom Vasastaden och förbi Linnéplatsen,: Through Vasastaden and past Linnéplatsen, where Slottsskogen park, laid out in 1874, begins.
Genom dagens Drakenbergsparken gick förr: The Western Main Line once ran through what is now Drakenbergsparken to Södra station. The tracks were closed in 1929 when the Årsta Bridge took over the traffic, and until the late 1960s the site was occupied by the Ligna industrial area.
Genom en folkomröstning 2005 bestämdes a: A local referendum in 2005 decided the tower should become a café. After a careful renovation in 2009 it now houses a restaurant, a café and exhibitions. The tower is protected and may not be demolished or have its exterior altered.
Genom ett kungligt brev 1822 bestämdes a: A royal letter of 1822 decreed that Kungsträdgården should be known as "Karl XIII:s torg" – Karl XIII's Square. The King's statue is surrounded by four lions modelled by Bengt Erland Fogelberg.
Genom ett titthål på sidan av trämodelle: Through a peephole in the side of the wooden model of Stora Haga Palace and a system of mirrors, you can see into the dome just as the architect Desprez imagined it. Parts of the model can be lifted off. Admission to the museum is free.
Genom hela centrum och ut till Gamlestad: Right through the city centre and out to Gamlestaden, where Nya Lödöse was founded in 1473 and where the ball-bearing giant SKF later grew up.
Genom området löper en 1 800 meter lång: An 1,800-metre church path runs through the area from Hågelby and Skrävsta to Botkyrka Church. It already appears in the geometric land register of 1636. In the middle of the area there's also Kyrkkulla, a Late Iron Age burial ground.
Genom reservatet går Stockholmsåsen med: The Stockholm esker runs through the reserve in four ridges: Nordkullen, Sydkullen, Järvakullen and Kvarnkullen. On their eastern slopes grows one of Sweden's northernmost beech woods.
Genom reservatets södra del går banvalle: The southern part of the reserve is crossed by the embankment of the once-secret Krutbanan, the 'Gunpowder Railway' from the 1940s, which mainly carried ammunition. The track was torn up in the late 1980s, and today it's used for horse riding.
Genom södra delen av reservatet går den: The old district road runs through the southern part of the reserve. It's been recorded in writing since the Middle Ages but probably dates back to the Iron Age, and it linked Järfälla church with Sollentuna church.
Genvägen och bullerplanken: The shortcut and the noise fences
Georg Scherman klädde entrésidan med rel: Georg Scherman clad the entrance front with cast-iron panels in relief. They were first left to rust, then treated with a liquid that stopped the rust and oven-baked with oil – a method the Näfvekvarn ironworks had used when making cannons.
Georg Varhelyi planerade att själv bo i: Georg Varhelyi planned to live in one of the top-floor studio flats himself. But his wife was afraid of heights, so nothing came of it. The light in the flats – with windows facing two ways and sometimes double-height ceilings – was, in his own view, what he got most right.
Georg och Hanna Pauli flyttade 1905 från: In 1905 Georg and Hanna Pauli moved from Laurinska huset on Södermalm to their new home 'in the country' at Storängen. There they each had a studio of their own, and they lived and worked there for the rest of their lives. From 1989 to 2024 the villa housed the local newspaper Nacka Värmdö Posten.
Gerd Ribbing föddes i kvarntorpet: Gerd Ribbing was born in the miller's cottage
Getter och grisar i parken: Goats and pigs in the park
Gibraltargatan en bit härifrån fick sitt: Gibraltargatan, a short way from here, was named in 1886 after the Gibraltar estate. In 1923 the street-naming committee wanted to change it to Gibraltarsgatan, but the city council turned the idea down. From 1922 the street was home to the Gibraltarvallen sports ground, until Mossen took over in 1959 and the old ground became mostly a car park. The footpath Syster Bojans backe, Sister Bojan's Hill, is named after Ingeborg Kastman.
Gillar du bröllop? Tuve kyrka, några min: Fond of weddings? Tuve Church, a few minutes away, is one of the most popular churches for weddings in the Diocese of Gothenburg. It's the parish church of Tuve, a parish that belonged to the Östra Hising hundred in Västergötland until it became part of the City of Gothenburg in 1967. Since 2010 the church has been part of Tuve-Säve parish.
Gipskrucifixet ovanför altaret, av skulp: The plaster crucifix above the altar, by the sculptor Carl Johan Dyfverman, was originally white. During the 1955 renovation it was painted to resemble medieval triumphal crucifixes, and the church also gained a new font in white marble.
Gitarrverkstad i källaren: A guitar workshop in the basement
Gjutjärn från egen verkstad: Cast iron from its own works
Glaskors och himmelska Jerusalem: A glass cross and the heavenly Jerusalem
Glasmonumentet vid trappan: The glass monument by the steps
Glasmålning från ett sjukhus: A stained-glass window from a hospital
Glasmålningen över altaret, Einar Forset: The stained-glass window above the altar, Einar Forseth's ‘Avsked och återkomst’ (Farewell and Return), was made for the chapel at Karolinska Hospital. It's made up of more than 600 pieces of leaded glass and has been here since 1988. The font is built from 318 hand-sawn bricks.
Glaspaviljongen som blev sjömärke: The glass pavilion that became a landmark
Glass i kvarnkontoret: Ice cream in the mill office
Glass och gatukök som lockar långväga: Ice cream and burgers worth the trip
Glasvägg mot skogen: A glass wall facing the forest
Globen invigdes den 19 februari 1989 och: Globen opened on 19 February 1989 as the world's largest spherical building, but in 2023 it was overtaken by the Sphere in Las Vegas. Inside, the ceiling is 65 metres high.
Globen syns från toppen: See the Globe from the top
Globen är utgångspunkten i Sweden Solar: Globen, the giant white globe of an arena, is the starting point of the Sweden Solar System – a scale model of the solar system in which the arena plays the part of the sun.
Glose gränsar till Ryskärsfjorden, där g: Glose looks out over Ryskärsfjorden, where shallow water and grazed shore meadows attract a wealth of plants and birds. The meadows are part of the Nordre älv estuary, a nature reserve and Natura 2000 site ranked among the most valuable natural areas in the county. Sveriges Radio's nature programme Naturmorgon has even broadcast live from here. And a little further on stands Burås kvarn, a mill from the 1890s.
Glose strandängar har uppmärksammats av: The Glose shore meadows have caught the attention of, among others, Swedish Radio, which broadcast its nature programme Naturmorgon live from here. The county administrative board ranks the Nordre älv estuary among the county's most valuable natural areas.
Glose strandängar har uppmärksammats bla: The Glose water meadows have drawn plenty of attention – Swedish Radio has even broadcast its nature programme Naturmorgon live from here.
Glose å är sex kilometer lång och mynnar: The Glose å stream is six kilometres long and flows into Ryskärsfjorden. Its lower reaches form the boundary between Glose and Glöskär, and sea trout are among the fish living in it.
Gloseby har en tät bygata där bostadshus: Gloseby has a tightly packed village street where homes and barns sit side by side. Every year the Fläskholmen farm hosts Artes, an exhibition of local crafts, and Glose harbour has around fifty moorings.
Gloseby kännetecknas av en tät bygata dä: Gloseby is known for its tightly packed village street, where houses and cowsheds alternate. Along the road down to the fjord, the wildflowers on the verges have been encouraged – something the Swedish Society for Nature Conservation highlighted in 2025 in its campaign 'The World's Longest Flower Meadow'.
Gloseby präglas av en tät bygata där bos: Gloseby is a tightly knit village street where houses and barns alternate. Every year the Fläskholmen farm hosts Artes, an exhibition of local crafts.

Gloseby is defined by its tightly packed village street, where farmhouses and cowsheds alternate. Several farms here are still working, and every year the farm at Fläskholmen hosts Artes, an exhibition of local crafts.

Gloseby is shaped by a tightly packed village street where farmhouses and cowsheds alternate. Several working farms remain, and every year the farm at Fläskholmen hosts Artes, an exhibition of local crafts.
Glödlampor som lyste upp hamnen: Light bulbs that lit up the harbour
Glömsta hör till Huddinges äldsta bosätt: Glömsta is one of Huddinge's oldest settlements, with burial grounds from the late Iron Age. The village is recorded from the 1400s, when it was written 'glomastom', after the Old Norse man's name Glume or Glome. The 18th-century main house still stands.
Glömstadalen är en rest av en forntida s: The Glömsta valley is what remains of an ancient sailing route between Orlången and Albysjön, an important link between the Baltic and Lake Mälaren. Stone Age settlements have been found on the heights around the valley. As the land rose, the waterway became wetland and later farmland.
Glömstahällen säger: ”Sverker lät göra b: The Glömsta rock carving reads: "Sverker had the bridge made in memory of Ärengunn, his good mother." It's unusual for a woman to be honoured like this. The word "good" ended up outside the runic band – perhaps for lack of space, or to give it extra emphasis.
Glömstastugan är en statarlänga från slu: Glömstastugan is a late-19th-century 'statarlänga', a row cottage for farm labourers paid in kind. In 1877–1878 five labourers' families lived here, with 24 children between them. The Fredriksdal croft by the old Göta highway is today the 'crown jewel' of the Gretas backe housing area, which won Huddinge's building award in 2017.
Glöstorpskyrkan inspirerades av Tempelpl: Glöstorp Church was inspired by Helsinki's Temppeliaukio rock church. It's partly blasted into the bedrock, and its long wall is built of blasted stone. From a distance you can spot a large round window whose glazing bars form a cross.
Gnistan som ändrade taket: The spark that changed the roof
Gnistängstunneln har fått namn efter gni: The Gnistäng tunnel takes its name from spark-gap transmitters, an early kind of radio transmitter. In 1911 the Swedish Naval Administration built a wireless telegraph station on this spot. Later known as Göteborg Radio, it kept in touch with ships at sea until 1948. In the early 1800s an optical telegraph stood here too.
Gnistängstunneln är den enda av Göteborg: The Gnistäng tunnel is the only one of Gothenburg's larger road tunnels that vehicles carrying hazardous goods are allowed through, as there is no tunnel-free main road between the port and the E6 south of the river. In 2020 it ranked fourth in the country for speeding convictions.
Godset har varit berömt för sin trädgård: The estate has been famous for its garden since the 1600s. During the 1960–1963 restoration, Sven A. Hermelin recreated part of a baroque garden with patterned hedges, fountains and a herb garden of 17th-century plants.
