Godset har varit känt för sin trädgård s: The estate has been famous for its garden since the 1600s. During the 1960–1963 restoration, Sven A. Hermelin recreated part of the baroque garden, with patterned hedges, fountains and a herb garden of 17th-century plants.
Godset hette från början Nockeby och ägd: The estate was originally called Nockeby and in the 15th century belonged to the alderman Peder Ålänning, one of the richest Stockholmers of his day. He sometimes acted as banker to Albert of Mecklenburg and Bo Jonsson Grip. The name Åkeshov came with Åke Axelsson Natt och Dag, who bought the estate in 1635.
Godsets siste enskilde ägare, C. Harry W: The estate's last private owner, C. Harry Winberg, ran a restaurant in the main house from 1928 to 1931. In 1926 he founded Vårbybaden, today Vårby strandbad, and in 1932 he built a factory bottling table water from the Vårby spring.
Golfboll på en peg: A golf ball on a tee
Golfhistoria i grannskapet! Lidingö golf: There's golf history in the neighbourhood! Lidingö Golf Club's parkland and woodland course at Sticklinge opened in 1927, and at the time it was the first 18-hole course in Sweden. If you'd rather go for a swim, there's Sticklingebadet, also called Sandviksbadet, a small beach on Stora Värtan bay. And the trail of Lidingöloppet, the famous cross-country race, passes through Sticklinge too.
Golv, altare, predikstol och dopfunt är: The floor, altar, pulpit and font are made of pale Ekeberg marble from Borghamn in Östergötland, and the pulpit is crowned with a white dove. Behind the altar is a red-and-gold mosaic by the architect himself, and the painted windows are the work of Johannes Schreiter.
Good to Great började i SALK-hallen i Br: Good to Great started out in the SALK hall in Bromma and moved to Järfälla in 2014. Its founder Magnus Norman has also coached Stanislas Wawrinka, and Mikael Tillström has coached the Frenchman Gaël Monfils.
Gospelkören som började 1996: The gospel choir that began in 1996
Gothia Arena har tre planer och är en av: Gothia Arena has three courts and is one of Sweden's largest club-owned basketball halls. The fixed stand holds around 500 spectators and the retractable seating about 300 more.
Gothia Arena är en av de största klubbäg: Gothia Arena is one of the largest club-owned basketball halls in Sweden and the only club-owned hall in Gothenburg. It has three courts, and with extra seating on match days it holds around 1,000 people.
Gothia Arena, Högsbo Baskets hemmahall,: Gothia Arena, home court of the Högsbo Basket club, is just a couple of hundred metres away. The whole area was part of the old parish of Västra Frölunda, which had about 13,500 inhabitants in 1944 and became part of the City of Gothenburg the following year. Its parish church, Västra Frölunda Church, now stands in the district of Järnbrott.
Goto 10 öppnade den 4 maj 2017 med grati: Goto 10 opened on 4 May 2017 with free workspace, wifi, a café, bookable 3D printers and a podcast studio. It spread to Malmö and Linköping, but in December 2024 Goto 10 in Stockholm closed.
Gottfrid Kallstenius bad 1906 arkitekten: In 1906 Gottfrid Kallstenius asked the architect Gustaf Petterson to design a villa with one studio for himself and another for his wife. The result was an imposing Art Nouveau stone house, pale yellow with red bay windows and railings.
Grand Curiosa Hotel ritades av Wingårdh: The nine-storey Grand Curiosa Hotel was designed by Wingårdh Arkitektkontor. It has 457 rooms, four restaurants and a roof terrace, and opened on 22 April 2023 – the same day the amusement park opened for the season.
Grand var från början en kyrkolokal. Kon: Grand started life as a church hall. The artist Gunnar Torhamn made the marquetry on the doors, where four film stars represent four continents: Joan Crawford for America, Anna May Wong for Asia, Greta Garbo for Europe and Josephine Baker for Africa.
Granen 14 vid Valhallavägen 92 byggdes 1: Granen 14, at Valhallavägen 92, was built in 1886–1887. Four Atlas figures support one of the bay windows facing the street, and the top floor is decorated with sgraffito paintings.
Graniten från Huvudsta blev inte bara ga: Huvudsta granite wasn’t just used for cobblestones. It’s also in the facades of the Parliament House and the Nordic Museum, and it was used for gravestones. At its peak, some 200 stonemasons worked in the quarry.
Granitmuren mot Birger Jarlsgatan följer: The granite wall along Birger Jarlsgatan follows the course of an old stream, "rännilen", that ran from the Träsket marsh at Jarlaplan to Nybroviken. The wall is in fact a sculpture, Vågrörelse (Wave Motion) by Torsten Fridh, from the redevelopment around 1990.
Granne med Frölunda torg, som Olof Palme: Frölunda torg, right next to us, was opened by Olof Palme in 1966 as the biggest shopping centre under one roof in the Nordic countries – and it's a good place to talk about Gothenburg humour. Kal and Ada, or 'Kal å Ada', are the stars of the classic Gothenburg jokes, and tradition has it that Aron Jonason, court photographer to King Oscar II, was one of the founding fathers of the Gothenburg pun. Beside the square is Frölunda kulturhus, the culture centre, with a library, a theatre and a swimming pool.
Granne med gymnasieskolan ligger Svandam: Next to the upper secondary school is Svandammen, a park and swimming spot popular with teenagers and families alike. A little further on is Spånga station on the Mälaren Line, 11.3 kilometres from Stockholm Central Station. On an ordinary winter weekday, around 7,900 people board trains there.
Granne med tenniscentret växer Råstapark: Next to the tennis centre, Råstapark is taking shape – AIK's future training ground and clubhouse for the men's team. It's due to be finished in autumn 2028 and will replace Karlberg, where the team has trained since 1999. A short walk away is Lake Råstasjön, Solna's only lake if you don't count Mälaren.
Granne med värdshuset gömmer sig en rikt: Tucked away next to the inn is a real gem: Confidencen, the Ulriksdal Palace theatre and Sweden's oldest rococo theatre. It was fitted out in 1753 by the architect Carl Fredrik Adelcrantz and restored in stages in the 1990s and 2000s. The inn itself is younger, built in 1868 on the initiative of King Karl XV.
Grannen Rådan nämns redan 1599. Sedan de: Neighbouring Rådan is mentioned as early as 1599. Since then it has been a croft, a farm bailiff's residence, a manor, a boarding school, a military camp and, from 1970, a police academy.
Grannen kallade huset kruthus: The neighbour called it a powder house
Grannkommundelen Viksjö i Järfälla har e: The neighbouring district of Viksjö in Järfälla has a name with a long history. It comes from Viksjö farm and is a corruption of the original Vikhusa, which already appears on an 11th-century runestone. The farm was sold in 1921, development began in 1963, and today the area is mostly detached houses.
Granntomten ägdes på 1600-talet av Chris: In the 1600s the neighbouring plot belonged to Christian Horleman, whom Karl XI brought from The Hague to tend the royal gardens. In the late 1660s he laid out a magnificent garden with orchards – Stockholm's first town garden. Horleman was the grandfather of the celebrated architect Carl Hårleman.
Grannön Fågelön ägs av Statens fastighet: The neighbouring island of Fågelön is owned by the National Property Board and can only be reached by private boat. Since 2014 the whole island has been a nature reserve, part of the Lovön nature reserve along with Kärsön and Lovön.
Granskogen där vargen bor: The spruce forest where the wolf lives
Grantorp byggdes för personalen på Huddi: Grantorp was built for the staff of Huddinge Hospital, and the names give it away. The blocks are called Medicinaren, Kirurgen and Vårdaren (the Physician, the Surgeon and the Carer), and the streets Diagnosvägen, Ortopedvägen and Terapivägen.
Gratis bad blir avgiftsbelagt: Free swimming comes to an end
Gratis bad på väg bort: Free swimming on its way out
Gratis boende mot visning: Free rent in return for viewings
Gratis för dig, inte för staten: Free for you, not for the state
Gratis studier och dagtraktamente: Free tuition and a daily allowance
Gravar från romartid och vikingatid: Graves from Roman and Viking times
Gravarna här är brandgravar: de döda brä: These are cremation graves: the dead were burned on a pyre and their bones placed in a pot or wooden box, sometimes with a gift, then covered with earth and stones. When grave number 8 was excavated in 1939, shards of pottery and a few iron nails were found.
Gravarna i Björklunds hage är brandgrava: The graves in Björklunds hage are cremation graves. The dead were burnt on a pyre, and their bones were placed in a pot or wooden box, sometimes with a grave gift, and covered with earth and stones. When grave number 8 was excavated in 1939, pottery shards and iron nails were found.
Gravarna i Lunda och Skesta är från yngr: The graves at Lunda and Skesta date from the late Iron Age and appear today as grass-covered mounds. These farm burial grounds were abandoned in the late 1000s, when Christianity arrived and people began burying their dead at churches instead.
Gravarna sköttes på sommaren av unga dal: In summer the graves were tended by young women from Rättvik in Dalarna, known as dalkullor, who lived in two dormitories in the north-west corner of the cemetery. They worked 12 hours a day, six days a week, and folk costume was compulsory until 1917. The arrangement ended in 1930.
Graverska huset byggdes som en del av En: The Graver House was built as part of the English Tannery, and Jacob Graver lived here in a household of 18. In the great hall are landscape paintings by Lars Gottman, with clipped formal parks and strolling rococo ladies and gentlemen.
Gravfält med utsikt: A burial ground with a view
Gravfält under flygfältet: A burial ground under the airfield
Gravfält vid kvarnbacken: A burial ground by the mill hill
Gravfältet består av omkring 15 gravhöga: The burial ground has around 15 burial mounds and 109 round stone settings, yet not one of the graves has been examined by archaeologists. The site was probably already in use in the Early Iron Age.
Gravfältets största hög, \"Kungshögen\",: The largest mound in the burial ground, Kungshögen, "the King's Mound", is 20 metres across. In 1925 Crown Prince Gustaf VI Adolf, a keen archaeologist, took part in the excavations. Finds include gaming pieces, bone combs and a gilded bronze mount shaped like an animal's head.
Gravhällen över tullmannen Olof Claeson: The grave slab of customs officer Olof Claeson once lay in the chancel of the old church. The oldest headstones in the churchyard date from 1680 and 1729, and they now stand in a row along the north wall.
Gravkammaren under kyrkans kor blev pann: The burial chamber beneath the chancel was turned into a boiler room during the 1905–1906 renovation. Today the crypt serves as a public toilet, reached by lift.
Gravkapellet blev lillkyrka: The burial chapel became a small church
Gravklot med kors: A grave ball with a cross
Gravkor blev pannrum: From burial vault to boiler room
Gravkullarna i Rissne har grävts ut. Fyn: The burial mounds in Rissne have been excavated. Finds of goshawks suggest that the people who lived here were upper class – only the elite trained birds for hunting.
Gravplats långt före Wallenbergs: A burial place long before the Wallenbergs
Gravplats på en handelsträdgård: A cemetery on a market garden
Gravplatsen fick grundarens namn: A cemetery named after its founder
Grenen som aldrig byggdes: The branch that was never built
Gretas backe har fått sitt namn efter Gr: Gretas backe, Greta's Hill, is named after Greta Berg, born in 1759, the first crofter's wife at the Fredriksdal croft. In 1801 she lived there with her husband, the shoemaker Erik Färnström, their two children and a maid.
Greve Filip Bogislaus von Schwerin på Ja: In 1844 Count Filip Bogislaus von Schwerin of Jakobsberg offered a plot for a school by the Lövhagen croft. The parish turned it down because the site wasn't central enough, and instead bought land from him at Aspnäs for 800 riksdaler banco.
Greve von Schwerin erbjöd först en skolt: Count von Schwerin first offered a plot for a school by the Lövhagen croft, but it was considered too out of the way. Instead, in 1845 the parish bought the land at Aspnäs, along with its newly built manor house, for 800 riksdaler banco. The school opened on 10 May 1846.
Grevegårdens kyrka byggdes 1992 på en ku: Grevegården Church was built in 1992 on a hilly, wooded plot, with its nave panelled in a variety of woods. The altarpiece is made up of seven copies of 16th-century Russian icons, and behind the altar is a cross-shaped window by Britta Reich-Eriksson.
Grevegårdens kyrka ligger några hundra m: Grevegården Church is just a few hundred metres away, but a little further on, in Älvsborg, is one of the area's sweetest stories. In the 1930s a Mrs Liljegren baked buns and sold them through a hatch in the wall of her house to children on their way to Påvelundsskolan school. She became known as Bullegumman, the Bun Lady, and in 1965 the street was named after her.
Griftegården började planeras 1952, och: Planning for the cemetery began in 1952, and after a Nordic architecture competition it was designed by the Finns Bengt Lundsten and Per-Mauritz Ålander. Their idea was to preserve the natural landscape, interfering with it as little as possible.
Grindstugan vid lindallén: The gatehouse by the lime avenue
Grindtorp har fått namn efter en grind v: Grindtorp is named after a gate on the road between Näsby and Tibble that marked the boundary between the manor and the farm. The croft became a pig farm in 1926 and was demolished in the 1960s. Today the streets here are called Kometvägen and Meteorvägen.
Grisarna som inte klarade sig: The pigs that didn't make it
Groens malmgård: Groens malmgård, an old country house
Groens malmgård är en riktig överlevare:: Groens malmgård is a true survivor. Its Carolean-style main building is the last of its kind in Stockholm, and its garden has been tended without a break for more than 300 years. A malmgård is an old country house on what was once the edge of the city. The street outside has had several names, among them Stadsträdgårdsgatan and Wintertullsgatan. From 1885 it was Vermdögatan, but that was thought misleading, so in 1939 it became Malmgårdsvägen. Back in the 1600s a windmill turned here too – Bengt Bagares kvarn, Bengt the Baker's mill.
Grosshandlaren David af Sandeberg, direk: The manor was built for David af Sandeberg, a wholesale merchant and director of the Swedish East India Company. His brother-in-law William Chambers, court architect in England, had sailed with him to Canton in 1748–49. Chambers sent designs by letter, while the Gothenburg architect Carl Wilhelm Carlberg drew up the working plans.
Grosshandlaren Jacob Schmidt byggde de n: The wholesale merchant Jacob Schmidt built the present buildings in 1812, in an austere Empire style. He had the old main house from the mid-1700s moved about 500 metres to Fittjaviken bay, where it still stands as 'Ängsbyggningen'. By 1815 his money had run out.
Grosshandlarna bakom villastaden: The merchants behind the garden suburb
Grottan är en blockgrotta: ett stort sty: This is a boulder cave: a huge chunk of rock broke away, crashed down and came to rest at an angle, leaving a hollow underneath. It's about 23 metres long and up to eight metres high, with openings in the roof that let in the light.
Grundaren Herman Lindholm sade att parke: The park's founder, Herman Lindholm, claimed it was pink "because the best pudding I know is lingonberries and milk". In fact, the architects behind the jubilee exhibition had chosen the colour.
Grundaren John Rudolphs bodde i Villa Pl: The founder, John Rudolphs, lived in Villa Plania by Kyrkviken bay – a three-storey villa with an equally tall veranda facing the water, built for sipping Swedish punch. The villa was demolished in 1986. The carbon brush factory behind it had a 43-metre chimney.
Grundstenen till Nasirmoskén lades 1975: The foundation stone of the Nasir Mosque was laid in 1975 by Caliph Mirza Nasir Ahmad from Pakistan, who also opened it. The mosque was designed by White Architects. In time it became too cramped, and a new, larger building opened in 2001. In 2026 the mosque celebrated its 50th anniversary.
Gruset som betalade bygget: Gravel that paid for the cemetery
Gruvan anlades 1938 och har tre kilomete: The mine was dug in 1938 and has three kilometres of tunnels on two levels, 20 and 40 metres down. The rock is Stockholm granite, 30 per cent harder than ordinary granite – perfect for testing drills.

The mine was dug in 1938 and has three kilometres of tunnels on two levels, 20 and 40 metres underground. The rock is Stockholm granite, 30 per cent harder than ordinary granite and perfect for testing drills.
Gruvan har funnits sedan 1938: The Mine has been here since 1938
Gruvan har varit inspelningsplats för bl: The mine has been used as a film location for productions including Joe Hill, Midnattssol and several films in the Beck detective series. Even Kenny Starfighter has passed through.
Grynkvarnsparken har fått sitt namn efte: Grynkvarnsparken is named after a groats mill that once ground grain here; the farm beside it was demolished in the 1940s. In the southern part of the park, at what is now Bolidenvägen 2, stood the croft of Linde, which served travellers as both a coaching station and a tavern. The park was designed in the 1950s by city gardener Holger Blom and Erik Glemme, and today Talltunneln, one of the slip roads onto the Södra länken ring road, runs right under the lawns.
Grädde och ost, det passar ju ihop. Alld: Cream and cheese – a natural pairing, wouldn't you say? Right beside Gräddgatan, Cream Street, rises Ostkupan, the Cheese Dome. That's the nickname for a 14-storey block from 1964, home mostly to students living in corridor rooms with shared kitchens. The name Kallebäck is even older: it means the stream with the kettle and is mentioned as early as 1496.
Gräddgatan, Smörgatan och Mjölktorget –: Gräddgatan, Smörgatan and Mjölktorget – Cream Street, Butter Street and Milk Square. The streets here are named after dairy products, thanks to the Arla dairy that stood in the district from 1956 to 2015.
Gränsberget är ett cirka 1,3 kilometer l: Gränsberget is a wooded ridge about 1.3 kilometres long and up to 51 metres high that lay on the border between the Hammarby and Enskede estates. The park was left in its natural state, with bare rock and mostly pine forest.
Gränsen för Rävekärr gick förr vid bäcke: Rävekärr used to end at the Sandbäck stream, also known as Alebäcken. When the housing estate was built in 1969–1974, some of the buildings ended up south of the stream, and that part of Sandbäck started being called Rävekärr too. Even the Sandbäck rectory found itself in Rävekärr.
Gränsen går vid gångvägen: The border runs along the footpath
Gränsen mellan Kattegatt och Skagerrak g: The boundary between the Kattegat and the Skagerrak runs from the Pater Noster skerries off Marstrand, in Kungälv municipality, to the northern tip of Skagen in Denmark. The municipality's highest point is Stora Kattås, 175 metres above sea level.
Gränsen mot Danmark gick under lång tid: For a long time the border with Denmark ran close to Fässberg, and the church was ransacked by the Danes in the 17th century. The oldest grave that still has its monument dates from 1775.
Gräsbacken Sjöbacken, som i folkmun kall: The grassy slope of Sjöbacken, which locals call Tippen, 'the Tip', was once a shallow bay of the sea. When Frölunda torg was built, the earth dug out for it was dumped here – and the result is a much-loved spot for picnics and kite flying, with ice skating in cold winters. Down in Fiskebäck harbour there's also a fishing museum with a café, opened in 1999.
Gräsbacken kallas både Sjöbacken och Sjö: The grassy slope is known as both Sjöbacken and Sjöbacka, as well as by the nickname Tippen. There's also a football pitch and a little stream, and the lovely natural setting makes it a popular place for walks.
Gräset som renar vattnet: The grass that cleans the water
Gräsplanen bara för A-laget: A grass pitch for the first team only
Gråviken är ett fågelskyddsområde. Från: Gråviken is a bird sanctuary. From 1 April to 31 October nobody is allowed on the water, and fishing is banned all year round. There's a birdwatching platform on the north side.
Gröna Lund öppnade 1883 och är Sveriges: Gröna Lund opened in 1883 and is Sweden's oldest amusement park. In summer you can hear the screams from its roller coasters far out across the water. Opposite is Liljevalchs, the art gallery.
Gröna och röda linjens station byggdes g: The station for the green and red lines was built by digging a huge trench through central Stockholm and then covering it with a concrete roof. Only the section under Klara church is a blasted tunnel. The blue line, 26–32 metres down, was blasted entirely out of the bedrock.
Gröndal var tänkt som ett mönstersamhäll: Gröndal was meant to be a model community, but a shanty town sprang up instead. In the summer of 1905 the newspaper Dagens Nyheter reported that Gröndal had neither proper roads nor water and sewage pipes.
Gröndal växte fram som en tidig arbetar-: Gröndal grew up as one of the early working-class and factory suburbs once the Western Main Line was built past Liljeholmen in the 1860s. The famous Gröndal terraced block, designed by Sven Backström and Leif Reinius, housed the Galjonen cinema from 1952 to 1962. The Riggen apartment building at Fågelsångsvägen 13 is a lot younger – it was nominated for Stockholm Building of the Year in 2016.
Gröndal är känt för stjärnhusen, och här: Gröndal is famous for its star-shaped apartment blocks – the first of their kind in Sweden were built right here. They were designed by the architects Sven Backström and Leif Reinius, with the master builder Olle Engkvist driving the project, and they've since become known around the world. From 1926 to 1934 the district was called Ekensberg; its present name comes from the Gröndal estate.
Gröndals kyrka från 1969 är också ritad: Gröndal church, from 1969, is also designed by Backström & Reinius. It's built into the slope, and at the very bottom are youth rooms entirely underground. The altar and the chancel organ are made of beech.
Grönområden var en del av miljonprogramm: Green space was part of the ideal behind the Million Programme, Sweden's great 1960s–70s housing drive. Söderhöjden has three large parks – Nybergsparken, Tallbohovsparken and Snapphaneparken – that wrap around the whole area. In winter the football pitch in Tallbohovsparken is flooded to make an ice rink, and there's a paddling pool for little ones.
Grönstakolonin anlades 1910 och är Sveri: The Grönsta colony was laid out in 1910 and is Sweden's oldest surviving area of weekend cabins, designated of national interest since 1987. In Trolldalen, founded by Carl Milles's brother Stig, much of the early summer-cottage idyll survives.
Grönt stråk över kommungränsen: A green corridor across the boundary
Gubbängens IP hette från början Bandhage: Gubbängens IP was originally called Bandhagens idrottsplats. In winter the artificial pitch is flooded to make a full-size bandy rink, and since the bandy hall opened in August 2020 there have been two rinks, one outdoors and one indoors. Bandy is a Nordic cousin of ice hockey, played with a ball.
Gubbängens IP hette ursprungligen Bandha: Gubbängens IP, the Gubbängen sports ground, was originally called Bandhagen sports ground, and it has a colourful past. In summer, the speedway bikes of Hammarby Speedway and Getingarna roared round the track, and back in the day it was even known for car speedway. Today it's used for bandy and field hockey – and since 2020, when Stockholm's first indoor bandy hall was finished, it's also home to IK Tellus.
Gubbängens första idrottsplats anlades p: Gubbängen's first sports ground was laid out in the 1940s south of the elementary school, and it survives as Gubbängen's ball pitch. Today's sports ground was built under a town plan from the late 1950s, with room for 1,500 spectators.
Gubbängshallen var från början gymnastik: Gubbängshallen started out as the gym for Gubbängen upper secondary school. The ceiling soars eleven metres high. Today it's used for everything from basketball and floorball to aikido, goalball and kendo, and the Stockholm City Museum has marked the building green as being of special value.
Guden Tor i namnet: The god Thor in the name
Gudsnamnet i taket: The name of God on the ceiling
Gudstjänst i skolan i tjugo år: Twenty years of services in a school
Gui Minhais torg som inte blev: The Gui Minhai Square that never was
Gul skola med röda knutar: A yellow school with red corners
Gul tegelvilla efter branden: A yellow-brick villa after the fire
Gula huset och röda magasinet: The yellow house and the red storehouse
Guldkrogen som föll: The fall of a star restaurant
Guldrummet i Historiska museet: The Gold Room at the Swedish History Museum
Guldrummet skapades 1994 med bidrag från: The Gold Room was created in 1994 with funding from the Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation. It's in the basement, where a great concrete vault was blasted out beneath the museum's main courtyard, with floors and pillars of limestone and diabase.
Gullmarsplan har fått sitt namn efter Gu: Gullmarsplan is named after Gullmarn, the fjord at Lysekil on the Bohuslän coast. The square was built in the 1940s along with the surrounding district, and the metro station opened on 1 October 1950 – before that, trams stopped here. Today it's one of Stockholm's biggest interchanges, where the metro, the Tvärbanan light rail and buses all meet.
Gullmarsplans tunnelbanestation har fått: Gullmarsplan metro station has landed a role on the opera stage: the opera Kurfursten (The Elector) is set right here at the station.
Gult tegel och en ljushall: Yellow brick and a light hall
Gunnar Asplund och Sven Ivar Lind vann a: Gunnar Asplund and Sven Ivar Lind won the 1927 architecture competition with a design called 'Olstorp', named after one of the old crofts in the area. Asplund wanted to make the most of the contrast between the heavy, rounded ridges and the leafy valleys, where farms and chapels huddle for shelter from the sea winds.
Gunnar Grens staty av Jan Steen avtäckte: Gunnar Gren's statue of Jan Steen was unveiled at Gamla Ullevi during a football match on 29 September 1993. It was later moved to a spot outside the stadium.
Gunnar Larsson provsimmade: Gunnar Larsson took the first dip
Gunnareds kyrka ligger bara några minute: Gunnared church is only a few minutes away and has been part of Angered parish since 2014. A little further on is Titteridamm pond, surrounded by roads such as Titteridammsvägen and Titteridammsstigen. Legend has it that the name comes from the girls who would gaze at their reflections in the pond's shiny surface before the Saturday dance – ‘titta’ means to look.
Gunnareds kyrka på Kråkekullen invigdes: Gunnared Church on Kråkekullen hill was consecrated in 1997. It was designed by Sven Magnus Sjögren, whose competition entry was called Hörnstenen – the Cornerstone. The interior takes its cue from a medieval basilica, and the roof trusses of northern Swedish pine are hand-hewn.
Gunnareds kyrka ritades av Sven Magnus S: Gunnared Church was designed by Sven Magnus Sjögren, who won an architecture competition in 1990 with his entry Hörnstenen (The Cornerstone). It stands on Kråkekullen hill and was consecrated on 12 October 1997.
Gunnareds kyrkogård invigdes i juni 2003: Gunnared Cemetery opened in June 2003 and covers 80 hectares. Its design was settled by an architectural competition, won by the landscape architect Åke Andersson.
Gunnared Cemetery covers 80 hectares. Its layout was decided in a design competition in the late 1990s, won by the landscape architect Åke Andersson.
Gunnareds kyrkogård, en kort promenad bo: Gunnared Cemetery, a short walk away, took a long time to happen. Plans for a new cemetery in north-eastern Gothenburg began back in the 1980s, the land was acquired in a land swap with the city, and in the late 1990s an architecture competition was held. The cemetery finally opened in 2003 and covers 80 hectares. Gunnared Church stands beside it.
Gunnebo bro över Gunneboåns utlopp i Ste: Gunnebo bro, where the Gunneboån stream flows out into Stensjön lake, already appears on a map from 1725. The old bridge had oak beams resting on piers of gneiss from local quarries. Today's bridge opened on 17 March 1999.
Gunnestorps mosse är en blandning av sjö: Gunnestorp bog is a mix of lake, fen and raised bog. Reeds, bulrushes and water lilies grow side by side with cranberries, sundews and cotton grass, and the damp meadows around it were once grazing land.
Gustaf Adolfs torg och Stora Hamnkanalen: Gustaf Adolfs torg square and the Stora Hamnkanalen canal
Gustaf Fröding vårdades på Villa Gröndal: The poet Gustaf Fröding was cared for at Villa Gröndal in the early 1900s and lived here with his nurse Signe Trotzig until his death on 8 February 1911. It was here he wrote his last collection of poems, Rekonvalescentia.
Gustaf VI Adolf invigde Torslandaverken: King Gustaf VI Adolf opened the Torslanda plant on 24 April 1964, touring the factory in the back seat of a Volvo ÖV4. The first car off the line, a Volvo Amazon, was given to the King.
Gustaf VI Adolf invigde fabriken den 24: King Gustaf VI Adolf opened the factory on 24 April 1964, riding through the halls in the back of a Volvo ÖV4. The first car off the line, a Volvo Amazon, was given to the king as a gift.
Gustaf Vasa kyrka ritades av Agi Lindegr: Gustaf Vasa Church was designed by Agi Lindegren, who usually designed palaces. He chose Italian neo-baroque, and the dome rises more than 60 metres. With 1,500 seats, it was one of Stockholm's largest churches when it opened in 1906.
Gustaf de Laval köpte marken 1895 och by: Gustaf de Laval bought the land in 1895 and built a factory with a saw-tooth roof. In 1911 a 200-metre-long assembly hall was added. Now called Turbinhallen, the Turbine Hall, its gable end dominates the district's square.
Gustaf de Laval köpte marken kring Järla: Gustaf de Laval bought the land around Järla farm in 1895 for his steam turbine factory. In 1911 a 200-metre assembly hall went up – today known as Turbinhallen, the Turbine Hall – and its gable end dominates the square. The old factories now house shops, restaurants and offices.
Gustav Adolfs väg är uppkallad efter pri: Gustav Adolfs väg is named after Prince Gustav Adolf, who was married to Princess Sibylla. The neighbouring roads have royal names too – Kristinavägen, Margaretavägen and Sibyllavägen – plus Per Albins väg, after the prime minister of the day.
Gustav Holmdahl ritade husen, som stod k: The buildings were designed by Gustav Holmdahl and completed in 1936. The western one was originally the home of the physicist Manne Siegbahn and now houses the Faculty Club. With their reddish-brown brick and copper roofs, the buildings echo their neighbour, Bloms hus.
Gustav III gav marken till sin gunstling: Gustav III gave the land to his favourite, Armfelt, in 1791, and the name Frescati comes from the king's journey to Italy. Armfelt called the villa 'this little folly'. He never lived there: by the time it was finished, the king had been assassinated and Armfelt had fled the country.
Gustav III köpte antika skulpturer i Ita: Gustav III bought ancient sculptures in Italy, among them Apollo and the Nine Muses, for a museum at Haga. When he died in 1792, building work stopped at the foundations. Three months later the Royal Museum was founded all the same, and it became the start of Nationalmuseum, Sweden's national museum of art and design.
Gustav III ritade i stor utsträckning sj: Gustav III designed much of his English-style park at Drottningholm himself, but he didn't live to see it finished. A memorial temple to the king was planned for Monumentholmen, but only the foundations were ever laid. Next to it is Svanholmen, Swan Island, where a swan house that looks like a Chinese pagoda gave the park's wing-clipped mute swans shelter in winter. And the Gothic Tower, begun in 1792, was never fully finished inside.
Gustav III:s bro från 1787 ersattes i mi: Gustav III's bridge from 1787 was replaced by a pontoon bridge in the mid-19th century. The bridge from 1926 was long known as one of Greater Stockholm's problem children, and today's 450-metre bridge opened in 1973. Its 80-metre central section can swing through 90 degrees.
Gustav Vasa lät riva kyrkan: Gustav Vasa had the church torn down
Gustav Vasa skänkte en gång Skuru gård t: King Gustav Vasa once gave Skuru gård, the Skuru estate, to Danvik's Hospital, so that the rent could help cover the hospital's costs. The estate, a short walk from here, was bought in 1922 by its manager, Mathilda Sundelin, who renamed it Solsunda. The manor-like main house has been a convalescent and treatment home since the early 1900s. Perch and roach swim in little Bastusjön, the lake beside it.
Gustav Vasa ägde gården från 1544 och by: Gustav Vasa owned the estate from 1544 and built a royal residence here as an overnight stop on his journeys across Lake Mälaren. In his own words: 'vij kunne haffve ther etth natläger när thet behoff giörs' – that we might have a night's lodging there when need arises. The stone foundations survive in the house at Brantstigen 12.
Gustavi domkyrka har brunnit två gånger,: Gothenburg Cathedral, Gustavi domkyrka, has burned down twice, in 1721 and 1802, and the building you see today was completed in 1815. The streets around it follow the grid of the city's earliest years, and Kungsgatan, one of the longest pedestrian streets in Sweden, is just a block away.
Gyllene Cirkeln öppnade den 7 april 1962: Gyllene Cirkeln opened on 7 April 1962 with Bud Powell, the father of modern jazz piano. He was followed by the likes of Coleman Hawkins, Dexter Gordon and Monica Zetterlund. On 10 September 1967 Pink Floyd played their first ever gig in Sweden here.
Gyllene ratten invigdes den 16 mars 1957: Gyllene ratten, the Golden Wheel, was opened on 16 March 1957 in the presence of King Gustaf VI Adolf. It was a Shell venture, designed by two Danish architects who had drawn inspiration from the United States. The construction was handled by Olle Engkvist’s company Bygg-Oleba.

Gyllene ratten – the Golden Wheel – opened on 16 March 1957 in the presence of King Gustaf VI Adolf. It was commissioned by Shell, which hired two Danish architects who took their inspiration from the United States. Olle Engkvist's company was in charge of construction.
Gymnasieeleverna en bit härifrån har lek: The sixth-formers a short way from here have their lessons in an old weaving mill. Krokslättsgymnasiet started out in 1992 as an upper secondary school for healthcare and rents space in the Krokslätt factories, a textile mill built in the 1890s. The buildings were listed in 1991 and are protected in the local plan today, even though their interiors have been rebuilt.
Gymnasieeleverna en bit härifrån pluggar: The students at the upper secondary school just nearby have their lessons in a genuine piece of industrial history. Hulebäcksgymnasiet opened in 1995 in the converted and extended Hulebäck factory, built in 1878 as a branch of Mölnlycke fabriker. The railway has moved too. Mölnlycke station opened in 1894 about 350 metres east of where it stands today, and it was moved here in 2003. Now the Västtågen regional trains between Gothenburg and Borås stop here.
Gymnasiet i universitetshuset: A high school in the university building
Gymnasium i en gammal fabrik: A school in an old factory
Gymnasium, kulturskola och media: Sixth form, arts school and media
Gädda och sutare i träsket: Pike and tench in the lake
Gäddviken var förr namnet på hela Svinde: Gäddviken was once the name of the whole of Svindersviken bay, and the shore has had industry ever since the mid-1600s – including a superphosphate factory from the 1870s. The old coffee roastery is now a store for the Royal Opera and Dramaten, the Royal Dramatic Theatre, so there may well be stage sets and costumes behind those walls. A little further on is the manager's house of Beckbruket, the old pitch works. It dates from the 1830s and is the oldest surviving building in Finnboda.
Gällstaöeken mätte 10,1 meter i omkrets: In 2006 the Gällsta Oak measured 10.1 metres in girth and stood 19 metres tall. When botanist Rutger Sernander measured it in 1925, it was 8.6 metres round. Back in the 1920s there were about ten massive oaks here.
Gärdesgården, byggd 1940 till 1941, pres: When Gärdesgården was built in 1940–41, the newspaper Svenska Dagbladet described it as a modern residential hotel, with a shared restaurant, a sun terrace and even a Finnish sauna for the residents. In Tessinparken next door is the 1973 sculpture Husmorssemester, ‘Housewife's Holiday’: a granite woman in a summer dress, carrying a suitcase. It recalls the state grant that let housewives take a holiday between 1946 and 1979.
Gärdet som inte gick att plöja: The field that couldn't be ploughed
Gästboken i romanen Amorina: The guestbook in the novel Amorina
Gästgivaren Carl Wahlström byggde i slut: In the late 1850s the innkeeper Carl Wahlström built a new manor house, Karlslund, north of the church. It was demolished in 1939 when the airfield was expanded, and the site is now part of the churchyard.
Gästgivaren Carl Wahlström byggde på 185: In the 1850s the innkeeper Carl Wahlström built a new manor house, Carlslund, north of the church. It was pulled down in 1939 when the airfield was extended. In 1864 the owners donated 2,000 riksdaler for food and clothing for poor schoolchildren.
Gästgiveri med michelinstjärnor: A coaching inn with Michelin stars
Gästgiveriet som blev Lasse-Maja Wärdshu: The coaching inn that became Lasse-Maja Wärdshus
Gå Friidrottens väg mot Slottsskogsvalle: Walk Friidrottens väg to the Slottsskogsvallen stadium
Gå Friidrottens väg vid Slottsskogsvalle: Walk Friidrottens väg, the Athletics Walk, by Slottsskogsvallen
Gå förbi Havrekvarnen vid vattnet: Walk past Havrekvarnen, the oat mill by the water
Gå förbi Kanalhuset, glashuset som byggd: Walk past Kanalhuset – the glass building built for Hasselblad, where Swedish Television and Swedish Radio broadcast today – down to the Lundbystrand ferry stop (about 7 min). The old shipyard halls are now used for curling and handball.
Gå förbi Oscarsteatern och jazzklubben F: Stroll past Oscarsteatern and the Fasching jazz club
Gå genom Gamlestadens fabriker med mat o: Walk through Gamlestadens Fabriker, the old factories now full of food and design (4 min), and on to the SKF stop. The ball-bearing company was founded here in 1907, and the factory site has been its home for more than a hundred years.
Gå genom järnåldersgravfältet i Kyrkpark: Walk through the Iron Age burial ground in Kyrkparken
Gå in i Botaniska trädgården (2 min). De: Step into the Gothenburg Botanical Garden (2 min). It opened in 1923 and has a rock garden, a Japanese valley and glasshouses with thousands of plants.
Gå in i Slottsskogen (2 min) med djur oc: Head into Slottsskogen park (2 min), with its animals and ponds, and carry on to the Museum of Natural History (10 min), home to a stuffed blue whale from 1865. Return the same way.
Gå längs Haga Nygata (3 min) med små but: Stroll along Haga Nygata, Haga’s main street (3 min), lined with little shops and cafés, and try a giant cinnamon bun as big as a side plate. Carry on through Haga to Järntorget.
Gå längs kajen till spårvagnshållplatsen: Walk along the quay to the Lindholmen tram stop (about 6 min). Where ships were once built, you’ll now find Lindholmen Science Park and part of Chalmers University of Technology.
Gå ner i tunnelbanan och det känns som a: Head down into the metro and it's like stepping into a child's drawing. The artists Elis Eriksson and Gösta Wallmark decorated the station with pictures that look as if children drew them, inspired by memories of their own childhood. The station opened on 31 August 1975, along with the first stretch of the blue line, between T-Centralen and Hjulsta.
Gå ner mot Magelungen och Rödkinda: Walk down to Lake Magelungen and Rödkinda
Gå ner till Apelsinvillan vid Kottlasjön: Walk down to Apelsinvillan, the Orange Villa, by Lake Kottlasjön
Gå ner till Fiskhamnen: Walk down to Fiskhamnen, the fishing harbour
Gå ner till Klippan och Klippans värdshu: Walk down to Klippan and the Klippan inn (4 min), then on to the ferry landing. Here you’ll find the remains of the Gamla Älvsborg fortress, which Sweden bought back from the Danes in 1619.
Gå ner till Klippans värdshus: Walk down to Klippans värdshus, the Klippan inn
Gå nerför Pipmakartrappan mot Tanto: Walk down the Pipmakartrappan steps to Tanto
Gå på bio på Filmstaden Kista: Catch a film at Filmstaden Kista
Gå på bio på Möllan: Catch a film at the Möllan cinema
Gå runt i Härlanda park, det gamla fänge: Stroll round Härlanda park, the old prison
Gå runt i Härlanda park, före detta fäng: Walk round Härlanda park, once a prison
Gå till Allmänna gränd (2 min) och ta Dj: Walk to Allmänna gränd (2 min) and take the Djurgården ferry.
Gå till Annelunds gård, Per Henrik Lings: Walk to Annelunds gård, Per Henrik Ling's home
Gå till Bofills båge och Fatbursparken (: Walk to Bofill's Arch and Fatbursparken (3 min). The semicircular building was designed by the Spanish architect Ricardo Bofill and completed in 1992, on the spot where Lake Fatbursjön lay before it was filled in.
Gå till Brännö brygga (5 min). Sommartid: Walk to Brännö brygga, the jetty (5 min). In summer its open-air jetty dances are famous all over Gothenburg, and the island has lovely smooth rocks to swim from.
Gå till Cornelisparken (2 min), tillägna: Walk to Cornelisparken (2 min), dedicated to the singer-songwriter Cornelis Vreeswijk. On Tjärhovsgatan, Kafé 44 has been going since 1984 in the old Swedish bottle-cap factory.
Gå till Dieselverkstaden (2 min). Här by: Walk to Dieselverkstaden (2 min). Atlas Diesel built diesel engines here until 1951, and since 2002 the old workshop has housed a cultural centre, library, climbing wall and cinema. There’s even a test mine underneath the Sickla shopping district.
Gå till Filmstaden i Råsunda (2 min), dä: Walk to Filmstaden in Råsunda (2 min), where nearly 400 feature films were shot between 1920 and 1973 – a place forever linked with Ingmar Bergman.
Gå till Finnstugorna och Stallgrunden (5: Walk to Finnstugorna and Stallgrunden (5 min). The larger of the Finnish cottages was already here when the king bought Haga, and Stallgrunden is all that remains of Gustav III's Great Stable, which was never finished.
Gå till Götaplatsen och Poseidon (4 min): Walk to Götaplatsen and the Poseidon statue (4 min), with the Gothenburg Museum of Art, the Concert Hall and the City Theatre around the square. Then stroll down Avenyn, the city's grand avenue, to the Valand stop.
Gå till Hellasgården och Källtorpssjön (: Walk to Hellasgården and Lake Källtorpssjön (3 min). This is the start of Källtorpssjön runt, a five-kilometre loop around the lake marked with yellow dots.
Gå till Hotel Rival (2 min), som ägs av: Walk to Hotel Rival (2 min), owned by Abba's Benny Andersson and named after the old Rival cinema in the same building. In the middle of the square stands the fountain Tors fiske (Thor's Fishing).
Gå till Jakobs stege (4 min), 187 granit: Walk to Jakobs stege, Jacob's Ladder (4 min) – 187 granite steps down towards Lake Mälaren – and on to Bellmanskällan (5 min), by tradition the spring in Bellman's Fredman's Epistle No. 82.
Gå till Koppartälten (5 min), där Haga p: Walk to the Copper Tents (5 min), where the Haga Park Museum displays a large wooden model of Stora Haga palace, which Gustav III had planned to build.
Gå till Kulturhuset Bergsjön (5 min) vid: Walk to Kulturhuset Bergsjön (5 min) on Rymdtorget, a culture house built in 1970 with a library, music studio, artists' studios and an exhibition hall.
Gå till Mölndals kvarnby (8 min). Längs: Walk to Mölndals kvarnby, the old mill village (8 min). Water power from the rapids has driven mills and factories here for several hundred years, and today the village is a heritage area with a museum and cafés.
Gå till Plaskis och badbollen: Head to Plaskis, the paddling pool with the giant beach ball
Gå till Skansen (2 min), världens äldsta: Walk to Skansen (2 min), the world's oldest open-air museum, founded in 1891, with old farmsteads from all over Sweden and Nordic animals.
Gå till Soundtrade Studios på Råsundaväg: Walk to Soundtrade Studios at Råsundavägen 45 (3 min). This is where ABBA recorded most of The Album in 1977, when the studio was called Marcus Music.
Gå till Stadshuset och tornet (2 min). S: Walk to the City Hall and its tower (2 min). Opened in 1923, Stockholm City Hall hosts the Nobel Banquet in its Blue Hall, and from the tower you can look out over Riddarfjärden and Gamla stan, the Old Town.
Gå till Sveaplan med Gösta Silléns stens: Head to Sveaplan for Gösta Sillén's stone sculptures
Gå till Wallenbergs minnesmärke i Kappst: Visit the Wallenberg memorial in Kappsta nature reserve
Gå till luftvärnsställningen Käppalastäl: Walk to Käppalaställningen, the old anti-aircraft battery
Gå trapporna genom Medborgarhuset Trappa: Take the stairs through Trappan, the civic centre
Gå upp mot Thielska galleriet och minnes: Walk up towards Thielska galleriet, the Thiel Gallery, and the Gravitational Ripples memorial on the southern slope at Blockhusudden (short walk). Catch the bus back from the Thielska galleriet stop. The headland is named after a blockhouse from Gustav Vasa's time that guarded the entrance to the city.
Gå upp på Skinnarviksberget (4 min, uppf: Walk up Skinnarviksberget (4 min, uphill), the highest natural point in the inner city, with views over Riddarfjärden, the City Hall and Kungsholmen.
Gå upp till Skansen Lejonet (8 min), för: Climb up to Skansen Lejonet (8 min), a 17th-century fortress with a gilded lion on top, built to protect the city from attack from the east.
Gå uppför Kvastmakarbacken till trähusen: Walk up Kvastmakarbacken to the wooden houses on Åsöberget
Gå uppför Slottsbacken till Kungliga slo: Walk up Slottsbacken to the Royal Palace (2 min), completed in 1754 after the old Tre Kronor castle burned down in 1697. Carry on through the narrow lanes of Gamla stan, the Old Town, to Riddarhustorget (about 10 min).
Gå uppför till Keillers park (10 min, br: Walk up to Keillers park (10 min, steep but short). From the top of Ramberget hill you get one of the best views of Gothenburg and the river.
Gå uppför till Skansen Kronan (10 min) o: Walk up to Skansen Kronan (10 min) and enjoy the view over the city.
Gå ut på Allébron över Sickla kanal: Walk out onto Allébron, the bridge over Sickla canal
Gå ut på Mariebergsbron och titta över M: Step out onto Mariebergsbron bridge for the view over the Mariebergssundet strait
Gågator som blev galleria: Pedestrian streets that became a mall
Gång- och cykelbron över Sickla kanal ka: The footbridge and cycle bridge over Sickla Canal is also known as the Apaté Bridge, after the winning entry in an international architecture competition in 1998. It was completed in 2002 and won both the Swedish Steel Construction Prize and the European Steel Design Award in 2003.
Gång- och cykeltunneln under Råsundaväge: The pedestrian and cycle tunnel under Råsundavägen to Solparken appears in the film Beck – Den svaga länken (The Weak Link). You see part of the park on screen before the scene suddenly carries on in a completely different park.
Gångvägen hette först Viljo Nousiainens: The footpath was first named after Viljo Nousiainen. In 2011 the high jumper Patrik Sjöberg revealed in his autobiography that the coach, who was also his stepfather, had sexually abused him, and other athletes came forward with similar accounts. That September the path was renamed Friidrottens väg, the Athletics Path.
Gård och privat kyrkogård: A farm with its own cemetery
Gårdahallen byggdes 1930 som komplement: Gårdahallen was built in 1930 to complement the Stampen tram depot, which was demolished in 1986. The hall is about 90 metres long, with eight tracks. Since 2011 it has housed a public transport museum run by the tramway society Spårvägssällskapet Ringlinien.
The women's names given to the courtyards aren't made up. They come from women who lived in the crofts that once stood here, such as Amanda Östberg, Gerda Karlsson and Juliana Sjöberg. Behind Pennygången 49–63 you can still see croft foundations and a root cellar.
Gården Råsta har gett halva namnet åt Rå: Råsta farm gave half its name to Råsunda in Solna: Råsta plus Frösunda became Råsunda.
Gården Stora Fågelsången är från 1700-ta: Stora Fågelsången is an 18th-century farm on the western shore of Trekanten, a small lake. The City of Stockholm has owned it since 1963, and the old garden is now given over to allotments – though without the usual little allotment cottages. The City Museum has marked the farm blue, meaning it's considered of exceptional cultural and historical value. A little further on, the Essingeleden motorway roars past on the Blommensberg viaduct, almost skimming the roofs of Blommensbergsskolan school.
Gården består av en mangårdsbyggnad från: The farm is made up of a mid-18th-century manor house with a 1940s extension in matching style, an early-19th-century farmhouse with a storehouse, joined by a building brought from Älvsjö, and an outbuilding from 1915. Today the farm is divided into private homes.
Gården bland vildsvinen?: The farm among the wild boar?
Gården brann omkring 1680, och den nuvar: The farm burned down around 1680, and the present main house, with its hipped, double-pitched manor-style roof, is thought to date from the early 1700s. The wing is believed to be older. The main house was damaged by fire again in 1993 but has been restored.
Gården byggdes omkring 1830 av Anders We: The house was built around 1830 by Anders Westman. The name Margretelund probably comes from his wife, Sophia Margareta Westman.
Gården där Willys ligger: The farm where Willys now stands
Gården döpt efter en hustru: A farm named after a wife
Gården hade en vattenkvarn som drevs av: The farm had a watermill powered by the dammed Sätraån stream. The mill burned down in the late 1960s and only the foundation stones remain, but the miller's cottage still stands on its hillock.
Gården har kakelugnar från 1780-talet, 1: The house has tiled stoves from the 1780s, the 1830s and 1910 – plus one specially commissioned in 2009, decorated with oak leaves and acorns, the estate's emblem. The same motif adorns the gable of the Empire-inspired main house.
Gården har stått på Svenska byggnadsvård: The estate has been on the Swedish Building Conservation Society's "yellow list" of threatened heritage sites. The façade was restored by 2014, but work on the interior, begun in 2020, was put on hold in 2022 because of problems with the water and drainage.
Gården hette 1381 ”ruuddobodha”. Ett ”ru: In 1381 the farm was called "ruuddobodha". A "rudde" was a medieval word for cleared or cultivated land, so the name means something like "the hut by the new clearing". The farm still stands at Elfviksvägen 17, with Lidingö's only surviving statare cottage – housing for farm labourers paid in kind – from the 1850s.
Gården hette från början Andersta eller: The estate was originally called Andersta or Anderstad. The name changed when it passed to the Fleming family, through Henrik Klasson Fleming's marriage to Ebba Erlandsdotter Bååt. In the mid-1600s it became a manor with noble privileges, and by 1688 it had eleven crofts under it.
Gården hette från början Segerstorp. För: The farm was originally called Segerstorp. The first part may come from an old word for waterlogged ground, though there are also legends of Swedish victories (seger) over the Danes. When villa plots began to be divided up in the 1900s, the name was changed to Segeltorp.
Gården invigdes i februari 1945 som hem: The farm opened in February 1945 as a home and rural housekeeping school with room for 30 pupils aged 14 to 18. Over two years they learned domestic skills. The school was run by Samariterhemmet in Uppsala and closed in June 1971.
Gården kallades Stora Brevik för att ski: The farm was called Stora Brevik to tell it apart from Lilla Brevik at Rödstuguviken. From there a rowing ferry, paid for by the Banér family, crossed between Lidingö and Djursholm.
Gården ligger på gammal kulturmark. Rest: The farm stands on long-settled land. Remains of stone settings and Iron Age graves show there was an ancient village here, and signs tell the story of some of the settlement sites.
Gården låg där Willys ligger: Where Willys stands, the farm stood
Gården låg precis intill Järfälla kyrka: The farm stood right next to Järfälla's 12th-century church, and the area around the church had been the community's religious centre ever since the Bronze Age. During clearance work in 1989, a well-preserved house foundation was uncovered, complete with a hearth cairn and a doorstone.
Gården nämns första gången 1397 som Sion: The farm is first mentioned in 1397 as Siondae, later Siunda and Söndöö – in modern Swedish Sjöända, "lake's end", after the northern tip of Drevviken. Under Queen Kristina the name was changed to Sköndal, and the estate became one of her hunting lodges.
Gården nämns redan 1366, som Skärfwesätr: The farm is mentioned as early as 1366, as Skärfwesätra on Lidingö. At that time it belonged to Bo Jonsson (Grip), who in the second half of the 14th century bought up most of Lidingö.
Gården och värdshuset Sandsborg har gett: Sandsborg, an old farm and inn, has lent its name to both a cemetery and a metro station here in Gamla Enskede. A little further on is the Museum of the Visually Impaired, in premises that once belonged to De blindas tekniska fabrik, a workshop for blind people. Its collections trace the history of blind and partially sighted people in Sweden back to the late 1700s. And inside Skogskyrkogården, the Woodland Cemetery, is Almhöjden, a hill crowned with weeping elms that looks like something out of a Caspar David Friedrich painting.
Gården som brann och låg öde: The farm that burned and lay deserted
Gården som fick makens namn: The manor named after a husband
Gården som fick vika för flyget: The farm that made way for the airfield
Gården som nunnorna bytte bort: The farm the nuns traded away
Gården är en allmän park: The courtyard is a public park
Gården är en liten herrgård där södra fl: The farm is a small manor house whose south wing is the oldest part, recorded in 1756 as 'the new build'. It was one of several small properties split off from Hägersten farm that became summer retreats in the late 1700s.
Gården är uppkallad efter vinhandlaren W: The estate is named after the wine merchant Werner Groen, who, like several owners before him, was of Dutch descent. He bought the property in 1702 for just under 10,000 daler in copper coin. The name is pronounced with a guttural 'ch', roughly 'chroen'. The family only lived here in summer; for the rest of the year the gardener ran the place.
Gårdens förste ägare Claes Arrhén von Ka: The estate's first owner, Claes Arrhén von Kapfelman, married Catharina Christina Bellman, sister of the poet and songwriter Carl Michael Bellman, in 1763. That's why several of Bellman's songs are set on the estate and its grounds.
Gårdens förste ägare, tullkontrollören P: The estate's first owner, customs controller Petter Eriksson-Svedberg, built a main house here in 1775. He laid out a garden where he planted 100 oaks and more than 100 willows. Before him there was just a small croft on the site, called Ödesküre backstuga on a map from 1720.

The farm's first owner, the customs inspector Petter Eriksson-Svedberg, built the main house in 1775 and laid out a garden where he planted 100 oaks and more than 100 willows. Before that, only a small cottage stood here.
Gårdens glansperiod började när justitie: The estate's heyday began when Supreme Court justice Johan Henric Peterson bought it in 1812. His love of singing and music sometimes earned him the nickname "the Nightingale". Sweden's first pomologist, the fruit scientist Olof Eneroth, was also born here, in 1825.
Gårdens gula uthus byggdes 1818–1825, bl: The farm's yellow outbuildings were built in 1818–1825, among them a distillery for brännvin, Swedish aquavit, which was important until 1863. The stables gained a riding hall in 1981, and since 1999 the farm has hosted conferences and a restaurant.
Gårdens hus stod länge kvar och användes: The farm buildings stood for many years and were used as offices by the cemetery administration. When they were demolished in November 1957, rolls of hand-painted 18th-century wallpaper were found in the southern attic room.
Gårdens lilla smedja finns numera vid So: The farm's little smithy is now at Charlottenburg, Solna's local heritage farm. In the 1760s the croft Snåltäppan was renamed Frösundavik, and neighbouring Annelund is now a listed building. In 2013 Canon moved on to Telegrafgatan 4.
Gårdens rötter i järnåldern: A farm with Iron Age roots
Gårdens stenhus från 1801 fick hård krit: The farm's stone house from 1801 was savaged by the neighbour at Ekholmsnäs, who called it a “powder house” and thought it should be buried so that future generations would be spared such bad taste. The house still stands, with the year 1801 in wrought-iron wall anchors on the facade.
Gårdens äldre namn var Rothugget, en typ: The farm's older name was Rothugget, a term for a kind of land clearance. Under a contract from 1799, the tenant promised to turn Rothugget into a thoroughly good meadow within ten years.
Gårdsbyggnaden i empirstil är från börja: The Empire-style farmhouse dates from the early 19th century and is now blue-listed for its heritage value. Above it stood the stable, cowshed and henhouse, and the farm kept two horses, three cows, pigs and chickens. The City of Stockholm bought it in 1904 as a land reserve.
Gårdsten har vänt en trend. När det komm: Gårdsten is a neighbourhood that turned itself around. When the municipal housing company Gårdstensbostäder was set up in 1997, more than 800 of its roughly 2,200 flats were standing empty. The company put its office right in the middle of the area so it could work closely with tenants. The renovation of eastern Gårdsten won the Stora Samhällsbyggarpriset, one of Sweden's top urban development awards, in 2006, and in 2019 Gårdsten became the first neighbourhood to be taken off the police list of 'particularly vulnerable areas'.
Gåshaga nämns redan 1379 i ett bytesbrev: Gåshaga is mentioned as early as 1379 in a deed of exchange, as Gasahaga. Until the mid-1600s, the point where Gåshaga pier stands today was an islet of its own called Galten.
Gåva till en italiensk adelsman: A gift to an Italian nobleman
Gåvan till gamla kyrkan: A gift to the old church
Görvälns griftegård anlades 1966–1977 på: Görväln cemetery was laid out in 1966–1977 on old farmland and a wooded hill. At its highest point, a memorial grove nestles in the forest.
Görvälns griftegård ritades av landskaps: Görväln cemetery was designed by the landscape architect Per Friberg and laid out between 1966 and 1977 on old farmland and a wooded hill. A 300-metre watercourse with eleven waterfalls runs down to a large reflecting pool. In 2017 a Muslim section with 220 coffin graves opened. Nearby is Görväln school, in use from 1896 to 1939 – the school building is still standing.
Gösta Mittag-Leffler levde som en storma: Gösta Mittag-Leffler lived like a grandee and often threw parties at the villa. But the financial crash of the 1920s and the Kreuger crash of 1932 swallowed up his fortune, and the institute only got going in 1969, on the initiative of Lennart Carleson.
Göta artilleriregemente flyttade in 1895: The Göta Artillery Regiment moved in in 1895 and stayed until 1962, when the Göta Air Defence Regiment took over until it relocated to Halmstad in 1994. That brought a century of military life at Kviberg to an end.
Göta artilleriregemente hade sedan 1798: Since 1798 the Göta Artillery Regiment had been based at Ekelundstorget – today's Kaserntorget – in the heart of the city. On 1 October 1895 the Kviberg barracks opened, and the regiment moved out here.
Göta landsväg gick här: The old Göta road ran here
Göta landsväg har anor åtminstone från m: Göta landsväg dates back at least to the Middle Ages, but the path was probably worn into the ground as early as the Bronze Age. Before Stockholm was founded, the ancient Tingsvägen ran here to Svartlöten, where assemblies were held each spring and autumn.
Göta landsvägs kurva syns än: The curve of Göta landsväg is still visible
Göta segelsällskap började arrendera Jun: The Göta sailing club began leasing the Jungfruholmarna islets in 1915 and bought them in 1936. The clubhouse was built in 1955. The islands lie about six nautical miles into Lake Mälaren from Stockholm.
Göta älv var en gång kantad av stora var: The Göta älv river was once lined with great shipyards. This route takes you by river ferry between Eriksberg, Lindholmen and Lundby, where the old shipyard halls are now offices, sports halls and TV studios.
Götalandsvägen följer ungefär den uråldr: Götalandsvägen roughly follows the ancient Göta landsväg highway. When the Western Main Line opened in 1860, the Lerkrogen inn stood at the crossing. Two tracks ran under the 1910s bridge with its SJ medallion; today six tracks pass under the current bridge from 1967.
Götas Vänner fick Partille kommuns kultu: Götas Vänner won Partille Municipality's culture prize in 2007 for its work with Göta Bio, the local cinema. Since 2014 the films have been shown digitally.
Göteborg Energi lät allmänheten tävla om: Göteborg Energi held a public competition to name it, and the jury chose Nya Solevi. The name plays both on the sun (‘sol’) and on the debate over the new and old Ullevi stadiums.
Göteborg Energi utlyste en namntävling f: Göteborg Energi held a competition to name the solar park. The jury picked Nya Solevi, a play on both the debate over the new and old Ullevi stadiums and on 'sol', the Swedish for sun.
Göteborg Energi held a competition to name the solar park. The jury chose Nya Solevi – a play on the debates over new and old Ullevi, Gothenburg's famous stadiums, and on sol, the sun.
Göteborg byggdes för att försvaras. Följ: Gothenburg was built to be defended. Follow the traces of the redoubts on the hills, the moat around the inner city and the Gamla Älvsborg fortress at the mouth of the river.
Göteborgare älskar att ge byggnader smek: Gothenburgers love giving buildings nicknames. The Opera is known as Ackordcentralen, the fountain at Götaplatsen as Blötaplatsen ("the Wet Square") or the Car Wash, and the Karlatornet skyscraper as both Gylfen and the Glennpire State Building.
Gothenburgers love giving places nicknames. The footpath between Dragspelsgatan and Pianogatan in Västra Frölunda is known as Klavertrampet – roughly ‘the piano bash’ – although its real name is Spinettstigen. The local tower blocks have been dubbed Lösgommarna (the False Teeth), Käppen (the Walking Stick) and Kommandobryggorna (the Bridges).
Göteborgarnas smeknamn finns även här i: Gothenburg's love of nicknames reaches out here to Västra Frölunda too. The footpath between Dragspelsgatan and Pianogatan is known as Klavertrampet ("the piano-stomp"), a long three-storey block is Käppen ("the walking stick"), and some of the tower blocks go by Lösgommarna ("the false teeth") and Kommandobryggorna ("the ship's bridges").
Göteborgs Kex grundades i Kungälv 1888,: Göteborgs Kex was founded in Kungälv in 1888, and its biscuits were baked here right up until production moved to Riga at the end of 2022. From 1909 to 1982 the ABC factories made sports and leisure gear here too, including ice skates and tents.
Göteborgs botaniska trädgård öppnade 192: Gothenburg Botanical Garden opened in 1923 and is one of the larger botanical gardens in Europe. It has a rock garden, a Japanese valley and greenhouses full of thousands of plants. Across the road is Slottsskogen, the city's big park.
Göteborgs fattigvård låg från 1816 i för: From 1816 Gothenburg's poor relief was housed in dilapidated wooden buildings on Smedjegatan known as the Holtermanska barackerna – the Holterman barracks. That's where the word “Bracka” comes from, which became a nickname for the city's poorhouses.
Göteborgs första barnsjukhus öppnade 185: Gothenburg's first children's hospital opened in 1859 on Östra Hamngatan and moved to Haga in 1866. From 1909 it was at Sahlgrenska, and in 1973 it moved to Östra Hospital. It was named the Queen Silvia Children's Hospital in 1999.

Gothenburg's first children's hospital opened on Östra Hamngatan in 1859 and moved to Haga in 1866. In 1909 the Annedal Clinic was built at Sahlgrenska, and in 1973 the children's department moved again, this time to the new Östra Hospital.
Göteborgs stad köpte Lärjeholm 1895 för: The City of Gothenburg bought Lärjeholm in 1895 to secure its drinking water. Beneath the farmland lies a huge bed of sand that filters water from the river naturally.
Göteborgs stad köpte gården 1895 för att: The City of Gothenburg bought the farm in 1895 to safeguard its drinking water. Underground lies a large bed of sand that naturally filters water from the river. As early as the 18th century the farm had ponds stocked with crucian carp, bream and carp.
Göteborgs stad tackade 1874 nej till att: In 1874 the City of Gothenburg turned down the chance to buy the Tingstadsvassen reed beds at ten öre per square foot – yet two years later it decided to buy the area for 300,000 kronor. Nearby are two veteran vessels: the sailing ship Isolda from 1902, the last Swedish merchant sailing ship in ocean trade, and the tug Sven from 1897, built as an icebreaking steam tug.
Göteborgs stad tog över gården 1963, och: The City of Gothenburg took over the estate in 1963, and it has featured on the Swedish Building Conservation Society's list of threatened sites. The façade was restored by 2014, but work on the interior was put on hold in 2022.
Göteborgs stadsmuseum i Ostindiska huset: Gothenburg City Museum in the East India House
Göteborgsoperan står ungefär där länscel: The Gothenburg Opera stands roughly where the county jail used to be, a prison that opened in 1857. From Lilla Bommen harbour, cargo and passenger boats once sailed all the way to Stockholm and Norrköping, by way of the Göta älv river, the Göta Canal and the lakes. Outside the opera house, water trickles down Källan, the Spring, a stone sculpture by Bård Breivik from 1994.
Göteborgsregionens första egnahemsområde: The Gothenburg region's first owner-built housing area grew up at Sörgården in 1902. The municipality couldn't afford to plan it, so the houses went up in all sorts of styles, scattered here and there. There were no streets, no electricity, no water and no sewers.
Göteborgsvägen var länge en viktig hande: For many years Göteborgsvägen was the main shopping street for the whole of Partille. Once the Allum shopping centre opened, Partille Bokhandel, the local bookshop, began losing customers, and in 2012 it moved into Gothenburg. It finally closed there in April 2013.
Güettler var en av de ledande inom den a: Güettler was one of the leading names in the folk-romantic architecture of the early 1900s, and he also designed Högloftet and Nyloftet at Skansen. The Laurin villa and Villa Tallom in Stocksund have been singled out as two of the most interesting villas in that style.
HSB byggde 1 548 lägenheter här 1961–196: Between 1961 and 1966 the housing co-op HSB built 1,548 flats here in four semicircular blocks. The planner Sune Lindström saw the buildings as large-scale sculptures, and Grindtorp has been called perhaps the best-known example of the new monumentalism of the 1960s.
HSB byggde 1 548 lägenheter i Grindtorp: Housing cooperative HSB built 1,548 flats at Grindtorp between 1961 and 1966, in four semicircular blocks, the tallest ten storeys high. Town planner Sune Lindström liked to think of them as huge sculptures with sweeping lines, and Grindtorp has been called the best-known example of Sweden's new monumentality in the 1960s.
HSB byggde 1 548 lägenheter i fyra halvc: Between 1961 and 1966 the housing co-op HSB built 1,548 flats here in four semicircular blocks. Sune Lindström liked to think of buildings as large sculptures with sweeping lines, and Grindtorp has been called perhaps the best-known example of Sweden's new monumentalism of the 1960s.
HSB byggde 1961–1966 hela 1 548 lägenhet: Between 1961 and 1966 the housing co-operative HSB built no fewer than 1,548 flats in Grindtorp, in four semicircular blocks of up to ten storeys. The town planner Sune Lindström liked to think of buildings as large-scale sculptures with long, sweeping lines. Grindtorp has been called perhaps the best-known example of the new monumentality of 1960s Sweden.
HSB köpte marken på Stora Billingen i mi: The housing cooperative HSB bought the land on Stora Billingen in the mid-1990s. Once every appeal had been rejected in 2006, work began on 50 houses here.
HSB köpte varvsområdet 1997 och byggde F: The housing association HSB bought the shipyard site in 1997 and built Finnboda Hamn from a competition entry by Nyréns architects. The old joinery, the steam-engine workshop and the canteen now house flats, offices and shops. Finnboda hamn is also a stop for the Sjövägen commuter boat.
HSB:s bostadsrättsförening City köpte ma: HSB's City housing cooperative bought the land in June 1955. Building began in 1958, and the first residents moved in in February 1959. The area includes the eight 17-storey tower blocks.
Hack Kampmann fick fria händer och ritad: Hack Kampmann was given a free hand and designed low buildings of glass, render and sheet metal around a square with a pond. City commissioner Walfrid Frank praised the architects for abandoning sky-high ambitions and returning to a human scale.

Hack Kampmann was given a free hand and designed low-rise centre buildings in glass, render and sheet metal around a square with a pond. City commissioner Walfrid Frank praised the architects for having 'abandoned the sky-storming and returned to the human scale'.
Haga Nygata och jättekanelbullar: Haga Nygata and giant cinnamon buns
Haga gård nämns redan 1331 bland Strängn: Haga gård appears as early as 1331 among the properties of Strängnäs Cathedral. In 1550 King Gustav Vasa gave the Vårby estate, including the small farm of Haga, to his secretary Clement Hansson.
Haga parkmuseum i Koppartälten: Haga Park Museum in the Copper Tents
Hagahuset inspirerades av Gio Pontis Pir: Hagahuset was inspired by Gio Ponti's Pirelli Tower in Milan. After the county council moved out it became an ordinary office block, and following a renovation in 2017–2018 it's now a hotel. Both Hotel Gio and the restaurant Mama Gio are named after Ponti.
Hagahuset är inspirerat av Gio Pontis sa: Hagahuset was inspired by Gio Ponti's Pirelli Tower in Milan, built around the same time. It consists of an eleven-storey tower and a five-storey wing, faced with pale brick. A bronze sculpture by Stig Blomberg stands by the main entrance.
Hagakyrkan byggdes efter engelska mönste: Hagakyrkan was built from English pattern drawings obtained by David Carnegie, making it one of Sweden's first Gothic Revival churches. The doorways and windows are framed in sandstone from Edinburgh.
Hagakyrkan invigdes 1859 och ligger vid: Hagakyrkan, the Haga Church, was consecrated in 1859 and stands at the edge of Haga, one of Gothenburg's oldest districts. Haga Nygata, Haga's main street, is lined with little shops and cafés – and this is where you'll find the famous giant cinnamon buns, as big as a side plate.
Hagaparken börjar nästan här. Gustav III: Hagaparken park starts almost right here. Gustav III had Övre Haga built as an inn in 1788–1789, with two kitchens and three dining rooms. Haga Trädgård is known from Bellman's song 'Fjäriln vingad syns på Haga' – 'The winged butterfly is seen at Haga' – and fittingly, the Butterfly House moved into one of its greenhouses in 1989. For a view, climb Frösundatoppen, about 72 metres above sea level.
Hagaviken är upp till 13 meter djup, och: Hagaviken is up to 13 metres deep, and the boundary between Huddinge and Botkyrka municipalities runs right down the middle of the bay. The name comes from Haga farm, an outlying farm belonging to Vårby manor.
Hagens kapell ritades av Yngve Rasmussen: Hagen Chapel was designed by Yngve Rasmussen and built in 1917. On 20 January 1918 it burnt to the ground, but it was rebuilt and consecrated in 1919.
Hagens kapell was designed by Yngve Rasmussen and completed in 1917. On 20 January 1918 the chapel burned to the ground, but it was rebuilt and consecrated in 1919.
Hagge Geigerts program började som Somma: Hagge Geigert's TV show started life as Sommarkväll från Långedrags brygga, "Summer evening on Långedrag jetty", in 1973–74, and Georg Rydeberg was his very first guest. Carin Mannheimer had her breakthrough here with Lära för livet in 1977 and later made the series Svenska hjärtan here too.
Hagstaeken hade en stamomkrets på 680 ce: The Hagsta oak had a girth of 680 centimetres and was protected as early as 1933. It was so well known that a bus stop was named Eken, "the Oak", after it. The stop was removed in 2012.
Hagsätra centrum invigdes 1960 efter bar: Hagsätra's shopping centre opened in 1960 after just a year of building work – the same year the metro arrived – and cost 25 million kronor in the money of the day. Its best-known feature is “Barnet med käpphästen”, The Child with the Hobby Horse, a copper sculpture by Marie Stenqvist. And if you need some greenery, Hagsätraskogen is close by – a forest that in 2021 became Stockholm's eleventh nature reserve.
Hagsätra centrum ritades av Hack Kampman: Hagsätra's centre was designed by Hack Kampmann, who was given a free hand and chose low facades of glass, render and sheet metal around a square with a pond. City property commissioner Walfrid Frank praised the architects for abandoning sky-high ambitions and returning to a human scale.
Hagsätra kyrka i torgets södra hörn ligg: Hagsätra church, in the southern corner of the square, is in the building put up for the Focus cinema in 1960. The chapel opened in 1992, and the cinema carried on in its shrunken auditorium until 2005.

Hagsätra kyrka, in the southern corner of the square, occupies a building that started life as the Focus cinema, opened in 1960. The chapel was consecrated in 1992, and the cinema carried on in a much-reduced auditorium until 2005. There used to be a petrol station under the square, too.

Hagsätra Church, in the southern corner of the square, occupies the building put up for the Focus cinema, which opened in 1960. The chapel was consecrated in 1992, and the cinema carried on in a much-reduced auditorium until 2005.
Haketjärnen ligger nästan 99 meter över: Haketjärnen lake lies almost 99 metres above sea level. Water from here flows through three streams and reaches the sea 16 kilometres later, via the Säveån river.
Hakon Ahlberg ritade församlingshuset i: Hakon Ahlberg designed the parish hall in typical 1920s Classicism, with an archway supported by Corinthian columns. Above the inner side of the portico is a fresco by Jurgen Wrangel depicting "The Battle of Brännkyrka 1519".
Hakon Ahlberg, Sven Backström och Leif R: The houses were designed by Hakon Ahlberg, Sven Backström and Leif Reinius. Abessinien in Hjorthagen had been criticised for its rigid straight lines, so here the functionalist boxes were placed a little more freely across the terrain.
Hallarna byggdes på ett gärde som en gån: The exhibition halls were built on a field that was once Lake Brännkyrkasjön. King Gustav VI Adolf opened the complex in 1971. The name Älvsjömässan caught on among locals, but the company was never actually called that.
The hall hasn’t only been used for tennis. Louis Armstrong, the Beatles and the Rolling Stones have all played here, and it has hosted professional boxing with the likes of Ingemar Johansson and Bosse Högberg.
Hallen med hajfena: The hall with a shark fin
Hallen planerades först i Tallkrogen, me: The sports hall was first planned for Tallkrogen, but those plans were scrapped in 2016. Ground was broken in Gubbängen on 15 June 2018, and the hall opened on 24 August 2020 at a cost of SEK 157 million.
Hallen som blev bostäder: A sports hall turned into homes
Hallunda var en levande jordbruksbygd än: Hallunda was a thriving farming area right up until the early 1970s, when the Million Programme – Sweden's huge state housing drive – arrived and Botkyrkastaden was built on the farmland. Hallunda manor, an 18th-century manor house nearby, was left out of the town plan, though, and it's still privately owned – one of the few old manor estates in the Stockholm area that is. Next to it lies a large Iron Age burial ground.
Hallundakyrkan från 1978 har gudstjänste: Hallunda church, built in 1978, holds services in Swedish, English and Urdu, one of Pakistan's official languages. Since 2011 there's also been a group for Spanish speakers.
Hallundaröset är fem till sex meter högt: Hallundaröset, the Hallunda cairn, is five to six metres high and about 35 metres across. It was built on a natural rocky knoll, which makes it all the more imposing. The cairn has never been excavated, so any graves are probably still in place on its sides or at its foot.
Halva Göteborg är en ö: Half of Gothenburg is an island
Hammargården ligger på sydöstra Färingsö: Hammargården lies in south-eastern Färingsö, and its small houses were once staff homes for the youth reform school that stood here. Just to the south, Lullehovsbron bridge crosses Lullehovssundet, a strait in Lake Mälaren just over 200 metres wide and about seven metres deep in the middle. At its southern end lies the little island of Kaninholmen, Rabbit Island. The bridge and the strait both take their name from the hamlet of Lullehov on Lindö.
Hammarkullen är känt för sin karneval, s: Hammarkullen is known for its carnival, which fills the district with music, dancing and colourful costumes every year. The stop is deep inside the rock, and you reach it by a long escalator.
Hammarkullens kyrka var en vandringskyrk: Hammarkullen Church was a travelling church. At the same time, a church that was practically identical was built in Länsmansgården.
Hammarkulletorget byggdes 1971 efter rit: Hammarkulletorget, the square, was built in 1971 to designs by White Architects and was given a new colour scheme and look in 1997. The tram stops here at what's known as Gothenburg's only underground station.
Hammarkulletorget was built in 1971 to designs by White arkitekter. In 1997 the square was rebuilt, with both its colours and its shape changed.
Hammarkulletorget byggdes 1971 och ritad: Hammarkulletorget was built in 1971 to a design by White arkitekter. When it was remodelled in 1997, the square got both a new colour scheme and a new shape.
Hammarkulletorget ritades av White arkit: Hammarkulletorget was designed by White Arkitekter. Today it's managed by the municipal company Göteborgslokaler.
Hamnbadet har både söt- och saltvattenba: Hamnbadet, the harbour baths, has both freshwater and saltwater pools. The salt water is pumped up from the wedge of seawater that lies along the bottom of the Göta älv – a clever technical fix that gives Gothenburg a clean city-centre pool.
Hamnen som var en fjord: A harbour that was once a fjord
