Hamninloppet där Marinstaden ligger kall: The harbour inlet where Marinstaden now lies was once known as the bay of dead ships, crammed with decommissioned vessels and rusty barges. The wrecks have been replaced by floating homes on unsinkable concrete platforms – the villas were built in Tallinn and shipped here on barges.

Handbollsklubben IK Sävehofs dam- och he: The women's and men's teams of handball club IK Sävehof play their home matches at Partille Arena. The arena replaced Partillebohallen, which was demolished in April 2017.
Handbollsspelaren Magnus Wislander, utse: The handball player Magnus Wislander, voted the world's best of the 20th century, has links to Tuve. So does Anette Börjesson, who played for Sweden in both football and badminton.
Handelshögskolan grundades 1909 som Sver: Handelshögskolan, the Stockholm School of Economics, was founded in 1909 as Sweden's first business school, and its main building on Sveavägen was designed by Ivar Tengbom in 1925. Its researchers have helped shape what economists call the Stockholm School. Around the corner is Betlehemskyrkan, Bethlehem Church. Its predecessor from 1840, near Hötorget, was Sweden's first free-church building. That church was demolished in 1953, and the new one was consecrated here in 1956.
Handelshögskolan i Göteborg var den förs: The School of Business, Economics and Law in Gothenburg was the first in Sweden to be accredited by all three bodies – EQUIS, AMBA and AACSB – known as the Triple Crown. The school has around 160 partner universities around the world.
Handelshögskolan öppnade den 1 oktober 1: The School of Business opened on 1 October 1923 with just 11 students in its first year. By 1932 there were over 100, and by autumn 1959 over 500 – 17 of them women.
Handelsträdgård blev spårvagnsstall: From market garden to tram depot
Handelsträdgård och en vit villa: A market garden and a white villa
Hangar 1 stod klar 1942 och beställdes a: Hangar 1 was completed in 1942, commissioned by AB Aerotransport, the forerunner of SAS. During the Second World War, however, the great hall was used for several years to build the FFVS J 22 fighter plane instead.

Hangar 1 was completed in 1942, commissioned by AB Aerotransport, the forerunner of SAS. During the Second World War, though, the great hall was used for several years to build the FFVS J 22 fighter plane instead.
Hangar 3 från 1948 byggdes för SAS stora: Hangar 3 was built in 1948 for SAS's big Boeing Stratocruisers, and its doors ran on rails. Today they're locked half-open and serve as glazed entrances. Inside you can see the roof's 1,500-tonne steel structure, and the control panel for the doors is still on the central pillar.
Hangar 3 invigdes 1948 och mätte 151 gån: Hangar 3 opened in 1948 and measured 151 by 62 metres. It was built for SAS's big Boeing Stratocruisers, and its enormous doors ran on rails and were powered by overhead lines. It closed as early as 1962, when SAS moved to Arlanda.
Hangar 3 invigdes 1948 och var Brommas s: Opened in 1948, Hangar 3 was Bromma's largest at 151 by 62 metres, built for SAS's big Boeing Stratocruisers. The doors ran on rails and were powered by overhead lines. Today they're fixed partly open, with glazed entrances.
Hangar 3 lades ner redan 1962 när SAS fl: Hangar 3 was shut as early as 1962, when SAS moved to Arlanda. Linjeflyg's old LIN logo is still on the facade of Hangar 2, and inside Hangar 3 the control panel for the door machinery remains on the central pillar.
Hangaren blev ispalats: The hangar that became an ice palace
Haninge kulturpark: Haninge kulturpark, the Haninge culture park
Harestads kyrka ligger ett stenkast häri: Harestad Church is a stone's throw from here, in the church village of Kyrkeby. The village was classed as a small locality in 1995, but it has since had fewer than 50 residents and lost that status. So the village may be too small for the statistics, but the church still stands, in Harestad parish – part of Kungälv municipality since 1971.
Harestads socken ligger vid kusten sydvä: Harestad parish lies on the coast south-west of Kungälv and takes in small villages such as Flateby, Toreby and Kornhall. In 2000 it had 951 residents. Its parish church, Harestad Church, stands in the church village of Kyrkeby, a little way off. The parish used to belong to the old hundred, or district, of Inlands Södre, and it has been part of Kungälv municipality since 1971.
Hasse och Tage sjöng om Rågsved: Hasse and Tage sang about Rågsved
Hasselblad och Mankell vilar här: Resting place of Hasselblad and Mankell
Havet kring Öckerö påverkas av sötvatten: The sea around Öckerö is fed with fresh water from the Göta älv and Nordre älv rivers, making it an important nursery for young fish and lobsters.
Havrekvarnen från 1927–1928, ritad av Ar: The oat mill of 1927–1928, designed by Artur von Schmalensee, was one of Sweden's first functionalist industrial buildings. For the first time, the building's function was put on show outside rather than hidden behind the facade. By 1929 it was already turning out rolled oats and oat drinks.
Havrekvarnen var en av Sveriges första f: Havrekvarnen, the oat mill, was one of Sweden's first functionalist industrial buildings. For the first time, its function was put on show on the outside instead of being hidden behind the facade. Fifteen silo tubes stand along the east side.
Havsguden Poseidon av Carl Milles har va: Carl Milles's sea god Poseidon has watched over the square since 1931 and is one of Gothenburg's best-loved landmarks. Gathered around him are the Gothenburg Museum of Art, the Concert Hall, the City Theatre and the City Library, the city's most visited cultural venue. In Götapalatset, the Göta cinema opened in 1936, closed in 1997 and was given a new lease of life in 2015. And don't miss Peter Linde's bronze statue of the writer Karin Boye.
Hazelius hade oavlönade medhjälpare, \"s: Hazelius had unpaid helpers – 'procurers' – all over the country. To one of them in Dalarna he wrote in 1876: 'Where you have to pay, haggle as hard as you can.' The letters are still in the museum's archive.
Hedbergs malmgård byggdes 1711 och hade: Hedberg's country house was built in 1711 and had a large garden with fruit trees, stables, a sheep shed, two summerhouses, a duck pond and a greenhouse. In the 1950s everything except the main house was torn down. When it was renovated in the 1980s, the house had stood unchanged for more than 200 years.
Hedqvists entrébyggnad har fasader av gu: Hedqvist's entrance building has yellow-painted board-and-batten facades with green-painted woodwork. The buildings are 'green-listed' by the Stockholm City Museum as culturally valuable. Following a residents' proposal in 2007, the long-closed changing wings were restored.
Hela 58 arkitektkontor deltog i tävlinge: No fewer than 58 architecture firms entered the competition to design Karlatornet. It was won by the American practice Skidmore, Owings and Merrill – the people behind One World Trade Center – with an entry called Polstjärnan, the Pole Star.
Hela Bergshamra ligger i Nationalstadspa: The whole of Bergshamra lies within the Royal National City Park. The land for the Kungshamra student housing was donated by King Gustaf VI Adolf – hence the name, ‘King's Hamra’. The 1951 water tower by Edsviken bay is a landmark visible from far around, and on Pipers väg stands Övre Karlsro, also known as Carl Malmsten's house.
Hela begravningsplatsen omges av ett 3,6: The whole cemetery is enclosed by a 3.6-kilometre black-painted cast-iron fence. The water basins are decorated with ships and have spouts shaped like dolphins, and the information pillars were designed by Gunnar Asplund.
Hela huset eller bara hatten: The whole mill, or just its cap
Hela huset vrids mot vinden: The whole building turns to the wind
Hela kommundelen har fått sitt namn efte: The whole district is named after Breviks gård, a manor whose roots go back to the 14th century. Its last main building was pulled down in 1987, and Brevik centre, with its stop on the Lidingöbanan light railway, stands there now. Next door is Blocket, one of Lidingö's oldest apartment buildings, built in 1914–1915. And in 1905 the owner of the manor offered to pay for a small primary school in the area out of his own pocket.
Hela kommundelen har fått sitt namn från: The whole district is named after the farm a couple of hundred metres away. Flemingsbergs gård, once spelt Flemmingsbergs gård, is a manor and former estate with a history going back to the 15th century. On the other side is the industrial area, where LM Ericsson's central warehouse was in its day quite a sight thanks to its automation.
Hela kvarnen vrids mot vinden: The whole mill turns to the wind
Hela linjen skulle bemannas av cirka 2 7: The whole line was to be manned by around 2,700 men, mostly from the Landstorm – conscripts over 32 armed with ordinary rifles. This was before armoured vehicles existed, and when machine guns were still rare.
Hela museet ryms på cirka 50 kvadratmete: The entire museum fits into about 50 square metres. When the building was renovated, the flat was kept as close to its original state as possible and kitted out with period fittings salvaged from other flats. Everything on display was collected by the Kortedala Museum Society.
Hela området gav vattenkraft åt Nacka br: The whole area supplied water power to Nacka bruk, an industrial works with roots in Gustav Vasa’s forge from 1558. The lakes were linked by dug canals and dammed so there would be enough water all year round.
Hela området vänder sig mot solen och Mä: The whole area turns towards the sun and Lake Mälaren, while the long block on the north side is designed as a tall screen, like a windbreak. There are 411 flats and terraced houses here.
Hela området är en lekplats: The whole area is a playground
Hela södra skärgården är bilfri, men på: The whole southern archipelago is car-free, but on Kössö all motor vehicles are banned – even moped trucks – and bicycles aren't welcome either. So residents ferry their belongings between the boat and their homes by wheelbarrow. You'll always see a whole fleet of them parked by the steamer jetty.
Hela vägen ut genom Majorna, förbi Älvsb: All the way out through Majorna, past the Älvsborg Bridge and the Långedrag marina.
Hela östra sidan upptas av Gröna Lund. P: The whole of the eastern side is taken up by Gröna Lund amusement park. On the western side stood its old rival, the Nöjesfältet funfair, where temporary exhibitions are sometimes held today.
Helenelunds station öppnade 1922 efter k: Helenelund station opened in 1922 after residents of the growing villa suburb campaigned for it, taking the matter all the way to the government. Today the commuter train takes ten minutes into central Stockholm.
Helga minns man och söner: Helga remembers her husband and sons
Helgad åt sjöfartens helgon: Dedicated to the patron saint of seafarers
Helgen innan Södra länken invigdes den 2: The weekend before the Södra länken road tunnel opened on 24 October 2004, a tunnel race was held. In all, 20,000 runners and inline skaters seized the chance to whizz through the tunnel before the cars arrived.
Helige Savas serbisk-ortodoxa kyrka är h: The Serbian Orthodox Church of Saint Sava is dedicated to Serbia's national saint, who founded the Serbian Orthodox Church in 1219, and it's the cathedral for the church's Scandinavian diocese. Nearby is Skagershuset, a block of flats with a wooden façade that was named Stockholm's Building of the Year in 2014. It's named after Skagersvägen, the street, which in turn takes its name from Lake Skagern on the border between the provinces of Värmland and Västergötland.
Helige kung Stefan Dečanskis kyrka, Göte: Church of the Holy King Stefan Dečanski, Gothenburg
Hellasgården har fått namn efter idrotts: Hellasgården is named after the Hellas sports club, founded in 1899 by the clergyman Ernst Klefbeck. Around the lake people played football and even water polo. The present main lodge was built by the club's own members and opened in 1945.
Hellasgården är en frisksportanläggning: Hellasgården is an outdoor sports centre and clubhouse on Lake Källtorpssjön, in the heart of the Nacka Reserve. It's the start and finish of Källtorpssjön runt, the yellow trail – a five-kilometre walk marked with yellow dots and arrows. On the north-western shore of the lake is Stengärdet, old farmland enclosed by a stone wall that's protected as an ancient monument.
Hembygdsmuseet ligger i Hässelby villast: The local history museum is housed in Hässelby villastad's old municipal hall from 1925, which was in use until 1949, when the small town became part of Stockholm. The building also held a police station and a post office.
Hembygdsmuseum i trettio år: A local history museum for thirty years
Hemgården på Östermalmsgatan blev 1906 S: In 1906, Hemgården on Östermalmsgatan became Sweden's first collective housing block. A shared central kitchen was meant to free up time so that residents, young women in particular, could go out to work. The building went up on the site of the 18th-century Brandel sugar refinery, which had also done duty as a cholera hospital. Nearby was Palmgrenska samskolan, the first school in Scandinavia to teach girls and boys together all the way to the upper secondary leaving exam.
Hemgårdens matsal serverade tre mål om d: The dining room at Hemgården served three meals a day, but you could also phone down on the internal line and have your food sent up to your flat in the central lift. The building is said to have been the first with double-glazed coupled windows and central heating – though the bedrooms were given tiled stoves just in case.

Hemliga markköp via bulvan: Secret land deals through a front

Hemmanet hette från början Skår, men 165: The farm was originally called Skår, but in 1651 the Crown gave it to Gothenburg's military commandant, Nils Påfve – later ennobled as Påfvenfelt – and it was renamed Påvelund. The timbered double cottage from the 1770s was lived in right up until 1906.
Hemmet bland askarna: The home among the ash trees
Hennigs svärson Bruno Wendel byggde en s: Hennig's son-in-law, Bruno Wendel, built himself a white, castle-like wooden villa north of the factories. Since 1908 it has housed Wendelsberg folk high school, an adult education college with its own theatre stage.
Hennigs svärson Bruno Wendel ledde fabri: Hennig's son-in-law Bruno Wendel ran the factories for many years and built himself a white, castle-like wooden villa just north of them. Since 1908 it has been home to Wendelsberg folk high school, which also runs its own theatre stage.
Henrik Palme köpte Svalnäs 1883, sex år: Henrik Palme bought Svalnäs in 1883, six years before he became the driving force behind the Djursholm garden city. He built a new main house and a barn for nearly 70 cows, and lived here until his death in 1932.
Henriksdalsringens borglika siluett syns: The castle-like silhouette of Henriksdalsringen can be seen from far and wide, and its ochre facades were chosen to match Södermalm. Locals call the area Henkan, or less often Dasslocket – 'the toilet lid' – because it sits right on top of the sewage works inside the rock.
Heron City var tänkt som en stor nöjesan: Heron City was planned as a big entertainment complex with a casino, bowling and restaurants, among other things. In 2017 AMC bought Filmstaden's owners, so the cinema is once again owned by AMC. Two of the screens have 500 seats each.
Herrestaskolan stod klar i januari 2016: Herrestaskolan was completed in January 2016 and is the first large school in modern-day Sweden built entirely of solid timber. The roof carries 1,400 square metres of solar panels, and inside there's a dance studio, a big library and a sports hall with spectator seating.
Herrey gick här: A Herrey went to school here

Herrgård med brutet tak: A manor with a mansard roof
Herrgård, sopstation och trädskola: Manor, refuse station and tree nursery
Herrgården Lilla Frösunda från 1700-tale: Lilla Frösunda is an 18th-century manor house whose owners included the gardener Anders Lundström. The Swedish state used the main building as an officers' mess until the late 1980s. When Canon moved to Frösunda in 2001, the company brought in the architects Tengboms, who designed its office on Gustav III:s boulevard to echo Canon's high-tech image.
Herrgården Riddersvik ligger vid Mälaren: Riddersvik manor stands on the shore of Lake Mälaren, beside Lövstafjärden bay, and you can still explore Tempeludden headland and the English Park, also called the Star Park. The garden cottage, probably 18th-century, was home over the years to estate workers and crofters' families, and every year the manor holds a Christmas market. The garden suburb also had its own station on the Spånga–Lövsta railway, which carried passengers from 1889 to 1956.
Herrgården Stensjöhill vid Stensjöns väs: The manor house Stensjöhill, on the western shore of Lake Stensjön, has led quite a varied life. It was built in 1917 for the manager of the margarine factory nearby, became offices in the 1980s and was later taken over by the Hare Krishna movement. After that it became a hotel and conference centre, and at the end of 2012 it was sold to become a residential care home for young people. Closest of all is the Kikås ridge, home to Sweden's largest free-standing insect hotel.
Herrgården byggdes av hovkällarmästaren: The manor was built as a family summer retreat by Elias von Langenberg the Elder, the royal cellar master. The doorway is dated MDCCLXII – 1762, the year the house was finished. At first there was only the two-storey central section; the side wings were added in 1810.
Herrgården byggdes på 1770-talet för Dav: The manor was built in the 1770s for David af Sandeberg, a director of the Swedish East India Company. His brother-in-law William Chambers, court architect in England, sent designs by letter, while Carl Wilhelm Carlberg in Gothenburg drew up the working plans.
Herrgården efter släkten Pik: The manor named after the Pik family
Herrgården i snigelfart: A manor on the move at a snail's pace
Herrgården och det tidigare säteriet Säb: Säby gård, a manor and former noble estate in the Järvafältet nature reserve, has been a state listed building since 1983. It's now owned by Järfälla Municipality, and the main building houses a Waldorf preschool – so the youngest children here have unusually grand surroundings. South of the farm is the rune slab U 90, a Viking Age inscription carved straight into the bedrock.
Herrgården på gula listan: A manor on the endangered list
Herrgården Ålstens gård står på en grund: The manor house of Ålstens gård, right here, stands on 16th-century foundations, and the massive stone walls in the cellar tell you just how old it is. In 1936 it was bought by Axel Gauffin, director of the Nationalmuseum, who restored the house and lived here until 1957. Below it stretches Ålstensängen, one of the estate's old fields, now an open meadow that runs down to a sandy beach on Lake Mälaren.
Herrgårdens fasader är slätputsade utan: The manor's plain rendered façades have no decoration, so the house owes its character to the limestone steps at the entrance and the half-moon lunette windows in the gables. Down in the cellar are cross vaults from the 18th century.
Herrgårdsvillan såldes enligt reklamen f: According to the advertisements, the manor-style villa sold for 35,000 kronor, more than twice the price of a standard villa. The staff rooms, laundry and maid's room were in a wing of their own with a separate entrance. For a long time the house was thought to be by Ferdinand Boberg, but signed drawings show that the architect was Carl Kempendahl.
Herrlandslagets första match på arenan s: The men's national team played its first match at the arena on 14 November 2012, when Sweden beat England 4–2. Zlatan Ibrahimović scored all four goals. The last, an overhead kick from around 25 metres, won FIFA's award for goal of the year.
Herrängens gård har anor från 1600-talet: Herrängens gård dates back to the 1600s, when it was a croft called Isbergatorpet belonging to the Långbro estate. It stands on the northern shore of Lake Långsjön and has given its name to the whole district of Herrängen. The City Museum has marked it in blue, meaning the buildings are judged to be of exceptional historical value.
Herrängens gård revs i mitten av 1940-ta: Herrängen farm was pulled down in the mid-1940s, and the shopping centre stands where its garden used to be. One of the farm's maples still stands on the corner of Lingvägen and Gubbängsvägen.
Hersby gymnasium: Hersby gymnasium, the upper secondary school
Hersby gymnasium, som tidigare hette Lid: Hersby gymnasium, the upper secondary school once known as Lidingö högre allmänna läroverk, got its first school building in 1914, which was rebuilt and extended until 1957. A stone's throw away are the terraced houses of the Tegen större and Tegen mindre blocks, built as early as 1908–1909 to designs by Jacob Gate and now classed as culturally and historically valuable. Hersby as a whole forms the core of Lidingö villastad, the garden suburb founded in 1906.
Hersby har fått sitt namn efter Hersby g: Hersby takes its name from Hersby gård, a farm dating back to the 15th century with a manor house from 1854. The farm buildings burned down in 1940, and only the granary could be saved.
Hersby vattentorn byggdes 1949–1950 på e: Hersby water tower was built in 1949–1950 on a hill 53 metres high. It is a concrete cylinder with a vertically ribbed facade, topped with a crown-like crest. The tank holds 3,000 cubic metres, and the water surface sits 80 metres above sea level.

Hisingen har länge varit mycket skogfatt: Hisingen has long had very little forest. In the late 18th century Anders Gustaf Barchæus wrote that not even a juniper bush grew on Rödjan, and blamed all the charcoal kilns. That makes Rya forest an unusual exception – it already appears in a drawing by Erik Dahlbergh from 1678.
Hisingen är Sveriges femte största ö, ef: Hisingen is Sweden's fifth-largest island, after Gotland, Öland, Södertörn and Orust. At 199 square kilometres, it makes up roughly half of the City of Gothenburg's area.
Hisingen är stor, cirka 199 kvadratkilom: Hisingen is big – about 199 square kilometres, roughly half the area of Gothenburg municipality – and about a quarter of the city's residents live here. The island is framed by the Göta älv river to the south and east, the Nordre älv river to the north and the Kattegat sea to the west. The area also includes the small settlement of Holm in Tuve parish.
Hisingen, ön vi befinner oss på, är till: Hisingen, the island we're on now, is Sweden's fifth-largest island by area – after Gotland, Öland, Södertörn and Orust – and the second most populous. It's bounded by the Göta älv river to the south and east, the Nordre älv to the north and the Kattegat to the west. At 199 square kilometres, it makes up roughly half of Gothenburg municipality.
Hit kom bönder från Spånga, Ekerö och Fä: Farmers came here from Spånga, Ekerö and Färingsö to have their grain ground. Below the mill is the miller's cottage, thought to date from the early 1700s. A millstone serves as the step outside the cottage door.

Hjalmar Andersson, som kallade sig Arwin: Hjalmar Andersson, who called himself Arwin from 1914, knew the value of advertising. In the first issue of the magazine Lutfisken in 1912, his ad showed a Stone Age giant churning out villas on a conveyor belt, under the slogan 'Remarkable progress! ONE HOUSE a week'.
Hjalmar Branting gick i Beskowska skolan: Hjalmar Branting went to the Beskowska school in Stockholm, where the future King Gustaf V was in his class. His favourite subjects were science and maths, and he later studied astronomy in Uppsala, though he never took a degree.
Hjalmar Brantingsgatan fick sitt namn 19: Hjalmar Brantingsgatan was named in 1939 in memory of Prime Minister Hjalmar Branting. The square beside the street got its name in 1946.

Hjalmar Brantingsgatan got its name in 1939. Before that, part of it was called Försänkta gatan, the Sunken Street, and the stretch through Brämaregården was known from 1922 to 1929 as Letsegatan, after the Lundby Letsegård homestead.
Hjalmar Brantingsplatsen ligger cirka en: Hjalmar Brantingsplatsen lies about a kilometre from Gothenburg Central Station, surrounded by the Backaplan shopping area. It's the second tram stop after Frihamnen as you head out of the centre across Hisingen island.
Hjalmar Brantingsplatsen är Hisingens st: Hjalmar Brantingsplatsen is Hisingen's main transport hub. Hisingen is Sweden's fourth-largest island, and it was once where both ships and cars were built. Volvo was founded in Gothenburg in 1927, and its head office is still here on Hisingen.
Hjorthagen var ursprungligen ett hägn fö: Hjorthagen – ‘the deer park’ – was originally an enclosure for the king's deer. In the late 19th century it became an industrial suburb, with the Värta gasworks and power station as its landmarks. The headland of Ropsten has a lovely name: ‘the calling stone’, where people shouted across the water for the ferry. A 54-storey, 187-metre skyscraper called Stockholmsfyren was once planned for the end of the Lidingö Bridge, but it never got off the ground.
Hjorthagens skola från 1902 är en av få: Hjorthagen school from 1902 is one of the few wooden buildings left standing. Today it's home to Gerlesborgsskolan, an art school. The streets were given their hunting-themed names in 1920.

Hjulsta gård och by är kända sedan 1480-: Hjulsta farm and village have been known since the 1480s. The village lay south of Enköpingsvägen and in the 17th and 18th centuries belonged to the Ålsten estate, later to Åkeshov. The cottages were pulled down in the late 1960s.
Hjulsta öppnade den 31 augusti 1975, när: Hjulsta opened on 31 August 1975, when the first section of the blue line was inaugurated. The station is 14.3 kilometres from Kungsträdgården, and escalators and a lift take you down in two stages to the platform blasted out of the rock.
Hjulsta, den västra delen av Tensta, är: Hjulsta, the western part of Tensta, is a textbook example of separating cars from people – a hallmark of the Million Programme, Sweden's big housing drive of the 1960s and 70s. A ring road runs around the more or less car-free housing area, and footbridges tie it together over sunken streets. The metro station, the end of line 10, was blasted out of the rock beneath Hjulstaskolan school.
Hjällbo centrum byggdes 1969 efter ritni: Hjällbo centrum, the local shopping centre, was built in 1969 to designs by White Arkitektkontor. In 2001 it was rebuilt and given a new look by Liljewall Arkitekter.
Hjällbo centrum byggdes 1969 och fick et: Hjällbo centrum was built in 1969 and given a new look when it was rebuilt in 2001. On the square there's a market hall selling fruit and veg, and the shopping building has an oriental grocery, a gift shop and a pizzeria. There's a library, a pharmacy and a church here too, so most of everyday life fits around a single square.
Hjällbo centrum ritades från början av W: Hjällbo's centre was originally designed by White Arkitektkontor in 1969. When it was rebuilt in 2001, it got a new look by Liljewall Arkitekter.
Hjällbo centrum ritades ursprungligen av: Hjällbo centrum, the local shopping centre, was originally designed by White Arkitektkontor. In 2001 it was rebuilt with a new look by Liljewall Arkitekter.
Hjällbo kyrka ritades av John Snis och i: Hjällbo Church was designed by John Snis and consecrated in 1973. The following year it won an award for fine architecture. The interior is a three-aisled basilica, and the north wall is made of glass, looking out onto an atrium courtyard.
Hjällbo är en stadsdel på hela 927 hekta: Hjällbo is a district covering a full 927 hectares in north-eastern Gothenburg, and Eriksbo lies within it. A little further on begins Nordöstra Göteborg, North-East Gothenburg, an urban area made up mainly of Hammarkullen and Gunnared, with Gårdsten, Lövgärdet, Rannebergen and Angered centre. It's the largest urban area in Sweden that isn't the main town of its own municipality.
Hjällbos byggnadsminne Lärjeholms gård h: Lärjeholm Manor, a listed building in Hjällbo, has a history reaching back to the mid-15th century. The buildings standing today were put up by Admiral Claes Adam Wachtmeister in the late 18th century.
Hjälmarsvägen namngavs 1941 efter sjön H: Hjälmarsvägen was named in 1941 after Lake Hjälmaren. Along the street you'll find Årsta centrum, the Årsta school and the Lilla Dalen preschool.
Holger Blom är mest känd som Stockholms: Holger Blom is best known as Stockholm's city gardener from 1938 to 1971. The path Blomstigen is named after him, and he's said to have paced up and down it to sort out a building error in which entrances were about to face the wrong way.
Holländaren Michael von Hamm tog över ef: The Dutchman Michael von Hamm took over from Freundt, and the office then passed to his son and grandson. The grandson, Carl Harald Constantin von Hamm, was Sweden's last royal falconer. He died at the residence in 1867, bringing 150 years of falconers' homes here to an end.
Holm bestod från början av tre skattegår: Holm started out as three freehold farms that were merged into one larger estate. In the 1690s it became the official residence that came with the post of colonel and commandant of Gothenburg, and in 1748 four crofts are recorded under the estate: Torpet, Hagen, Boekullen and Grimman.
Holmens äldsta kända namn var Myntholmen: The islet's oldest known name was Myntholmen. When the Holmen church was built here for the Admiralty in 1629, the place began to be called Kyrkholmen, Church Islet. The museum park was laid out in the mid-1860s.
Holmia är det latinska namnet för Stockh: Holmia is the Latin name for Stockholm. The first building on the block was probably Skeppargården from 1906, built for the garden suburb's manager Erik Andersson, known as 'the skipper'.

Hoppbacken invigdes inför storpublik den: The ski jump opened in front of a huge crowd on 17 February 1924. The bigger of the two hills had a tower about 20 metres high that became a landmark, and it allowed jumps of more than 35 metres. Åke "Flying" Persson from Farsta was one of the last to jump here before competitions ended in 1990.

Hornstull har fått sitt namn efter tulle: Hornstull is named after the toll gate – the 'tull' – that once stood here on the old city boundary. This used to be a working-class neighbourhood; today it's one of the liveliest corners of Södermalm, with restaurants lining Hornstulls strand and views out over the water.

Hornstull is named after the toll gate that once stood here on the old city boundary. This used to be a working-class neighbourhood; today it's one of the liveliest corners of Södermalm, with restaurants lining the Hornstulls strand waterfront and views out over the water. To the south lies Tantolunden park, with its allotments and big lawns.
Hornstulls strand, restauranger vid vatt: Hornstulls strand and its waterside restaurants
Hotel The Weaver har ett torn på 22 våni: Hotel The Weaver has a 22-storey tower linked to a lower building. Between them they hold 370 hotel rooms and a conference centre with space for 600 people.
Hotell The Weaver reser sig 22 våningar,: Hotel The Weaver rises 22 storeys, with 370 rooms and conference space for 600 people. The name is a nod to Krokslätts fabriker, the Krokslätt mills, where weaving went on from start to finish right into the 1970s. Where the looms once clattered, business travellers now sleep.
Hotell i kontorshuset: A hotel in the office block
Hotellet ritades 1966 av Lennart Billgre: The hotel was designed by Lennart Billgren in 1966 for Esso Motorhotell and built next to an Esso station, like many similar hotels along the main roads. When Esso sold the chain in 1984, the hotels were renamed Scandic.
Hotellets kaffeservitör i fez: The hotel's coffee waiter in a fez
Hovet hade tre likadana Cadillac från 19: The royal court had three identical 1939 Cadillacs. The car museums at Skokloster and Sparreholm both claimed to own the real 'King's Curve' car, and according to one motoring historian there's no way of telling today which one it was.
Hovfotografen Aron Jonason räknas som en: The court photographer Aron Jonason is regarded as one of the founders of the göteborgsvits, Gothenburg's famous brand of pun. When Oscar II remarked that Jonason flashed a great deal, he replied: 'Yes – when one flashes, the other thunders!'

Court photographer Aron Jonason is counted among the founders of the famous Gothenburg pun. When King Oscar II remarked that he used his flash an awful lot, Jonason shot back: 'Well, when one flashes, the other thunders!' – a play on the Swedish words for lightning and thunder.
Huddinge centrum ligger mitt i en villas: Huddinge centrum sits in the middle of a garden suburb that never happened. In 1902 the owner of Fullersta gård began selling off plots for Huddinge villastad, since selling building land close to Stockholm paid better than farming. Only a few of the old villas are left.
Huddinge centrum samarbetar med Jokkmokk: Huddinge Centrum has a partnership with Jokkmokk in Lapland, and the Jokkmokk Days are held here every year. The centre is also adorned with 22 works of art, and its annual events include an ice sculpture competition.
Huddinge har elva naturminnen med tretto: Huddinge has eleven protected natural monuments comprising thirteen objects: ten oaks, an ash and two glacial boulders. That's largely down to the local heritage society, which applied for their protection around 1960. Stockholm municipality has only two.
Huddinge har elva naturminnen, bland dem: Huddinge has eleven natural monuments, ten of them oak trees. That's a lot compared with the City of Stockholm, which has just two. It was mainly the local heritage society that pushed for them to be protected in the late 1950s and early 1960s.
Huddinge har elva naturminnen: tio ekar,: Huddinge has eleven protected natural monuments: ten oaks, an ash and two glacial boulders. The credit goes to the local heritage society, which sought protection for the trees around 1960. Stockholm municipality has just two.
Huddinge station inrättades 1860, när jä: Huddinge station opened in 1860, when the railway between Stockholm South and Södertälje was built. A small railway town grew up around the station and was marketed in 1902 as Huddinge villastad, the Huddinge garden suburb.
Huddingegymnasiet ritades av Åke E. Lind: Huddingegymnasiet, the upper secondary school, was designed by Åke E. Lindqvist and opened in 1973, planned for 900 students around a central square. The façades are of yellowish-red brick and timber with exposed concrete elements. The school magazine, HGY Magazine, was named school magazine of the year in 2005.
Hulebäcksgymnasiet invigdes 1995 i och r: Hulebäcksgymnasiet, an upper secondary school, opened in 1995 in and around the old Hulebäck factory. Originally owned by Mölnlycke fabriker, the building has been a weaving mill, a furniture factory and an engineering workshop.
Humlegården och Kungliga biblioteket: Humlegården park and the National Library of Sweden
Hummelmoraberget i Järfälla når 65 meter: Hummelmoraberget in Järfälla rises 65 metres above sea level. Up top you'll find fields of rounded shingle and old beach ridges, and the hill is largely covered in broadleaf woodland.
Hummelmoraberget är Järfälla kommuns hög: Hummelmoraberget is the highest point in Järfälla, 67.4 metres above sea level. From the north side of the hill there's a sweeping view all the way to the Globe arena.
Hummelmoraberget är Järfällas högsta pun: Hummelmoraberget is the highest point in Järfälla, at 67.4 metres above sea level. From the north side of the hill there’s a sweeping view that reaches all the way to the Globe arena.

Hummelmoraberget is Järfälla's highest point, 67.4 metres above sea level. From the north side of the hill you can see all the way to the Globe arena. On the southern slope is a field of beach shingle, considered the hill's finest sight.
Hummelmoraberget is Järfälla's highest point, 67.4 metres above sea level. From its north side you can see all the way to Globen, the giant spherical arena.
Hundhamras tidigaste kända ägare var her: Hundhamra's earliest known owners were the dukes Valdemar and Erik Magnusson. In 1306 they set off from here to Håtuna to capture their brother, King Birger. The brothers' struggle for the crown ended in 1317 with the notorious Nyköping Banquet.
Hundkyrkogården i parken: The dog cemetery in the park
Hundra ekar och hundra pilar: A hundred oaks and a hundred willows
Hundra var en enkelstuga med tillbyggd v: Hundra was a simple cottage with an added veranda, and it burnt down in winter 1924. The foundations are still clearly visible and marked with a sign from the Salem local history society.
Hungrig? Kville saluhall öppnade 2013 me: Hungry? Kville saluhall, the food hall, opened in 2013 with meat, fish and seafood counters, a bakery and plenty of restaurants. Further on was the Gnistan cinema. It opened in 1938 with the military farce Kamrater i vapenrocken, and the curtain came down for good in 1968 after Django Shoots First. On Kvilletorget stands Carl Milles' statue Susanna, also known as Girl with a Shell.
How Linboda got its name is disputed. One theory is that it comes from 'linbod', a flax or rope shed, since the Helin siblings ran a rope shop. The other is that it means 'Lina's home', after the ropeworks' founder, Hulda Karolina Helin.
Hus i park utan motsvarighet: Houses in a park, without equal
Hus på fjädrar i berget: Buildings on springs inside the rock
Hus som bara delar balkong: Houses that only share a balcony
Husargatan hör till Hagas allra äldsta g: Husargatan is one of Haga's very oldest streets, dating from 1798, and was once called Timmermansgatan. The hussars' barracks at the end of the street were built in 1828, and by 1935 it was being described as Haga's main street.
Husarviksbron är byggd i blästrat rostfr: Husarviksbron is built of blasted stainless steel and weighs 35 tonnes. Its clearance is three metres, so around two-thirds of the boats in the bay can pass underneath without the bridge having to open.
Husby byggdes 1972–1977 på en höjdplatå,: Husby was built in 1972–1977 on a raised plateau, with traffic planning that strictly keeps cars and pedestrians on separate levels. Footbridges cross the sunken roads, and the metro was put underground so as not to split the district in two.
Husby gårds jordbruk lades ned 1959, men: Farming at Husby gård came to an end in 1959, but the farm buildings remain. The late 19th-century barn, which burned in 1994 and was rebuilt, is where Husby Konsthall holds its exhibitions. The farm is part of the Igelbäcken cultural reserve.
Husby gårds ladugård byggdes på 1880- el: The cowshed at Husby farm was built in the 1880s or 1890s, burnt down in 1994 and was rebuilt, though looking a little different. Today Husby Konsthall holds its exhibitions there, and since 2006 the farm buildings have been part of the Igelbäcken cultural reserve.
Husby, en bit härifrån, är byggt på norr: Husby, a short way from here, is built on the northern part of Järvafältet, which the army used as a training ground right up until 1965. From 1971 to 1980 the district was officially called Husby gård. Here you'll also find Husby Church, designed by Karl Erik Hjalmarson and consecrated in 1976, which the City Museum has given a green heritage listing – and the Husby baths, with an adventure pool and a diving tower.
Husbybadet är inte bara äventyrsbad. Här: Husbybadet isn’t just a water park. There’s also a 25-metre pool, a teaching pool and diving boards at 1 and 3 metres.
Husbybadet öppnade kring millennieskifte: Husbybadet opened around the turn of the millennium, tempting swimmers with a water park, a jacuzzi and a sauna. A little further on is Akalla church, which has an unusual story. It was consecrated in 1976, and in 2020 the Church of Sweden sold it to the Catholic Diocese of Stockholm. Today it's the home church of the Syriac Catholic Church.
Husdelar som flyttade till stan: Building parts that moved to town
Husen byggdes 1958–1961 efter ritningar: The buildings went up in 1958–1961, designed by Sune Lindström, Åke Arell and Alf Bydén. The eight 17-storey tower blocks bring to life Le Corbusier's vision from the 1930s. The writer Jerker Söderlind has called the area a utopia made real – “The House that Sune built”.
Husen byggdes med statliga lån, så byggn: The houses were built with state loans, so their footprint couldn't exceed 140 square metres. SIAB delivered its houses in large prefabricated sections, while Skånska Cementgjuteriet built on site, giving a more varied set of homes that fit the terrain.
Husen byggdes på uppdrag av varuhuskedja: The buildings were commissioned by the department store chain EPA as housing for the young women who worked in its stores. The first residents moved in in 1947, and a housemother living in one of the buildings kept an eye on the tenants.
Husen byggdes som Enskede hemgård, invig: The buildings started out as Enskede hemgård, opened in 1947 mainly for local pensioners. Back then the flats were bedsits with a kitchenette, about 25 square metres each. After flats were knocked together and a large shared kitchen was added, the Sockenstugan cohousing scheme opened in 1999.
Husen fick egna namn: Houses with names of their own
Husen från 1940- och 50-talen har grov s: The buildings from the 1940s and 50s have a coarse spatter render in warm earthy shades of brownish grey, red, ochre and green. Several façades are broken up with geometric patterns, and the balconies, doorways and windows vary, bringing the whole ensemble to life.

The houses from the 1940s and 50s have coarse roughcast render in warm earth tones, often with paler window surrounds and geometric patterns. Between the neighbourhoods, nature and parkland were kept in what's known as the Stockholm style, shaped by the park planners Holger Blom and Erik Glemme.
Husen från 1980-talet ritades av Lars Br: These 1980s buildings were designed by Lars Bryde's architecture firm, with yellow brick façades and balconies of yellow corrugated metal. The ground is so hilly that some of them have as many as three lower floors. The tall yellow boiler-house chimney has become a well-known feature of western Gröndal.
Husen glesnar och villor tar över. Snart: The buildings thin out and villas take over. Keep watching – the sea is coming up soon.
Husen hade ett rum och kök på 35 kvadrat: The flats had one room and a kitchen in 35 square metres, with a wood-burning range, a tiled stove, a gas cooker and electricity, but the privies were out in the yard. For all the overcrowding, some tenants kept their only room as a 'best room'. On the slopes down to Karlbergskanalen there were two ski jumps, 22 and 10 metres.
The buildings faced demolition in 1990 and 1995. Instead, young people aged 16 to 25 were given the chance to rebuild them themselves in a project called Framtidsloftet, and in 1998 they were able to move in.
Husen här är mest lamellhus från 1930-ta: The buildings here are mostly slab blocks from the 1930s. Among them are the Gräset block, designed by Sven Markelius, and Eriksdal School, designed by Helge Zimdal and Nils Ahrbom.
Husen i Karlastaden har fått namn från s: The buildings in Karlastaden take their names from the night sky. Auriga is Latin for the constellation of the Charioteer, Capella is its brightest star, and Callisto is Jupiter's second-largest moon. Lynx means just that – the lynx.
Husen i Kristinedal ritades i Malmö av a: The houses in Kristinedal were designed in Malmö by the architect Ingemar Wennström. In the 1960s housing estates, parking was solved right by the home, and the carport made its debut. The houses sit around little cul-de-sacs, and the old gravel pit is now a football pitch.
Husen i berget kläddes med svetsade stål: The buildings inside the rock were clad in welded steel plates to protect the electronics from electromagnetic pulses. They rest on shock-absorbing springs, clear of the rock walls. The only visible sign above ground is the radio mast on the hill.
Husen i putsat tegel liknar varandra men: The rendered brick houses resemble each other but come with variations, and each has a large wooden veranda. The attics have been partly opened up to the floor below, giving the flats double-height ceilings with lofts. The gatehouse has a large arched entrance.
Husen inne i Vargen står fritt från berg: The buildings inside the Vargen complex stand clear of the rock walls on shock-absorbing springs, so they can withstand the vibrations of powerful explosions. The outside – roofs and undersides included – is clad in fully welded steel plates to protect against electromagnetic pulses.
Husen inne i berget står på dämpande fjä: The buildings inside the rock rest on shock-absorbing springs, clear of the rock walls, so they can withstand the vibrations of an explosion. They are also completely clad in welded steel plates to shield them from electromagnetic pulses.
Husen längs Solvädersbyn är friliggande: Along Solvädersbyn the houses are detached semis and terraced homes set on crofter-style foundations. Each one has its own garden with a patio, an outdoor storeroom and a parking space.
Husen på Lidingsberg är byggnadsminnen s: The houses at Lidingsberg have been listed buildings since 1954, and every renovation is carried out together with Stockholm County Museum. The area is private land, and visitors can go no further than the gate.
Husen ritades av Rudolf Steen och heter: Designed by Rudolf Steen, the buildings are called "Emil Ekmans minne" and "Emilie Landgrens gåva" – "In memory of Emil Ekman" and "Emilie Landgren's gift". In front of the lower building is a terrace with a natural stone wall, where six stone bollards are linked by iron chains, as on a quayside. The buildings have been listed since 1984.
Husen ritades av arkitekten Andrew Perss: The buildings were designed by the architect Andrew Persson and are among the few lavish brick houses along Lilienberg's broad main streets. The assembly hall is architecturally unique and stands as a monument to the shipowner Axel Broström.
Husen runt Alléparken blev klara omkring: The buildings around Alléparken were finished around 1920, with shops on the ground floor. Today you'll find a café, a bookshop, a hairdresser and several restaurants here, among other things.
Husen runt Götaplatsens södra del, byggd: The buildings around the southern end of Götaplatsen, built between 1923 and 1935, share large cubic forms and yellow brick. Their heights rise step by step towards the Gothenburg Museum of Art, whose seven tall arches make a grand backdrop to the Avenyn. The square is paved with Fjärås gneiss from northern Halland.
Husen runt det piazzaliknande Rudboda to: The buildings around the piazza-like Rudboda torg were designed in the 1960s by Sten Samuelson and Fritz Jaenecke, the same architects behind Lidingö's town hall. The façades are of brick, concrete and scalloped panelling, and in the square stands Aston Forsberg's fountain sculpture Bevingad kub ('Winged Cube') from 1969.
Husen runt torget ritades av Edvin Engst: The buildings around the square were designed by Edvin Engström, with shops on the ground floor. There are still small local businesses here, such as a cobbler, a tailor and a hairdresser. Once upon a time almost every stop along tram line 12 had its own shops.
Husen som inte heter Högsätra: The houses that aren't in Högsätra
Husen står på en sluttning och samlas kr: The buildings stand on a slope, gathered around half-open courtyards facing the lake, with windows and balconies placed asymmetrically. The original multicoloured paintwork survives. The Ahlsén brothers tried out the same geometric patterns at Årsta Centrum at around the same time.
Husen vid Draget var först tänkta för by: The houses at Draget were originally meant for the construction workers at the waterworks. Today the old workers' homes are mostly used as summer houses.
Husen är byggda av fabrikstillverkade be: The buildings are made of factory-built concrete panels using the Skarne system – the same as in the Million Programme, Sweden's great 1960s–70s housing drive. Working with the artist Åke Pallarp, the window frames were originally painted yellow, blue and red to bring some life to the sombre weight of the concrete.
Husen är enkla volymer som får spänning: The buildings are simple volumes given tension by slight shifts of angle and corrugated aluminium cladding. Not even the balconies are allowed to break the form – they're recessed so their front edge lines up with the facade. The windows are square, with no glazing bars.
Husens fasader har ett tydligt vertikalt: The façades have a strongly vertical look, with the rows of windows and balconies separated by panels of corrugated aluminium sheet. Not even the balconies are allowed to break the lines: they're recessed so that their front edge sits flush with the façade.
Huset blev klart precis under bankkrisen: The building was completed right in the middle of the banking crisis of the early 1990s and became a symbol of the 1980s building boom. Its rival Nordbanken planned an office complex of its own next door, but the crisis put a stop to it. A Toyota dealer is among the businesses there today.
Huset byggdes 1930 av Sundbybergs Folket: The building went up in 1930 for the Sundbyberg People's House association and was called Nya Folkets Hus – the New People's House. The architects Eskil Sundahl and Artur von Schmalensee designed it in a blend of 1920s classicism and functionalism.
Huset byggdes 1939 för biografen Kaza, m: The building went up in 1939 for the Kaza cinema, with 460 seats. It closed in 1965, and two years later the space became the Rainbow roller rink. In 1969 EMI moved in. A 2019 proposal to demolish the building was met with thousands of signatures in protest, and in 2024 came the news that it can stay.
Huset byggdes 2016–2017 efter att en äld: The house was built in 2016–2017 after an older villa on the plot burned down. It's a two-storey cube clad in larch. A large oak was allowed to stay and now grows straight up through the veranda and the balcony above.
Huset byggdes av ett konsortium mellan H: The building was put up by a consortium of Hufvudstaden, SIAB and Lundbergs, but was sold in 2006 to Alecta, which owns it today. Tenants include the steel companies SSAB and Sandvik.
Huset byggdes av gult tegel, fick tak av: The house was built of yellow brick, with a copper roof and custom-made mahogany windows. The floors in the hall and living room were laid with red brick tiles, and the house was heated partly by underfloor heating.
Huset byggdes av ingenjör Nils Nessen ef: The building was put up by the engineer Nils Nessen to designs by Olle Zetterberg, with a plain facade in yellow brick from the Mälaren valley. Elias Svedberg and Sven Erik Skawonius did the interiors, which Svenska Dagbladet called unusually cosy and graceful.
Huset byggdes längs gamla Ladugårdslands: The building was put up along the old Ladugårdslands Tullgata, even though the city plan said the street was to be closed. Unclear ownership meant the land couldn't be compulsorily purchased, so there's an enclosed stub of street in front of the building whose owner is still a mystery today.
The building was put up in the 1670s as a riding hall. In 1753, at Queen Lovisa Ulrika's initiative, Carl Fredrik Adelcrantz converted it into a theatre seating just over 200.
Huset byggdes som arbetarbostad under bo: The building went up as workers' housing during the housing shortage of the First World War. It was meant to be part of a larger block, but only the wing facing Nynäsvägen was finished. The flats had toilets but no bathrooms, and in autumn 1915 a furnished show flat was opened to visitors.
Huset byggdes åt falkeneraren Christian: The house was built for the falconer Christian Freundt, huntsman to King Frederick I. The king loved falconry so much that he set up an official royal falconry establishment in Sweden. Documents on the building of the house are still kept in the palace archives.
Huset där Aspen ligger byggdes redan 194: The building that houses Aspen went up in 1940, and even then it was designed with a cinema on the lower floor. Still, it was twelve years before the first film was shown.
Huset där Bullegumman sålde sina bullar: The house where Bullegumman sold her buns is in its original state, and the hatch in the wall was still there as late as 2011. For a while the house belonged to the City of Gothenburg and served as a reception centre for refugees.
Huset från 1934 hade flyttbara väggar oc: This 1934 building had movable walls and heating from the ceilings. The walls let every sound through and the ceiling heating worked poorly, so residents saw it as a shoddy experimental building – hence its nickname, the EPA house, after the cut-price EPA department store chain.
Huset har fått sitt namn efter byggmästa: The building is named after the master builder Frans August Kling, born in Virserum in 1878, who both commissioned and built it himself. The architect J.V. Söderström drew inspiration from the 1920s Classicism of central Stockholm, and the entrances were given red granite surrounds with volutes.
Huset har kvar flera kakelugnar från 170: The house still has several 18th-century tiled stoves with different motifs. One is known as 'dead bird under a parasol' and is attributed to Jean Eric Rehn. The six-part floor plan is typical of fine 18th-century houses.
Huset höll på att förfalla och skulle ri: The house was falling into disrepair and due to be demolished, but was saved after a debate about its preservation. During the restoration, parts of a painted 17th-century ceiling were found in the attic, showing a hovering cherub and the Stenbock family coat of arms. It now hangs in the entrance hall.
Huset kallas också Mördarslottet. Enligt: The house is also known as Mördarslottet, the Murderers' Castle. According to tradition, it was here in 1792 that Count Claes Horn, Jacob Anckarström, Carl Fredrik Pechlin and Adolph Ribbing plotted the assassination of Gustav III.
Huset kom sjövägen: The house that came by water
Huset lånade 200 000 kronor i Uppsala sp: The building borrowed 200,000 kronor from Uppsala savings bank, on terms that meant the loan couldn't be called in. When the bank manager was arrested in a bribery scandal, the bank wanted its money back but couldn't get it. The low interest rate turned out to be worth its weight in gold when rates rose in the 1940s and 50s.
Huset med kopparkupolen: The house with the copper dome
Huset murades av holländsk klinker som f: The house was built of Dutch clinker bricks, shipped by sailing vessel to Gothenburg and then hauled up the Säveån river to Partille. It is said to have been the largest private three-storey brick house on any farm in Sweden.
Huset på Bastugatan 48 byggdes med lån u: The building at Bastugatan 48 was built with loans from the Poor Housing Fund as homes for poor working families. The eastern part was finished around 1853, and the flats were a single room and kitchen of about 20 square metres.
Huset på Sockenvägen 368 ritades 1931 av: The building at Sockenvägen 368 was designed by Eskil Sundahl in 1931 and had a Konsum co-op shop on the ground floor. Today it's known for the mural ‘Flickan i fönstret’ (The Girl in the Window) by Lars Tärning and Tor Svae. In the middle of the roundabout stands the artwork Girland (Garland) by Graham Stacy.
Huset restes på tre dagar: A house raised in three days
Huset ritades av Niels Lund-Hansen och h: The building was designed by Niels Lund-Hansen and is triangular in plan. Its roof has 63 pyramids shaped like tetrahedrons. Travelators linked the two floors so you could take your shopping trolley from one level to the other.
Huset ritades i kraftfull nationalromant: The building was designed in a bold National Romantic style, with dark patterned Helsingborg brick and granite from Lysekil. The tower's copper-clad onion dome is topped by a weather vane in the shape of a locomotive.
Huset ritades som en fristående, kyrklik: The building was designed as a free-standing, church-like structure with buttresses and a steep pitched roof at two heights. To keep costs down the plans were simplified: the windows were made smaller and decorative urns on the ridges were dropped.
Huset skulle avlasta familjer så att båd: The building was designed to take the load off families so that both parents could work. It had a restaurant, a reception, a supermarket, a day nursery, a photo lab, a garage for 80 cars, a petrol station and a chapel. When the restaurant closed in 1976, the residents took over the cooking themselves.

Huset som fångar solen: The building that catches the sun
Huset som gör sin egen energi: The building that makes its own energy
Huset som liknar en gryta: The house that looks like a cooking pot
Huset som skulle flytta: The house that was meant to move
Huset som slapp tunnelbanetaket: No building on the metro roof
Huset står bland smalhus från 1940- och: The building stands among narrow slab blocks from the 1940s and 50s and echoes their shape. But instead of render or brick, its façade is clad in fire-treated cedar. The city architect Karolina Keyzer spoke of "living façades of cedar".
Huset var en av fem finalister till Året: The house was one of five finalists for Stockholm Building of the Year 2011. After the much-publicised project, a family bought it and it became an ordinary home. Surplus electricity from the solar panels charged the family's electric car.
Huset är ett prefabricerat trähus på 156: This prefabricated 156-square-metre timber house has a staircase rising through an open space seven metres up to the roof ridge. Every south-facing surface carries solar panels or solar collectors, and the walls can be moved as the family grows or shrinks.
Huset är ett tvåvåningshus av trä i empi: This is a two-storey wooden house in the Empire style, originally painted yellow. Some of the windows are false, there purely for strict symmetry. After the 1983–1985 renovation it was painted pink.
Huset är helt vitt. Mot torget varieras: The building is completely white. On the side facing the square, the facade is broken up by bands of windows at different heights and the odd square window, while the east side is dominated by balconies that look like sugar cubes. On the north gable you can see the stairs through small glass-block openings.
Huset är murat av tunt mörkrött holländs: The house is built of thin, dark red Dutch clinker bricks, shipped by sailing vessel to Gothenburg and then hauled up the Säveån river. The window frames and doors came from England. As early as 1776 it was said to be the largest private three-storey brick house on any farm in the country.
Huset är sedan 1987 upptaget i kommunens: Since 1987 the building has been on the city's conservation list. Inside are five different venues that hold anywhere from 30 to 200 people.
Huset är timrat och brädfodrat, i en vån: The house is timber-built and clad in boards, with a single storey, a converted attic and a large dormer gable. Downstairs there was a big hall, two rooms and a kitchen; the rooms were hung with French wallpaper and heated by tall tiled stoves.
Husets läge, längd på 64 meter och höjd: The building's position, its 64-metre length and its nine storeys were already laid down in the 1962 town plan. Even so, the architects Britta and Kjell Abramson gave it a character of its own, with distinctive balconies and reddish-brown tiles in the entrances, which survive in their original state.
Husets tre biografer heter Bio Victor, B: The building's three cinemas are called Bio Victor, Bio Mauritz and Bio Julius, after Victor Sjöström, Mauritz Stiller and Julius Jaenzon. Bio Victor, with 364 seats, and Bio Mauritz are open to the public.
Huslängan från 1951 ritades av Folke Löf: The 1951 wing was designed by Folke Löfström as a single-storey building where the classrooms got light from two sides. At the time this was seen as an experiment.
Huslängor för lä och sol: Rows of houses for shelter and sun
Husmuren mot Nytorps gärde var tänkt som: The wall of buildings facing Nytorps gärde was meant to be Kärrtorp's frontage onto a major road, Ulricehamnsvägen. The road was never built, and neither was the later planned Skarpnäcksleden. So arriving in Kärrtorp feels a little like coming in through the kitchen door.
Huvudbyggnaden består delvis av två hus: The main building is partly made up of two houses that were shipped here by water from Fogdön. The facades were originally clad in wooden panelling but were rendered in the late 1800s.
Huvudbyggnaden fick sitt nuvarande utsee: The main building took on its present look after 1791: a single-storey rendered timber house with a hipped mansard roof. The east wing survives from that time, while the west wing burned down in 1808 and was rebuilt in the 20th century.
Huvudbyggnaden från 1770–1772 ritades tr: The main house from 1770–1772 was probably designed by the Swedish-British court architect William Chambers. His sister Sara married the estate's owner, Martin Törngren, in 1772. The house is built entirely of timber in the neoclassical style.
Huvudbyggnaden från 1770–72 ritades trol: The main house, built in 1770–72, was probably designed by the Swedish-British court architect Sir William Chambers. In 1772 his sister Sara married the estate's owner, Martin Törngren.

The main house from 1770–72 was probably designed by the Swedish-British court architect Sir William Chambers. His sister Sara married the estate's owner, Martin Törngren, in 1772. The house is built entirely of timber, but the panelling on the courtyard side is made to look like stone.
Huvudbyggnaden från 1811 fick på 1840-ta: The main house from 1811 was given its ochre-yellow panelling in the Karl Johan style in the 1840s. Next to it stands a red house from the 1850s – Lidingö's only surviving statarbostad, a home for married farm labourers paid partly in kind, with a big hearth room for baking and washing.
Huvudbyggnaden i karolinsk stil uppförde: The main house, in the Caroline style, was probably built in the 1680s by a descendant of the privy councillor Johan Skytte. The two red-painted wings served for a time as granaries, and the stable was built in 1744–1745. The City Museum has given the farm its blue rating for its exceptionally high cultural and historical value.
Huvudbyggnaden låg ungefär mitt på Gubbä: The farm's main house stood roughly in the middle of today's Gubbängen School playground. The architects lined the school buildings up with the farm's avenue, whose trees are still standing – as is the farm's food cellar beside it. Gubbängsfältet, the open field, is a remnant of the farm's meadows.
Huvudbyggnaden som flyttades: The main house that was moved
Huvudbyggnaden är av sten med slätputsad: The main house is built of stone, with smooth rendered facades and no ornament. Its character comes from the limestone steps up to the entrance and the half-moon lunette windows in the gables. A 150-metre avenue of trees leads up to the house.
Huvudbyggnaden är av trä, 1½ våning hög: The main building is a timber house of one and a half storeys with a tiled roof, raised up on a stone terrace. The facade has red-painted board-and-batten panelling with green-painted trim and shutters, and some of the small-paned windows still have their old glass.
Huvudbyggnaden är ett gult trähus i två: The main building is a two-storey yellow wooden house with columned wings, probably dating from around 1820. The Jakobssalen has restored wall paintings from the mid-1700s, and the rustic south wing has a dance floor. The woods running down to Lake Mälaren were once an English-style park.
Huvudbyggnaden är helt av timmer, men på: The main building is made entirely of timber, but on the courtyard side it's clad in flush boarding – the type of panelling that looked most like a stone house. On the outside it has barely changed since it was built.
Huvudbyggnaden, Kristinahuset, uppfördes: The main building, Kristinahuset, was built in 1686 as a single-storey, yellow-painted timber house with a tall hipped roof. The court architect Jean de la Vallée was probably involved. Today it houses a restaurant.
Huvudbyggnaden, kallad Slottet, stod kla: The main house, known as Slottet ('the Castle'), was completed in 1905 and the art gallery in 1913, both designed by Ferdinand Boberg and Prince Eugen himself. The estate covers 70,000 square metres and is surrounded by water on three sides.
Huvudbyggnadens mittparti byggdes på 174: The central part of the main house was built in the 1740s as a summer retreat for Herman Petersen, a wealthy director of the Swedish East India Company. In the 1760s the next owner, the French ambassador Louis Auguste le Tonnelier de Breteuil, added the billiard wing and the reflecting pool.
Huvudbyggnadens portik i trä har toskans: The main house's wooden portico has Tuscan columns and a semicircular top that looks like the stern of a ship. That's probably the source of the rumour that the shipbuilder af Chapman designed the house, but the architect's identity is unknown.
Huvudcentralerna fick djurnamn, som Varg: The main exchanges were given animal names, such as Vargen (the Wolf) and Elefanten (the Elephant), while the smaller units got plant names – Krokusen (the Crocus) on Kungsholmen, Liljan (the Lily) at Brommaplan and Pionen (the Peony) on Södermalm, for example.
Huvudgatan Gustav Adolfs väg är uppkalla: The main street, Gustav Adolfs väg, is named after Prince Gustaf Adolf, who was married to Princess Sibylla. Other streets are called Kristinavägen, Margaretavägen and Sibyllavägen, while the prime minister got Per Albins väg. In 1931 buses began serving Glömsta, replacing horse-drawn transport.
Huvudgatan Sturegatan hette från början: The main street, Sturegatan, was originally called Storgatan, but in the late 1800s it was renamed after Sten Sture the Elder. Along it you'll find shops and restaurants, Folkets hus, the community hall, and Sundbybergs köksbryggeri, a brewery – and there was once a cinema here too. The Allaktivitetshuset cultural centre opened in 2013.
Huvudsta Centrum byggdes 1972 efter ritn: Huvudsta Centrum was built in 1972 to designs by Erik Thelaus, with an indoor square lit by a roof lantern. When it was modernised in 2010–2011 it became bigger and brighter, and a residential block with 113 flats was built on top.
Huvudsta gamla slott är beryktat som pla: Huvudsta's old palace is notorious as the place where the assassination of Gustav III was plotted.
Huvudsta har fler slott än man kanske tr: Huvudsta has more palaces than you might expect: Karlberg Palace, Huvudsta gård and Huvudsta Old Palace. By Lake Ulvsundasjön there's also the popular Huvudstabadet pool. And 25 metres beneath your feet, in the rock, is the metro station, decorated with Per Holmberg's artwork Hängande trädgårdar, 'Hanging Gardens', from 1985.
Huvudsta nämns i ett tingsprotokoll 1356: Huvudsta is mentioned in a court record from 1356 as Hudhastum. The name is thought to come from the personal name Hudhe and the Old Swedish 'stadher', meaning place – so 'Hudhe's places'.
Huvudstabron byggdes 1964–1967 och är 28: Huvudstabron was built in 1964–1967 and is 286 metres long. Its longest span, 100 metres, crosses Bällstaviken with 24 metres of clearance for shipping. During planning the name Ulvsunda Bro was proposed, but it ended up as Huvudstabron.
Huvudstagranit i Riksdagshuset: Huvudsta granite in the Parliament House
Huvudstråket genom Akalla heter Sibelius: Akalla's main pedestrian street, Sibeliusgången, is named after the Finnish composer Jean Sibelius, and it runs for 900 metres. Along the way, Bertil Johnson's fountains from 1976 bubble away. But the name Akalla goes back to the Middle Ages: in Akalla village stands the 17th-century Storgården, in one of the best-preserved village settings around Stockholm, complete with a 4-H farm and a café.
Huvudtrappan i ek och de engelskinspirer: The oak main staircase and the English-inspired fireplaces, rare in Swedish architecture, were probably Maud's idea. The servants had to use a well-hidden spiral staircase in the west wing of the house.
Huvudvägen Gustav Adolfs väg är uppkalla: The main road, Gustav Adolfs väg, is named after Prince Gustav Adolf, who was married to Princess Sibylla. Other streets are called Kristinavägen, Margaretavägen and Sibyllavägen, while the prime minister got Per Albins väg.
Hägernäs omnämns första gången 1549 som: Hägernäs is first mentioned in 1549 as Hegrenes, after the herons that nested by Stora Värtan bay. In the 18th century people rowed from here into Stockholm to collect the townspeople's laundry.
Hägerstens gård är en herrgård vars mang: Hägerstens gård is a manor house whose main building and wings are still standing, but since 1997 it has been a housing cooperative with just five flats. At Hägerstens torg – also known as Axelsbergs centrum – the main building is modernist, its façades clad in dark red ceramic tiles. And at night, the trees on Axelsbergs torg are lit up from below by spotlights.
Hägerstensviadukten invigdes den 21 augu: The Hägersten viaduct opened on 21 August 1966. Scaffolding couldn't be put up over Hägerstensvägen and the depot, so the bridge was made from 64 ready-made concrete beams weighing up to 85 tonnes each. They were cast in a temporary factory behind the abutment and lifted into place.
Häggvikstunneln är den kortaste av Norro: Häggvikstunneln is the shortest of the three road tunnels on the Norrortsleden ring road, at just 289 metres, and there's a park on its roof. A little further on is Klasroskolan, a school built in 1804 that was Sollentuna's only school until 1871. It was put up beside the parish's most famous spring, where travellers used to water their horses – the diarist Malla Silfverstolpe called it “la bonne fontaine”. Today the old school is a museum.
Hällen föll i glömska och hittades först: The rock slab fell into obscurity and wasn't found again until the early 1860s, after a long search, when Richard Dybeck made a drawing of it. The carving is shallow and hard to read, but it has recently been filled in with red paint.
Hällen hamnade mitt i vägbygget för Botk: The rock slab ended up right in the path of the new Botkyrkaleden road. The archaeologist Rudolf Hansson grew curious and lifted away a little moss – revealing the image of a ship. The road authorities changed the route at the last minute so that the slab could stay where it was.
Hällen sluttar mot en svacka som en gång: The rock slopes down towards a dip that was once a strait – perhaps the one that gave Sundby farm its name. In the mid-11th century the carving sat barely a metre above sea level and could probably be seen from passing ships. All that's left of the waterway is the Spångaån/Bällstaån stream.
Hällen sluttar mot en svacka som trolige: The rock slopes down to a dip that was probably once a strait – perhaps the one that gave Sundby farm its name ('sund' means strait). In the mid-1000s the bottom edge of the carving sat barely a metre above sea level, so it may have been visible from passing ships. All that's left of the waterway today is the Spångaån/Bällstaån stream.
Hällkistan var omkring fyra meter lång o: The stone cist was about four metres long and two metres wide, and several people were buried in it. Flint objects such as arrowheads and scrapers were left as offerings.
Hällsvik ligger i en dalgång mellan Anda: Hällsvik lies in a valley between Andalen to the south and Hjuvik to the north. There's also a marina run by the Hällsvik Boat Club, and the Bycentret village centre is both a meeting place and a school.
Hällsvik vid Hälleviken var förr en lite: Hällsvik, on the Hälleviken bay, was once a small fishing village where people made their living from fishing and, in time, farming – and some of the original buildings are still here. In the heyday of the shipyards, many yard workers bought themselves summer cottages here. Over the years the plots have been divided up, and the cottages have either been demolished or rebuilt as proper houses.
Hälsa på Bellmansbysten: Say hello to the bust of Bellman
Hälsa på Ingo – the Champ (2 min), Peter: Say hello to Ingo – the Champ (2 min), Peter Linde's statue of the heavyweight world champion Ingemar Johansson. Then walk past Nya Ullevi, where the stands famously shook when Bruce Springsteen played in 1985, to the Scandinavium stop (about 8 min).
Hälsa på bronskvinnan Väntan: Say hello to Väntan, Waiting, the bronze woman
Hälsö hette tidigare Hällesö, efter berg: Hälsö used to be called Hällesö, after the flat rocks, or hällar, along its shores.
Hälsö är en liten ö i Göteborgs norra sk: Hälsö is a small island in Gothenburg's northern archipelago, just 1.28 square kilometres, with around 590 permanent residents. On its south side a bridge takes you over to Öckerö, and from there you can carry on to Hönö and catch the ferry to Hisingen and the mainland. The islands hang together like pearls on a string.
Här bjuds på namnförvirring: Skarpnäcks: Get ready for some confusing names: Skarpnäck's old school from 1928 is in Enskededalen, while Skarpnäck School from 1952 is just across the way in Kärrtorp. The younger one has been called both the New School and Skarpnäck New School before getting its old name back, and since 1992 the two have been one school in two buildings. Both have been given the City Museum's green listing for buildings of special value.

Here's a name muddle for you: Skarpnäck's old school from 1928 is in Enskededalen, while Skarpnäck school from 1952 is across the road in Kärrtorp. The younger school has been called both Nya skolan, the New School, and Skarpnäcks nya skola before getting its old name back, and since 1992 it has served as an annex to its older neighbour. The Stockholm City Museum has classed both school buildings as culturally valuable.
Här byggdes för första gången i Sverige: This was the first place in Sweden where flats were built on top of an ordinary railway. To meet the requirements for quiet homes, the tracks were laid on elastic mats and the buildings were set on rubber cushions.
Här började Lotta Schelin: Where Lotta Schelin got her start
Här delar sig blå linjen mot Akalla och: This is where the blue line splits towards Akalla and Hjulsta. Tracks 2 and 3 both run towards Kungsträdgården, so trains from the two branches can wait for each other at a station rather than in the tunnel. The blue line's control centre is here too.
Här doftar det konspiration. En bit bort: There's a whiff of conspiracy in the air here. Not far off is Huvudsta gamla slott, Huvudsta Old Palace, a wooden house from 1750 where, rumour has it, the murder of Gustav III was plotted. It was originally the main house of Huvudsta Farm but was moved in 1834. Down by the water you may also spot the schooner Constantia, built in Denmark in 1908 and now a sail training ship for young people and adults alike.
Här fanns en fiskodling från 1917 till 1: A fish farm operated here from 1917 to 1974, raising crucian carp, common carp and rainbow trout among others. Once it closed, the area became overgrown, and in 1988 a new pond was dug to encourage birdlife.
Här fanns en gång Vårby gård, även kalla: This is where Vårby gård, also known as Vårby Castle, once stood – an estate the City of Stockholm bought in 1931. The main house burned down on 5 May 1975, and today the grounds are mostly park and allotments. Close by, at Duvberget, the Vårby hoard, a buried silver treasure, was discovered in 1871. In the manor park you'll find Myrstugan, a boatswain's croft from the early 1700s that was moved here in 1986.
Här fanns en järnvägsstation: There was once a railway station here
Här fanns förr en bangård, godsskjul, lo: There used to be a goods yard here, with freight sheds, an engine shed and a station building that was demolished in 1963. Two sidings ran right into the Henriksdal sewage treatment works. All that's left is an old platform, a foundation, a few tracks and a buffer stop.
Här fanns först två cyklotroner och seda: First there were two cyclotrons here, then the CRYRING accelerator, a storage ring 52 metres in circumference. When the laboratory closed in 2011, CRYRING was moved to a new research facility in Darmstadt, Germany.
Här fanns redan en vattendriven mjölkvar: There was already a water-powered flour mill here, Danviks kvarn, built in the 1540s on royal orders. The modern steam mill soon outcompeted it, and the old mill closed in the late 1890s.
Här fick HSB sitt första samlade bostads: This was where the housing cooperative HSB built its first complete residential area. The flats were unusually modern: all had flushing toilets and shower rooms, and the kitchens had marble worktops and gas cookers. The laundry rooms were given washing machines and steam dryers early on, and the ground-floor windows had white or green shutters.
Här finns Göteborgs längsta rulltrappor,: Gothenburg's longest escalators are here, rising 24 metres over a length of 58 metres. There's also an inclined lift, a kind of funicular, which was replaced in 2021. From the station the tram gets you to Brunnsparken in 15 minutes.
Här finns Stockholms stads största våtma: This is the City of Stockholm's largest wetland, with a wealth of birdlife. The landscape has been grazed by livestock for at least 1,500 years, perhaps as many as 3,000, shaping meadows and ancient trees.

This is home to the City of Stockholm's largest wetland, broadleaf woodland and a wealth of birdlife. The landscape has been shaped by grazing animals for at least 1,500 years, and perhaps as many as 3,000.
Här finns drygt 5 000 arkiv, över 600 pe: The collection holds more than 5,000 archives, including over 600 personal archives, along with photographs, posters, films, sound recordings, banners and badges. Around 100 new archives arrive every year.
Här finns ett av Stockholms mer udda mus: Here you'll find one of Stockholm's quirkier museums: Sveriges VVS-museum, the Swedish Plumbing and Heating Museum. The collection started out in Katrineholm and reopened here in Bromma in 2016. Further off, in Tuvanparken, stood Tuvan, a home for people with nervous disorders, in the 1890s. Three patients died in a fire there in 1940, and the building was pulled down in 1960. Where the nursing home once stood, there's now a park.
Här finns gator uppkallade efter bland a: Streets here are named after, among others, Cajsa Warg, the housekeeper and cookery writer, and the opera singer Kristina Nilsson. Barbro Stigsdotters väg remembers the woman who helped Gustav Vasa escape at Ornäs.
Här finns gott om skolbänkar: Nacka gymn: There's no shortage of school desks around here. Nacka gymnasium is one of Sweden's biggest schools, and its neighbour, Eklidens skola, is one of the country's largest secondary schools for 13- to 16-year-olds, with an ice rink and a swimming pool right next door. The name Järla comes from the title jarl, meaning earl. In nearby Vikdalen, Stockholm families built summer villas in the late 19th century and came out by steamboat. Then a car engine factory opened in Augustendal, workers moved in, and the villas became workers' housing.
Här flyttade de första Farstaborna in: Where Farsta's first residents moved in
Här föddes Hem till byn: Where Hem till byn was born
Här föddes The Final Countdown-videon: Birthplace of The Final Countdown video
