I själva Nyckelviken finns sju skeppsvra: Nyckelviken bay itself has seven shipwrecks recorded in the national register of ancient monuments. The only footpath to the houses at Fredriksvik runs through Helveteshålet – Hell's Hole – a damp, fern-filled rift valley.
I sjöns nordvästra hörn, i Gröndal, ligg: In the north-west corner of the lake, in Gröndal, is Trekantenbadet, which opened in 1972. It has a little sandy beach, a big grassy slope for sunbathing, a floating jetty and an outdoor shower.
I skogarna en bit härifrån ligger Natura: Out in the forests not far from here is the Natura 2000 site Maderna-Haketjärn, with small lakes such as Haketjärnen and Långevatten. Haketjärnen is shared between the municipalities of Härryda and Partille and is just over seven metres deep. Lilla Långevatten covers only 0.03 square kilometres, yet it's almost ten metres deep. Partille is also home to Partille SC, the oldest field hockey club in Sweden that's still going.
I skogen en bit härifrån ligger Södra Lu: In the woods not far from here is Södra Lundtjärnen, a small lake with a quirky detail: the coordinates given for it actually point to a nameless lake just south of the real one. In the other direction is the village of Pinntorp, near Tahult, where the road-racing motorcyclist Kent Andersson has lived.
I skogen en kort promenad härifrån låg s: In the woods a short walk from here stood Kappsta, a summer villa also known as Wisingska villan, where Raoul Wallenberg was born. The house burned down in 1931, but its foundations are still there in Kappsta nature reserve, along with a memorial by Gustav and Ulla Kraitz called Attachéväska R.W., Attaché Case R.W. Nearby are Villa Ekbacken, built in 1912–1913 for Gustaf Dalén, and Skärsätra water tower from 1912.

In the woods a short walk from here stood the summer villa Kappsta, also known as the Wising villa, where Raoul Wallenberg was born. It burned down in the early 1930s, but its foundations survive in the Kappsta nature reserve, along with the memorial 'Attaché Case R.W.' by Gustav and Ulla Kraitz. The reserve also holds the foundations of Villa Nidaros, Trondheim's pavilion from the 1897 Stockholm Exhibition.
I skogen har bland annat kattuggla, korp: Birds that have nested in the woods include tawny owls, ravens, black woodpeckers, lesser spotted woodpeckers and woodcock. You'll also find grass snakes, slow worms and the rare toothwort.
I skogen mellan Fisksätra och Igelboda,: In the woods between Fisksätra and Igelboda, just south of the Saltsjöbanan railway, you can still find the stone foundations of Vinterbrinken, a lineman's cottage where a railway worker lived with his family. The last to live here were the Nordgrens: first Ludvig, his wife Kristina and their five children, and then their son Ragnar, a station hand, with his own family until the end of the 1920s. The name lives on in Vinterbrinksvägen.
I skogen väster om idrottsplatsen byggde: In the woods west of the sports ground, a ski slope and ski jump were built in 1932. It burned down in 1950, was repaired, and burned down again. Between the upper secondary school and the sports ground was Äppelviken riding school, from 1920 until it moved to Åkeshov in 1986.
I skogen öster om Baset ligger Basetkärr: In the woods east of Baset lies Basetkärret, the only rich fen in Järfälla. It has been drained and planted with spruce, yet several hundred heath spotted orchids still grow here.
I skogens södra del byggdes 2018–2019 tr: In 2018–2019 three nature playgrounds were built in the southern part of the forest. One of them has a gigantic flying ant and concrete ant eggs to climb on – a nod to the second half of the name Svedmyra, myra being Swedish for ant.
I skulptursamlingen finns verk av bland: The sculpture collection includes works by Gustav Vigeland, Marino Marini, Henri Laurens and Bror Hjorth, among others. They were bought by the chocolate maker Marabou, largely thanks to its art-loving director Henning Throne-Holst.
I slottet finns en praktfull sandstenssp: The castle has a magnificent sandstone fireplace said to have been brought here as war booty from Prague in the mid-1600s. The same room has a ceiling painted in grisaille.
I slottsparken ligger Brygghuset, där gå: In the palace grounds stands Brygghuset, where the estate's laundry was once boiled before being rinsed down at the shore. The singer Magnus Rudbeck converted it into a home in 1946, and today it's a summer café.
I slutet av 1700-talet besöktes dårhuset: In the late 18th century the asylum was visited by Francisco de Miranda, who fought for the independence of Venezuela, Colombia and Ecuador. In his diary he wrote that the building was comfortably and thoughtfully designed.
I slutet av 1700-talet låg värdshuset Kr: In the late 18th century the Kräftriket inn stood nearby. Carl Michael Bellman, Sweden's great song poet, describes the tavern and the rural area outside the Roslagstull toll gate – also known as Kattrumpstullen – in Fredman's Epistle No. 80.
I slutet av 1800-talet blev Curmanska vi: In the late 1800s the Curman villa became a hub of Stockholm's cultural social life. The Curman family owned the house until the 1950s. Today it's the Thai embassy, while the neighbouring villa at number 1 houses Malaysia's.
I slutet av 1800-talet bodde Johan Augus: In the late 19th century Johan August Löf, known as Lötgubben, lived alone by the lake in a home-made earth hut with windows facing the water. The walls were papered with the newspaper Stockholms-Tidningen. He called it Löfhyddan and lived there for almost 30 years.
I slutet av 1800-talet byggdes sommarvil: In the late 1800s, the summer villa Rasta was built here with a magnificent park. When it became surrounded by oil tanks, the owner had had enough and sold up to Shell. The villa was torn down in the 1960s, but the name lives on in the Rasta tanks and the Rasta block.
I slutet av 1800-talet fick huset liggan: In the late 1800s the house was given horizontal cladding, fretwork decoration and green oil paint in two shades. When it was renovated in 2015, the original colour scheme was recreated with help from Stockholm City Museum. The north wing burned down in the 1960s and was replaced by a simpler building.
I slutet av 1800-talet stod vid torget e: In the late 1800s a wooden house on the square was known as Lilla Helvetet, "Little Hell" – a corruption of the property's old name, Hellewe. Opposite, where Bangatan begins, stood a small house popularly called Himmelriket, "Heaven". Both were pulled down when the square was enlarged in the 1880s.
I slutet av 1800-talet var Styrsö en eft: In the late 1800s Styrsö was a sought-after seaside resort, as sea air was considered good for your health. The well-to-do mostly bathed here at Styrsö Bratten, which had hotels as well as both warm and cold bathhouses.
I slutet av 1920-talet gick en båt på lö: In the late 1920s, a boat left Stockholm City Hall on Saturday evenings and came here via the Karlberg Canal for the dancing, then took everyone home again. Each dance cost a few öre, but there was no entry fee. The dance floor closed in 1941, and today the lawn is used for picnics and sunbathing.
I slutet av 1940-talet byggdes de första: The first blocks of flats in Viggbyholm went up in the late 1940s – star-shaped buildings known as stjärnhus. In the late 1960s another 600 flats were added at Viggbygärdet.
I slutet av 1940-talet köpte Volvo ön, o: Volvo bought the island in the late 1940s, and in the early 1950s built a holiday resort for its employees, with a cluster of cabins, a restaurant, a kiosk and places to swim. Three trade unions within the Volvo group ran it until 1990.
I slutet av 1960-talet bodde cirka 5 000: By the late 1960s around 5,000 people lived in Grindtorp. The streets have heavenly names: alongside Grindtorpsvägen there are Kometvägen and Meteorvägen – Comet Road and Meteor Road.
I slutet av 1960-talet byggde Pripps sit: In the late 1960s Pripps built its big brewery near Huvudsta Bridge. The brewery is gone, and the premises now house a hypermarket and a wholesale centre. Since 2013 there's also been a depot for 56 trams at Johannesfred.
I slutet av 1970-talet var Rågsved den v: In the late 1970s Rågsved was the most important place in the Swedish punk movement, centred on the Oasen music club. In the premises now occupied by Nya Rågsveds Folkets Hus, you can still see the first posters for gigs by Ebba Grön, KSMB and Helikoptern kräks.
I slutet av 2010-talet började Karlatorn: Construction of Karlatornet began in the late 2010s; at 246 metres, it's Sweden's tallest building. Once complete, Karlastaden is expected to be the most densely populated part of Gothenburg.
I slutet av 2019 började arbetet med att: At the end of 2019 work began on laying track for the Kista branch of the Tvärbanan light rail, which will have a stop on Rissne torg.

In late 2019, work began on laying track for the Kista branch of Tvärbanan, the cross-city light rail line. It will have its own stop right in the middle of Rissne torg, so soon you'll be able to change between metro and tram here.
I slutet av Gröndalsvägen ligger ett sto: At the end of Gröndalsvägen lies a 392-kilo stock anchor. It was raised from Mörtviken bay in 1998 and dates from the shipyard era.
I socknen finns omkring 170 fornlämninga: The parish has around 170 ancient sites, roughly 100 of them Stone Age settlements. At Tumlehed there are rock paintings of four ships, a deer and four fish, probably also from the Stone Age.
I socknen har man hittat boplatser och t: Stone Age settlements and two stone cists have been found in the parish. From the Iron Age there are stone settings, a judgement ring – a circle of standing stones – and a hillfort.
I socknen har man hittat drygt 35 stenål: More than 35 Stone Age settlements and three stone cists have been found in the parish. The Bronze Age left burial cairns and around ten rock carvings, and there's an Iron Age hill fort too.
I socknen har man hittat ett 60-tal bopl: Some 60 settlements, a dolmen and two stone cists from the Stone Age have been found in the parish. The Bronze Age left burial cairns and a couple of rock carvings, and the Iron Age seven burial grounds and a hill fort.
I socknen har man hittat ett trettiotal: Around thirty Stone Age settlements have been found in the parish, and from the Iron Age there are eight burial grounds and a hill fort. The landscape alternates between plains along the Kvillebäcken stream and wooded rocky plateaus to the west.
I socknen har man hittat omkring 35 bopl: Around 35 Stone Age settlements have been found in the parish. From the Bronze Age there are burial cairns and rock carvings, and from the Iron Age two burial grounds and a few stone circles.
I socknen har man hittat över 50 stenåld: More than 50 Stone Age settlements, a dolmen and four stone cists have been found in the parish. From the Iron Age there are 27 burial grounds and four hill forts, and on the Nordre älv river stands the castle ruin of Ragnhildsholmen, also known as Nyklaborg.
I socknen är omkring 170 fornlämningar k: Around 170 ancient sites are known in the parish, about a hundred of them Stone Age settlements. At Tumlehed there are rock paintings of four ships, a deer and four fish, which are probably from the Stone Age too.
I spårvagnens gamla vändslinga fanns två: The tram's old turning loop had two stops. Passengers got off at Källviken, the tram went round the loop, and new passengers got on at Nockeby. When the loop was removed in 1960, Källviken was renamed Nockeby.
I stadsarkitekten Albert Lilienbergs pla: In city architect Albert Lilienberg's 1916 plan, the Majvivan block was to be built around a large enclosed courtyard. But it wasn't built until the mid-1930s, when Functionalism had taken hold, so instead it got an open courtyard between two long rows of buildings.
I studions diskografi finns bland andra: The studio's discography includes Avishai Cohen, Linda Lampenius, Lars Danielsson, and Steve Swallow with the Bohuslän Big Band. Royal wedding music has been recorded here too, with the Stockholm Royal Symphony Orchestra. The company also works in sound design.
I södra Pixbo låg förr herrgårdens hande: Southern Pixbo was once home to the manor's market garden. When terraced houses were built there in the early 1970s, the roads were named after the fruit tree varieties that had grown in the garden.
I södra Sticklinge ligger ett av Lidingö: Southern Sticklinge has one of Lidingö's largest ancient burial grounds, with around 60 graves from the Late Iron Age. A Viking Age shipping lane ran west of Sticklinge udde. When the graves were excavated, all that was found were burnt bones, pottery shards and iron rivets.
I södra Tyresö tar Tyresta nationalpark: In southern Tyresö you reach Tyresta National Park, created in 1993, with primeval forest and clear lakes. After the forest fire of 1999, a completely new species of fly was discovered in the burnt area: the Tyresta fly.
I taket på Midsommarkransens station hän: Hanging from the ceiling of Midsommarkransen station is a wooden midsummer wreath, made in 1979 by local residents under the guidance of three students from Konstfack, the University of Arts, Crafts and Design. The station also has Lisbet Lindholm's Blommor till Midsommarkransen (Flowers for Midsommarkransen) from 1990 and a painted wooden relief by Dag Wallin.
I tjärnen finns gott om småväxt ruda, li: The tarn is full of small crucian carp, along with perch and roach. Life on the bottom is of real conservation value, thanks to rare species such as the water bee, the flat valve snail and a water boatman that goes by the Latin name Sigara scotti.
I torgets södra hörn låg biografen Focus: The Focus cinema stood in the southern corner of the square from 1960. In 1992 the building became Hagsätra Chapel, now Hagsätra Church, and films were shown in a smaller auditorium until 2005. Until the 1990s there was a petrol station with a garage under the square.

The Focus cinema, designed by Kampmann and opened in 1960, stood in the square's southern corner. The building was converted into Hagsätra Chapel, consecrated in 1992, and the cinema carried on in a much-reduced auditorium until 2005.
The staff lived on the tower's lower floor. Despite having 275 cubic metres of water above their heads, they had to fetch their drinking water from the palace courtyard. Their root cellar still stands beside the tower.
I tornrummet ligger en kopia av filosofe: In the tower room, a copy of the philosopher Friedrich Nietzsche's death mask lies in a glass case – Thiel was a great admirer of his. From up here there's a sweeping view over the sea approach to Stockholm.
I trakten finns gott om natur. En bit hä: There's plenty of nature round here. Not far away is the Älta mosse – Strålsjön reserve, created in 1995 and owned and run by Nacka municipality. In the other direction is Stensö, named after the peninsula that used to be an island in Lake Ältasjön, with a swimming spot at its tip.
I trakten finns gott om runor. Vid Sundb: This area is rich in runes. At Sundby is U 80, a large, elaborately carved rock slab, with an unfinished one, U 81, right beside it. Flysta had a Viking Age runestone too, but despite several searches it has never been found and is probably lost. And in the Bromsten industrial area was Fascinate, Sweden's oldest surviving large-scale graffiti painting – until the wall was torn down in early December 2021.
I trakten flyter Lärjeån, som börjar nor: The Lärjeån river runs through the area, rising north of Gråbo and flowing into the Göta älv at Lärjeholm. On the eastern bank of the Göta älv, by the E45 road and the Bergslagsbanan railway, is Agnesberg, an old coaching inn that belonged to Angered municipality until 1967. The railway station arrived in 1880, and industry soon followed.
I trakten ligger Långsjö gård, som på 16: In this area is Långsjö gård. In the 17th century it was a croft belonging to Långbro farm, and it later gave its name to the whole district of Långsjö. Nearby runs Långsjövägen, which partly follows the old Göta landsväg – the highway travellers once took heading south from Stockholm.
I trädgården vid Stocksundstorps gård fi: In the garden at Stocksundstorp farm is Agape, a multi-faith meditation space with art from Buddhist, Jewish, Hindu and Islamic traditions. There has also been a permanent sculpture park here since 2009.
I trähuset i backen har Djurgårdsskolan: Djurgårdsskolan has been in the wooden house on the slope since 1878, making it one of Stockholm's oldest schools. Not far off stand Karl Johans-ekarna, the Karl Johan oaks, where tradition has it the king rested in the 1820s. Slätten, the meadow here, used to attract a colourful crowd, and according to the national librarian Rydqvist, Gustav III himself came here incognito. The poet Bellman is said to have sat beneath an oak, improvising songs on his mandolin.
I tunnelbaneplanen från 1965 fanns en fö: The 1965 metro plan included extending the Bagarmossen line to Bollmora, with a station in Älta. It never happened.
I tävlingsförslaget var fasaderna ljusgr: The competition entry had pale green facades, but they ended up pale pink, with details in white Terrasit render. The building is counted among the breakthrough works of modern architecture in Sweden.
I ungdomshotellet fanns 70 rum för kvinn: The youth hotel had 70 rooms for women and 67 for men. To limit contact between the sections, the lift only stopped at every third floor. Tenants had to be aged 15–21 and could stay on until they turned 24.
I vattentornsbyggnaden fanns två cistern: At the top of the water tower building were two tanks holding 35 cubic metres each, and the water was pumped up from Bällstaviken. The building also housed offices, switchgear and overnight rooms, and the wood-panelled section is still used for overnight stays.
I vattenvaktarstugan bodde förr en vakt: The water keeper's cottage was once home to a watchman whose job was to keep Stockholm's main water pipeline running smoothly between Norsborg waterworks and Nybohov reservoir. The first pipeline was laid in 1902–1904, and it's still one of the city's most important drinking-water mains. Not far away, in Gömmaren nature reserve, there are also the remains of a farm from the middle Iron Age.
I viadukten under Etsarvägen finns mosai: In the underpass beneath Etsarvägen is the mosaic 'Grått i grått' ('Grey on Grey') by Maria Ängquist-Klyvare. It's made from clinker tiles in 16 shades of grey and shows a child bathing – but the image only appears when you look at it from a distance.
I villastaden fanns ingen elektricitet f: The villa suburb had no electricity until the 1920s. The residents' association lit the roads with 'lux' lamps, a type of paraffin lamp. There was no running water or sewerage, and the wells ran dry in dry summers.
I vändslingan framför Hotel Eggers har S: The tram loop in front of Hotel Eggers is the regular stop for the Ringlinien tramway society. In summer and around Christmas you can ride a vintage tram from here to the Liseberg amusement park on the Liseberg line.
I västra Birka ligger Birkahöjden, ett b: In western Birka rises Birkahöjden, a rocky hill of just over two hectares. Two-thirds of it is covered in pine growing on bare rock, and the rest is open slabs. Several pines and oaks here are considered especially worth protecting.
I västra Ösby finns det enda större beva: Western Ösby has the only sizeable surviving area of early functionalist architecture in Danderyd municipality. In the Tjalve block stand owner-built homes from around 1920 by Karl Güettler, built for clerks, craftsmen and workers who wanted a modest villa in Djursholm.
I växthusen växer påsköträdet, Sophora t: The glasshouses are home to the toromiro, Sophora toromiro, from Easter Island. Extinct in the wild, it has survived in cultivation – thanks in part to the Gothenburg Botanical Garden.
I växthusets centralhall växer medelhavs: In the central hall of the greenhouse, Mediterranean plants grow among rocks and terraces around a reflecting pool ringed by columns that recall classical antiquity. Four corner rooms show rainforest and desert, and there's a small café by the entrance for a fika – a coffee and a bite.
I våtmarken vid sjöns nordvästra del bor: A colony of beavers lives in the wetland at the north-western end of the lake. The reserve is also home to the Skarpnäck cave, an ancient hillfort and a sheer cliff with some of Stockholm's hardest climbing routes. The trail around Flaten is six kilometres long.
I Ålstensskogen ligger ett bronsåldersrö: In Ålstensskogen woods, a Bronze Age cairn 8 metres across sits on a rocky ridge. When it was built it stood 15 metres above sea level; thanks to post-glacial land uplift, it's now at 30 metres.
I Årsta har gatorna fått namn efter sven: In Årsta the streets are named after Swedish lakes, like Skagern and Hjälmaren, so a stroll here is almost a geography lesson. Vättersparken used to have a supervised playground, Vättersdälden, which closed in 1992 – but the paddling pool, swings and sandpits are still there. A little further on stands Skagershuset, a block of flats with a wooden façade that was named Stockholm's Building of the Year in 2014.
I Öckerö gamla kyrka är taket målat 1792: In Öckerö's old church, the ceiling was painted in 1792 by Johan Liljedahl: the Holy Trinity, the Last Judgement and Hell. In the vision of hell you can spot a creature resembling a giant stinging jellyfish. The paintings have never been painted over.
I Örtagården på Nordgårdsvägen arbetar m: At Örtagården, the herb garden on Nordgårdsvägen, many volunteers work to preserve garden plants, especially roses of many varieties. On the island's weather-beaten west side there are public bathing spots at Hjälvik and Saltarsviken.
I århundraden gick färjor från Färjenäs: For centuries ferries crossed from Färjenäs to Klippan. Then, at 9 am on 1 April 1967, the last one – the John E. Olson – cast off. The Älvsborg Bridge had opened. The ferry was later converted into a container crane.
I öster reser sig Ekensbergshöjden, 25 m: To the east rises Ekensbergshöjden, 25 metres above sea level, with wide views north and east. There were plans for about ten blocks of flats up here, but the 1944 town plan put a stop to them, so the hill is still undeveloped.
I östra Gudö finns vägbanken kvar efter: In eastern Gudö you can still see the embankment of the old road between Stockholm and Vendelsö, in use until 1922. One of the villas is the former Alliance Chapel, which several free-church congregations shared, and an outbuilding was once a mangle house for pressing laundry.
I östra Högdalen står traditionella folk: In eastern Högdalen stand traditional folkhem buildings from the era of the Swedish welfare state: narrow three-storey blocks around planted courtyards. To the west things get bigger, with tower blocks. Here you can see how 1950s suburban planning moved from small-scale to modern.
I östra delen omges Högalidsgatan av fem: At its eastern end, Högalidsgatan is flanked on both sides by natural stone walls five to seven metres high. They create a streetscape typical of this part of Stockholm, and the street's diagonal line breaks up the grid.
For over 250 years, leather was tanned in this block. When Norr Mälarstrand was built in 1905 the tannery was cut off from the water, and Ernst Willhelm Lundin soaked the very last hide. He marked it SLUT – 'THE END' – on both halves of the tail.
I övergången mellan stadsdelarna vid San: Where the districts meet at Sannaplan, rows of free-standing landshövdingehus – Gothenburg's typical stone-and-wood tenements – were built without courtyards. They were the last of their kind before functionalism took over.
IKEA var först på plats i Kållered köpst: IKEA was the first to arrive at Kållered’s shopping area in 1972, drawing customers from all over western Götaland and Halland. More shops soon sprang up around the store, and in 2023 IKEA opened a brand-new one.
Ibsen och Lagerlöf på besök: Ibsen and Lagerlöf came to visit
Idag finns två åttkantiga pjäsvärn på ci: Two octagonal gun emplacements, each about seven metres across, survive today; each once held a 40 mm Bofors gun. Behind the apartment block at Gullmarsvägen 43–48 you can also see two concrete anti-tank obstacles, known as 'concrete pianos'.
Idag heter färjan M/S Gerd och går var 2: Today the ferry is called M/S Gerd and runs every 20 minutes during the day, and every 15 at rush hour. A few late-night and early-morning crossings have to be booked by phone.
Idrottshallen som aldrig byggdes: The sports hall that never was
Idrottsmuseet har en Hall of Fame med 14: The Sports Museum has a Hall of Fame honouring 148 Gothenburg sporting figures. Besides the objects, it holds around 30,000 photographs and a library with more than 70 metres of shelves of sports literature.
Idrottsplatsen vid Kyrkvikens inre del h: The sports ground at the head of Kyrkviken bay has everything from athletics to ice hockey. But walk a little further and you'll come to Lidingö's oldest farm, Bo gård, whose history goes all the way back to the late Iron Age. Right next to it are the Trisshusen from 1909 – an early type of terraced housing designed by Jacob Gate.
Idtjärnet är bara 0,03 kvadratkilometer: Idtjärnet covers just 0.03 square kilometres. Even so, like the bigger lakes up here, it belongs to the main catchment of the Göta älv river.
Idén att lyfta bort våningarna kom från: The idea of lifting off the upper floors came from Helmut Junkers, head of development at the housing company Göteborgshem. The removed building elements were reused in the houses on the Båtsmansgatorna streets in Backatorp, and new buildings on Vegagatan in Linnéstaden were given façade panels from here.
Idén att ställa tre symmetriska flyglar: The idea of placing three symmetrical wings around a stairwell was Backström and Reinius's own. The buildings can stand alone or be joined in a honeycomb pattern around hexagonal courtyards. Gröndal has both versions, and before long the star-shaped blocks were being copied across Europe.
Idén föddes 1983 när kommunen ville skap: The idea came about in 1983, when the city wanted to create jobs and optimism in the region and Skanska wanted to strengthen its position as a builder. Built in 1986–1989, the building served as Skanska's Gothenburg headquarters. Today it is owned by Vasakronan.
Idén föddes i början av 1900-talet, inna: The idea was born in the early 1900s, before the welfare state had taken shape: elderly Freemasons of limited means should have somewhere to live. The initiative was launched in 1910 on a Danish model, with the backing of the order's Grand Master, King Gustaf V. The plot was donated by Hjalmar Arwin, founder of the Lidingö villastad garden suburb.
Idén om kollektivhus fördes fram av Alva: The idea of the kollektivhus – a block of flats with shared services – was put forward by Alva Myrdal in the Professional Women's Club. The plan was that laundresses and cleaners would make sure the family came home to a tidy flat, clean dishes and ironed laundry. In practice, though, the service never lasted.
Idén till museet kom från konstsmeden Ma: The idea for the museum came from the art blacksmith Martin Ahlsén, grandson of the architect Erik Ahlsén, and the local historian Olle Flodby. It opened on 6 December 2008.
Igelbäcken rinner förbi alldeles i närhe: The Igelbäcken stream winds past close by on its 10.5-kilometre journey from Lake Säbysjön to Edsviken bay, and its valley is one of Stockholm's ‘green wedges’ of open countryside reaching into the city. A short way off is Akalla village, a name known since the Middle Ages. The oldest house, Storgården, dates from the 17th century, and today the village has a 4H farm, a café and bike hire – in one of the best-preserved village settings in the Stockholm area.
Igelbäcken är känd för den lilla fisken: Igelbäcken stream is known for the stone loach, a little fish that's rare in these parts. Its discovery in 1985 sparked the idea of a nature reserve. Stockholm Vatten has promised to pump drinking water into the stream during prolonged droughts.
Igelbäcken är känd för fisken grönling,: Igelbäcken is known for the spined loach, a fish rarely found in these parts. Its discovery in 1985 led to the creation of the nature reserve. South-east of Hästa gård is Hästa damm, a pond made in 2007 for the frogs.
Ikeas andra svenska varuhus, efter det i: IKEA's second store in Sweden, after the original in Älmhult, opened here on 18 June 1965. Its round original section was inspired by the Guggenheim Museum in New York, and after later rebuilding and extensions it became the second-largest IKEA in the world by floor space. One of its very first neighbours was the Esso Motorhotell from 1968 – today the Scandic Kungens Kurva hotel.
Ikeas fastighet fick namnet Kurvan och E: IKEA's property was named Kurvan (the Curve) and the Esso hotel Radien (the Radius). The neighbouring blocks carried on the geometric theme with names such as Diagonalen, Kvadraten (the Square), Sekanten and Pyramiden, and the streets include Modulvägen and Tangentvägen.

IKEA's property was named Kurvan (the Curve) and the Esso hotel Radien (the Radius). Then came blocks such as Diagonalen, Kvadraten (the Square), Pyramiden and Sekanten (the Secant), and streets like Modulvägen and Tangentvägen.
Imam Ali-moskén har ett bibliotek med öv: The Imam Ali Mosque has a lending library of more than 3,000 books in several languages. At an open house for local residents in 2017, visitors were treated to calligraphy, an art exhibition, a guided tour and a meze buffet, among other things.
In på 1950-talet sa man Frölanns socken: Into the 1950s people still said Frölanns socken, and the locals were called frölänningar; well into the 1800s they were nicknamed koljenackar, 'haddock necks'. From the 1200s until 1658, Frölunda and Askim were the only part of mainland Sweden that reached the North Sea.
Industrimannen Carl Frans Lundström köpt: The industrialist Carl Frans Lundström bought the plot for his daughter, Calla Curman. Afraid a big apartment block would block the view, he bought the plot opposite too and allowed only a smaller, villa-style house there. That became Villa Sandrew.
Industriområde blev spårvagnshållplats: From industrial estate to tram stop
Industriområdet delades först upp i fyra: The industrial estate was first divided into four blocks with fitting names: Fabriken (the Factory), Förrådet (the Store), Verkstaden (the Workshop) and Hantverket (the Craft). Later additions include Brandstegen (the Fire Escape), Lagret (the Warehouse), Axeln (the Axle) and Tonfisken (the Tuna).
Industriområdet startade 1938 som en for: The industrial area began in 1938 as an extension of Hägerstenshamnen, where Olsson & Rosenlund had a sawmill, brickworks and timber yard. In the 1920s the land was still undeveloped. The harbour and timber yard disappeared in the late 1980s and were replaced by housing.
Inflyttningen började den 7 november 195: The first residents moved in on 7 November 1953, on Månadsgatan and Kalendervägen. Nostalgia for the 1950s lives on at Kortedala museum on Adventsvägen.

The first residents moved in on 7 November 1953, on Månadsgatan and Kalendervägen. While building was under way, delegations came from all over the world, fascinated that ordinary people were getting homes with bathrooms, fully fitted kitchens and parquet floors.
Inför 1980 debatterades om Björn Borg ku: Ahead of the 1980 tournament, people debated whether Björn Borg could win on the hall's fast surface. A temporary carpet was laid, and in a classic final against McEnroe, Borg became the tournament's first Swedish champion.
Inför bygget av radhusområdet Pauli Back: In November 1975, ahead of building the Pauli Backe terraced houses, a ten-metre trench was dug here. No trace of the churchyard turned up. Perhaps it wasn't in exactly this spot – the first maps to show it were drawn almost 100 years later.
Inför friidrotts-VM 1995 hörde Coca-Cola: In the run-up to the 1995 World Athletics Championships, Coca-Cola asked about painting the whole gasholder as a drinks can. The gasholder was also nominated by readers of the GT newspaper as one of Gothenburg's ugliest buildings.
Inför invigningen byggdes en tredje läkt: For the unveiling a third grandstand was built, with tickets costing a couple of days' wages, so ordinary people could barely see a thing. Young men started smashing up the stand, and in the end the Life Guards charged the crowd on horseback. Several people were hurt, but the ceremony went ahead anyway.
Inför nya sjukhuset på Ringön 1967 ordna: In 1967, to raise support for the new animal hospital on Ringön, Harry Hjörne, editor-in-chief of the newspaper GP, organised an animal parade in which more than 35,000 people marched up Avenyn, the city's grand boulevard. Volvo donated a Volvo Duett to carry sick animals.
Inför riksdagsvalet 1962 släpptes den så: Ahead of the 1962 general election came what was dubbed the Järva bombshell: homes for 160,000 people were promised on the Järva field within eight years. Tensta centrum opened just in time for the Christmas shopping in 1969.
Inför sammanslagningen med Stockholm 194: Ahead of the merger with Stockholm in 1949, street names that resembled names elsewhere in the city were weeded out. Strandvägen became Hässelby strandväg, and every street named after birds or Norse mythology vanished.
Inför säsongen 2007/2008 blev Danske Ban: Ahead of the 2007/2008 season, Danske Bank became the club's sponsor and the arena was renamed. The next name change came in spring 2014, to today's Childhood Hallen.
Ingemar Frodbom var källarmästare på Kas: Ingemar Frodbom was cellar master at Kastenhof, the tavern under Norrmalm's town hall. By the end of the 17th century he also owned a house on Drottninggatan, where he ran the Tre Tunnor (Three Barrels) tavern.
Ingemarsgatan har troligen fått sitt nam: Ingemarsgatan is probably named after Ingemar Frodbom, a wine merchant who ran an inn at the Ingemarshof country house in the 1700s. When he died, he left a plot of land to his loyal head waiter, Clas Browall, who in 1731 opened his own inn, Browallshof – today the Clas på Hörnet hotel and restaurant. Incidentally, the surrounding area was nicknamed Siberia, because moving this far out of town felt like being sent into exile.
Ingen anledning att åka in: No reason to go into town
Ingen av de samtida källorna nämner Brän: None of the contemporary sources mentions Brännkyrka. One speaks of a skirmish at 'Aerstede' in a meadow, which has been interpreted as Årsta or Ersta. Several historians point to the Årsta field, and one of them to Valla gärde in particular.
Ingen bild av livet i Olskroken: No portrait of life in Olskroken
Ingen säger Köpstadsö. I dagligt tal het: Nobody actually says Köpstadsö. Everyone calls the island Kössö, and it's famous for its wheelbarrows. Just over a square kilometre in size, with 129 year-round residents in 2020, it's part of Gothenburg's southern archipelago. Look out for the wheelbarrows when you step ashore – they're the island's trademark.
Ingen vet exakt när Landsnora kvarn bygg: No one knows exactly when Landsnora mill was built, but its load-bearing beams date from 1632. The mill and sawmill are considered Sollentuna’s oldest secular buildings – the oldest, that is, apart from churches.
Ingen vet exakt vilken pråm som sjönk vi: Nobody knows exactly which barge sank off Pråmholmen. Since 2017, a bronze sculpture by Martin Karlsson Tebus has stood on the waterfront promenade opposite, showing a cargo barge in the act of sinking.
Ingen vet hur gammal Stuvsta gårds kvarn: No one knows how old the Stuvsta farm mill was or what it looked like, but it was almost certainly a post mill. It was built without permission, so no drawings exist. It fell into disrepair during the 19th century.

Nobody knows how old Stuvsta farm's mill was or what it looked like, though it was surely a post mill. It was built without permission, so there are no drawings. Two millstones are set into the footpath by Kvarnbergsgården.
Ingen vet hur gammal kvarnen var eller h: Nobody knows how old the windmill was or what it looked like, but it was certainly a post mill. It was built without permission, so there are no drawings. The mill is said to have fallen into ruin during the 19th century.
Nobody knows how old the mill was or what it looked like, though it was certainly a post mill. Because it was built without permission, no drawings exist.
Ingen vet var Knuts bro låg. Troligen gi: No one knows where Knut's bridge stood. It probably crossed the low-lying, once marshy land between Jakobsberg and Viksjö, where the Bällstaån stream has its source.
Ingenjör Antenor Nydqvist, ägare till Gö: In 1896 the engineer Antenor Nydqvist, owner of Görväln, no longer wanted to lend the inn out as a school. Instead he donated land in Oxhagen and timber, and the schoolhouse for 42 children opened on 25 October that same year.
Ingenjören Carl Robert Lamm köpte slotte: The engineer Carl Robert Lamm bought the palace in 1902 and had it restored after the fire of 1897, using Tessin's drawings. He built up a large art collection, and works by Bruno Liljefors, Anders Zorn and Carl Milles can still be seen here.
Ingenting fick påminna om en anstalt: in: Nothing was allowed to feel like an institution: no assembly hall, no special rules and no communal meals. The houses were meant to look like pleasant private homes, known as pavilions, and at first living here was free.
Ingmar Bergman gick på Palmgrenska samsk: Ingmar Bergman went to Palmgrenska samskolan and wrote about its teachers in his memoir ‘The Magic Lantern’. The film ‘Hets’ (‘Torment’) is autobiographical and is about the school. Its teachers included Oskar Lindberg and Eric Ericson, and among its pupils was the journalist Ester Blenda Nordström.
Initiativtagare till arkivet 1902 var Os: The archive was founded in 1902 on the initiative of Oscar Borge, who worked at the Stockholm Workers' Library while also being a distinguished marine biologist. Borge ran the archive right up until 1937.
Inloppet till Göteborg har länge bevakat: For centuries, this area has guarded the approach to Gothenburg. On Lilla Billingen, a headland a short way off, you can still see an angular fortification from 1741–1742, and in 1789 a square redoubt was added, with batteries facing the river. Gothenburg's saluting station was here too. The neighbouring hill, Stora Billingen, has military chambers blasted into the rock.
Innan Aspnäs blev skola var huset vägkro: Before Aspnäs became a school, the house was a roadside tavern on Gamla Enköpingsvägen. In 1836 the parish meeting wanted it closed down, and a wholesale merchant pointed to the district court records as proof of 'the disorderly conduct practised there'.
Innan Ekhagen byggdes bodde en förmögen: Before Ekhagen was built, a wealthy wholesale merchant lived in the Ekhagen croft. The local children called it the Castle because it was so big and elegant. The area's five blocks were given names such as Ollonskogen (the Acorn Wood) and Ekstubben (the Oak Stump).
Innan Ersta tog över var Sjötorp ett tvä: Before Ersta took over, Sjötorp was a laundry, like many waterside crofts on Södertörn. Crofting families washed Stockholmers' clothes to earn a little extra. For 20 öre a kilo, well-to-do Stockholmers had their washing collected and delivered to the door.
Innan Frösunda bebyggdes på 1990-talet d: Before Frösunda was built up in the 1990s, the area was dominated by the military, including the Signal Regiment. Some military buildings survive: the old headquarters now houses SIPRI, the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute, and one of the barrack blocks has become a preschool.
Innan Frösunda började bebyggas på 1990-: Before Frösunda started to be built up in the 1990s, the area was given over to the military, home to the Signal Regiment and the Svea Engineer Regiment. In its final years it was known as the Frösunda detachment and housed, among others, the units that served as the royal guard. A little further off is Annelunds gård, where Per Henrik Ling, the father of Swedish gymnastics, lived from 1822 to 1839.
Innan Järfälla fick egen skola gick barn: Before Järfälla had a school of its own, from 1810 to 1845 the children shared one with Spånga parish, housed in a building on the Hjulsta farm estate.
Innan LO köpte huset 1926 rymde det para: Before LO, the Swedish Trade Union Confederation, bought the building in 1926, it housed state apartments and rooms for the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences' Nobel committees, and from 1909 to 1921 the Swedish Academy's Nobel Library. When LO remodelled it, the entrance was given wall frescoes of working-class scenes by Olle Hjortzberg.
Innan Landvetter flygplats byggdes 1977: Before Landvetter Airport was built in 1977, Gothenburg’s main airport was at Torslanda.
Innan Långsjöbadet invigdes 1938 var pla: Before the Långsjöbadet bathing place opened in 1938, the site was marshland with sewage ditches and big alders, and the shore was an impenetrable mass of reeds. Today there's a sandy beach about 50 metres long and a few bathing jetties.
Innan Marieholmstunneln öppnade var Ting: Before the Marieholm Tunnel opened, the Tingstad Tunnel about 700 metres to the south was overloaded, carrying more than 120,000 vehicles a day. The new tunnel is roughly 500 metres long, with three lanes in each direction.
Innan Nacka Forum fanns här köpcentrumet: Before Nacka Forum, this was the site of Skvaltan, a makeshift shopping centre in temporary huts that ended up staying for twenty years. The centre's real name was Forum Nacka, but everyone said Nacka Forum, and in 2010 the name was officially changed.
Innan Sankt Eriksmässan hade en egen hal: Before the Sankt Erik trade fair had a hall of its own, the tennis hall was rented for exhibitions. At the fair in September 1944, the Volvo PV 444 was shown here for the very first time.
Innan Segeltorps första skola byggdes 19: Before Segeltorp's first school was built in 1917, children had to walk to Vårby school on Södertäljevägen, just south of today's Kungens kurva. It was a long way, and there was no public transport. The teacher lived in the school attic.
Innan Stureby valdes diskuterades att dö: Before the name Stureby was chosen, there was talk of naming the community after the crofts Bjule, Rothugget or Tussmötet, but these were not thought suitable. The Tussmötet croft was demolished in 1937 to make way for the Corso cinema, which was first called Tusse-bio.
Innan Torslanda flög man från Kvibergs h: Before Torslanda airport, planes took off from Kvibergs hed, an open heath. It was there, on 23 March 1911, that the Belgian René Cozic made a five-minute test flight in a biplane he had built himself. It needed just 30 metres to take off and land.
Innan bostadsområdet byggdes fanns här b: Before the housing area was built, there was nothing here but forest and the odd crofter's cottage. In 1967 work began on 14 eight-storey slab blocks and a larger number of three-storey apartment buildings.
Innan bron kom 1925 hade Norra och Södra: Before the bridge arrived in 1925, the Northern and Southern Lidingö railways each had their own ferry landing, at Islinge and Herserud. Only once the bridge was built did they start coordinating their timetables – but the wait could still be long, which is why the shelter was needed.
Innan den första riktiga kyrkan invigdes: Before the first proper church was consecrated in 1633, a temporary one stood here: Brädekyrkan, the Plank Church, one of the city's very first buildings. Gustav II Adolf paid for the building work with a barrel of grain from every church farm in Västergötland, for several years running.
Innan det renade vattnet når Saltsjön pa: Before the treated water reaches the Saltsjön, it passes through the Norrenergi heat-pump plant at Bällstaviken. There the residual heat is captured and turned into district heating and cooling for Solna and Sundbyberg.
Innan familjen Palme flyttade hit bodde: Before the Palme family moved here, they lived next door at Tornedalsgatan 18. That's where, in 1967, Vilgot Sjöman filmed his interview with Olof Palme about the class system for I Am Curious (Yellow).
Innan familjen Palme flyttade till Atlan: Before the Palme family moved to Atlantis, they lived in a terraced house at Tornedalsgatan 18. That's where, in 1967, the director Vilgot Sjöman came to film his much-discussed interview with Olof Palme about class society for the film I Am Curious (Yellow).
Innan förstaden fanns bara några torp hä: Before the suburb was built there were only a few crofts here, among them Grönbrink, which served as an inn from 1755 to 1849. It stood at what is now the junction of Södertäljevägen and Hägerstensvägen and was demolished in 1964.
Innan gatan fick namnet Scheelegatan 188: Before it was named Scheelegatan in 1885, the street was called Trädgårdsgatan (Garden Street) because of the many gardens here. As a cross street it was also known as tvärgränden, "the cross alley", or simply gränden. It wasn't extended north to Barnhusbron bridge until the 1970s.
Innan husen kom fanns här en parkering,: Before the houses arrived, there was a car park, a clubhouse and a small patch of green next to Skarpnäck's football pitch. The city wanted to grow inwards, placing new homes within existing neighbourhoods. The plot was just under 3,000 square metres.
Innan kyrkan byggdes 1972 höll man gudst: Before the church was built in 1972, services were held in a grey wooden hut known as Edsbergsgården. The 2004 altarpiece is a painted steel cross surrounded by coloured glass, designed by the architect Lars Olof Torstensson and his son Jonas.
Innan kyrkan byggdes användes en proviso: Before the church was built, the congregation used a temporary church from 1965 – the first 'travelling church' in Sweden, designed to be moved. Once Brunnsbo Church was finished in 1972, it was taken down and rebuilt elsewhere as Furåsen Church.
Innan kyrkan byggdes hölls gudstjänstern: Before the church was built, services had been held since around 1960 in a grey wooden hut called Edsbergsgården. The organ was built in 1972 in Hillerød, Denmark, and is the first the church has ever had.
Innan man började dika ut på 1700-talet: Before drainage began in the 18th century, the field was waterlogged and heavy with clay. The draining led to long disputes over water with the mill owners at Nacka ström. The conflict only ended in 1888, when the owners of Skarpnäck bought the entire mill complex.
Innan partihallarna byggdes grävde arkeo: Before the wholesale market halls were built, archaeologists spent eleven months digging here in 1958–1959. They found several burial grounds and some 400 ancient remains. The cup-mark stone, about 1.5 metres tall, originally stood around 500 metres west-south-west of where it is now and was moved when the area was developed.
Innan partihallarna byggdes pågick utgrä: Before the wholesale market halls were built, excavations went on for eleven months in 1958–1959. Around 400 ancient remains were found, including a cup-marked stone that now stands outside Fiskhallen 2, the fish hall.
Innan punkthusen planerades här ett områ: Before the tower blocks, the plan was for an area of many small villa plots called Västra Förstaden, and a few villas did get built. The developer of the first phase was Einar Joel Örell, head of AB Elektroljus, which owned most of the land.
Innan sjösänkningen låg Hammarby sjö och: Before the water level was lowered, Hammarby sjö and Sicklasjön were at the same height. Until 1913 the steam launch Nackanäs ran from Södermalm to the popular Nackanäs inn. When the inn lost its licence to sell spirits, the service stopped.
Innan skolhuset byggdes trängdes elevern: Before the schoolhouse was built, pupils were squeezed into the premises of Djurgården Church – by 1876 there were 217 of them. Where the school stands today there used to be an alehouse, and when it was pulled down the parents saw their chance to build a proper school.
Innan tunnelbanan kom stannade spårvagns: Before the metro came, tram line 19 stopped here, at Enskedefältet. On 9 September 1951 the tram stop gave way to the metro station, and today the trains cross Sockenvägen on a viaduct. Next door is Enskedefältets skola, a school designed by Paul Hedqvist and built in 1933. A little further off was the Enskede ski jump, where in 2016 the district council decided to build a viewpoint.
Innan tunnelbanan tog över trafikerades: Before the metro took over, the line was served from 1956 by trams, routes 14 and 17. An aerial photo from the early 1960s shows the station under construction and the trams' turning loop.
Innanför lekplatsen vid korsningen Jätte: Just behind the playground at the corner of Jättestensgatan and Baltzersgatan you'll find älvkvarnar, or 'elf mills' – ancient cup marks hollowed into the rock.
Inside the playground at the corner of Jättestensgatan and Baltzersgatan are "fairy mills" – ancient hollows ground into the rock, right in the middle of the housing estate.
Just beyond the playground at the corner of Jättestensgatan and Baltzersgatan are älvkvarnar, ancient cup marks carved into the rock – prehistoric remains right in the middle of the housing estate.
Innanför tegelväggarna i olika röda nyan: Behind brick walls in assorted shades of red, the church interior takes its cue from a medieval basilica. The open roof trusses are hand-hewn pine from Norrland in the north, and the altar, pulpit and pews are solid oak.
Inne finns en 60 meters sprintbana och e: Inside there's a 60-metre sprint track and a banked 200-metre track that tilts up to 11.3 degrees on the bends. Every track is surfaced with recycled car tyres.
Inne i Folksamhuset finns konst av bland: Inside the Folksam building is art by Isaac Grünewald, Carl Eldh and Barbro Nilsson, among others. The swimming pool is decorated with Bengt Olson's tile paintings, made up of 18,000 French tiles.
Inne i Fredhällsberget, alldeles intill,: Right beside us, the Essingeleden motorway roars through the Fredhäll tunnel deep inside Fredhällsberget hill, then carries straight on over the 270-metre Fredhäll bridge across the Mariebergssundet strait. Up above ground it's much calmer. Leafy Rudbecksparken is full of oak trees, and Fredhäll primary school, designed by Paul Hedqvist and opened in 1938, has been given a green listing for its heritage value by the City Museum.
Inne i berget en bit härifrån döljer sig: Hidden away inside the rock not far from here is Aeroseum, an aviation experience centre in an underground cavern. It was once the rock hangar of the Göta Wing, one of only five ever built for the Swedish Air Force. Since 2000, visitors have been able to head down into the bunker and get up close to aviation history.
Inne i berget en bit härifrån gömmer sig: Hidden inside the rock nearby is Vargen, the Wolf, a secret nuclear-proof command centre from the 1970s with room for 200 people. It was built to shelter the leaders of Stockholm and Huddinge in the event of war, but it was eventually decommissioned and turned into a data centre. North of Stockholm it has an almost identical twin called Elefanten, the Elephant. Nearby Lake Lissmasjön has shrunk to a third of its original size after several attempts to drain it.
Inne i berget fanns plats för fyra insat: Inside the rock there was room for four emergency vehicles. To turn them in the cramped space there was a turntable, like the ones used on the railways, rotated by hand with poles. Next to it was the command centre, with beds for about 60 people.
Inne i berget valdes färgerna för att sk: Inside the rock, the colours were chosen to create a sense of calm. In some rooms a horizon was painted to evoke a landscape; one canteen got a blue sky above, another green meadows below. Over the tables hangs the Hinken (Bucket) lamp, a design classic from 1970.
Inne i den runda kupolen mot Observatori: Inside the round dome facing Observatorielunden park are four small elliptical floors of bookshelves and reading spaces, linked by a spiral staircase. They're known as the Book Tower. Below lies the elliptical lecture hall, which seats 300.
Inne i hallen möter du en kolossal Gusta: Inside the great hall you're greeted by Carl Milles's colossal Gustav Vasa. When the museum opened in 1907 the statue existed only in plaster – it wasn't finished in painted and gilded oak until 1925.
Inne i huset har källaren kryssvalv från: Inside, the cellar has cross vaults from the 1700s, and a plaque in the hall records how the house came to be built. One room has an 18th-century tiled stove brought here from Lärjeholm manor; before that, it stood in the vicarage of the German Church.
Inne i kapellet har väggarna horisontell: Inside the chapel, the walls are lined with horizontal bands that get narrower as they rise. Light enters through a slim strip of windows between wall and ceiling, and angled pine pews stand on a limestone floor.

Inside the chapel, the walls are lined with horizontal bands that grow steadily narrower. A slim strip of windows between wall and ceiling lets in the light, and the angled pine pews stand on a limestone floor.
Inne i kyrkan dominerar det blåmålade ta: Inside the church, the eye is drawn to the blue-painted ceiling and the blue glass mosaic on the chancel wall by Elsa Hansson-Winnberg. The altar and font are made of white concrete and marble.
Inne möts puts, stål och glas av stavlim: Inside, render and steel meet walls of glued laminated pine and a floor of grey limestone. The benches have steel frames and pine bodies, upholstered in chrome-tanned leather.
Inne på gravfältet finns en sentida rist: Within the burial ground is a fairly recent carving with a circular ornament, an unfinished human figure and the letters IOGT. It's linked to the neighbouring Björklundstorpet, which was for a time the meeting hall of a temperance organisation.
Inom Härryda kommun ligger Göteborg-Land: Härryda municipality is home to Göteborg Landvetter Airport, Sweden's second-largest international airport – and the municipality's biggest workplace.
Inom Tibble låg kapplöpningsbanan Täby G: Tibble was home to the Täby Galopp racecourse until 2016, when it was replaced by Bro Park in Upplands-Bro. The site is set to become the Täby park housing area. The name Tibble comes from a farm that once stood here.
Inom reservatet finns lämningar av odlin: Within the reserve are remains of fields and buildings from the 18th and 19th centuries, as well as prehistoric burial cairns.
Inomhustorget får dagsljus genom två sad: The indoor square is lit by daylight through two saddle-shaped roof lanterns and a fully glazed south gable. On the floor below the shops, Vårberg's flea market has had its sales space since 2005.
Inomhustorget i Huvudsta Centrum var ins: The indoor square at Huvudsta Centrum was the setting for several scenes in the youth drama Lycka till! (Good Luck!), shown on Swedish Television in 1980.
Inre Kyrkviken anses vara platsen där de: Inre Kyrkviken is thought to be where the first settlers on Lidingö made their home. A thousand years ago the sea stood about five metres higher, so their settlements were close to the shore. The bay takes its name from Lidingö Church at its far end.
Inredningen från stora salen och ett för: The interiors of the great hall and a drawing room were donated to the Röhsska Museum of design and applied art, where they stayed from 1916. In 1994 the rooms were moved back to the manor. For a time the house was also a boarding school for girls, run by the Misses Zander until 1871.
Inredningen i kyrkorummet, bland annat k: The furnishings of the church interior, including the cross Nålsögat – the Needle's Eye – in the chancel, were designed by Fritz Sjöström.
Inredningen är helt mobil, med flyttbar: The interior is entirely mobile, with a movable pulpit and chairs instead of fixed pews. Behind the altar hang textiles by Kaisa Melanton, and in 1991 the roof was given a weathercock in black sheet metal.
Insamling med 25-öresrutor: Raising funds 25 öre at a time
Insekterna har det lyxigt i Kikås. Vid K: In Kikås, the insects live in luxury. By the lake Kikås Långvatten is Sweden's largest free-standing insect hotel, built to boost biodiversity, especially for wild bees, butterflies and birds. Kikås is the name of the high ridge on the southern shore of Lake Stensjön, and Fågelberg church is not far from here.
Insektshotellet vid Södra Långvattnet, i: The insect hotel by Södra Långvattnet, now known as Kikås Långvatten, is there to boost biodiversity, with a focus on wild bees, butterflies and birds.
Insjön har en yta på knappt en halv kvad: Insjön covers just under half a square kilometre and lies only 1.4 metres above sea level. The whole lake is part of the Velamsund nature reserve.
Inskriften berättar att Åsgöt lät resa s: The inscription tells us that Åsgöt had the stone raised in memory of her husband. The carver is unknown, but the stone dates from some time between 1060 and 1100. It's grey granite and stands 110 centimetres tall.
Inskriften berättar: ”Helga lät resa ste: The inscription reads: “Helga had the stone raised in memory of Svärting, her husband, and of Östen and of Häming, her sons.” The carver was called Igulfast. A piece of the top is missing, and with it about ten runes.
Inskriften lyder i nusvensk översättning: In modern English the inscription reads: "Tägn and Dan had the stone raised in memory of Torsten, their father, and Gunvar in memory of her husband." The rune serpent frames a Christian cross, and judging by the style, the carver was probably Fot.
Inskriften lyder i översättning: \"Spjal: Translated, the inscription reads: 'Spjallbode and Une had the stone raised in memory of Tidkume, Ingetora's (husband).' Together with U 89, it's known as the Häradsvägen runestones.
Inskriften lyder ungefär: Åfrid lät hugg: The inscription reads roughly: “Åfrid had the slab carved in memory of Svarthövde and Igulfast, her sons, and of Åsgöt.” A rune animal in the carving suggests it was made in the late 11th century.
Inskriften på Kistastenen lyder i översä: Translated, the inscription on the Kista Stone reads: 'Sigvid had this stone raised in memory of his father Egvid and his mother Holmfrid, and Jovurfrid.' The woman's name Jovurfrid is very rare and known almost only from here.
Inskriften på Kvarntorpshällen lyder: Is: The inscription on the Kvarntorp rock reads: Isa had the stone carved in memory of her stepsons, and Helga had it carved in memory of her sons Dan and Sven. The carving is faint and partly worn away.
Inskriften på U 127 lyder: \"Jarlabanke: The inscription on runestone U 127 reads: "Jarlabanke had these stones raised in memory of himself while alive, and made this bridge for his soul, and alone owned all of Täby." In other words, he put up his own memorial while he was still very much alive.
Inskriften på U 78 lyder: \"Hosve och Si: The inscription on runestone U 78 reads: "Hosve and Sigrid and Kättilö had this stone raised in memory of Holmsten, their brother." A large piece of the stone is missing, but thanks to a 17th-century drawing by Martin Aschaneus, the whole text has been reconstructed.
Inskriften på U 88 lyder: \"Spjallbode o: The inscription on U 88 reads: "Spjallbode and Une had the stone raised in memory of Tidkume, Ingetora's (husband)."
Inskriften på Ängbystenen lyder ungefär:: The inscription on the Ängby stone reads roughly: 'Udd had the stone raised in memory of Björn, Ingrid's father. He was Vide's heir.' The end is damaged and has been lost. The stone is gneiss and about 2.3 metres tall.
Inspektorsbostaden byggdes troligen 1785: The inspector's residence was probably built in 1785–1787 for the palace gardener Johan Daniel Happée, who worked at Drottningholm for no less than 45 years, from 1770 to 1815.
Institutet hör till Kungliga Vetenskapsa: The institute belongs to the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences and invites researchers from all over the world. It also publishes the journals Acta Mathematica and Arkiv för Matematik.
Inte en enda av gravarna på Edsängen har: Not one of the graves at Edsängen has been excavated by archaeologists. The burial ground probably came into use as early as the Early Iron Age.
Inte långt härifrån ligger Anstalten Sag: Not far from here is Anstalten Sagsjön, a women's prison in Lindome. It takes its name from Sagsjön, a little further on – a tiny, very shallow lake, just 1.5 metres deep, that sits 20 metres above sea level and drains into the Kungsbackaån river basin.
Inte långt härifrån reser sig tre konstg: Not far from here rise three man-made hills, built up from demolition rubble and bulky rubbish. The first, Högdalstoppen, was finished in 1964, and the rock on that spot had previously been the highest point in Högdalen and Fagersjö. Today the summits are an outdoor recreation area with a skatepark and a disc golf course. Högdalstoppen 3 is still growing, topped up with soil dug out during road building.

Intill Fanfaren låg restaurangen Postilj: Next to Fanfaren was the Postiljonen restaurant. It has long since closed, but you can still see its statue of a mounted postilion in the covered indoor square.
Intill Rinkeby Östergård ligger Länsmans: Next to Rinkeby Östergård is Länsmansgården, home of Danderyd's district police chief in the 1920s. Opposite stands the old lock-up, a small 18th-century log building. Both were moved in 1968 when the motorway was built.
Intill Stora Torp ligger Delsjö golfbana: Delsjö golf course lies right next to Stora Torp. By the fourth tee there's a grave where the estate's owners buried their hunting dogs.
Intill kvarnen finns en dansbana och en: Next to the mill there's an open-air dance floor and a hut selling coffee during events. The millstones are on the upper floor, while the ground floor houses the lifting gear that supports the rotating upper stone.
Intill kyrkogården ligger Backa skola, e: Next to the churchyard is Backa School, also called Askimsskolan, built in 1865 and extended in 1926. To the north of the school stands Mikaelskyrkan, from 1976.
Intill kyrkogården ligger Backa skola, ä: Next to the churchyard stands Backa skola, also known as Askimsskolan, built in 1865 and extended in 1926. Just north of the school is Mikaelskyrkan, St Michael's Church, from 1976.
Invalidkyrkogården: Invalidkyrkogården, the old military veterans' cemetery
Invid Medborgarhusets trappa står ett mo: Beside the steps of Medborgarhuset stands a glass monument designed by Leif Bolter in memory of Anna Lindh. It was here that the foreign minister gave her last speech on 9 September 2003, and the monument was unveiled on the anniversary in 2004.
Invigd av kronprinsen 1923: Opened by the Crown Prince in 1923
Invigningen av Sveriges då största stads: The opening of what was then Sweden's largest district centre drew more than 100,000 people. Among the 1,200 specially invited guests were Princesses Sibylla and Margaretha.
Invigningen den 27 oktober 2012 var en f: The opening on 27 October 2012 was a show in 22 acts, ‘Svenska ögonblick’ (Swedish Moments), directed by Colin Nutley. Roxette and Sven-Ingvars sang, and Crown Princess Victoria gave a speech.
Invigt av kungaparet: Opened by the King and Queen
Isa och Helga minns sina söner: Isa and Helga remember their sons
Isfabriken gav hållplatsen namn: The ice factory that named the stop
Ishallen en bit härifrån blev känd i hel: The ice rink a short way from here became famous across Sweden thanks to the TV series HCZ. It has changed its name several times: first Dalénhallen, after the inventor Gustaf Dalén and the nearby AGA factory, then Danske Bank Hallen, and now Childhood Hallen. Lidingö Vikings Hockey Club play here, and figure skaters train here too.
Isjakter på den forna sjön: Ice yachts on the vanished lake
Isklassad kryssare blev hamnbåt: From ice-class cruiser to harbour boat
Islandstorget fick sitt namn 1936, men d: Islandstorget, Iceland Square, got its name in 1936 – but not because of exiled Icelanders or fishmongers. The connection is vaguer than that: when the streets and squares of Norra Ängby were being named, the planners drew inspiration from the ancient remains in the area. From the autumn of 1944, trams on the Ängby line, route 11, turned round here. A short walk away is Björklunds hage, the burial ground of Viking Age Ängby.
Isolda byggdes för Göteborgsrederiet Kor: Isolda was built for the Gothenburg shipping firm Korn & Kjellberg and rigged as a three-masted schooner without topsails. She only called at her home port now and then, to load timber or be inspected.
Ivar Tengbom ritade också bankhuset för: Ivar Tengbom also designed the Enskilda Bank building and the Stockholm School of Economics. Together with his partner Ernst Torulf he designed the Hagalund water tower in Solna, built in 1911.
Ivar Tengbom ritade väntkuren som ett li: Ivar Tengbom designed the waiting shelter as a small neoclassical round temple in wood, with a gilded sun on a tall spire. It was originally open on the Stockholm side – hence its draughty nickname.

Ivar Tengbom designed the tram shelter as a small Neoclassical round temple in wood, topped by a gilded sun on a tall spire. The temple was originally open on the Stockholm side, which is where its nickname comes from. When the old bridge is demolished, the temple is to be moved, restored and lit up.
Ivar Tengboms blå konserthus från 1926 h: Ivar Tengbom's blue Concert Hall from 1926 turns its classical colonnade towards the bustling square rather than Sveavägen – quite deliberately. It's considered one of the finest examples of Swedish 1920s Classicism. In front of the steps stands Carl Milles' Orpheus group.
J.G. Törnblom tog över Viksjö gård 1870,: J.G. Törnblom took over Viksjö farm in 1870, first as a tenant and then as owner. He invested in the farm, building a new cowshed, a sawmill and a crosscut saw powered by a portable steam engine.
J.V. Svenson ville egentligen bygga bila: J.V. Svenson really wanted to build cars here. But by the time the factory was finished it was harder than expected to keep up with car development, so while waiting for a good design he started making paraffin hot-bulb engines instead, under the name Avance.
Jacob Gate ritade villan 1917 i italieni: Jacob Gate designed the villa in 1917 in Italian-inspired classicism, with yellow pebble-dash render, a colonnade of bush-hammered granite and Ionic columns in oak. The name Villa Brevik only came along in the 1990s.

Jacob Gate designed the villa in 1917 in an Italian-inspired Classical style. It has yellow roughcast render, a colonnade in pale bush-hammered granite and large windows adorned with Ionic capitals carved in oak. The name Villa Brevik only came along in the 1990s.
Jakobs stege fick sitt namn 1924. Trappa: Jakobs stege – Jacob's Ladder – got its name in 1924. The stairway is an important route for people walking to and from Fridhemsbryggan, the jetty down on Lake Mälaren.
Jakobs stege är en trappa med 187 granit: Jakobs stege, or Jacob's Ladder, is a flight of 187 granite steps leading down towards Lake Mälaren, named after the biblical patriarch Jacob's dream of a ladder reaching from earth to heaven. Nearby is Bellmanskällan, a spring that local tradition says is the one the poet Carl Michael Bellman sings about in Fredman's Epistle No. 82, “Vila vid denna källa” – Rest by this spring. The water still trickles out, if slowly, and it's safe to drink.
Jakobsberg är uppkallat efter majoren Ja: Jakobsberg is named after Major Jakob Lilliehöök, who died in October 1657, just six months after marrying Brita Cruus. His widow named the estate Jakobsberg in his honour and lived on there for almost 60 years.

Jakobsberg is named after Major Jakob Lilliehöök, who married Brita Cruus in March 1657 and died just six months later. His widow named the manor Jakobsberg in his honour and lived on there for almost 60 years.
Jakobsbergs Centrum, alldeles intill, är: Right here is Jakobsbergs Centrum, Järfälla's big shopping centre, with around sixty shops as well as homes and offices under the same roof. A couple of minutes away stands Gula villan, the Yellow Villa, the old station building from 1876, and where Vasavägen meets Ynglingavägen is Maria kyrka, St Mary's Church.
Jakobsbergs centrum är bilfritt. För att: Jakobsberg's town centre is car-free, and concrete sheep are dotted around to keep traffic out. Together with the windmill, the Järfälla sheep is the municipality's best-known symbol – it even appears on the coat of arms.
Jakobsbergs folkhögskola: Jakobsbergs folkhögskola, the folk high school
Jakobsbergs gård var från början ett tor: Jakobsbergs gård started life in the early 17th century as a croft belonging to the Sätra estate. The manor-like house was added in the 1750s, when the farm had become a summer retreat for well-off Stockholmers, and today the City Museum gives it a blue heritage rating. Down by the water is Mälarhöjdsbadet, a public beach that, despite its name, isn't in Mälarhöjden at all but in Bredäng.
Jakobsbergs kvarn från 1840-talet hade o: Jakobsberg's windmill from the 1840s had no luck with fire: it burned in 1980, 1997 and 2005, and after that third blaze it was never rebuilt. Next to it, in the buildings of the old manor, is Jakobsbergs folkhögskola, a folk high school for adult education. Two runestones in the park were moved here from the lands of Vibble farm, and one of them tells us that Gunnvar and Kättilfrid had the stone raised.
Jakobsbergs kvarn var en så kallad hollä: Jakobsberg mill was a Dutch-style windmill, where only the cap with its sails turned to face the wind. It was ten-sided and tapered towards the top. A photo from 1919 shows six sails, but a postcard from 1926 only four.
Jakobsbergs simhall hade fyra bassänger: Jakobsberg swimming baths had four pools and a five-metre diving tower, plus a Roman bath and a solarium. It closed on 28 March 2018, two weeks before the new Järfällabadet opened next door.
Jakobsbergs sporthall stod klar 1967 och: Jakobsberg sports hall was completed in 1967 and is home to teams including Järfälla Basket. The club was founded in 1973, and its men's team was already playing in the top division, Elitserien, by 1981, with the women's team following a year later. Since a refurbishment in 2009, the main hall holds about 1,100 people. A stone's throw away is Järfällabadet, the swimming centre that opened in 2018.
Jakobssalen och dansgolvet: The Jakob room and the dance floor
Jaktplan och skyddsrum i berget: Fighter planes and a shelter in the rock
James Turrells ljusverk Dawning från 199: James Turrell's light installation Dawning from 1992 was, until 2020, the only artwork on permanent display at Magasin III. Since 2017 the museum has also had a permanent satellite exhibition space in Jaffa.
Jan-Pers stuga från senare 1700-talet är: Jan-Per's cottage, from the late 18th century, is the only building left from the old farming village of Vällingby. It's named after the farm owner Jan Persson and is now a handicraft studio.
Jarlabankes sten berättar att Häming och: Jarlabanke's stone tells how Häming and Jarlabanke cleared a road and built bridges in memory of their father, and how Estrid did the same for her sons Ingefast and Ingvar. The stone ends with the words: May God help their souls.
Jarlabergs vattentorn är 47,5 meter högt: Jarlaberg water tower stands 47.5 metres tall and has been a landmark in south-east Stockholm ever since it was finished in 1987. A little further on, in Augustendal, Johan Victor Svenson bought two old summer houses in 1899, planning to build a car factory. But car technology was moving too fast, so he made paraffin engines instead, sold under the name Avance – and they soon became a hit.
Jennyhill från 1862 är det enda huset på: Jennyhill, from 1862, is the only house on the Oakhill estate that predates the palace. The sculptor Christian Eriksson lived there from 1890 to 1908, and in 1910 Boberg had it converted into stables and staff quarters.
Johan Celsing ville först släppa in ljus: Johan Celsing first wanted to let light in from above through skylight shafts, but changed his mind because the building would then steal the show. The church interior is square, 15.7 metres on each side, and the church won the Helgo Prize in 2013.
Johan Celsings vinnande förslag till det: Johan Celsing's winning design for the new crematorium went by the motto 'A stone in the forest'. The façades and roof are clad in brick, and the sloping roof follows the lie of the land. The building opened in 2014.
Johan Oliveholm köpte 1774 en del av Skä: In 1774 Johan Oliveholm bought part of Skälltorps Östergård, the land where the private Friedländer burial ground was later laid out. After 1800, Bäckebol belonged to three related families: the Lindqvists, the Friedländers and the Bratts.
Johan Oliveholm köpte gården 1759 och ge: Johan Oliveholm bought the farm in 1759 and two years later pushed through a major land redistribution across the whole of Lärje village. In the 1830s the stone house gained an extra storey. During the 1940s restoration, designed by Anders Funkquist, the farm buildings were pulled down.
Johan Wedberg från Nora kom till Stockho: Johan Wedberg from Nora came to Stockholm at 17 and found work as an assistant in a grocer's shop. In 1822 he married Anna Gustava Lundblad, heiress to the estate, and Lidingsberg has belonged to the Wedberg family ever since.
Johan von Beijer köpte gården 1655. Hära: Johan von Beijer bought the estate in 1655. The district court warned him that he could lose the estate's tax exemption if he didn't build it handsomely and well. He was probably the one who put up its first buildings worthy of a manor.
Johannebergs vattentorn från 1924 byggde: The Johanneberg water tower from 1924 was turned into housing in 1995, with just two flats on each floor. The top floor is 134 metres above sea level, and for many years these were the highest homes in Gothenburg – until Karlatornet took the record in 2023. All around is Chalmers, a university of technology founded back in 1829.
Johannebergs vattentorn ritades av Eugen: Johanneberg water tower was designed by Eugen Thorburn. Today it has 14 floors with 24 one-room flats, managed by SGS Studentbostäder.
John Lundqvist inspirerades av Albert Ba: John Lundqvist was inspired by Albert Bartholomé's monument Aux Morts in Père-Lachaise cemetery in Paris. A full-scale plaster study was shown at the Stockholm Exhibition of 1930. In the end, Asplund cut an opening in the roof and placed the sculpture beneath it.
Jonsered var ett säteri som från 1830-ta: Jonsered was a noble estate that grew into a mill town under the Gibson family from the 1830s onwards. The brick buildings from its industrial heyday still shape the place, and the Swedish National Heritage Board has designated Jonsered a heritage site of national interest. Nearby is Göta Bio, where the film society Götas Vänner has been running the screenings since 1996.
Jordbruket i Rud lades ner på 1960-talet: Farming at Rud ended in the 1960s, but the village of Grimmered, first mentioned back in 1546, has been preserved. Two complete farms remain, along with three houses and a couple of farm buildings, and the village has been part of the city's conservation programme since 1975.
Josephson inredde huset i 1700-talsstil: Josephson furnished the house in 18th-century style with details rescued from demolitions, including door overpieces from the Gustavian opera house. He had his architect's office on the ground floor and his home above it, and lived here until his death in 1929.
Jubileumsparken anlades till Göteborgs 4: Jubileumsparken, the Jubilee Park, was created for Gothenburg's 400th anniversary. There's a public sauna and a place to swim in the river, and the park is a testing ground for ideas for the new district due to be built around Frihamnen.
Jubileumsparken i Frihamnen växte fram i: Jubileumsparken, the Jubilee Park in Frihamnen, grew up in the run-up to Gothenburg's 400th anniversary as an experiment in city planning. It's home to Hamnbadet, also known as Pöl Harbour, with saltwater pools and a diving tower, and to Allmänna bastun, the public sauna. The sauna is built from recycled materials, its changing rooms are made of 12,000 glass bottles, and it stands four metres above the water. Plans for 5,000 homes on nearby Bananpiren, the Banana Pier, were dropped in 2020 because the ground was too poor to build on.
