Julmarknad på gården: A Christmas market at the farm
Jungfrukammare med ringklocka: A maid's room with a bell
Jungfruplatsen och husen runt torget rit: Jungfruplatsen and the buildings around the square were designed by Johannes Olivegren. When the square opened in 1959, 120 new flats in the area were ready at the same time. It also had a post office, which stayed from 1959 right up until 1996.
Jungfruplatsen, några hundra meter bort,: Jungfruplatsen, a few hundred metres away, was named in 1958 after the constellation Virgo – Jungfrun in Swedish – and opened on 6 December 1959. Built by Wallenstam, it was Mölndal's first proper shopping centre. It's also home to Mölndal's first piece of public outdoor art, Bossanova by Bertil Lundgren, unveiled in 1964. All around, the streets of Bifrost have names linked to farming.
Jungfrusund hette tidigare Jungfruhamn,: Jungfrusund used to be called Jungfruhamn, and the strait was a narrow channel between Gällstaö and Ekerön that has since disappeared. The "jungfru" (maiden) part of the name suggests an ancient pagan site here.

Jungfrusund used to be called Jungfruhamn, and the strait was a narrow channel between Gällstaö and Ekerön that has since vanished. The first part of the name, ‘jungfru’ (maiden), suggests there was once an ancient pagan site here.

Jungfrusund used to be called Jungfruhamn, and the sound was a narrow channel between Gällstaö and Ekerön that has since disappeared. The first part of the name, 'jungfru' (maiden), suggests there was once an ancient pagan site here.
Jungfrusund är både bostadsområde och ha: Jungfrusund is both a residential area and a harbour on Vårbyfjärden bay, on the east side of the island of Ekerön. Just offshore are the Jungfruholmarna, two islets that belong to the Göta Sailing Society. The club began leasing them in 1915, bought them in 1936 and built its own clubhouse there in 1955. They lie about six nautical miles from Stockholm out into Lake Mälaren.

Jungfrusund is both a residential area and a harbour on Vårbyfjärden, on the east side of Ekerön. Out in the water are the Jungfruholmarna, two islands belonging to the Göta sailing club. The club leased them in 1915, bought them in 1936 and built a clubhouse in 1955. The Ekerö ferry also crosses the bay here.
Juringe gård var en gång utgård till det: Juringe gård was once an outlying farm belonging to the large Vårby estate. The old main house was pulled down in 2001 and replaced by a lookalike, which is now a preschool. Still standing from the farm's working days are the storehouse, a laundry and dairy shed, and the farmhands' house, Väderluven. The croft of Nytorp was also here, beside the new road of 1673 that replaced the old Götha vägen route.
Jussi Björling höll sin första konsert p: Jussi Björling gave his first concert at Liseberg in 1931. Two years later, the French singer Mistinguett arrived with an entourage of 50, six tonnes of luggage and more than 700 costumes.
Juveleraren som räddade huset: The jeweller who saved the house
Jägarboställe blev ambassad: A royal huntsman's lodge turned embassy
Järfälla gymnasium har funnits här nära: Järfälla gymnasium, an upper secondary school, has stood here near Jakobsberg centre under various names since 1962, and in 2020 it had just over 1,000 students. Among the schools once based here was SAM-gymnasiet, which offered social sciences with specialisms ranging all the way to football. Close by is the Imam Ali Mosque, considered the largest Shia Muslim congregation in the Nordic countries.
Järfälla kyrkas fönster fick sin nuvaran: Järfälla Church's windows got their current layout during a rebuild in 1825. In the chancel gable is a round window whose lead glazing bars spell out the year '1825'.
Järfälla är en kommun där det mesta är b: Most of Järfälla is built up, and that has led to some creative ways of saving what nature is left. The Norra Igelbäcken nature reserve, for instance, includes an old airfield – and a metro line is being built underneath it. Otherwise, the municipality is best known for shopping, thanks to the Barkarby retail park.
Järfälla är rikt på runor. I Skylsta fin: Järfälla is rich in runes. At Skylsta there's a Viking Age inscription carved straight into the rock, while a fragment of a runestone that, according to Richard Dybeck, stood on the same hill has vanished without a trace. A little further on, on the Stockholm side, is Backlura, where every street is named after a flower or plant.
Järfällabadet har en 50 meter lång bassä: Järfällabadet has a 50-metre pool, a 3-metre diving tower, two water slides and two multi-purpose pools with floors that can be raised and lowered. It replaced the old Jakobsberg swimming baths.
Järfällabadet har förutom 50-metersbassä: As well as its 50-metre pool, Järfällabadet has a three-metre diving tower, springboards, a play area, a sauna and a hot tub. There's also a gym and a café.
Järfällabadet, en bit härifrån, invigdes: Järfällabadet, a short way from here, opened on 14 April 2018. It has a 50-by-25-metre pool, two water slides and pools with floors that can be raised and lowered. It replaced the Jakobsberg swimming baths, which opened on a Monday in August 1971 and had a 48-metre water slide. The old building was originally going to be demolished but will instead be turned into a space for leisure activities.
Järfällas förste ordinarie lärare, klock: Järfälla's first permanent teacher, the parish clerk and organist Ludvig Ulric Öberg, started in 1847. His pay included 53 riksdaler, eight barrels of grain, grazing and fodder for a cow, a vegetable plot, two church collections a year and free lodgings.
Järfällas sydligaste kommundel heter Bar: Järfälla's southernmost district, Barkarby-Skälby, had about 12,000 residents in 2011. It's home to Kyrkbyn, the old church village, with the Gästgivargården coaching inn – in recent years known as Wärdshuset Lasse-Maja – and the old courthouse. Closer to the sports ground is the manor of Skälby gård, whose current main building dates from 1802.
Järfällas tak med utsikt mot Globen: Järfälla's rooftop, with views to the Globe
Järfällas tak – utsikt till Globen: Järfälla's rooftop – with a view of Globen
Järla gård är en riktigt anrik herrgård:: Järla gård is a manor with deep roots: the first farm called Järla is believed to have been built around the year 900. It appears in Stockholm's court records in 1453, and a map from 1690 shows it on the northern shore of Lake Järlasjön. Industry later grew up all around it, and branch lines once ran from Saltsjö-Järla station to a yeast factory and to De Laval's steam turbine works.
Järla har anor från vikingatiden, då led: Järla goes back to the Viking Age, when the route to Birka ran via Järlasjön lake. The first farm at Järla was probably built around the year 900, and in later centuries both Sten Sture the Elder and Gustav Vasa owned it.

Järla goes back to the Viking Age, when the route to Birka ran through Lake Järlasjön. The first farm here was probably built around the year 900. Both Sten Sture the Elder and Gustav Vasa have owned Järla farm.
Järnbrottsmotet i närheten är en ovanlig: The nearby Järnbrottsmotet is an unusual type of motorway junction, known as a double trumpet interchange. It was built in the 1990s on the site of the Europa roundabout, a gigantic roundabout with the Söderleden road cutting straight through it at traffic lights. In the wall of Västra Frölunda cemetery next door there are still iron rings where churchgoers once tethered their horses.
Järnbrottsmotet är helt planskilt och i: The Järnbrottsmotet interchange is fully grade-separated and essentially a true motorway junction, yet none of its roads is signposted as a motorway. The Europa roundabout that stood here before it dated from the 1970s.
Järnbärarna bar stångjärnet mellan vågar: The iron porters carried bar iron between the weighing scales on an iron hook resting on their backs. They were paid a share of the weighing fees, and a good porter could earn up to 1,700 riksdaler a year. The team was led by an alderman who swore an oath of loyalty to the king.
Järnkrok på ryggen: An iron hook on the back
Järnspis och bakugn kvar: Iron range and bread oven intact
Järntorget har fått sitt namn av järnet: Järntorget, Iron Square, is named after the iron that was once weighed and shipped from here. The fountain in the middle dates from 1927 and depicts the world's five continents. This is where the old working-class districts begin. To the south is Haga, with its cafés and landshövdingehus – Gothenburg's typical houses with a stone ground floor and wooden upper storeys – and to the west run the Långgatorna streets, packed with vintage shops and bars.
Järnvägen Göteborg–Borås invigdes 1894 o: The Gothenburg–Borås railway opened in 1894, and Pixbo got a small station where trains stopped until 1978. The railway tempted well-off Gothenburgers to build large villas looking out over Rådasjön lake.

The Gothenburg–Borås railway opened in 1894 and Pixbo got a station, where trains stopped until 1978. In the early 1900s wealthy Gothenburgers built large villas overlooking Rådasjön lake, in Art Nouveau and Old Norse styles, and most are still standing.
Järnvägen Göteborg–Borås öppnade 1894, o: The Gothenburg–Borås railway opened in 1894, and Pixbo had its own station until 1978. The train tempted well-off Gothenburgers to build large villas with lake views, some in art nouveau and some in Old Norse style. Most of them are still standing.
Järnvägen har gått genom Årstaberg sedan: The railway has run through Årstaberg since the Årstabron bridge opened in 1929, but there was no station then. The commuter rail station didn't open until January 2006, with a platform squeezed between the existing tracks on two parallel viaducts – which is why it's rather narrow for so many passengers.
Järnvägen skapade villorna: The railway that made the suburb
Järnvägen som köpte en herrgård: The railway that bought a manor
Järnvägsstationen hette först Jordfallet: The railway station was first called Jordfallet, and from here a steamboat ran to Kungälv, which had no railway of its own. In 1907 it was renamed Bohus after the fortress – even though the town lies in Västergötland, not Bohuslän.
Järnvågen började byggas 1624 på en holm: Work on Järnvågen, the iron weigh house, began in 1624 on an islet in the Stora Hamnkanalen canal, where Brunnsparken is today. The last remains of the old weigh house burnt down in the great fire of 1813.
Järnvågen i Göteborg var den sista i Sve: Gothenburg’s iron weighhouse, the Järnvågen, was the last in Sweden to close. The guild of iron porters was dissolved in 1893, and they are remembered by the sculpture ‘Järnbärare’ (‘Iron Porters’) on Olof Palmes plats, at the northern end of Järntorget.
Järnåldersbyn Hogslaby består av sex små: The Iron Age village of Hogslaby is made up of six small wooden houses by Lake Aspen. Pupils felt sheep's wool, spin yarn and dye it with plants, bake bread and shape pots and jewellery from clay that's fired the Iron Age way.
Järnåldersgravar på backen: Iron Age graves on the hillside
Järva City som aldrig byggdes: The Järva City that was never built
Järva krog låg strategiskt där vägarna m: Järva inn stood at a strategic spot where the roads to Uppsala and Enköping parted. It's first mentioned in the 1690s but was probably here as early as the Middle Ages. Farmers on their way to market, carters and other travellers stopped here on their way to and from Stockholm.
Järva krog var en vägkrog cirka 3,5 kilo: Järva krog was a roadside inn on the Uppsala road, about 3.5 kilometres north of Norrtull, Stockholm's northern gateway. Its name lives on in the motorway junction. A short walk away is something far older: the Mellanjärva burial ground. With around 175 visible graves, it's one of the largest farm burial grounds in the Stockholm area.
Järvastaden ligger mest i Solna men strä: Järvastaden lies mostly in Solna but stretches into Sundbyberg, where it forms the district of Brotorp. Around 5,000 homes are planned once it's finished.
Järvastaden är ett stadsbyggnadsprojekt: Järvastaden is a building project that's taking its time. The first residents moved in in September 2007, and once it's finished it's planned to be home to more than 15,000 people. The ninth and last phase won't happen until after 2030, though, because a high-voltage power line has to be moved first. To the east is the neighbouring residential area of Agnesberg.
Jättekast och kyrkvaktarstuga: A giant's throw and a sexton's cottage
KFUM:s scoutkår startade tidningen Boo-P: The YMCA scout troop launched the newspaper Boo-Posten in 1949, aimed at first at the church, the scouts and local clubs. When Yngve Kämpe became editor in 1955, he made it more political. The paper closed in 1973.
KV konstskola började som en studiecirke: KV konstskola began as an evening drawing class led by the Valand student Wivi Bark, and it quickly became popular. In 1970 the school moved into Valand's old premises in Guldheden, but in 2023 it moved to Lindholmen.
Kaffe och hemslöjd på gården: Coffee and crafts at the farm
Kafé i tvättstugan: A café in the old laundry
Kafé uppkallat efter en fisk: A café named after a fish
Kajen 4 är klätt i svart aluminium, med: Kajen 4 is clad in black aluminium, with balconies on all four corners. The balconies get gradually longer the higher they go, so the building looks wider at the top than at the bottom.
Kakelugnen som flyttat två gånger: The tiled stove that moved twice
Kalifen lade grundstenen: The Caliph laid the foundation stone
Kalken som liknar klockstapeln: A chalice like the bell tower
Kallebäck Nordgården became an inn in 1735. In the 1780s a water main was laid from Kallebäck spring into the city, and the farm later had a brickworks.
Kallebäcks röda skola i trä användes 188: Kallebäck's little red wooden school was in use from 1885 to 1974. When it closed it was one of Gothenburg's oldest schools, and the only one without a flushing toilet. It was built from the timber of Örgryte's first school and has been preserved for its historical value.
Kallebäcks skola, en röd envåningsbyggna: Kallebäck school, a red single-storey wooden building, was in use from 1885 to 1974. It was built from timber salvaged from Örgryte's first school. When it closed, it was the only school in Gothenburg without a flushing toilet.
Kallhäll ligger intill Mälaren i Järfäll: Kallhäll lies on Lake Mälaren in northern Järfälla, and at its centre is the Folkets hus community centre, with a cinema and a library. A little further away is Stockholm Mejeri, Arla Foods' big dairy, which began production in 1984. Beneath the library is the Bolinder Museum, displaying products from Bolinders Mekaniska Verkstad, the Bolinder engineering works.
Kallhälls gård byggdes 1863 i schweizers: Kallhäll manor was built in 1863 in the Swiss chalet style. From 1906 it was Erik August Bolinder's summer villa, and after his death it became the head office of the Bolinders company. The brick buildings by Lake Mälaren are still a reminder of the factory.
Kalven blev 1865 socknens första badort,: In 1865 Kalven became the parish's first seaside resort, and its steamboat jetty was the most important stop between Gothenburg and Marstrand. In 1933 the summer visitors built a party hall known as Såsen, which is still in use. Today the island is car-free.
Kammarrådet Hauswolff byggde den gula ti: In the mid-18th century the official Hauswolff built the yellow, timbered two-storey main house with its attic. Parts of the house are even older: the vaulted cellar dates from the 17th century.
Kammeckers kvarn var en holländare där b: Kammecker's mill was a Dutch-style windmill, where only the cap turned to face the wind. It was torn down in 1794, but in 1810 a new one was built to grind grain for the Crown distilleries on Ladugårdslandet. On 29 November 1854 it burned down, bringing the era of mills on the hills to an end.
Kampementsbadet invigdes den 26 juli 196: Kampementsbadet opened on 26 July 1962 and cost 510,000 kronor. The low entrance building was designed by city gardener Holger Blom, and the name comes from the nearby Kampementsbacken hill.
Kanaguris lopp blev känt som världens lä: Kanaguri's race became known as the longest marathon in the world. A hundred years later, on 14 July 2012, an anniversary marathon was held and a memorial plaque was put up where the Petré family's house had stood.
Kanalen grävdes på uppdrag av Karl XV ef: The canal was dug on the orders of Karl XV, because the stream had become too shallow as the land rose. The water level of Brunnsviken dropped by about 1.25 metres, leaving some shallow canals in Hagaparken dry. Since 2000, traffic lights have controlled boats in the canal.
Kanalhuset har 13 000 kvadratmeter, hela: Kanalhuset has 13,000 square metres – a full 12,000 fewer than the old Synvillan in Torp – and two studios instead of three. That reflects digital technology, which needs less space and fewer staff.
Kandidat till betongunderverk: In the running as a concrete wonder
Kaninburarna och biografen: The rabbit hutches and the cinema
Kanonernas spår i skogen: Traces of the guns in the forest
Kanonsalut för skalden: A cannon salute for the poet
Kanotklubben hette först Gustav Vasa Ung: The canoe club was originally called Gustav Vasa Ungdomsförening. In 1948 its members Hasse Berglund and Lennart Klingström won Olympic gold in London, followed by silver in Helsinki in 1952.
Kanske skrevs svensk kungahistoria i när: Swedish royal history may well have been made just near here. Korseberget, a little village on the northern bank of the Nordre älv river close to its mouth, could be the same place as Horsaberg – where King Magnus Ladulås held peace talks with his brother Valdemar on 26 June 1274. A small community with a possibly big place in the history books.
Kanske uppkallat efter tre gubbar: Perhaps named after three old men
Kanton var en liten hantverksby som Lovi: Kanton was a little craft village that Queen Lovisa Ulrika and King Adolf Fredrik had built beside Kina slott, the Chinese Pavilion. Craftspeople here made ironwork and lace and wove silk ribbons. The queen even tried her hand at silk farming, but the mulberry trees didn't take to the cold and the venture lasted only about ten years. Today the houses are private homes, and they're regarded as a forerunner of the Swedish garden city.
Kaparbror högg kompassrosen: A privateer's brother carved the compass rose
Kapellet blev en villa: The chapel that became a villa
Kapellet byggdes av Sällskapet för Främj: The chapel was built by a society devoted to promoting pastoral care, which wanted to help people who had moved to the city from the countryside. It built cheap housing and small churches on a Danish model, and Stefanskapellet from 1900 was its first church.
Kapellet byggdes på frivilliga gåvor eft: The chapel was paid for by voluntary donations after an appeal in 1912 by the vicar, Gustaf Franck. Collection cards were printed with squares worth 25 öre each, and the property company Fastighets AB Carnegie donated the site.
Kapellet i Vasastaden var bara tillfälli: The chapel in Vasastaden was only temporary and was due to be demolished to make way for housing. But Brännkyrka parish bought it for 37,000 kronor, because the growing industrial area of Liljeholmen needed a church.
Kapellet invigdes 1970 och ritades av ar: The chapel was consecrated in 1970 and designed by architect Wolfgang Huebner in brick, patinated steel and glass. The plan is mirrored, with low entrances and lofty chapels. The gold and silver interior decoration is by Professor Olle Nyman.
Kapellet mäter 9 gånger 11 meter och rym: The chapel measures 9 by 11 metres and holds no more than 35 people. That wasn't enough for long, and in 1925 the Chapel of the Resurrection was completed.
Kapellet och griftegården är sedan 1996: The chapel and cemetery have been protected under the Cultural Heritage Act since 1996. In December 2017 a Muslim burial section with 220 coffin graves was consecrated.
Kapellet på Fridhems kyrkogård invigdes: The chapel at Fridhem cemetery was consecrated in 1982 by Bishop Bertil Gärtner. The cemetery holds around 5,627 Christian graves.
Kapellet på det lilla berget: The chapel on the little hill
Kapellet röstades 2023 fram till Sverige: In 2023 the chapel was voted Sweden's most beautiful brutalist building. The walls are bare concrete and the roofs clad in copper, and a tower-like lantern rises above the chancel.
Kapellet som blev kyrka: The chapel that became a church
Kapellet som flyttade till Aspudden: The chapel that moved to Aspudden
Kapellet är en monteringsfärdig träbyggn: The chapel is a prefabricated timber building with an octagonal nave, designed by the architect Erik Otto Ulrich in the Gothic Revival style, complete with a tower and a roof turret.
Kapellet är fullt av symboler. Förhallen: The chapel is full of symbols. The entrance hall rests on twelve columns, one for each apostle, and the keyhole in the door is the eye of a skull. On the roof is Carl Milles's little Angel of Death – now a copy after several attempted thefts.
Kapplandsgatan intill känns igen på sina: Kapplandsgatan next door is easy to spot by its red three-storey buildings, and at the southern end of the street is Högsbo Hospital. The nearest square is Axel Dahlströms torg, which stands out with a 16-storey tower block from 1956 and a marble inlay by Endre Nemes on the community centre. Along Marklandsgatan you'll find a pizzeria, a bakery and a grill.
Karl August Johansson kom till Tyresö 19: Karl August Johansson came to Tyresö in 1924 to run the sawmill and the mill by the rapids. He supplied timber for many of the new weekend cabins and sometimes built them too. One of the biggest plots was bought for the staff of the PUB department store.
Karl Erik Hjalmarson hämtade tydlig insp: Karl Erik Hjalmarson clearly took his cue from the medieval churches of Uppland when he designed Husby Church. The congregation has about 290 members and a vision of being “A house of prayer for all peoples”.
Karl Güettler ritade villan åt överdirek: Karl Güettler designed the villa for Paul Laurin, director-general and head of the Insurance Inspectorate. It's a two-storey house of dark brown tarred timber, with blue-painted windows and decorative chimneys. Inside are roughly hewn logs, exposed ceiling beams and painted ceilings.
Karl Güettler var en av förgrundsgestalt: Karl Güettler was one of the leading figures in the folk-romantic architecture of the early 1900s, which drew on rural building traditions. He designed Högloftet and Nyloftet at Skansen, and the villa here was built for Paul Laurin, head of the Insurance Inspectorate.
Karl Johansgatan fick sitt namn 1882 eft: Karl Johansgatan was named in 1882 after King Karl XIV Johan. The stretch between Stigbergstorget and Carl Johan’s Church is often called Hängmattan – the Hammock – because it dips through a hollow between two hills.
Karl XI lät bygga ett tjugo kilometer lå: King Karl XI had a fence twenty kilometres long and three metres high built around Djurgården, to keep wolves out and deer in. Around 1803, 183 deer were shut into a new enclosure here. When the city bought the land in 1889, the deer were moved to an enclosure outside Mariefred.
Karl XII står i brons och pekar mot Ryss: Karl XII stands in bronze, pointing towards Russia – a reminder of his wars. Johan Peter Molin's statue was unveiled on 30 November 1868, the 150th anniversary of the king's death. It was cast on Kungsholmen and weighs two and a half tonnes. The mortars around the plinth are war trophies from Riga. The Green Party has put forward a proposal to move the statue.
Karl XII:s hund ligger här: Charles XII's dog is buried here
Karl XIV Johan avtäckte bysten den 26 ju: Karl XIV Johan unveiled the bust of Bellman on 26 July 1829 to kettledrums, trumpets and a cannon salute from Strömmen, in front of thousands of onlookers. It inspired Esaias Tegnér to write a poem about 'the image of the greatest singer the North has known'.
Karl XIV Johans tandläkare Jean Baptiste: Jean Baptiste Dubost, dentist to Karl XIV Johan, bought the Lilla Ersta estate in 1817 and in 1827 built an 18-metre lookout tower on the hill. Locals nicknamed it Tandpetaren, "the Toothpick" – a nod to his profession. The tower stood until around 1870.
Karl XV köpte stugan och flyttade den hi: Karl XV bought the cottage and had it moved here, furnishings and all. Upstairs, the king fitted out a studio for himself. From 1921 the house became home to artists such as the sculptor Gustaf Sandberg and the painter Axel Wallert.
Karl XV, som hade Ulriksdals slott från: King Karl XV, who had Ulriksdal Palace from 1857, leased Bergshamra farm for experimental agriculture and built summer villas for his friends. Dairy farmers hung on in southern Bergshamra until 1965.
Karl, som högg stenen, tros ha fått sin: Karl, the stonemason, is thought to have trained abroad – perhaps in England, Lund or on Gotland. His interlacing and animal motifs resemble those on a font from Sigtuna, and the two masters may have worked in the same workshop: both used a coarse-grained reddish sandstone.
Karlsro var kanske stadens mest svårspel: Karlsro was perhaps the trickiest pitch in town: its eastern side rose so steeply that playing down the wings was a struggle. Players changed in the open air, and the pioneers remembered all the time they spent hunting for the ball – usually the only one they had – in the rye fields south of the pitch.
Karolinsk herrgård vid Magelungen: A Caroline manor by Lake Magelungen
Karolinska Institutet grundades 1810 bla: Karolinska Institutet was founded in 1810, partly to train more surgeons for the army. During the war of 1808–09, young men with very little knowledge had been given crash courses and sent out as assistant doctors – which prompted the physician Eric Carl Trafvenfelt to propose an institute.
Karolinska Institutets lärarkollegium rö: Karolinska Institutet's teaching staff voted 19–6 against the sculpture, arguing that its subject brought sickness and deformity to mind more than the healing art of medicine. The matter went all the way to the King in Council and was settled by the government.
Karptjärnen är som djupast bara 1,8 mete: Karptjärnen is only 1.8 metres at its deepest and its water is slow to renew. A species of stonewort grows here, and the pond drains into Kalvfjärden.
Karsviks hage brukades som åker in på 19: Karsvik's pasture was farmed as a field until the 1930s. The ridge running along its north-facing slope is an end moraine, a feature found in several places in Bromma.
Karsviks Östergård är en knuttimrad pars: Karsvik's Östergård is a corner-timbered double cottage, probably from the 17th century, long home to the farmhands and estate workers at Åkeshov. Its last resident, Johanna Christina Burman, lived here until 1932, by which time she was 75.
Kasernerna ritades av Erik Josephson i s: Erik Josephson designed the barracks in the Baltic Brick Gothic style, inspired by medieval civic architecture. Every building has red brick walls and black metal roofs, and the site originally included a drill hall, winter and summer stables and a riding hall.
Kasernerna ritades av arkitekten Erik Jo: The barracks were designed by architect Erik Josephson in Baltic brick Gothic, inspired by medieval castle architecture. Every building has red-brick walls and a black metal roof, grouped around a lower, an upper and a rear barrack yard.
Kasernområdet hade både vinterstall, som: The barracks had winter stables, summer stables and a riding hall, and new stable buildings were added in 1903–1905. Today the Kviberg market is held in the former stables.
Kastalakyrkans dopfunt består av fem fra: Kastala church's font is made up of five fragments of a 13th-century font carved by the Lödöse Master. The pieces were found during the excavation of the site of Ny Kongelf's church. The church was consecrated in 1980, and the first portable church that stood here was moved to Nyköping.
Kastellegården blev kungsgård 1658, när: Kastellegården became a royal estate in 1658, when Charles XI gave it to Harald Stake, governor of Bohuslän. The wings probably date from the late 18th century, and the main building is a villa from 1862. Since 1935 the estate has been a state-listed historic building.
Katt och råtta över porten: Cat and mouse above the door
Kattugglor och Adam och Eva: Tawny owls and Adam and Eve
Kattuntillverkaren som ägde torpet: The calico maker who owned the croft
Kavelbron som gav Långbro namn: The log bridge behind the name Långbro
Keillers park och utsikten från Ramberge: Keillers park and the view from Ramberget hill
Keillers verkstad tillverkade långt mer: Keiller's works made far more than ships: steam boilers, turbines and cranes, but also church bells, washing machines, iron bedsteads and railway carriages. From 1845 it was home to Sweden's first steam-hammer forge.
Kejsarens hotell i en roman: The Emperor's Hotel in a novel
Kent och The Hives på 44:an: Kent and The Hives at the 44
Kika in på Malmstens möbelskola: Peek into Malmstens, the furniture-making school
Kikås kyrkogård anlades på gammal betesm: Kikås cemetery was laid out on old grazing land owned by a mill owner in Kvarnbyn. The old chapel was used until 1937, when a new one in the functionalist style was built to designs by Ville Berglund.

Kikås cemetery was laid out on old grazing land. In 1937 it gained a new funeral chapel in the functionalist style, designed by the architect Ville Berglund. Today the chapel is adorned with an icon triptych by the icon painter Erland Forsberg.
Kikås kyrkogård omtalas 1888 och anlades: Kikås cemetery is first mentioned in 1888 and was laid out on old grazing land. In 1937 a new funeral chapel in the functionalist style was built, designed by Ville Berglund. Today's altarpiece is an icon triptych by Erland Forsberg.
Kikås är den höga åsen vid Stensjöns söd: Kikås is the high ridge on the southern shore of Lake Stensjön, and it's home to Sweden's biggest free-standing insect hotel, where wild bees and butterflies check in. Not far from here is Södra Långevattnet, a long, narrow lake with clear water, surrounded by rocky hills and wooded ridges. It's a popular place for a swim – but if you want to fish, you'll need a licence.
Kiosken och taxistationen: The kiosk and the taxi stand
Kista Centrum invigdes 1977 av kung Carl: Kista Centrum was opened in 1977 by King Carl XVI Gustaf and Queen Silvia. After major extensions it was renamed Kista Galleria in 2009, and the following year it was Stockholm’s most visited shopping centre.
Kista Nod, alldeles intill, kostade 700: Kista Nod, right next door, cost 700 million kronor and was completed in 2014. Stockholm University carries out research there in computer and systems sciences. The area is also home to the Electrum laboratory, with a complete production line for semiconductor chips. And, rather more discreetly, Kista houses Försvarsunderrättelsedomstolen, the Defence Intelligence Court, which decides on permits for signals intelligence.
Kista brandstation i gult tegel ritades: Kista's yellow-brick fire station was designed by Hans Borgström. Its seven-level training tower, just over 17 metres high, is identical to the one at Brännkyrka fire station, which Borgström designed at the same time. Both opened in 1980.
Kista kyrka ritades av Zoltán Bedecs och: Kista Church was designed by Zoltán Bedecs and completed in 1978. Beneath the nave is a crypt shaped like an amphitheatre. The architect also designed the stained-glass windows and the octagonal font with its gilded decoration.
Kista torn blev klart 2016 och är Stockh: Completed in 2016, Kista Torn is Stockholm’s second-tallest residential building, with 35 floors of flats. Its little brother, K2, is 60 metres tall. Together the towers hold 362 homes, and the project was nominated for Construction of the Year 2017.
Kista tunnelbanestation är den enda på b: Kista is the only station on the blue line that's above ground. It sits on a viaduct 1,120 metres long – the longest anywhere on the metro. When the station was being named, the naming committee first wanted to add 'Gård', meaning farm, so that nobody would think of a 'likkista', a coffin. Rising above the shopping centre is Kista torn, the Kista Tower, 120 metres tall.
Kista är fullt av forskning. Rise SICS,: Kista is packed with research. Rise SICS, formerly the Swedish Institute of Computer Science, does non-profit computer science research to help Swedish companies compete. The Electrum Laboratory, part of the KTH Royal Institute of Technology, has a complete production line for semiconductor circuits and carries out research in micro- and nanotechnology.
Kistamässan har sina rötter i Sollentuna: Kistamässan has its roots in Sollentunamässan, which opened in 1973. When Kistamässan got going in September 2008, Sollentuna closed for good and all its trade fairs moved here.
Kistas tunnelbanestation är den enda på: Kista is the only station on the blue metro line that's above ground. The trains glide in along a 1,120-metre viaduct – the longest bridge on the whole metro network. Near the centre you'll also find the eight-sided Kista Church, and on Kista torg is Kista folkhögskola, Sweden's first folk high school – a kind of adult education college – with a Muslim profile.
Kistastenen står inte på sin ursprunglig: The Kista stone isn't in its original location. It was moved here during road works around 1900, and nobody knows where it first stood. The top is decorated with a ring cross with four equal arms.
Klaffbron från 1973 öppnade för trafik s: The bascule bridge from 1973 opened to traffic on the same day as the Nockeby and Drottningholm bridges. In 2023 it was due to be replaced by a new swing bridge as part of the Förbifart Stockholm bypass. With the bridge closed, the clearance for boats is six metres.
Klaffbron från 1973 öppnades samtidigt s: The 1973 bascule bridge opened at the same time as the Nockeby and Drottningholm bridges. As part of the Stockholm Bypass road project it is being replaced by a brand-new, wider swing bridge. Incidentally, Tappström was a town in its own right until 1975.
Klare mosse har länge varit ett populärt: Klare mosse has long been a favourite outing for school classes studying frogs and newts. Its restoration was partly funded by the EU through the PURE North Sea programme.
Klare mosse has long been a popular outing for school classes keen to study frogs and newts. Its restoration was partly funded with EU money through the PURE North Sea programme.
Klare mosse är 6–8 meter djup och cirka: Klare mosse is 6–8 metres deep and about 100 metres across. It's full of crucian carp, if rather small ones, along with perch and roach.
Klareberg i Kärra är en plats där bussar: Klareberg in Kärra is where the buses get to catch their breath. Drivers like to take their breaks here, and the big bus stop serves routes to Kungälv, Angered and Gothenburg. But the area is also popular with riders and dog owners, who come here to ride and train their dogs.
Klassiska Göteborg på en förmiddag. Kult: Classic Gothenburg in a morning: Götaplatsen, the city's cultural square, a stroll down the Avenyn boulevard and cinnamon buns in Haga.
Klingska huset, i hörnet av Älvsjövägen: Klingska huset, on the corner of Älvsjövägen and Johan Skyttes väg, is the oldest surviving block of rented flats in Solberga. Built between 1923 and 1925 in a town-style design, it was Älvsjö's first piece of town-centre development. A couple of hundred metres away is Älvkvarnstenen, an ancient cup-marked stone that has been moved twice and has stood next to Lerkrogen since 1994.
Klippan är en av Göteborgs äldsta miljöe: Klippan is one of Gothenburg's oldest neighbourhoods, with old seamen's cottages and the remains of the earlier Älvsborg fortress. Right beside it towers the Älvsborg Bridge, and beneath the bridge is the Röda Sten art centre.
Klippan är fullt av historia. Här låg Ga: Klippan is steeped in history. This was the site of Gamla Älvsborg, a mighty fortress from the 1300s to the 1600s that's now a ruin. The old sugar refinery, Sockerbruket, was home to 24 kvadrat, Sweden's smallest dance stage. And Klippans värdshus, the inn from 1762, was made famous by the ship's chaplain Jacob Wallenberg in his book Min son på galejan, 'My Son on the Galley'. The trams sleep in the Majorna tram depot next door.
Klippans sommarteater byggdes 1923 och l: Klippan's summer theatre was built in 1923 in a beautiful spot overlooking Strömmen. Siegfried Fischer was its first director and also appeared on stage. The theatre closed after 1942, but the block name Friluftsteatern – 'the open-air theatre' – keeps its memory alive.
Klippans värdshus arrenderades 1762–1770: The Klippan inn was leased from 1762 to 1770 by James Carnegie, who then moved into Gothenburg and ran a coffee house on Köpmansgatan next to the German Church. The house had wallpaper, five tiled stoves, and a bread oven in one of the kitchens.
Kliv av i Vällingby och se biografen Fon: Hop off in Vällingby to see the Fontänen cinema on the square (2 min), then take the steps through the Trappan civic centre (3 min). Both opened in 1956 and were designed by Backström & Reinius.
Kliv av och gå fram till Eriksbergskrane: Hop off and walk over to the Eriksberg crane (3 min). The gantry crane from 1969 stands just over 70 metres tall and almost 110 metres wide. It's a listed structure and a symbol of the city's lost shipbuilding era.
Kliv av och se dig om bland stjärnhusen: Hop off and take a look around the star-shaped blocks of Gröndal. Sweden's first were built here, designed by Sven Backström and Leif Reinius, and the buildings have become internationally famous.
Kliv av och titta på Krokslätts fabriker: Hop off and take a look at Krokslätts fabriker (2 min), old textile mills that now house businesses, restaurants and flats.
Kliv av vid Finnboda hamn och strosa bla: Hop off at Finnboda hamn and wander among the old shipyard buildings (5 min). Finnboda shipyard was founded in 1874, and its joinery, steam-engine works and canteen now house homes, offices and shops.
Kliv av vid Luma och gå till Lumaparken: Get off at Luma and walk to Lumaparken and the waterfront promenade along Hammarby sjö (2 min). The big functionalist building is the Luma factory, where light bulbs were once made.
Kliv ner i Rinkeby tunnelbanestation och: Step down into Rinkeby metro station and you'll find yourself in a Viking treasure chamber. The artist Nisse Zetterberg took small Viking Age objects dug up in the area and blew them up into huge mosaics on brick-red walls, with gold inlays and runes. The station opened in 1975, when the blue line was launched.
Kliv rakt in i 1950-talet på Kortedala m: Step straight into the 1950s at Kortedala museum (2 min), a two-room flat preserved just as it was when working-class families moved in. Citytorget square next door was built in 1955–1957.
Kliv rakt in i 1950-talet! Ett stenkast: Step straight back into the 1950s! A stone's throw away is Kortedala museum, a completely ordinary two-room flat with a kitchen, kept just as it was when the working-class families first moved in. It's so authentic that it's been used as a set for period films. Citytorget, the square right next to it, was built at the same time, between 1955 and 1957, with tower blocks, rows of shops and a street kiosk.
Kliver du av bussen vid Lissma skola kan: Get off the bus at Lissma skola and you can hike in the Paradiset nature reserve – out to the Paradiset croft and Tornberget hill, for instance. The reserve has lakes such as Trehörningen, Ådran and Ormputten.

Klockan 16.09 den 30 november 1977 inträ: At 4.09 pm on 30 November 1977, a massive landslide struck Tuve. Nine people were killed, and the Tuve landslide is counted among the worst natural disasters in modern Swedish history.

Klockardottern Dagmar Gerdelius beskrev: Dagmar Gerdelius, the parish clerk's daughter, described the clerk's house of the 1890s as an idyll, with Virginia creeper covering the whole south wall and bird cherry and lilac in bloom. The downsides were the cold and the rats – and there was no proper well.
Klockaren på 1600-talet sålde enligt käl: According to the records, the 17th-century parish clerk sold beer and schnapps. This competed with the coaching inn in Barkarby and drew criticism from the congregation.
Klockaren som sålde brännvin: The parish clerk who sold schnapps
Klockargården vid kyrkan är känd från 16: The parish clerk's house by the church is known from the 1620s. In the 17th century the clerks sold beer and brännvin (Swedish schnapps) there, competing with the coaching inn at Barkarby and drawing criticism from the parish.

The parish clerk's farm by the church dates back to at least the 1620s. According to the records, the 17th-century clerk sold beer and schnapps, competing with the coaching inn in Barkarby and drawing criticism from the congregation.

Klockstapeln brann 1966 och båda kyrkklo: The bell tower burned in 1966, and both church bells cracked. The older one, from 1638, was considered so unique that it wasn't allowed to be recast. It's now displayed as a museum piece in the church porch.
Klockstapeln från 1821 står högt uppe på: The bell tower, from 1821, stands high on a rocky hill west of the churchyard. Its bell is older still, cast in Stralsund in 1656. Inside the church, the pulpit dates from 1627 and still has its 17th-century hourglass.
Klockstapeln i trä är från 1825 och har: The wooden bell tower dates from 1825 and has a copper-clad cap. The small bell is from 1653 and the large one from 1725. The weathervane on top comes from the earlier bell tower, built in 1652.
Klocktorn med gyllene kors: A bell tower with a golden cross
Klocktornet är byggt för fyra klockor me: The bell tower was built for four bells but only has two: the big one is called Syster Trofast (Sister Faithful) and the small one Broder Barfot (Brother Barefoot). Including its stainless-steel cross, the tower is 47 metres high.

Klotter som gav dödsstraff: Graffiti that earned a death sentence
Klubben byggde grannhallen: The club built the rink next door
Klubben som kör på banan sedan 1984 är e: The club that has raced on the track since 1984 is a youth branch of the Motorists' Total Abstinence Association. The tarmac circuit is 330 metres long and the gravel one 340 metres. In winter, electric cars race on an indoor track.
Klubben som lämnades i sticket: The club that was left in the lurch

Knappnålen är gjord av glasfiberarmerad: Knappnålen, "the Pin", is made of glass-fibre-reinforced plastic and stainless steel, and the arms of its cross point north–south and east–west. It went up in 2006 but wasn't officially unveiled until 2007. In 2008 an identical sculpture was raised in Kumla.
Knarrholmen var en present till arbetare: Knarrholmen was a gift to the workers. In 1940 the shipowner Axel Ax:son Johnson donated the island to the shipyard workers at Götaverken, and summer cottages went up here after 1945. In 2014 the trade unions sold the island, with its 33 cottages, restaurant and village shop. Neighbouring Sillfarsholmen was bought by the Aeolus sailing club in 1935 for a single krona.
Knattebio för de minsta: Toddler cinema for the littlest ones
Knut Gadelius var född och delvis uppvux: Knut Gadelius was born and partly raised in Japan, and had close contacts there through his trading house. The villa was meant to serve both as a home and for entertaining, so the living room could be enlarged with sliding walls.

Knutpunkt för spårvagnar och Mälaröbussa: A hub for trams and Mälaren island buses
Knuttehaket i Farlig kurva: The bikers' café in Farlig kurva
Knuttehaket som blev film: The biker café that made it into a film
Kock & Vin hamnade på delad tredjeplats: Kock & Vin came joint third among Sweden's best restaurants in The White Guide 2012. After 14 years, the restaurant closed on 2 February 2014.
Kol på pråm och tidiga maskiner: Coal by barge, machines ahead of their time
Kolerakyrkogårdar som denna anlades utan: Cholera cemeteries like this one were laid out beyond the town limits. Between 1834 and 1884 Sweden was struck by no fewer than nine cholera epidemics, and Bräcke was used again during the later outbreaks.
Kolerakyrkogården från 1866 ligger vid D: The cholera cemetery from 1866 lies beside Delsjö golfbaneväg and measures 35 by 18 metres. It is enclosed by a well-built stone wall and has a memorial stone 2.1 metres tall. Right next to it is the passage grave known as Kung Rings grav, King Ring's Grave.
Kolet till verket lades upp på två stora: Coal for the plant was stockpiled on two large caissons by the shore of Lake Mälaren, which form the outer quay. They had been towed all the way from Normandy, where the Allies used them in the 1944 landings.
Kolfabrik där tennisbanorna ligger: A charcoal works where the tennis courts are
Kolla in Flatenbanan för radiostyrda bil: Check out Flatenbanan, the track for radio-controlled cars

Kollektivet vänder sig till dig som är 4: The co-housing community is for people aged 40 and over. Cooking and washing up, cleaning and gardening are all compulsory, and some twenty working groups keep everything running.
Kollektivhuset Sockenstugan är ett gemen: Sockenstugan is a cohousing block for people in the second half of life – one of many created in Stockholm after a political decision in 1980. One report called it a real success story. Right next door is Gränsberget park, an old moraine hill shared between the districts of Enskededalen and Kärrtorp.
Kollektivhuset hade centralkök med resta: The collective house had a central kitchen with a restaurant, a takeaway counter, a shop and cleaning help. One advert tempted residents with: ‘Try our home-baked Danish pastries! Lunch and dinner guests welcome in the collective house restaurant.’
Kolonilotterna stakades ut söndagen den: The allotments were pegged out on Sunday 4 May 1919, and the first cabin went up that same summer. Its owner – the very first – was Anders Fredman.
Kolonin hette först Godhemskolonien och: The allotment garden was first called Godhemskolonien, then Kungsladugårdskolonien until 1969. That year it became Slottsskogskolonin, as the link to Slottsskogen park was felt to help secure the garden's future.
Kolonin som fick flytta: The allotments that had to move
Koloniområdet har ett 85-tal lotter. På: The allotment area has around 85 plots. On the cabin plots you may build a house of up to 8 m², and if you follow the municipality's standard design, no planning permission is needed. Every cabin is painted in a different shade of grey-green.
Koloniområdet ligger i en dalgång längs: The allotments lie in a valley along the Spångaån stream that once belonged to Hjulsta farm and Stora Tensta. When housing went up to the north, the valley was spared. In 1973 there were 242 plots; today there are around 120, each about 150 square metres.
Koloniträdgårdarna i Stockholm startades: Stockholm's allotment gardens were started by Anna Lindhagen and her friend Anna Åbergsson. Stora Mossen got going in 1915, a year after the tramway to Bromma opened. In the middle of the area today there's an open-air stage and a dance floor.
Koloniträdgården grundades 1916, mitt un: The allotment garden was founded in 1916, in the middle of the First World War, when food shortages made allotments an important way of feeding the cities. The plots average 250–300 square metres, and there were 155 of them to begin with.
Kombinationen av högt bostadshus, låg ce: A tall residential block, a low shopping centre and a metro station all in one complex – there's nothing else like it in Stockholm. The architectural style was unusual in Sweden, though fairly common on the Continent.
Komettorget fick sitt namn 1965 som del: Komettorget, Comet Square, got its name in 1965 as part of a group of names on the theme of space and the universe. That's why the streets around it include Meteorgatan, Nebulosagatan and Kometgatan.
Kommunalhus med polisfinka: A town hall with a police cell
Kommunalhuset från 1905 är en putsad jug: The municipal building from 1905 is a rendered Art Nouveau building with a roof turret and clock. Above the main door St Erik sits enthroned amid bladderwrack. The building housed the customs and harbour offices, the police, the fire brigade and homes for harbour workers.
Kommunalvägen löper genom Huddinges hjär: Kommunalvägen runs right through the heart of Huddinge, with the station, the shopping centre, the church and the municipal offices all along its 1.3 kilometres. There's been news here recently too: Sjödalsgymnasiet, an upper secondary school that opened in 1994, closed in 2026. In its final year it had 185 students, compared with 608 just three years before.
Kommunalvägen var tidigare en del av Hud: Kommunalvägen was once part of Huddingevägen, the first direct road between Huddinge and Skanstull. When the new Huddingevägen was built west of the tracks in the 1960s, it became a local street and was named after the municipal hall.
Kommundelen Tibble rymmer både Täby cent: The Tibble district is home both to Täby Centrum and to the church that has been called the Cathedral of Roslagen. Täby Centrum has 215 shops and, since 2022, the official name Westfield Täby Centrum. Its library holds a Viking Age runestone fragment found at Lissby in 1930. A piece found at the same time turned out to belong to a different stone.

The Tibble district is home to both Täby centrum, the shopping centre, and the church that's been nicknamed “the Cathedral of Roslagen”. The shopping centre has 215 shops, and since 2022 its official name has been Westfield Täby Centrum. Its library keeps two fragments of Viking Age runestones that were found in Lissby in 1930 – though it later turned out that several of the pieces actually belonged to a different stone.
Kommunen består mest av skog. Mölndalsån: The municipality is mostly forest. The Mölndalsån river runs through it from east to west, passing Västra Nedsjön, Landvettersjön and Rådasjön lakes. There are several nature reserves too, among them Klippan, Risbohult and Gallhålan.
Kommunen köpte Vendelsö efter att jordbr: The council bought Vendelsö after farming had stopped, and ran a primary school in the main house until 1939. In the 1950s a bus company kept its garage where the farm buildings had once stood.
Kommunen köpte herrgården 1969, lät den: The municipality bought the manor in 1969, left it to decay for twelve years and planned to demolish it. But the Kumla Manor community association, formed in 1982, restored the house and reopened it in 1988. The City Museum lent three 18th-century tiled stoves with floral decoration.
Kommunen som växte ur sina lokaler: The council that outgrew its offices
Kommunens centrala delar följer Säveåns: The heart of the municipality follows the valley of the Säveån river, hemmed in by steep rocky slopes. Up on the heights grows pine forest on bare rock, here and there mixed with oak and beech. To the south-west lies the Knipeflågsbergen nature reserve, an untouched rocky plateau with natural woodland.
Kommunens största arbetsplats är en flyg: The biggest employer is an airport
Kommunens största företag, Berg Propulsi: The municipality's biggest company, Berg Propulsion, makes propellers. Öckerö's sailing upper secondary school is here too, with around 300 students.
Kommunens äldsta bro: The oldest bridge in the municipality
Kommungräns mitt i älven: A boundary down the middle of the river
Kompassrosen i berget under Valen höggs: The compass rose carved into the rock below Valen was probably the work of Sven Gathenhielm, brother of the privateer captain Lars Gathenhielm and a privateer himself. Compass roses like this were carved where the pilots kept watch. Valen is one of only two listed sea marks on the west coast; the other is on Vinga.
Kompassrosen under Valen höggs troligen: The compass rose beneath Valen was probably carved by Sven, brother of the privateer captain Lars Gathenhielm and a privateer captain himself. It's now protected as an ancient monument. Valen is one of only two listed navigation marks on the west coast; the other stands on Vinga.
Komplexet ritades av Carl-Axel Acking oc: The complex was designed by Carl-Axel Acking and has 340 flats in four tower blocks and several low-rise buildings around four courtyards. They range from 25-square-metre studios with their own little garden to six-room flats with roof terraces looking out over Lake Mälaren.

Konditoriet grundades av skånske Kurt Lu: The patisserie was founded by Kurt Lundberg from Skåne, who had previously worked at Oscar Berg's patisserie. He ran it until 1972. The 1940s interior is almost unchanged, and in the evening the classic blue neon sign glows above the entrance.
Konditoriet ligger i en V-formad hörnbyg: The café sits in a V-shaped corner building designed by Backström & Reinius in 1946, which also housed a post office and a clothes shop. Rising above it are Gröndal's well-known star-shaped apartment blocks.

Kongahälla Center invigdes i mars 2019 o: Kongahälla Center opened in March 2019 and spreads across 37,000 square metres. As well as the express buses in the story, the travel centre next door is also served by the X4, among others.
Kongahälla förstördes flera gånger. År 1: Kongahälla was destroyed several times over. In 1614, on the orders of King Christian IV, the town was moved to Fästningsholmen, under the protection of Bohus Fortress. After more fires it moved again, and by around 1680 it stood where it is today.

Konst i rättarbostaden: Art in the farm manager's house
Konsten på Västra skogens station är gjo: The art at Västra skogen station is by Sivert Lindblom, who was inspired by the mystery of the old name Ingentingskogen – the ‘Nothing Forest’. Look out for the tiled shapes along the walls, and for the artist’s own profile, which pops up in several places.
Konstfack började 1844 som en söndagsrit: Konstfack, now Sweden's largest university of arts, crafts and design, began in 1844 as a Sunday drawing school for craftsmen, founded by Nils Månsson Mandelgren. The first intake included stove makers and silk weavers. The first women students arrived in 1857.
Konsthallen Accelerator har sina utställ: The Accelerator art gallery has its exhibition halls in a former underground lab for accelerator physics, and it opened in 2019 with a work by Tino Sehgal. Its neighbour is Villa Frescati, designed by Louis Jean Desprez in 1791–1792 as a summer retreat for Gustaf Mauritz Armfelt, facing Gustav III's pavilion across the water. And at the Swedish Museum of Natural History is Cosmonova, Sweden's only domed IMAX cinema.
Konsthallen Kummelholmen ligger i en gam: Kummelholmen art gallery occupies an old oil-fired hot-water plant, designed by Ingmar Benckert in 1967 and decommissioned in 1997. The exhibition hall is down one flight of stairs, and artists shown here include William Kentridge and Lars Kleen.
Konsthallen ligger i en före detta oljee: The art gallery is housed in a former oil-fired hot-water plant designed by Ingmar Benckert in 1967 and in use until 1997. The exhibition hall is one floor down, and William Kentridge is among those who have shown work here.
Konstnären Axel Törneman flyttade till J: The artist Axel Törneman moved to Johannisberg in 1924, the year before he died. From his time here there's a large mural in the entrance hall of the main house, which he painted together with his friend Isaac Grünewald.
Konstnären Carl Larsson skrev 1891 om vi: In 1891 the artist Carl Larsson wrote of the villa: 'That is how all scientists ought to live.' He dreamed of sitting in the great study with a well-stocked library, gazing out over land and water.
Konstnären Josabeth Sjöberg bodde 1847–1: The artist Josabeth Sjöberg lived at Högbergsgatan 60 from 1847 to 1855. She called many of her watercolours Utsigt från mitt fönster – 'View from my window' – and two of them show the Brinckan house.
Konstnären Olle Nyman föddes på Duvnäs ö: The artist Olle Nyman was born at Duvnäs övre gård and stayed in the area all his life. His studio and the farm are now owned by a foundation that holds exhibitions there.
Konstnären Olle Olsson Hagalund bodde he: The artist Olle Olsson Hagalund spent his whole life in the same wooden house, built in 1897 by the master carpenter Carl Jakob Brolin. Today it's a museum, both for his art and for the old shanty town of Hagalund, which was demolished in the 1960s to make way for the Blåkulla tower blocks. Inside you'll find a model of old Hagalund. Nearby stands Hagalund water tower from 1912.
Konstnären Sivert Lindblom inspirerades: The artist Sivert Lindblom was inspired by the mystery in the name 'Ingentingskogen' – the Forest of Nothing. The walls are decorated with tiled shapes, and a tile pattern runs along the platform edges. Look closely and you'll spot the artist's own profile in several places.
Konstnären Tor Svae, som byggt sagomiljö: The artist Tor Svae, who built the fairy-tale settings at Junibacken, created the park together with George Johansson and Jens Ahlbom, the creators of Mulle Meck. Here you'll find Mulle and his dog Buffa, the Linlyftet lift, Daisy Diesel's garage and Restaurant Chez Nous.

Konstnären med tomtar som specialitet: The artist who specialised in tomtar
Konstnärens signatur i barnkammaren: The artist's signature in the nursery
Konstnärsparet Isaac Grünewald och Sigri: In 1913 the artist couple Isaac Grünewald and Sigrid Hjertén set up their studio at the very top of the station building. The view from Katarinaberget appears in several of their finest works.
Konstprojektet Det mekaniska undret har: The art project Det mekaniska undret made music about a ride on the number 11 tram. The song Mariaplan, featuring Svartbjörn, was voted one of Göteborgs-Posten's 130 best songs in 2011. The folk singer Clas Kristiansson wrote the ballad "Sommar på Mariaplan".
Konstsamlaren på slottet: The art collector at the manor

Konsums Samköp-bandet var ett av tidens: Konsum's Samköp-bandet was one of the largest self-service shops of its day. On your way to work you dropped your order slip into a box on the facade, then collected your groceries in the evening, by 6.30 pm at the latest. You could also buy goods from vending machines with 390 compartments. Today it's home to the Cafe Chateau patisserie.
Kontorsdelen i stål och glas har ett utv: The steel-and-glass office wing has an external cylindrical stair tower and orange awnings controlled by the amount of sunlight. The small square ventilation panes in the big windows are meant to recall the perforations along a strip of film – 'the image of precision'.
Kontorshusen vid Solna strand står på ga: The office blocks at Solna strand stand on old industrial land – the area used to be called Vretens industriområde. Granite was once quarried nearby: from 1875 the City of Stockholm leased Huvudsta quarry on Lake Ulvsundasjön to make cobblestones, but by the early 1880s the rock was considered worked out. And the metro station here sits in a rock cavern a full 28 metres underground.
Kontorshuset från 1966 fick smeknamnet M: The office building from 1966 earned the nickname Munspelet, 'the Harmonica', because of its distinctive look. As early as 1932 the Spisbröd factory for crispbread was added, and in the early 1970s it was converted into a bakery.
Kontorshöghuset har 13 våningar ovan mar: The office tower has 13 floors above ground and became famous for its paternoster lifts. The façade panels have exposed light and dark aggregate, using stone from an esker near Södertälje. The building was designed by Bo Möller and opened on 12 September 1963, with Prince Bertil among those present.
Kontorsjätte vid Cityterminalen: An office giant by the City Terminal
Kontorsområdet domineras av två grupper:: Two groups of buildings dominate the office district: the gently curving yellow-brick blocks of Alviks strand and the cube-shaped red-brick buildings with glazed top floors in Alviks terrass. Most were designed by Arndt & Malmquist.
Kontorsområdet hette förr Virebergs indu: This office district used to be called Virebergs industriområde, the Vireberg industrial estate. It was planned in the 1950s by Valvet, a Wallenberg-owned property company that had bought the land from Huvudsta gård in 1947. Being close to the railway, with a siding of its own, was a big selling point, but building didn't really get going until the 1960s. Next door is Löfströms gymnasium, an upper secondary school that takes in just over 55 elite athletes a year in football, ice hockey and floorball.
Kooperativa förbundet byggde kafferoster: The Swedish Co-operative Union built the coffee roastery in 1969–1970, in brick with a red-orange metal front facing the bay. The coffee was sold as Cirkelkaffe. In spring 2013 the Royal Opera also opened a small stage here, Scen Gäddviken.
Kopparhusen byggdes som rena kontorshus: The copper-clad buildings were built purely as offices, with shops on the ground floor. In the early 2000s the two southern buildings were converted into owner-occupied flats, and the copper façade was given glazed balconies.
Kopparhusen har fått sitt namn av fasade: Kopparhusen, the Copper Houses, get their name from the copper panels on their facades. They were designed by Gunnar Jacobson and Olof Strömberg, and the consulting firm Jacobson & Widmark had its head office in one of them. At street level there were once both the town library and Systembolaget, the state-run off-licence.
Koppartak och mahognyfönster: A copper roof and mahogany windows
Korkskruvstrappan i Ericssonhuset: The corkscrew staircase in the Ericsson building
Kornhall är en liten hamnby vid Nordre ä: Kornhall is a little harbour village on the Nordre älv river, with a small shipyard and a marina. From here, the Kornhall ferry – a cable ferry – crosses the river to Brunstorpsnäs on Hisingen. The crossing dates back to 1850, and it got its first motor ferry in 1951, when traffic had grown because the route made the journey to Gothenburg so much shorter.
Korset som heter Nålsögat: The cross called the Needle's Eye
Korsvägen är porten till Göteborgs evene: Korsvägen is the gateway to Gothenburg's events district. Here you'll find the Liseberg amusement park, opened in 1923, the Universeum science centre and the Museum of World Culture – and Svenska Mässan, the Swedish Exhibition and Congress Centre, is right next door.
A short hop south along the park.
Kort hopp till S:t Eriksplan, där du byt: A short hop to S:t Eriksplan, where you change to bus 3.
A short ride via Trekanten to Gröndal.
Kortedala byggdes på 1950-talet som en m: Kortedala was built in the 1950s as a modern suburb with everything close at hand – homes, a square, schools and green spaces. A lot of the architecture from that era is still here today.
Kortedala byggdes som Göteborgs första f: Kortedala was built in the 1950s as Gothenburg's first suburb, on the city's north-eastern outskirts, where until then there had been little more than crofters' cottages. A few farms hung on right into the 1960s. Not far from here, at the entrance to Bergsjön, the long blocks of flats on Siriusgatan stand in a row along a hilltop, a landmark for the whole area.
Kortedala was built as Gothenburg's first suburb. The square itself was finished in 1955.
Kortedala was built as Gothenburg's first suburb. Its square was completed in 1955 to a design by Johan E. Tuvert of Ragndal och Tuvert Arkitektkontor.
Kortedala har sin motsvarighet i Välling: Kortedala's counterpart in Stockholm is Vällingby, and both were called satellite towns back when satellites like Sputnik were circling the Earth. For a taste of the 1950s, visit Kortedala Museum on Adventsvägen.
Kortedala torg, en bit härifrån, hette f: Kortedala torg, just along from here, was originally called Kortedalstorget. But Göteborgs Spårvägar, the Gothenburg tramways company, pointed out that everyone actually said 'Kortedalatorget', and that the official name was a mouthful. The city council voted 24 to 17, and in 1959 the square got the name it has today. That same year the Forum cinema opened on the square – only to close at the end of 1965.
Kortedala var första gången i Göteborg s: Kortedala was the first district in Gothenburg built with no link to the existing city. Like Vällingby in Stockholm, it was called a satellite town, and delegations came from all over the world to see good homes with bathrooms and parquet floors for ordinary people.
Kosläpp och laxfiske: Cows let out and salmon fishing
Kosläpp varje vår: Cows out to pasture every spring
Kovikshamn ligger vid havet, strax norr: Kovikshamn lies by the sea just north of where the Nordre älv river flows out, and it has not one but two marinas. The northern one, Kovikshamns Norra Småbåtshamn, is privately owned and the bigger of the two. Since 2015 Kovikshamn has officially counted as an urban area, and at the same time the neighbouring villages of Sundhammar and Tofta, along with Brunnefjäll, were merged into it.
Kring 1750 byggdes ett sockerbruk öster: Around 1750 a sugar refinery designed by Carl Hårleman was built east of the islet. It stood until 1841, and parts of its foundations still lie beneath Hotel Palace.
Kring 1753 döpte köpmannen Johan Anders: Around 1753 the merchant Johan Anders Lamberg renamed Geteberget hill ‘Lisas berg’ – Lisa's hill – after his wife Elisabeth, whom he called Lisa. Before that, tobacco was grown here on the Bratt plantation.
Kring 1900 låg fem torp under gården, bl: Around 1900 the farm had five crofts, among them Björnkulla, Visättra and Vistaberg. Their names live on in some of Huddinge's residential areas. In the 1930s there were 60 cows and eight horses here – and even a mink farm.
Kring Bromma kyrka ligger en liten klung: Around Bromma Church is a small cluster of old rectory buildings with a long history. The red Sockenstugan, the 17th-century parish cottage, was the vicar's home right up until 1850, when the new rectory was finished. On the same plot is a tithe barn, where the priest once collected the Bromma farmers' taxes – paid in produce rather than cash. And up on Kråsberget hill, north of Sockenstugan, stands the church's bell tower.
Kring Lötsjön i reservatet Lötsjön-Golfä: The area around Lötsjön lake in the Lötsjön-Golfängarna nature reserve teems with birdlife. Old, sturdy pines grow here too, some of them 150–200 years old.
Kring Siriusgatan finns uppgifter om fle: Records point to more ancient remains around Siriusgatan: a cairn between numbers 22 and 24, and stone circles and stone settings in a burial ground about 150 metres east of number 96. Many disappeared during the big building projects of the 1960s and 70s.
Kring förra sekelskiftet byggdes sommarv: Around 1900 summer villas sprang up here, drawn by the views of Lake Mälaren and the steamboat jetty. At the same time a steam-powered sawmill operated at Jungfrusund, and charcoal stacks smouldered on Gällstaö to keep it supplied with energy.
Kring förra sekelskiftet fanns flera trä: Around the turn of the 20th century, the Malmvik estate had several gardens and orchards alongside its farmland. There were smaller orchards here at Betlehem and at Lindö too.
Kring förra sekelskiftet köpte grosshand: Around 1900 the wholesale merchants Fredric Althainz and Carl Bengtsson bought land here to build an exclusive suburb, Södertörns villastad. Plots sold slowly and only a handful of houses were built. In 1912 the land was sold to the City of Stockholm.
Kring köpcentrumet i norra Botkyrka finn: The area around this shopping centre in northern Botkyrka has an unusually close-knit cluster of churches. Botkyrka folkhögskola, a folk high school – a kind of adult education college – founded in 1997, is owned by five Christian congregations, three of them Syriac Orthodox, yet it's open to everyone, whatever their faith. Ljusets kyrka, the Church of Light, on Tomtbergavägen, sits right next to the Syriac Orthodox Church of St Peter and St Paul, while Hallundakyrkan is practically wall to wall with the shopping centre.
Kring norra Magelungen har man hittat se: Six Stone Age axes have been found around northern Lake Magelungen, including a miniature boat axe some 4,500 years old, found behind Spårfinnargränd in Rågsved. The open green space also has a large boulder with 32 cup marks.

Six Stone Age axes have been found around the northern end of Magelungen lake. One is a miniature boat-shaped axe that turned up behind Spårfinnargränd in Rågsved, possibly from a grave. In the Stone Age, Magelungen was linked to the Baltic via Drevviken.
Kring sekelskiftet var det vanligt att g: Around the turn of the 20th century it was common to give houses their own names. Linboda no. 7 was christened Sofiero after the lady of the house, Sofia Ekberg, and the neighbouring houses had names like Sjögeberg and Skogsborg.
Kring år 1800 hade operadansösen Sophie: Around 1800 the estate belonged to the opera dancer Sophie Hagman, best known as the mistress of Prince Fredrik Adolf. During her time large sums were spent beautifying it, and a double avenue of lime trees was planted down to the water.
Kring år 1800 ägdes gården av slottssten: Around 1800 the farm belonged to J.A. Göthe, stonemason at the Royal Palace. He installed a large carved fireplace in the main room – taken from Stockholm Palace, where it had been removed during a modernisation in the 1790s.
Kring år 1900 växte hamnen med sommarvil: Around 1900 the harbour grew with summer villas, drawn by the views over Lake Mälaren and the steamboats to Stockholm. There was also a steam-powered sawmill, and charcoal stacks burned on Gällstaö to fuel it.
Kritik mot storskaligheten och enformigh: Before long, people began criticising the sheer scale and monotony. From 1984, over roughly ten years, Hallonbergen was given a makeover: the courtyards were redesigned and some buildings got colourful façades.
Kritiken var enhällig när kyrkan invigde: The critics were unanimous when the church was consecrated in 1859. The writer Viktor Rydberg noted that its tower was lower than those of the German Church and the cathedral, but "more powerful, more resolute, more devout than they".

Krogen Stocksundsbro från 1788 hade dåli: The Stocksundsbro inn from 1788 had a bad reputation for heavy drinking and drunken brawls; one traveller wrote that he shuddered whenever he had to pass by. The new inn was built in 1814–1816, probably to raise the tone.
Krogen grundades 1626 av proviantmästare: The inn was founded in 1626 by the quartermaster Henrik Olofsson, who was granted the right by King Gustav II Adolf to run a hostelry on the highway between Stockholm and Uppsala. A copy of the charter – the first of its kind – hangs in the entrance.

Krogen stängde 1872 när gästerna blev fö: The inn closed in 1872 when customers dried up. The building then became a primary school and later housing for statare, the contracted farm labourers. On Walpurgis Eve 1983 Christer Lingström reopened it as a restaurant, since it was Sweden's oldest surviving inn building.

Krokslätts fabriker är gamla industribyg: Krokslätts fabriker are old industrial buildings where textiles were once made. Today they're home to businesses, restaurants and flats – a good example of old factories getting a new lease of life.
Krokängsparken var folkpark 1903–1934. P: Krokängsparken was a folkpark, or people's park, from 1903 to 1934. On Sunday mornings people marched here from the ferry landing with music and banners. There was a dance floor, a carousel and a shooting gallery, and you could buy hot dogs, sweets and cigars. Political speeches shared the bill with entertainers and folk comedies.
Krokängsparken var folkpark mellan 1903: Krokängsparken was a folkpark – a popular open-air entertainment park – from 1903 to 1934. On Sunday mornings people marched with music and banners from the ferry landing to the festival ground, where there were political speeches, a dance floor, a carousel, a shooting gallery and hot dogs. In the end the competition from Liseberg proved too stiff, and in 1934 the company went bankrupt.
Krokängsparken, en promenadpark på cirka: Krokängsparken, a park for walking of about 7.5 hectares, was laid out as far back as 1902 between Bratteråsberget hill and Pölsebo. A little further on, towards the river, towers the Eriksberg crane, a gantry crane from 1969 that's just over 70 metres tall and almost 110 metres wide. It's a listed structure and a symbol of the shipyard era, when everything about shipbuilding was on a giant scale.
Kronprins Gustav Adolf invigde flyghamne: Crown Prince Gustav Adolf opened the airport on 5 August 1923, the same year Gothenburg celebrated its 300th anniversary. Bad weather pushed the ceremony back by a day. The airfield was laid out on land belonging to the farms of Amhult Uppegård, Röd Sörgård and Amhult Nedergård.

Kronprinsesse Märtha gick i trafik Sandn: Kronprinsesse Märtha sailed the Sandnes–Stavanger–Bergen route. In 1942 the German occupying forces made her change her name to Ryfylke, but in May 1945 she got her own name back.
Krontorpet Hökmossen nämns första gången: Hökmossen, a croft owned by the Crown, is first mentioned in 1748 in a document in the Military Archives. Back then it was called Hökmåsen, after a bog north of the farm that has since disappeared. A little way off, in an old co-op building in the villa suburb of Långbro, was the restaurant Aloë, which served luxurious tasting menus from 2015 to 2025 and earned two Michelin stars.

The crown croft of Hökmossen is first mentioned in 1748, in a document in the Military Archives, where it's called Hökmåsen. The name comes from a bog (mosse) north of the farm that has since disappeared.
Krossgatan ligger i Vinsta industriområd: Krossgatan runs through the Vinsta industrial area, where Vällingby fire station opened in December 1964. Its firefighters have special training in roof ventilation and climbing at height. Johannelund metro station was built as an 'industrial station' with two side platforms – the only one like it on the Stockholm metro – and until October 1997 it opened only at rush hour. The Vinsta district takes its name from the old village of Vinsta.
Krucifixet som fick färg: The crucifix that was given colour
Krusboda byggdes under åren 1970–1975 oc: Krusboda was built between 1970 and 1975 and has its own school. Not far away, on Lake Albysjön, is Nyfors, a well-preserved 1940s holiday-cottage area where more and more people now live all year round. Between the branches of the Wättinge stream lies Bullerholmen – ‘Noisy Islet’ – which, despite its name, is now completely uninhabited. North of the cottages begins the Alby nature reserve.
Krusboda täcker cirka 840 000 kvadratmet: Krusboda covers about 840,000 square metres, roughly half of it jointly owned land – making it one of the largest joint property associations in Sweden. There are 798 terraced houses, 328 atrium houses and a shared pool and sauna.
Krusboda är indelat i delområden som oft: Krusboda is divided into sections usually called 'gångar', or lanes, which also serve as addresses – Lummergången (Clubmoss Lane), Musserongången, Renlavsgången (Reindeer Lichen Lane), Fårtickegången and Pärlröksgången, to name a few.

Krusboda is divided into sections usually known as 'gångar' – walkways – which also serve as addresses. They include Musserongången, Renlavsgången, Fårtickegången and Lummergången, named after mushrooms, lichens and clubmoss.
Kryddhandlaren Carl Peter Eneroth hade a: The spice merchant Carl Peter Eneroth had a shop at Västerlånggatan 45 and grew up on Kevinge farm. His godfather was Zacharias Strindberg, grandfather of August Strindberg. Klimpen was the rocky knoll where Calle cast his fishing rod.

Kråkan var förr krokig och stensatt och: Kråkan was once a winding cobbled hill, and wasn't tarmacked until 1956, ahead of the Swedish cycling championships. In the 1980s the hill was straightened, its crest blasted away and the gradient reduced by a third.
Kråkan var stensatt och asfalterades för: Kråkan was cobbled and only got its asphalt in 1956, ahead of the Swedish cycling championships. Plans for a new road that would have meant demolishing many houses in Kvarnbyn were dropped after fierce opposition. Instead the hill itself was reworked in 1985: the crest was blasted away and the gradient cut by a third.
Krögaren Eric Nordström, som gjorde krog: The innkeeper Eric Nordström, who made the inn more profitable than the garden, had once been a garden hand at the house where Bellman was born. He was also the father-in-law of Maria Kristina Kiellström, better known as Ulla Winblad in Bellman's Epistles.
Krögaren och kocken Mikael Öster värvade: Restaurateur and chef Mikael Öster was brought in to run Westra Piren. Upstairs was the gourmet restaurant, seating 70, where the kitchen cooked in the classic French tradition. Downstairs there was a bar and a brasserie.
Kulan på kullen är Bällsta radartorn, i: The ball on the hill is the Bällsta radar tower, nicknamed the Golf Ball, standing between Bromma Airport and Solvalla. The Solvalla trotting track opened in 1927, holds 35,000 spectators and hosts the Elitloppet race every year. In Bällsta itself, around 200 cottages were built by their owners with their own hands, using materials and instructions from the city's small-house office.
The ball-bearing giant SKF has deep roots here. Not far away in Gamlestaden was Mariedal's landeri, a small country estate, where SKF had its office from 1910 to 1914. Nearby was also Torpavallen, the old home ground of Qviding FIF, with two gravel pitches and a grass pitch with a stand. Where footballs once rolled, the Torpavallen shopping centre now stands.
Kullen är cirka 20 meter högre än den ur: The hill is about 20 metres higher than the original gravel ridge, because slalom slopes were planned on its north side. They were never built. From the top you can see the Globe, Högdalstoppen, Söder Torn and the Wenner-Gren Center, though trees now hide some of the view.
Kultur i oväntade lokaler finns en bit h: Culture in unexpected places awaits a short way from here in Fullersta. Fullersta bio is now an art gallery and theatre, housed in former Konsum co-op shops and an old cinema. And since 2009, the manor house Fullersta gård – once the centre of an estate whose lands covered the whole area – has been home to a contemporary art gallery.
Kulturföreningen Hökmossens Gård bildade: The Hökmossens Gård cultural society was founded in 1994 and is funded by raffles, bazaars and auctions. It runs study circles, literary cafés and cultural trips, and the buildings are green-listed by the Stockholm City Museum.

Kulturhuset invigdes 2002 som en symbol: The cultural centre opened in 2002 as a symbol of the municipality's journey from crisis to success. In the library hall, tree-like pillars reach up to a ceiling of wooden slats, and plants and wood blur the line between inside and out.

Kumla allé är cirka 850 meter lång och l: Kumla allé is about 850 metres long and still leads up to the manor house. The old line of trees survives along its southern stretch. At the northern end of the avenue is Alléplan, generally known as Trollbäcken's centre.
