Kung Gustaf V invigde Lovö vattenverk de: King Gustaf V inaugurated the Lovö waterworks on 25 May 1933. Until then the Norsborg waterworks in Botkyrka had supplied all of Stockholm with drinking water.
Kung Oscar II invigde gasverket den 25 n: King Oscar II opened the gasworks on 25 November 1893, together with Crown Prince Gustaf and Princes Carl and Eugen. A special train ran from Central Station right onto the works' own tracks. Boberg was awarded the Order of Vasa for his work.

All three opened on the same day with spectacles, illuminations and a comedy by Carl Michael Bellman.

Kungen var på väg hem från jakt och hade: The King was on his way home from a hunt in tall hunting boots, so he made it ashore with dry feet while everyone else got theirs wet. He took it calmly, smoked a cigarette and said it was "a blessing in disguise".
Kungen var på väg hem från jakt vid Tull: The King was on his way home from hunting at Tullgarn. Thanks to his tall hunting boots he stepped ashore dry-shod, while everyone else got wet feet. He smoked a cigarette and declared it "a blessing in disguise".

Kungens kurva har fått namn efter att Gu: Kungens kurva, "the King's Curve", got its name after Gustaf V's Cadillac ended up in the ditch here on 28 September 1946, on the way home from a hunt. The car slid into a waterlogged ditch, and Dagens Nyheter reported that the King "stepped out dry-shod after car tumble into marshy pool".
Kungens kurva har fått sitt namn efter d: Kungens kurva, 'the King's Curve', got its name on 28 September 1946, when King Gustaf V's Cadillac left the road here on the way home from a hunt. The car came to rest in a water-filled ditch, and Dagens Nyheter reported that the King stepped out with dry feet. Both Sparreholm Castle and the Skokloster motor museum have claimed that their car was the real one.
Kungens kurva har fått sitt namn från en: Kungens kurva, 'the King's Curve', is named after a real accident. On 28 September 1946, King Gustaf V's chauffeur came off Södertäljevägen near here and ended up stuck in a water-filled ditch – and the name stuck too. IKEA opened its second store here in 1965, and the round building was inspired by the Guggenheim Museum in New York.

Kungl. Maj:t krävde att den nya kyrkan s: The Crown insisted that the new church be built of dressed stone, which pushed up the cost. The stone came from the granite quarry at Smögen, and the church was set on the Sörgårds vale hill with a fine view. It was consecrated on 16 September 1906.
Kungliga Vetenskapsakademien lät bygga S: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences built Stockholm's old observatory in 1753 to designs by Carl Hårleman. Research here covered astronomy, geography and meteorology. Astronomy moved out to Saltsjöbaden in 1931, and the building became a geography department.

Kungseken har en omkrets på sju meter oc: The King's Oak has a girth of seven metres and is one of Stockholm's 100 stoutest oaks. It's estimated to be around 400 years old. On 10 October 2016 the tree caught fire, but the fire brigade arrived quickly and the oak survived.
Kungsgatan 65 har levt många liv. Biogra: Kungsgatan 65 has worn many hats. The Palladium cinema opened here in 1918, with the Bal Palais dance restaurant in the basement. Later it became the Heaven nightclub, and from 2003 to 2025 it was Casino Cosmopol. Next door is Oscarsteatern from 1906, a listed theatre named after King Oscar II. The same building is home to Fasching, Scandinavia's largest jazz club since 1977.
Kungshamns fyr anlades 1905 med en fotog: Kungshamn lighthouse was built in 1905 with a paraffin-fuelled wick lamp. The paraffin was replaced by gas-powered AGA lighting, and in 1956 the lighthouse switched to electricity.
Kungshamra planerades bilfritt, med park: Kungshamra was planned to be car-free, with parking kept outside. Landscape architect Gunnar Martinsson argued that no purpose-built playgrounds were needed, since the whole area could serve as one big outdoor playroom. Kitchens in the family flats face the courtyards so parents can keep an eye on the children.
Kungshamra planerades bilfritt. Landskap: Kungshamra was planned to be car-free. Landscape architect Gunnar Martinsson saw no need for playgrounds – the whole area was meant to work as one big space for play and outdoor living.
Kungshatt saknar bro och bilfärja, så vä: Kungshatt has no bridge and no car ferry, so its roads are car-free. The island has fewer than 20 permanent residents but 140 built-on plots, and boat line 89 serves the Kungshättan jetty all year round.
Kungshatt var ett av Stockholmstraktens: Kungshatt was one of the biggest brickworks in the Stockholm area. In the early 1900s about 100 men made some four million bricks a year, which were shipped by barge to Stockholm. The works burned to the ground in 1947.
Kungshatts gård nämns som säteri på 1680: Kungshatt farm is recorded as a manor in the 1680s. In the early 1700s Hedvig Taube, mistress of King Fredrik I, spent her summers here. The farm's cross-shaped avenue of lime trees survives to this day.

Kungshatt farm is recorded as a manor in the 1680s. In the early 1700s Hedvig Taube, mistress of King Frederick I, spent her summers here. The cross-shaped lime avenue from the estate's heyday is still there.
Kungshatts tegelbruk var ett av Stockhol: The Kungshatt brickworks was one of the largest in the Stockholm area. In the early 1900s some 100 men made around four million bricks a year, shipped to Stockholm by barge in the spring. The works burned down on 17 September 1947.
Kungsholmens barnkrubba grundades 1854 a: Kungsholmen's crèche was founded in 1854 by Professor Magnus Huss, who had been inspired by the crèches of Paris. The idea was to look after the children of poor families so their parents could go out to work. It lives on as Sweden's oldest preschool.
Kungsholms folkskola var Sveriges störst: Kungsholms folkskola was Sweden's biggest primary school and one of the largest in the world, with room for 4,000 pupils. Only the northern part survives today, home among other things to Stockholm's arts school. This neighbourhood is full of firsts: Kungsholmen's crèche was the first of its kind in Sweden, and Kvinnohuset, a fourteen-storey cooperative block of flats for women, opened here in 1947.
Kungsholms villastad startades av Ulvsun: Kungsholms villastad was started by Max Wibom, owner of Ulvsunda Castle, and Per August Kindgren. The development company didn't bother with roads or sewers, and sanitary conditions were dreadful. The city bought the land, and parts of the villa town were demolished to make room for the garden suburb.
Kungsklippan var först tänkt som kyrktom: Kungsklippan was first earmarked as a site for a church, but in 1945 it was decided it should become a park instead. This is where the people of Essingen light their Walpurgis Night bonfire on 30 April, with the band marching up from Essingetorget. The view stretches all the way to Kaknästornet tower.
Kungsladugård har den största sammanhäng: Kungsladugård has the largest continuous area of landshövdingehus, Gothenburg's stone-and-wood tenement houses. They were built between 1916 and 1938, and the area was planned by the chief city engineer, Albert Lilienberg. The town plan is of national interest.
Kungsladugård är tidigt bostadsbyggande: Kungsladugård is an early chapter in Gothenburg's housing history. The Svärdsliljan block from 1927 was one of HSB's first blocks of landshövdingehus – Gothenburg's typical houses with a stone ground floor and wooden upper floors. The district also has a bronze statue, Ung man, Young Man, made by Astrid Noack in 1948 and set up on the corner of Ståthållaregatan and Fågelfängaregatan in 1968. Kungsladugård Church is just a short walk away.
Kungsladugårds kyrka invigdes 1960 av bi: Kungsladugård Church was consecrated in 1960 by Bishop Bo Giertz. Much of it was paid for with money a sewing circle had raised over thirty years. The pulpit and font are built of brick.
Kungsladugårdsgatan fick sitt namn 1918: Kungsladugårdsgatan got its name in 1918 from Älvsborgs Kungsladugård, the royal farm that supplied Älvsborg Castle with horses, grain and more. Its land covered what is now Majorna and Kungsladugård.
Kungsladugårdsgatan är bred av en anledn: There's a reason Kungsladugårdsgatan is so wide. In Albert Lilienberg's town plan of 1916, it was drawn at double width to leave room for a future railway between the harbour and the city. The name comes from Älvsborgs Kungsladugård, the royal farm that supplied Älvsborg Castle with horses and grain. Along the street stands the Broström Foundation's building from 1924, listed since 2017.
Kungsporten låg ungefär där Kungsportsbr: The King’s Gate, Kungsporten, stood roughly where Kungsportsbron bridge is today. This was where people and goods were checked and customs duties collected. The gatehouse also housed the town watch, with a lock-up on the first floor. The gate was made of wood from 1621 to 1653, and of stone after that.
Kungspudeln och Bulldoggen: The King Poodle and the Bulldog
Kungssten lies close to the mouth of the Göta älv river. From here you can see Älvsborgsbron, the Älvsborg Bridge, which was the longest suspension bridge in Sweden when it opened in 1966. Out in the estuary is the 17th-century New Älvsborg Fortress, built to defend the city against the Danes. Down by the water is Klippan, with old seamen's cottages and the remains of the older Älvsborg Fortress.
Kungsstol i röd sammet: A royal seat in red velvet
Kungsträdgården var från början kungens: Kungsträdgården, the King's Garden, began life as the royal kitchen garden. Today it's one of the city's best-loved parks, and in spring its cherry trees burst into pink and white blossom.
Kungälv hette först Kongahälla och låg t: Kungälv was originally called Kongahälla and lay three kilometres further west, on the Nordre älv river. According to Snorri Sturluson, the three Nordic kings met here in 1101 and made peace. Arvid Källström's statue Tre kungar, "Three Kings", has commemorated the meeting on Nytorget since 1959.
Kupolen bärs av 48 böjda stålpelare upp: Up to the 'equator', the dome is supported by 48 curved steel columns. Above that, the shell is a space frame with 2,200 joints and 13,000 aluminium tubes.
Kurdiska biblioteket grundades av Nedim: The Kurdish Library was founded by Nedim Dagdeviren and opened on 10 October 1997 by the culture minister, Marita Ulvskog. Its premises in the Alvik community centre were opened in 2011 by Birgitta Ohlsson, minister for democracy and EU affairs.
Kursgård ägd av fem förbund: A conference centre owned by five unions
Kusinen som var präst här: The cousin who was vicar here
Kvar i dag är den gula huvudbyggnaden, d: What survives today is the yellow main house, the red workers' row and the red storehouse, which is probably the oldest. For a while the workers' row was the clubhouse of the Mälarhöjden scout troop, and the stable was used by a riding school before it was pulled down.
Kvarnbygatan har haft många namn genom å: Kvarnbygatan has gone by many names over the years, among them Allmänna vägen, Lessgatan, Lerskalla and Regeringsgatan. The name Kråkan is recorded as early as 1662.
Kvarnen Brinckan ägdes av brännvinsbränn: The windmill known as Brinckan belonged to the schnapps distiller Måns Brinck, which is why Timmermansgatan was also called Brinckan-backen in the 1740s. In 1733 there were no fewer than six windmills in the neighbourhood.
Kvarnen bakom en storbrand: The mill behind a great fire
Kvarnen byggdes av fogden Henrik Olofsso: The mill was built by the bailiff Henrik Olofsson, who also put up Edsberg manor and founded the Edsbacka inn in 1626. In 1638 the estate and mill were owned by Count Gabriel Bengtsson Oxenstierna.
Kvarnen flyttades 1813 närmare Söderby g: In 1813 the mill was moved closer to Söderby farm and became Söderby mill, run by the Grip family from 1923 to 1962. Mjölnare Grips väg – Miller Grip's Road – is named after David Grip. Street names such as Turbinvägen and Elevatorvägen also recall the milling days.
Kvarnen gick i två tolvtimmarsskift månd: The mill ran two twelve-hour shifts from Monday to Saturday, and in the early years a mill worker earned 75 kronor a month. In 1911 it switched from steam to electric power. When the mill closed in 1992, 370 people lost their jobs.
Kvarnen i Agnesberg, P.O. Stokkebye Kvar: The mill at Agnesberg, P.O. Stokkebye Kvarnaktiebolag, produced AXA rolled oats among other things. This is where the method of steam-treating oats was developed. The mill closed in 1979 and production moved to Järna.
Kvarnen malde fram till 1947 och använde: The windmill ground grain until 1947 and was then used for a while as a summer cottage. From 1977 it was restored by Thure Andersson together with the local heritage society, Burås Gille.
Kvarnen på Vårdkaseberget brann ned till: The windmill on Vårdkaseberget burnt to the ground at Easter 1939. The miller's house survives and is used by the scouts, and every year the Walpurgis Night bonfire on 30 April is lit where the mill once stood.
Kvarnen på Vårdkaseberget nordväst om gå: The mill on Vårdkaseberget, north-west of the farm, burned down at Easter 1939. Every year the Walpurgis Night bonfire is lit where it stood, and the old miller's house is used by the scouts.
Kvarnen ritades av Wilhelm Bergström i o: The mill was designed by Wilhelm Bergström in bare brick with stepped gables, eight storeys high. In 1915 the central tower was raised to hold a water cistern for a sprinkler system, gaining the castle-like battlements it still has today.
Kvarnen som blev skola: The windmill that became a school
Kvarnen som brann tre gånger: The windmill that burned three times
Kvarnen som dödade en ko: The windmill that killed a cow
Kvarnen som flyttade från stan: The windmill that moved out of town
Kvarnen som malde i 300 år: The mill that ground for 300 years
Kvarnen som står här i dag byggdes 1855: The windmill that stands here today was built in 1855 for the farmer Knut Bennet of Bällsta farm, about three kilometres north-west of here. It was designed by his 19-year-old nephew Karl Abraham Saxenberg, who was given a gold watch as thanks. The weathervane still reads "KB 1855".
Kvarnen som vrids mot vinden: The mill that turns to face the wind
Kvarnen stod på en liten kulle som kalla: The mill stood on a small hill called Väderkvarnsberget, Windmill Hill, south-west of Hässelby Palace. A map from 1652 shows it as a post mill. Where Qvarnhagen once lay there's now an allotment garden and a street called Kvarnhagsvägen.
Kvarnen var en holländare, där bara topp: The mill was a Dutch-style windmill, where only the cap with its sails turned to face the wind. It was ten-sided and tapered towards the top. A photo from 1919 shows it with six sails, but by 1926 it had four. In 1929 the sails were blown away in an autumn storm.
Kvarnen var ett svartbygge: The mill was built without permission
Kvarnen är blåmärkt av Stadsmuseet, den: The windmill is marked blue by the Stockholm City Museum, the highest heritage rating. It has been restored but now stands without its sails.
Kvarnen är en stolpkvarn, där hela byggn: This is a post mill, where the entire building is turned to face the wind. The name Stampan hints that it may have pounded flax and hemp for rope and sails, but there's no record of that.
Kvarnen är i dag renoverad, men saknar v: The windmill has been restored, but it has no sails. It stands among the houses of Solhem, far from its original hill in the inner city.
Kvarngatan på Södermalm har fått sitt na: Kvarngatan in Södermalm is named after the windmills that stood here in the 17th and 18th centuries. It was probably Christian Hansson's mill that started the great Katarina fire of 1723.
Kvarnholmen hette från början Hästholmen: Kvarnholmen, "Mill Island", was originally called Hästholmen, "Horse Island". To build the mill in 1897, 14,000 cubic metres of rock were blasted out of the hillside and used to push the shoreline out 15 metres and build a harbour. The mill was 84 metres long, with towers 38 metres high.
Kvarnholmen hette först Hästholmen. Men: Kvarnholmen was originally called Hästholmen. But there's also a postal town called Hästholmen in Östergötland, and the post was often delayed. So the name was simply changed to Kvarnholmen, which had its own post town status from 1938 to 1957.
Kvarnholmen var en gång en ö full av mjö: Kvarnholmen, ‘Mill Island’, was once all about flour and bread. The Tre Kronor mill started up in 1897, and there was also a macaroni factory, an oat mill and a crispbread bakery. Today people live in the old silos – when Silo III was turned into flats, for a while nothing but its outer walls was left standing. The old bakery, Bageriet, is now Kvarnholmen's centre, and the oat mill, Havrekvarnen, has been listed since 2016.
Kvarnholmen var från början en ö, men su: Kvarnholmen used to be an island, until the channel separating it was filled in during the 1970s to give the factories a better transport link. This was home to the Tre Kronor flour mill, and its oat mill, Havrekvarnen, built in 1927–28, is now a listed building. Around Tre Kronors väg the company built a model village for its workers, with terraced houses, narrow blocks of flats and its very own Konsum co-op store, open from 1935 to 1977. The Munspelet office building from 1966 – nicknamed “the Harmonica” – is listed for its striking modernist architecture.
Kvarnholmens centrum ligger i Bageriet,: Kvarnholmen's centre is Bageriet, the Bakery – the old crispbread factory, whose earliest drawings date from 1929. Today people live where the crispbread used to be baked. Right next door is Disponentvillan, the manager's villa, built in 1931 for the head of Kvarnen Tre Kronor, the Three Crowns Mill. Makaronifabriken, the macaroni factory, is still here too, and the Lilla Kvarnholmen playground is themed on the island's old industrial buildings.
Kvarnkontoret ritades av Edward Ohlsson,: The mill office was designed by Edward Ohlsson, an experienced industrial architect who had worked for the Nürnberg and Hamburger breweries. For almost 30 years the building was the workplace of Emil Hamring, the cooperative KF's managing director.
Kvarnsjöns utlopp drev förr Lissma kvarn: The outflow from Lake Kvarnsjön once powered Lissma mill. Low walls of dressed grey stone still line both sides of the stream, with an old wooden cart bridge across it. The lake is only 1.7 metres deep.
Kvarnskolan bekostades av Edvard Witte p: Kvarnskolan was paid for by Edvard Witte of Gåshaga farm, who wanted to give the parish's girls a school for reading and handicrafts. Boys were admitted as early as 1890. The building also housed a poorhouse, and the schoolmistress lived in the miller's cottage by the mill.
Kvarnstenen fick ny plats: A new home for the millstone
Kvarnstenen flyttades efter ett medborga: The millstone was moved following a residents' proposal in 2011, and since 2013 it has stood on Gymnasievägen. It's sandstone, about 1.25 metres across, with radial grooves that channelled the flour out to the edge. Two more millstones are set into the footpath by Kvarnbergsgården.
Kvarnstenen vid Gymnasievägen är av sand: The millstone on Gymnasievägen is made of sandstone and measures about 1.25 metres across. Grooves in the stone channelled the flour out to the edge, where it could be collected. It was moved here in 2013 following a suggestion from a local resident.
Kvarnstenen är av sandsten, cirka 1,25 m: The millstone is made of sandstone and measures about 1.25 metres across. Its radiating grooves carried the ground grain out to the edge, where the flour could be collected.
Kvarntorpshällens text lyder i översättn: Translated, the inscription on the Kvarntorp rock reads: ‘Isa had the stone carved for her stepsons, and Helga had it carved for her sons Dan and Sven.’ Note that the word for stepsons is in the plural.
Kvarter med stjärnnamn: A neighbourhood named after the stars
Kvarter och gator i Husby är uppkallade: Husby's blocks and streets are named after Norwegian places and people, such as Oslogatan, Trondheimsgatan and Edvard Griegsgången. Cars and pedestrians are kept apart on separate levels, with footbridges spanning the sunken roads.
Kvarteren Sol, Vind och Vatten: The Sun, Wind and Water blocks
Kvarteren här har namn från fotografins: The blocks here take their names from the world of photography, such as Blixtlampan (the Flash), Filmremsan (the Film Strip), Stillbilden (the Still) and Filmkameran (the Film Camera). To the south rises Högdalstoppen, an artificial hill of excavated soil and demolition rubble that began to be piled up in 1955.
Kvarteren här heter bland annat Uppfinna: The blocks here have names such as Uppfinnaren (the Inventor), Solventilen, Agaspisen and Geodimetern, and the streets are called Optikvägen, Radiovägen and Prismavägen – all reminders of the AGA company. The machine shop with its sawtooth roof survives from the days of inventor Gustaf Dalén.
Kvarteren i Annedal har fått namn efter: The blocks in Annedal are named after Swedish children's books: Kulla-Gulla, Lasse Liten, Skalman, Kusin Vitamin, Tant Brun, Tant Grön and Tant Gredelin. The first tenants moved in in February 2011, on Pippi Långstrumps gata – Pippi Longstocking Street.
Kvarteren i Solna strand har fått namn e: The blocks in Solna strand are named after fruit, berries, nuts and vegetables – Smultronet (the Wild Strawberry), Päronet (the Pear), Aprikosen (the Apricot) and Apelsinen (the Orange), for example. In summer the electric boat E/S Movitz sails from here to Klara Mälarstrand.
Kvarteren längs Saltvägen heter bland an: The blocks along Saltvägen have names like Kryddosten, Bordssaltet, Peppardosan, Kardemumman and Muskotblomman – spiced cheese, table salt, the pepper pot, cardamom and mace. By Kaffebalen and Kardemumman is Hökarängen's highest point, 61 metres above sea level.
Kvarteren och gatorna i Husby har fått n: The blocks and streets of Husby are named after Norwegian places and people – Oslogatan, Trondheimsgatan and Edvard Griegsgången, for example. Norgegatan, sunk into a rock cutting, slices straight through the district.
Kvarteren runt Wieselgrensplatsen består: The blocks around Wieselgrensplatsen are made up of landshövdingehus – Gothenburg's tenements with a stone ground floor and two wooden storeys above – and Lundby Hospital stands on the square.
Kvarteren skulle heta Tillflykten, Lycka: The blocks were to be called Tillflykten (Refuge), Lyckan (Happiness), Paradiset (Paradise) and Lustgården (Pleasure Garden), and the roads Rosenstigen, Jägarstigen, Ulvstigen and Lärkstigen – Rose, Hunter, Wolf and Lark paths. In 1925 Ulvstigen was renamed Warfvinges väg.
Kvarteren vid Åkerbyvägen hör till HSB:s: The blocks along Åkerbyvägen are part of HSB's low-rise housing in Tibble, one of the areas built in the 1950s and 60s. A little further away is Täby centrum, with the Filmstaden cinema, opened in 2013, which has five screens and 516 seats. In the other direction is Ensta station on the Roslagsbanan railway, where around 500 people get on on an ordinary winter weekday.

The blocks along Åkerbyvägen are part of HSB's low-rise housing in Tibble, one of the areas built in the 1950s and 1960s. A little way off is Täby Centrum, with the Filmstaden cinema, opened in 2013, which has five screens and 516 seats. The Roslagsbanan railway has no fewer than three stations in Tibble, so the train is never far away.
Kvarteren väster om tunnelbanan heter ti: The blocks west of the metro have names such as Fyrkantsfilen, Falshyveln and Skruvtvinget – the square file, the rebate plane and the screw clamp, all borrowed from cabinetmaking. The buildings were designed by Nils Hjelm in the influential architecture of the Swedish welfare-state era.
Kvarteret Bergholmen ritades av Britta o: The Bergholmen block was designed by Britta and Kjell Abramson. Some of the stairwells are semicircular with slits of glass block, and the entrances look like glass display cases mounted on the outside.
Kvarteret Gamlebo, intill Svedmyra tunne: The Gamlebo block, beside Svedmyra metro station, was originally built as Gamlebo, the City of Stockholm's old people's home, later known as Gammelbyn. Its ten original residential buildings are now owner-occupied flats. Much closer, on the corner of Bandhagsvägen and Tussmötevägen, was the Corso cinema, which opened in 1938 as Tusse-Bio and closed in 1969.
Kvarteret Holmia bildades 1906 av det ny: The Holmia district was founded in 1906 by a newly formed company, AB Lidingö Villastad, and its early 20th-century character is still beautifully preserved, with villas in National Romantic, Art Nouveau and Art Nouveau Baroque styles. Here you'll find Lidingö museum, in the former Villa Fornboda from 1907, with exhibitions on 20th-century Lidingö and a turn-of-the-century salon. It's run by Lidingö's local heritage society – one of the largest in Sweden – which among other things organises Bellman Day.
Kvarteret Kabbelekan består av sex hus i: The Kabbelekan block consists of six buildings in 1920s Classicism, designed by Allan Berglund in 1924. The central building facing Mariagatan has three gables crowned with spires, and the dormers have half-moon windows.
Kvarteret Lojo är uppkallat efter Liding: The Lojo block is named after Lidingö’s twin town Lohja (Lojo in Swedish) in Finland. Its 24 houses have facades of brick and wood panelling in red or yellow – one colour per terrace – and white balconies. They sit carefully placed in the rocky, pine-covered terrain.
Kvarteret Loket har fått namn efter Atla: The Loket block – ‘the Locomotive’ – takes its name from the Atlas area, where AB Atlas made locomotives among other things. The neighbouring blocks are called Lokstallet, Tendern and Kolven (the engine shed, the tender and the piston). On the porcelain side, they’re called Fajansen, Leran and Terrakottan instead – faience, clay and terracotta.
Kvarteret Malmgården vid platsens västra: The Malmgården block on the western side of the square consists of two five-storey buildings from 1914, designed by Oscar W Nilsson. With their reddish-brown brick, steep tiled roofs and small-paned windows, they're a fine example of the National Romantic style.
Kvarteret Paris har inget med den fransk: The Paris block has nothing to do with the French capital. The name probably goes back to the German-born innkeeper Jakob Paris, who ran an eating house here in the 1600s.
Kvarteret Paris och krögaren: The Paris block and the innkeeper
Kvarteret Plankan var länge ett skräpigt: For years the Plankan block was a scruffy area of little workshops in sheds. In 1964–68 a single continuous building designed by Lars Bryde was put up, filling the entire block. The same architect designed the buildings in Drakenberg opposite.
Kvarteret Rosteriet har fått namn efter: The Rosteriet block – ‘the Roastery’ – is named after a German firm that roasted coffee substitute here from 1913 to 1920. Pharmacia then made medicines on the site, and in the 1950s and 60s AB Atomenergi produced fuel rods here for Swedish research reactors. Up on Liljeholmsberget hill is Brännkyrka's old parish hall from the 1920s, which since 2003 has been home to Nordic Music, an upper secondary school.
Kvarteret Sörgården öster om Spånga kyrk: The Sörgården block east of Spånga Church is Tensta's only original area of small houses. Its 76 terraced houses from 1969–1970 were built by the residents themselves, with pale render and red timber cladding.
Kvarteret Taklampan med 64 lägenheter är: The Taklampan block, with 64 flats, is a zero-energy property: over a year, the buildings produce as much energy as they use for heating, water and shared electricity. In 2017 it was named "Property of the Future".
Kvarteret Tjalve, ritat omkring 1920 av: The Tjalve block, designed around 1920 by Karl Güettler, shows that clerks, craftsmen and workers wanted villas of their own in Djursholm too. Western Ösby has the municipality's only surviving larger area of early functionalist architecture.
Kvarteret heter Klamparen efter en gamma: The block is called Klamparen after an old trade: a foreman who sorted timber at a lumber yard. In the second half of the 19th century there were large lumber yards here.
Kvarterets praktfullaste hus är Villa Ol: The grandest house in the block is Villa Oldenburg from 1909–1910, designed by town planner Per Olof Hallman for the notary public Uno Oldenburg. Look for his initials on the cartouche in the gable facing Lejonvägen.
Kvartersnamnen i nordöstra Björkhagen ko: The block names in north-eastern Björkhagen date from the 1930s and are all about lamps. Besides Taklampan, the ceiling lamp, there's Kristallkronan (the chandelier), Bordslampan (the table lamp) and Lampetten (the wall sconce).
Kvastekulla griftegård, en bit härifrån,: Kvastekulla cemetery, not far from here, was designed by the Finnish architects Bengt Lundsten and Per-Mauritz Ålander, who won a Nordic architecture competition. Their idea was to keep the beautiful landscape intact and disturb nature as little as possible. Planning began in 1952, the cemetery opened in 1959, and the chapel followed four years later.
Kvastekulla kapell röstades 2023 fram ti: In 2023 Kvastekulla Chapel was voted Sweden's most beautiful building in the brutalist style. A tower-like lantern rises above the chancel.
Kvibergs kaserner var militärförläggning: The Kviberg barracks were an army base from 1895 to 1994. Today they're listed buildings with a restaurant, museum and market. They're also home to the Sports Museum, Idrottsmuseet, founded in 1983, which has had two Olympic medals among its exhibits. Just to the north is Prioritet Serneke Arena, the largest multi-sports venue in the Nordic countries, with an indoor ski track 1.2 kilometres long.
Kvibergs marknad håller till i det gamla: Kvibergs marknad, the Kviberg market, is held in the old horse stables of the artillery regiment. Every weekend 10,000–15,000 visitors browse 160 stalls for antiques, curios and odds and ends. A little further away is Prioritet Serneke Arena, the biggest multi-sport venue in the Nordic countries, with a full-size football pitch and a 1.2-kilometre indoor ski track.
Kvibergs museum visade bland annat artil: Kviberg Museum displayed artillery, horse-drawn equipment and uniforms, among other things. It closed on 9 April 2013 because of the high rent, and at a ceremony the museum’s colours were handed over to the Air Defence Regiment.
Kvibergsnäs landeri: Kvibergsnäs landeri, a historic country estate
Kville saluhall ritades av Gustav Appell: Kville market hall was designed by Gustav Appell Arkitektkontor. In 2014 it won the Yimby Prize and the award for Gothenburg's best building of the year, and it was nominated for the EU Prize for Contemporary Architecture.

Kville market hall was designed by Gustav Appell Arkitektkontor. In 2014 it won both the Yimby Prize and the award for Gothenburg's best building of the year. It was also nominated for the EU Prize for Contemporary Architecture.
Kvilletorget fick sitt namn redan 1922 o: Kvilletorget was named as long ago as 1922 and lies close to the Kvillebäcken canal. The Salvation Army has premises on the square, and Brämaregården Church and the Gothenburg Mosque are both just round the corner.
Kynäs var på 1740-talet ett dagsverkstor: In the 1740s Kynäs was a croft under Stuvsta, its tenants paying their rent in days of labour. In the 1920s farming stopped and the land was divided into villa plots. The croft stood south of Ågestavägen, at what is now Lövtäcktsvägen 26.
Kynäsberget delas av bostadsområdet Högm: The Högmora housing estate splits Kynäsberget into a north-western and a south-eastern part. The highest point, 71 metres above sea level, is in the south-east, and towards Ågestavägen the hill drops away in a steep rock face.
Kynäsberget har fått namn efter dagsverk: Kynäsberget is named after Kynäs, a croft whose tenants paid their rent in labour, and whose name has been spelt Kinäs, Könitz and Kynitz. One possible explanation is that 'kya' means a pen for animals, making Kynäs 'the headland with a pen'.
Kynäsberget har fått namn efter torpet K: Kynäsberget takes its name from the Kynäs croft, also spelt Kinäs, Könitz and Kynitz. The first part, 'kya', may mean a pen for animals, making the name 'the headland with a pen'.
Kynäsberget har fått sitt namn efter dag: Kynäsberget is named after Kynäs, a croft whose tenants paid their rent in labour to the Stuvsta estate in the 1740s. The name was also spelt Kinäs, Könitz and Kynitz. One theory is that kya means a pen or fold – so the name would mean the isthmus with a fold.
Kynäsberget, ett par hundra meter bort,: A couple of hundred metres away is Kynäsberget, a large expanse of forest and rock of national interest for outdoor recreation. Further south, in Lake Trehörningen, lies Storholmen, which was originally an island. In the 1920s it was divided into plots for summer cottages, mostly sold to working people from Stockholm, and the island was linked to the mainland by a footbridge. Today most of it is forest and shoreline that everyone is free to enjoy.
Kynäsbergets skog har knappt påverkats a: The forest on Kynäsberget has barely been touched by modern forestry, which is why it has been classified as a key habitat for its rich variety of species. There are several well-trodden but unmarked paths.
Kynäsbergets skog är ganska opåverkad av: The forest on Kynäsberget has been left largely alone by modern forestry and is classed as a key habitat for its wealth of species. Its highest point, 71 metres above sea level, is in the south-east.
Kynäsbergets skog är relativt opåverkad: The forest on Kynäsberget has been left relatively untouched by modern forestry and has been classified as a key habitat for its rich variety of species. Its highest point, in the south-east, is 71 metres above sea level.
Kyrka av stenen på platsen: A church built of local stone
Kyrka i en gammal biograf: A church in an old cinema
Kyrka insprängd i berget: A church blasted into the rock
Kyrka med fristående klocktorn: A church with a free-standing bell tower
Kyrka och bibliotek i samma hus: Church and library under one roof
Kyrka och moské i samma hus: A church and a mosque under one roof
Kyrka och äldreboende i ett: Church and care home in one
Kyrka ritad av en slottsarkitekt: A church by a palace architect
Kyrka, höghus och torg i ett: Church, tower block and square in one
Kyrkallén fick sin form på 1750-talet, n: Kyrkallén, the Church Avenue, took shape in the 1750s, when the Chinese Pavilion was built: a dead-straight avenue of lime trees some 1,800 metres long. Both Carl Fredrik Adelcrantz and Fredrik Magnus Piper later drew up grand parks around the avenue, but neither plan was carried out.
Kyrkan användes i många år innan den inv: The church was in use for many years before it was consecrated on 5 October 2014, at a ceremony attended by Patriarch Irinej and the Serbian crown prince and princess, among others. Inside are paintings by the well-known Serbian church painter Marko Ilic.
Kyrkan bakom bostadshuset: The church behind the apartment block
Kyrkan bakom ett höghus: A church behind a block of flats
Kyrkan bestod av ett långhus med ett rak: The church consisted of a nave with a square-ended chancel. Excavations uncovered finely worked, squared ashlar granite in the lowest courses of the walls – a find considered unique in Västergötland.
Kyrkan brann under gudstjänsten: The church that burned during a service
Kyrkan byggd av spillvirke: A church built from scrap wood
Kyrkan byggdes 1972 för Svenska kyrkan o: The church was built in 1972 for the Church of Sweden and was called Vårfrukyrkan, Our Lady's Church. Fittingly, it was consecrated on Lady Day, 19 March. The Church of Sweden stopped using it in 2007, and in 2009 it was reconsecrated as a Serbian Orthodox church.
Kyrkan byggdes 1974 av Svenska Missionsf: The church was built in 1974 by the Mission Covenant Church of Sweden and was originally called Tomaskyrkan, St Thomas’s Church. In 2011 the Church of Sweden and the Uniting Church in Sweden formed a joint church here, and it was renamed Mariakyrkan, St Mary’s Church.

The church was built in 1974 by the Mission Covenant Church of Sweden and was originally called Tomaskyrkan, St Thomas's Church. In 2011 the Church of Sweden and the Uniting Church in Sweden formed a shared congregation here, and it was renamed Mariakyrkan, St Mary's Church.

The church was built in 1974 by the Mission Covenant Church of Sweden and was then called Tomaskyrkan, St Thomas's Church. In 2011 the Church of Sweden joined it as a shared congregation, and the name became Mariakyrkan i Hammarkullen, St Mary's Church.
Kyrkan byggdes av rött Börringetegel frå: The church was built of red Börringe brick from Skåne and consecrated in 1890. Svaleberget was chosen because the ground by the old church was so poor that it would have needed extensive piling.
Kyrkan byggdes om och till och återinvig: The church was rebuilt and extended, and reconsecrated in November 2004. Since 2010 it has belonged to Lundby parish.
Kyrkan byggdes omkring år 1200 intill Ky: The church was built around 1200 next to Kyrksjön, a lake that no longer exists. The first known priest was called Thor and is mentioned in 1300. The tower collapsed in 1645, and today's tower was added in 1877–1878.
Kyrkan byggdes på 1100-talet, men område: The church was built in the 12th century, but the area around it had been the religious and geographical heart of the district since the Bronze Age.
Kyrkan byggdes på Dahlins berg, uppkalla: The church was built on Dahlins berg, a hill named after the merchant Samuel Dahlin, who had a shipping company and timber yards nearby. It was consecrated on Easter Sunday, 2 April 1893, and cost around 515,000 kronor.
Kyrkan byggdes på privat initiativ med i: The church was a private initiative, built with donated funds in 1920–1921, and the first service was held on 19 June 1921. At first the chapel was run by volunteers, until it was handed over to Säve parish in 1928.
Kyrkan byggdes troligen på 1100-talet. V: The church was probably built in the 12th century. During restoration work in the 1930s, runestones from the first half of the 11th century were found built into the foundations. Today the five stones stand in front of the spots where they were found.
Kyrkan byggdes under förra hälften eller: The church was built in the first half or middle of the 12th century, with a nave and a square-ended chancel. Excavations revealed finely worked, squared ashlar blocks of greystone in the lower walls – something considered completely unique in Västergötland.
Kyrkan byggdes under första halvan av 11: The church was built in the first half of the 1100s, and the memorial stone calls the ruin Gothenburg's oldest Christian monument. It was excavated and restored in 1925.
Kyrkan började användas första advent 19: The church was first used on Advent Sunday 1976, at a ceremony with Bishop Ingmar Ström, but wasn't consecrated until 1978. The organ was built in 1977 by Frederiksborgs Orgelbyggeri in Hillerød, Denmark.
Kyrkan där prästgården stod: A church where the vicarage stood
Kyrkan hamnade på stadens lägsta punkt,: The cathedral ended up on the lowest point in the city, which had to be raised with at least two metres of fill. Bedrock lies about 30 metres down. A proposal to build between the Otterhällorna rocks was dropped, partly because the site was thought too out of the way.
Kyrkan har ingen vanlig altartavla. Den: There's no ordinary altarpiece in this church. In its place, high up in the apse, is Lotta Söder's tile mosaic Livets träd – the Tree of Life. The font and the floor are limestone.
Kyrkan har också en nordtysk barockorgel: The church also has a North German Baroque organ with 54 stops, built in a research project run by the University of Gothenburg and Chalmers. It was modelled on Arp Schnitger's organ in Lübeck Cathedral, as the one in Hamburg turned out to have too large a façade.
Kyrkan har två dopfuntar. Den ursprungli: The church has two fonts. The original is made of dark reddish-brown porphyry; a second, in light brown clay with reliefs of biblical scenes by the artist Märta Taube-Ivarson, was added in 1966. The organ, from 2006, is modelled on 19th-century English and French instruments.
Kyrkan i logens ställe: A church in place of a barn
Kyrkan i romansk stil byggdes i början a: The Romanesque church was built in the early 12th century. Under the eaves on the north side of the tower you can see traces of arrow slits, a sign that it also served as a stronghold. The font is as old as the church itself.
Kyrkan i slutet av Värmlandsgatan bär ku: The church at the end of Värmlandsgatan carries King Oscar II's full name, and the king himself came to visit in 1898 and signed the guestbook. Round the corner runs Nordhemsgatan, with the Briggen food hall. The area is also home to SS Manhem, Gothenburg's biggest chess club, with more than 400 members – one of the top clubs in Sweden.
Kyrkan i spårvagnens vändslinga: A church in the tram loop
Kyrkan inbyggd i ett hyreshus: A church built into a block of flats
Kyrkan invigdes den 19 december 1970. På: The church was consecrated on 19 December 1970. On the chancel wall hangs the altarpiece Varde ljus (Let There Be Light) from 1986: 35 gleaming silver aluminium reliefs covering a full 40 square metres, by the sculptor Bertil Berggren Askenström. The pulpit is built of brick.
Kyrkan kallades länge Sankt Halvards kyr: For a long time this was known as Sankt Halvards kyrka, as it was dedicated to St Hallvard, patron saint of seafarers and of Oslo Cathedral. He was a merchant in Drammen and, alongside St Olaf, counted as Norway's most active saint.

For a long time the church was known as St Halvard's. Halvard, patron saint of seafarers, was a merchant from Drammen who drowned trying to save a woman. He was also the patron saint of Oslo Cathedral, under which Ytterby fell at the time.
Kyrkan ligger där torpet Vidängen fanns,: The church stands where the Vidängen croft used to be – a market garden in the early 1900s and an allotment garden by 1936. The buildings were torn down in 1943 when the tram depot was built.
Kyrkan ligger i ett skogsparti vid gamla: The church stands in a patch of woodland by the old Nynäsvägen road. The church interior is small, seating about a hundred people, and the whole western long wall facing the forest is made of glass. The bells hang in a wooden bell tower.
Kyrkan ligger på fjärde våningen: A church on the fourth floor
Kyrkan med de två tornen här bredvid är: The church with the twin towers right beside us is Högalidskyrkan, consecrated in 1923. Keep watching now, because we'll soon be heading up onto Västerbron, the bridge with one of the best views in Stockholm.
Kyrkan med prinsen bland gästerna: A church with a prince among the guests
Kyrkan nämns första gången 1388, när bis: The church is first mentioned in 1388, when Bishop Eystein came on a visitation. The fifteen oak roof trusses over the nave are the only known medieval ones to survive in Bohuslän, and may be as old as the church itself.
Kyrkan placerades högt uppe på ett berg: The church was placed high on a rocky hill in Aspudden, with views over Trekanten lake, Gröndal and the inner city. That view was cut short when the Essingeleden motorway was built in the 1960s.
The church was set high on a hill beside the old winter road, with views over Trekanten, Gröndal and the inner city. The view was cut short when the Essingeleden motorway was built in the 1960s.
Kyrkan på fjärde våningen: The church on the fourth floor
Kyrkan på gamla vändslingan: The church on the old turning loop

Kyrkan på prästgårdens tomt: A church on the vicarage plot
Kyrkan ritades av Hans Wieland i mörkröt: Designed by Hans Wieland in dark red brick, the church is 15 metres long, 15 metres wide and 15 metres high. A band of windows runs all the way round just beneath the flat roof.
Kyrkan ritades av Helena Tallius Myhrman: Designed by Helena Tallius Myhrman, the church has a square plan with curving lines and sharp, drawn-out corners. On its turf roof sits an almond-shaped lantern that lets in light from the south. Bishop Eva Brunne consecrated the church on 5 December 2010.

The church was designed by Helena Tallius Myhrman and consecrated on 5 December 2010 by Bishop Eva Brunne. It has sharp, drawn-out corners and an almond-shaped dormer that lets in light from the south. The roof is covered in turf.
Kyrkan ritades av Oskar Fuchs och byggde: The church was designed by Oskar Fuchs and built in dark red brick between 1968 and 1970. Bishop Helge Ljungberg consecrated it on Saturday 19 December 1970.
Kyrkan ritades av Sidney White och invig: The church was designed by Sidney White and consecrated in 1973, in the same style as the rest of the 1970s centre. The square worship space had no separate chancel, and in front of the entrance stood a bell tower shaped like a cube on slender legs.

The church was designed by Sidney White and consecrated on the first Sunday of Advent 1973. In front of the entrance stands a free-standing bell tower clad in brown and white panelling – a cube perched on slender legs.

Designed by Sidney White, the church was consecrated on the first Sunday of Advent 1973. The worship space was square with no separate chancel, and in front of the entrance stood a cube-shaped bell tower on slender legs.
Kyrkan ritades av Torsten Hansson och in: Designed by Torsten Hansson, the church was consecrated on 15 September 1972. The former church hall has a tall, steep roof reminiscent of a tent, and light enters only through skylights and the windows at each end. The concrete bell tower still stands.
Kyrkan ritades av Ville Berglund och inv: Designed by Ville Berglund, the church was consecrated in 1967 by Bishop Bo Giertz. Almost half the cost was met by donations. Inside, the roof rests on glulam arches, and the chancel has glass mosaic windows by Joël Mila.
Kyrkan ritades av arkitekten Folke Hjort: The church was designed by the architect Folke Hjortzberg and consecrated in 1939 by Archbishop Erling Eidem. The painting on the chancel wall, showing Jesus preaching to people dressed in the clothes of different eras, was by his father, Olle Hjortzberg. The tower is an open brick arch with two bells visible one above the other.
Kyrkan ritades av arkitekten Frans Linds: The church was designed by the architect Frans Lindskog. The artist José Samson made the shimmering gold glass cross that adorned the altar from the 1960s, as well as the 1957 stained-glass window The Heavenly Jerusalem.
Kyrkan ritades av arkitekten Theodor Wåh: The church was designed by architect Theodor Wåhlin in the National Romantic style. Hamburgsund Chapel and Nösund Chapel were built to almost identical plans. Its tall, pointed tower is clad in copper and topped with a gilded cross.
Kyrkan ritades av arkitekterna Pierre de: The church was designed by the architects Pierre der Hagopian and Josef Bandi, and consecrated on 2 February 1990 by Bishop Hubertus Brandenburg.
Kyrkan ritades av lidingöbon John Åkerlu: The church was designed by Lidingö resident John Åkerlund and is an early example of modern functionalism. The architect and consultants did their work without pay. South of the church is a terrace with rose bushes, intended for open-air services.
Kyrkan ritades i brutalistisk stil av Jo: Johannes Olivegren designed the church in Brutalist style, using construction methods and materials that were highly advanced for their day. A white-painted triangular concrete roof reaches towards a free-form concrete tower, topped by a weathercock.
Kyrkan som brann under gudstjänst: The church that burnt during a service
Kyrkan som brann under mässan: The church that burned during Mass

Kyrkan som kunde flyttas: The church that could be moved
Kyrkan som revs: The church that was torn down
