The church stands on an old vicarage plot. The first vicarage was built early in the 19th century and paid for by the Riksbank, Sweden’s central bank, which owned the paper mill. People wanted a chapel in Tumba as early as the 1920s, but the Second World War, among other things, pushed the plans back.
Kyrkan står på en grovhuggen sockel av g: The church stands on a rough-hewn plinth of granite from Sundbyberg's stonemasons' yard. The original tiled roof was of poor quality and was replaced with copper in 1936. The name Sundbyberg refers to the Bällstaån river, whose water once stood higher.
Kyrkan tog vändslingans plats: The church took the turning loop's place
Kyrkan var klar för invigning redan höst: The church was ready to be consecrated as early as autumn 1910, but a dispute with Bromma over the burial ground pushed the ceremony back to 4 June 1911. Sundbyberg had become a parish in its own right in 1909.
Kyrkan vid danska gränsen: The church by the Danish border
Kyrkan vid den försvunna sjön: The church by the vanished lake
Kyrkan visade sig vara svårt mögelskadad: The church turned out to be badly damaged by mould and has been abandoned. The plan is to demolish it and build a care home with a church in the same building, ready in 2029. In the meantime, services and activities carry on in temporary buildings next door.
Kyrkan är byggd av trä, men väggarna är: The church is built of wood, but its walls are clad in pale grey slate and its roof in black. It was designed in 1925 and consecrated in 1929. The altar is carved from Kinnekulle marble.
Kyrkan är byggd i brunt tegel mitt i Fle: Designed by Gunnar Cedervall, the church is built of brown brick in the heart of Flemingsberg centre. The base of its silver communion chalice has the same shape as the free-standing bell tower outside the main entrance.
Kyrkan är byggd i trä på betonggrund run: The church is built of wood on a concrete base around an atrium courtyard, with a pale facade and a large dark cross. The brick walls of the nave are partly whitewashed and partly tinted grey.

The church is built of wood on concrete foundations around an atrium courtyard, with a pale façade and a large dark cross. Inside, the walls of the nave are partly brick, some whitewashed and some tinted grey.
The church is built of wood on a concrete base around an atrium courtyard. A large dark cross adorns the pale façade, and the walls of the nave are partly limewashed, grey-toned brick.
Kyrkan är svårt mögelskadad och har lämn: The church has been badly damaged by mould and is no longer in use. The plan is to demolish it and build a care home with its own church on the same site, due for completion in 2029. In the meantime, activities carry on in temporary buildings next door.
Kyrkan är uppförd i gjuten naturbetong o: Designed by the architect Johan Tuvert, the church is built of cast, unfinished concrete. Daylight enters through four low bands of windows in the roof. Inside, the church keeps a fragment of the relics of Saint Nektarios of Aegina.
Kyrkans 17 meter höga torn är ett av fyr: The church's 17-metre tower is one of four medieval stone towers in the diocese, topped with an 18th-century half-timbered upper section. On the north side, a spiral staircase of cut stone known as the monks' passage leads up to the top of the stone tower.
Kyrkans Willisorgel byggdes för St. Step: The church's Willis organ was built for St Stephen's Church in Hampstead, London, and was probably completed in 1871. When that church closed, the organ ended up in Holland before finding its way here. It's the largest British Victorian organ in Sweden and the only three-manual Willis organ outside England.
Kyrkans altaruppsats är från 1627 och ko: The church's altarpiece dates from 1627 and comes from the pulpit of the chapel at Gothenburg's old hospital. A gravestone from the hospital cemetery has been set into the chancel floor.
Kyrkans barockinspirerade inredning med: The church's Baroque-inspired, white-walled interior has been well preserved since it was built. The artistic decoration, including a monumental altarpiece, is by Kristian Lundstedt.
Kyrkans dopfunt från 1200-talet gjordes: The church's 13th-century font was carved by the font master Thorkillus. Today it's kept at the Gothenburg City Museum, and the church has a newly made stone font in its place.

The church's 13th-century font was carved by the master font-maker Thorkillus. Today it is kept at the Gothenburg City Museum, and a newly made stone font stands in the church instead. The 1726 altarpiece was damaged in the fire and restored in 1881.
The church's 13th-century font was made by the font master Thorkillus. The original is kept at the Gothenburg City Museum, and a newly carved stone copy has taken its place.
Kyrkans dopfunt i täljsten gjordes på 12: The church's soapstone font was made in the 13th century by the font-maker known as Master Thorkillus and comes from the earlier wooden church. The wooden altar cross is thought to have been brought home from Italy by a sea captain in the 18th century.
Kyrkans dopfunt i täljsten är från 1100-: The church's soapstone font dates from the 12th century and has a cross in relief on each side. It belongs to a group of fonts made by the master craftsmen Sven and Torbjörn, and it is completely undamaged.
Kyrkans dopfunt i täljsten är från 1200-: The church's soapstone font dates from the 13th century and is attributed to the font maker Thorkillus. Decorated with spirals and leaf patterns, it's practically undamaged. The brass basin that goes with it was given to the church in 1647.

The church's soapstone font dates from the mid-13th century. When the church got a brass font in 1839, the stone one served as a flowerpot at the parish clerk's house until 1923. That same year another soapstone baptismal bowl turned up on a farm, where it had been used to feed the hens.
Kyrkans dopfunt i täljsten är troligen f: The church's soapstone font probably dates from the 13th century. When the church got a brass font in 1839, the old stone one was put to use as a flowerpot. Another baptismal bowl had ended up as a feeding dish for the hens.
Kyrkans första orgel kom från Härlanda k: The church's first organ came from Härlanda kyrka in 1960. When a new one was built in 1987, the old organ moved on to Brännö kyrka out in the archipelago.
Kyrkans första orgel med 31 stämmor förs: The church's first organ, with 31 stops, was destroyed when the church interior burned in 1988. In 1993 a new mechanical organ with 32 stops, from the same organ builder in Torshälla, was inaugurated. The church's organs have been recorded on both LP and CD.
Kyrkans klocka har tidigare hängt ombord: The church bell once hung aboard the Svinbådan lightship, and it is on loan here from the Swedish Maritime Administration. The original bell tower stayed behind in Brunnsbo.
Kyrkans långhus bärs av femton takstolar: The nave is held up by fifteen oak roof trusses – the only medieval ones known to survive in Bohuslän. They may be as old as the church itself, which was probably built sometime between the late 1100s and the mid-1200s.
Kyrkans nuvarande orgel invigdes 2021 oc: The church's current organ was inaugurated in 2021 and built by Paschen Kiel Orgelbau in Germany. The Ansgar Chapel has another, a mechanical organ from 1957 built by Werner Bosch in Kassel.
Kyrkans orgel byggdes 2007 av Jānis Kaln: The church organ was built in 2007 by Jānis Kalniņš in Ugale, Latvia. It has twelve stops spread over two manuals and pedals.
Kyrkans orgel med 32 stämmor invigdes 19: The church's 32-stop organ was inaugurated in 1993 and built by Walter Thür Orgelbyggen in Torshälla. The organs have been recorded, among other things on the 1980 LP Preludium with Erik Lundkvist.
Kyrkans platsgjutna betongväggar har oli: The church's walls of concrete cast on site vary in texture and colour. That's because the mould boards soaked up different amounts of water while the concrete was setting. The roof is a steep monopitch, and the church narrows towards the chancel.
Kyrkans stora mosaikfönster av Berndt He: The church's great mosaic window by Berndt Helleberg tells the life of Jesus from top to bottom: the Star of Bethlehem at the top, the empty tomb at the very bottom. The font, made of solid glass, stands in front of the window and catches its coloured light.
Kyrkans trätak målades 1710 av Erik Erik: The church's wooden ceiling was painted in 1710 by Erik Eriksson Grijs – his last known church painting. It shows the name of God in Hebrew letters, the Transfiguration of Jesus and the Last Judgement, and the paintings seem never to have been painted over.

The church's wooden ceiling was painted in 1710 by Erik Eriksson Grijs – his last known church painting. It shows the name of God, JHWH, in Hebrew letters, along with the Transfiguration of Jesus and the Last Judgement. The paintings appear never to have been painted over.
Kyrkans votivskepp från 1600-talet är un: The church's 17th-century votive ship is unique because it has a crew on board. The trumpeting angel in the chancel dates from the same century.
Kyrkans votivskepp är från 1600-talet oc: The church's votive ship dates from the 17th century and is unique because it has a crew on board. The trumpeting angel in the chancel and the pew doors date from the same period.
Kyrkans äldsta föremål är dopfunten från: The church's oldest object is the font from the medieval church, carved in soapstone some time after 1250. Its original base is missing, so the current one was made in 1934. A memorial stone in the churchyard marks where the medieval chancel stood.
Kyrkans äldsta föremål är dopfuntens cup: The oldest object in the church is the bowl of the font, carved from amphibolite in the 12th century. In the porch there's also an iron-bound poor box from the 18th century, and the bell in the octagonal bell tower dates from 1770.
Kyrkbygget började i mars 1939 och redan: Work on the church began in March 1939, and by Michaelmas on 1 October that same year it had already been consecrated. The silver crucifix on the altar was made the same year by the sculptor Carl Eldh.
Kyrkbygget började med en insamling till: The church began with a collection in memory of the polar explorer Finn Malmgren, a son of Äppelviken who died on the polar ice in 1928. The foundation stone, taken from the hill itself, was laid in 1931, and by December 1932 the church was consecrated in the presence of King Gustav V.
Kyrkbyns mangård Karlslund revs 1939 när: Karlslund, the main farmhouse of Kyrkbyn, was demolished in 1939 when the airfield was extended. During the work, a burial ground with 60–70 graves from the Roman Iron Age was found, along with a stone-paved road, perhaps a processional way.
Kyrkbytorget fick sitt namn 1948. Husen: Kyrkbytorget got its name in 1948. The buildings went up in 1955–1956 to designs by Tuvert Arkitektkontor, and in 2002 a courtyard street was added to link the properties around the square.
Kyrkbytorgets hus byggdes i mitten av 19: The buildings around Kyrkbytorget square went up in the mid-1950s, and the Roxy cinema here showed films from 1956 to 1965. The library opened the same autumn as the cinema, in November 1956, and much of its 1950s interior was kept when it was renovated for its 60th anniversary. Nearby runs the Lundby Tunnel, which at 2,060 metres is one of Sweden's longer road tunnels.
Kyrkeby och Nereby är ett gott exempel p: Kyrkeby and Nereby are a good example of how statisticians keep redrawing the map. Before 2015, there was a small settlement here officially called Nereby and Sjöhed. When the boundaries were redrawn, a larger built-up area was marked out instead and named Kyrkeby and Nereby. A little way off is the church village of Kyrkeby, with Harestad Church.
Kyrkklockan från en fyr: A church bell from a lighthouse
Kyrkklockan, som syns inifrån kyrkorumme: The church bell, visible from inside the church, was cast in 1674 from the metal of a 12th-century church bell that had cracked from ringing in 1588. It used to hang in Fässberg's old church.
Kyrkklockan, som väger 300 kilo, skänkte: The 300-kilo church bell was donated by a private individual in 1926. The church has two fonts; the newer one, from 1966, was made in clay by Märta Taube-Ivarson, with reliefs of biblical scenes.
Kyrkklockorna skänktes 1882 och göts vid: The church bells were donated in 1882 and cast at the Götaverken works. The great bell weighs 2,367 kilos, and the 49-metre tower is topped by a three-metre cross of gilded copper.
Kyrkogård formad av landskapsarkitekt: A cemetery shaped by a landscape architect
Kyrkogården anlades efter ett beslut i a: The cemetery was laid out following a decision by the general town council in 1859, to replace Gamla kyrkogården, the old cemetery. A mortuary was built in its north-west corner in the 1940s.
Kyrkogården bytte namn: The cemetery that changed its name
Kyrkogården gjordes i ordning på 1830-ta: The churchyard was laid out in the 1830s, but the first burial didn't take place until 1855, when Hanna Nordwall from Lunda was laid to rest. Her gravestone is still there.
Kyrkogården har medeltida ursprung. Här: The churchyard dates back to the Middle Ages. The medieval old church of Västra Frölunda stood here until it was demolished in the 1860s.
Kyrkogården kom till när Karl XIV Johan: The cemetery came about when King Karl XIV Johan made Ulriksdal Palace available in 1822 as a home for veterans of the wars of 1788–1814. Around 200 of them were buried here. The memorial from 1824 reads: "H H (Here rest) invalids from the wars of the years 1788–1814."
Kyrkogården omges av en gråstensmur med: The churchyard is enclosed by a fieldstone wall with three lychgates dating from 1738. Set into the wall are iron rings where churchgoers tethered their horses. The soapstone font, carved with a crowned and bearded head, is the work of Master Thorkillus.
Kyrkogården som bytte namn: The cemetery that changed its name
Kyrkogården utvidgades söderut under 192: The churchyard was extended southwards in the 1920s and 1940s, and most recently in 1987. Today it holds 1,247 graves across 1.5 hectares.
Kyrkogården är 25 hektar stor och växlar: The cemetery covers 25 hectares, alternating between open parkland and enclosed woodland. Next to the memorial grove there's a viewpoint looking out over Lake Drevviken.
Kyrkogårdsmuren är från 1646. På utsidan: The churchyard wall dates from 1646. On the outside are rings marked with farm names, where churchgoers tied up their horses during the service.
Kyrkoherde Gustaf Franck vädjade 1912 om: In 1912 the vicar, Gustaf Franck, appealed for donations towards a chapel, since there was no public money for one. Collection cards were printed with squares, each worth 25 öre, and the property company Fastighets AB Carnegie donated the plot.
Kyrkoruinen kallas Göteborgs äldsta kris: The church ruin is called Gothenburg's oldest Christian monument and dates from the 12th century. In 1528 King Gustav Vasa ordered the church demolished, because it stood so close to the town that enemies could make use of it in wartime. Its stones went into building the church in Nya Lödöse instead.
Kyrkorummet har ett platt trätak med tre: The nave has a flat wooden ceiling with three cross beams. Filip Månsson's decorative paintings in grey, blue and red create the illusion of beams running lengthwise too. The same artist decorated the small apse of the chancel.
Kyrkorummet är ljust med grå toner och h: The church interior is light, in grey tones, with high-set windows. On the chancel wall hangs a cross with a Christ monogram in fused art glass. The space seats 200.
Kyrkorummets enda utsmyckning är glasmos: The only decoration in the church is its glass mosaic, covering a full 950 square metres of wall. It was made by the artist Mogens Jørgensen and his wife Gudrun Steenberg, who also designed the tall pine cross.
Kyrkorådet bjöd in två arkitekter. Gusta: The church council invited two architects. Gustaf Hermansson's neo-Gothic proposal was more expensive and aroused little interest. Instead they chose the young Axel Sjögren, who had worked on Hjorthagen church. Sundbyberg church is the only church he ever designed.
Kyrksal i femtio år: A church hall for fifty years
Kyrksalen byggdes i platsgjuten betong e: The church hall was built of in-situ cast concrete to designs by Lars Bjursten and Kerstin Holmer, while the red-brick centre from 1963 was designed by Sven Hesselgren. The ceiling and altar painting is by Laris Strunke.
Kyrksalens fondvägg pryddes av en metall: The end wall of the church hall was adorned with a metal sculpture showing scenes from the life of Jesus. It bore the letters INRI, short for Jesus of Nazareth, King of the Jews – the inscription placed on Jesus's cross.
Kyrkskatter på stadsmuseet: Church treasures at the city museum
Kyrkstolar av PET-flaskor: Church chairs made from plastic bottles
Kyrktuppen i förgylld aluminium formgavs: The gilded aluminium weathercock was designed by the sculptor Arne Jones. It was voted Sweden's Church Weathercock of the Year in 1997 and has become Högdalen's emblem.
Kyrktuppen på Vantörs kyrka i förgylld a: The gilded aluminium weathercock on Vantör Church was designed by Arne Jones. In 1997 it was named Sweden's Church Weathercock of the Year, and it also became Högdalen's emblem.
Kyrkvaktmästaren blev lärare: The church caretaker became the teacher
Kyrkvägen 16 byggdes 1922 av fjärdingsma: Kyrkvägen 16 was built in 1922 by the parish constable John Lif. He became well known as the local policeman, as a writer for Järfälla-Bygden and for his many photographs of the parish.
Kyrkvägen och Årstafrun: The Church Road and the Lady of Årsta
Källan som trycker upp vattnet: The spring that pushes up its own water
Källan vid stranden tog in saltvatten, s: The spring on the shore let in salt water, so a new well was drilled about 80 metres further up. The well house's doorway came from the 18th-century tavern Källaren Druvan in Gamla stan.
Källarmästaren med flera krogar: The cellar master with several taverns
Källö i södra skärgården ska inte förväx: Källö in the southern archipelago shouldn't be confused with Källö-Knippla in Gothenburg's northern archipelago. The island's little lanes only got official names in 2013: Källö Bryggväg, Källö Byväg and Källöstigen.
Källö, officiellt Stora Källö, har fått: Källö, officially Stora Källö, is named after a pothole on the island – a ‘giant's kettle’ worn into the rock. Islanders once made their living from fishing and farming, and the oldest houses date from the 1700s. In 1932 Gothenburg's motorboat club bought land here and built a jetty, a dance floor and a kiosk. Today there are around 30 summer cottages on the island.
Kälvesta gravhögar är Stockholms kommuns: The Kälvesta burial mounds form the largest burial ground in Stockholm municipality, with around 145 ancient remains: mounds, about a hundred round stone settings, three-pointed settings and three ship-shaped stone settings.

The Kälvesta burial mounds form the largest burial ground in the City of Stockholm, with around 145 ancient remains. There are mounds, round and rectangular stone settings, three-pointed 'treudd' stones and three stone ships.

The Kälvesta burial mounds make up the largest prehistoric cemetery in the City of Stockholm, with around 145 ancient remains: 11 mounds, about a hundred round stone settings, two three-pointed settings and three ship-shaped stone settings.
Kälvesta har fått namn efter en gammal b: Kälvesta is named after an old village dating back to the Middle Ages. The ending '-sta' means place, and the first part of the name was originally a man's name.
Kälvesta kallas ett \"horisontellt\" mil: Kälvesta is known as a ‘horizontal’ Million Programme area – part of Sweden's big 1960s–70s housing drive. From 1966 to the mid-1970s around 2,000 terraced houses, link houses, atrium houses and villas were built, most of them four-room terraced homes with a kitchen.
Kälvesta kallas ett horisontellt miljonp: Kälvesta is known as a 'horizontal' Million Programme area – part of Sweden's big 1960s–70s housing drive, but built low. Some 2,000 single-family homes went up between 1966 and the mid-1970s, planned with Höjer & Ljungqvist. Most residents live in four-room terraced houses with a kitchen.
Kälvesta kallas ibland ett ”horisontellt: Kälvesta is sometimes described as a 'horizontal' Million Programme area – part of Sweden's huge 1960s–70s housing drive – with around 2,000 small houses. Building started in 1966 and continued until the mid-1970s. Most people live in terraced houses with four rooms and a kitchen.
Kälvesta kan kallas ett ”horisontellt” m: Kälvesta could be called a “horizontal” Million Programme estate – part of Sweden's big 1965–1975 housing drive – with around 2,000 single-family homes. The architects Höjer & Ljungqvist helped plan its terraced and linked houses, and building went on from 1966 to the mid-1970s.
Kälvesta kvarn kallas också Lilla Stampa: Kälvesta mill is also known as Lilla Stampan and Lunda mill. In 1884 it was moved from Observatoriegatan to Lunda, and in 1892 on to its present spot on Skestavägen in Solhem.
Kälvesta kvarn är en stolpkvarn från 160: Kälvesta kvarn is a 17th-century post mill, where the entire mill house turns to face the wind. It originally stood on Observatoriegatan in central Stockholm and was moved to Solhem in 1892. The City Museum has given it a blue rating, its highest level of cultural and historical value.
Kälvesta kvarn är en stolpkvarn. Det bet: Kälvesta windmill is a post mill, which means the entire mill building is turned to face into the wind.
Kälvestas radhus och villor har en helt: Kälvesta, with its terraced houses and villas, has a very different neighbour to the north-east: Lunda, a district taken up mostly by a large business and industrial estate just south of Hjulsta and west of Spånga. Two very different worlds, then, at a comfortable distance from each other – a good example of how varied Västerort, Stockholm's western suburbs, can be.
Käppalaställningen började byggas 1939 o: Work on the Käppala battery began in 1939. Its 75-millimetre anti-aircraft guns were among the most powerful around Stockholm. Today a gun donated by Bofors is on display here, and all the emplacements survive intact.

Construction of the Käppala battery began in 1939. Its 75-millimetre anti-aircraft guns were among the most powerful around Stockholm, and its position on Lidingö made it a strategic last outpost to the east.
Käppalaverket ligger huvudsakligen i ett: Most of the Käppala wastewater treatment plant is housed in a rock cavern. A 60-kilometre network of tunnels carries sewage here all the way from Märsta, mostly by gravity.
Kärleksstigen vid Isbladskärret: Kärleksstigen, the Lovers' Path, by Isbladskärret
Kärleksstigen är bara cirka 390 meter lå: Kärleksstigen, the Love Path, is only about 390 metres long, and not everyone liked it. The columnist Cecilia Hagen called the idea "utterly daft" and wondered whether WWF perhaps saw royals as an endangered species.
Kärna bokskog ligger nära, ett naturrese: Kärna beech forest is close by: a nature reserve of about 18 hectares, created in 2008 and managed by the West Coast Foundation. The rare wood fescue grass grows among the beeches, along with several red-listed lichens. Parts of the reserve have been made accessible, so the forest isn't just for seasoned hikers.
Kärna bokskog ligger några kilometer nor: Kärna beech forest lies a few kilometres north-west of Kärna and covers about 18 hectares. The nature reserve is managed by the West Coast Foundation, Västkuststiftelsen.
Kärnan i Flygtekniska försöksanstaltens: Wind-tunnel testing was at the heart of the Aeronautical Research Institute's work and was used extensively when Swedish aircraft were being designed. The first tunnel was built in 1940. Supersonic tunnels followed in time, and in 1960 the first hypersonic tunnel came into use.
Kärra hörde till Säve socken, som tillhö: Kärra was part of Säve parish, which belonged to Norway until 1658. The area was ravaged by many wars, and Orrekulla redoubt was built here in the late 1600s. It was strengthened in 1719 but then left to decay.
Kärra ingick i Säve socken, som tillhörd: Kärra was part of Säve parish, which belonged to Norway until 1658. The area was ravaged by many wars, and in the late 17th century the Orrekulla redoubt was built. It was strengthened in 1719 but then left to fall into ruin.
Kärra kyrka alldeles intill hette faktis: Kärra church, right next to us, was actually known as Kärra chapel right up until 2001. North of the church is a parish hall from 1978. And Kärra was once a place of justice: from 1824 to 1887 the district court for the Askim area held its sessions here.
Kärra kyrka ritades av Theodor Wåhlin oc: Kärra Church was designed by Theodor Wåhlin and built in 1920–1921 with money raised by the community. Two more churches were built to almost identical plans: the chapels at Hamburgsund and Nösund. The tower is clad in copper and topped with a gilded cross.
Kärrdal hör till Östra Sjöberg, en kommu: Kärrdal is part of Östra Sjöberg, a district tucked between Edsviken bay, Lake Rösjön and the Rinkeby forest. Further on, on the eastern shore of Edsviken, is Bergendals herrgård, Bergendal Manor. The site is known from the 1650s, when the croft of Snickartorpet stood here, and the grand manor house was built in 1913 at the initiative of landowner Ragnar Liljenroth. Today it's a hotel and conference venue. Along the same road is Landsnora kvarn, a mill that is Sollentuna's oldest secular building.
Kärret som korsar halvön var en gång sun: The marsh cutting across the peninsula was once the strait between the island and the mainland, and today you cross it on a boardwalk some 400 metres long. The peninsula consists mostly of glacial outwash, with deep kettle holes.
Kärringstan är inget officiellt namn, me: Kärringstan – roughly 'Old Wives' Town' – isn't an official name, but this villa area has earned it. The streets are named after famous women, and the blocks have names like Baderskan, Barnjungfrun, Kallskänkan and Tvätterskan: the Bath Attendant, the Nursemaid, the Cold-Kitchen Maid and the Washerwoman. So the Barnmorskan block, the Midwife, fits right in – its terraced houses won Stockholm's Building of the Year award in 2011. Just around the corner is Modellvillan 21, which took the same title in 2017.
Kärrtorp låg längst söderut på Hammarby: Kärrtorp lay at the far southern edge of Hammarby manor's land, beside a fen that had mostly dried out – hence the name, which means 'fen croft'.
Kåhög nämns redan 1496 och antas betyda: Kåhög is mentioned as early as 1496 and is thought to mean "the bend by the height" – a reference to the bends of the Säveån river here and to the Kåhögsberget hill. Jonsered even had its own apple variety, the Kåhögsäpple.
Kåhög nämns redan 1496 och namnet antas: Kåhög is mentioned as early as 1496, and the name is thought to mean 'the bend by the hill' – a reference to the bends the Säveån river makes here and to Kåhögsberget hill. Jonsered even had its own apple variety once, the Kåhög apple.
Kåhög nämns redan 1496 och namnet tros b: Kåhög is mentioned as early as 1496, and the name is thought to mean 'the bend by the height' – a reference to the bends the Säveån river makes here and to the Kåhögsberget hill.
Kåhög växte under 1800-talet i takt med: Kåhög grew during the 19th century alongside the Jonsered mill under William Gibson. Jonsereds Fabriker sold land cheaply to its employees, provided they promised to work at the mill for ten years. That's why Kåhög's farm has the same kind of brick architecture as Jonsered.

Kåhög grew during the 19th century in step with the mill town of Jonsered. Jonsereds Fabriker sold land cheaply to employees who wanted to build a house, on condition that they promised to work ten years at the mill. That's why Kåhög has the same brick architecture as Jonsered.
Kåhög är ett litet villasamhälle vid Säv: Kåhög is a small village of houses on the Säveån river, with the Western Main Line railway to the south. At the bridge in Kåhög begins the Jonsereds strömmar nature reserve, the Jonsered Rapids, which follows the Säveån valley all the way to Lake Aspen. With a bit of luck you might spot kingfishers and dippers.
Kåkstaden utan vatten och vägar: The shanty town without water or roads
Kållered ligger precis vid gränsen till: Kållered lies right on the border with the province of Halland. It used to be farming country, but today western Kållered is dominated by hypermarkets. A short distance away is Kållered station – the first station here opened back in 1891 – and the area also has the Shopping Park Kållered retail park.
Kållered ligger vid gränsen mot Halland: Kållered sits on the border with the province of Halland and was once farming country. Today it has big out-of-town stores such as IKEA, a small hotel and a golf course beside the Torrekulla nature reserve. Not far from here is Kållered Church, the oldest building in Mölndal municipality.
Kållered var en gång lantbruksbygd, men: Kållered was once farming country, but today western Kållered is all about big-box retail. Shopping Park Kållered is right here, and nearby was EkenCenter, a shopping centre from 1990 with about 25 shops. The competition proved too tough, the building was demolished in 2013, and yet another retail building went up in its place.
Kållered var länge lantbruksbygd. År 197: Kållered was farming country for a long time. In 1972 IKEA became the first to set up here, drawing customers from all over western Götaland and Halland. More shops followed, and in 2023 IKEA opened a brand-new store.
Kållereds socken hörde till Askims härad: Kållered parish was part of the old Askim district and existed long before any motorways were built through here. Its parish church, Kållered Church, stands on a hill in the village and is in fact the oldest building in the whole of Mölndal municipality. This area was also once home to the EkenCenter shopping centre, which was demolished in 2013.
Kållereds station har haft två liv. Den: Kållered station has had two lives. The first station opened in 1891 but closed in 1972. When commuter trains between Gothenburg and Kungsbacka came back, a new station opened on 17 August 1992, and in the rush hour there are now trains every fifteen minutes in each direction.
Kårhuset ritades i funkisstil av Paul He: The student union building was designed in functionalist style by Paul Hedqvist, and Prince Eugen contributed decorations to the interiors. From 1976 to 1988 it housed the music venue Glädjehuset, and after the student union moved out, the building was converted for the Stockholm School of Economics.
Kåsjön har litet tillflöde och är en käl: Few streams feed Kåsjön; it's a spring-fed lake, where groundwater wells up from below. It is 32 metres deep and divided into Stora Kåsjön, Lilla Kåsjön and, furthest west, Kåtjärn.
Kåsjön är en förkortning av Kåres sjö, e: Kåsjön is short for Kåres sjö – Kåre's lake – after a man who settled at the eastern end of the lake in the early 1500s. He and his family lived off farming, fishing and hunting.
Kåsjön är en förkortning av Kåres sjö. E: Kåsjön is short for Kåres sjö, Kåre's lake. A man called Kåre settled on the eastern side of the lake in the early 1500s and lived off farming, fishing and hunting.
Kåsjön is short for Kåres sjö, "Kåre's lake". In the early 1500s a man named Kåre settled with his family at the eastern end of the lake, living off farming, fishing and hunting.
Kåsjön är en källsjö där grundvatten trä: Kåsjön is a spring-fed lake, where groundwater wells up from beneath. It has been limed since the 1980s to stop it becoming permanently acidified, and its fish and wildlife have recovered.
Kåsjön är en källsjö: den har litet till: Kåsjön is a spring-fed lake: few streams flow into it, and groundwater wells up from below instead. It lies in a rift valley and is made up of three parts – Stora Kåsjön, Lilla Kåsjön and, furthest west, Kåtjärn.
Kåsjön är en populär badsjö med ganska k: Lake Kåsjön is a popular place for a swim, with fairly clear water. Around its shores you'll find shallow sandy beaches, flat rocks, grassy spots and stony stretches.
Kölnan från 1763 är ett av bruksområdets: The kiln house from 1763 is one of the oldest buildings on the site, built eight years after the works opened in 1755. The fire station from 1926 served the works and now houses an exhibition on fire safety, complete with a fire engine from the 1940s.
Köpcentret Allum har ett namn från forns: The Allum shopping centre has an Old Swedish name: it's the dative form of ‘alla’, all, and means roughly ‘for everyone’. It opened in 2006 and spans the E20 motorway with shops and a walkway. Not far away, Partille herrgård – the manor house locals call Slottet, the Castle – sits on a hill overlooking the Säveån river valley. It has been listed since 1995.
Köpcentret Allum, alldeles intill, har e: The Allum shopping centre, right beside us, has a name with a story. Allum, or allom, is an Old Swedish dative form of 'all', meaning something like 'for everyone'. Work began in September 2004, and it opened in April 2006. A building with shops and a passageway spans the E20 motorway, linking the northern and southern halves.
Köpcentret Stinsen invigdes 1995 av Ingv: The Stinsen shopping centre was opened in 1995 by the TV presenter Ingvar Oldsberg, in a former car showroom where Mercedes-Benz cars used to be sold. One reminder of those days remains: the two big car lifts are still in use, now as goods lifts. The centre was extended in stages and reopened in 2009.
Köpcentret här hette Mörby Centrum ända: The shopping centre here was called Mörby Centrum until May 2026, when it was renamed Danderyds Centrum – though the metro station in the northern part of the building kept the old name. It opened on 29 January 1978. Not far off is Villa Markelius, which the architect Sven Markelius designed in 1945 for himself and his family. And down by Edsviken bay stands Berzelii ek, Berzelius' Oak, today what's known as an oak ruin.
Köpcentret invigdes den 13 november 1975: The shopping centre was opened by King Carl XVI Gustaf on 13 November 1975. An extension in 2007–2010 doubled its size, and in 2011 Sollentuna Centrum won an international award at a ceremony in Paris.
Köpmannen Erik Larsson planterade två li: The merchant Erik Larsson planted two lime trees at Malmvik in 1618. When he was ennobled in 1631, he took the name von der Linde – 'of the lime tree' – after the farm and its trees. One of the limes survived until 1999, when it blew down in a November storm.
Köpmannen Robert Ditzinger köpte Långsjö: The merchant Robert Ditzinger bought Långsjö farm in 1881, and the following year he had two identical, mirror-image manor-style houses built for his two sons. They still stand today, as does the farm's old root cellar.

The merchant Robert Ditzinger bought Långsjö farm in 1881, and the following year he built two identical, mirror-image manor-style houses for his two sons. The style was inspired by the decorative timber architecture of the day, typical of wealthy Stockholmers' summer villas. Both houses still stand.
Köpmannen Robert Ditzinger köpte gården: The merchant Robert Ditzinger bought the farm in 1881, and the following year he had two identical, mirror-image manor-style houses built for his two sons. They're in the wooden panelled style typical of summer villas outside the city, and both are still standing.
Köpstaden dominerades i början helt av I: At first the shopping area was completely dominated by IKEA, which opened here in 1972 and drew customers from across western Götaland and Halland. In 2023 IKEA opened a brand-new store.
Köpt för silver och två oxar: Bought for silver and two oxen
Körkarlen kom först, men sist: The Phantom Carriage came first – and last
Körsbärsträden kom på 90-talet: The cherry trees came in the 90s
L'Escargot betyder snigeln på franska. H: L'Escargot is French for 'the snail'. Hans Mörk opened the restaurant in 1980, with a menu shaped by the new French cuisine. The papers were quick to call it the place to be seen.
L.M. Ericsson testade ny teknik på gårde: L.M. Ericsson tried out new technology at the estate. Hågelby had its own power station and was self-sufficient in electricity into the 1930s. There was also an apiary for pollination and honey, and a water tower with a viewing platform on the hill.
LM-staden var första gången Olle Engkvis: LM-staden was the first place where the builder Olle Engkvist fully succeeded with his series-built housing. Using rigidly standardised methods, the houses were built – in his own words – on an assembly line, but in reverse. Today the area is listed as green, its top heritage rating, by the City Museum.
Laboratorium för lukt och buller: A laboratory for smell and noise
Ladan för kungens hjortar: The barn for the king's deer
Ladan som blev dansställe: The barn that became a dance hall
Ladugården som födde slottet: The farm that fed the castle
Lagändringen Lex Bollmora från 1959 gav: The 1959 change in the law known as Lex Bollmora gave municipal housing companies the right to build in other municipalities. Stockholm was short of buildable land, and the city's companies started building in Bollmora straight away.
Lamellhusen i kvarteren Gurkan och Morot: The slab blocks in the Gurkan and Moroten blocks were built in the early 1970s with uniform façades in beige brick. The street crosses the old open-cast mine on a short bridge. The Swedish National Heritage Board calls these buildings the best built in Solna during the boom years of the 1960s and 70s.
Lamm byggde upp en stor konstsamling med: Lamm built up a large art collection of Italian sculpture and works by famous painters. Some of it was sold, but you can still see works by Bruno Liljefors, Anders Zorn and Carl Milles today.
Landala kapell, ritat av Carl Fahlström,: Landala Chapel, designed by Carl Fahlström, was consecrated right here on 11 October 1885. In 1919 the little wooden church was physically moved closer to what became Chalmers. The tower burnt in 1960 but was rebuilt.
Landsfiskalens gård och arresten: The police chief's house and the lock-up
Landshövdingehus i kvarteren runt omkrin: Landshövdingehus – Gothenburg's stone-and-wood tenement houses – in the blocks around
Landshövdingehusen i kvarteret Renen, lä: The landshövdingehus – Gothenburg's stone-and-wood tenement houses – in the Renen block, along the north-west side of the square, were due to be demolished in the 1970s. After widespread protests they were sold instead and renovated in the 1980s.
Landskampen som inte spelades här: The international that wasn't played here
Landskapet är ett typiskt sprickdalsland: This is classic fissure-valley country, with rocky outcrops and low valleys. From Gåseborg, Gåsberget and Hummelmoraberget you get wide views over Lake Mälaren, and at Gåseborg and Dikartorp there's broadleaf woodland of lime and oak.
Landsnoravägen börjar vid Edsbacka Wärds: Landsnoravägen starts at Edsbacka Wärdshus, an inn founded in 1626. At Landsnora mill the road bends sharply and squeezes between the mill building and the miller's cottage – a passage so narrow that it's controlled by traffic lights.
Landstingshus blev Hotel Gio: From county offices to Hotel Gio
Landstingshuset, där Region Stockholms p: Landstingshuset, where Region Stockholm's politicians meet today, spent more than 150 years as a military hospital, Garnisonssjukhuset, from 1811 to 1969. Next to it stands Graverska huset, built in 1754 as a home for the tanner Jacob Graver. And for food lovers: at Bergsgatan 33, the chef Mathias Dahlgren ran the restaurant Bon Lloc – Catalan for “good place” – which held a Michelin star from 1997 to 2005.
Lars Bryde ritade 34 kubiska trevåningsh: Lars Bryde designed 34 cube-shaped three-storey buildings with flat roofs. The façades came in three colours: reddish brown in Klacklappen, orange in Pliggen and yellow in Skohornet. The white corrugated balconies make a sharp contrast, and the area was made car-free.
Lars Israel Wahlman undervisade i timmer: Lars Israel Wahlman taught timber construction at KTH, the Royal Institute of Technology, and tried out his ideas on his own house. He had his architecture office in the annexe, where among other things he designed the nearby Cedergren Tower.
Larsbodatorpet norr om Edsvallabacken nä: Larsbodatorpet, north of Edsvallabacken, is mentioned as a tavern as early as the 18th century and is the oldest surviving building in the district. Until the 1950s Larsboda was mostly forest with a few crofts.
Larsbodatorpet, strax norr om Edsvallaba: Larsbodatorpet, just north of Edsvallabacken, is mentioned as an inn as far back as the 1700s. It's the oldest surviving building in the district, though the present house probably dates from after the mid-1800s.
Lasse and Maja have moved to Skogås! Härbreparken, nearby, is a themed play park inspired by Valleby, the fictional little town where the children's detective agency Lasse-Majas detektivbyrå solves its mysteries. The park won Huddinge's architecture award in 2020. In the middle of Skogås centrum, on Yttertorget, stands Mariakyrkan, the parish church of Trångsund-Skogås.
Latrin blandades med torv till pudrett o: Latrine waste was mixed with peat to make 'poudrette' and sold as fertiliser to the market gardens round about. In the 1920s Hässelby's market gardens grew half of Stockholm's vegetables.
Laurinska villan har varit byggnadsminne: The Laurin villa has been a listed building since 1987, and its interior is well preserved, with heavy interior doors and sturdy ironmongery.
Laurinska villan är ett timmerhus i två: Laurinska villan is a two-storey timber house with dark brown tarred walls and blue-painted windows. Inside are roughly hewn logs, exposed ceiling beams, carved ornaments and ceiling paintings. The villa has been a listed building since 1987.
Lax och kosläpp: Salmon and cows let out to pasture
Laxfisket i Säveån har långa traditioner: Salmon fishing in the Säveån river has a long tradition, and the pool at Kåhögs löd was one of the most popular spots. Every spring thousands of people gather at Kåhögs gård to watch the kosläpp, when the cows are let out to pasture for the first time.
Leden räknades förr som motorväg. På 199: The road used to be classed as a motorway. In the 1990s the city took it over and had the motorway status removed, as it wanted to avoid urban motorways. Plenty of road maps still show it as a motorway, though, and a few green motorway signs remain.
Leden är uppkallad efter FN:s generalsek: The road is named after UN Secretary-General Dag Hammarskjöld, who died in a plane crash in Africa in 1961. Shortly after his death the city council decided on the name, at first as Dag Hammarskjölds Väg. The road got its current name in 1968.
Ledningen går förbi Botkyrka kyrka, unde: The pipeline runs past Botkyrka Church, under the strait at Fittja and on through Vårby gård, Segeltorp, Herrängen and Midsommarkransen to Nybohov by Lake Trekanten. With few exceptions it follows Gamla Södertäljevägen, the old Södertälje road.
Leif Dahlén planerade en stor utbyggnad: Leif Dahlén planned a major expansion, including a 150-metre tower to house conference guests. But the trade-fair market turned when the dot-com bubble burst, and in 2008 the centre closed for good as Kistamässan took over.
Leif Dahlén planerade en stor utbyggnad,: Leif Dahlén planned a major expansion, including a 150-metre tower for conference accommodation. But when the dot-com bubble burst and rents doubled, the exhibition centre stopped paying its way.
Leksaksmuseet visar allt från Barbiedock: The Toy Museum shows everything from Barbie dolls, Lego and Star Wars figures to model steam engines, a large collection of tin soldiers and the railway society's model railway. The museum opened in 1980 on Mariatorget and moved here in 2018.
Leksaksmuseet visar bland annat Star War: The toy museum's displays include Star Wars figures, Barbie dolls, porcelain dolls, Lego and mechanical toys, a large collection of tin figures and the Railway Society's model railway. Nine out of ten items belong to the foundation itself.
Leksaksmuseet öppnade 1980 i gamla skoll: The Toy Museum opened in 1980 in old school premises by Mariatorget and moved in 2004 to the Söderdepån depot, next door to the Tramway Museum. When the depot was due to be demolished, the museum had to move again, reopening in Fisksätra on 26 May 2018.
Lemmingvallen heter fotbollsanläggningen: Lemmingvallen, the Lemming Ground, is the football ground a stone's throw away – a name that makes many people think of little mountain rodents. Here in Utby, in eastern Gothenburg, there's a grass pitch and an artificial pitch for eleven-a-side, plus two gravel pitches for seven-a-side. Utby Church is close by too.
Lerkrogen är ett hus som har flyttat. De: Lerkrogen is a house that has moved. The old tavern first stood near Brännkyrka Church, but it was taken down in 1968 to make way for new roads and the Stockholmsmässan exhibition centre. In 1986 it was put back up near Älvsjö station, and today local heritage societies use it. Next to it is the Älvkvarn stone, an ancient cup-mark stone that has also been moved twice.

Leta upp Lidingös kortaste väg vid Lidin: Find Lidingö's shortest road at Lidingsberg
Leta upp betongsnigeln i Snigelparken: Find the concrete snail in Snigelparken
Leta upp runristningen U 52 i berghällen: Track down the U 52 rune carving on the rock slab
Leta upp statyn Ung man: Find the statue Ung man, Young Man
Lettlands ambassad upprättades 1919 men: Latvia's embassy was established in 1919 but closed in 1940. After independence from the Soviet Union it reopened in 1992. Before moving to Odengatan it was at addresses including Birger Jarlsgatan 24, Valhallavägen 74 and Storgatan 38.
Lewerentz ledde bygget varje dag och kun: Lewerentz oversaw the building work every day and could be very firm. When a tiler complained that it wasn't coming out straight, he replied: 'Straight, straight – why must everything be straight? It should be beautiful, even if it's crooked.'
Lex Bollmora från 1959 gav kommunala bos: Lex Bollmora, passed in 1959, gave municipal housing companies the right to build in other municipalities. Buildable land was scarce in Stockholm, so the city's housing companies immediately started building in Bollmora.
Lex Bollmora från 1959 lät kommunala bos: Lex Bollmora, a law from 1959, allowed municipal housing companies to build outside their own municipality. Stockholm was short of land, and the city's housing companies started building here straight away.
Lex Bollmora från 1959 var en lagändring: Lex Bollmora, from 1959, was a change in the law that allowed municipal housing companies to build in other municipalities. Stockholm was short of land to build on, and the city's housing companies immediately started building in Bollmora.
Lexby var landsbygd ända tills radhusen: Lexby was open countryside right up until the terraced houses arrived in the 1950s, followed by the Vintergäcken estate in the late 1960s. The actor and director Sissela Kyle grew up here and writes about it in her memoir. Partille IF and the rugby club Spartacus both play their home games in Lexby, and a little further away is Partille Arena.
Lidingö Arena har långa fönsterband med: Lidingö Arena has long ribbons of windows with red-painted metal sun shades, and the red is echoed in the reddish-brown brick and the sheet-metal details. The building has an eight-storey section to the west and a lower, three-storey section to the east.
Lidingö centrum, kommunens största centr: Lidingö Centre, the island's biggest shopping area, opened in 1995 and combines shops with owner-occupied flats. Next door is Lidingö Town Hall from the early 1970s, designed by Sten Samuelson and given the blue rating for its high architectural and historical value. The Grand cinema, which opened in autumn 1993, is the only cinema in the whole municipality.
Lidingö friförsamling bildades 1888 och: Lidingö's free church congregation was founded in 1888 and in 1895 got its first mission house, Emanuelsberg, paid for with collected donations. Ansgarskyrkan was its third church. The architect Janne Feldt designed more than 50 churches, and this was one of his last.
Lidingö har bara tre vattentorn, och ett: Lidingö has just three water towers, and one of them stands a short walk from here, at the end of Tallbergsvägen. Käppala water tower is sometimes called Brevik water tower, even though it's actually in western Käppala. The area also has Villa Brevik from 1920, which for many years hosted HSB's in-house training courses.
Lidingö har en lång radhustradition. De: Lidingö has a long tradition of terraced housing. The Canada Houses at Bo, built in 1908–1909, are counted among the very first terraced houses in Sweden.
Lidingö har inget eget dricksvatten utan: Lidingö has no drinking water of its own and buys around 3.2 million cubic metres a year from Stockholm. In the past, the water came from deep-drilled wells and from Kottlasjön lake.
Lidingö villastad byggde inte bara villo: Lidingö villastad built not just villas but also "linked single-family houses", an early kind of terraced house – making Lidingö the first place in Sweden with terraced housing. The oldest are in the Canada block, from 1907–1908.
Lidingö växte snabbt, från 1 310 invånar: Lidingö grew fast, from 1,310 inhabitants in 1900 to 9,003 in 1920. Between 1917 and 1937, services for the south of the island were held in Skärsätra school, until Archbishop Erling Eidem consecrated Breviks kyrka on Midsummer Day 1937.
Lidingöbanan går över Lidingöbron, länge: The Lidingöbanan line crosses Lidingöbron, for many years the only road link to the island.
Lidingöbanan och båten hem: The Lidingö line and the boat home
Lidingövallen började anläggas 1936. Eft: Work on Lidingövallen began in 1936. After a major rebuild, the "new Lidingövallen" opened on 11 September 2021, and the running track was extended to 400 metres from the previous 369.
Liljeholmens station låg exakt mitt emel: Liljeholmen station sat exactly halfway between Älvsjö and Stockholm Central, four kilometres in each direction. The railway embankment across Liljeholmsviken bay was 270 metres long and only three metres above the water.
Liljevalchs byggdes för arvet efter indu: Liljevalchs was built with the fortune left by the industrialist Carl Fredrik Liljevalch. It opened in 1916 to make art accessible to everyone, and its first exhibition featured Carl Larsson, Anders Zorn and Bruno Liljefors.
Lilla Alby var i slutet av 1800-talet en: In the late 1800s Lilla Alby was a farm owned by Carl Abraham Humble. It was a long way to the nearest church, so in 1878 he had a chapel built on his land. The Mission Covenant congregation that also used it called it the Immanuel Chapel.
Lilla Bommen och Göteborgsoperan: Lilla Bommen and the Gothenburg Opera
Lilla Tissan var en stolpkvarn där hela: Lilla Tissan was a post mill, where the whole mill house turned to face the wind. Stora Tissan, from the 1750s, was a more modern Dutch-style mill, where only the cap with the sails turned. The artist Albert Theodor Gellerstedt painted them both in 1885, two years before they disappeared.
Lilla Tissan är känd sedan februari 1658: Lilla Tissan is on record from February 1658, when Erich Andersson was granted a site for a windmill by the Rörstrand wall. The wall ran where Dalagatan passes Sabbatsberg Hospital today. Nobody knows where the name Tissan comes from.
Lilla Ursvik har en oväntad industrihist: Lilla Ursvik has a surprising industrial past. In 1906 the brothers Alexander and Patrick Graham founded their lift company, Graham Brothers, here, and from 1929 it made neon signs as well. A new factory went up in 1937. Lifts were still being made here until the late 1970s, by which time the Finnish company Kone had taken over.
Lilla Varholmen är porten till Öckeröarn: Lilla Varholmen is the gateway to the Öckerö islands. It's linked to Hisingen by a bridge, and from here the car ferries head out to the islands of Öckerö municipality on two routes, the Björkö ferry and the Hönö ferry. The Björkö crossing is only about 900 metres long and takes roughly five minutes. The island has its own lighthouses too: the leading lights that guide ships in today date from 1927.

Lilla Varholmen is the gateway to the Öckerö islands. A bridge links it to Hisingen, and from here the car ferries head out to the islands of Öckerö municipality on both the Björkö and Hönö routes. The Björkö route is only about 900 metres long, and the crossing takes roughly five minutes. The island has lighthouses too: the first light station came as early as 1889.
Lilla Ösbysjön är bara 4,1 meter djup oc: A couple of minutes away, in the middle of the villa area, is Lilla Ösbysjön, a small lake only 4.1 metres deep. Close by is Vendevägen station on Roslagsbanan, the Roslagen railway. It opened in 1912 as Parkvägen and didn't change its name until 1956. The waiting shelter was designed by the architect Sigge Cronstedt.
Lilleby var länge ren landsbygd och hörd: For a long time Lilleby was pure countryside, part of Björlanda parish until the area became part of Gothenburg in 1967. The land was redistributed in 1846, and the old village site is now made up of three farms on a rise.
Lilleby vid havet på Hisingen var länge: Lilleby, by the sea on Hisingen, was pure countryside for a long time and belonged to Björlanda parish until it became part of Gothenburg in 1967. As early as 1846, the farmland here was redistributed in a land reform. Today the housing areas are growing fast. The district covers 1,330 hectares and is also home to Sillviks Havskoloni, a seaside holiday colony with its cabins preserved from the 1950s.
Lillklockan i klockstapeln, gjuten 1963,: The small bell in the bell tower, cast in 1963, bears the inscription: 'From tower blocks and villas you are called as guests to the preaching of the Word and the feast of Communion.' The large bell weighs 500 kilos and the small one 300.
Lillkyrkan som revs: The little church that was torn down
Lillpigan och Vallpojken: The Dairymaid and the Herd Boy
Lillsjön är en rest av Linta-sundet, som: Lillsjön is what's left of the Linta strait, which linked Ulvsundasjön with Lake Mälaren and could still be navigated by boat in the early Viking Age. A footpath of about 1.5 km runs round the lake, and in spring you can hear nightingales singing here.
Lillsjöstationen omvandlade växelström t: Lillsjö substation converted alternating current into direct current. Gustaf de Frumerie gave it red brick facades with National Romantic touches, and even the inner walls of the machine hall have patterned brickwork. The hall is seven metres high and is now used as a store and workshop.
Lillstugan byggdes 1919 av slaktare Joha: Lillstugan was built in 1919 by Johansson the butcher for his daughter Margareta, who wanted to open a café. Later on its customers were mostly soldiers, lorry drivers and bikers, and it appears as a bikers' haunt in the 1952 film Farlig kurva ('Dangerous Curve') with Varg-Olle Nygren.
Lillstugan byggdes 1919 åt slaktardotter: Lillstugan was built in 1919 for the butcher's daughter Margareta, who wanted to open a café. Later on its customers were mostly soldiers, lorry drivers and bikers. It appears as a bikers' haunt in the 1952 film Farlig kurva ('Dangerous Curve'), with Varg-Olle Nygren.
Lillstugan byggdes 1919 åt slaktarens do: Lillstugan was built in 1919 for the butcher's daughter Margareta, who wanted to open a café and bakery. Later its customers were mostly soldiers, lorry drivers and bikers, and it appears as a biker hangout in the 1952 film Farlig kurva. In the 1980s it was extended into an inn.
Lillängen har 161 villor, de flesta i tr: Lillängen has 161 villas, most of them timber-clad and one or two storeys high. The plots are small and the houses often stand well forward, close to the road. The road layout and plot divisions survive from the start.
Lillängen nämns första gången 1653 och v: Lillängen is first mentioned in 1653, when it was a grazing and hay meadow belonging to the Järla estate. The villa area was planned in 1937, and the first families moved into their new houses that same autumn. The same year, the area got its own stop on the Saltsjöbanan railway, and the functionalist waiting shelter from 1937 – green with white corners – is still standing today.
Linas boställe eller linbod?: Lina's home or a flax shed?
Lind och en varnande gravsten: A linden and a warning gravestone
Lindallén ner till ångbåten: A lime avenue down to the steamer
Lindarna som gav ön namn: The lime trees behind the name
Linden på Torslanda kyrkogård är minst 8: The linden tree in Torslanda churchyard is at least 800 years old. Beside it stands the gravestone of the vicar Arfwid Gren, who died in 1799. Its inscription ends: “Touch not this Stone. For Death Dwells within.”
Linden på kyrkogården är minst 800 år ga: The linden tree in the churchyard is at least 800 years old. Beside it stands the 1799 gravestone of the vicar Arfwid Gren, which ends: "Gnag ey de Dödas Ben Förvara Deras Minne. Rör ey vid denna Sten. Ty Döden Bor där inne." – roughly, "Gnaw not the bones of the dead, keep their memory. Touch not this stone, for Death dwells within."

The lime tree in the churchyard is at least 800 years old. Beside it stands the 1799 gravestone of the vicar Arfwid Gren, which ends: 'Touch not this stone, for Death dwells within.' Most of the elms along the wall were planted in 1837.
Lindevägen fick sitt namn 1917, och vill: Lindevägen got its name in 1917, and the villa area along it was first known as Nya Enskede, 'New Enskede', or Palmeska förstaden, 'the Palme suburb'. The name Linde comes from a croft, an inn and a coaching station that stood nearby from 1762. Since 2012 the metro station has been decorated with Maria Miesenberger's Ögonblick i rörelse, 'Moments in Motion', with granite-ceramic walls and aluminium sculptures.
Lindhagsskrapan består av två förskjutna: Lindhagsskrapan is made up of two offset blocks in pale concrete, with a patterned relief that hides the joints. The glazed balconies are set into the façade, forming broad bands. The building was nominated for Stockholm Building of the Year 2012.
Lindholmen nämns första gången 1333, då: Lindholmen is first mentioned in 1333, when King Magnus Eriksson dated a letter at his fortified Lindholmen. The castle on what is now Slottsberget had stood since at least 1250 and was given to Queen Blanka as a morning gift, the bride's present on the day after the wedding. By 1410 it had fallen into such disrepair that no one could live there.
Lindholmen var länge ett av Göteborgs st: For many years Lindholmen was one of Gothenburg's great shipyards. Where ships once took shape, you'll now find Lindholmen Science Park and part of Chalmers University of Technology. From the quay there's a view straight across the river to the city centre.
Lindholmspiren ligger vid den gamla varv: Lindholmspiren is in the old shipyard district of Lindholmen, where ships were built for more than a hundred years. Today it's home to Lindholmen Science Park and part of Chalmers University of Technology, and from the quay you can look straight across the river to the city centre.
Lindome ligger cirka 15 kilometer söder: Lindome lies about 15 kilometres south of Gothenburg, but still counts as part of the Gothenburg urban area. It's the church village of Lindome parish, in the province of Halland, wedged between the E6 motorway and the West Coast Line. A short way off is Lindome station, where commuter trains call and buses have a larger stop.
Lindome socken är stor, hela 81,7 kvadra: Lindome parish is a big one, covering a full 81.7 square kilometres, and it takes in both the town of Hällesåker and Lindome itself, with its parish church. Lindome Church is a short walk from here. The parish used to belong to the province of Halland and the old Fjäre district, but since 1998 it has been part of Västra Götaland County.
Lindome station har varit död och återup: Lindome station has died and come back to life. It opened on 1 September 1888, when the Gothenburg–Halland railway was completed, but passenger trains stopped calling in 1970, and in 1989 the station shut altogether. Then, when commuter trains between Gothenburg and Kungsbacka started up again, it made a comeback on 17 August 1992. In 2012 it was rebuilt to take longer trains.
Lindome station öppnade redan 1888. Pers: Lindome station first opened as far back as 1888. Passenger services were withdrawn in 1970, and in 1989 the station closed altogether. When commuter trains started running between Gothenburg and Kungsbacka, it reopened on 17 August 1992.
Lindome var i århundraden danskt område: For centuries Lindome was Danish territory, becoming Swedish along with the rest of Halland after the Treaty of Roskilde in 1658. The hills to the north long marked the border with Sweden. Minor boundary disputes rumbled on, and the final border adjustment wasn't settled until the mid-1950s.
For centuries Lindome was Danish territory. Halland became Swedish for 30 years under the Treaty of Brömsebro in 1645, and for good under the Treaty of Roskilde in 1658.
Lindome är känt för sin möbeltillverknin: Lindome is known for its furniture-making in the 19th and early 20th centuries. Among other things, this is where the Gothenburg chair – often called the Lindome chair – was made. Furniture was a winter sideline for the farmers, who carried their pieces on foot all the way to Järntorget square to sell them.

Lindome is known for its furniture-making, not least the Gothenburg chair, often called the Lindome chair. The furniture was made as a winter sideline, and the pieces were carried on foot to be sold around Järntorget.
Lindomesnickarnas möbeltorg: Furniture market of the Lindome joiners
Lindvreten var ett torp under Vårby gård: Lindvreten was a croft belonging to Vårby gård, and its name probably means 'the patch of land with the lime trees'. Nearby was the croft of Månskär, whose curious name has nothing to do with the moon. It comes from Måns, one of its first tenants, and kärr, the Swedish word for wetland. This is also where you'll find Södra djursjukhuset, an animal hospital that started out in 1967 with two people working from a villa.
Lindötunneln går genom en klippa på östr: The Lindö tunnel runs 178 metres through a rock outcrop on the east side of Lindö. Before, the road wound through a couple of sharp, narrow bends between Tillflykten and Lindö lada. The new route brought both fewer accidents and shorter queues.
Ling begravdes på udden norr om gården,: Per Henrik Ling, father of Swedish gymnastics, was buried on the headland north of the farm, where a 3.5-metre standing stone bears the inscription Ling 1776–1839. His grandson Alarik Liedbeck, Alfred Nobel's closest collaborator, also lies here.
Ling byggde 1825 om den rödmålade uthusl: In 1825 Ling rebuilt the red-painted outbuilding, widening and lengthening it to fit a gymnasium for his gymnastics system. He gave the main house a simple Empire style, with a vaulted hall beneath a small dome.
Ling gav huset dess enkla empirstil. I d: Ling gave the house its simple Empire style. The tall dormer gables were fitted out with a vaulted hall, crowned by a small four-sided dome in the middle of the ceiling. A semicircular room on the ground floor shows as a bulge on the north facade.
Ling vilar på udden norr om gården under: Ling, father of Swedish gymnastics, lies on the headland north of the estate beneath a 3.5-metre standing stone inscribed "Ling 1776–1839". His grandson Alarik Liedbeck, Alfred Nobel's closest collaborator, is buried here too. The site is a private burial ground and an ancient monument.
Lingström valde Edsbacka för att det var: Lingström chose Edsbacka because it was the oldest surviving inn building in Sweden. The restaurant won its first Michelin star in 1992 and its second in 2000.
Linné fick vänta på hästar: Linnaeus had to wait for horses
Liseberg ligger alldeles i närheten. Där: Liseberg amusement park is just nearby. One of its rides is the Flume Ride, opened in 1973, where log-shaped boats float along a 610-metre water channel with drops of up to 14 metres. Beside the park, the Grand Curiosa Hotel opened in 2023, just in time for Liseberg's 100th birthday. Eklandagatan, by the way, is named after the village of Eklanda – and the ending 'landa' means land by the shore.
Lisebergsbadet invigdes 1936 och ansågs: Lisebergsbadet opened in 1936 and was considered the most modern swimming baths in Europe. The pool was 32 metres long and 5 metres deep at one end, with underwater lighting and artificial waves. It was demolished in 1962.
Lissmasjön är en grund fågelsjö med fåge: Lissmasjön is a shallow bird lake with a bird-watching tower and a trail on wooden boardwalks. It has one of the county's largest populations of the red-listed blue-headed wagtail and a big black-headed gull colony. Every now and then a white-tailed eagle drops by.
Listan över artister som spelat i hallen: The list of artists who've played the hall is long: Black Sabbath, Suede, Saxon, Yngwie Malmsteen, Thåström, the Cult, Rammstein and Iggy Pop, to name a few. Not bad for a sports hall in Solna.
Listan över band som spelat in i Studio: The list of bands who have recorded at Studio Fredman is a long one. Besides the best-known names, it includes Dark Tranquillity, Soilwork and The Haunted, and from Britain, Bring Me the Horizon. The studio has also worked with labels such as Nuclear Blast, Century Media and Metal Blade Records.
Listuddens huvudbyggnad från 1740- eller: Listudden's main house, from the 1740s or 1750s, was originally painted yellow but turned Falu red in 2013, when it gained a modern octagonal extension. The Gustavian-style front door was salvaged from a demolished house in Nacka.
Litterära kaféer i gamla torpet: Literary cafés in the old croft
Livets träd i absiden: The Tree of Life in the apse
Livränta åt stadshusets arkitekt: A pension for City Hall's architect
Ljudet av speedway har ekat här. Arendal: This place has echoed to the roar of speedway. Arendalsbanan, a 336-metre track, was home to the Kaparna team. The attendance record of 5,940 was set in September 2002, against Rospiggarna, and Tony Rickardsson set the lap record riding for Masarna in 2004. A little further on, in Rödjan, is Rya skog, a nature reserve since 1928 and a last remnant of the mixed oak woodland that once covered much of the west coast.
Ljusets kyrka: Ljusets kyrka, the Church of Light
Ljusets kyrka är åttkantig och klädd i f: Ljusets kyrka, the Church of Light, is octagonal and clad in Falu red boarding. The walls lean outwards by 15 degrees so that it resembles a ship, like Noah's Ark. From inside, the walls are meant to recall a flower unfolding its petals towards the light.
Ljusets kyrkas orgel är köpt från S:ta B: The organ in Ljusets kyrka, the Church of Light, was bought from St Birgitta's chapel crematorium in Skövde. Neon-tube chandeliers hang from the ceiling, and the altarpiece is a three-metre sheet of steel cut with water and sand.
Ljusgul senempir och träflyglar: Pale yellow Empire and timber wings
Ljushall bakom glasfasaden: A light hall behind the glass
Ljuskonst på klippväggen: Light art on the rock face
Logen som inte finns: The dance hall that doesn't exist
Lojo har fått namn efter Lidingös vänort: Lojo is named after Lidingö's twin town in Finland. Its 24 houses are carefully fitted into the rocky pine-covered terrain. The facades are lightweight brick and timber panelling in red or yellow – one colour for each row – and all the balconies are white.
Loket 1 och Porslinsbruket 29 på norra s: Loket 1 and Porslinsbruket 29 on the north side, and the Sportpalatset and Sankt Erikspalatset on the south, together form a grand gateway around the Sankt Eriksbron bridge. The buildings have façades facing the streets three storeys down beneath the bridge as well.
Lokstallet är halvcirkelformat, med fasa: The engine shed is semicircular, with red-brick façades and gables decorated with stepped friezes and round windows. The locomotives rolled in through large wooden doors on the inner curve. Outside is a restored turntable that still works.
Loppis under torget: A flea market beneath the square
Lotternas växtval i Hjulsta speglar odla: What grows on the allotments in Hjulsta reflects the gardeners' backgrounds. One grower from Peru, for instance, doesn't grow Swedish potatoes but a Peruvian variety he imported himself.
Lotuskolonner och rosa salong: Lotus columns and a pink auditorium
Loviseberg, en bit härifrån, är till sto: Loviseberg, a little way from here, is mostly a lovely area for getting outdoors, with a ski slope, a beach and walking trails. By Lake Albysjön is the Gömsta äng nature reserve. Set up in 1966, it's both the oldest and the smallest reserve in Huddinge, with meadows, alder woods along the shore and a grove full of wild flowers. Part of the 80-kilometre Huddingeleden trail runs through it.
Lovisebergs högsta punkt är Flottsbrobac: Loviseberg's highest point is Flottsbrobacken, 103 metres above sea level, but it's artificial. The highest natural summit, at 82 metres, is about 300 metres to the east.
Lovö skogskyrkogård anlades på 1830-tale: Lovö Woodland Cemetery was laid out in the 1830s, after complaints that the old churchyard at Lovö Church had grown too cramped and sat on marshy ground. It lies on Lovö kyrkallé, inside the Drottningholm Palace World Heritage area. From here you can also join Lovöns fornstig, an 18-kilometre heritage trail across the island of Lovön that links ancient remains, memorials and interesting buildings.
Lovö socken omfattar öarna Lovön, Kärsön: Lovö parish takes in the islands of Lovön, Kärsön, Fågelön and Kungshatt, plus a few smaller islets. The landscape is gently hilly, with both fields and forest. The oldest parts of the church date from the 12th century.
Lovö socken rymmer både Drottningholms s: The parish of Lovö is home to both Drottningholm Palace and the old parish church, Lovö kyrka, a little way from here. Outside the church stand five runestones, and one of them has had quite an adventure. In the 17th century it stood by the door of the church porch, but when the porch was pulled down in 1798, the stone ended up buried. It wasn't found again until 1935, when the church was being restored – all 2.7 metres of it, raised in memory of a woman.
Lovö vattenverk är en funktionalistisk b: Lovö waterworks is a functionalist building from 1933 by Paul Hedqvist, and it supplies drinking water to much of the Stockholm region. South of the golf course stands Lådan ('the Box'), a replica of the architect Ralph Erskine's first home in Sweden.
Lovön is full of traces of the Viking Age. About 500 metres south of Edeby farm is a runic inscription carved straight into the bedrock, known as U 52. It's a reminder that people have lived and travelled here for a thousand years – long before the buses started running to Ekerö.
Lovön är ön i Mälaren där Drottningholms: Lovön is the island in Lake Mälaren where Drottningholm Palace stands, linked to the mainland by the Drottningholm and Nockeby bridges. A short walk away is Lovö Church, with no fewer than five runestones outside – among them a little sandstone one barely more than a metre tall. From the church, the Lovö church avenue runs ruler-straight for about 1,800 metres towards the palace grounds.
Lovös gamla prästgård har en huvudbyggna: Lovö's old vicarage has a main building from 1766 with 18th-century tiled stoves. The old kitchen survives in the cellar, complete with bread oven and open hearth, and today the place is run as an organic dairy farm.
Lovö's old vicarage has a main house from 1766. The old kitchen survives in the cellar, with its bread oven, open hearth and limestone floor. Today it's an organic dairy farm.
Luftvärn och skjutbana i dalen: Anti-aircraft guns and a firing range in the valley
Lugnet kallades också Farsta Lugnet, Asp: Lugnet, also known as Farsta Lugnet, Asplund or Grindstugan, belonged to Farsta manor. Towards the end of the 19th century the house was rebuilt as a manager's residence with an upper floor and a glazed veranda. At that time, along with Starrmyran and Bergholm, it was the only house in what is now Hökarängen.
Lullehovsbron spänner över det drygt 200: Lullehovsbron bridge crosses the Lullehovssundet strait, just over 200 metres wide, between Färingsö and Lindö. Both the bridge and the strait are named after the hamlet of Lullehov at the bridge's eastern end. Today's bridge opened to traffic in 1980. The water is about seven metres deep in the middle of the strait, and at its southern end lies the little island of Kaninholmen, Rabbit Island.
Lullehovssundet ligger mellan Färingsön: Lullehovssundet runs between Färingsön and Lindö. To the south-west it joins the bay of Långtarmen, and to the north-east it opens out into Mörbyfjärden and Malmvikssjön.
Lumas fabrik byggdes 1929–1930 och lades: The Luma factory was built in 1929–1930 and closed in 1977. Its distinctive glass-walled superstructure down by the quay still stands. Light bulbs were put through long-term tests there, and their glow spread across the harbour and southern Södermalm.
Lunda nämns första gången 1441, då Gotsk: Lunda is first mentioned in 1441, when Gotskalk Bengtsson sold land in Lunda and Skesta to the Holy Ghost hospital in Stockholm. The farm was later bought by the City of Stockholm in 1931.
Lunda nämns första gången 1441, när Gots: Lunda is first mentioned in 1441, when Gotskalk Bengtsson (Ulv) sold land in Lunda and Skesta to the Holy Spirit hospital in Stockholm. The City of Stockholm bought the farm in 1931.

Lunda is first mentioned in 1441, when Gotskalk Bengtsson sold land here to the Helgeandshuset hospital in Stockholm. By 1541 the village had three farms. The City of Stockholm bought the farm in 1931.
Lundbergs konditori: Lundbergs konditori, a classic café and patisserie
Lundbergs konditori grundades 1946 av sk: Lundbergs konditori was founded in 1946 by Kurt Lundberg, a pastry chef from Skåne who had previously worked at Oscar Bergs Konditori. He ran it until 1972. The interior has barely changed since the day it opened.
Lundby Bio på Jägaregatan 6 öppnade den: Lundby Bio at Jägaregatan 6 opened on 5 November 1932 and showed films for almost 28 years, until 27 March 1960.
Lundbybadet ritades av Eugen Thorburn oc: Lundbybadet was designed by Eugen Thorburn and completed in November 1915. It was the fourth bathhouse built thanks to a donation from Sven Renström. Its swimming hall rose through two storeys, but it no longer survives.
Lundbybadet var det fjärde badhuset som: Lundbybadet was the fourth bathhouse built for the Renström public baths, funded by a donation from Sven Renström. The swimming hall rose through two storeys but no longer survives.
Lundens vattentorn byggdes 1930 och är o: Lunden's water tower was built in 1930. It is around 45 metres high with eight sides. Water was pumped up here from a new pumping station in Bagaregården, and at the base the corners are shaped like columns that 'carry' the top of the tower.
Lundens vattentorn, en åttkantig putsad: Lunden water tower, an eight-sided rendered building about 45 metres tall, was built in 1930 to a design by Eugen Thorburn, the architect who also designed Lundenskolan school. A little further away, on the corner of Sankt Pauligatan and Femkampsgatan, is Kolerakyrkogården, the Cholera Cemetery, with a memorial stone to those who died in the cholera epidemic of 1834. The front of the stone simply reads År 1834 – 'The year 1834'.
Lundenskolan invigdes den 15 maj 1914, o: Lundenskolan school opened on 15 May 1914, and its architect, Eugen Thorburn, went on to design the district's water tower too. Next door is Örgryte New Cemetery from 1890, with almost 3,900 graves. A short way off is Tån cemetery. Its name comes from ‘tun’, the patch of land beside the home fields where livestock were let out to graze.
Luxgatan är en blinkning till AB Lux, se: Luxgatan is a nod to AB Lux, later Electrolux, whose factories stood on the south-eastern part of the island – lux is Latin for light. This was also the site of Nya Chartago, the stronghold of a fraternal society called the Coldinu Order, and the Fridberg inn welcomed guests from the 18th century until the 1850s. Over on the Marieberg side, Gideon Forslund built fast motorboats known as flat-iron racers.
Lyssna efter Almedahls linnefabrik, tänd: Listen out for the Almedahl linen mill, the match factory in Elisedal that became part of Ivar Kreuger's empire, and the sofa on the roof at Krokslätts torg.
Lyssna vid Henriksdalsviadukten: hos Ryl: Listen out at Henriksdalsviadukten: from 1882 until the late 1950s, the Rylander & Rudolph factory here made batteries for crank telephones and carbon rods for arc lamps.
Lägenheterna var på 24 kvadratmeter, med: The flats were 24 square metres, with one room, a bathroom and a cooking cupboard in the hall. In 1948 the rent for a single person was 35 kronor a month, electricity, heating and water included.
Lägenhetsmuseet har synts i långfilmen \: The Apartment Museum appears in the feature film ‘Monica Z’. Peter Birro’s TV series ‘Upp till kamp’ and the drama series ‘Vår tid är nu’ (‘The Restaurant’) were also filmed here.
Lägg märke till gatunamnen: Sedelvägen,: Take a look at the street names: Sedelvägen, Riksdalervägen and Sparbanksvägen – Banknote Road, Riksdaler Road and Savings Bank Road – with blocks named Valutan, 'the Currency', and Förskottet, 'the Advance'. In the Förskottet block is Hägerstensåsen's old post office from 1951, designed by Lars-Erik Lallerstedt and blue-listed by the City Museum. You can't post letters here any more, but the mail is still sorted inside. The district sits on a ridge that rises to 67 metres above sea level.
Läkare och sjuksköterskor har gett namn: In Guldheden, the streets are named after doctors and nurses. Doktor Allards gata honours the doctor who started free seaside trips to Askim for Gothenburg's children – known as 'Doktor Allard's bathing children'. In the middle of the square, Fina fisken, 'the Fine Fish', spouts water. Palle Pernevi made this steel sculpture in 1961, welding it together himself, and its five jets are meant to evoke Lyrön in Bohuslän, where it was created.
Läkaren Per Johan Wising köpte tomten 18: The doctor Per Johan Wising bought the plot in 1882 and named it Kappsta after his father-in-law's manor. The Swiss-style villa came to 300 square metres, and a grey-stone retaining wall about five metres high was built to create level ground.
Länge låg kvarnstenen ensam uppe på kvar: For a long time the millstone lay alone up on the mill hill. In 2011 a citizens' proposal called for it to be cleaned and moved to where more people could see it, and since summer 2013 it has stood on Gymnasievägen. Two other millstones are set into the footpath by Kvarnbergsgården.
Länge var Stora Essingens Wärdshus öns e: For a long time Stora Essingens Wärdshus was the only building on the island – an inn by the shipping lane into Stockholm from the 18th century until 1876. Its skittle alley survived into the early 1900s, and the west wing still stands as a private home.
