Even closer is the Fructus building, the white functionalist factory where the soft drink Pommac was made.
Mitt bland villorna i Smedslätten, på en: Right among the villas of Smedslätten, on an empty plot on Aladdinsvägen, lies Kämpakumlet – a Bronze Age burial ground with round, cairn-like stone settings. It was partly excavated in 1922, while the garden suburb was being built. The district is named after Smedslätten farm. All that's left of it is the early 19th-century main house, now surrounded by terraced homes.
Mitt emot Solna centrum ligger Eric Grat: Opposite Solna centrum is Eric Grate's park, named after the sculptor who spent his last fifteen years in Solna. Three of his bronze sculptures stand here: Oberon, Nike de Sant Andria and Sparvguden, the Sparrow God. The shopping centre itself is one of the largest in the region, with more than 95 shops and 22 restaurants.
Mitt genom Mölnlyckes centrum rinner Möl: Right through the middle of Mölnlycke runs the Mölndalsån river, flowing from Landvettersjön – also known as Gröen – to Lake Rådasjön.
Mitt hjärta i världen: Mitt hjärta i världen, 'My Heart in the World'
Mitt i Ekerö ligger Ekebyhovs slott, ett: In the middle of Ekerö stands Ekebyhov Castle, an estate that Klas Horn created in the 1620s by merging the farms of Ekeby, Hovgården and Gällsta.
In the middle of Ekerö stands Ekebyhov Palace, a former estate that Klas Horn created in the 1620s by merging the farms of Ekeby, Hovgården and Gällsta.
Mitt i Eklanda, en stadsdel där cirka 3: In Eklanda, where around 3,100 people live in some 700 homes, the forest is never far away. The area borders the Änggårdsbergen nature reserve and Högsbo. Most of it was built after 1993, and the plan is for Eklanda eventually to grow together with the village of Fässberg.
Mitt i Liseberg ligger parken Fem Fålars: In the middle of Liseberg is the park Fem Fålars brunn, 'the Five Foals' Well', named in 1953 after the five horses in Staffansvisan, the traditional St Stephen's Day song. The streets around it have names such as Annandagsvägen and Ottesångsvägen, after Boxing Day and the early Christmas morning service.
Mitt i Lövgärdet, ett primärområde i sta: In the middle of Lövgärdet, part of the Gårdsten district, stands a church that has retired from its role. Lövgärdet Church was deconsecrated on 19 June 2016, after belonging to Gunnared parish from 1973 and to Angered parish in its final years. The building is still right nearby, but the services have moved elsewhere.
Mitt i Rävekärr står de gråa, kvadratisk: In the middle of Rävekärr stand the grey, square terraced houses nicknamed 'lådhus' – box houses – giving the estate a geometry all of its own. Right next door is Fågelberg Church, part of Stensjön parish. To the south-east are two lakes, Horsikan and Rävekärrs Långevatten – perfect if you'd like to swap boxes for water.
Mitt i Solberga ligger Solbergaskogen, m: In the middle of Solberga is Solbergaskogen, a wood of bare rock and pine trees that the Swedish Forest Agency classed as a key habitat in 2009. It holds ancient remains, among them the Solberga burial ground, and takes its name from Solberga farm, mentioned as early as 1636. A little further away is Apelsinlunden, the Orange Grove – a Million Programme housing estate from 1967 that owes its nickname to its orange-red colour scheme.
Mitt i Stockholms inlopp står Gustaf Dal: Right in the middle of the sea approach to Stockholm stands Gustaf Dalén's first lighthouse with his famous sun valve, from 1912. Today the lighthouse runs on electricity.
Right in the approach to Stockholm stands Gustaf Dalén's first lighthouse, fitted in 1912 with his sun valve, which switched the light on and off by itself. Today the lighthouse runs on electricity.
Mitt i Täby Park planeras en stadspark p: In the heart of Täby Park, plans are under way for a city park of about 10 hectares, where the racecourse grounds and natural hillocks will be turned into one continuous green space with meadows, trees and play areas.
Mitt i Volvos värld står Volvohallen, en: In the heart of Volvo country stands Volvohallen, a domed exhibition hall on a square plan, built in 1975 beside what was then the company's head office and designed by Lund & Valentin. Right next to it is Torslandaverken, the Volvo Cars plant. When it opened, it was the largest single-storey factory in the Nordic region.
Mitt i centrum ligger Viksjö kyrka, som: In the middle of the centre is Viksjö church, consecrated by Bishop Caroline Krook on 19 June 2005, the fourth Sunday after Trinity. The name Viksjö itself is far older: it's a corruption of an original Vikhusa, which already appears on an 11th-century runestone.
Mitt i ett industriområde gömmer sig en: Tucked away in the middle of an industrial estate is a true survivor: Rya skog, a remnant of the mixed oak forest that once covered much of Sweden's west coast. Most of it became a nature reserve as early as 1928, and a survey in 2007 found 22 rare and endangered species here. It's a favourite with botanists and birdwatchers, especially in spring.
Mitt i ett svenskt villaområde vid kuste: In the middle of a Swedish residential area on the coast, there's a copy of Kina slott, the Chinese Pavilion at Drottningholm. Skintebo, in Billdal, was farmland for many years, but in the 1970s Skintebodalen was built up with car-free footpaths, terraced houses, two-storey wooden houses and what are known as båtmansgårdar – “boatswain's houses” – an odd cross between a terraced house and a villa.
Mitt i handelsområdet Kungens kurva finn: Right in the middle of the Kungens kurva shopping area there's an oasis – at least in name. The sculpture Oas, 'Oasis', was created in 2009 by the artist and designer Thomas Nordström, working with the landscape architect Torsten Wallin. A little further on is Kolartorp, a croft with plenty of names: it has also been known as Kålartorp, Crone and Ryttartorp nummer två, 'Cavalryman's Croft No. 2'.
Mitt i kontorshuset finns ett atrium med: At the heart of the office building is an atrium lit by daylight from above. A corkscrew-like staircase winds up through all eight floors, sweeping in a free-standing semicircle from one level to the next. The facades are clad in glass.
Mitt i kvarteret står Coldinuorden 3, et: In the middle of the block is Coldinuorden 3, one of Bredäng's many long slab blocks from the mid-1960s – yet the only one the City Museum has rated blue for its exceptional cultural and historical value. Nearby Slättgårdsskolan school burned down in June 2020, and the owner decided to rebuild it with a fresh look. A new gym opened as early as 2021.
Mitt i nuvarande Emågatan låg Mosstugan,: Right where Emågatan runs today stood Mosstugan, a forest workers’ cottage. From 1935 to 1951 it was leased by the Goterna orienteering club as a rest hut, and it gave its name to the Mosstugan block.
Mitt i området, i parken, står en betong: Right in the middle of the area, in the park, stands a concrete sculpture by Pablo Picasso. It was donated to the student housing area in 1969 by the master builder Allan Skarne.
Mitt i parken ligger den gamla sjukhusda: In the middle of the park lies the old hospital pond, almost unchanged since the area was built. The trees are so magnificent that plans for an arboretum have been floated several times.

In the middle of the park lies the old hospital pond, almost unchanged since the area was built. The trees are so magnificent that plans for an arboretum have been floated several times. The hospital used to have large gardens of its own, both as therapy and to grow food.
Mitt i reservatet ligger gamla åkrar som: In the middle of the reserve lie old fields that belonged to the croft of Ormkärr, mentioned as early as 1617. The croft's fields still look much as they do on 18th-century maps, and stone foundations, a clearance cairn and field ditches remain.
Mitt i rondellen står en 4,5 meter hög k: In the middle of the roundabout stands a 4.5-metre pin, pushed through a cross in the ground. The sculpture, by Ebba Matz, is called Här – ‘Here’. The square's name was controversial: the city property office would have preferred Reutersplatsen, partly because Wavrinsky was so hard to pronounce. On the hill next door, students now live in Guldheden's old northern water tower.
Mitt i skogen mellan sjöarna Flaten och: Deep in the forest between the lakes Flaten and Drevviken is Torpet i Orhem, a culture café that has been going since the 1940s. Artists such as Frida Hyvönen and Joel Alme have played on its little stage, which now lives in a converted shipping container. Right next door is Orhems gård, a farm going back to the 15th century, and down by Lake Drevviken is Gebers, a former convalescent home that in 1997 became one of Sweden's first eco co-housing communities.
Mitt i studentområdet Kungshamra står en: In the middle of the Kungshamra student housing stands a concrete sculpture by Pablo Picasso, donated in 1969 by the builder Allan Skarne. The window frames were originally painted yellow, blue and red to bring the concrete to life.
Mitt i villaområdet ligger Björnberget,: In the middle of the villa district lies Björnberget, once known as August Strindberg's Park. It's hilly, rocky terrain with a stone setting, probably a Bronze Age grave.
Mitt i Översjön ligger ön Getholmen, som: In the middle of Översjön lake lies the island of Getholmen, a bird sanctuary where black-throated divers have nested for many years. The lake holds perch, pike, rudd and bream, among others, and you'll need a fishing permit to fish.
Mitt på torget står Farstafontänen av Pe: In the middle of the square stands the Farsta Fountain by Per-Erik Willö, from 1960. The north-eastern part of the square once had a paddling pool, but it has since been decked over.
Mitt på torget, som hette Adolf Fredriks: In the middle of the square, known as Adolf Fredriks torg until 1959, stands Tors fiske, Thor's Fishing, a fountain by Anders Wissler unveiled in 1903. Also on the square is Hotel Rival, owned by the composer Benny Andersson and named after the old Rival cinema in the same building. This was once the site of Sutherska huset, a private palace from 1774. From 1811 the Philipsen school taught poor children there, until the building was demolished in 1909.
Mitt på ön ligger fritidsanläggningen Vä: In the middle of the island is the Västerhav leisure resort, with cabins to rent and a restaurant. Two sailing clubs have Grötö as their home port, and near the harbour there's both a sandy beach and rocks with a swimming ladder.
Mittemot Segeltorpsskolan, vid nuvarande: Opposite Segeltorpsskolan, the Segeltorp school, at what is now Kapellvägen 1, there was once a croft called Holmtorp. Its first family of crofters were Jonas Olsson and his wife Kjärstin Eriksdotter, both born in 1710, and in the 1760s the place went by the name of either Holmtorp or Cronan. The croft was pulled down in 1859. Another croft, Segeltorp, survived until 1964, when the terraced houses of Jakobslundsvägen were built on the site.
Mittemot slottet ligger Tessinska palats: Facing Stockholm Palace stand the Tessin Palace, built in 1692–1697, and the Fleming Palace from the 1650s. The Finnish Church was built in 1648–1653, but wasn't consecrated as a church until after a rebuild in 1725.
Mjuka gator i stället för raka: Gentle curves instead of straight lines
Mjölet från kvarnarna här såldes under n: Flour from the mills here was sold under the brand name Kejsarkronan, 'the Imperial Crown'. In the 1980s, Saltsjöqvarn produced 10 per cent of all Sweden's flour. The yellow Mannagrynskvarnen from 1923 was Scandinavia's first mill built specifically for semolina.
Mjölkgård i prästgården: A dairy farm at the vicarage
Mjölktåg till kvarteret Mejeristen: Milk trains to the Mejeristen block
Mjölnarbostaden står kvar vid Julitaväge: The miller's house still stands at Julitavägen 2. Of the mill itself, only a round, grass-covered mound remains, about 12 metres across, with large stones on the surface. The old Göta landsväg road next to it is now a footpath and cycle track.
Mjölnare som skrev med bomärken: Millers who signed with house marks
Mjölnarstugan på kullen: The miller's cottage on the hill
Modellen för Flicka med fruktkorg var Up: The model for ‘Flicka med fruktkorg’ (‘Girl with a Fruit Basket’) was Birgitta Larsson, a student at Uppsala. The sculpture was commissioned with money left over from the donation for the council chamber’s art.
Modellvillan 21 ersatte en butikslokal f: Model villa 21 replaced a shop from 1944. The whole façade and roof are clad in larch, which turns grey over time. The jury called it "a bold choice of material".
Moderna museet: Moderna Museet, the Museum of Modern Art
Modernt sjukhem vid sjön: A modern nursing home by the lake
Mogningslagret för bananer står kvar ute: The old banana-ripening warehouse still stands out on the pier. During Gothenburg's Kulturkalas festival and other events, the pier becomes a party and concert venue, and now and then it even hosts car races.
Moment teaters konstnärlige ledare är An: Moment teater's artistic director is Andreas Boonstra. He and the director Pontus Stenshäll won the newspaper Svenska Dagbladet's Thalia Prize in 2008 for their work on theatre classics.
Monumentet var för stort för att formas: The monument was too big to model in clay, so Carl Eldh carved it straight in plaster in his studio in Bellevueparken. The model was finished in 1942, but during the war it was sawn into pieces and stored until it could be cast in bronze.
Monumentet är ett massivt block av rödak: The monument is a solid block of reddish sandstone, 172 centimetres long. The relief probably shows Christ, along with a scene of Björn rising from the grave as an angel sounds the trumpet. It's likely the first time this kind of leaf ornament appears in Scandinavia.
Mordet på Lilly Lindeström löstes aldrig: The murder of Lilly Lindeström was never solved, and the case was time-barred in 1957. Much later, a retired crime-scene investigator brought out a box containing a tea towel and a dented soup ladle with reddish-brown stains. The criminologist Leif G.W. Persson has since questioned whether the stains were definitely blood.
Morgon och kväll, när solen står lågt, s: Morning and evening, when the sun is low, it’s reflected in Brommahöjden’s glass gables. The building was nominated for Stockholm Building of the Year 2010 and came fifth in the final vote.
Morgonen den 23 september 2009 använde r: On the morning of 23 September 2009, robbers flew a stolen helicopter in to collect their haul from a cash depot in the Västberga industrial area. It was the first helicopter robbery in Swedish history. The police helicopters never got off the ground – someone had left a fake bomb on their landing pad. The building, Vreten 17, was originally built for Volvo, among others.
Mosaikfönster som altartavla: A mosaic window for an altarpiece
Moskén började byggas 1998 och stod klar: Work on the mosque began in 1998 and it was completed in 2007, in the Turkish style. The central dome has windows and birch panelling, the walls of the prayer hall are covered in hand-painted tiles, and the minaret is 32.5 metres tall.
Moskén har ett bibliotek med över 3 000: The mosque has a lending library of more than 3,000 books in several languages. At an open house for Järfälla residents in 2017, visitors were treated to calligraphy, an art exhibition, a guided tour and a meze buffet.
Mossens gård från 1800-talets andra hälf: Mossen farm, from the second half of the 19th century, is the oldest surviving building in Tallkrogen. In the farmyard stands a mighty oak with a crown 27 metres across, protected by the local plan.
Mosstorp stavades först Måstorp, efter e: Mosstorp was first spelled Måstorp, after a large bog – a “Måse” – south of the croft, which appears on a 1774 map of Lidingö. Per Olof Hallman began planning the garden suburb in 1907.
Mot gatan är huset slutet, men baksidan: The house turns a closed face to the street, but at the back it opens up towards Lake Mälaren. A semicircular section on pillars juts out like the bridge of a ship. There’s no big garden: nature was to be enjoyed as a view, Markelius believed.
Mot slutet går stråket över Mariakyrkans: Towards the end, the path crosses the churchyard of Mariakyrkan, where the beloved troubadour Evert Taube is among those buried.
Motellet hade 55 rum med 110 bäddar, i t: The motel had 55 rooms with 110 beds in two low wings. Its mast was topped by a three-spoke steering wheel and the neon words 'Motell', 'Bar' and 'Grill', visible from far away.
Motellet var påkostat, med inredning frå: No expense was spared on the motel, with furnishings from the NK department store, built-in radios and wall-to-wall carpets. The restaurant served both chips and béarnaise sauce, and in the early days there was evening entertainment.

No expense was spared on the motel, with interiors from the NK department store, built-in radios and wall-to-wall carpets. The restaurant served both chips and béarnaise sauce, and in the early days there was evening entertainment too.
Motionsanläggningen Fysiken vid Mossen h: The Fysiken sports centre by Mossen had a stormy start. Its predecessor, Plastiken, opened in 1969 – a tent of coated fabric held up by air pressure from inside – and that very autumn a storm almost brought it to a sorry end. Its replacement, Fysiken, opened in 1983, and for a few years students paid ten kronor extra in their term fees to help fund it.
Motorbranschens tekniska gymnasium start: The motor industry's technical upper secondary school opened in Flatås in 2002 and moved to the Högsbo industrial area in 2014. Students can specialise in electrified cars, bodywork or paintwork, among other options.

The motor industry's technical upper secondary school started in Flatås in 2002 and has been based in the Högsbo industrial area since 2014. Students can specialise in electric cars, bodywork or paintwork, among other options.
Motorhotell vid bensinmacken: A motel by the petrol station
Motorn som kom 1928 var en Polar Diesel: The engine fitted in 1928 was a 110-horsepower Polar Diesel. Fully laden, it gave Isolda a speed of eight knots.
Motorvägen bröt utsikten: The motorway cut off the view
Motorvägen som aldrig byggdes: The motorway that was never built
Motorvägen som slutade vara det: The motorway that stopped being one
Mulle Meckparken, ett par minuter härifr: A couple of minutes from here is Mulle Meckparken, created under the direction of the artist Tor Svae and opened in autumn 2008. Two years later it won Solna's urban environment prize. Nearby there's a small mystery, too: a runestone found by a spring in 1900 was last seen in 1908, and only a small fragment of it has turned up since.
Munkagången i tornet: The monks' passage in the tower
Munkebäckstorget fick sitt namn 1947 eft: Munkebäckstorget was named in 1947 after Munkebäcken, an old name for the Härlandabäcken stream. The monks – munkar in Swedish – were probably those of Nya Lödöse. Right beside it stand the ruins of the old Härlanda Church, a reminder of a parish that was merged into Nylöse parish as far back as 1528. Next to the ruin is Härlanda New Church.
Murar kvar på toppen: Walls still standing on the summit
Muraren som byggde Folkets hus: The bricklayer who built Folkets hus
Murarna fick sprängas: The walls had to be blown up
Murbruket har fått sitt namn från murnin: The Murbruket block ("mortar") is named after bricklaying and brick, like its neighbours Skalmuren, Pettringen, Rullskiftet, Löpskiftet, Hålkälen and Glasteglet – all masonry terms.
Muren följer en gammal bäck: The wall follows an old stream
Muren runt kolerakyrkogården: The wall round the cholera cemetery
Muren som sparade skogen: The wall that saved the forest
Museerna här lockar upp till en miljon b: The museums here draw up to a million visitors a year. The Swedish Museum of Technology, Tekniska museet, was named Museum of the Year in 2025 and once had Sweden's only 4D cinema, where the seats moved and the audience got gusts of wind, splashes of water and smells. The 1930 Stockholm Exhibition was held here, and in 1936 Tekniska museet became the first museum on the site, followed by the Maritime Museum in 1938.

The museums around here attract up to a million visitors a year. Tekniska museet, the National Museum of Science and Technology, was named Museum of the Year in 2025 and once had Sweden's only 4D cinema, where the seats moved and you were treated to gusts of wind, splashes of water and smells. In the grounds of the Ethnographic Museum is the teahouse Zui-Ki-Tei, the Dwelling of the Promising Light. Zui means both 'promising' and 'Sweden'.
Museet byggde på utgrävningar av slaget: The museum was based on excavations of the Battle of Stäket, fought between Russian and Swedish troops on 13 August 1719. An area of 735,000 square metres was searched and around 1,300 objects were found. In 2010 it became the first battlefield of its kind to be classed as an ancient monument.
Museet ligger i Hässelby villastads gaml: The museum is housed in the Hässelby villastad's old municipal hall from 1925, which also contained a police station and a post office. Today the basement holds a cobbler's workshop, a carpentry workshop and a police cell – while the other old cell is now a laundry room.
Museet på tunnelbaneperrongen: The museum on the metro platform
Museet som kungen aldrig fick: The museum the king never got
Museet som lämnade över fanan: The museum that handed over its colours
Museet öppnade 1987 i det gamla polishus: The museum opened in 1987 in Kvarnbyn's old police station, as a school museum for children. Since 2002 it has been housed in Strumpan, a former factory building at the top of the hill. You're free to browse its open storerooms.
The museum opened in 1987 in the old police station in Kvarnbyn, then as a school museum for children. Over New Year 2001/2002 it moved into Strumpan, a former industrial building.
Museets allra första inventarienummer, S: The museum's very first inventory number, SHM 1, is the Elisabeth Reliquary. It has an agate bowl from late antiquity, mounts from the 11th century and parts of two royal crowns from the 13th century. It fell into the hands of the Swedish army in 1632, when Marienberg in Würzburg was captured.
Museets huvudbyggnad är dagsverkstorpet: The museum's main building is Svensro, a labourer's croft that once belonged to Sanda farm on Dalarövägen. Threatened with demolition, the cottage was taken apart in 2001 and rebuilt here – with a grass-topped turf roof in place of its old tiles.
Museets samlingar rymmer över elva miljo: The museum's collections hold more than eleven million animals, plants, fungi, minerals and fossils from all over the world. Every year over four hundred visiting researchers come here.
Museets tyngsta föremål är tryckpressen: The museum's heaviest object is the printing press "Johanna" from 1897, built in Geisenheim on the Rhine. She measures 4.6 by 2.4 metres and weighs seven tonnes. Johanna is one of only two known presses of her kind in the world.
Museilägenheten är en trea på 85 kvadrat: The museum flat is an 85-square-metre, three-room home with oak parquet in the living room and vinyl tiles in the hall and kitchen. The kitchen had a fridge but no freezer. There was also a second toilet – with a bidet.
Museiparken är platsen för Stockholmsuts: Museiparken is where the 1930 Stockholm Exhibition was held. Afterwards the museums began to go up: first the National Museum of Science and Technology in 1936, then the Maritime Museum in 1938.
Museum i fabriken Strumpan: A museum in the Strumpan factory
Museum i gammal vagnhall: A museum in an old tram depot
Musikalen som fick ett hem: The musical that found a home
Musikvideo i det kaklade garaget: A music video in the tiled garage
Musikvideo i garaget: A music video in the garage
Musikvideon till Europes \"The Final Cou: The music video for Europe's "The Final Countdown" was filmed at two concerts in Solnahallen on 26 and 27 May 1986. Europe also features on the list of artists who have played here.
Mycket av inredningen finns kvar på andr: Much of the interior survives elsewhere. The Gothenburg City Museum holds, among other things, a 17th-century votive ship and the Ytterby cloth, an embroidered late-medieval linen cloth. Today's Ytterby Church has a pulpit from 1741 and the great bell from the old church.
Mycket av marken runt Hammarby sjö fanns: A hundred years ago, much of the land around Hammarby sjö lake simply wasn't there. In 1925 a new canal was blasted through the Danvik cliffs, and the lake dropped by about five metres. The newly exposed shoreline was built up with blasted rock, and an area of car workshops and small industries called Lugnet grew up on it. Today it's the site of Hammarby sjöstad, a new waterfront district built between 1994 and 2020.
Mycket i kyrkan kommer från den gamla me: Much of the church's furnishing comes from the old medieval church. The font dates from 1150–1250, the pulpit from 1689 and the altarpiece from 1724. The altarpiece spent some time in a museum before returning to Fässberg.
Mynt i striden om tre kronor: Coins in the battle over three crowns
Myran som barnen klättrar på: The ant children love to climb
Myrstugan stod ursprungligen vid Albysjö: Myrstugan originally stood by Albysjön lake in Vårby-Haga. The croft's naval boatmen were always called Myrman, and the last was Anders Gustaf Myrman, born in 1856. The croft ceased to be a boatman's croft in 1889.
Mysterna har ett namn med mystik, men fö: Mysterna sounds mysterious, but the explanation is down to earth: myst means a small bog. The village lies a kilometre west of the Göta älv river, and on its edge is the Svankälla wetland park. Created in 2003–2004, it's rich in birdlife, including marsh harriers, little grebes, lesser spotted woodpeckers, coots and mallards.
Mälarbadet tvingades stänga redan 1918 n: Mälarbadet had to close as early as 1918, as visitor numbers fell and more and more people had bathrooms at home. The baths became a potato store, and the pools were demolished in the 1960s. The Art Nouveau building facing Norr Mälarstrand still stands.
Mälarhöjdens IP anlades kring 1940 och v: Mälarhöjden sports ground was laid out around 1940 and was the first thing to be built in Fruängen. Just north-east of it stood the tenant croft of Wästertorp, which gave the district of Västertorp its name. It was demolished in the late 1940s.
Mälarhöjdens första skola var ett rött t: Mälarhöjden's first school was a two-storey red wooden house with white corners, opened in autumn 1905 as Johannisdal elementary school. It started out with three classrooms, is known today as Röda stugan – the Red Cottage – and is still used for teaching.
Mälarhöjdens skola är stadsdelens störst: Mälarhöjden school is the biggest in the district, with more than 1,100 pupils in 2016, from the reception year up to year nine. A little way off was Mälarbio – also known as Mälarhöjdsbio, Kvistoperan and later Färglådan – where regular film shows started in the spring of 1924 and carried on until January 1959. Today the old cinema building houses a school.
Mälarhöjdsbadet började anläggas i slute: Work on Mälarhöjdsbadet began in the late 1930s, with a jetty and a two-metre diving tower. Today there's a 400-metre sandy beach with changing huts, a café and a floating diving tower, all inside the Sätraskogen nature reserve.
Mälarskogens naturreservat, ett par hund: A couple of hundred metres away is the Mälarskogen nature reserve, protected since 2022, with the Mälarpromenaden walking trail running through it. The trail passes Hallundaröset, the second-largest known Bronze Age burial cairn in Södermanland. The cairn survived when the housing went up in the 1970s, thanks to its spot on a hilltop at the edge of the forest.
Mälarstrand runt hörnet: Lake Mälaren just round the corner
Mälarstranden här var förr full av sjökr: This stretch of the Lake Mälaren shore was once lined with lakeside inns. Arboga kök, near Sätra shipyard, was probably built in 1829 and burned down in 1967. In what is now the Sätraskogen nature reserve stood Råstock, an inn that ran from 1665 to 1813 – well into the days of the poet Bellman. Down on the shore, at Sätra varv, sailing ships and barges were repaired between 1878 and 1935, and several of the workers' houses still stand on the hill.
Mälaröarna består av 140 öar, kobbar och: The Mälaröarna islands number 140 islands, islets and skerries. Some former islands have joined together as the land has risen, and on Björkö there's a small nature reserve where many of the trees are more than 200 years old.
Mälaröarnas broar och vägar byggdes för: The bridges and roads of the Mälaren islands were built for horse-drawn vehicles. When heavy motor traffic began to appear just before the First World War, all cars had to be banned beyond Drottningholm.
Mälaröbussarnas nya hem: A new home for the island buses
Människofiskare i fönstren: Fishers of men in the windows
Mässan bakom stationen: The exhibition centre behind the station
Mässan grundades av Gustaf Dahlén, som 1: The trade fair company was founded by Gustaf Dahlén, who handed it over to his son Leif Dahlén in 1986. At its peak it employed about 90 people.
Mässan på en gammal sjö: A trade fair on an old lake
Mässan på sjöbotten: A fair on the lake bed
Mässan som flyttade från Sollentuna: The fair that moved from Sollentuna
Mässan var ett familjeföretag grundat av: The exhibition centre was a family business founded by Gustaf Dahlén, and the first fair was held in 1973. The crowd favourite was the annual 'Antik & Kuriosa' antiques fair, but there were also garden, crafts and angling fairs.
Mästaren Karl signerade: Signed by the master carver Karl
Mästaren och Margarita på väggen: The Master and Margarita on the wall
Måla tornet med telefonen: Paint the tower with your phone
Målningarna är signerade med arkitektern: The paintings are signed with the initials of the architects and of Thorvald Rasmussen, and dated 4/10 1890. Thorvald, Yngve's brother, was an artist whose speciality was tomtar – Swedish Christmas gnomes. Whether they actually painted them themselves isn't entirely clear, but the master painter Q.W. Bergqvist was involved in the work.
Måndalsfortet bestod av minst sex bunkra: The Måndal fort consisted of at least six bunkers and was meant to block the Kumla pass between Drevviken, Långsjön and Tyresö-Flaten. Here 120 men with four machine guns were to defend Stockholm. The trench, with its closely spaced firing slits, still runs along the cliff face.
Många av villorna i Näsbypark är från 19: Many of the villas in Näsbypark date from the 1940s and 1950s and are built in the functionalist style known in Sweden as funkis. The shopping centre opened on 8 October 1961 with around ten shops, a library and restaurants.
Många fornlämningar i området försvann v: Many ancient remains in the area were lost during the big building projects of the 1960s and 70s. There are records of a burial cairn between Siriusgatan 22 and 24, and of stone circles and stone settings east of Siriusgatan 96.
Många författare har vuxit upp eller ver: Many writers have grown up or worked around Hornstull – Nelly Sachs, Rudolf Värnlund, Irja Browallius, Ulf Lundell and Jonas Hassen Khemiri, to name but a few.
Många gator i Hässelby strand har fått n: Many streets in Hässelby strand are named after berries and fruit, like Persikogatan (Peach Street) and Måbärsstigen (Alpine Currant Path). Others refer to old crofts or the lie of the land.
Många gator i Skälby börjar med ord som: Many streets in Skälby start with words linked to space, such as Plutovägen, named after the dwarf planet Pluto. One of the schools is even called Neptuniskolan.
Många gator i Skälby har namn med koppli: Many of Skälby's streets have space-related names – Plutovägen, for instance, after the dwarf planet Pluto. That explains Neptunivägen, and one of the schools is called Neptuniskolan too.
Many of Skälby's streets have names linked to space, such as Plutovägen after the dwarf planet Pluto. Perhaps you've already guessed where Castorvägen got its name.
Många scener i Bergmans Det sjunde inseg: Many scenes in Bergman's The Seventh Seal were shot in and around Filmstaden in just 35 days. The witch-burning was watched by a large crowd, many of them children, from the tower blocks next door. The crew tried to keep the Råsunda buildings out of shot, but window reflections show up in a couple of scenes.

Many scenes in Bergman's The Seventh Seal were shot in and around Filmstaden, the film studios, in just 35 days. The witch-burning was prepared with the help of a fire brigade captain and watched by crowds of children from the high-rises next door. The crew tried to keep the buildings out of shot, but reflections from their windows can be seen in a couple of scenes.
Många säsongsarbetare var bryggerikullor: Many of the seasonal workers were bryggerikullor, "brewery girls" from the province of Dalarna. A full crate of 100 bottles weighed 90 kilos and took two women to lift. Even so, it was the best-paid heavy work available to women.
Många tyckte först att Poseidon var ful: At first, many people thought Poseidon was ugly and badly proportioned. According to the best-known story, Carl Milles was forced to shrink the god's genitals and took his revenge by shaping the fish so that, seen from the steps of the Concert Hall, it looks like a large penis. What really happened has never been confirmed.
Mårbacka byggdes 1966–1969 i prefabricer: Mårbacka was built in 1966–1969 from prefabricated concrete panels with red window frames. It has 900 office rooms, 80 per cent of them identical – yet, according to the jury of the Kasper Salin Prize, Sweden's top architecture award, every space still has its own identity.
Måtten var bestämda i förväg: The dimensions were set in advance
Möbelsnickare på riktigt utbildas en bit: Just up the road, real cabinetmakers learn their craft. At Malmstens, formerly the Carl Malmsten school, about 65 students study furniture design, cabinetmaking and upholstery in purpose-built workshops. The area was also once home to Bodal church, since demolished, and Bodals gård, the old farmhouse of an agricultural estate.
Mölla är ett sydsvenskt ord för kvarn, s: ‘Mölla’ is a southern Swedish word for mill, so Mölndal translates as Mill Valley. Long before industry arrived, salmon fishing and milling were the main trades at the falls.
Möln kommer av fornsvenskans mølna, kvar: Möln comes from the Old Swedish mølna, meaning mill, so Mölndal means roughly "mill valley". Over the years the name has been written Mølnadalaa (1406), Möldall (1530), Möllendall (1567) and Möllnedaalls (1638).
Mölndal betyder kvarndalen, och forsen s: Mölndal means 'mill valley', and the rapids that gave the town its name are just nearby. Mills have stood beside the rapids in Kvarnbyn, the Mill Village, since the 1300s, and until the 1600s most of them belonged to the Crown. The falls run for about 800 metres and drop some 45–48 metres. Later, the water powered local industry. Today Kvarnbyn is protected as a heritage area of national interest, and Mölndal City Museum sits right by the rapids.
Mölndal hade förr två järnvägsstationer,: Mölndal once had two railway stations, a lower one and an upper one. The lower station opened in 1888 on the West Coast Line, and its building was pulled down in 1977. The upper one, on the Borås Line, opened in 1894 in red brick and was demolished in 1983. Not far from here is the steep hill on Kvarnbygatan known as Mölndals kråka, Mölndal's Crow, or simply Kråkan.
Mölndal har fått sitt namn efter kvarnar: Mölndal is named after the mills that have stood by the rapids of the Mölndalsån river since the Middle Ages. Not far from here, at Göteborgsvägen 1, was the Grand cinema, which opened on Boxing Day 1938 and closed in 1966. A little further on is Mölndal travel centre, on a 500-metre bridge over the motorway, used by about 3.5 million passengers a year.
Mölndal var en kvarnby ända till 1930, d: Mölndal remained a mill village until 1930, the last year flour was ground here. More than sixty historic mills are known by name, and the old mill village survives with many listed buildings.
Mölndal är ett ställe för både simtag oc: Mölndal is a place for both swimming strokes and hoofbeats. A few hundred metres from here is Åbybadet, a swimming centre that opened in summer 2023 at a cost of 500 million kronor. In the same area is Åbytravet, Sweden's second-biggest trotting track, run by the Åby Travsällskap association. So you can take your pick: go for a swim yourself, or watch the horses race.
Mölndals sjukhus invigdes 1924 och ersat: Mölndal hospital opened in 1924, replacing a municipal infirmary, and is now part of Sahlgrenska University Hospital. The Möllan cinema in Mölndal's Folkets hus, the community hall, has been showing films since 1959. It has 289 seats and has been modernised and gone digital with the municipality's support.
Mölndals stadsmuseum ligger sedan 2002 h: Since 2002, Mölndal's city museum has stood at the top of the steep hill known as Mölndals kråka, the Mölndal Crow – and there's a café if you need a rest after the climb. Just below, the Mölndal rapids, Mölndalsfallen, rush past; in the 1800s their power drove cotton mills, paper mills and a weaving mill. Nearby Royens gata is named after three Roy brothers who emigrated from Stirling in Scotland.
Mölndalsfallen strax intill har gett sta: The Mölndal rapids, Mölndalsfallen, just next to us, gave the town both its food and its name: there was salmon fishing and there were mills, and Mölndal means something like Mill Valley. The steep hill east of the square goes by the name Mölndals kråka, the Mölndal Crow. The streets round here have their secrets too. Götaforsliden has been called both Glada gatan, Happy Street, and Tysta gatan, Quiet Street – nobody knows why – while Royens gata is named after three Roy brothers from Stirling in Scotland.
Mölnlycke station en bit härifrån har fl: Mölnlycke station, a little way from here, has moved house. It opened in 1894 about 350 metres east of where it is today, and moved to its present spot in 2003. The old station building was demolished in 2013. Today Västtågen regional trains stop here on their way between Gothenburg and Borås, on the Kust till kust line – the Coast-to-Coast line.
Mölnlycke växte fram kring Mölnlycke fab: Mölnlycke grew up around the Mölnlycke mills, founded in 1849 by Gustav Ferdinand Hennig from Saxony. Textiles were made here right up until the late 1990s, and today the old factory site is home to a wide range of businesses.
Mölnlycke växte fram som bostäder för ar: Mölnlycke grew up as housing for workers at the Mölnlycke mills, founded in 1849 by Gustav Ferdinand Hennig, an immigrant from Saxony. Textiles were made here right up until the late 1990s. Today the old factory site is home to a range of businesses.
Mölnlycke växte fram som bostäder åt arb: Mölnlycke grew up as housing for the workers at Mölnlycke fabriker, the mills founded in 1849 by Gustav Ferdinand Hennig from Saxony. Textiles were made here right up until the late 1990s. The white, castle-like wooden villa that his son-in-law Bruno Wendel built for himself has housed Wendelsberg folk high school since 1908.

Mölnlycke grew up as housing for the workers at the Mölnlycke mills. They were founded in 1849 by Gustav Ferdinand Hennig, an immigrant from Saxony, and made textiles right up to the late 1990s. Today the renovated factory site houses a range of businesses.
Mölnlycke är kyrkbyn i Råda socken, och: Mölnlycke is the church village of Råda parish, and the old Råda rural municipality was run from here. Although it's mostly villas, terraced and linked houses, the town is full of greenery, including the Rådasjön nature reserve and the Finnsjön outdoor recreation area. A handful of properties actually lie in Mölndal municipality.
Mölnlycke, centralort i Härryda kommun,: Mölnlycke, the main town of Härryda municipality, lies about ten kilometres south-east of Gothenburg and is made up mostly of detached, terraced and linked houses. Even so, it's a green place, with the Rådasjön nature reserve and the Finnsjön outdoor recreation area close by. The Mölndalsån river flows through the centre on its way from Landvettersjön lake to Rådasjön, and right in the middle of town is the little lake Massetjärnen.
Mölnlyckes centrum låg först vid järnväg: Mölnlycke's centre first sat by the railway station south of Massetjärn, but during the 20th century it moved to its present spot between Rådasjön and Massetjärn lakes. The station in turn moved in 2003 and now shares a site with the bus terminal.
Mörby centrum byggdes 1961 och glasades: Mörby centrum was built in 1961 and given a glass roof in 1977. In 2026, after ten years of rebuilding, it got a new name too: Danderyds Centrum. The metro ends here – Mörby centrum is the terminus of route 14 on the red line. The new look was designed by Gatun Arkitekter.
Mörby centrum byggdes 1961 som ett U-for: Mörby centrum was built in 1961 as a U-shaped open-air shopping centre facing south. Since its rebuild in 1977, when the metro got its terminus here, it has been an indoor centre on four floors.
Mörby centrum var aldrig tänkt som sluts: Mörby centrum was never intended to be the end of the line. The 1965 metro plan had the line continuing past Täby centrum to Hägernäs, but Täby preferred to upgrade the Roslagsbanan railway instead, and the plans were dropped.
Mörby centrum var aldrig tänkt som ändst: Mörby centrum was never meant to be the end of the line. Under the 1965 metro plan, trains would have carried on past Täby centrum to Hägernäs. But Täby preferred to keep and upgrade the Roslagsbanan railway, so the extension was cancelled.
Mörby station har legat på Roslagsbanan: Mörby station has been on the Roslagsbanan railway since 1906, and just south of it are the line's workshops, there since 1907 and designed by the architect Sigge Cronstedt. A few hundred metres away is Danderyd hospital, one of the county's emergency hospitals, where around 6,300 babies are born every year. That's a lot of people who took their first breath right here.

Mörby station has been on the Roslagsbanan railway since 1906, and just south of it are the line's workshops, there since the early 1900s and designed by the architect Sigge Cronstedt. A few hundred metres away is Danderyd Hospital, one of the county's emergency hospitals, where around 6,300 babies are delivered every year. So plenty of people took their very first breath here.

Mörbyleden slingrar sig mellan E18 och V: Mörbyleden winds between the E18 and Vendevägen and runs right past the Mörbyskogen housing area. Not far from here is Danderyd Hospital, one of the county's emergency hospitals, taking in around 90,000 emergency patients a year. And in May 2026 the nearby shopping centre changed its name from Mörby Centrum to Danderyds Centrum.
Mörk sålde restaurangen 1985 för att i s: Mörk sold the restaurant in 1985 to open La Grenouille instead. The Michelin-starred restaurant later went bankrupt when the recession hit Stockholm's top-end restaurants hard.
Mörtsjön är bara 2,3 meter djup och ligg: Mörtsjön is just 2.3 metres deep and lies 23.5 metres above sea level. Test fishing has turned up perch, roach, crucian carp and tench. The lake is part of the Tyresån river system.
Mörtvik nämns första gången i början av: Mörtvik is first mentioned in the early 18th century as a croft belonging to Trångsund manor. Thanks to its location, it grew into an independent farm. Parts of the main house may date from the 1680s.
Mörtviks gårds huvudbyggnad är ett panel: The main house at Mörtvik farm is a two-storey, timber-clad building with a mansard roof, and parts of it may date from the 1680s. A large garden runs down to Drevviken, where there's both a bathhouse and a summer house.
Mörtviks huvudbyggnad är ett panelat två: The main house at Mörtvik is a two-storey, board-clad building with a mansard roof. A large garden runs down to Lake Drevviken, and on the shore there's a bathhouse and a summerhouse.
Mötesstation på enkelspår: A passing place on a single track
Mötet 1603 handlade bland annat om rätte: Among the issues at the 1603 meeting was the right to use the Three Crowns coat of arms. Both Duke Karl, later King Karl IX, and the Danish king Christian IV took part.
NK och Tempo vid torget: NK and Tempo on the square
Nacka Forum öppnade den 1 mars 1989 och: Nacka Forum opened on 1 March 1989, replacing a makeshift centre in prefab huts that had served for many years. Right next to it, the leafy villa suburb of Storängen begins, where Villa Wållgren from 1907 has been judged irreplaceable. A stone's throw away is Villa Yngve Larsson, designed by Ragnar Östberg and built in 1907 for the future city commissioner and his wife, Elin, née Bonnier.
Nacka gymnasium höll först till i Eklide: Nacka upper secondary school started out in the premises of Eklidens skola. In 1976 work began on workshops for the vehicle and construction programmes, and once the expansion was finished the school moved into the new buildings. The main building dates from 1980 and was renovated in 1996.
Nacka kommun köpte villan 1950 och använ: Nacka municipality bought the villa in 1950 and used it for, among other things, a health insurance office, a junior school, evening classes and a youth hostel. In 1983 it was sold to private owners, and today it's protected as a listed building.
Nacka kyrka byggdes 1891 i nygotisk stil: Nacka Church was built in 1891 in the Gothic Revival style and stands in Nacka North Cemetery. Around it lies Birka, one of Nacka's oldest residential areas. The first houses went up in the 1880s for workers at the area's booming industries, such as Atlas Copco in Sickla and de Lavals Ångturbin, the steam turbine company, in Järla. The area has changed its name several times – it has been Järla, Järlaby and Birka-Järla.
Nacka musikskola startade 1934 och har s: Nacka Music School opened in 1934, growing out of an amateur orchestra that played in the gym at Järla School. To find more musicians they began teaching schoolchildren, and at first the lessons were paid for with film screenings, raffles and bazaars.
Nacka strand hette länge Augustendal. 18: Nacka strand was known for a long time as Augustendal. In 1899 the industrial pioneer J.V. Svenson bought the area, and by 1916 his engine works employed 500 people, making it one of the biggest workplaces in Sweden. After going bankrupt in 1922, the company was taken over by Handelsbanken. Offices and homes followed in the 1980s, and in 1988 the area got its current name, Nacka strand. Down in the marina, since 1995, Carl Milles' sculpture God the Father on the Rainbow has been sending an arc of water out over the Saltsjön bay.
Nacka ström rinner genom en sprickdal i: Nacka ström tumbles through a rift valley in three sets of rapids from Lake Dammtorpssjön down to Lake Järlasjön. In just 500 metres the water drops 18 metres – and it was that power that drew the early industries here.
Nackanäs värdshus med sin åttkantiga sjö: With its octagonal lakeside pavilion, the Nackanäs inn was a popular day-trip destination for a full century. From 1863 the steam launch S/S Nackanäs called at its jetty, but when the inn lost its licence to serve spirits in 1913, the passengers stopped coming and the boat service ended.

Namnberedningen oroade sig inte bara för: The naming committee didn't just worry about the name sounding like kista, coffin. They also pointed out it might be mispronounced: "The genuine pronunciation has a long i and a grave accent."
Namnberedningen ville att villastaden sk: The naming committee wanted the garden suburb to be called Tussmötet, but both the property company and the homeowners objected. The compromise was the invented name Stureby, after Sten Sture the Younger and the Battle of Brännkyrka.
Namnen nedre och övre kom 1925 och syfta: The names 'lower' and 'upper' date from 1925 and reflect the fact that the upper station sat about 40 metres higher than the lower one, with a walk of roughly 900 metres between them. Before that, the lower station was called Fässberg for a while.
Namnet 79&Park kommer från adressen Sand: The name 79&Park comes from the address, Sandhamnsgatan 79, and the Gärdet park. The building steps up to ten storeys, its roof is made up of many small squares at different heights, and the pleated facade is partly clad in cedar. It came third in Stockholm Building of the Year 2019.
Namnet Akalla kommer från fornsvenskans: The name Akalla comes from the Old Swedish akarlar – men who lived by a river. That river is Igelbäcken, which in the Bronze Age was part of a sea inlet running from the Baltic via Edsviken to Säbysjön. The village is first mentioned in writing in 1323.

The name Akalla comes from the Old Swedish akarlar, men who lived by a river. The river is Igelbäcken, which in the Bronze Age was part of an inlet stretching from the Baltic to Lake Säbysjön. The village is mentioned in writing as early as 1323.
Namnet Allmänna vägen syftar på att väge: The name Allmänna vägen – the public road – refers to the fact that it was open to all and maintained with public funds. In 1771 and 1818 it was called Stora wägen, and in 1850 Stora Gatan or Allmänna Wägen.
Namnet Arendal kommer av det närliggande: Arendal takes its name from the nearby hill Ardalsberget. What the first part, Ar-, means is disputed: it may be the Old Swedish arna, eagle, or the man's name Arne. Until 1967 the name was usually spelled Ardal.
Namnet Arendal kommer från det närbelägn: Arendal takes its name from the nearby Ardalsberget hill, but no one knows for sure what the first part means. It may come from the Old Swedish 'arna', meaning eagle, or from the man's name Arne. Until 1967 the name was usually spelt Ardal.
Namnet Arendal kommer från det närliggan: Arendal takes its name from the nearby Ardalsberget hill, but the meaning of the first part is disputed: it's either the Old Swedish 'arna', eagle, or the man's name Arne. In the 1500s and 1600s it was spelt in various ways, including Arndal, Arnedal and Ahrendal.
Namnet Askim kommer av trädet ask och or: The name Askim comes from ask, the ash tree, and hem, home, in the sense of a district. The oldest form appears in an Icelandic text from the first half of the 1200s, as Askheims herað.
The name Askim comes from the ash tree (ask) and the word hem, meaning home or district. Its oldest form, "Askheims herað", appears in an Icelandic text from the first half of the 13th century.
Namnet Asperö kommer av trädet asp och f: Asperö takes its name from the aspen tree, and it's recorded as Aspærø as early as around 1300. An old nickname for the islanders was ‘Krabbor’ – the Crabs. The island has its own church, consecrated in 1990.
Namnet Bagarmossen kommer från hovbagare: The name Bagarmossen – 'the baker's bog' – comes from the royal baker Nils Lychou, who leased the bog in the 1790s. It was drained and cultivated, and the bakers owned and leased flour mills at Nacka Ström.
Namnet Beckomberga betyder ungefär de so: The name Beckomberga means roughly "those who live by the stream" and was written bœkneberghœ in 1347. In the Middle Ages the village consisted of three farms: Södergården, Mellangården and Norrgården – the South, Middle and North farms.
Namnet Beckomberga betyder ungefär ”de s: The name Beckomberga means roughly 'those who live by the stream' and has been known since the 14th century, when it was written bœkneberghœ.
Namnet Beckomberga är gammalt. Det äldst: Beckomberga is an old name. Its earliest recorded form, Bäknaberga, dates from 1319, and it means 'the people who live by the stream'. In the Middle Ages the village was made up of three farms: Södergården, Mellangården and Norrgården – South, Middle and North Farm. In the 1950s the Runda husen, the Round Houses, went up on the corner of Bällstavägen and Spångavägen as homes for the nurses at Beckomberga Hospital.
Namnet Blåsut kommer från en krog vid et: The name Blåsut – roughly 'blow out' – comes from a tavern at a forester's lodge, and in the 19th century it was a common name for windswept spots. The metro station opened in 1950, and in 2008 it was given artwork by Ann Edholm: speed stripes in black and white tiles. A little further on is Framtiden 1, 'the Future', from 1915. In the building next door – fittingly called Nutiden, 'the Present' – was the Enskede Kvarn cinema.
Namnet Brevik betyder \"breda viken\". P: The name Brevik means 'the broad bay'. On Lidingö's oldest known map, from 1661, the farm is marked with a tower and flag – the symbol for a manor.
Namnet Bromsten tros syfta på ån vars vå: The name Bromsten is thought to refer to a river whose spring floods 'roared', and to a cluster of boulders – almost certainly the area's ancient hillfort. Bromsten's first known owner was the nobleman Johannes Ingevaldsson, in 1291.
Namnet Bräcke kommer av fornsvenskans br: The name Bräcke comes from the Old Swedish word brækko, meaning a broad slope or hillside. A stone's throw away is Bräcke diakoni, the foundation set up in 1923 as Göteborgs diakonissanstalt to train deaconesses. A short walk off is Bräcke cemetery, laid out during the cholera epidemic of 1834, when the disease reached Sweden through Gothenburg.
Namnet Cyklopen, efter de enögda jättarn: The name Cyklopen – after the one-eyed giants of Greek myth – came from a large round window on the front of the first building. It was built of wood around shipping containers so it could be packed up and moved, and was also known as the Container Castle. It even had a drawbridge.
Namnet Drakenberg kommer från värdshuset: The name Drakenberg comes from the Draken ('Dragon') inn, which Melchior Schipman opened here in 1669 when the first Liljeholmen bridge was built. After his death two rivals fought a bitter feud over the inn, and Draken closed as early as 1681.
Namnet Drevviken gällde först bara den s: The name Drevviken originally applied only to the southern bay, from which firewood was shipped from the Hanveden forests to Stockholm. The lake itself was probably called Vendeln or Vendelsjö, until the bay's name took over.
Namnet Ersta Villastad fick diakonissorn: The name Ersta Villastad provoked protests from the deaconesses of the Ersta Deaconess Institution. So people went looking for historical events and thought of the Battle of Brännkyrka, where Sten Sture the Younger drove out Christian II.
Namnet Fornboda speglar tidens intresse: The name Fornboda reflects the period's interest in antiquity and folk culture, but the building itself was modern, with pale rendered walls and large windows. The local heritage society's logo, a Viking ship, was drawn in 1931 by the artist Einar Nerman.
Namnet Frölunda kan komma från en lund p: The name Frölunda may come from a grove on Toftaåsen ridge where the Norse god Frey, also known as Frö, was worshipped. An offering stone has survived outside the church sacristy. Another theory points to the fertile land by the water.
Namnet Frölunda kan komma från vikingati: The name Frölunda may come from Viking Age settlements on the Toftaåsen ridge, where there was a grove in which the Norse god Frey, also known as Frö, was worshipped. An offering stone survives outside the vestry of Västra Frölunda church.

The name Frölunda may come from Viking Age settlements on Toftaåsen ridge, where there was a grove for worshipping the Norse god Frey, also called “Frö”. An offering stone survives outside the vestry of Västra Frölunda church.
Namnet Gnistängen kommer från gnistsända: The name Gnistängen, "spark meadow", comes from the spark-gap transmitter, an early kind of radio transmitter. In 1911 the Naval Administration built a wireless telegraph station here; from 1916 it was called Göteborg Radio, and it kept in touch with ships at sea until 1948.
Namnet Grötö har inget med gröt att äta: The name Grötö has nothing to do with gröt, the porridge you eat. It comes from the West Swedish dialect word gröt, meaning 'stones, rubble', a reference to the coarse shingle and big boulders on the west side of the island.
Namnet Gubbängen är känt sedan tidigt 16: The name Gubbängen – roughly “Old Men's Meadow” – has been known since the early 17th century, but its origin is uncertain. One theory is that it comes from three old men who lived at the croft in 1627: Jösse, the soldier Simon and the crofter Erik.
Namnet Gårda dyker upp redan 1550 och är: The name Gårda goes back to at least 1550 and is simply a grammatical form of the word gård, meaning farm. A stone's throw away is Hästskosömsfabriken, the old horseshoe-nail factory, whose buildings from around 1890 and 1900 are now protected by the state as a heritage site. And Drakegatan is named after the Drake brickworks, founded by Anders Drake in the mid-1700s.
Namnet Hallonbergen kommer troligen av a: The name Hallonbergen – 'Raspberry Hills' – probably comes from the raspberry bushes that once grew all over the area. Where the district stands today there used to be a farm called Freden, where tobacco was grown.
Namnet Hisingen anses svårtolkat, men de: The name Hisingen is considered hard to interpret, but the most common explanation is that "his" means to split or cut off – making it roughly "the island the river's arms have cut off from the mainland". Until the Middle Ages the island was also divided by a narrow strait where Kvillebäcken stream flows today.
Namnet Hisingen tolkas oftast som \"den: The name Hisingen is usually interpreted as "the island cut off", separated from the mainland by the arms of the river. Until the Middle Ages the island was also divided by a narrow strait through Kvilledalen, where the Kvillebäcken stream flows today.
Namnet Hosve, som betyder grå, är bara k: The name Hosve, meaning 'grey', is known only from the two Råsta runestones. Read the stones together and a family emerges: Jobjörn and Gyrid and their children Holmsten, Hosve, Sigrid and Kättilö.
Namnet Husby tyder på en lång historia:: The name Husby hints at a long history: in the Viking Age and Middle Ages, a 'husby' was a farm where the king's official lived. West of Husby gård lie Iron Age burial grounds, and beside one of the oldest roads across Järvafältet stand two 11th-century runestones, Husbystenen and Granbyhällen.

The name Husby points to a long history: in the Viking Age and Middle Ages, a husby was a farm where the king's official lived. West of Husby farm there are Iron Age burial grounds, and along one of Järvafältet's oldest roads stand runestones from the 11th century.
Namnet Hässelby nämns första gången i en: The name Hässelby first appears in a deed of sale from 1344, spelled Elisby. There was already a village here in the 1300s, and the mound east of the palace driveway is a Viking Age burial ground.
Namnet Högmora betyder ungefär högt belä: The name Högmora roughly means a high-lying, dense, grassy conifer forest. It comes from two crofts, Lilla and Stora Högmora, both recorded since 1689.
Namnet Högsätra betyder högre belägen än: Högsätra means 'the higher meadow', and the name comes from an area with three 19th-century villas. The complex was built to provide public services for every age group, with a school, sports facilities, healthcare and a pharmacy. Högsätrahuset, which once housed Lidingö hospital, is due to be demolished to make way for the new Kärnan neighbourhood.
