Namnet Hökälla betyder ungefär \"källan: The name Hökälla means roughly “the spring by the mounds”. The first part comes from an old plural form of hög, meaning mound. In 1388 the name was written Hauga kiœldu.
Namnet Hökälla betyder ungefär ”Källan v: The name Hökälla roughly means "the spring by the mounds" – the first part is an old plural of hög, mound. In 1388 it was written Hauga kiœldu.
Namnet Hönö kommer från det fornvästnord: The name Hönö comes from the Old West Norse word hein, meaning whetstone. It refers to the island's smooth, rounded rock slabs – look out for them when you get there.
Namnet Hönö kommer från fornvästnordiska: The name Hönö comes from the Old West Norse 'hein', meaning whetstone, a nod to the island's smooth, rounded rocks. The island is also known for Hönökaka, a flat bread that has been baked here since 1904.
Namnet Hötorget är känt sedan 1640-talet: The name Hötorget, the Haymarket, has been known since the 1640s. A square on the same site already appeared on Anders Torstensson’s 1637 plan for Norrmalm, making it Sweden’s first axial square – one laid out on a street’s central axis. The trade in hay and straw moved away as early as 1856.
Namnet Islinge kommer av ”Ist” och ”ling: The name Islinge comes from 'Ist' and 'linge', a reference to the ice lingering longer in the bay than in the water between Stockholm and Lidingö.
Namnet Jonsered kommer av mansnamnet Joh: The name Jonsered comes from the man's name Johan and the word 'ryd', meaning a clearing. It is first recorded in 1526, spelt 'Iogenszredh'.
The name Juringe first appears in 1538. Scholars aren't entirely sure, but most of the evidence suggests it comes from iur, an old word for wild boar.
Namnet Jättesten kommer från de stora st: The name Jättesten – “giant stone” – comes from the huge boulders on the hill behind the houses. The next street along has an amusing story behind its name. A C Lindblads gata was named in 1954 after Anders Christensen Lindblad, a newspaper editor and pioneer of the labour movement. The naming committee wanted to call it Lindbladsgatan, but at the city council meeting Hugo Höglund pointed out that everyone used to call Lindblad simply “A C” – and so A C it was.
Namnet Kallebäck betyder bäcken med kitt: Kallebäck means 'the stream with the kettle', and the name first appears in 1496. The district sits on Gothenburg's south-eastern edge, hemmed in by major roads. It's also home to Ostkupan, 'the Cheese Dome' – a 14-storey student block from 1964 with a nickname that's appetising, to say the least. A little further on is a cholera cemetery from the epidemic of 1866, now protected as an ancient monument.

The name Kallebäck means 'the stream with the kettle' and first appears in 1496. The district lies on Gothenburg's south-eastern edge, between the big main roads. It's also home to Ostkupan, 'the Cheese Dome', a tall student block from 1964 with a rather appetising nickname. A little further on is a cholera cemetery from the 1866 epidemic, now protected as an ancient monument.
Namnet Kjulak, på runsvenska Kiulakʀ, fi: The name Kjulak – Kiulakʀ in runic Swedish – also appears on another runestone, Sö 339. The stone here is granite and a metre wide.
Namnet Klippan anses komma från berget L: Klippan is thought to take its name from the rock Lilla Klippan, also called Skinnareklippan, which partly formed the harbour itself. Klippan is already mentioned in Karl's Chronicle from the 1450s. Its neighbour, Stora Klippan, was levelled long ago.
Namnet Kornhall syftar enligt ortnamnsfo: According to place-name experts, the name Kornhall refers to korn, barley, and hall, a place where barley was loaded or unloaded. The name is recorded from 1774.
Namnet Korsvägen dök upp första gången 1: The name Korsvägen – "the crossroads" – first appeared in the newspaper Götheborgska Nyheter in 1785. In 1915 it was renamed Johannebergsplatsen after the neighbouring Johanneberg country estate, but in 1929 Korsvägen was made official again.
Namnet Kortedala kommer från ett torp st: Kortedala takes its name from a croft just south of where Runstavsgatan meets Minutgatan, recorded in 1827 as Korta dahlen. It refers to exactly that – the short valley – as opposed to the nearby Djupedalen, the deep valley.
Namnet Krokslätt syns första gången 1397: The name Krokslätt first appears in 1397, spelt Krokslætho. It's thought to mean "the plain that bends" or "the plain by the bend", krok meaning a curve or turn.
Namnet Kråkan förekommer redan 1662, och: The name Kråkan – the Crow – crops up as early as 1662, and the road can be seen on a copper engraving from 1678. The name may refer to Kråkeberget hill, or perhaps to Kråkekvarnen, a mill the slope ran past. Over the years the street has also been called Lerskalla and Regeringsgatan, among other things.
Namnet Kumla kommer troligen från kummel: The name Kumla probably comes from 'kummel', a cairn used as a sea or boundary marker that stood here as far back as prehistoric times. The name first appears in writing in 1460, or possibly 1470.
Namnet Kummelby kommer av ordet kummel,: The name Kummelby comes from kummel, a cairn marking a grave. The farm existed back in prehistoric times, and by Helenelundsskolan school there's a burial ground with 17 low graves from around 600–1000.
Namnet Kummelby kommer från ordet kummel: The name Kummelby comes from 'kummel', a cairn marking a grave. Beside Helenelund School is a burial ground with 17 low graves dating from about AD 600 to 1000.
The name Kummelby comes from kummel, a cairn of stones marking a grave. By Helenelundsskolan there's a burial ground with 17 low graves from around AD 600 to 1000.
Namnet Kungens kurva kommer från en alld: The name Kungens kurva – 'the King's Bend' – comes from a genuinely royal trip into a ditch. On a Saturday afternoon, 28 September 1946, King Gustaf V's chauffeur ran off Södertäljevägen road and got stuck in a water-filled ditch, and the press was there in no time. Today the area is one of the biggest shopping centres in Scandinavia, and together with Skärholmen centrum it pulls in 30 million visitors a year.
Namnet Kungssten låter gammalt, men det: Kungssten ("King's Stone") sounds like an old name, but it was simply made up and has no historical basis. It's sometimes spelt Kungsten too.
Namnet Kvarnskogen passar bra: en bit bo: The name Kvarnskogen, 'Mill Wood', is well chosen: a little way off, on the north-east shore of the Edsviken inlet, there has been a mill for more than 400 years. The first one was abandoned some time in the late 1500s – nobody knows why – but a new one soon went up on the same spot. The mill and the sawmill beside it were in use until the 1950s and are now a museum.
Namnet Käppala klingar bekant för många: For many people the name Käppala rings a bell for quite another reason: Käppalaverket, the sewage treatment plant that opened in 1969 and is considered one of the most efficient in the world. Not far from here is Käppalaställningen, too – an anti-aircraft position from the Second World War, rededicated in 1994 as a memorial to Stockholm's air defences.
Namnet Landala brukar knytas till koppar: The name Landala is usually linked to the master coppersmith Bengt Landin, who owned the farm from 1782. But researcher Sören Skarback suggests that Elisabeth van Eijk, visiting in 1659, called a pretty valley here Laandal – after the Dutch laan, meaning avenue.
Namnet Lindholmen kommer från en lindbev: Lindholmen takes its name from an island covered in lime trees, which was cut off from Hisingen right up until 1855. The channel around it was called Kvillen, and Sannegårdshamnen harbour is what remains of it.
Namnet Lindome kommer av lyng, som betyd: The name Lindome comes from ‘lyng’, meaning heather, and ‘hem’, meaning a dwelling or farm.
Namnet Långpannan är troligen en skämtsa: The name Långpannan is probably a tongue-in-cheek pun. The first part comes from the many local place names beginning with Lång-, like Långbro, Långsjön and Långängen, while 'pannan' refers to the still for making brännvin, Swedish schnapps. The inn was opened in 1769 by Magnus Askerqvist and his wife.
Namnet Marievik har använts sedan 1930-t: The name Marievik has been in use since the 1930s. It's a Swedish version of Maryvik, one of four estates that once stood here. Right next door was Liljeholmen station, which opened to passengers on 1 December 1860 and handled goods until 1998. Up on Liljeholmsberget hill stands the old parish hall from the 1920s. Since 2003 Nordiska Musikgymnasiet, a music school, has filled its halls with music.
Namnet Masmo bär på en gammal rädsla: fö: The name Masmo hints at an old fear. The first part, 'mas', is thought to be a taboo word for wolf – a way of avoiding saying the real name – and the whole name is said to mean something like 'the forest where the wolf has been seen'. Just a stone's throw away, Myrstuguberget clings to the hillside above Albysjön lake. It was completed in 1986 and was the architect Ralph Erskine's first housing area in the Stockholm region. The name comes from Myrstugan, a boatswain's croft that was moved when the houses were built.
Namnet Masmor, känt sedan 1600-talet, be: The name Masmor, known since the 17th century, probably means the spruce forest where the wolf roams. Mo or mor means spruce forest, and mas is a noa-name for the wolf – a euphemism used to avoid saying the animal's real name.
Namnet Murbruket hör ihop med grannkvart: The name Murbruket (Mortar) goes with the neighbouring blocks, all named after bricklaying terms: Skalmuren, Pettringen, Rullskiftet, Löpskiftet, Hålkälen and Glasteglet.
Namnet Mysterna kommer av ordet myst, en: The name Mysterna comes from 'myst', a word for a small bog. The village, mostly newly built villas and terraced houses, lies a kilometre or so north of Hisings Kärra and has counted as part of the Gothenburg urban area since 2015. On its outskirts is the Svankälla wetland park, a great spot for birds, where coots and mallards are among the residents.
Namnet Måns kärr har feltolkats i namn s: The name Måns kärr ("Måns's marsh") has been misread as "moon" in names such as Restaurang Månskäran and Hotel Månen. The only tangible traces of the croft's land are a few fruit trees beside the E4/E20 motorway.
Namnet Månskär har inget med månen att g: The name Månskär has nothing to do with the moon (månen). It comes from one of the first tenants, Måns, and the word kärr, meaning fen. So Restaurang Månskäran and Hotel Månen are based on a misunderstanding. Incidentally, the crofter Carl Öhman gave up tobacco to get his tax reduced.
Namnet Mölndal kommer från det fornsvens: The name Mölndal comes from the Old Swedish 'mølna', meaning mill, so it simply means 'mill valley'. More than sixty historical mills along the rapids are known by name. The last flour was ground in 1930.
Namnet Mölnlycke betyder ungefär inhägna: The name Mölnlycke roughly means 'the enclosure by the mill'. The first part comes from mölna, a mill, just as in Mölndal, while lycke means a fenced-in piece of land. In 1609 it was spelled Molnelyckie.
Namnet Nacka, skrivet Nackaa år 1505, in: The name Nacka, spelled Nackaa in 1505, contains the word nacke in the sense of a rocky height. It refers to the steep rock edges along the Nackaån stream.
Namnet Nysätra betyder äng på utmark, oc: The name Nysätra means a meadow on outlying land, and a map from 1744 marks the headland as pasture. Villa Nysätra at Nackanäsvägen 16, built in 1873 in the Swiss chalet style, still stands. In 1923, villa plots sold for between 2.64 and 4.95 kronor per square metre.
Namnet Nysätra betyder äng på utmark. Nä: The name Nysätra means a meadow on outlying land. When the house plots were advertised in 1923 they cost between 2.64 and 4.95 kronor per square metre, and demand was high. The blocks were given names like Hasseln, Granen, Necken and Neptun (the Hazel, the Spruce, the Water Sprite and Neptune).
Namnet Oakhill kommer från det brittiska: The name Oakhill comes from the British envoy, Admiral Sir Thomas Baker, who had his summer residence on the oak-covered hill. Prince Wilhelm's palace was a wedding present, and the building costs of 700,000 kronor were paid by the Russian imperial family.
Namnet One Tonne Life kommer av målet: e: The name One Tonne Life comes from the goal: for six months, a family would try to get their emissions down to one tonne of carbon dioxide per person per year while living a normal life. At the start they were at 7.29 tonnes. Experts from Chalmers University helped with the measurements.
Namnet One Tonne Life kommer från ett fö: The name One Tonne Life comes from an experiment: a chosen family with children would live normally for six months while cutting their emissions to one tonne of carbon dioxide per person per year. When the project began, the family was at 7.29 tonnes.
The name Rinkeby means "rich man's village". It started out with three farms and was one of the largest villages in the parish. The post road between Stockholm and Turku also passed through here.
Namnet Rinkeby betyder \"rik mans by\",: The name Rinkeby means "rich man's village", and it was one of the largest farms in the parish. People have lived here since the Iron Age, a couple of hundred metres north of Danderyd church.
Namnet Rissne kommer av Risö, som platse: The name Rissne comes from Risö, as the place was called in the Viking Age. The burial mounds here suggest that the upper classes lived in the area – among the finds were goshawks, which only the nobility used for falconry.
Namnet Rud är gammalt, belagt redan 1495: The name Rud is old. It's recorded as early as 1495, spelled Rudh or Rwdh, and it means a clearing. A short way from here is Ruddalens IP, a football ground for 3,000 spectators, with artificial turf since 2003. The first match was played on 27 April 1985, when Västra Frölunda IF took on IFK Malmö.
Namnet Ruda lär komma av ett äldre ord f: The name Ruda is said to come from an old word meaning to clear land. Another theory is that the two lakes were once full of ruda, crucian carp.
Namnet Sikreno dyker upp första gången 1: The name Sikreno first appears in 1829, when the forester's lodge Stocksberg, or "Sikreno", was sold to Captain Axel Wilhelm Schmidt. In 1915 John Klingspor had Villa Stocksberg built, designed by Thor Thorén. Today the villa is housing for older people.
Namnet Sinar, pappan som stenen restes e: The name Sinar, the father the stone was raised for, is extremely rare. Apart from here, it appears on just one other runestone, U 830.
Namnet Skarpa har oklart ursprung. En fö: Nobody quite knows where the name Skarpa comes from. One theory is that it refers to hard clay soil that was difficult to work with medieval tools. Another suggests Skarpnäck comes from the Scharfeneck estate in northern Germany, to which the Oxenstierna family had ties.
Namnet Skarpa kan syfta på hård lerjord: The name Skarpa may refer to hard clay soil that was difficult to work with medieval tools. According to one theory, the name Skarpnäck comes from the Scharfeneck estate in northern Germany, to which the Oxenstierna family had ties.
Namnet Skogås saknar historisk anknytnin: The name Skogås has no historical roots and was probably invented by town planners in the 1930s: skog (forest) and ås (ridge) describe the landscape. Länna, on the other hand, is an old name derived from land, meaning a landing place on Drevviken lake.
Namnet Skra Bro sägs komma av det skrapa: The name Skra Bro is said to come from the scraping noise of sledge runners on the bare ground during a thaw. The old bridge over the Osbäcken stream is still here right next to us, but these days it's just a footbridge between the park-and-ride and a supermarket. Cars now cross a bigger road bridge north of the roundabout.
Namnet Skra Bro sägs komma från det skra: The name Skra Bro is said to come from the scraping sound the sledge runners made against the ground during a thaw.
Namnet Skvaltan minner om en sjö vars ut: The name Skvaltan recalls a lake whose outflow through Vikdalen once powered several 'skvaltkvarnar', simple horizontal water mills. A little further away in Storängen is Villa Waern, built in 1905 for the merchant Charles Waern to designs by Torben Grut and rated irreplaceable. Close by is Villa Kallstenius, designed for the artist couple Gottfrid Kallstenius and Gerda Roosval-Kallstenius.
Namnet Sköndalsbro är känt sedan 1699. D: The name Sköndalsbro has been known since 1699. It comes from a bridge (bro) just west of the farm, where the road to Dalarö passed. The croft belonged to Stora Sköndal.
Namnet Slotz bakken finns redan 1478. På: The name Slotz bakken is recorded as early as 1478. In the Middle Ages the area south of Tre Kronor Castle was known as Sanden, ‘the Sand’ – a broad gravel slope running down to the Saltsjön. In the 1470s it was also called Stallbacken, after the butchers’ stalls that stood here.
Namnet Spånga finns i skrift redan år 13: The name Spånga turns up in writing as early as 1300, as ‘apud Ecclesiam spangar’. It belonged to the old church village and simply means footbridges – narrow plank walkways. The station is on the Mälarbanan line, just over eleven kilometres from Stockholm Central. A little further on is Svandammen, the Swan Pond, a park with a swimming spot that's popular with teenagers and families alike.
Namnet Spånga kommer från den gamla kyrk: The name Spånga comes from the old church village and is recorded as early as 1300. It's simply the plural of 'spång', a footbridge or plank bridge.
The name Spånga comes from the old church village and is recorded as early as 1300. It's the plural of spång, a simple plank footbridge.
Namnet Stensättra är känt sedan 1460, oc: The name Stensättra has been known since 1460, and the first part, Sten, probably refers to the nearby Stensättra hillfort. Around 1900 the farm became a model farm. The cultural landscape here is considered one of Huddinge's best preserved.
Namnet Stuvsta, skrivet Studzta, dokumen: The name Stuvsta, spelled Studzta, was first recorded in 1353. In the late Middle Ages Stuvsta consisted of four homesteads. Until 1908 Stuvsta farm was owned by the Lagerbielke family, and in 1910 plots began to be sold off for owner-built homes.
Namnet Stuvsta, skrivet Studzta, finns d: The name Stuvsta, written Studzta, is first recorded in 1353. It is thought to come from stutar, meaning oxen. In the late Middle Ages Stuvsta consisted of four farmsteads.
Namnet Säve kommer av äldre sæva och sæv: The name Säve comes from the old words sæva and sæver, meaning calm and still – the same root as sävlig, “sluggish”. It refers to the river's gentle flow. The Säveån meets the Göta älv at Gullbergsvass, about 350 metres east of the Tingstad Tunnel.
Namnet Tegeludden är belagt sedan 1649 o: The name Tegeludden is recorded as early as 1649, for a head forester's house on Royal Djurgården – but nobody knows how it got the name. On the street stands Philipshuset, the Philips Building, built in the early 1960s as Svenska Philips' headquarters and warehouse. Today the Administrative Court sits in the old offices, and TV4 makes television in the warehouse.
Namnet Tensta antas komma av tena, ett s: The name Tensta is thought to come from tena, a kind of fishing gear, and sta, an enclosed area. The village is first mentioned in 1538, when it consisted of two farms, both owned by Spånga church.
Namnet Tensta tros komma av tena, ett sl: Tensta probably takes its name from tena, a type of fishing gear, and sta, meaning an enclosure. The village first appears in the records in 1538, when it was made up of two farms owned by Spånga church.
Namnet Tingstad finns belagt från 1388 o: The name Tingstad is recorded as early as 1388 and comes from the village where the local court, the 'ting', used to meet. Tingstadsvassen was one of Gothenburg's three great reed marshes, known together as the town marshes. The land was dredged and drained in 1885–1898.
Namnet Trolldalen har använts sedan 1700: The name Trolldalen, the Troll Valley, has been in use since the 18th century. It referred to the ravine in the middle of the woods on Henriksdal hill, a rift valley that easily sets the imagination running. Up on the hill is Henriksdalsringen, built between 1964 and 1969 to designs by the brothers Erik and Tore Ahlsén, who liked the result so much they moved in themselves. Nearby, in Finnboda, the Finnboda shipyard was in operation from 1884 to 1991.
Namnet Tulebo kan lura en. Den gamla tät: The name Tulebo can be misleading. The old village of Tulebo lies north-east of Lake Tulebosjön, but newer housing areas on the south-west side of the lake have been given Tulebo names too, such as Tulebo Villastad and Tulebo Park – even though they're actually in the villages of Hultet and Stretered. The Nilento Studio recording studio is also nearby.
Namnet Tussmötet har fantasifulla förkla: There are some colourful explanations for the name Tussmötet. One says the gnomes held their meetings here; another that 'tuss' or 'tusse' means wolf, making it the wolves' meeting place. The croft was previously called Pettersborg.
Namnet Täby Park är inte helt nytt. Komm: The name Täby Park isn't entirely new. The municipality launched it back in the 1980s for the industrial estate on Kemistvägen, north-west of the racecourse, and has now reused it for the whole new district.
Namnet Ullevi betyder ungefär ”Ulls egen: Ullevi means roughly “Ull's estate or temple”. In Norse mythology, Ull was the god of games and play.
Namnet Vantör är riktigt gammalt. Den me: The name Vantör is truly old. It was the name of the medieval parish, but after a fire in the 1400s its church became known as Brännkyrka, the Burnt Church. Today's Vantör church is in Högdalen, a short walk away. Högdalen centre also used to have a cinema, the Rondo, which showed films from January 1961 right up to May 1983.
Namnet Viksjö har en lång historia: det: The name Viksjö goes back a long way. It's a corruption of an original Vikhusa, which appears on a runestone as early as the 11th century. In 1963 a building consortium began developing the land, and today Viksjö is mostly houses from the 1960s, 70s and 80s. Not far off is Hummelmoraberget, a hill where old beach ridges show that the sea once reached all the way up here.
Namnet Viksjö är äldre än gården. Det dy: The name Viksjö is older than the farm. It appears on an 11th-century runestone, making it the oldest place name in Järfälla recorded in writing. The stone says that 'Knut in Vikhusum had the stone raised and the bridge made' in memory of his parents and siblings. The farm itself is recorded from 1734, and the neighbourhood around it was built in the 1970s.
Namnet Västra kyrkogården kom troligen p: The name Västra kyrkogården – the Western Cemetery – probably came about in the 1910s, when yet another burial ground, Skogskyrkogården, was laid out in Kungälv. A new way of telling them apart was needed.
Namnet Vårberg kom till 1961. Det är nyt: The name Vårberg was coined in 1961. It's new, but inspired by the Viking Age Vårdberg, a lookout where beacon fires were lit when enemy ships approached.
Namnet betyder troligen vägkrök: The name probably means a bend in the road
Namnet blinkar åt Ullevi: A name that winks at Ullevi
Namnet dyker upp första gången 1550 som: The name first appears in 1550 as Fiskebäch, and means simply "the stream where people fish". The stream is still there, but it now runs in a culvert underground, almost parallel with Stora Fiskebäcksvägen, out to the sea.
Namnet dyker upp första gången 1694, som: The name first appears in 1694, as Möndahls Bro. The roads to Gothenburg and Kungsbacka ran along the west bank of the river, so anyone heading up to the mill village of Mölndals Kvarnby had to cross over here.
Namnet finns belagt 1421 som Kolarid, se: The name is first recorded in 1421 as Kolarid, later as Kollarudh and Kålleredz. Its meaning is uncertain, but one theory is that the first part comes from the name Kolle, which may refer to someone with no hair.
Namnet finns belagt från 1421 som Kolari: The name is recorded as Kolarid as early as 1421. Its meaning is unclear, but the most common theory is that the first part comes from the name Kolle, which may refer to someone without hair.
Namnet finns belagt redan 1609, då som M: The name is recorded as early as 1609, as Molnelyckie. The first part comes from mölna, 'mill' – just as in Mölndal – while the ending -lycke means 'enclosed land'.
Namnet finns i ett tingsprotokoll från 1: The name appears in court records from 1356 as Hudhastum. It's thought to come from the personal name Hudhe and the Old Swedish word for a place – roughly 'Hudhe's places'.
Namnet finns i källorna redan 1609, då s: The name crops up in records as early as 1609, as Molnelyckie. The first part, Möln-, means mill – just as in Mölndal – and -lycke means an enclosed piece of land.
Namnet finns i skrift redan 1609, som Mo: The name is on record as early as 1609, as Molnelyckie. 'Möln-' means mill, just as in Mölndal, and '-lycke' means an enclosed field.
Namnet från Botvidslegenden: A name from the legend of St Botvid
Namnet från ett tåg i Portugal: A name found on a train in Portugal
Namnet har sin förklaring: här låg Hande: There's a reason for the name: this is where Handen's old folkpark, or people's park, used to be. What's left today is Haninge kulturpark, where local groups look after the last of the old buildings – among them RoJteatern, in the old Folkets hus community hall. Every June the park comes alive with music, theatre and dance during the Kulturparksfestivalen. A stone's throw away is Handens museum och smedja, a museum and smithy with goats and hens, where schoolchildren go on trips back in time.
Namnet har stavats på många sätt genom å: The island's name has been spelt in many ways over the years. In 1597 it was written "Kiöbstedsöen", and from 1691 comes the spelling "Tiösöö". A map of the year 1277 shows the island as belonging to the Danish king and to Halland.
Namnet har tolkats som \"stig till betes: The name has been interpreted as 'path to the cows' pasture'. Gångsätra farm was demolished in 1981, and all that remains is one of its stone gateposts, preserved as a memorial near the entrance to the Willys supermarket.
Namnet hittades på en runsten: A name found on a runestone
Namnet kan vara en ordlek: The name may be a pun
Namnet kommer av en lindbevuxen ö som än: The name comes from a linden-covered island that was separated from Hisingen until 1855 by a canal, the Kvillen. Sannegårdshamnen harbour is a surviving stretch of that old canal. Today the area has a new avenue of lindens, Lindholmsallén.
Namnet kommer från Djurgården: A name that comes from Djurgården
Namnet kommer från Stuvsta gårds väderkv: The name comes from the windmill of Stuvsta gård, which once stood on Kvarnberget, the Mill Hill. The mill itself is long gone, but several millstones survive, and the municipality has put one of them on display on Gymnasievägen. One Saturday evening in 1908, a train came off the rails on the bend north of Huddinge station. Nobody was killed, and the accident was immortalised on two postcards.
Namnet kommer från Viggbyholms gård. Vig: The name comes from Viggbyholm manor. Viggby is a corruption of Vikby, 'the village in the bay', and refers to an older settlement in the inlet where the marina is today.
Namnet kommer från det närliggande Ardal: The name comes from nearby Ardalsberget hill. Whether the first part, Ar-, means eagle (from the Old Swedish arna) or comes from the man's name Arne is still debated. Until 1967 it was usually spelt Ardal, though Arndal, Arnedal and Ahrendal also turn up.
Namnet kommer från en krog som nämns red: The name comes from an inn mentioned as early as 1668. In fact there were three – Stora, Lilla and Gamla Tallkrogen – along the old country road to Dalarö. The district could just as well have been named after the crofts of Sophem or Pottmyran.
Namnet kommer från en skans som Karl XIV: The name comes from a skans, a small fort, that Karl XIV Johan had built as a playground for his son Oscar I. It stood where the Håsjö bell tower is now. The oldest of Skansen's roughly 140 buildings is the Vastveit storehouse from the 14th century.
Namnet kommer från en våg. Här vägdes jä: The name comes from a set of scales. This is where iron shipped out through Gothenburg's harbour was weighed, including iron from the ironworks of Värmland. In the 1780s the city's iron weigh-house was moved to a plot just north of today's Järntorget, 'the Iron Square', which was named after it. The men who carried the iron bars settled in the blocks round about. The weigh-house itself was pulled down long ago.
Namnet kommer från ett torp som 1545 skr: The name comes from a croft recorded in 1545 as Granhambertorp, roughly where the hospital stands today. In 1688 the crofter and his family owed 107 days' labour a year to Flemingsberg farm.
Namnet kommer från gården Eriksdal, som: The name comes from Eriksdal farm, which stood roughly where the Eriksdalsbadet swimming baths are today. In the 1820s it was owned by Erik Almgren, who probably gave the place its name. In the 1880s the city bought the land to build the Eriksdal waterworks.
Namnet kommer från gården Östby söder om: The name comes from Östby farm, south of Lake Ösbysjön. In the early 1400s Nils Jönsson Oxenstierna, founder of the Djursholm estate, acquired the farm in an exchange with the nuns of St Clare's Convent.
Namnet kommer från hovbagaren Nils Lycho: The name comes from the royal baker Nils Lychou, who leased the bog from the von Schantz family of Skarpnäck farm in the 1790s. Back then it was known as Pungpina mosse, among other names. It was drained and turned into farmland.
Namnet kommer från idrottsföreningen Hel: The name comes from the sports club Hellas, founded in 1899 by the vicar Ernst Klefbeck. Football was played by the lake – and even water polo. The club's own members built the big lodge, which opened in 1945.
Namnet kommer från torpet Majro, eller M: The name comes from the Majro croft, also called Mariero, which belonged to Herrängen farm. It stood near where Bordsvägen meets Knektvägen and was demolished in the mid-1940s.
Namnet kommer troligen från Ryssviken ne: The name probably comes from Ryssviken, the bay below, which may share its origins with Ryssviken by Djurgården, where Russian ships were allowed to anchor a short way from Stockholm. In 1915 an Iron Age spearhead of iron was found in Ryssviken.
Namnet sitter i fasaden: The name is on the facade
Namnet skrevs 1377 Thoresby och kommer f: In 1377 the name was written Thoresby, and it comes from a settlement by the church. It combines the man's name Tore with by, meaning village or farm.
Namnet skrevs 1388 Harondastaf. Förleden: In 1388 the name was written Harondastaf. The first part comes from Harund, ‘the rocky one’ – the name of the peninsula the parish sits on. The ending, ‘stav’, may refer to steep ground or to a raised cult marker.
Namnet skrevs 1388 Thorlandum och innehå: In 1388 the name was written Thorlandum, combining the name of the god Thor with the word ‘land’. So Torslanda means roughly Thor's land.
Namnet skrevs 1403 Lyngemä och betyder u: In 1403 the name was written Lyngemä, meaning roughly ‘the settlement by the heather’. At times the vast heathlands produced large amounts of heather honey, and beekeeping was an important sideline.
Namnet skrevs 1421 Kollarud. Efterleden: In 1421 the name was written Kollarud. The second part means a clearing, while the first may be the man's name Kolle – "the one without hair" – or the word kulle, a hill.
Namnet skrevs Askym år 1489 och kommer f: Written Askym in 1489, the name comes from the village of Askim. The first part is 'ask', the ash tree, and the second is 'hem', meaning a home or farm.
Namnet skrevs Bakka år 1388 och kommer f: The name was written Bakka in 1388 and comes from the church village. It refers to the slope – the rise on which the church stands.

The name was written Bakka in 1388 and comes from the church village. It refers to the rise where the church stands – the rest of the parish is flat country between the Göta älv river and Kvillebäcken.
Namnet skrevs Danarö 1291 och innehåller: In 1291 the name was written Danarö and probably contains the words for 'Danish' and 'rör', a burial cairn. A local historian has suggested instead that 'dana' means marshland and 'ör' a pile of stones.
Namnet skrevs Harondastaf år 1388. Förle: In 1388 the name was written Harondastaf. The first part comes from Harund, 'the rocky one', the name of the peninsula the parish sits on. The second part, 'stav', may refer to a steep rock formation or a raised cult marker.
Namnet skrevs Thorlandum år 1388 och kom: In 1388 the name was written Thorlandum, after the church village. It combines the name of the god Thor with the word land.
Namnet som undvek en förväxling: A name chosen to avoid confusion
Namnet som var för tungt: A name too hard to say
Namnet står på en runsten: The name is on a runestone
Namnet syftar på ett läge närmare havet: The name refers to a position closer to the sea than Kungälv. As early as the 1140s, a copy of the Borgarting church law mentions 'Kungahälla ytri', and in 1353 the place was called 'Yttra by'.
Namnet syns först i mantalslängden 1786: The name first appears in the 1786 tax register and was probably the idea of county governor Anders Rudolf du Rietz, who had fought as a major in the Seven Years' War. That same year he granted the croft here to the watchman Eskil Svensson.
Namnet syns första gången 1887 som ”Falu: The name first appears in 1887 as 'Falu Torg å Gullbergsvass'. In the past there was some greenery here, along with a football pitch and a playground.
The name first appears in 1887 as 'Falu Torg å Gullbergsvass'. There used to be greenery, a football pitch and a playground here. The square has just one street number: 1.
Namnet syns som Röda bärget på en karta: The name appears as Röda bärget (the Red Hill) on a map from 1733 and probably refers to the reddish granite the area rests on. In the mid-1800s the district was still rural, and wolves were said to roam close to the city and to be seen in the Rörstrand pastures in winter.
Namnet uttalas med kort a: Rammbergsvall: The name is pronounced with a short ‘a’: Rammbergsvallen. That’s because the first part, ‘ram’ or ‘ramn’, is an old word for raven.
Namnet Älvsborg betyder troligen borgen: The name Älvsborg probably means the fortress at the mouth of the river. In west Swedish place names, öse means a river mouth, as in Lödöse. In 1366 the name was written Eluesborgh.
Namnet Ängby kommer från Engiaby, \"byn: The name Ängby comes from Engiaby, "the village by the meadows". In ancient times Lake Ängbysjön filled the valley where Bergslagsvägen runs today. All that's left of the lake is Råcksta träsk.
Namnet Ängby kommer från Engiaby, 'byn v: The name Ängby comes from Engiaby, 'the village by the meadows', first mentioned in 1315. In the Middle Ages there were four farms in Ängby, three of which belonged to the Helgeandshuset hospital in Stockholm.
Namnet Ålkistan är belagt sedan 1640-tal: The name Ålkistan has been recorded since the 1640s and comes from an ålkista, an eel trap, in the stream between Brunnsviken and Saltsjön. A map from 1709 also shows a watermill and a miller's cottage here.
Namnet Öjersjö har inget med någon sjö a: Despite appearances, Öjersjö has nothing to do with a lake (‘sjö’). The name means Øiar's clearing, after a settler who cleared land here in the 15th century. Over time its origin was forgotten and the word ‘sjö’ crept in.
Namnet, belagt från 1647, kommer från ti: The name, recorded from 1647, comes from the ships' masts made in the harbour. On 4 October 1647 thirteen mast-cutters were granted burghership and set up in business for themselves, and that day is usually counted as Masthugget's birthday. Right up to the 1660s the area was officially called Haga.
Namnets förled kan motsvara det fornsven: The first part of the name may correspond to the Old Swedish name Fly, but it could also come from fly or gungfly, meaning marshland. Well into the 1950s, the stream towards Beckomberga would still flood after snowy winters.
Namnkommittén ville att gatan skulle het: The naming committee wanted to call the street Klippgatan, but the popular choice, Royens gata, won in the end. John Roy bought the waterfall and its mill rights in 1803 and built the white manor house.

The street-naming committee wanted to call this Mjölnaregatan, "Miller Street". But the manager of the Götafors cotton mill backed the popular local name Götaforsliden instead – and in 1926 that's what it became.
Nationalmuseum: Nationalmuseum, Sweden's national museum of art
Nationalmuseum står på det som en gång v: Nationalmuseum, Sweden's museum of art and design, stands on what used to be a tiny island of its own, Kyrkholmen. When the city gave the land for the museum in 1846, the head of construction, Johan af Kleen, simply filled in the canal separating it from Blasieholmen – without asking anyone's permission. The museum was finished in 1866 and is the largest art museum in Sweden. Just outside stands Theodor Lundberg's sculpture The Foster Brothers; its twin is in Copenhagen.
Nationalteatern hade under många år på 1: For many years in the 1970s the band Nationalteatern was based at the youth centre on Selma Lagerlöfs torg. In their song Barn av vår tid the square is called EPA's square, after the EPA department store that stood here at the time.

For many years in the 1970s the band Nationalteatern was based at the youth centre on the square. The square features in their song 'Barn av vår tid', though there it's called 'EPAs torg', after the department store that stood here at the time.
Natten efter att Frantz Zinck dött 1690: The night after Frantz Zinck died in 1690, high-ranking gentlemen arrived at two in the morning and sealed the house – and a few nights later they broke the seal and carried off bedding and a cabinet. They were probably looking for papers about Zinck's dealings with the Crown.
Natten till den 7 februari 1993 eldhärja: On the night before 7 February 1993 the old church was gutted by fire, leaving only the outer walls standing. It was insured, and that same autumn the church council voted unanimously to build a new one on the same spot.
Nattklubben i Tre Remmare hette Club Moa: The nightclub in Tre Remmare was called Club Moatjé. As early as 2006 the space was split and the burger chain Max took over part of it, and in January 2007 the venue was given a warning under the Alcohol Act before its licence was revoked.
Naturhistoriska museet och blåvalen: The Natural History Museum and its blue whale
Naturhistoriska riksmuseet: Naturhistoriska riksmuseet, the Swedish Museum of Natural History
Naturhistoriska riksmuseet och Cosmonova: Naturhistoriska riksmuseet, the Swedish Museum of Natural History, and Cosmonova
Naturhistoriska riksmuseet, Sveriges stö: Naturhistoriska riksmuseet, the Swedish Museum of Natural History, is Sweden's largest museum complex. It was founded in 1819, and its present building, designed by Axel Anderberg, opened in 1916. Next door is Bergianska trädgården, the Bergius Botanic Garden. Its biggest building is the Edvard Anderson greenhouse from 1995, named after the wholesaler who left money in his will for a winter garden of Mediterranean plants. The nearby Ekhagen neighbourhood is one of the few built entirely in the functionalist style.
Naturligt rinner cirka 75 procent av Göt: Left to itself, about 75 per cent of the Göta älv's water flows out through Nordre älv. When the flow drops below 300 cubic metres per second, the gates start to rise so that more water goes down the Gothenburg branch.
Naturligt rinner ungefär 75 procent av G: Left to itself, about 75 per cent of the Göta älv river's water flows out through the Nordre älv. When the flow drops below 300 cubic metres per second, the barrier begins to rise, and at 150 it's fully raised. Most of the water then takes the Gothenburg branch instead.
Naturområdet Långsjöhöjden når 73 meter: The Långsjöhöjden nature area reaches 73 metres above sea level, making it the second-highest natural point in the City of Stockholm after Vikingaberget. From the top you can look out over Huddinge and south-west Stockholm.
Naturområdet Långsjöhöjden på sjöns norr: The Långsjöhöjden nature area on the north side of the lake rises to 73 metres above sea level, making it the second-highest natural point in the City of Stockholm.
Naturreservatet Välen ligger några minut: The Välen nature reserve is a few minutes' walk away, at the far end of the Askimsviken inlet. It has a wetland museum, a bird-watching platform, a nature trail and a 'time trail' through history. The reserve was set up in 2014 and covers about 68 hectares, and within it are a Bronze Age cairn and stone setting.
Nedanför Albyberget låg Svartlötens ting: Below the Albyberget hill lay the Svartlöten assembly site, where a 'ting', the local court and assembly, was already being held when Stockholm was founded in the 13th century. The site gave its name to the Svartlösa hundred and later to Svartlösa district court.

Below Albyberget lay the Svartlöten thing site, an assembly and court where meetings were held as far back as the founding of Stockholm in the 1200s. Just north of Albykistan, a 70-metre stretch of the ancient Tingsvägen road that led there still survives.
Nedanför Baggeby, ner mot Lilla Värtan,: Below Baggeby, down towards Lilla Värtan, is Lidingsberg, one of the best-preserved 19th-century summer houses on Lidingö. Owned by the Wedberg family, it has the island's largest private plot, about six hectares, and is reached by Lidingsbergsvägen, the shortest named road on Lidingö. The buildings have been listed since 1954.
Nedanför Fridhemsplan, i kvarteret Slagg: Below Fridhemsplan, in the Slaggen block, stands the building called Fridhem. It has also earned the nickname Tegeltraven – 'the brick stack'.
Nedanför Konserthuset växer en ask som k: Below the Concert Hall grows an ash known as Framtidsträdet, the Tree of the Future. It was planted in 1986 for the first Future Meeting organised by the Globträdet association, and serves as a multicultural meeting place.
Nedanför Sankt Pauli kyrka står fontängr: Below Sankt Pauli kyrka, St Paul's Church, is Anders Jönsson's fountain group Elementens kamp, 'the Struggle of the Elements', unveiled on Swedish Flag Day in 1930. It originally stood on Olskrokstorget, but had to move when that square vanished to make way for the approach roads to the Tingstad tunnel. Along Redbergsvägen is Flamman, a 684-seat cinema that showed films from 1935 to 1982 and is now a listed building.
Nedanför Tahultsdrumlinen ligger lilla A: Below the Tahult drumlin – a ridge left by the ice sheet – lies little Agntjärnen, a pond just 6.5 metres deep. The slope down to the water is protected as the Gallhålan nature reserve: a large, unbroken oak wood on hilly ground, where wood vetch, wood violets, wood anemones and liverleaf grow. Out on the pond, look out for mallard, goldeneye, goosander and tufted duck.
Nedanför Torsvik vid Lilla Värtan står T: Down below Torsvik, on the Lilla Värtan strait, stands Torsvik lighthouse. Built in 1950 and taken out of service in 1980, it now marks the finish line for the Lidingö Runt sailing race. Where the old Lidingö bridge came ashore there's a small waiting shelter designed by Ivar Tengbom – so exposed to the wind that it earned the nickname the Temple of the Winds. The Torsvikshöjden housing area from the 1940s is seen as an early example of the planned post-war neighbourhood.
Nedanför bassängbadet finns sedan sommar: Since summer 2018 there's been a small cold-water bathing spot in Lake Ulvsundasjön just below the outdoor pool, with a café next door. The cold bath is free, while you pay to use the 50-metre pool.
Nedanför bassängbadet, med sin 50-meters: Below the outdoor pool, with its 50-metre basin, there has been a smaller cold-water bath out in Lake Ulvsundasjön since summer 2018, with a café next to it. The cold bath is free for everyone, while the pool charges admission.
Nedanför husen står Acke Oldenburgs verk: Below the buildings stands Acke Oldenburg's work Detta är mitt Huddinge (This is my Huddinge): two curved walls covered in 210 square metres of hand-painted tiles. Installed in 1990, it depicts scenes from his life in Huddinge.
Nedre Söderby är en knuttimrad parstuga: Nedre Söderby is an 18th-century log-built 'parstuga', a traditional double cottage, with an unusual layout: you have to walk through a small chamber to reach the kitchen. Today the local handicraft society holds open days here, with crafts for sale and coffee, and in summer cows and sheep graze the meadows.

Nedre Söderby is an 18th-century log-built double cottage with an unusual layout. To reach the kitchen you had to pass through a small chamber, often the bedroom of the old farmer and his wife, which was kept warm by the chimney stack of the bread oven.
Nelly Sachs park är uppkallad efter den: Nelly Sachs Park is named after the German writer and Nobel laureate. It fits right in with the surrounding streets, named after Pär Lagerkvist, Harry Martinson and Eyvind Johnson – all winners of the Nobel Prize in Literature.
Neon, bingo och ett kvartersnamn: Neon, bingo and a block name
Neonskylten som kom tillbaka: The neon sign that came back
Neonskylten som startade en rörelse: The neon sign that started a movement
Ner mot Lilla Värtan ligger Kappsta natu: Down towards Lilla Värtan is the Kappsta nature reserve, dotted with the foundations of unusual houses. One of them belonged to Wisingska villan, where Raoul Wallenberg was born; today the memorial Attachéväska R.W., Attaché Case R.W., marks the spot. Nearby stood Villa Nidaros, Trondheim's pavilion at the 1897 Stockholm Exhibition. It was shipped here to serve as a summer house and burned down after being struck by lightning in 1960.
Nere i Klippans kulturreservat ligger An: Down in the Klippan heritage area is Ankarsmedjan, the old anchor forge. Anchors and chains were made here for the ships of the Swedish East India Company, which used Klippan as its outer harbour. The building is said to date from the 1770s. Its grey stone walls were one ell and nine inches thick – around 80 centimetres – and there was a cooper's workshop here too.
Nere vid Lilla Värtan ligger Ekhagens st: Down on Lilla Värtan is Ekhagen beach, also known as Lappis Beach. The student village of Lappkärrsberget – ‘Lappis’ for short – is close by. It's Stockholm's largest, with more than 3,000 student flats built in 1968–1970, and the streets have fitting names such as Professorsslingan, Amanuensvägen and Forskarbacken – Professor's Loop, Assistant's Road and Researcher's Hill.
Nere vid Lilla Värtan ligger Lidingsberg: Down by Lilla Värtan is Lidingsberg, one of the best-preserved 19th-century summer houses on Lidingö. Owned by the Wedberg family, it sits on the island's largest private plot – about six hectares – and is reached by Lidingö's shortest named road, Lidingsbergsvägen. The area is also crossed by Södra Lidingöstråket, a walking trail of about 18 kilometres that runs all the way from Gåshaga jetty to Stortorget, the main square in Gamla stan, the Old Town.

Down by the water of Lilla Värtan is Lidingsberg, one of the best-preserved 19th-century summer residences on Lidingö. It belongs to the Wedberg family and sits on the largest private plot on Lidingö, at about six hectares. The way in is along Lidingö's shortest named road, Lidingsbergsvägen, and the buildings have been listed since 1954.
Nere vid Magelungen står en stor röd trä: Down by Lake Magelungen stands a large red wooden villa from 1916–1917, built as a children's home. Its name, Rödkinda – ‘Red Cheek’ – reflects the hope that the fresh air would give the children rosy cheeks. The villa sits on a hill, with a south-facing slope running down to the lake. The old Farsta gymnasium building is now used by Farsta grundskola, a primary school, and the Adolf Fredrik music classes.
Nere vid vattnet står en sjöbod, byggd t: Down by the water stands a boathouse, built half of brick and half of wood. It was once a smokehouse for fish caught in the lake. Today it’s used by Marieborg Boat Club, and the meadow running down to the lake was once a large garden.
Neumüller lät bygga det stora rödmålade: Neumüller had the big red-painted granary built north-west of the farmhouse. Today it's considered one of Stockholm's best-preserved farm buildings from the second half of the 1800s.
Ni står på era egna gravar: You stand upon your own graves
Niclas Jönsson kom från Lux och Bon Lloc: Niclas Jönsson came from Lux and Bon Lloc, and Daniel Höglander from Esperanto, Vassa Eggen and Operakällaren. Their restaurant was at Svartlösavägen 52 in Långbro and served luxury tasting menus.
Nidaros var ritad i fornnordisk stil med: Nidaros was designed in Old Norse style, with dragon scrolls, runic inscriptions and a turf roof. The house was prefabricated, designed by the Norwegian Christian Thams, who also created Norway's pavilion at the 1889 World's Fair in Paris. After the exhibition it was taken apart and rebuilt here.
Nietzsches dödsmask i tornet: Nietzsche's death mask in the tower
Nilento Studio grundades 1993 av musiker: Nilento Studio was founded in 1993 by the musicians Lars and Jenny Nilsson and began life as a mobile studio. Avishai Cohen, Linda Lampenius and Bohuslän Big Band are among those who have recorded here, and since 2013 the studio has also run its own record label.
Nils Dahlgrens Palme-minnesmärke från 19: Nils Dahlgren's memorial to Olof Palme, from 1989, is a large openwork heart in mirror-polished stainless steel that reflects its surroundings. The plinth bears words such as "Alla folks frihet" and "Allas lika värde" – freedom for all peoples, equal worth for all. The original plan was a rotating globe.
Nils Ericsons gamla sluss finns kvar i s: Nils Ericson’s old lock survives in its original form. Since a rebuild in July 2024 it has served as a fish pass, so fish can make their way between Lake Mälaren and the Saltsjön.
Nils Ericsonsplatsen är uppkallad efter: Nils Ericsonsplatsen is named after Nils Ericson, who built Sweden's first main railway lines – and was the brother of the inventor John Ericsson. Right beneath us, Västlänken, the West Link, a railway tunnel under central Gothenburg, is being built.
Nils Ericsonterminalen ritades av norske: Designed by the Norwegian architect Niels Torp, the Nils Ericson Terminal forms a 150-metre waiting hall made entirely of glass and steel. The floors are limestone, and the benches and kiosks pale oak. When it was built, reversing cameras for the buses were a rarity.
Nils Georg Sörensen, som gatan är uppkal: Nils Georg Sörensen, after whom the street is named, lived from 1833 to 1917. Today the street is lined by Rosendal School, the church, and terraced and semi-detached houses.
Nils Tesch ritade samtidigt en egen vill: At the same time, Nils Tesch designed a villa for himself next to Mölna gård, but it turned out too expensive and he never took possession. The villa at Utsiktsvägen 2 was also meant for him, but he didn't move there either.
Nio hus och en glaskorridor: Nine buildings and a glass corridor
Nisse Zetterberg utgick från vikingatida: Nisse Zetterberg took Viking-age finds from local excavations and blew them up into glittering gold mosaics. In real life the Rinkeby goat is no bigger than a ten-krona coin. The central vault also has mosaics of two runestones.
Noaks ark på skolväggen: Noah's Ark on the school wall
Nobelkommittéer i LO-borgen: Nobel committees in the LO building
Nobelpalatset skulle ha tornat upp sig f: The Nobel Palace was meant to tower over Djurgårdsbrunnsviken bay from a rocky ledge about 20 metres up. The great hall was first planned for 1,200 people, but the Academy of Sciences and Karolinska wanted more, so Boberg drew alternatives for 1,600 and 2,000.
Nobelparken är ett arboretum där det fin: Nobelparken is an arboretum with a specimen of almost every tree that grows wild in Sweden. One of the exceptions is the mountain birch, as the climate here is too different from that of the mountains.
Nobels far byggde flottbron: Nobel's father built the pontoon bridge
Nobis byggdes 1711 som tyghus åt sjöarti: Nobis was built in 1711 as an arsenal for the naval artillery, about 150 metres north of where it stands today. In 1818 the building was moved and became an inn called Norra Kasernen (the North Barracks), renamed Nobis in 1870.
Nockeby nämns första gången år 1400 som: Nockeby is first mentioned in 1400 as Nokkaby, probably after a man with the Old Swedish name Nokke. The manor of Åkeshov grew out of the village in the 17th century, and the City of Stockholm bought it in 1904.
Nockeby is first mentioned in 1400 as Nokkaby. The village is thought to be named after a man called Nokke, an Old Swedish name. In the 17th century the Åkeshov manor estate grew out of the village.
Nockeby torg är cirka 250 meter långt oc: Nockeby torg is about 250 metres long and ends at the green space of Brålunden. It’s lined with smooth-rendered two-storey buildings designed by Edvin Engström, where you’ll still find a cobbler, a tailor and a hairdresser.
Nockeby torg, en kort promenad härifrån,: Nockeby torg, a short walk from here, was laid out in the early 1930s as a long, narrow piazza – a classic garden-suburb square. Tram 12 had already been extended this far in the autumn of 1929. Less romantic, but impressive all the same, is the Bromma sewage treatment plant nearby. Since 1989 its treated water has flowed through a tunnel some twelve kilometres long, under Solna and Stockholm, all the way out to the Saltsjön waters at Kastellholmen.
Nockebybanans hållplats här har ett spår: The Nockebybanan tram stop here has a crossover where the line switches from right-hand to left-hand running. That makes for an easier connection with the metro at Alvik, which runs on the left.
Nora gård nämns första gången 1310. Namn: Nora farm is first mentioned in 1310. The name comes from ‘nor’, a narrow strait that once lay south of the farm. The 18th-century watermill by Kvarnparken is still standing.
Nora gård nämns första gången i skrift å: Nora gård is first mentioned in writing in 1310, but the place is older than that. In the bedrock is Norahällen, a runic inscription from the 11th century. The name Nora comes from the word nor, a narrow strait that once lay south of the farm.
Norahällen ristades vid 1000-talets mitt: The Nora rock was carved in the middle or second half of the 11th century. Björn, son of Finnvid, had it cut in memory of his brother Olev. The inscription declares the farm to be their ancestral land and inheritance, making the rock a kind of Viking Age title deed.
Nordens modernaste storkök: The Nordic region's most modern kitchen
Nordens största sjukhus 1834: The largest hospital in the Nordic region, 1834
Nordic Wellness Arena är en nyckelfärdig: Nordic Wellness Arena is a turnkey arena, assembled from ready-made parts shipped to the site. Identical arenas exist in Paderborn and Offenbach, but in Sweden it's one of a kind.
Nordiska Musikgymnasiet är inriktat på k: Nordiska Musikgymnasiet specialises in classical music and was founded in 2000 by the pianist and piano teacher Monika Kowalska. It has room for 60 students from all over Sweden, the Nordic countries and the rest of Europe.
Nordost om Skärholmens gård ligger en fo: North-east of Skärholmen farm lies a Viking Age hillfort. It sat strategically on a rocky knoll near the ancient sea route to Helgö and Birka. The name Skärholmen itself comes from the farm by Lake Mälaren.
Nordost om centrum står Triangelhuset fr: North-east of the centre stands Triangelhuset, the Triangle House, from 1955, with a unique triangular floor plan. It was designed by the German architect Werner Taesler. Cylindrical tunnels take pedestrians under the main roads.
Nordväst om Hällsvik låg Batteri Torslan: North-west of Hällsvik stood Batteri Torslanda, also known as the Hjuvik battery. Today the old military area is open for rambling, but the remains of the heavy coastal artillery are still plain to see.
Nordväst om bebyggelsen ligger den lilla: North-west of the houses lies little Mörtsjön lake, with a 2.5-kilometre floodlit trail around it. It's now linked up with Enebyberg's ten-kilometre trail.
Nordväst om sjön stod förr Sisjöns vatte: North-west of the lake stood the Sisjön water tower, a landmark visible from far away. In June 2006 the area between Sisjön and Oxsjön was hit by a severe forest fire.
Norge mitt i Västerort: Norway in the heart of Västerort
Norr och söder om Stockholm byggdes två: Two almost identical facilities were built north and south of Stockholm: Elefanten (the Elephant) in Sollentuna and Vargen (the Wolf) in Huddinge. That way, crisis management could move between them and feel instantly at home. Main command centres were given animal names, while smaller units got plant names like Pionen (the Peony) and Liljan (the Lily).
Norr om Askims norra kyrkogård ligger et: North of Askim's northern cemetery is an Iron Age burial ground from between 800 and 1050, with around eighty burial mounds. The churchyard itself dates back to the Middle Ages.
Norr om Humlegården skapades på 1870-tal: North of Humlegården park, a whole town of villas was laid out in the 1870s, modelled on English and German suburbs. Most of the villas later made way for grand apartment buildings, and Floragatan is now one of the most expensive addresses in Sweden. The Curman Villa, built in 1880–1881, is one of the few survivors – a free take on a Roman country house, with a tall, glass-roofed atrium at its heart. Its neighbour is Villa Sandrew.
Norr om Hägernäs ligger Rönninge by, ett: North of Hägernäs is Rönninge by, an open-air museum that draws big crowds, especially at Midsummer. The village was already inhabited in the late Iron Age.
Norr om Hågelby gård skulle det en gång: North of Hågelby gård, there were once plans for the biggest amusement attraction in northern Europe. The Lindgren family, who have run Stockholm's Gröna Lund amusement park for generations, were set to lease the land for a family theme park, Familjeparken Hågelby, but the plans were scrapped in 2014. What's still here is the Älvestaån stream, which drops 17 metres on its way from Lake Aspen to Lake Tullingesjön and runs partly hidden in a culvert beneath the Hågelby estate.
Norr om Långedragsvägen ligger ett litet: North of Långedragsvägen is a small residential area on the same hill that's called Sjöbergen when seen from the river. Many of the houses are old and the lanes tight and narrow. Down on the street you'll find a bakery, a florist and a sweet shop.

North of Långedragsvägen is a small residential area on the same hill that's known as Sjöbergen on the river side. Many of the houses are old and the roads are narrow. Along Långedragsvägen there's a bakery, a florist and a sweet shop.
Norr om Nedre Söderby finns ett system a: North of Nedre Söderby is a network of sunken lanes, not built but worn into the ground by feet and hooves over a very long time. The Söderby runestone from the 11th century shows that people were travelling this way as early as the Viking Age.
Norr om Tumlehed, en bit härifrån, finns: North of Tumlehed, not far from here, is an area of countryside criss-crossed by footpaths and trails, hiding several ancient monuments. Among them are rock paintings of four ships, a deer and four fish. Something to think about next time you're out walking in the woods here on western Hisingen.
Norr om bostadsområdet ligger naturreser: North of the housing area lies the Rinkebyskogen nature reserve. In the 1970s there were plans to build homes in part of the forest, but they were shelved when the metro was never extended towards Täby.
Norr om butikshallen står fem punkthus a: North of the shopping hall stand five tower blocks by Sven Brolid, their balconies decorated with blue and white ceramic tiles. The buildings are protected and may not be demolished. By the church, look for the marks of the wooden formwork in the concrete façade of Bo Cederlöf's deck-access block.
Norr om butikshallen står fem punkthus r: North of the shopping hall stand five tower blocks by Sven Brolid, their balconies decorated with blue and white ceramics. They are protected and may not be demolished. On the deck-access block by the church you can see the imprint of the timber formwork in the concrete.

North of the shopping hall stand five tower blocks designed by Sven Brolid, their balconies decorated with blue and white ceramic tiles. The buildings are protected in the local plan and may not be demolished or altered out of character.
Norr om fotbollsplanen vid Siriusgatan 6: North of the football pitch at Siriusgatan 66–70 is a hällkista, a stone cist grave from the late Stone Age. It has never been excavated. When it was built, a lake lay below it, where today you'll find the boggy ground of Gärdsås mosse.

North of the football pitch at Siriusgatan 66–70 lies a stone cist – a burial chamber of upright stone slabs covered with more slabs – from the end of the Stone Age. When it was built, a lake lay below, where the Gärdsås bog is now. The grave has never been excavated.
Norr om kyrkogården ligger ett gravfält: North of the churchyard lies an Iron Age burial ground from AD 800–1050, with around eighty burial mounds. In other words, this spot mattered long before the first church went up.
Norr om mossen finns ruinerna efter Moss: North of the bog lie the ruins of Mosstorpet, an old croft. Today they form part of Fruktträdgården, the Orchard, an adventure playground for day trips.
Norr om sjön Flaten, inne i Flatens natu: North of Lake Flaten, tucked away in the Flaten nature reserve, is Skarpnäcksgrottan, a cave protected as an ancient monument. The Flaten district borders both Lake Drevviken and Lake Ältasjön, which is only about four and a half metres deep. Test fishing there has turned up perch, bream and ruffe, among others.
Norr om villorna ligger Lillängsskogen,: North of the houses lies Lillängsskogen, a wood that the municipality's own surveys identify as a corridor for species that live on oak. Plans to build 5,000 homes here were halted in 2015, and in 2019 plans for a preschool in the wood were dropped too.
Norra Biskopsgårdens kyrka byggdes 1970: Norra Biskopsgården church was built in 1970 as a parish hall, when Lundby parish was at its biggest and needed more room. It has a free-standing bell tower. The Church of Sweden deconsecrated it in 2004, and it's now used by the City Mission and the Finnish parish. Not far away is Jättesten, named after the giant boulders on the hill behind the houses.
Norra entrén ligger söderut: The north entrance is to the south
Norra tornen ritades av Reinier de Graaf: The Norra Tornen towers were designed by Reinier de Graaf of OMA. They step inwards as they rise, and every facade unit doubles as a balcony for the flat above. In 2020 they won Frankfurt's International Highrise Award, the Internationaler Hochhaus Preis.
Norra vattentornet ritades av Ragnar Oss: The northern water tower was designed by Ragnar Ossian Swensson and completed in 1936. The entire outer shell was cast in just eight days. The tower held 300 cubic metres of water and was easy to spot thanks to the 24 windows at the top.
Norra Ängby bebyggdes 1933–1945 som själ: Norra Ängby was built between 1933 and 1945 as a self-build scheme. Instead of a cash deposit, the future owner helped build the house, putting in work worth ten per cent of the construction cost.
Norra Ängby byggdes 1933–1945 som självb: Norra Ängby was built between 1933 and 1945 as a self-build scheme. Instead of paying a cash deposit, the future owner helped build the house, with their labour counting for 10 per cent of the cost. The garages on Anundsvägen are painted pale blue and yellow.
Norra Ängby was built between 1933 and 1945 as a self-build scheme. Instead of a cash deposit, the future owner did their own building work equivalent to 10 per cent of the cost.
Norrbacka värdshus var välbesökt av blan: Norrbacka inn was a favourite haunt of Carl Michael Bellman and Bengt Lidner, among others, and lively political debates went on here. August Strindberg mentions the inn in his novel The Red Room.
Norrmannen Hans Mustad valde platsen för: The Norwegian Hans Mustad chose this spot because it had everything a margarine factory could need. Cold springs by the gravel ridge provided clean water, and in winter blocks of ice were sawn out of Stensjön lake to keep things cool.
Novums byggnader ska bilda en övergång m: The Novum buildings are designed to bridge the gap between Karolinska University Hospital in Huddinge, built in concrete from Småland, and the tower blocks of Flemingsberg. The project was initiated by Professor Jan-Åke Gustafsson of the Karolinska Institute.
Nu har staden blivit kust. Långedrag är: Now the city has turned into coastline. Långedrag is Gothenburg's sailing harbour, and in summer the jetties are packed with boats. From here you can look out over the archipelago – and on a clear day, all the way to Vinga lighthouse, far out where the open sea begins.
Nu har vi kört över bron till Södermalm: We've crossed the bridge to Södermalm and reached Bergsund. Back in 1769 a Scot, Thomas Lewis, set up an iron-pot foundry here, right by the bridge to Reimersholme, and until 1929 the site was home to the Bergsund engineering works. Across the water is Långholmen, where Stockholm's central prison stood until 1975 – today it's a hotel and hostel.
Nu kör vi ner mot Göta älv och Stenpiren: Now we're heading down towards the Göta älv river and Stenpiren, the old stone pier. During the 19th and early 20th centuries, more than a million Swedes emigrated in search of a new life in America, and most of them left via Gothenburg – many boarding their ships right here. Today the Älvsnabben ferry crosses the river from this spot, and your tram ticket is valid on it too. Over on the far bank you can see Lindholmen and Eriksberg, once home to the city's great shipyards.
Nu kör vi över den lilla bron ut till Re: We're now crossing the little bridge over to Reimersholme. The island is named after Anders Reimers, who owned it in the 18th century. For many years there was a distillery here, and the name Reimersholms lived on on its bottles. Today the island is a quiet residential area with a waterfront path running all the way round. We'll soon reach the final stop. Thank you for riding with us!
Nu passerar vi Lisebergs södra sida. Här: We're now passing the south side of Liseberg amusement park, where you'll often catch a glimpse of the roller coasters. Lisebergshöjden, the hill behind the park, was once part of the Liseberg estate – the country house that gave the park its name.

We're now passing the south side of Liseberg, and you'll often catch a glimpse of the roller coasters here. The area used to be called Geteberget, but in the 1750s the merchant Johan Anders Lamberg renamed it Lisa's Hill, after his wife. Hence the name Liseberg.
Nu är vi i SoFo, området söder om Folkun: We're now in SoFo, short for ‘south of Folkungagatan’. It's full of little shops, cafés and bars, and at its heart is Nytorget, one of Södermalm's best-loved parks. Many of the buildings in the surrounding blocks date from the late 1800s.
Nu är vi på Södermalm. Västerbron, som v: We're now on Södermalm. Västerbron, the Western Bridge we've just crossed, opened in 1935 and is more than six hundred metres long. The twin-towered church right here is Högalidskyrkan, consecrated in 1923.

We're now on Södermalm. Västerbron, the bridge we've just crossed, opened in 1935 and is more than six hundred metres long. The twin-towered church right beside us is Högalidskyrkan, consecrated in 1923. You can see it from far away, and it's a landmark for the whole of western Söder.
Nu är vi vid Hornstull, uppkallat efter: Now we're at Hornstull, named after the toll gate that once stood here on the old city boundary. From here we carry on right across Södermalm, from the west of Söder to the streets around Sofia in the east.
Nuvarande kyrka ritades av Johan Fredrik: The present church was designed by Johan Fredrik Åbom in the Romanesque Revival style and came into use in 1864. It originally had a pointed tower, but the spire was in such poor shape that in 1927 it was replaced by today's pyramid-shaped one.
Nuvarande kyrkan ritades av Adolf W. Ede: The present church was designed by Adolf W. Edelsvärd and consecrated on 15 July 1866 by Peter Wieselgren. In the 1900s, four allegorical paintings from the old church turned up in a barn in Askim. Today Chastity, Gentleness, Religion and Truth adorn the gallery.

Nya Ullevi byggdes till fotbolls-VM 1958: Nya Ullevi was built for the 1958 football World Cup and is still one of Sweden's biggest arenas. It's famous for its concerts too: when Bruce Springsteen played here in 1985, the stands swayed so much that the stadium later had to be reinforced.
Nya Varvet blev örlogshamn kring år 1700: Nya Varvet became a naval base around 1700, and in 1717 and 1719 it came under attack from Danish warships led by Vice Admiral Peter Tordenskjold. Right next to it is Nya Varvet cemetery from 1701, with a memorial to the crew of the submarine HMS Ulven, sunk by a mine in 1943. Nobis, the officers' mess a little way up the hill, is a listed building.
Nya badet öppnade direkt: The new pool opened straight away
Nya hus längs vägen 2010: New homes along the road in 2010
Nya hus vid gamla torget: New buildings by an old square
Nya kedjehus bland egnahem: New link houses among the old self-builds
Nya Åbybadet invigdes den 16 juni 2023 o: The new Åbybadet swimming centre opened on 16 June 2023 at a cost of 500 million kronor. While it was being built, a temporary pool, Lilla Åbybadet, stood across the road for swimming lessons and clubs.
Nybohovshissen invigdes den 5 april 1964: The Nybohov lift opened on 5 April 1964. Until the 1970s a single ride cost 25 öre, but the fare was deducted if you carried on by metro.
Nyckelviksskolan grundades 1955 av Herth: Nyckelviksskolan was founded in 1955 by Hertha Olivet, inspired by Carl Malmsten and the Bauhaus approach to teaching. The teachers are all working artists, designers, architects and craftspeople.
Nygotiskt kapell i rött tegel: A neo-Gothic chapel in red brick
Nykterhetsvärdshus en tid: A temperance inn for a time
Nynäs nämns sedan 1689 som torp under Åg: Nynäs has been recorded since 1689 as a croft under Ågesta farm. As recently as 1920–1930 it was worked by Anders Johan Nyström and his wife Karolina, who had five children. Today the cottage serves as a rest hut and, in winter, a changing room.
Nytorp kallades också Smörpundet, och på: Nytorp was also known as Smörpundet, and a map from 1704 shows both Smörpundsängen and Smörpunds Kierret. The name probably comes from a nearby rocky knoll shaped like a butter tub.
Nytt bad samma år: A new pool the same year
Nyårsrevy varje vinter: A New Year revue every winter
Näckrosens konst är ett stort collage av: The art at Näckrosen is a large collage of texts, stones and pieces of tiled stove, with glazed bricks from the demolished Strindberg House at Karlaplan. Display cases hold film props and photos from Filmstaden. The station lies 21 metres below ground, right under the old film studios.

Näckrosen's artwork is a large collage of texts, stones, fragments of tiled stoves and glazed brick from the demolished Strindberg house on Karlaplan. Display cases hold film props and photos from Filmstaden, the old film studios directly above. The station lies 21 metres underground.
Näckrosor i skogssjön: Water lilies in a forest lake
Näktergal och sju fladdermöss: A nightingale and seven bat species

Nälsta skrevs 1354 som Nærdharstaff. För: Nälsta was written Nærdharstaff in 1354. The first part comes from the name of the deity Njärd, so the district's name carries an ancient god's name within it.
Nälsta skrevs Nærdharstaff år 1354, och: Nälsta was written Nærdharstaff in 1354, and the first part comes from the name of the deity Njärd. Settlement sites have been found in the area from as far back as the late Stone Age, as well as from the Bronze Age, the Iron Age and the Viking Age.
Nälsta är en av nio stadsdelar i Hässelb: Nälsta is one of nine districts in Hässelby-Vällingby, with a mix of villas, terraced houses and blocks of flats. Not far away is Spånga torg, the square by Spånga station, served by both commuter trains and buses. It has a good selection of shops, services and restaurants, so you'll find most things you need, whether you're hungry or have errands to run.
När Aeolus tog över Sillfarsholmen 1935: When Aeolus took over Sillfarsholmen in 1935, Bengt and Emma Larsson were living there. They had looked after the island's oil depot and were promised they could stay, which they did until their deaths in 1946 and 1945.
När Allum öppnade den 9 april 2006 kom 7: When Allum opened on 9 April 2006, 75,000 people came on the very first day. There's a bus station underneath the walkway over the E20.
When Allum opened on 9 April 2006, 75,000 people came to take a look. Today the shopping centre welcomes about 5.6 million customers a year.
När August Strindberg bodde i Djursholm: When August Strindberg lived in Djursholm in 1891–1892, he planned to set up a theatre in the restaurant's large dining room. Nothing came of it, as the restaurateur Strandberg needed the room for his business.
När Basketligan bildades blev hallen hem: When the Basketligan, Sweden's top basketball league, was formed, the hall became home to JB Knights, a joint team from Järfälla Basket and Blackeberg Basket. JB Knights folded in 1994. Today Järfälla Basket's women's team plays in the Basketligan.
När Bio Kaskad återinvigdes 14 juli 2018: When Bio Kaskad reopened on 14 July 2018, the auditorium was fitted with 120 second-hand seats from the Fontänen cinema in Vällingby. Originally it seated 339, and the blue neon sign in joined-up script still hangs above the entrance.
När Björken 18 stod klart fanns varken e: When Björken 18 was finished, it had no electricity, central heating or bathrooms. The building was heated with tiled stoves and lit by gas lamps. Central heating and bathrooms only arrived in 1927–1929.
När Bollmora blev egen tätort 1965 bodde: When Bollmora became a separate built-up area in 1965, it had 9,414 residents. Five years later the population had almost doubled, to 18,548.
When Bollmora became a separate built-up area in 1965, it had 9,414 residents. Five years later the population had nearly doubled, to 18,548. Bollmora centrum opened on 12 September 1965.
När Bromma flygplats anlades i mitten av: When Bromma Airport was built in the mid-1930s, the windmill stood in the way on the western side of the airfield and had to be moved. Ideally it would have gone up on the mill hill, but that wasn't allowed for reasons of air safety.
När Brommaplan planerades 1940 kallades: When Brommaplan was planned in 1940, the area was known as Centrala Bromma, Central Bromma. Bromma Airport had opened in 1936 and was then one of Europe's most modern. In the 1930s people took the bus into town, before the Ängby line and the metro took over.
När Brunnsviken låg tio meter högre: When Brunnsviken was ten metres higher
När Charles Lindbergh besökte Sverige 19: When Charles Lindbergh visited Sweden in 1933, he was allowed to fly one of the Air Force's Sk 10 aircraft at Barkarby.
När Edsbergs centrum öppnade 1964 var de: When Edsbergs centrum opened in 1964 it was the largest shopping centre in Sollentuna, with 18 shops. The colourful tower blocks on Drevkarlsstigen can be seen from far away.
När Electrolux fabrik revs 2000 sparades: When the Electrolux factory was demolished in 2000, a few buildings of historic value were spared. One is Vita villan, the White Villa, on the corner of Luxgatan and Primusgatan – AB Lux's office from 1906, designed by Sigge Cronstedt. The island's oldest surviving block of flats is Föreningshuset from 1910.
När Ericsson köpte kabelverket 1928 var: When Ericsson bought the cable works in 1928, it was Sweden's largest maker of electric cables and the only one producing underground cable. Among its big deliveries were the oil-filled cables laid under the Öresund strait in 1958 and 1963, each seven kilometres long.
När Farsta Centrum invigdes 1960 var det: When Farsta Centrum opened in 1960, it was Sweden's largest suburban shopping centre. More than 100,000 people came, and among the 1,200 invited guests were Princesses Sibylla and Margaretha. It cost 60 million kronor to build.
När Fruängens station invigdes den 5 apr: When Fruängen station opened on 5 April 1964, King Gustaf VI Adolf travelled out here on the new metro. He was greeted by scouts and a choir of pupils from the Adolf Fredrik music school.
När Frölunda torg öppnade 1966 hade det: When Frölunda Torg opened in 1966 it had two department stores, a bowling alley and its own tram stop. In the first four days alone, 50,000 people visited. Ekebäck village used to stand here – one of its houses survives east of the cultural centre.
När Fullersta gårds ägare Carl-Erik Lind: When Carl-Erik Lindell, owner of Fullersta farm, gave up farming in 1902 and started selling attractive plots for villas, the brochure made a point of stressing that the trip from Stockholm Central took just half an hour.
När Gais ekonomi havererade 2012 tvingad: When Gais's finances collapsed in 2012, the club was forced to sell its Gaisgården ground for around SEK 12 million. In December 2025 it announced it had bought it back for 8.8 million.
När Garnisonssjukhuset invigdes 1834 var: When the Garrison Hospital opened in 1834, it was the largest and most modern hospital in the Nordic countries, with 430 beds. Construction was overseen by a committee chaired by Crown Prince Karl Johan, and it ended up costing more than twice the estimate.
När Gullbergsvassen torrlagts blev stati: Once Gullbergsvassen had been drained, the station building became the first large structure on the new land. In 1930 passenger services moved to Centralstationen and the tracks outside were torn up. BJ-parken, the park by the entrance, was laid out in 1935 as the area's only patch of green.
När Gustav II Adolf gifte sig med Maria: When King Gustav II Adolf married Maria Eleonora on 25 November 1620, the bridal procession set out from Bergshamra. For a time the estate was owned by Lord High Chancellor Axel Oxenstierna, who built a pleasure palace here designed by Nicodemus Tessin the Elder. The palace no longer survives.
När Götatunneln byggdes 2001 hittades et: When the Göta Tunnel was being built in 2001, workers found the wreck of a boat from the mid-1600s, nicknamed "Götabåten", under more than three metres of fill. The 12-metre boat was built mostly of oak and pine. The name Lilla Bommen comes from the booms that once closed off the waterway so that tolls could be collected.
När Göteborg växte byggdes nya stadsdela: As Gothenburg grew, new neighbourhoods went up with squares, schools and green spaces. Ride from 1950s Kortedala and 1970s Bergsjön to Guldheden and Frölunda Torg.
När Hangar 2 renoverades 2005 fick Linje: When Hangar 2 was renovated in 2005, the old ‘LIN’ logo of the airline Linjeflyg was left on the facade. During the Second World War the J 22 fighter was built in Hangar 1.
