Its best-known landmark is “Barnet med käpphästen”, The Child with the Hobby Horse, a copper sculpture by Marie Stenqvist. And close by is Hagsätraskogen, 31 hectares of protected woodland.
Ormkärr var ett torp under Älvsjö gård,: Ormkärr was a croft belonging to Älvsjö farm, mentioned as early as 1617. In the nature reserve's valley you can still make out the croft's old fields as they appear on early 18th-century maps, along with stone foundations and a clearance cairn.
Ormkärrs lamellhus i rött tegel byggdes: Ormkärr's red-brick lamella blocks were built in 1959–1960 by the HSB housing cooperative to designs by Curt Strehlenert. A pedestrian tunnel clad in turquoise mosaic runs right through the building.
Ormkärr's red-brick slab blocks were built by HSB in 1959–1960 to designs by Curt Strehlenert. A pedestrian tunnel lined with turquoise mosaic runs right through the building.

Ormkärr's red-brick slab blocks were built by HSB in 1959–1960. A pedestrian tunnel lined with turquoise mosaic runs right through the building. Hagsätra's streets are named after places in the province of Närke, such as Fjugestagränd and Vintrosagatan.
Ormkärrsbäcken slingrar sig i meandrar g: Ormkärrsbäcken meanders through the reserve, and in 2012 the Ormkärr pond was dug for frogs and other amphibians. In the old pine forest you might spot crested tits, black woodpeckers and goshawks.
Ormkärrsskogen har gott om promenadvägar: Ormkärrsskogen, a forest, has plenty of walking paths and is a good spot for mushroom picking. The 31-hectare Hagsätraskogen nature reserve was created in 2021, becoming Stockholm's eleventh nature reserve.
Ormo naturreservat ligger nära, 25 hekta: Ormo nature reserve is close by: 25 hectares of broadleaf woodland and pasture along the valley of the Ormbäcken stream, between wooded hills and open grazing. It has been protected since 2018. Not far off, on the Nordre älv river, is the Ormo barrier, an adjustable dam that can divert water from Nordre älv into the Gothenburg branch of Göta älv, the Göta River.
Orten Kil i Boo har fått sitt namn efter: The village of Kil in Boo takes its name from Kils gård, a well-preserved manor on Graningevägen. The main building and its wings were given their Empire-style look in the 1820s under Major General Louis Marie de Camps. Not far away is Lake Insjön, almost twelve metres deep, with the old Velamsund estate and a swimming spot at its northern end.
Orten växte upp kring stationen Näsby på: From 1885 the town grew up around Näsby station on the Stockholm–Rimbo railway. Carl Robert Lamm, who owned Näsby Palace from 1901, sold villa plots carved out of the estate. The name Roslags Näsby came in 1916.
Ortnamnen här har bytt skepnad flera gån: The place names around here have changed several times. Until 2010, Statistics Sweden used the name Bårhult for the houses at Röset and Pusta, on the north shore of Lake Landvettersjön. And Landvetters-Kärret only got the “Landvetter” part of its name to avoid confusion with another Kärret in the same municipality. Today both areas are counted as part of Landvetter.
Oscar Fredriksskolans rödbruna tegelfasa: The reddish-brown brick façades of Oscar Fredrik School closely resemble those of nearby Oscar Fredrik Church. The architect Adrian C. Peterson gave the school typical 1890s features: patterned brickwork, blind windows and decorative wall anchors.
Ostindiefarare och hovarkitekt: An East India trader and a court architect
Ostindiefararen byggdes här: Where the East Indiaman was built
Ostindiefararens gravkor: The East India man's burial vault
Ostkupan ligger på Mejerigatan 2, och ga: Ostkupan – 'the Cheese Dome' – stands at Mejerigatan 2, and the surrounding streets have dairy names like Gräddgatan (Cream Street), Smörgatan (Butter Street) and Mjölktorget (Milk Square), after the dairy that once stood nearby. In the basement there's a student bar with darts and table football.
Ovan jord vid Rissnedepån finns skötselh: Above ground at the Rissne depot are the maintenance hall and the only turntable on the entire metro. The workshop and offices are in the Maden block.
Ovanför Fiskebäcksbadet finns omfattande: Above Fiskebäck beach lies an extensive spread of ancient remains – cairns and stone settings, including the Fiskebäck stone ship. Next to the beach is a large marina with boatyards and chandlers.
Ovanför Skärholmstorget ligger Flamingop: Above Skärholmstorget lies Flamingoparken, with water play in summer. It's reached by stairs and a lift and was designed by Johan Ferner Ström. Down towards Lake Mälaren runs a waterside promenade with two swimming spots.
Ovanför Vårberg reser sig Vårbergstoppen: Rising above Vårberg is Vårbergstoppen, known locally as Tippen, ‘the Tip’ – a man-made hill built up between 1965 and 1982 that reaches 90 metres above sea level. Don't mix it up with its neighbour Vikingaberget: at just over 77 metres, that's Stockholm's highest natural point! Close by is the Kummelholmen art gallery, named after the building's land registry name.
Ovanför gatan reser sig Stadshagsberget,: Above the street rises Stadshagsberget, the highest natural point on Kungsholmen at 52 metres above sea level. From the top you can see Karlberg Palace, home to the Karlberg Military Academy – the oldest military academy in the world still in its original location and building. Across Lake Karlbergssjön, Rörstrand porcelain was once made. The brand dates from 1726 and is the second-oldest porcelain brand in Europe, after Meissen.
Ovanför oss reser sig Ramberget med Keil: Above us rises Ramberget hill and Keillers park. From the top you get one of the best views over Gothenburg and the river. It's a steep but short climb.
Ovanför spårvagnshållplatsen ligger buss: Above the tram stop is the Frölunda Torg bus station, the biggest bus interchange in western Gothenburg. Just south of the stop, the trams turn around on a loop.
Ovanpå Guldhedens vattentorn, med sina v: On top of the Guldheden water tower, with its arches and yellow brick, there was once a café for 40 guests, which opened in 1953. Since 2020 the tower has been a protected site, closed to the public. A little further away stands Hästen, 'the Horse', a two-metre teak horse by Ivar Lindekrantz from 1956, put together using boatbuilding techniques – rather like a barrel.
Owe Ohlsson fostrades i Hälsö Bollklubb,: Owe Ohlsson came up through Hälsö Bollklubb, became IFK Göteborg's fifth-highest goalscorer of all time and was in the squad that won silver at the 1958 World Cup. The actress Maria Lundqvist also grew up on the island.
P.C. Jersilds roman Babels hus utspelar: P.C. Jersild's novel The House of Babel is set in the large hospital planned here, called Enskede Hospital in the book. Parts of the TV series based on it were filmed at Dalen Hospital.
P.O. Stokkebye Kvarnaktiebolag började m: P.O. Stokkebye Kvarnaktiebolag started milling in Agnesberg in 1901, producing among other things AXA rolled oats. This is where the method of steam-treating oats was developed. The mill closed in 1979 and production moved to Järna.
Paddan, båttur på kanalerna: Paddan boat tour on the canals
Paintball-VM på fotbollsplanen: Paintball World Cup on the football pitch
Palats 20 meter över viken: A palace 20 metres above the bay
Palatsen på södra sidan: The palaces on the south side
Palatset som sprängdes: The palace that was blown up
Palladium hade troligen Stockholms äldst: Palladium probably had Stockholm's oldest neon sign, put up in 1926. When it was taken down in 1996, it prompted the founding of Stadsljusgruppen, a group devoted to city lighting, and the creation of the Lysande skylt ("Brilliant Sign") award.
Palladium var först i Stockholm med utru: Palladium was the first cinema in Stockholm equipped for sound films. On 10 August 1930 it hosted the premiere of the first Swedish-made talkie, För hennes skull (For Her Sake), starring Gösta Ekman the Elder and Inga Tidblad. Many of Greta Garbo's hits were also shown here.
Palladiums stora långkörare var Borta me: Palladium's great long-runner was Gone with the Wind, which played for 47 weeks straight in 1941–1942. A temporary temple-like entrance was built in front of the façade, and at the premiere more than 5,000 people stood in the street to see the celebrities and the royal family.
Palme invigde Nordens största: Palme opened the Nordic region's largest
Palme: bästa bostadsmiljön: Palme: the best place to live
Pappersbruket som tog ansvar: The paper mill that took responsibility
Paraplyorganisationen Mölndals Amatörtea: The umbrella group Mölndals Amatörteaterförening, MATF, was set up in 1992. Its current theatre opened in 1998, and when the curtain isn't up the building doubles as a conference venue.
Paret Brunius var välkända kulturpersonl: The Brunius couple were well-known cultural figures, and the press dubbed their villa “A literary home on Lidingö”. In the summer of 1917 Célie Brunius took leave from work to run the house and look after the children, and later wrote a book about it, Sin egen tjänare (One's Own Servant).
Paret Clas och Annika Browall öppnade vä: Clas and Annika Browall opened the inn in 1731, originally under the name Browallshof. It boasted the city's biggest dance hall, and in 1745 King Fredrik I attended a celebrated dance here.
Paret är Carl och Olga: The couple are Carl and Olga
Park i stället för tunnelbana: A park instead of a metro line
Park-Bio i Örby Folkets hus invigdes 192: Park-Bio, the cinema in Örby's Folkets hus community hall, opened in 1928 and showed films until 1968 – and since 2021 the building has been screening films again. Nearby is Park Studios, where Ace of Base, Stina Nordenstam and Dan Hylander were among those who recorded in the 1990s; the band Kent owned it from 2004 to 2016. And Örby Castle? Since the 1970s it has been leased to the Embassy of Vietnam.
Park-Bio ritades av Eskil Sundahl och Da: Park-Bio was designed by Eskil Sundahl and Dag Ribbing in the 1920s Classicist style, with a tall, columned entrance portal. It's an unusual style for Sundahl, who became better known for functionalism. The neon 'Park' sign still glows above the entrance.

Park-Bio was designed by Eskil Sundahl and Dag Ribbing in the 1920s Classicist style, with a tall entrance portal facing the street. It's an unusual style for Sundahl, who became best known for functionalism.
Parken Bergsgruvan har bollplan och en s: Bergsgruvan park has a ball pitch and a big playground. In winter people skate on the pitch and go sledging down the hill. The name, 'the rock mine', suggests that stone was once quarried here.
Parken började anläggas 1936 efter ritni: Work on the park began in 1936 to designs by Erik Glemme, and it was one of Stockholm's first parks in the functionalist style. The amphitheatre was built for the city's 700th anniversary in 1953 and holds 5,000 people.
Parken där tornet stod: The park where the tower stood
Parken fick sitt namn 1924 och parkleken: The park got its name in 1924, and the parklek – a staffed play park for children – opened in 1949. When the park building went up in 1969, Aspuddsparken became an all-year-round park.
Parken fick sitt namn 1993 efter skulptö: The park was named in 1993 after the sculptor Eric Grate, who spent his last fifteen years in Solna. As well as Oberon (1953–54) and Sparvguden, the Sparrow God, you'll also find his bronze Nike de Sant Andria from 1968 here.
Parken formades mellan 1937 och 1955 av: The park was laid out between 1937 and 1955 by landscape architects Sven Hermelin and Inger Wedborn, taking the old park of Sundbyberg manor as its model. Sundbyberg council bought the park in 2006.
Parken har 20 018 paneler på ett område: The solar park has 20,018 panels spread over an area roughly the size of 16 football pitches. In a year, it produces about as much electricity as 1,400 flats use.
Parken har 20 018 solpaneler och tar upp: The park has 20,018 solar panels and covers 10.7 hectares – almost 16 football pitches. The panels themselves cover 32,000 square metres but need about four times as much space so they don't shade each other.
Parken har 20 018 solpaneler på cirka 32: The park has 20,018 solar panels covering about 32,000 square metres, but it takes up roughly four times as much land because the panels mustn't shade each other. Each year it produces as much electricity as some 1,400 flats use.
Parken har byggts på med en liten damm,: The park has gained a small pond, a boat and a children's book library with Bagar-Birgits konditori, Baker Birgit's café, open in summer. In 2010 the park won Solna's urban environment award.
Parken här är kärnan i det som en gång v: This park is the heart of what was once Långbro Hospital, a psychiatric hospital built between 1905 and 1910 to designs by Gustaf Wickman, which closed in 1997. Two of its distinctive buildings, Stora Mans and Stora Kvinns – the large men's and women's wards – still stand in the park. And the old chief physician's residence? That's now Långbro värdshus, an inn.
Parken köptes med donation: A park bought with a bequest
Parken som blev radhus: The park that became terraced houses
Parken som gav området namn: The parks that named the area
Parken uppkallad efter tre Tessin: A park named after three Tessins
Parken var en sjöbotten: The park was a lake bed
Parken var först tänkt som tillfällig, m: The park was meant to be temporary at first, but it was a hit. Even so, 22 September 1924 was Liseberg's worst day ever, with just 46 visitors. Over that whole year 473,319 came.
Parken var samlingsplats för strejkande: The park was a gathering place for striking and locked-out workers, especially during the general strike of 1909. But its popularity waned, and in 1934 the company that ran it went bankrupt. Competition from Liseberg, opened in 1923, had become too stiff.
Parken var större förr: The park used to be bigger
Parken vid Hågelby gård är barockinspire: The park at Hågelby gård is Baroque-inspired. A main axis runs from the gate down to Lake Aspen, emphasised by an avenue of lime trees. Along the central axis lies a canal some 140 metres long, widening into a small pond.
Parken är 2,9 hektar och präglas av berg: The 2.9-hectare park is dominated by rocky slopes edged with tall pines. The little pond in the north-east has been restored and now collects stormwater.
Parken öppnade 8 maj 1923 till Göteborgs: Liseberg opened on 8 May 1923 for Gothenburg's 300th anniversary and was only ever meant to be temporary. It was such a hit that it simply carried on. Its worst day ever was 22 September 1924, when just 46 visitors turned up.
Parkens första badstrand, Playan, fick s: The park's first beach, Playan, was given sand and wooden decking on the Göta älv river. In 2023 the permanent green areas opened, designed with wild nature in mind and to open up the riverbanks to everyone.
Parkens västra allé heter sedan 1998 Jus: Since 1998 the park’s western avenue has been named after the tenor Jussi Björling, and since 2007 the eastern one after the soprano Birgit Nilsson. The Royal Opera is right next door.
Parkeringshuset byggdes i fyra plan för: The four-storey car park was built for 4,000 cars and became the largest in northern Europe. The cars never came in those numbers, and part of the building was used by the Skärholmen flea market instead.
Parkeringshuset mittemot Danvikcenter rö: The car park opposite Danvikcenter was voted Nacka's ugliest building. In 2019 the Chilean street artist Nelson Cekis painted a mural on it during the Wall Street festival.
Parkeringsplatsen där planet störtade br: The car park where the plane came down was usually full of children playing on the snowbanks left by the ploughs. But SVT happened to be showing children's programmes at that moment, and the car park was empty. No one on the ground was hurt.
Partille Arena invigdes 2016, och Sverig: Partille Arena opened in 2016, and Swedish Radio held its P3 Guld music awards here four years running, from 2017 to 2020. In April 2018 Bryan Adams set the attendance record with an audience of 5,503.
Partille Bokhandel delade 1994–2010 ut e: From 1994 to 2010, the bookshop Partille Bokhandel awarded a writers' grant: two months at the Hôtel Chevillon in Grez-sur-Loing, south of Paris. Back in the 1880s, Nordic artists and writers such as Carl Larsson, P.S. Krøyer and August Strindberg gathered there.
Partille SC grundades 1975 och har vunni: Partille SC was founded in 1975 and has won many Swedish championship titles in both field hockey and indoor hockey. In 2019 the men's team won the European club cup.
Partille gymnasium finns både här i Kult: Partille's upper secondary school is split between Kulturum here and Teknikcentrum on Laxfiskevägen. It offers a national sports programme, and most courses can be taken with a sports focus. The arts programmes specialise in music.
Partille kan verka som en ren förort, me: Partille might look like just another suburb, but a remarkable 60 per cent of the municipality is protected nature. It's small in size but medium-sized in population, and its main town merged with Gothenburg long ago. The municipality has four parts: Partille, Sävedalen, Öjersjö and Jonsered.
Partille kyrka byggdes någon gång mellan: Partille Church went up some time between 1150 and 1250, probably on the foundations of an even older wooden church. Being so close to the Säveån river, it has subsided again and again – at one point the decision was taken to pull the whole church down. A fundraising drive paid for repairs instead.
Partillebohallen hette Partille Idrottsh: Partillebohallen was known as Partille Idrottshall until 1999. When Partille Arena opened in September 2016 it became the new home of the Sävehof handball club, and the old hall was demolished in April 2017. In its place, a new sports hall was planned, with a boules hall and flats.
Partilles vapen visar en klockstapel av: Partille's coat of arms shows a golden bell tower, modelled on the one beside Partille Church. The blue mountain and the two mussel shells come from the arms of the noble af Sandeberg family, whose seat is Partille Manor.
Patent- och registreringsverkets hus: The Swedish Patent and Registration Office building
Patron Pehr, som köpte gården 1848, hade: Patron Pehr – 'Squire Pehr' – who bought the farm in 1848, had once been a statare, a farm labourer paid largely in kind, and made his fortune from aquavit. He gave land free of charge to the State Railways in return for a promise of a station outside his house – today's Huddinge station. With 300 dairy cows, he had the largest herd in the country.
Paul Hedqvist började rita skolan redan: Paul Hedqvist started designing the school as early as 1939, but construction went quickly, from spring 1946 to summer 1948. For the façade he chose yellow brick, a favourite material of the 1940s, but he gave the inner walls of the hall building red facing brick.
Paul Hedqvist ritade stationsbyggnaden,: Paul Hedqvist designed the terminal, control tower and hangars in a blocky functionalist style – hence the name Bromma Blocks. In the first hangar he reused truss girders from the old Traneberg bridge, which had just been demolished.
Paviljongen består av två parallella trä: The pavilion consists of two parallel timber ranges joined by a short corridor at the north end. Between them lies a paved courtyard with yellow façades, opening to the south.
Pegmatitbrottet består av två brott cirk: The pegmatite quarry is really two quarries, about 200 metres apart. The northern one has a short, curving mine tunnel; the southern one is a small open pit. Every year plenty of students from the University of Gothenburg and Chalmers come out here, and the rare mineral columbite has been found on the site.
Pehr Pettersson, kallad Patron Pehr, had: Pehr Pettersson, known as Patron Pehr, had been a statare – a farmworker paid largely in kind – before he made a fortune from brännvin (schnapps) and bought Fullersta farm in 1848. With 300 dairy cows he had the largest herd in the country. He gave land to the railway in return for a station outside his house: today's Huddinge station.
Pelare från Rikssalen: Pillars from the Hall of State
Pelarfritt tak över 200 meter bana: A pillar-free roof over a 200-metre track
Pendeltågen började stanna här 1987, och: Commuter trains started stopping here in 1987, and when the mainline station opened in 1990 it got the double name Stockholm Syd–Flemingsberg. Since 2001 it has simply been called Flemingsberg. The commuter train to Stockholm City takes 18 minutes.
Pendeltågen stannar vid Huddinge centrum: Commuter trains stop at Huddinge centrum, the municipality's heart and main shopping area. Kommunalvägen runs almost parallel to the Western Main Line tracks for about 1.3 kilometres, and along it you'll find both Huddinge Church and the municipal hall. Nearby are traces of Svartlösa domsaga, a former court district. Its courthouse was designed in 1959 by the architect Karl Karlström, yet the district itself lasted just twelve years before it was abolished in the court reform of 1971.
Pennygången byggdes 1959 för att snabbt: Pennygången was built in 1959 to provide cheap flats quickly. Almost all of them are four-room flats with identical layouts, and to save money none were given balconies. One of the buildings snakes along as the longest residential block in Gothenburg.
Pepparreds naturreservat är bara 3,5 hek: Pepparred nature reserve covers just 3.5 hectares on a west-facing slope between the E6 motorway and the houses. It's made up of old wooded pasture with noble broadleaf trees such as oak and ash.
Pepparred nature reserve covers just 3.5 hectares. It sits on a west-facing slope between the E6 motorway and the houses south of Pepparred farm.
Per Anders Fogelström skildrade det gaml: The author Per Anders Fogelström wrote about Barnängen, the old factory district on Hammarby sjö, in his novel Vävarnas barn – “Children of the Weavers” – and this is also where the Hammarby IF sports club has its roots. Barnängsparken runs down to the waterfront, with lawns and a ferry jetty looking across to Hammarby sjöstad. A little further on is the Toy Museum, with collections ranging from 19th-century dolls to Lego, Barbie and Star Wars.

Per Anders Fogelström wrote about the old factory district of Barnängen, on the shore of Hammarby sjö, in his novel Vävarnas barn ('Children of the Weavers'), and this is where the Hammarby IF sports club has its roots. Barnängsparken, the park, slopes down to the quay with its lawns and a ferry jetty facing Hammarby Sjöstad. The park got its name in 1979, and the ferry crosses the lake from Barnängsbryggan pier.
Per Fritzell från After Shave, programle: Per Fritzell of the band After Shave, TV presenter Harald Treutiger and author Jakob Wegelius all grew up in Björkekärr. Treutiger went to Rosendalsskolan by Stabbetorget, and Leif Pagrotsky grew up near Trätorget.
Persontrafiken på Spånga–Lövsta järnväg: Passenger services on the Spånga–Lövsta railway ended in 1956, but the rubbish trains, nicknamed Silverpilen ("the Silver Arrow"), kept running until 1970. By passenger train the journey to Stockholm Central took about 33 minutes.
Persontrafiken vid Surte lades ner 31 ma: Passenger services at Surte ended on 31 May 1970. The station reopened on 9 December 2012, when the line was upgraded to double track, and today the Alependeln commuter train stops here.
Persontågen till Spånga slutade gå 1956,: Passenger trains to Spånga stopped running in 1956, but the rubbish trains, nicknamed Silverpilen (the Silver Arrow), carried on until 1970. A passenger train journey to Stockholm Central took about 33 minutes.
Perstorpsvägen är en del av Dalarövägen,: Perstorpsvägen is part of Dalarövägen, the old route between Stockholm and Dalarö. A quarter-mile milestone still stands at the junction of Perstorpsvägen and Tårtvägen.
Peter Celsing ritade Filmhuset åt Svensk: Filmhuset, the Film House, was designed by Peter Celsing for the Swedish Film Institute and opened in 1971. The institute, which among other things hands out the Guldbagge awards, Sweden's national film prizes, is run from here. Just up the hill on Hakberget stands the 1986 sculpture Protest: three blocks of red granite, the middle one shaped like a clenched fist. From 1890 to 1965 this was where the labour movement's May Day marches ended. And right next to it is a military heliport with no special facilities at all.

Peter Celsing designed Filmhuset, the Film House, for the Swedish Film Institute, and it opened in 1971. The institute, which among other things hands out the Guldbagge Awards, Sweden's film prizes, is run from here. A stone's throw away on Hakberget rises the 1986 sculpture Protest, three blocks of red granite, the middle one shaped into a clenched fist. This was where the labour movement's May Day marches ended from 1890 to 1965. The building itself is 140 metres long and was meant to suggest a camera, with its lens facing north.
Peter Celsing ritade biljetthallen med e: Peter Celsing designed the ticket hall with a shallow, free-spanning domed roof in raw concrete over a square 22 metres along each side. The glazing was by Sigurd Lewerentz, and the architectural historian Fredric Bedoire calls it one of the most beautiful halls in the metro's concrete.
Peregrine falcons took a liking to the gasholder. In May 2012 two chicks hatched in a nest on the structure.
Pilgrimskapellet är ett träkapell helt u: Pilgrimskapellet, the Pilgrim Chapel, is a wooden chapel with no religious symbols whatsoever, consecrated in 1977 by Bishop Ingmar Ström. The chapel and the cemetery around it were both designed by the landscape architect Per Friberg, and together they form Järfälla's entire burial ground. Graves lie both out in open fields and in the forest, and a 300-metre watercourse with eleven little waterfalls runs down to a large reflecting pool.
Pingstförsamlingen hade tidigare lokaler: The Pentecostal congregation previously had premises in Aspudden from 1913, in Mälarhöjden – including the Mälarbio cinema – and in Älvsjö. Today's white-and-brown church of brick and timber was consecrated in 1979.
Pinnharv, rullharv och släpharv: Peg harrows, roller harrows and drag harrows
Pipbruket startades 1739 av Olof Forsber: The pipe works was founded in 1739 by Olof Forsberg and Olof Aspegren. Clay pipes were fragile, so a lot of them were needed – up to a million a year at its peak, all shaped by hand by around 30 workers. Production continued until 1766.
Pippi och Lejonhjärta i stenbrottet: Pippi and the Lionhearts in the quarry
Piren blev bussterminal: The pier became a bus terminal
Piren som kapades: The pier that was cut short
Pistolskyttebanan byggdes 1984–1995 och: The pistol range was built in 1984–1995 and is home to the Mälarhöjden pistol club. It has a 25-metre range with 40 firing points for national-style shooting and a 50-metre range for sport shooting.
Pixbo herrgård har funnits sedan medelti: Pixbo manor has been here since the Middle Ages and takes its name from a family called Pik. There was also a small sawmill here until the 1920s.

Pixbo manor has existed since the Middle Ages and is named after a family called Pik. From the 1880s until 1935 it was home to a market garden growing fruit and vegetables for Gothenburg. Water came from ponds on the hills above, and most of them are still there.

Pixbo manor dates back to the Middle Ages and takes its name from a family called Pik. When the Gothenburg–Borås railway opened in 1894, Pixbo got a small station, and well-off Gothenburgers built large villas in Art Nouveau and Old Norse style overlooking Lake Rådasjön.
Pixbo ligger vid Rådasjön, en sjö som är: Pixbo lies on Rådasjön, a lake 23 metres deep that also supplies drinking water to Mölndal municipality. The Mölndalsån river flows through the lake and, further downstream, changes its name to Gullbergsån. Pixbo itself is built on and around the Björnåsen hill, so there are plenty of slopes to climb.
Pixbo är ett bostadsområde där man får g: Pixbo is a neighbourhood where you get fit for free: it's built on and around the Björnåsen ridge, and it's very hilly. It lies on the south side of Lake Rådasjön and has its own postal town. Little Lake Vällsjön forms its south-eastern edge, and the Vällbäcken stream runs along the east.
Planen var elva triangelhus – ett högt o: The plan was for eleven triangular buildings – one tall and ten lower ones in a chain – with 130 flats for around 600 residents. A new town plan in 1956 scrapped the low-rise buildings, leaving only the tower. No more houses were ever built to Werner Taesler’s design.
Planen var två lamellhus i fem våningar,: The plan was for two five-storey slab blocks, but Kampmann changed it to a single six-storey block on top of the shopping centre's low building. That avoided putting a large building on the roof of the metro, with its costly foundations, and freed up space for parking and a playground into the bargain.
Planen är 60 gånger 100 meter och har lö: The pitch measures 60 by 100 metres and is ringed by a running track, so it works for athletics too. It has had artificial turf since June 2009, and next to it is a clay tennis court.
Planen är att Barkarby ska bli en knutpu: The plan is for Barkarby to become a hub called Stockholm Väst. Buses via the Förbifart Stockholm bypass, regional trains from the Mälaren valley, commuter trains and the metro's blue line are all set to meet here.
Planer på en inomhusarena fanns redan i: Plans for an indoor arena existed as early as the late 1940s, but there was no money. As Gothenburg’s 350th anniversary drew near, the idea was revived as a lasting memorial. Before building began there were rows over the funding, the name and the orange colour.
Planerarna gjorde något nytt: i stället: The planners tried something new: instead of keeping the shoreline free for outdoor recreation, they built the houses right up close, with just a waterfront promenade in between. On the lower floors nearest the water were some twenty studio flats, and artists such as Inga Bagge and Olle Lindgren moved in.
Planerarna räknade med minst en och en h: The planners counted on at least one and a half cars per household and built a four-storey car park for 4,000 cars. It was the biggest in northern Europe, but that many cars never turned up, and part of it was later taken over by Skärholmen's flea market.

The planners reckoned on at least one and a half cars per household. A multi-storey car park for 4,000 cars – the biggest in northern Europe – was built in the centre. The cars never came in those numbers, and parts of the building have been used for flea markets.
Planerarna trodde att äldre med utflugna: The planners assumed older people whose children had left home would move to Silverdal, so they focused on housing for the elderly. When the homes went on sale in 2002, it turned out nearly everyone moving in had young children – and there was a sudden, acute shortage of nursery places.
Planerna på en ny kyrkogård i nordöstra: Plans for a new cemetery in north-east Gothenburg began back in the 1980s. In the late 1990s an architectural competition was held for its design, won by the landscape architect Åke Andersson.
Planerna på ett höghus började redan 200: Plans for a tower block began as early as 2004 but were halted by the financial crisis. Ground was finally broken for Tyresö View, designed by Archus arkitektur, on 19 June 2012.
Planerna på ett höghus här fanns redan 2: Plans for a high-rise here existed as early as 2004, but the financial crisis put them on hold. Ground was finally broken for Tyresö View on 19 June 2012, and the building was finished in spring 2013.
Planerna på ett höghus i Tyresö centrum: Plans for a high-rise in Tyresö centrum were already on the table in 2004, but the financial crisis put them on hold. Ground was broken in June 2012, and the building was finished in spring 2013.

Plans for a high-rise in Tyresö centre existed as early as 2004 but were halted by the financial crisis. Ground wasn't broken until 19 June 2012, and the same developer then laid out the town park in front, which opened in September 2015.

Plans for a high-rise in Tyresö centrum were already in place in 2004 but were halted by the financial crisis. Ground was finally broken on 19 June 2012, and the building was finished in spring 2013. The same construction company went on to build Tyresö's town park, opened in 2015.
Planerna var stora: flyghamnen skulle ku: The plans were ambitious: the airport was to be able to receive airships and grow to around 200 hectares, which would have meant filling in the Torsviken inlet. The seaplanes needed at least 1,000 metres of water with two landing lanes.
Planerna var storslagna: en stugby med 2: The plans were grand: a holiday village of 200–250 themed cabins, a "Magic House" in partnership with the magician Joe Labero, and a playful learning centre in the style of Tom Tits Experiment science centre. Last of all, a water park and a fairy-tale park based on the Brothers Grimm were to be built.
Plaskdamm under däck: A paddling pool under the deck
Plastiken var en hall av belagd väv som: ‘Plastiken’ was a hall made of coated fabric, held up entirely by air pressure inside, with no supports at all. In the 1960s these were known as Barracuda halls, and this one was only ever meant to be a stopgap for ten years at most.
Plats för 17 tåg i berget: Room for 17 trains in the rock
Platsen bär namnet Wieselgren, och enlig: The square bears the name Wieselgren, and according to Gothenburg City Museum it honours Peter Wieselgren and his son Sigfrid. Peter became Dean of Gothenburg and is seen as a pioneer of the Swedish temperance movement. His followers promised to give up brännvin, Swedish schnapps – though beer and wine were still allowed. The square lies in Rambergsstaden, at the foot of the Ramberget hill.
Platsen efter en man: A place named after a man
Platsen fick namnet Fridhemsplan 1935, m: The square was named Fridhemsplan in 1935, but nobody knows for sure where the name comes from. Before the 1880s, Kungsholmen's new toll gate stood right here.
Platsen har fått namn efter Frantz Zinck: This area is named after Frantz Zinck, who lived on the farm for just five years in the 17th century and never even officially owned it. Yet his name lives on. The neighbourhood has a place in food history too: Gässlingen, at Brännkyrkagatan 93, won a Michelin star in 1999. And the Samariten children's hospital was extended with money left in the will of the singer Jenny Lind.
Platsen har fått namn efter Nybrogatan,: The square is named after Nybrogatan, which in turn was named after a bridge built around 1640 over the inner part of a bay where Berzelii Park is today. The bridge disappeared when the bay was filled in during the 19th century.
Platsen har i alla tider varit en mötesp: People have always met here. Back when the area was Norwegian, before 1658, the crossroads lay just below the Bärby thing site, the local assembly and court, which may be one reason so many roads came together at this very spot.
Platsen hette förr Geteberget, och 1740: This spot was once called Geteberget, and in 1740 tobacco was grown here. Around 1753 the merchant Johan Anders Lamberg renamed it Lisas berg – Lisa's Hill – after his wife Elisabeth Söderberg, whom he called Lisa. And that's how Liseberg got its name.
Platsen som bär ett mansnamn: A place named after a man
Platsen valdes nog för att en gammal byv: The spot was probably chosen because an old village road runs right past it. The carving could also be seen from an area that was most likely a harbour in the Viking Age. Next to it is a burial ground with some fifty graves.
People were already living here in the Iron Age. The name Närlunda may derive from a sacrificial grove dedicated to Nerthus, a Germanic mother and fertility goddess.
Platsen var först en holme i Stora Hamnk: This spot was once an islet in Stora Hamnkanalen, the Great Harbour Canal, known as Järnvågsplatsen after the city's iron weighhouse. During rebuilding in 2019–2020 the foundations of the weighhouse were uncovered – along with three cannonballs by its eastern end.
Plattformarna ligger helt i Nacka kommun: The platforms lie entirely within Nacka municipality – the boundary with Stockholm runs just before the footpath over the tracks. Beyond the station, trains disappear into the Henriksdal tunnel towards Sickla.
Plattformarna är byggda för att kunna bl: The platforms were built so they could be extended to 120 metres, but today they're only 70 metres long. The station sits in the middle of the Hammarkulle Tunnel, just over two kilometres long and opened in 1972. On the express tram you'll reach Brunnsparken in 15 minutes.
Poddstudio vid kajen, som var: A podcast studio by the quay – once
Pojken med den första båten: The boy with his first boat
Pokaler för kung och drottning: Trophies for a king and a queen
Polhemsplatsen fick 1883 sitt namn efter: Polhemsplatsen was named in 1883 after the inventor Christopher Polhem. This is where you'll find the GP building, which the newspaper Göteborgs-Posten moved into in 1935 and which is still the main building of the Stampen media group. A stone's throw away is a statue of Gunnar Gren – one third of the famous Gre-No-Li trio, and one of Gothenburg's most successful footballers of the 20th century.
Polisen som fotograferade socknen: The policeman who photographed the parish
Polisfinka i museets källare: A police cell in the museum basement

Porslinsmuseet visar formgivning från Gu: The Porcelain Museum shows designs from the Gustavsberg studio by Wilhelm Kåge, Stig Lindberg, Berndt Friberg and Lisa Larson, among others. The collection runs to some 40,000 objects, from everyday tableware to bathroom fittings.
Portal med dödsåret: A portal with the year he died
Porten såldes till en kopparslagare: The gate sold to a coppersmith
Portföljen finns i New York: The briefcase is also in New York
Poseidon har klätts ut många gånger, bla: Poseidon has been dressed up many times – as a Chalmers student in a white lab coat, as the Hulk and as Scrooge McDuck, among others. One of Gothenburg's trams also carries his name: today it's car M31 310.
Posten hamnade i Östergötland: The post ended up in Östergötland
Postens huvudkontor Arken ritades av Lis: Arken, the Swedish Post Office's head office, was designed by Lise-Lott Söderlund and got its name in an internal naming competition: the building looks like Noah's Ark stranded on a mountain. The glass surface is roughly the size of six football pitches.
Posthornet sitter kvar: The post horn is still there

Potatisodlingen var länge viktig i Säve,: Potato growing was long important in Säve, and being so close to Gothenburg meant the harvest quickly found buyers. Many of the oldest farms have earth cellars for storing potatoes. Having one could even let you stay put during the land reforms, when other farms were pulled down.
Precis här intill, vid Stensjön, låg Mus: Right here by Lake Stensjön, Mustad's margarine factory was in business from 1897 to 1960. Not far away is Kristinedal, a small-house area completed in 1964, with about a hundred villas, terraced houses and linked houses. It was built by Skånska Cementgjuteriet to designs from Malmö, following the ideal of the day: single-storey houses with brick façades.
Precis intill doftar det jul året om. Gö: Right next door, it smells of Christmas all year round. Göteborgs pepparkaksbageri, the Gothenburg gingerbread bakery, opened in 1924, and these days it bakes just one thing: gingerbread biscuits with a hint of citrus, made to a secret recipe. The shop on Sankt Sigfridsgatan still has its original 1940 interior, and the bakery has been awarded a diploma by the Swedish Gastronomic Academy for its unbeatable gingerbread.
Precis intill ligger Skändla sörgård, en: Right next door is Skändla sörgård, a typical Hisingen farm from the early 1800s and one of the best-preserved farmsteads in the Gothenburg area. The City of Gothenburg bought it in 1966 to save it, and today it's a listed building rented by the Tuve local history society. A little further away rises Skändla rös, a Bronze Age cairn.
Precis intill står Villa Brevik, byggd 1: Right next to us is Villa Brevik, designed by Jacob Gate and built in 1920 for the district judge Franz Stolt. For many years the housing cooperative HSB ran its staff training courses here, and the facade is protected so that it can't be altered. A short way off is Abeniuska villan from 1910, designed by Ferdinand Boberg and Bror Almquist and classed as being of irreplaceable historical value.
Precis vid kajen där operan ligger fanns: Right by the quay where the opera house now stands, there were two buildings out in the river between 1835 and 1850, each with its own pool. They were known as Simskolorna, the Swimming Schools.
Precis vid korsningen mellan Vårby allé: Right where Vårby allé crosses Mogårdsvägen stood Vårby grindstuga, the gatekeeper's cottage – a croft belonging to the Vårby gård estate from 1689. At first it was home to craftsmen, and the last crofters were Johannes Larsson and his wife Eva Charlotta. The cottage was pulled down around 1970. A little further on, a milestone marks the spot where Vårby School stood from 1901 to 1942.
Predikstolen från 1809 sitter ovanför al: Unusually, the 1809 pulpit sits above the altar. The little church bell from 1727 is inscribed 'In Salem is God's tabernacle, and his dwelling place in Zion'.
Predikstolen i Nacka kyrka är från 1600-: The pulpit in Nacka church dates from the 17th century and comes from Nacka's old chapel on the other side of Järlasjön. So does a votive ship with fifty cannons, donated by the sailor Anders Bruun in 1697.
Predikstolen är äldre än kyrkan och komm: The pulpit is older than the church. It comes from the old Nacka chapel, built in 1697 on the other side of Lake Järlasjön, as does a votive ship – a Dutch fifty-gun vessel – donated by the sailor Anders Bruun in 1697.
Premiär med en engelsk mil: Opening day with an English mile
Premiärtåget 1958 kördes av Karl Johan G: The first train in 1958 was driven by Karl Johan Gustavsson, the tramway's oldest driver, and decked out with six flags front and back. The 320 guests rode through almost the entire metro network of the day. At five o'clock the next morning the line opened to ordinary passengers.
Premiärtåget åkte först till Farsta och: The inaugural train first went to Farsta, then at 2.12 pm set off for Hässelby strand with just one stop, at T-Centralen. At 3.24 pm it turned back towards Högdalshallen, so the guests travelled over practically the entire metro network of the day. At five o'clock the next morning the line opened to ordinary passengers.
Premiäråret 1927 fanns ett lopp just för: In the opening year, 1927, there was a race just for farm horses, alongside races for warmbloods and coldbloods. Today Solvalla trotting track is run by the non-profit association Stockholms Travsällskap.
Premiäråret 1927 kördes tolv lopp på Sol: In its first year, 1927, Solvalla held twelve races. By 1930 there were already 36 race days with 225 races and a turnover of more than five million kronor. The Elitloppet, its showpiece trotting race, was first run in 1952.

Pressen Bonnier inte fick köpa: The press Bonnier wasn't allowed to buy
Prins Bertil invigde Skärholmens centrum: Prince Bertil opened Skärholmen Centre on 8 September 1968. It was planned as a regional shopping centre serving 250,000 people across southern Greater Stockholm and is still one of the largest shopping centres in Sweden. It was built during the Million Programme, Sweden's huge housing drive, and is listed in the SOS Brutalism database of brutalist concrete architecture.
Prins Eugen dog 1947 och var den första: Prince Eugen died in 1947, the first member of the Swedish royal family to be cremated. His urn lies by the shore behind the Yellow House. He left the entire estate, art collections and all, to the Swedish state.
Prins Eugen gjorde om det gamla industri: Prince Eugen transformed this former industrial site into a landscaped park. The garden has sculptures by Auguste Rodin, Carl Milles, Antoine Bourdelle and Carl Eldh, among others.
Prinsessan har en lillasyster: The princess has a little sister
Prioritet Serneke Arena hette först Ängl: Prioritet Serneke Arena was first called Änglagården and then Göteborgs Nya Arena. The sponsor's name was announced on the opening day, 10 July 2015.
Prioritet Serneke Arena invigdes den 10: Prioritet Serneke Arena opened on 10 July 2015 at a cost of 800 million kronor. Until the sponsor's name was announced on opening day it was called Göteborgs Nya Arena, and before that Änglagården.
Prisad vagnhall med bilar på taket: An award-winning tram depot with a car park on the roof
Prisma öppnade den 21 november 1960 med: Prisma opened on 21 November 1960 with the film Let's Make Love, starring Marilyn Monroe. The name had been chosen in a vote by readers of the local paper Västerort. The auditorium had 375 blue armchairs.

Privat ända fram till grinden: Private right up to the gate
Pro Patrias barnbördshus vid Thorildspla: Pro Patria's maternity hospital at Thorildsplan opened in 1930 and delivered babies until the turn of the year 1951/52. It was originally intended for women on low incomes or none at all. Today the building is flats.
Processen i Saltsjöqvarn var så automati: The process at Saltsjöqvarn was so automated that no human hand ever needed to touch the food. On the quay, an elevator could lift 100 tonnes of grain straight from the ships up into the tower, and the silos held 6,000 tonnes.
Produkterna fick utmärkelser vid världsu: Almedahls' products won awards at the World's Fairs in Paris in 1857 and London in 1862. By 1900, together with the Jonsered mills, the company was producing roughly half of all the linen made in Sweden.

Programledaren Petra Mede, krögaren Marc: TV presenter Petra Mede, restaurateur Marcus Samuelsson, actor Morgan Alling and singer Björn Rosenström all have ties to Sävedalen. The footballer Bertil “Bebben” Johansson began his career at Sävedalens IF before IFK Göteborg signed him in 1954.
Programledaren och artisten Ayla Kabaca: The TV presenter and performer Ayla Kabaca grew up in Näsbydal with her family – as did her sister, the singer and stage performer Nesrin Kabaca.

Prols fabrik har en röd taktopp med text: The Prol factory has a red roof ridge bearing the name PROL. It's painted with a heat-sensitive pigment that Prol developed in-house, and shifts from light to dark when the temperature changes by more than five degrees. It's best seen at sunrise and sunset.

Promenad upp längs Avenyn: Walk up Avenyn, Gothenburg's grand boulevard
Promenad upp på Västerbron för utsikten: Walk up onto Västerbron, the Western Bridge, for the view
Promenera genom Vita staden: Stroll through Vita staden, the White Town
Promenera längs Långa raden (2 min), anl: Stroll along Långa raden (2 min), laid out at Gustav III’s behest, and see Kavaljershuset, where the gentlemen of the court lived. Since 1991 it has all been part of the Drottningholm World Heritage Site.
Promenera längs bryggorna (2 min) i Göte: Stroll along the jetties (2 min) of Gothenburg's sailing marina. On a clear day you can see Vinga lighthouse far out on the edge of the archipelago.
Promenera på Östra kyrkogården: Take a stroll through Östra kyrkogården, the Eastern Cemetery
Promenera till Guldhedstorget från 1945: Stroll up to Guldhedstorget, a square from 1945
Promenera till Näsby slott vid vattnet: Stroll to Näsby Castle by the water
Promenera till gästhamnen vid Tappström: Stroll to the guest harbour at Tappström
Promenera till parken och badplatsen Sva: Stroll to Svandammen, the park and swimming spot
Promenera till runstenarna i folkhögskol: Stroll to the runestones in the folk high school's park
Promenera till Älvsjö gård: Walk to Älvsjö gård, the Älvsjö estate
Promenera upp till Hersby vattentorn: Walk up to Hersby water tower
Protest i rymdfilm: A protest in a space film
Prova curling i Göteborgs Curlinghall: Have a go at curling at Göteborgs Curlinghall
Provgruvan under köpkvarteret har använt: The test mine beneath the shopping district has been used as a location for films including Joe Hill, Midnight Sun and several Beck crime films. Even Kenny Starfighter has been down here.
Provisoriet som varade i 20 år: The temporary fix that lasted 20 years
Pruta så mycket du kan: Haggle as hard as you can

Prästgården byggdes på 1950-talet på en: The rectory was built in the 1950s on a plot beside the six millraces of Otterbäck along Gamla Särövägen, about 400 metres north-east of the church. The house stands on iron piles driven down to the bedrock.
Prästgården vid sjöns spets: The parsonage at the tip of the lake
Prästtjärnens vatten rinner via Säveån o: Water from Prästtjärnen pond flows out via the Säveån river and reaches the sea 14 kilometres later. Most of the catchment around the lake – 60 per cent – is forest.
Publicisten och riksdagsmannen Sven Adol: Newspaperman and MP Sven Adolf Hedlund bought the Bjurslätt estate as a summer retreat in the 1850s. Around 1860 he had a bog dammed, creating Slätta damm pond, and he also planted woodland all around it.
Publikrekord på bandyfinalen: Record crowd at the bandy final
Publikrekord, sedan parkering: A record crowd, then a car park
Publikrekordet sattes 1945, när 8 526 ås: The attendance record was set in 1945, when 8,526 spectators watched the ice hockey league final between Hammarby and Södertälje SK. More than 4,000 people had to be turned away at the gates.
Publikrekordet är 52 943 åskådare, vid V: The attendance record is 52,943, set at the World Cup qualifier between Sweden and West Germany on 26 September 1965. The club record belongs to Djurgården: 50,750 watched their title decider against IFK Göteborg in 1959.
Publikrekordet, 6 408 åskådare, sattes d: The attendance record, 6,408 spectators, was set on 6 November 2022, when Häcken were presented with the Swedish championship gold after their match against IFK Norrköping.
Pucken är i centrum här: på Björkängens: Here it's all about the puck. Björkängen sports ground has a football pitch and two ice rinks, and Björkängshallen is the home rink of the ice hockey club Huddinge IK. The second rink used to be called Nickehallen, after one of the club's key figures, Bengt 'Nicke' Nilsson. Further on is Kvarnberget, where Stuvsta gård's windmill once stood.
Pumor och giraffer i kvarteren: Pumas and giraffes in the blocks
Punkthusen placerades en bit in på höjde: The point blocks were set back on the heights to preserve the skyline as seen from Lidingöbron bridge. Much of the original vegetation was left standing, and the park with its pond was designed in 1944 by Hermelin & Wedborn.
Punkthuset Filipstadsbacken 36 blev klar: The tower block at Filipstadsbacken 36 was finished first, and on 1 May 1957 the very first Farsta residents moved in. That was no coincidence: only here were there decent transport links, thanks to the station below the hill.
Punschbål i ostindiskt porslin: A punch bowl in East India porcelain
Punschveranda och Kosta-glas: A punch veranda and Kosta glass
Putsaren, Eldaren och Föraren: The Cleaner, the Stoker and the Driver

Pyramiden, Kvadraten och Radien: The Pyramid, the Square and the Radius
Pyramidtakens villastad: The garden suburb of pyramid roofs
På 1100-talet var dagens Hjorthagen en ö: In the 12th century, today's Hjorthagen was an island called Husarne, a name that lives on in Husarviken bay. In 1288 King Magnus Ladulås gave the island to the convent of St Clare on Norrmalm. When Gustav Vasa broke with the Catholic Church, it passed to the Crown.
På 1200-talet skrevs Donsö Dunsø i Valde: In the 13th century Donsö was written Dunsø in King Valdemar Sejr's land register. The name probably comes from dun – down, meaning cotton grass, which grows all over the island.
På 1200-talet skrevs namnet Dunsø i Vald: In the 13th century the name was written Dunsø in King Valdemar Sejr's land register. It probably comes from ‘dun’ – down – meaning the cotton grass that grows in abundance on the island.
På 1300-talet hörde Näsby till Uppsala ä: In the 1300s, Näsby belonged to the Archbishopric of Uppsala. The palatial main house was built by Per Larsson Sparre, probably to designs by Nicodemus Tessin the Elder.
På 1300-talet tillhörde Näsby Uppsala är: In the 14th century Näsby belonged to the Archbishop of Uppsala. In 1571 it was given to the councillor of the realm Gustav Axelsson Banér, and his grandson Per Larsson Sparre probably had the castle-like main house built to designs by Nicodemus Tessin the Elder.
På 1450-talet tog kronan upp ett kronohe: In the 1450s the Crown took over a farm in Ekeby that had long lain deserted. In the 1500s there was both a crown farm and an outlying field here, which became a farm of its own in 1559.
På 1480-talet målade Albertus Pictors ve: In the 1480s Albertus Pictor's workshop painted Bible stories on the church vaults. The paintings were later whitewashed over but uncovered again in 1905–1906. In 2021 the church gained a new concrete chapel, nominated for Stockholm Building of the Year.
På 1500-talet fanns två skattebetalande: In the 1500s there were two tax-paying farmers in Önnered named Räf – fox. That's why people from Önnered are still sometimes known as “foxes”.
På 1500-talet var Skälby en by med två g: In the 1500s, Skälby was a village of two farms, Östergården and Västergården. In 1599, Anders Eriksson, the farmer at Västergården, paid the highest wealth tax in the whole parish.
In the 16th century Skälby was a village of two farms, Östergården and Västergården. In 1599 Anders Eriksson, the farmer at Västergården, paid the highest wealth tax in the parish.
På 1600-talet började Hundhamra kallas B: In the 1600s Hundhamra began to be called Borg. In the 1790s the estate was bought by Johan Liljencrantz, Gustav III's finance minister, who in 1812 built new houses closer to Lake Mälaren. He renamed it Norsborg after his wife, Eleonora.
På 1600-talet drogs en ny väg från Horns: In the 17th century a new road was laid from Hornstull towards Södertälje past Fittja farm, 16 kilometres from Stockholm. This was where travellers heading south changed horses for the first time. The journey to Helsingborg could take around twelve days.
På 1600-talet gick Göta landsväg förbi A: In the 17th century Göta landsväg, the great road south, ran past Alby – the first day's stage from Stockholm. The owner, Jakob Grundel, opened an inn. When the road was rerouted via Fittja in the 1660s, his customers went to the Fittja inn instead.
På 1600-talet gick gränsen mot Danmark s: In the 17th century the border with Denmark ran just south of Tulebosjön lake, and several small border skirmishes broke out here. Cannonballs have been found in the area. A large boundary stone with a 17th-century inscription still stands beside Tulebo Strandväg.
På 1600-talet hade Vårby gård ett tegelb: In the 17th century Vårby farm had a brickworks here, which later became the croft of Bleket. In the 1790s the silk weaver Jakob Jakobsson Hoving turned it into the summer retreat of Johannesdal, and the manor house is still standing.
På 1600-talet hette gatans norra del Ers: In the 1600s the northern part of the street was called Ersta Backe and the southern part Beckgårdz Gatan. A map from 1733 calls the southern stretch Tiärhofs twär gr. Only in the great street-name overhaul of 1885 did the whole thing become Erstagatan.
På 1600-talet kom man vanligen med båt f: In the 17th century people usually came here by boat from Stockholm. A grand Italian-inspired staircase led up to the timber main house, probably the work of one of the leading architects of the day.
På 1600-talet stod de båda runstenarna \: In the 1600s both runestones stood 'within a circle of smaller, round stones'. The piece missing from U 89 was already gone in the earliest drawings, from the 1600s.
På 1600-talet stod stenarna inom en kret: In the 1600s the stones stood within a circle of smaller round stones. U 88 is pale grey gneiss, 110 centimetres high, and an old fracture below the runic band suggests it hasn't been standing upright very long.
På 1600-talet tog man färja över sundet,: In the 17th century people crossed the strait by ferry, and in 1715 the first temporary bridge was built. Today three bridges span it: one for the red metro line, one for the E18 and one for the Roslagsbanan railway.
På 1640-talet byggde friherre Göran Gyll: In the 1640s Baron Göran Gyllenstierna turned Viksjö into a manor with the tax privileges that came with it. In 1679 those privileges were withdrawn because the buildings were dilapidated and the estate badly run. They were restored a few years later, but complaints about the buildings continued.
På 1660-talet fick stora salen stucktak: In the 1660s the great hall was given a stucco ceiling by Giovanni Anthoni and Hans Zauch, known for their work at Skokloster Castle. The walls were hung with gilt leather, and the library is said to have held over 1,000 volumes. Four rooms still have their stucco ceilings.
På 1660-talet köpte den rike Wilhelm Böö: In the 1660s the wealthy Wilhelm Böös Drakenhielm bought the land here, which was mostly useless rock. The reason was probably to dig carp ponds – a must for any 17th-century financier.
På 1660-talet ritade Erik Dahlbergh av R: In the 1660s Erik Dahlbergh drew Rissne farm, and according to his sketch the manor house had four storeys and stepped gables. In 1811 the top two floors were taken down because of rot. The farm has been a listed building since 1983.
På 1680-talet delades marken in i båtsma: In the 1680s the land was divided into båtsmansrotar, units that had to supply the navy with a sailor. Three whole farms together had to provide one seaman with a cottage, a cowshed and clothing. Storegården belonged to unit number 44, along with Högen and Lunnegården.
På 1700- och 1800-talen kallades sträcka: In the 18th and 19th centuries the route across the field was called Kyrkvägen, the Church Road, as it led to Brännkyrka church. Among the Sunday churchgoers was Märta Helena Reenstierna, known as Årstafrun, the Lady of Årsta.
På 1700-talet döpte ägaren Olof Siöberg: In the 1700s the owner, Olof Siöberg, renamed the estate Margreteberg after his wife – he had two wives, both called Margareta. But people kept saying Zinkensdamm, and that name won out.
På 1700-talet kom industrierna hit: en k: Industry arrived in the 18th century: a gunpowder factory and a pitch works at Svindersviken, and Sweden's first calico printing works at Lake Sicklasjön in 1729. In the 19th century well-to-do Stockholmers had summer retreats here, such as the villa Fannyudde.
På 1700-talet kom regler om att gärdesgå: In the 18th century rules were introduced requiring wooden fences to be replaced with stone walls to save timber. This wall kept livestock out of the fields. Today the meadow is used for footgolf.
På 1700-talet var Kristineberg handelsma: In the 18th century Kristineberg was the summer retreat of the merchant Roland Schröder, complete with a pleasure garden and fountains. From the 1860s it became the Freemasons' Orphanage, which eventually housed 120 boys and 50 girls.
På 1700-talet växte industrier fram på g: In the 1700s industries sprang up on the estate's land, including a gunpowder factory and, in 1729, Sweden's first calico printworks by Sicklasjön lake.
På 1760-talet lät Ostindiska kompaniets: In the 1760s Johan Henrik Lefebure, a director of the Swedish East India Company, added a storey to the main house and built two wings. When the Järla sjö housing area was completed in 2004, the manor and its wings were converted into flats.
På 1770-talet byggdes Ingemarshof om eft: In the 1770s Ingemarshof was remodelled on French lines. The main building gained projecting corner pavilions, the courtyard was closed off from the street by two wings and a monumental entrance, and the garden was redesigned in Baroque style.
På 1770-talet hade bergsrådet Gustaf von: In the 1770s the mining official Gustaf von Engeström ran a works on the western part of the island making 'skedvatten' – nitric acid. The name Charlottenburg probably comes from his wife, Abela Charlotta.
På 1770-talet ägdes Skuru gård av majore: In the 1770s Skuru farm was owned by Major Carl Råberg, who improved the buildings and laid out the park and garden.
In the 1770s, Skuru gård was owned by Major Carl Råberg. He improved the buildings and laid out the park and garden.
På 1770-talet ägdes gården av majoren Ca: In the 1770s the estate was owned by Major Carl Råberg, who improved the buildings and laid out the park and garden.
På 1780-talet upplät Nils Anton Barck Ti: In the 1780s Nils Anton Barck made the Tivoliudden headland available to Gustaf Philip Creutz, Gustav III’s chancellor. Barck had Tivoli farm built, along with the Tivoli Pavilion, a party and music pavilion dating from some time between 1780 and 1810.
På 1790-talet blev värdshuset orangeri,: In the 1790s the inn became an orangery growing apricots, lemons and grapes. Haga's garden also grew tomatoes, then known as pommes d'amour – love apples. The harvests were so big that the gardener could sell the surplus.
På 1790-talet bytte gården ägare flera g: In the 1790s the estate changed hands several times. One owner was the wholesaler Peter Hinrik Schön, married to Giovanna Bassi, a famous dancer at the Gustavian opera. In 1795 it was bought by the acting couple Joseph and Marie Anne Desguillons.
På 1800-talet blev kraften från Mölndals: In the 19th century the power of the Mölndal falls laid the foundations for the first industries. Among them were cotton mills, paper mills, a chalk mill, an oil mill and a weaving mill.
På 1800-talet byggdes Stockholm med tege: In the 19th century Stockholm was built with bricks from the Mälaren islands. In 1863, 19 million bricks were delivered, and just over 20 years later 60 million. Barges were towed back and forth to the city in a shuttle service. The street name Tegelbruksvägen (Brickworks Road) near Ekerö centrum recalls the works.
På 1800-talet fanns tobaksodlingar och t: In the 1800s there were tobacco fields and drying barns here. Rålambshov School started out in 1939 as Kungsholmen's municipal girls' school, and until the 1960s a villa stood by Västerbron bridge where a firm sold garden sculptures.
På 1800-talet hade slottet kända gäster: In the 19th century the palace welcomed famous guests such as Fredrika Bremer, Carl Jonas Love Almqvist and Anders Zorn. Today part of the Royal College of Music's chamber music programme is based here.
På 1800-talet ägdes Råcksta gård av gros: In the 1800s Råcksta gård belonged to the wholesaler Knut Ljunglöf, known as the snuff king. His tobacco factory was the biggest snuff factory in the world. In his day Råcksta was a well-run farm with its own mill and sawmill at Kvarnviken.
På 1830-talet byggdes stenhuset på med e: In the 1830s the stone house gained an extra storey, and a new wooden house was built alongside it. In 1870 that wooden house was moved to Fredrikshamn farm on the Göta älv river. Today a 150-metre avenue of trees leads up to the manor.
På 1830-talet kom ångbåtarna till Mälare: When steamboats arrived on Lake Mälaren in the 1830s, Fittja saw fewer and fewer guests. In 1841 Crown Prince Oscar wrote that Fittja shone like the North Star among coaching inns, but that it had fallen quiet and empty now that steamboats splashed off in every direction.
På 1830-talet var Gröndal främst en plat: In the 1830s Gröndal was mainly a place for summer retreats. At the time there were six scheduled rowing-boat routes and four hand-cranked paddle-boat routes running here and to Liljeholmen from central Stockholm, most of them from the Riddarholmen canal.
På 1830-talet, när Gröndal mest var somm: In the 1830s, when Gröndal was mostly summer retreats, there were six regular rowing-boat services and four hand-cranked paddle-boat services out here from central Stockholm. Most of them left from Riddarholmskanalen.
På 1850-talet byggde Frans Oskar Hagman,: In the 1850s Frans Oskar Hagman, managing director of Krooks Petroleum, built a Swiss-style summer villa here: Villa Alphyddan, the 'Alpine Hut'. His children and grandchildren added more villas in the area, but the wooden houses were demolished in the 1960s to make way for new housing.
In the 1850s this was mostly summer villas. Övre Minneberg was owned by the merchant Carl Wilhelm Brink, Stockholm agent for Carnegie Porter. His wife was called Wilhelmina, and she was probably the one who named the place Mineberg, later Minneberg.
På 1870-talet försökte bankiren J. Henri: In the 1870s the banker J. Henrik Palme tried to create a villa suburb in Östermalm, but blocks of flats soon took over. The company behind Hornsberg wanted to avoid that, so it drew up its own plan with precisely defined plots, plenty of greenery and winding roads.
På 1870-talet köptes Stora Villan av hov: In the 1870s Stora Villan was bought by Henrik Wilhelm Bredberg, president of the Court of Appeal, and his family spent their summers on the island until the 1960s. His great-grandson Gunnar Brusewitz spent the summers of 1925–52 here and has written a book about the island.
På 1880-talet skulle här byggas en roman: Back in the 1880s, this was meant to become a romantic villa suburb, Hornsbergs villastad. The project was a complete flop – the company didn't manage to sell a single plot. All that's left of the dream are a few block names and Nelly Sachs park, which used to be called Hornsbergsparken. Instead, the skyline is now dominated by Lindhagsskrapan, a 24-storey, 78-metre tower by Lake Ulvsundasjön. And nearby Hornsbergs hage, a stretch of open meadow, was once where the workers of Kungsholmen used to gather.
På 1890-talet startade Arendals Idrotts-: In the 1890s Arendals Idrotts-Klubb founded a golf club and laid out a course – both among the first in Sweden. Viktor H. Setterberg created an 18-hole course of 1,692 metres at Skalebackarna. During the First World War the course was ploughed up for crops.
På 1920-talet drevs sågen och kvarnen av: In the 1920s the sawmill and the flour mill were powered by a 30-horsepower hot-bulb engine made by Drott in 1924. Since 2010 the sawmill has had a new water wheel.
På 1920-talet var Källhagen förfallet, o: By the 1920s Källhagen was run down, and there were plans to clear the lot before the Stockholm Exhibition of 1930. Hesslingeberg was demolished, but Röda stugan (the Red Cottage) was spared and became the exhibition's site office. Afterwards the inn was revived, with pavilions designed by Torsten Stubelius.
På 1930- och 40-talen byggdes många småh: In the 1930s and 40s many small houses were built here from standard plans, most of them by Edvin Engström. If you were short of money, you could borrow up to 90 per cent of the building costs.
På 1930-talet bodde familjen Järnström i: In the 1930s the Järnström family lived at Kärrtorpet with a workhorse, a pig and a few hens. Mr Järnström hauled gravel and ploughed snow. The cottage was built in 1895 on foundations from the 1790s.
På 1930-talet bodde och arbetade fortfar: In the 1930s around fifty people still lived and worked on the farm, including a maid, cowhands and milkmaids. Potato growing and pig farming were the main business. The farm had some fifteen buildings, among them a smithy and a pigsty.
På 1930-talet byggde Olle Engkvist 600 l: In the 1930s Olle Engkvist built 600 flats in narrow slab blocks, an early experiment in large-scale prefabricated construction. The building site was so chaotic and muddy that the area was nicknamed “Abyssinia”, after the war between Italy and Abyssinia raging at the time.
På 1930-talet döptes kyrkogården om till: In the 1930s the churchyard was renamed Mölndal's West Cemetery. Around 1960 it got its old name back: Fässberg Churchyard.
På 1930-talet fanns 60 kor, 8 hästar, et: In the 1930s the farm had 60 cows, 8 horses, around a hundred hens and a mink farm. Huddinge Hospital was built on part of the land in 1968–1977, and the manor's old park now holds allotments.
På 1930-talet fanns fyra hästar, 15 kor: In the 1930s Slätten had four horses, 15 cows and 15 hens. As the new housing went up in Mälarhöjden and Aspudden, the farm supplied the neighbourhood with milk. Farming carried on right up to the mid-1960s.
På 1930-talet hittade man i ett hål i en: In the 1930s, a whole dozen silver spoons from 1821, stamped 'Kungl. Husgerådskammaren' – the Royal Household's silver store – were found in a hole in one of the oaks. Perhaps one of the servants hid them while Karl XIV Johan sat eating and watching the crowds.
På 1930-talet var Långbrodalsvägen centr: In the 1930s, Långbrodalsvägen was the high street of what was then the district of Långbrodal, buzzing with shops and businesses. When the big shopping area at Kungens kurva opened, the crowds moved there instead. Right next door is Linboda, one of the earliest self-build housing areas in Långbro, where the hundred plots were once simply numbered from one to a hundred. Fewer than twenty of the original houses are still standing today.
På 1930-talet var Sjöberg ett stort spor: In the 1930s Sjöberg was a large area of weekend cabins where the middle classes spent their free time. People took the bus from Norra Bantorget to Edsviken and then a small ferry across to Sjöberg. The villas and terraced houses didn’t arrive until the 1970s.

In the 1930s Sjöberg was a big area of weekend cottages where the middle classes spent their free time. They took the bus from Norra Bantorget to Edsviken and then a small ferry across to Sjöberg and Bergendal.

In the 1930s Sjöberg was a large area of weekend cabins for the middle classes. People took the bus from Norra Bantorget to Edsviken and then a ferry across the water. In the 1970s the cabins gave way to villas, terraced houses and owner-occupied flats.
På 1940-talet byggdes chefsbostaden om t: In the 1940s the manager's house was converted into the shipyard's switchgear station. Windows were blocked with steel plates, and tall doors were made so transformers could be brought in on rails. The building has stood empty since around 1959.
På 1940-talet började det berättas om sp: In the 1940s stories began to circulate about a ghost on ward 7 of the Södra BB maternity hospital. A nurse in full dress uniform was said to appear in rooms 2 and 3.
På 1940-talet vårdades krigsinvalider fr: In the 1940s, soldiers wounded in Finland's Winter War were cared for at Solsunda, and between 1953 and 1968 it treated polio patients. Since 1968 it has been a treatment centre.
In the 1940s war invalids from the Finnish Winter War were cared for at Solsunda. From 1953 to 1968 it took in people affected by polio.
På 1950- och 1960-talen var Bagarmossen: In the 1950s and 60s Bagarmossen was a suburb full of children, and the supervised playgrounds were important meeting places. Two of them have names that suit a district whose name means 'Baker's Bog': Tråget (the Kneading Trough) and Brödkaveln (the Rolling Pin). The third is called Skölden, the Shield.
På 1950-talet fanns ett långt gånget för: In the 1950s there was a well-advanced plan for a tunnel from Johannesplatsen to Lindholmen, with cycle lanes on two levels. It would have been finished around 1965.
På 1950-talet fanns här ett grustag. Top: In the 1950s there was a gravel pit here. The top was built up with demolition rubble to become the highest man-made point on the ridge, 82 metres above sea level. The longest run is 510 metres, with a drop of 84 metres.
På 1950-talet fanns kemtvätten Stensjötv: In the 1950s part of the factory was taken over by the dry cleaner Stensjötvätt, and in 1965 AB Volvo bought the property for an experimental workshop. The factory was demolished in 1978. What remains is the railway embankment, the brick-red office building and a 50-metre retaining wall; the homes on Tallkottegatan were built in 1981.
På 1950-talet grävdes gravfältet Beckomb: The Beckomberga-Råcksta burial ground was excavated in the 1950s, and 190 graves were found. Finds of glass beads, gold rings, gaming pieces, combs and bear claws show that a prosperous farming community lived here from the 3rd century right up to the Viking Age.
På 1950-talet lyste en stor neonskylt fö: In the 1950s a large neon sign for Thule Cacao glowed from the tower of Loket 1, later replaced by an advert for Tulo throat lozenges. Neither sign survives, but on the other side of the bridge the Tulo sign is preserved on Choklad-Thule's old factory.
På 1950-talet lyste små neonskyltar i rö: In the 1950s, little neon signs in red, blue and green glowed outside the shops with words like BLOMMOR, FRISÖR, TOBAK and KONDITORI – flowers, hairdresser, tobacco, patisserie. Most are gone today. This sign hangs above Råcksta krog, facing Multrågatan.
På 1950-talet trodde många att Nybergs c: In the 1950s many people expected Nybergs centrum, south of the station, to become the heart of Järfälla. But because the municipal building with a doctor's surgery went up beside the station in 1949, the centre ended up in eastern Jakobsberg instead. Vällingby was the model for the planning.
På 1950-talet var den nya och den gamla: In the 1950s the new and old schools together had more pupils than any other in Stockholm – 2,240 at their peak. A pedestrian tunnel under Kärrtorpsvägen links the two.
På 1950-talet var träbron så fallfärdig: By the 1950s the wooden bridge was so rickety that it was torn down and replaced by an identical one, with piles driven down to the bedrock. It helped the people of Farsta farm reach their land on Farstanäset. Today's bridge, from 1998, rests on steel beams and concrete.
På 1950-talet visade provborrningar att: In the 1950s, test drilling showed that the infill had settled, leaving a gap about a metre high under the bridge vault. Given the heavy traffic overhead, it was filled with concrete.
På 1960- och 70-talen leddes Kummelbykör: In the 1960s and 70s the Kummelby choir was led by the church musician Anders Lindström, who introduced Anglican choral music into Swedish church life and released several records. In 1995 Sweden's first Alpha course was also held here.
På 1960- och 70-talen verkade Kummelbykö: In the 1960s and 70s the Kummelby choir was based here under church musician Anders Lindström, who introduced Anglican choral music to Swedish church life and released several records. In 1995 the church hosted Sweden's first Alpha course.

In the 1960s and 70s the Kummelby Choir was based here under the church musician Anders Lindström. He introduced Anglican choral music to Swedish church life and released several records. In 1995 the church hosted Sweden's first Alpha course.
På 1960-talet fanns här en slalombacke k: In the 1960s there was a ski slope here called Ullerstupet, with a drag lift and a ski lodge serving coffee – a forerunner of Flottsbrobacken. Nothing of it remains today, and the meadow is now kept open by scything and grazing sheep.
På 1960-talet fyllde Huddinge kommun ut: In the 1960s Huddinge council filled in the water between Storholmen and the mainland with blasted rock and soil. That gave the island a fixed link to the mainland and turned it into a peninsula.
På 1960-talet köpte Göteborg i hemlighet: In the 1960s Gothenburg secretly bought up farmland in Angered and Bergum through front men. In the end the city owned 85 per cent of the land that could be built on, and in 1967 Angered became part of Gothenburg. The newspaper Stockholms-Tidningen called it ‘a Chicago-style land grab’.
På 1960-talet låg Storängens idrottsplat: In the 1960s this was the site of the Storängen sports ground, and in the early 1970s it was covered by an inflatable plastic hall. Today's hall has a vaulted roof spanning the whole facility without pillars, 14 metres high.
På 1960-talet låg in- och utfarten med t: In the 1960s the entrance and exit, with customs checks, still faced Tegeluddsvägen. Between 15 May and 15 September customs staff had to wear white covers on their caps. Some of the checkpoint buildings remain, closed and fenced off.
På 1960-talet reserverades en del av Hag: In the 1960s part of Hagsätra forest was set aside for Salemsleden, a motorway-style road. A 1987 local plan instead proposed keeping the land for recreation, and the road reservation was dropped.
På 1960-talet reserverades en del av sko: In the 1960s, part of the forest was set aside for Salemsleden, a motorway between Huddingevägen and Södertörnsleden. In 1987 it was proposed that the land become a recreation area instead, and the road reservation was dropped.
In the 1960s part of the forest was set aside for Salemsleden, a motorway between Huddingevägen and Södertörnsleden. In 1987 the plan was scrapped and the land kept for recreation.
På 1960-talet saknade Göteborg mark för: In the 1960s Gothenburg was short of land for housing. City secretary Torsten Henrikson secretly bought up 2,600 properties in Angered and Bergum for 60 million kronor, using front men. Stockholms-Tidningen called it a "Chicago-style land grab", and in 1967 Angered became part of Gothenburg.
På 1970-talet fanns planer på bostäder i: In the 1970s there were plans for housing in part of the Rinkeby woods, at Danderydsberg. They were scrapped when the metro wasn't extended towards Täby. Today Rinkebyskogen is a nature reserve.
På 1970-talet grävde Stockholms stadsmus: In the 1970s the Stockholm City Museum excavated some 30 burial grounds with around 1,000 graves, plus ten settlements, around Akalla. It's the museum's largest excavation ever, with finds from the Bronze Age, the Iron Age and the Viking Age.
På 1970-talet undersökte Stockholms stad: In the 1970s the Stockholm City Museum investigated about 30 burial grounds here, with some 1,000 graves, plus ten settlement sites. It was the museum's biggest excavation ever, with finds from the Bronze Age, the Iron Age and the Viking Age.
På 1970-talet var KMH Studios en ren dan: In the 1970s KMH Studios was a veritable dansband factory – home to the Swedish dance-band genre – where Vikingarna recorded their ‘Kramgoa låtar’ albums. In December 1975 Roger Palm recorded a hi-hat overdub for ‘Dancing Queen’ here. The national ice hockey team’s ‘Nu tar vi dom’ was recorded here too.
På 1980-talet byggdes sjukhuset ut kraft: In the 1980s the hospital was greatly expanded, partly because the psychiatric unit at Sankt Jörgen's Hospital was closing. Over 30 houses and a block of flats were demolished, and the new buildings, with an emergency department and operating theatres, opened in 1984 and 1988.
På 1980-talet kalkades sjön för att den: In the 1980s lime was added to the lake to stop it becoming permanently acidified, and the fish and wildlife recovered. Liming continues at regular intervals.
På 1980-talet åkte Stockholm Suburban Su: In the 1980s the Stockholm Suburban Surfers snowboarded here, trudging back up the slopes on foot. In 2004 the club's skate festival, Highvalley Classic, drew more than 2,000 spectators and marked the beginning of Highvalley Skatepark.
På 1990-talet fick tunnelmynningen ljudd: In the 1990s the tunnel mouth was given sound-absorbing walls of yellow perforated brick, and yellow clinker tiles were put up inside the tunnel. The bridge was designed by Ahlgren-Olsson-Silow, the same architects behind Gröndalsbron and Essingebron.
På 1990-talet var Bromsten ett namn blan: In the 1990s Bromsten was a name to reckon with among graffiti writers. It had one of Stockholm's legal walls at the time, a "Hall of Fame", and several of Sweden's leading graffiti artists, such as Circle, Weird, Rustle and Pure, came from here.
