Ritorp anlades redan på 1600-talet som e: Ritorp goes back to the 1600s, when it was a croft belonging to the village of Nederjärva, just south of the country road to Enköping. Today's farmhouse dates from the 1770s. It's a private home, but Stockholm County Museum calls it irreplaceable. Two thousand years ago this spot was under water: the bay of Fröfjärden linked the Baltic waters of Saltsjön with Lake Mälaren, and the shoreline of Brunnsviken was about ten metres higher than it is today.
Ritorp började som ett torp på 1600-tale: Ritorp started out as a croft in the 17th century, and the current farmhouse from the 1770s is described by Stockholm County Museum as irreplaceable. The buildings around it have charming nicknames: the Tower Villa from 1903, the Majhill house from 1911 and the Horseshoe Stable from 1929, which was moved in 1993. And in the northern part, look out for the houses known as Rödingarna, 'the Red Ones'.
Rivningshotet på 1950-talet väckte debat: When the house faced demolition in the 1950s, the newspaper Göteborgs Handels- och Sjöfartstidning took up the debate. The city paid for the move and the company that owned the house donated it. In February and March 1953 it was shifted about 125 metres, a job that took around two weeks, and it became a meeting hall for Sällskapet Länkarna, a sobriety fellowship.
Rivs på Gustav Vasas order: Torn down on Gustav Vasa's orders
Rivö är cirka 0,8 kvadratkilometer och s: Rivö covers about 0.8 square kilometres and has only sparse vegetation. For several hundred years the people of Asperö have brought their cows and sheep here to graze. On the south side you'll find a cholera cemetery, a stone enclosure measuring 13 by 18 metres.
Robert Carlsson köpte kvarnen 1924 och d: Robert Carlsson bought the mill in 1924 and ran it and the sawmill into the 1950s. After that everything fell into disrepair until the municipality took over in 1983. The miller's cottage, the millpond and the stone-lined channel are still there.
Robinia på taket av tunneln: Locust trees on the tunnel roof
Roller derby och Näsan i blöt: Roller derby and an outdoor classroom
Romerskt bad i gamla hallen: A Roman bath in the old pool
Rondellen vid Brommaplan är 100 meter i: The roundabout at Brommaplan is 100 metres across, with six streets feeding into it. This is where Drottningholmsvägen turns off south towards Drottningholm and Ekerö, and county road 275 becomes Bergslagsvägen.
Rondo ritades av Arne Rudberger och gick: Designed by Arne Rudberger, the Rondo was almost entirely brown – façade, velvet sofas, walls and fitted carpet. Only the armchairs were green. Its modern equipment could handle CinemaScope, and from 1976 the cinema was run by Svensk Filmindustri.
Ropsten har blivit större med åren. Sprä: Ropsten has grown over the years. Blasted rock has been dumped into Lilla Värtan ever since 1884, most recently around 2005–2007 for the park-and-ride. On top of that, post-glacial land rise since a painting from 1795 amounts to the sea sitting about a metre lower.
Ropsten har fått sitt namn efter en lite: Ropsten takes its name from a tiny islet off Ropudden, known as Roparstenen, Rope Sten or Roop Sten – the stone where you stood and shouted for the ferry on the other side. The islet was only about 4–6 metres wide above the waterline.
Rosens och Liljans kapell: The chapels of the Rose and the Lily
Roslags Näsby är Roslagsbanans stora väg: Roslags Näsby is the main junction on the Roslagsbanan railway, where the line splits towards Kårsta – formerly Rimbo – and towards Österskär. The station has two island platforms, reached by a footbridge over the tracks. Not far away is Kvarntorpshällen, a rock with a runic inscription discovered in 1943 by the writer Jan Fridegård while he was living in Täby. It contains an unusual word: styvsöner, stepsons.
Roslagsbanan nådde Lahäll 1928, när linj: Roslagsbanan, the Roslagen railway, reached Lahäll in 1928 with the opening of the line from Altorp, and in 1937 it was extended to Näsbypark. Further on, by Näsbyviken bay, is Näsby Castle, today a conference hotel with a restaurant. And to the south, in Djursholm, lies the Svalnäs burial ground, with graves from around 500 to 1000 AD – one of the largest and most impressive in Danderyd.
Roslagsbanan nådde hit 1937, när Stockho: The Roslagsbanan railway arrived in 1937, when the Stockholm–Roslagens Järnvägar company extended the line from Lahäll, and this is where that branch ends. Näsbypark is known as one of Täby's more exclusive neighbourhoods, with villas and terraced houses close to the water at Stora Värtan bay. Right next to the station is Näsbypark Church, part of Täby parish.
Rotundan och Uggleklubben: The Rotunda and the Owl Club
Rud var jordbruksbygd ända tills jordbru: Rud was farming country right up until farming stopped in the 1960s and housing estates sprang up. Grimmered village, first mentioned in 1546, has been preserved with two complete farmsteads, three farmhouses and a few outbuildings.
Rudan klarade isvintern: The crucian carp survived the freeze
Rudan som klarade vintern: The crucian carp that survived winter
Rudbecksparken omfattade tidigare även n: Rudbecksparken once also took in what is now Spårvägsparken, along with the area in between, south of Rålambsvägen.
Rudbecksskolan invigdes den 8 juni 1970: Rudbecksskolan was opened on 8 June 1970 by Ingvar Carlsson, then Minister of Education. The school is named after Reinhold Rudbeck and is Sollentuna's largest workplace.
Rudboda har fått sitt namn efter Rudboda: Rudboda takes its name from Rudboda gård, a farm first mentioned in writing in 1381. The area includes the Lojo block, built in 1970–1973 as part of the Million Programme, Sweden's great housing drive – though the municipality describes it as a smaller-scale, higher-quality version. Out on Bosön there's a student campus from 1998–1999, built to show what the Olympic Village might have looked like had Stockholm won its bid for the 2004 Summer Games. It didn't.

Rudboda is named after Rudboda farm, mentioned in writing as early as 1381. The Lojo block was built between 1970 and 1973 during the Million Programme, Sweden's big housing drive, and the municipality calls it an excellent example of the programme's ideas applied on a smaller scale. On Bosön, student flats were built to show what an Olympic village might look like – ahead of the 2004 Summer Games, which Stockholm never got.
Rudboda kyrka från 1972 är en monterbar: Rudboda Church, from 1972, is a prefabricated "travelling church" that can be dismantled. Services stopped in 2009, and in 2021 the municipality decided it should be demolished or partly relocated. On the square next to it stands the fountain sculpture Winged Cube from 1969.
Rudboda nämns redan 1381 som ruuddobodha: Rudboda is mentioned as early as 1381, as ruuddobodha. Rudde was the medieval word for cleared land, so the name means roughly “the hut by the new clearing”. The Banér family owned every farm on Lidingö from the 1500s until 1774.
Ruddalens IP är hemmaplan för hela fem k: Ruddalen sports ground is home to no fewer than five clubs: Västra Frölunda IF, Utsiktens BK, Assyriska BK, SG Ruddalen IF and Kaverös BK. They've been playing on artificial turf since 2003.
Ruin och sommarvilla: A ruin and a summer villa
Ruinen grävdes ut och restaurerades 1925: The ruin was excavated and restored in 1925, at the city's expense. The dig revealed finely dressed ashlar granite in the lowest courses of the walls – something considered entirely unique in Västergötland.
Ruinen visar en enkel kyrka med långhus: The ruin reveals a simple church with a nave and a square-ended chancel. Excavations turned up finely worked, squared fieldstone in the lowest courses of the walls – a find thought to be completely unique in Västergötland. The remains were dug out and restored in 1925.
Rullande trottoar till torget: A moving walkway to the square
Rundjur under ett kors: A rune beast beneath a cross
Rundtur genom hela nätet: A tour of the whole network
Runhällarna U 80 och U 81: The rune-carved rock slabs U 80 and U 81
Runhällen U 80 berättar: \"Andvätt och G: The rune-carved rock U 80 says: "Andvätt and Gärdar had these runes carved in memory of their father Sven, and Kättilvi in memory of her husband." The carving and its winding ornament are cut so deep that they're easy to see, even though they haven't been repainted for a long time.
Runhällen U 90 söder om gården har inskr: The runic rock U 90, south of the farm, bears the inscription: "Vilfrid had this rock carved in memory of his brother Tärv, and Munde in memory of his brother-in-law."
Runhällen lyder i översättning: Isa lät: Translated, the runes on the rock read: Isa had the stone carved in memory of her stepsons, and Helga had it carved in memory of her sons Dan and Sven.
Runhällen upptäcktes 1927 när en gärdesg: The rune-carved rock was discovered in 1927 when a man building a fence slid down the mossy hillside, dragging the moss with him. It was once painted in several colours, probably black, red and white, and a spring trickles over the rock. It's the only runic inscription in Huddinge still in its original place.
Runhällen är inte signerad, men runforsk: The rune-inscribed rock isn't signed, but the runologist Elias Wessén believed it was probably made by the well-known rune master Fot. The careful craftsmanship, the spelling and the rune forms all resemble his other work.
Runor och latin på samma sten: Runes and Latin on one stone
Runorna berättar att Björn lät hugga häl: The runes tell how Björn had the rock carved in memory of his brother Olev, who was betrayed in Finnveden. They also state that the farm is the ancestral land and inheritance of the Finnvid brothers – a sort of Viking Age deed of inheritance.
Runorna i berghällen i Skylsta säger: ”S: The runes on the rock face at Skylsta say: "Sven had the runes carved in memory of Torbjörn, his brother." The inscription is 1.7 metres long and the runes are six centimetres high.
Runorna lyder: \"Sverker lät göra bron e: The runes read: 'Sverker had the bridge made in memory of Ärengunn, his good mother.' It's unusual for a woman to be honoured like this. A thousand years ago the bridge carried the Göta landsväg highway across the boggy valley. The word 'good' was carved outside the rune band – perhaps for lack of space, or for emphasis.
Runorna lyder: Helga lät resa stenen eft: The runes read: ‘Helga had the stone raised in memory of Svärting, her husband, and of Östen and Häming, her sons. And Igulfast carved.’ The stone was found on 20 October 1953 during digging for fill.
Runorna på Farstastenen lyder: Tore och: The runes on the Farsta stone read: Tore and Sven had the stone raised for Vinut, their brother, Helga's son. The stone is thought to belong together with the Ågesta stone on the other side of Lake Magelungen.
Runorna på U 89 berättar att Helga och H: The runes on U 89 tell us that Helga and Holmfrid had the stone raised in memory of Holmfast, their father. The runes are 7–9 centimetres high, and the carving is well cut and fairly well preserved.
Runorna på berghällen i Skylsta lyder i: Translated, the runes on the rock face at Skylsta read: ‘Sven had the runes carved in memory of Torbjörn, his brother.’
Runristaren hette Öpir: The rune carver was called Öpir
Runskriften berättar: \"Karl gjorde sten: The runic inscription reads: "Karl made the stone in memory of Björn, his kinsman, son of Sven and Bänkfrid in Hammarby … Here he lies beneath this stone." Hammarby is the farm where, according to legend, St Botvid grew up.
Runsten som grindstolpe: A rune stone as a gatepost
Runsten som trappsteg: A runestone used as a doorstep
Runstenen U 121 säger: \"Jobjörn och Sve: Runestone U 121 reads: "Jobjörn and Sven (or Sten) raised the stone in memory of Torfred, Ingetora's husband." It is 1.8 metres tall and originally stood in a burial ground that was cleared when the Hagalund tunnel and Solna station were built.
Runstenen U 122 tecknades av Johannes Bu: Runestone U 122 was drawn by Johannes Bureus in the early 1600s, and even then the top of the stone was missing. The last recorded sighting was in 1763, when the antiquarian Nils Reinhold Brocman noted it on his way to Hälsingland.
Runstenen U 32 är känd från teckningar p: Runestone U 32 is known from drawings made in the 1600s but then disappeared. In the mid-1800s Richard Dybeck found it lying across a drainage ditch, runes facing down. The name Botne on the stone isn't found on any other known runic inscription.
Runstenen U 79 stod från början vid Skes: Runestone U 79 originally stood at Skesta, three kilometres away. The banker Carl Gustaf Cervin had it moved here in the 1860s – reportedly without permission and against the wishes of the people of Skesta. The stone was raised by Gy and Sven in memory of their father Bärsa and carved by Ärnfast.
Runstenen U 88 användes under 1800-talet: In the 1800s runestone U 88 was used as a doorstep in Lindal, and then went missing for a while. In 1938 it was found lying on a burial mound at Skälby gård and was raised next to U 89. In the 17th century the stones stood within a ring of smaller round stones.
Runstenen U 88 i Skälby, en bit härifrån: Runestone U 88 in Skälby, not far from here, has had an eventful life. For at least part of the 19th century it served as a doorstep in Lindal, so people walked over the Vikings' words every day. Then it disappeared for a while, until it was found in 1938 at Skälby Farm, lying on a burial mound. Today it stands beside its companion, U 89.
Runstenen U 91 föll omkull med texten ne: Runestone U 91 toppled over, face down, and was forgotten. When it was found in 1886 it was blasted apart to be used in building a barn – and only then did anyone realise what it was. The pieces were put back together and the stone was raised in the park.
Runstenen flyttades i hemlighet: The runestone was moved in secret
Runstenen hittades den 20 oktober 1953 v: The runestone was found on 20 October 1953 during digging at Nyodlingsvägen 4. It reads: Helga had the stone raised in memory of Svärting, her husband, and of Östen and Häming, her sons. The stone is two metres tall.
Runstenen i Eneby är delvis skadad, men: The Eneby runestone is partly damaged, but what can be read runs roughly: Asbjörn ... Gunnälv had the stone raised in memory of Åsulv, their father.
Runstenen i Troxhammar bär en kort men g: The runestone at Troxhammar bears a short but moving inscription: "Kjulak had the stone raised for Kvig, his good son." It dates from the Viking Age, and the runes are 5–6 centimetres tall.
Runstenen i Troxhammar säger: Kjulak lät: The runestone at Troxhammar says: “Kjulak had the stone raised in memory of Kvig, his good son.” The runes are 5–6 centimetres tall. The name Kjulak also appears on another runestone, Sö 339.
Runstenen lät Forkunn resa, och en bro b: Forkunn had the runestone raised, and a bridge built, in memory of her son Torger and of Åsgisl. Luckily, a paper rubbing was made and photographed in 1902. The fragment found in 1934 is grey granite and is kept in the Swedish History Museum's collections in Tumba.
Runstenen restes av Anund efter Vikinge,: The runestone was raised by Anund in memory of Vikinge, his father, 'Store's son'. The decoration is a serpent coiled in a figure of eight, its upper loop enclosing a Christian cross and its lower loop holding an extra line of runes.
Runstenen ristades av Ärnfast mellan 105: The runestone was carved by Ärnfast between 1050 and 1080 and is counted among his finest work. The banker Carl Gustaf Cervin is said to have moved it here without permission and against the wishes of the people of Skesta, and there's no historical basis for its position on a Viking grave.
Runstenen som blev grindstolpe: The runestone that became a gatepost
Runstenen som blev tröskel: The runestone that became a doorstep
Runstenen som flyttades i smyg: The runestone moved on the quiet
Runstenen som inte kunde stå still: The runestone that couldn't stay put
Runstenen som murades in i kyrkväggen är: The runestone set into the church wall is made of an unusual pink sandstone. It was raised by sons in memory of their mother, and they also had a bridge built.
Runstenen som sitter inmurad under torne: The runestone set into the wall below the tower's south-west corner reads "...and Tove, they had this stone raised in memory of...". The name Tofi is unusual in Swedish runic inscriptions. Part of the stone was covered over when the tower was repaired.
Runstenen som sprängdes: The runestone that was blown up
Runstenen som var trappsteg: The runestone used as a doorstep
Runstenen säger: ”Sibbe och Jorun och To: The runestone reads: 'Sibbe and Jorun and Torgun and Ingegärd, the siblings, had this stone raised in memory of Tjarve, their father, and Gudmod in memory of her husband.' The name Tjarve also appears on a runestone in Uttran, only about 3 km away – perhaps the same man.
Runstenen utanför hembygdsmuseet bär ins: The runestone outside the local history museum bears the inscription: Björn and Fulluge had the stone cut ... their. The rest of the text has been lost.
Runstenen utanför museet flyttades hit i: The runestone outside the museum was moved here in October 1988. The inscription says that Björn and Fulluge had the stone carved in memory of someone, but that part of the text is missing.
Runstenen vid hembygdsmuseet bär inskrif: The runestone by the local history museum reads "Björn and Fulluge had the stone carved ... their". The end is damaged, so we don't know who it was raised for.
Runstenen vid porten säger att Jarlabank: The rune stone by the gate says that Jarlabanke raised the stones in his own memory while he was still alive, built a bridge for his soul and ‘alone owned all of Täby’. In the 17th century the stone served as the threshold of the church door.
Runstenen vid slottets infart: The runestone at the palace entrance
Runstenens inskrift berättar att ”Björn: The runestone's inscription reads: 'Björn and Fulluge had the stone carved … their …'. The end is damaged, so we don't know who the stone was raised for.
Runstensfragmentet U 63 i Spånga kyrka ä: The runestone fragment U 63 in Spånga kyrka is made of red sandstone. The first piece was found in 1910, but drawings of the stone exist from as early as the 17th century. The little that can still be read says: '... stone in memory of Björn ...'.
Runstensfragmentet i Täby centrums bibli: The runestone fragment in Täby centrum's library bears only a few words. In modern English they read "Holmi had …" – the rest of the sentence is missing.
Runt 14 000 studenter läser vid Södertör: Around 14,000 students attend Södertörn University, which offers police training and teacher training with an intercultural focus, among other things. Much of the research here is about the Baltic Sea and Eastern Europe, backed by Östersjöstiftelsen, the Foundation for Baltic and East European Studies, which the government set up in 1994. The library is open to everyone, and right next to it is Flemingsberg Park, winner of Huddinge's building award in 2021.
Runt 1572 samlade Johan III:s kanslist R: Around 1572, John III's clerk Rasmus Ludvigsson collected old Swedish coins as part of the dispute with Denmark over the right to the three crowns on the national coat of arms. When the castle burnt in 1697, the royal coin collection was rescued and taken to Helgeandsholmen.
Runt 1900 köpte staden husen för att riv: Around 1900 the city bought up the houses to demolish them under the Lindhagen plan, and Ringvägen was supposed to end here. That it didn't is largely thanks to Anna Lindhagen, daughter of the plan's author Albert Lindhagen, who as early as the 1910s was campaigning to preserve old Stockholm neighbourhoods.
Runt 1950 fanns mer än 100 växthus i sta: Around 1950 there were more than 100 greenhouses in the district. The market gardens were sold off one by one, and the last, Solbackens Handelsträdgård, closed in 2006. Houses now stand on the land.
Runt Farsta torg fanns förr varuhusen No: Farsta torg was once ringed by the department stores Nordiska Kompaniet (NK), Kvickly and Tempo. By 2008 only Åhléns – the old Tempo – was left. The square was designed by Backström & Reinius and opened on 23 October 1960.
Runt Järfälla kyrka har runstenar kommit: Runestones have a habit of coming and going around Järfälla Church. In 1728 Olof Celsius the Elder found one inside the church, probably used as a step. It then vanished until seven fragments turned up in 1939. Another stone lay outside the porch door and was already described back then as lost and worn – it's still missing today. Next door is Kyrkbyn, the church village, once known as Järfälla gård.
Runt Rådasjön breder ett naturreservat u: A nature reserve surrounds Lake Rådasjön, with pastures, broadleaf woodland and alder swamp forest teeming with wildlife. The area around Mölnlycke is famous for its masses of wood anemones, which turn the ground white in spring. Also by the lake is Råda säteri, a manor with wings and farm buildings, listed since 1969.
Runt Titteridamm slingrar sig Titteridam: Titteridammsvägen, Titteridammsstigen and Titteridammshöjden all wind around Titteridamm pond, and next to it is a neighbourhood of detached houses that shares the pond's name.
Runt för att slippa hörn: Round, so there were no corners
Runt hela ön slingrar sig Lovöns fornsti: The Lovön heritage trail winds right round the island – an 18-kilometre walking route past farms, an Iron Age burial ground and a rune-carved rock from the late 11th century. Since 2014 the island has been part of the Lovö nature reserve, which covers just over 3,000 hectares.
Runt hörnet ligger kvarteren Kampö och H: Around the corner are the Kampö and Hartsö blocks, terraced houses from the late 1950s that the City Museum has marked green as especially valuable. A short way off rise the offices of Televerket, the old national telecoms agency – the headquarters of Telia Company until 2016. They were designed by Bengt Hidemark and Gösta Danielson, and the buildings on Mårbackagatan won the Kasper Salin Prize, Sweden's top architecture award.
Runt sekelskiftet 1900 byggdes sommarvil: Around the turn of the 20th century summer villas were built here, drawn by the views over Lake Mälaren and the steamboats to Stockholm. At the time a steam-powered sawmill stood by the strait, and on Gällstaö charcoal stacks smouldered to fuel it.
Runt sjön går en 1,8 kilometer lång slin: A 1.8-kilometre loop called Lugna promenaden, the 'calm walk', runs around the lake and is easy going even if you have limited mobility. The lake is 5.6 metres deep at its deepest.
Runt sjön går ”Lugna promenaden”, en 1,8: The "Lugna promenaden", the Easy Walk, circles the lake: a 1.8-kilometre loop that's easy going even if you have limited mobility. There are picnic spots along the way, and you can both swim and fish in the lake.
Runt torget låg en gång flera varuhus: N: Several department stores once stood around the square: Nordiska Kompaniet, Kvickly and Tempo. By 2008 only Åhléns, the former Tempo, was left. In 2000 a link was built between the old NK and Tempo buildings.
Runt torget står vita skivhus på elva vå: The square is ringed by white eleven-storey slab blocks. Tallest of all is Frölunda Specialist Hospital, at 55 metres and 17 floors.
Runt år 1900 styckade godsägaren Max Wib: Around 1900 the landowner Max Wibom divided up plots he called Nya Hufvudsta. The area got two railway stations of its own, Huvudsta station and Huvudsta central – both now closed.
Runtexten börjar ”Karl gjorde stenen eft: The runic inscription begins: 'Karl made the stone in memory of Björn, his kinsman.' The rune carver Karl is thought to have trained abroad, perhaps in England, Lund or on Gotland. The Latin text asks Christ that Björn be free from sin.
Rutschbanorna som lockade: The slides that drew the crowds
Rya skog är ett litet urskogsparti mitt: Rya skog is a small patch of ancient forest squeezed between the Rya works and the refineries west of Älvsborg Bridge. Hisingsparken is Gothenburg's largest park.
Rya skog är känd för sitt fågelliv, och: Rya Forest is known for its birdlife, and species such as the lesser spotted woodpecker still breed here. In spring 1849 a pair of white storks built a nest in an oak here, and in the second half of the 1800s hobbies are also said to have nested in the woods.
Ryaverkets skivfilteranläggning, ritad a: The disc filter plant at the Ryaverket sewage works, designed by KUB arkitekter, won the Kasper Salin Prize in 2010. It's not often that part of a wastewater plant wins Sweden's best-known architecture award.
Rylander & Rudolphs främsta produkt var: Rylander & Rudolph's main product was manganese dioxide batteries, made under the Frenchman Georges Leclanché's patent. About half the workers were women, and some ten children in their early teens also worked at the factory.
Rymdstation vid spåret: A space station by the tracks
Rymdtorget byggdes 1970 och är hjärtat i: Rymdtorget, Space Square, was built in 1970 and is the heart of Bergsjön, where the streets are named after space and the universe – Tellusgatan, for instance. On the square is Kulturhuset Bergsjön, the Bergsjön Culture House, with a library, café, studios, an exhibition hall and even a music studio. It offers everything from music and art to crafts and children's events.
Rymdtorget byggdes 1970, och gatunamnen: Rymdtorget, Space Square, was built in 1970, and the streets around it keep up the space theme, with names such as Tellusgatan and Merkuriusgatan. On the square is the Bergsjön Culture House, with a library, a music studio, artists' studios and an exhibition hall, offering a mix of concerts, crafts and activities for children.
Rymdtorget, Kometgatan, Kosmosgatan, Uni: Rymdtorget, Kometgatan, Kosmosgatan, Universumsgatan, Meteorgatan – Space Square, Comet Street, Cosmos Street, Universe Street and Meteor Street. Here in Bergsjön, the street names are straight out of outer space. Just up the road is Rymdtorget, built in 1970, home to Kulturhuset Bergsjön, the local cultural centre. It has a library, café, studios, a music studio and an exhibition hall, with everything from music and art to events for children.
Rysk empir med stenar i putsen: Russian Empire style with pebbled render
Ryska ikoner i skogsbacken: Russian icons on a wooded hillside
Ryska revolutionen gav företaget en kris: The Russian Revolution plunged the company into a crisis that ended in bankruptcy in 1922. After several mergers and name changes, it's now Volvo Construction Equipment. The old factory buildings are used for trade fairs and events.
Räddad av en bit mossa: Saved by a scrap of moss
Räddat av planerarens egen dotter: Saved by the planner's own daughter
Rävekärr byggdes 1969–1974. Förut gick o: Rävekärr was built between 1969 and 1974. The area used to stop at Alebäcken stream in the south, but the new housing went up on the far side of it too. The first tenants moved in in 1973, and the school and nursery were finished in December 1974.
Rävekärr har fått sitt namn efter hemman: Rävekärr takes its name from the old Rävekärr homestead in Fässberg parish. One of its farms was the Rävekärr vicarage, on the site where Fågelbergskyrkan church stands today. The last vicar moved out in 1978, and the vicarage was demolished in January 1984.
Råcksta träsk är bara 2,3 meter djup men: Råcksta träsk is only 2.3 metres deep, but it's an important home for dragonflies and amphibians. Its outflow runs down to Lake Mälaren past the Kvarnviken mill from 1883, which is still put to work once or twice a year.
Rådan is first mentioned in 1599 as a croft. It went on to be a farm foreman's residence, a manor, a boarding school in 1890, military quarters in the 1940s and a police academy in 1970. Silverdal farm, for its part, was an inn until 1860 and then a village shop until the late 1950s.
Rådasjöns naturreservat bildades 2006 oc: The Rådasjön nature reserve was created in 2006 and lies between Mölndal, Mölnlycke and Pixbo. It stretches across both Härryda and Mölndal municipalities.
Rådhuset byggdes troligen 1767 som tillb: The town hall was probably built in 1767 as an extension to a stone customs house. It has also housed a jail, and there was a library here from 1868 until the mid-1930s. It served as the courthouse until 1928.
Rådmannen som bytte namn: The alderman who renamed the farm
Rådsparken, alldeles i närheten, har båd: Just nearby is Rådsparken, a park with both an animal park and a sports ground, next to Huddinge Church, which has been the parish church since the Middle Ages. A fragment of a runestone is set into the church's outer wall, and just east of the church lay the assembly site of Tomtabergh, mentioned as early as 1433. The church school close by opened in 1914 and was threatened with demolition in the 1950s, but it survived – today the parish choirs rehearse there.
Rågsved nämns första gången 1627, då som: Rågsved is first mentioned in 1627, as Rogsueedh. Cottages belonging to the Älvsjö estate stood here, and two of them, Bjursätra and Snösätra, have given their names to parts of today's district.
Rågsved är en stadsdel med två ansikten,: Rågsved is a district with two faces, split down the middle by the metro. On one side is the iconic horseshoe-shaped shopping centre; on the other, the buildings climb up a hill. The station opened in 1959 and is about 8.5 kilometres from Slussen.
Rågsved är känt för sin ikoniska hästsko: Rågsved is known for its iconic horseshoe-shaped shopping centre, and the metro station was the end of the line when it opened in 1959. On the platform stands the bronze sculpture Fågel Grön, Green Bird, by the artist Björn Selder. A little further away in Högdalen is Cyklopen, a self-run cultural centre staffed entirely by volunteers. Its first building was destroyed in 2008 in an arson attack thought to be the work of Nazis, but the association simply built a new one.
Rågsved, skrivet Rogsueedh, nämns första: Rågsved, spelt Rogsueedh, is first mentioned in 1627. The City of Stockholm bought the land from the Älvsjö estate in 1930, but it remained undeveloped until the mid-1950s.
Rågsveds station öppnade den 14 november: Rågsved station opened on 14 November 1959 and was the terminus until 1960. From here it's 8.5 kilometres to Slussen.
Råsta nämns som kronoegendom 1375 och va: Råsta is mentioned as Crown property in 1375 and was one of four large farms in northern Sundbyberg in the Middle Ages. The main house from 1779 no longer exists, and today the farm is given over to horses, including for the Sundbyberg riding club.
Råsta nämns som kronoegendom redan år 13: Råsta is mentioned as crown property as early as 1375. The main house from 1779 no longer survives; the present one dates from the 1940s. Today the farm is used for equestrian activities, including by Sundbyberg Riding Club.
Råstasjön är en känd fågelsjö, och näkte: Råstasjön is a well-known birding lake, and nightingales breed here unusually densely. Seven species of bat have been recorded around the lake, which is a rich tally even by national standards. The footpath around the lake is 2,117 metres long.
Råsunda kyrkas 22 meter höga klockstapel: Råsunda church's 22-metre bell tower is crowned by a gilded cockerel designed by Erik Höglund. The three bells are named Faith, Hope and Love, and the forecourt is called God's Green Pastures.
Råsunda smygöppnade den 18 april 1937 nä: Råsunda had a soft opening on 18 April 1937, when AIK beat Malmö FF 4–0. At the official opening on 17 May, King Gustaf V cut the ribbon before the international against England – which also ended 4–0, but to England.
Råsunda vattentorn, ritat av Sigge Crons: Råsunda water tower, designed by Sigge Cronstedt, opened in 1910 and was taken out of service in the early 1950s. Since 1994 it's been a home – the tower has been converted into flats. On a rocky hill by Näckrosparken, the Water Lily Park, stands Råsunda Church. And on the southern shore of Lake Råstasjön is Råstahällen, Solna's only natural monument, a slab of bedrock where you can see three criss-crossing sets of scratches left by the ice during the last Ice Age.
Råsunda är en av bara två arenor i värld: Råsunda is one of only two stadiums in the world to have hosted both a men's and a women's World Cup final – the other is the Rose Bowl in Pasadena. Brazil beat Sweden 5–2 in the 1958 men's final, and Norway beat Germany 2–0 in the 1995 women's final.

Råsunda is one of only two stadiums in the world to have staged both the men’s and the women’s World Cup final. Norway won the 1995 women’s final, beating Germany 2–0. The other stadium is the Rose Bowl in Pasadena.

Råsunda is one of just two stadiums in the world to have hosted both the men’s and the women’s World Cup final. In 1958 Brazil beat Sweden 5–2, and in 1995 Norway beat Germany 2–0. The other stadium is the Rose Bowl in Pasadena.
Råsundavägen hette från början Stockholm: Råsundavägen was originally called Stockholmsvägen and was built as an embankment between rocky ridges so the tram line to Råsunda and Sundbyberg could be laid. Most of it was built by Kreuger & Toll, as one of the company's first contracts.
Röd våg och lysande tefat: A red wave and glowing saucers
Röda Korsets Högskola: Röda Korsets Högskola, the Swedish Red Cross University
Röda Korsets folkhögskola startade 1990: The Red Cross folk high school – a Swedish adult education college – opened in 1990 in the old crown distillery by Gripsholm Castle in Mariefred. In 2004 it moved to Stockholm, and since 2010 all its courses have been held in Skärholmen's town centre.

The Red Cross folk high school started in 1990 in the old Crown distillery at Gripsholm in Mariefred. In 2004 it moved to Stockholm, and since 2010 the whole school has been in Skärholmen's centre. Some courses travel, with part of the teaching held abroad.
Röda Sten konsthall: Röda Sten konsthall, the art centre
Röda Sten konsthall under Älvsborgsbron: Röda Sten art centre, beneath the Älvsborg Bridge
Röda skolan från 1903 hade åtta lärosala: The Red School from 1903 had eight classrooms: one for each year of the seven-year elementary school, plus a room for cardboard crafts. At first the school was lit by paraffin lamps and heated with iron stoves. Today Örby library occupies part of the ground floor.
Rödakorssystrar till kriget: Red Cross nurses off to war
Rödbo saknade länge egen kyrka, och begr: For a long time Rödbo had no church of its own, and funerals had to be held in the open air. A funeral chapel paid for by local donations was built in 1929. Even so, the first regular Sunday service wasn't held until New Year's Day 1974, and that autumn the chapel was consecrated as the parish church.
Rödbo socken tillhörde Norge fram till 1: Rödbo parish belonged to Norway until 1658. From 1783 to 1940 a ferry crossed at Vedbacka, later replaced by a bridge. Rödbo only became part of Gothenburg in 1974.
Rödingarna byggdes som bostäder åt SJ:s: The Röding houses were built for Swedish Railways staff at Ulriksdal station. When two of them were threatened by a new road ramp, Solna decided to move them instead. They then sat propped up on beams beside Ulriksdal golf course until November 2020.
Rödkinda barnhem är en stor rödfärgad tr: Rödkinda children's home is a large red-painted wooden villa with a mansard roof, built in 1916–1917 to designs by Kellgren & Hammarling. It sits on a hill sloping down towards Lake Magelungen. In 1924, eleven children lived here and were taught the ordinary elementary school curriculum.
Röhsska museet för design och konsthantv: Röhsska museet, the museum of design and craft
Rökstenen på stationsväggen: The Rök runestone on the station wall
Rönneberga ägs av fem fackförbund: Byggn: Rönneberga is owned by five trade unions: the building workers', painters', electricians', property workers' and Seko unions. Today businesses use the venue as well.
Rörstrands slott har kvar sin 1600-talsk: Rörstrand Castle has kept its 17th-century character, with smooth rendered facades and black-glazed roof tiles. Inside are some of the Rörstrand factory's finest tiled stoves – and a castle café for a fika, a coffee and cake.
Röset ligger vid gränsen mellan Bohuslän: The cairn stands on the border between Bohuslän and Västergötland. Until the Treaty of Roskilde in 1658, this was the border between Sweden and Norway.
Röset som gav sjön namn: The cairn that named the lake
Röset som låg vid stranden: The cairn that stood on the shore
Rösjön anses ha fått sitt namn efter ett: Rösjön is thought to be named after a cairn (röse) on an island in the southern part of the lake. The cairn marked the boundary between the old districts of Danderyd skeppslag and Sollentuna hundare.
Rösjön är cirka 1 500 meter lång och 300: Rösjön is about 1,500 metres long and 300 metres wide. Its waters are home to perch, pike, roach, bream, tench, burbot, rudd and bleak, among others, and there are crayfish too. The lake drains through the Fjätursbäcken stream into Lake Fjäturen.
Rösjön lake is about 1,500 metres long and 300 metres wide. It's home to perch, pike, roach, silver bream, common bream, tench, burbot, rudd and bleak – and crayfish too.
Rösjön är en avlång sjö, 7,3 meter djup,: Rösjön is a long, narrow lake, 7.3 metres deep. Most of it belongs to Sollentuna, with a smaller part in Danderyd – while Täby, right next door on the eastern side, doesn't get a single metre of shoreline. A little further on, Landsnoravägen runs for about three kilometres past Edsberg Palace and Landsnora kvarn, a mill that is Sollentuna's oldest secular building.
Rösträtt och åttatimmarsdag: Votes for all and the eight-hour day
Rött hus med vita knutar: A red house with white corners
Rött och gult, en färg per länga: Red and yellow, one colour per row
S.A. Hedlund var huvudredaktör för Göteb: S.A. Hedlund was editor-in-chief of Göteborgs Handels- och Sjöfartstidning and a leading cultural figure in the city. Around 1860 he had Slätta damm pond created, and today it's home to many species of birds.
S:t Ansgars kyrka från 1963 ritades av O: St Ansgar's church from 1963 was designed by Olof Malmgren, who also drew the parish hall and the tower block next door. The 16-storey tower first housed YMCA student accommodation but is now partly a hotel. Together they frame a small square.
S:t Eriksgatan, kaféer och butiker: S:t Eriksgatan, for cafés and shops
S:t Tomas kyrka murades på Celsings förs: At the suggestion of the architect Peter Celsing, S:t Tomas church was built by trainee bricklayers. This kept costs down and gave the walls a more irregular, lively surface. The façades have no eaves, plinth or drainpipes.
SF lanserade Fontänen som premiärbiograf: SF launched Fontänen as a premiere cinema, screening the same new releases as the cinemas in the city centre. During the 1960s the premieres dwindled, and Fontänen became an ordinary suburban cinema.
SF lämnade Reflexen 1977, och sedan dess: The SF cinema chain left Reflexen in 1977, and since then it has been run by a non-profit cultural association. During the 2006 renovation the old neon sign went back up after many years' absence and received an honourable mention as Sign of the Year. SF's old projectors kept running until 2013.
SIAB levererade sina hus i storelement s: SIAB delivered its houses as large prefabricated sections assembled on site, while Skånska Cementgjuteriet built its houses on the spot. That's why Skånska's areas are more varied and fit the terrain better. Because of the state loans, the houses could be no bigger than 140 square metres.

SIAB delivered its houses as large prefabricated panels assembled on site, while Skånska Cementgjuteriet built its houses on the spot. Skånska's areas ended up more varied and better suited to the terrain. Because of state loans, no house could be larger than 140 square metres.
SICS bildades 1985 på initiativ av Erics: SICS, the Swedish Institute of Computer Science, was founded in 1985 on the initiative of Ericsson and the national telecoms agency Televerket. In part it was a response to Japan's investment in "fifth-generation" computers, which were meant to communicate in natural language.
SJ skaffade byggmark genom att fylla ut: The state railways, SJ, created building land by filling in Årstaviken bay with rock blasted from the Nyboda tunnel and from a rocky knoll that was blown away – and that's where Marievik stands today. Next door was Maryvik's felt factory, which made lubricating pads and boiler felt.
SKF började med Wingquist och 15 anställ: SKF started out with Wingquist and 15 employees. By 1909 it already had branches in Copenhagen, Paris and Milan, and warehouses as far away as Melbourne and Yokohama. By 1912 the workforce had reached 1,300.
SKF:s allra första kullagerorder kom frå: SKF's very first ball-bearing order came from ASEA in Västerås and is dated 16 March 1907. Just four years later the company opened its first factory abroad, in Luton, England.
SM-final på sjöisen: A national final on the frozen lake
SM-finalen i bandy 1912 spelades på Råst: The 1912 Swedish bandy championship final was played on the natural ice of Råstasjön lake. Since the 1960s the annual Två sjöar runt race – Round Two Lakes – has circled Råstasjön and Lötsjön.
SM-finalen i bandy spelades här 2013 och: The Swedish bandy championship final was played here in 2013 and 2014. In the first year Hammarby faced Sandviken in front of 38,474 spectators – a record for a championship final.
SS Manhem bildades 1906 och har runt 15: SS Manhem was founded in 1906 and fields around 15 teams in the chess league system – more than any other club in Sweden. It has also produced several Swedish junior champions.
SVT Väst lät folk rösta fram namn. Bastu: Swedish broadcaster SVT Väst let the public vote on names. The sauna became Svettekörka (Svettekôrka in local dialect – roughly 'Sweat Church'). In the vote for the pool, Pöl Harbour won, with Inälvsbadet and Kallhalla coming second and third.
Safjället har använts av människor under: People have made use of Safjället for a very long time. The nature reserve holds burial cairns, stone settings, a couple of stone cists and a hillfort.
Salems allra första kyrka var av trä. En: Salem's very first church was built of wood. According to the legend of St Botvid, the saint lay buried here for nine years before his brother moved his remains in 1129 to a new church on Hammarby land. That church was later replaced by the stone church that bears his name: Botkyrka.
Salems centrala bebyggelse hette förr Sa: The centre of Salem used to be known as Salemstaden. For a long time the area was crofters' land belonging to the Fågelsta farm. One of the crofts, Bergfana, was built in the late 1840s, and the first to move in were Eric Ode – a former soldier who worked on the estate – and his family. When the railway arrived in 1860, Bergfana became one of Salem's four lineman's cottages, where the people who kept watch over the track lived.
Salems kyrka står på en udde söder om Bo: Salem Church stands on a headland south of Lake Bornsjön, surrounded by great oaks, limes and birches. The old Södertälje road, Gamla Södertäljevägen, runs right past, and the whole area is rich in ancient remains. Follow the road east and you'll reach St Botvid's Spring, a cold-water spring at the south-eastern tip of the lake. About fifty metres from the spring stands the Söderby runestone.

Salem Church stands on a headland south of Lake Bornsjön, framed by big oaks, limes and birches. The old Södertälje road, Gamla Södertäljevägen, runs past the church, and the whole area is rich in ancient remains. Follow the road east and you'll reach Sankt Botvid's spring, a cold spring at the south-eastern tip of Bornsjön. About fifty metres from it stands the old Söderby runestone.
Salemstaden byggdes i slutet av 1960-tal: Salemstaden was built in the late 1960s, mostly as three-storey blocks and terraced houses. By Salem's centre you'll find the library and the Murgrönan cinema, and there's a swimming baths nearby.
Salen som bär arkitektens namn: The hall named after its architect
Salong för kulturlivet: A salon for the cultural set
Salongen hade 375 blå fåtöljer och kunde: The auditorium had 375 blue armchairs and could screen films in CinemaScope. The curtain was designed by the artist Tor Hörlin and showed the view from his studio at Kornhamnstorg.
Salongen hade från början 339 platser, r: The auditorium originally had 339 seats, red wall panels and a white-and-silver curtain. When the cinema was refurbished in 2017–2018, it was fitted with 120 second-hand seats from the Fontänen cinema in Vällingby. The neon sign in blue script is still in place.
Salongen hade kraftig lutning och 375 få: The auditorium had a steep rake and 375 blue-upholstered armchairs, and the screen could show CinemaScope. The curtain was designed by the artist Tor Hörlin and showed the view from his studio at Kornhamnstorg.
Salthandlaren Gustav R. Setterberg byggd: The salt merchant Gustav R. Setterberg built a villa out of old salt barges. It's said to have been the first villa in Arendal, probably from the 1870s, and was later rebuilt by a paediatrician who bought it in 1903.
Salthandlaren Gustav R. Setterbergs vill: The salt merchant Gustav R. Setterberg's villa was built from old salt barges and was probably the first house at Arendal. The neighbouring villa, Rosenborg, appears in Berndt Lindholm's painting Arendal 1879, with a funny little tower that still had a flat roof back then.
Saltsjö-Järla station invigdes 1 april 1: Saltsjö-Järla station opened on 1 April 1894 under the name Jerla and is 4.9 km from Slussen. From 2030 you'll be able to change to the metro's blue line at the new Järla station.
Saltsjö-Järla station invigdes 1894 unde: Saltsjö-Järla station opened in 1894 under the old-fashioned name Jerla, and branch lines once ran from here to a yeast factory and to De Laval's steam turbine works. Today the old industrial buildings by Lake Järlasjön have been reborn as Järla sjö, with around 700 homes, shops and restaurants, and about 1,200 people working there. In 2004 the area won the Urban Environment Council's award for improving the townscape.
The Saltsjöbanan railway station here opened in 1894. While the new Slussen was being built, Henriksdal served as the line's city-end terminus from 2016 until the end of 2022. Large parts of the line have been closed since 2023, and the stretch to Slussen isn't expected to reopen until 2028 at the earliest. Danvikstull was once home to the Klippan summer theatre, where audiences laughed along with John Elfström and Arthur Fischer.
Saltsjöbanans station invigdes 1894, då: The station on the Saltsjöbanan railway opened in 1894, when the name was spelled Jerla. Branch lines ran from here to a yeast factory and to De Laval's steam turbine works. Here's a fun fact: Anna Book was a pupil at Nacka music school when she sang “ABC” in Melodifestivalen, Sweden's Eurovision selection, in 1986. And from 2030 you'll be able to change to the blue metro line at a new station here.
Saltsjön, Djurgården och Nackareservatet: Saltsjön, Djurgården and the Nacka reserve
Saltsjötunneln är borrad 50 meter under: The Saltsjö tunnel is bored 50 metres beneath the city and measures 3.5 metres across. The tunnel boring machine that dug it was called Ormen Långe, the Long Serpent. Its outlet is in the harbour off Kastellholmen, about 250 metres from the shore.
Saluhall med frukt och grönt: A market hall of fruit and veg
Samariten öppnade 1890 som Nya barnsjukh: Samariten opened in 1890 as the New Children's Hospital, at a time when people pouring into Stockholm meant cramped housing and the spread of childhood diseases. It closed in 1974 and every building except the administration block was demolished. That building is now a nursery school.
Samlingen omfattar omkring 40 000 leksak: The collection numbers some 40,000 toys from the 1600s onwards, making it the largest toy collection in northern Europe. The museum started out in 1974 at Tidö Castle outside Västerås, where it was opened by King Carl XVI Gustaf.
Samma dag som Skarpnäck öppnade 1994 inv: On the same day Skarpnäck station opened in 1994, Bagarmossen's new underground station opened too. Bagarmossen's old station at ground level had closed a few months earlier.
Samma år som arenan öppnade, 2013, spela: In 2013, the year the arena opened, Swedish Television filmed parts of the show Summercamp at Angered Arena and Angeredsvallen.
Sammanlagt har det funnits fyra slussar: There have been four locks here in all: Queen Kristina's lock, Christopher Polhem's lock, Nils Ericson's lock and the Karl Johan lock. The new lock channel is called Victoriaslussen and is expected to open to boats in 2027.
Samme arkitekt som på Skansen: The same architect as at Skansen
Samtidigt med tunneln byggdes Södra Mari: Södra Marieholmsbron, a railway bridge over the river, was built at the same time as the tunnel. A 72-metre section of the bridge opens to let ships through.
Sandbäck är ingen ny plats. Redan på 155: Sandbäck is no newcomer. As early as the 1550s – more than four hundred years ago – there were two farmsteads here. Today it's in the south-western part of Östra Mölndal, and a little way off is the Pepparred nature reserve, with old pastures and broadleaf trees, protected since 1925.
Sandsborg låg där den gamla vägen mot Da: Sandsborg stood where the old road to Dalarö and the country road to Tyresö parted ways – a fitting spot for an inn. It opened in 1803 in the farm's main house and became a popular, well-known place during the 19th century.
Sandsjöbacka naturreservat har många van: Sandsjöbacka nature reserve has lots of hiking trails. It takes its name from Sandsjön lake below Sandsjöbräcka, a ridge that is geologically a drumlin. Near the church is Södra Barnsjön, a lake for swimming, and the Bohusleden trail passes close by.
Sandsjöbacka naturreservat, som socknen: Sandsjöbacka nature reserve, which the parish shares with Fässberg and Lindome, is part of the EU's Natura 2000 network. Its largest lake is Finnsjön, shared with Råda parish in Härryda.
Sandås ligger i Askim, och namnet Askim: Sandås is in Askim – and Askim, by the way, is actually pronounced “Ashim”. The parish dates back to the Middle Ages. To the south, Sandås borders Skintebo, a residential area by the coast that was farmland until the 1970s. It has car-free footpaths, båtmansgårdar – a sort of boatswain's cottage – and, more surprisingly, a copy of the Chinese Pavilion at Drottningholm.
Sankt Botvids källa är artesisk, vattnet: St Botvid's spring is artesian: the water rises under its own pressure, at 5–10 litres a second. It's rich in iron, which is why yellow and green algae grow on the bed of the stream.
Sankt Botvids källa är artesisk: vattnet: St Botvid's spring is artesian: the water wells up under its own pressure, at 5–10 litres a second. Its high iron content produces yellow and green algae on the bed of the stream.
Sankt Georgios stod klar 1890 i nygotisk: St Georgios was completed in 1890 in the Gothic Revival style, with machine-made red brick, pointed-arch windows and a tall copper-clad spire. The Greek Orthodox congregation added an iconostasis and stone altar, while the organ was removed in the 1970s.
Sankt Olofs kyrka byggdes 1929 som Krist: St Olof's Church was built in 1929 as Kristineberg Chapel in the parish of St Göran. The chapel was moved and rebuilt, and consecrated as St Olof's Church in 1941.
Sankt Olofs kyrka, Täby: Sankt Olofs kyrka, St Olaf's Church, Täby
Sankt Olofs kyrka, en kort bit bort, hör: St Olof's Church, a short way off, belongs to Täby parish. Through neighbouring Hägernäs runs the E18 motorway, completed on the Danderyd–Ullna stretch in 1957, cutting straight through the area. A little further north is Rönninge, which has no built-up areas at all – just the Rönninge by-Skavlöten nature reserve and the Skavlöten outdoor recreation area.
Sankt Pauli kyrka: St Paul's Church, Sankt Pauli kyrka
Sankt Pauli kyrka invigdes 1882 och kall: Sankt Pauli kyrka, St Paul's Church, was consecrated in 1882 and was first known as Redbergskyrkan. The hill it stands on, Höga Lyckan, was donated by Commander Jakob Emil Ekman. The church originally seated 1,200 people; today it seats 600.
Sankt Pauli kyrka, delvis i romansk stil: St Paul's Church (Sankt Pauli kyrka), partly in Romanesque style, was consecrated in 1882 and paid for entirely with private money. The hill it stands on is called Höga Lyckan. Its working name was Redbergskyrkan until the city council settled on the name in 1881.
Sankt Paulus av Korsets kyrka alldeles i: Right next door is the Church of Saint Paul of the Cross, Angered's Catholic parish church. A short walk away stands Alexander Calder's steel sculpture The Three Wings, which spent twelve years on Götaplatsen before it was finally allowed to move to Angered in 1979. Since 2013 it has stood on an open lawn in the town park.
Sankt Paulus av Korsets kyrka ritades av: Sankt Paulus av Korsets kyrka was designed by the architects Pierre der Hagopian and Josef Bandi. It was consecrated on 2 February 1990 by Bishop Hubertus Brandenburg.
Sankt Sigfrids kyrka: Sankt Sigfrids kyrka, St Sigfrid's Church
Sankt Sigfrids kyrka är en monteringsfär: St Sigfrid's Church is a prefabricated timber building with an octagonal nave, designed by Erik Otto Ulrich. It was due to be torn down once the stone-built Stefanskyrkan was finished in Vasastaden, but was bought for 37,000 kronor to serve the growing industrial district of Liljeholmen.
Sankt Sigfrids kyrka är en riktig flyttf: Sankt Sigfrids kyrka has done some travelling. The red wooden church originally stood in Vasastaden and was moved here in 1904, when it was called Sankt Stefans kapell. Designed to be portable, it looks a lot like the flat-pack timber villas of the period, and it has been a listed building since 1993. Further along Hägerstensvägen is the Aspen cinema – when it opened in 1952, it was the first privately run cinema to open in Stockholm since 1943.
Sankta Birgitta kyrka: Sankta Birgitta kyrka, St Birgitta's Church
Sankta Birgitta kyrka byggdes 1960–1962: Saint Birgitta's Church was built between 1960 and 1962 and consecrated in December 1962. The architect Rolf Bergh designed the church, its bell tower and the parish hall next door. And here in Nockeby, the architect Sven Markelius built his own villa in 1930 – one of the very first houses designed to the new ideals of functionalism.
Sankta Birgitta kyrka byggdes på marken: Sankta Birgitta church was built on the land where the tram's old terminus and turning loop used to be. The loop was no longer needed once modern trams had a driver's cab at each end, so it was removed in 1960 and the Källviken stop took over the name Nockeby.

St Birgitta's Church was built on the site of the old tram terminus and turning loop. The loop was removed in 1960, as the newer trams had a driver's cab at each end. The church was designed by Rolf Bergh and consecrated in 1962.
Sankta Birgitta kyrka i Nockeby står på: Sankta Birgitta kyrka, St Birgitta's Church in Nockeby, stands where the trams used to turn round. This was the old terminus of the number 12, with its turning loop, until work on the church began in November 1960. It was consecrated on 9 December 1962. All around, Nockebyhov is lined with terraced houses from the late 1940s that the City Museum has marked blue for their exceptional cultural and historical value.
Sankta Birgitta kyrkas fristående klockt: The free-standing bell tower of St Birgitta's Church was built for four bells but has only two: Syster Trofast and Broder Barfot, Sister Faithful and Brother Barefoot. The tower is 39 metres tall, with the cross adding another eight, and was meant as a landmark for both land and sea, visible far and wide.
Sanna betyder ungefär sandmark. Här i nä: Sanna means something like 'sandy ground'. Close by is Plaskis – or Älvsborgsdammen, to give it its proper name. In summer, families paddle in 20 to 45 centimetres of water, and when the pond is drained, the skateboarders move in. At the edge is the sculpture Boll, 'Ball': a two-metre blue steel sphere that looks like a giant beach ball.
Sannegårdshamnen invigdes i januari 1914: Sannegårdshamnen, the Sannegården harbour, opened in January 1914, though these days the name usually means the residential area around it. Culture has moved into the old industrial buildings: Backa teater, one of Sweden's leading theatres for children and young people, performs in a converted sheet-metal workshop on Lindholmen. And a stone's throw away is Aftonstjärnan, a cinema and theatre that has been a listed building since 1995.
Sara Stridsbergs roman Beckomberga: ode: Sara Stridsberg's novel Beckomberga: Ode to My Family was nominated for the August Prize in 2014 and adapted for the stage at the Royal Dramatic Theatre. Back in 1977, Barbro Lindgren portrayed life at the hospital through a child's eyes in Stora Sparvel.
Satellitstad i Sputniks tid: A satellite town in the Sputnik age
Saxe nöjde sig inte med en sten. Ristnin: Saxe wasn't content with just a stone. The carving at Törnby says he had the stone cut and a bridge built in memory of his mother. The man who carved the runes signed it too: Sven carved.
Scandic Talk Hotel är 19 våningar och 72: Scandic Talk Hotel has 19 storeys and stands 72 metres tall, making it the third-tallest hotel building in Sweden. The tower is made up of two offset volumes, one with screen-printed glass façades and the other clad in boldly textured aluminium panels.
Scandinavium invigdes 1971. Läs om Abba,: Scandinavium opened in 1971. Read about ABBA, Eurovision and Kiss at the arena.
Scen på kvällen, möten på dagen: Stage by night, meetings by day
Scenen 24 kvadrat drevs av koreografen G: The stage Scenen 24 kvadrat was run by choreographer Gun Lund and Lars Persson of the company E=mc2 danskonst. On this little stage in Sockerbruket, the old sugar refinery, they welcomed dancers from some twenty countries.
Scheelegatan hette förr Trädgårdsgatan,: Scheelegatan used to be called Trädgårdsgatan, but in 1885 it was renamed after the chemist Carl Wilhelm Scheele. On the corner of Fleminggatan and Pipersgatan is Separatorhuset, built around 1900 as the head office of AB Separator – later Alfa Laval – whose factory once filled the whole large site by Barnhusviken bay. The City Museum has now given the building its blue heritage rating.
Schering Rosenhane gjorde Säby till säte: Schering Rosenhane made Säby a manor estate in the 1630s and, in the 1650s, had the Carolean-style main house built that still stands today. The architect may have been Nicodemus Tessin the Elder, but Rosenhane was himself keen on architecture and probably had a big say.
Schmidt lät också bygga en stor kringbyg: Schmidt also had a large barn built around a courtyard, made of timber from Norrland in northern Sweden. Until the Second World War it housed some forty cows. After that, ‘Fittja loge’ became a popular spot for dances and parties for young people from the area and from Stockholm.
Schweizerstil på en stödmur: A Swiss-style villa on a retaining wall
Schweizervilla blev huvudkontor: A Swiss-style villa turned head office
Scouternas tidning blev politisk: A scout paper that turned political
Se AGA:s gula optiktorn på nära håll: See AGA's yellow optics tower up close
Se AGA:s gula optiktorn på nära håll (1: Take a close look at AGA's yellow optics tower (1 min), built in 1943 to make periscopes for submarines, among other things. The area is called Dalénum, after the inventor Gustaf Dalén.
Se Ahlby säteri: See Ahlby säteri, the Ahlby manor
