The villas round about started going up in 1896, when Djursholms AB began selling plots near the station. In the 1970s and 80s the whole Roslagsbanan railway was under threat of closure.
Stationen öppnade 1890 och hette först D: The station opened in 1890. It was called Djursholm at first, then Ösby, and from 1920 Djursholms Ösby. The line was electrified as early as 1895. With trains running in four directions – around 340 a day, freight included – it was once reckoned to be the busiest railway station in Sweden. The villas round about started going up in 1896, when building plots near the station were put on sale.
Stationen öppnade 1922 som hållplats för: The station opened in 1922 as a stop for local trains on the Northern Main Line. Residents of the growing suburb of detached houses had taken the matter all the way to the government. Today's station came into use in 1994, when the line was widened to four tracks.
Stationen öppnade 1937, när Roslagsbanan: The station opened in 1937, when the Roslagsbanan railway was extended to Näsbypark. At first it was called Alléparken, but the name lasted only four months. The trains here run on a single track with just one platform. Down by the bay of Näsbyviken is Näsby Castle, now a conference venue with a hotel and restaurant.
Stationen öppnade 1944 som spårvagnshåll: The station opened in 1944 as a tram stop on the Ängby line, under the name Färjestadsvägen. It became a metro station in 1952, but it wasn't called Ängbyplan until 1962. Not far from here, as far back as the 16th century, stood Karsvik farm, on the shore of Lake Ängbysjön, which has since disappeared. Today the Mälaren Scouts have their base in Karsvik's meadow. And nearby Ängby torg square only got its official name in 2005.
Stationen öppnade 1946 under namnet Joha: The station opened in 1946 as Johanneshov. But Johanneshov was the postal address for much of southern Stockholm and was thought too broad, so in 1958 the station was renamed Gullmarsplan. Between 1950 and 1964 trolleybuses ran here too.
Stationen öppnade den 5 juni 1977 och li: The station opened on 5 June 1977 and lies 13 kilometres from Kungsträdgården, the terminus at the other end of the blue line. Buses from the neighbouring bus terminal go to Sollentuna, Danderyd, Vällingby and Jakobsberg, among other places.
Stationens första räddningsbåt 1983 var: The station's first rescue boat, in 1983, was the former pilot boat Alice Olsson, built in 1949. In 1987 she was replaced by Gustaf Olsson, a 10.3-metre covered boat with twin engines, donated by Sten A. Olsson.
Stationens konst av Jörgen Fogelquist är: The station art by Jörgen Fogelquist is inspired by Andrée's balloon expedition towards the North Pole in 1897. Before the metro arrived in 1964, trams ran here from 1952, on a line built so it could later be converted to metro.
Stationens konst är mosaiktavlor som för: The station's artwork consists of mosaics depicting the hands of men, women and children. They were created by the artist Maria Ängquist Klyvare and installed in 1996.
Stationens konst, Röster från det förflu: The station's artwork, Röster från det förflutna (Voices from the Past) by Göran Dahl, Carl Johan De Geer and Kristina Anshelm, shows fossils and runic inscriptions – among them a complete reproduction of the famous Rök runestone. From the north entrance it's 20 metres down to the platform.
Stationens längsta konstverk av Eva Nybe: The station's longest artwork, by Eva Nyberg, shows a procession of people dressed in black, banners waving, marching through countryside, industry and city. Look out too for Sjöfåglar (Seabirds) by Christina Rundqvist Andersson.
Stationens längsta konstverk är gjort av: The station's longest artwork, by Eva Nyberg, shows a protest march with banners winding through a landscape of countryside, industry and city. Other works include 'Seabirds' by Christina Rundqvist Andersson and 'The Last Harvest in Northern Botkyrka' by Olle Magnusson.
Stationens signatur är Sst, som ska läsa: The station's code is Sst, short for Södra bangården, STockholm. The slightly odd order of the letters goes back to the 19th-century telegraph system.
Stationens tak och väggar är målade i gr: The station's ceiling and walls are painted green and red. Among other things, the artists Karl-Olov Björk and Anders Åberg created scenes of Sweden depicting the country's problems in the 1970s, along with little peep-show boxes to look into.
Stationshus som var eventbåt: A station that was once a party boat
Stationshuset byggdes 1917–1918 efter ri: The station building went up in 1917–1918 to designs by the architect Folke Zetterwall. The yellow rendered building, with STUVSTA on its gable, is still standing today.
Stationshuset invigdes den 12 december 1: The station building opened on 12 December 1876, the same day King Oscar II opened the railway between Stockholm and Västerås. It was Järfälla's only station with a stationmaster from the start, and the building was originally painted red.

The station building opened on 12 December 1876, the same day King Oscar II inaugurated the railway between Stockholm and Västerås. It is the only one of Järfälla's four old station buildings on the line still standing; Barkarby, Kallhäll and Stäket have all been demolished.

The station building opened on 12 December 1876, the same day King Oscar II opened the railway between Stockholm and Västerås. It was the only station in Järfälla to have a stationmaster from the start.
Stationshuset som ersattes av plåt: A station building replaced by sheet metal
Stationshuset är äldre än hållplatsen: d: The station building is older than the stop itself: it first stood at the steam ferry landing in Herserud and was moved here in 1914. It's in the National Romantic style, with dragon heads on the ends of the gutters.
Stationsnamnet är en ledtråd. En kort bi: The station name gives it away. A short distance from here was Täby Galopp, the biggest gallop racecourse in Scandinavia, opened by King Gustaf VI Adolf in 1960 to replace the Ulriksdal racecourse in Solna. The last race day was 18 May 2016, after which the horses moved to Bro Park. Where the track used to be, a new district, Täby Park, is now taking shape, planned for around 20,000 residents.

The stop's name is a clue: Galoppfältet means 'the gallop field'. A short way off was Täby Galopp, Scandinavia's largest flat-racing track, opened by King Gustaf VI Adolf in 1960 to replace the Ulriksdal racecourse in Solna. The last race day was 18 May 2016, and the horses moved to Bro Park. Where the track once was, the new district of Täby Park is now taking shape, planned for many thousands of residents.
Statskontorets villastad: A garden suburb from the State Office
Statyn Avskedet på polarisen: The statue Avskedet på polarisen, Farewell on the Polar Ice
Statyn Såningskvinnan av Per Hasselberg: Per Hasselberg's statue The Sower was unveiled on Johanna's name day, 21 July 1883, which is why locals call her Johanna. She was cast in bronze in Paris, and the original plaster is in Gothenburg's Museum of Medical History.
Statyn mitt på platsen föreställer Karl: The statue in the middle of the square is King Karl IX – Charles IX – on horseback, but to Gothenburgers it's simply Kopparmärra, the Copper Mare. It went up in 1904. This is where Kungsportsavenyn, the city's grand avenue, begins, and on the canal alongside, the flat Paddan sightseeing boats glide by, ducking under the low bridges. A short distance away is Stora Saluhallen, the big market hall, from 1889.
Statyn som Landalapojkarna samlade till: The statue the Landala boys paid for
Statyn var från början tänkt att heta Ne: The statue was originally going to be called Neptune, the sea god's Roman name. Poseidon stands seven metres tall, with a water-spouting fish in his right hand and a shell in his left. The basin around him teems with lobsters, crabs, mermaids and tritons.
Stearinljus vid Mälarstranden: Candles on the shores of Lake Mälaren
Stefanskyrkans fasader är klädda med lju: St Stephen's Church (Stefanskyrkan) is faced with pale sandstone from Närke, and the south gable bears a stone crucifix by the sculptor Carl Eldh. In the chancel stands a triptych-style altarpiece with ten paintings by Einar Forseth, dating from the 1926 refurbishment.
Sten A Olsson, som grundade Stenasfären,: Sten A Olsson, founder of the Stena group, was born on Donsö. Every shipping company on the island has a flag on the harbour pier, and a Stena flag still flies there. The island's first bunkering boats, Anna Mari and Oljaren, were built in 1914 and 1920.
Stenarna är av Göteborgsgnejs och bröts: The stones are Gothenburg gneiss, mostly quarried from a hill 250 metres away. Each weighs 1–2 tonnes, and the roof stone nearly 3 tonnes. Thin flat stones were stacked between the blocks to support the chamber.
Stenbrottet öppnade 1866 och ägdes då av: The quarry opened in 1866, owned at the time by the engineer Johan Adolf Berg. His workforce included some 60 convicts from Långholmen prison. The bluish-grey granite was exported as far as England, and Berg used it for, among other things, the quay by the Nationalmuseum.
Stenen från sprängningarna användes unde: In the second half of the 1800s, rock from the blasting was used to fill in nearby Stora Träsket, the 'Great Swamp'. That created more building plots for the new Östermalm.
Stenen har ungefär 120 inhuggna gropar,: The stone has around 120 carved hollows, known as älvkvarnar or "elf mills". According to folklore, elves ground grain in the hollows – hence the name. Cup-marked stones like this had their heyday in the Bronze Age.
Stenen hittades vid odling i Islinge och: The stone turned up during ploughing at Islinge and is mentioned in 1847. In the 1860s it was set up by the main house at Islinge farm, and in 1943 it was moved to the hill at Dalängen so more people could see it.
Stenen låg från början i Hästhagen, som: The stone originally lay in Hästhagen, which belonged to Älvsjö farm. When the State Railways expanded the track area in 1966, it was moved to a wooded slope, where it lay forgotten for many years. The Brännkyrka local history society rediscovered it and had it moved to Lerkrogen in 1994.
Stenen låg ursprungligen i Hästhagen vid: The stone originally lay in Hästhagen by the Älvsjö estate. When SJ, the state railway, built a carriage shed in 1966, it was moved to a wooded slope by Huddingevägen, where it lay forgotten for many years. The local heritage society tracked it down and moved it here in 1994.
Stenen ristades mellan 1050 och 1080 av: The runestone was carved between 1050 and 1080 by Ärnfast and is reckoned among his finest work. It says that Gy and Sven raised the stone in memory of Bärsa, their good father.
Stenen saknar helt de djurslingor som an: The stone has none of the animal-shaped ribbons usually seen on runestones in Uppland. Even so, the rune forms suggest it probably dates from the late 11th century. In the summer of 1682 the antiquarian Johan Hadorph and the draughtsman Johan Leitz travelled through Järfälla, drawing every runestone they came across.
Stenen som inte får nå marken: The stone that mustn't touch the ground
Stenen som kan få jorden att gå under: The stone that could end the world
Stenen vänder ryggen mot vägen: A stone with its back to the road
Stenen är av grå granit och daterad till: The stone is grey granite, dated to around 1060–1100. The inscription reads roughly ‘Åsgöt had the stone raised … (in memory of her) husband’. Its Urnes-style ornament shows a ribbon-like beast coiling beneath a Christian ring cross.
Stenen är från mitten av 1000-talet och: The stone dates from the mid-1000s and its inscription reads roughly: 'Kari and Ingjald and … in memory of Björn, their father. God help …'. The rest was lost along with the missing top.
Stenen är utsmyckad i så kallad Urnessti: The stone is decorated in the Urnes style, with a rune beast coiling beneath a Christian ring cross. The runes were repainted by the National Heritage Board's runestone team on 11 September 2012.
Stenens ornamentik består av två runorma: The stone is decorated with two rune serpents framing a Christian cross. The serpents are bound together in two places by heart-shaped loops. The stone has been repaired and has stood right beside the church entrance since 1915.
Stenhamra, på västra sidan av Färingsö m: Stenhamra, on the western side of Färingsö island in the middle of Lake Mälaren, is best known for its disused 19th-century quarry and the industrial village that grew up around it. Neighbouring Törnby is far older: it's first mentioned in 1342, in connection with a land swap with Vårfruberga convent, and has since grown together with Stenhamra.
Stenhamra, på västra sidan av Färingsö,: Stenhamra, on the western side of Färingsö, is best known for its disused 19th-century granite quarry and the company town that grew up around it. If you'd like to go even further back in time, look for runestone U 32, which stands in a patch of woodland just under a kilometre from the centre. Ekerö municipality, by the way, is made up of a cluster of islands in Lake Mälaren long known as Mälaröarna, the Mälaren Islands.
Stenhuggarfamiljernas tjänstebostäder fi: The tied cottages of the stonecutters' families survive in excellent condition. Together with the quarry, the school and the co-op shop, they offer a rare picture of a late-19th-century industrial community, and the area is designated of national interest for cultural heritage.
Stenpiren byggdes 1844–1845 och fick sit: Stenpiren, the Stone Pier, was built in 1844–1845 and got its name in 1883. Before that, this was the site of Träpiren, a wooden jetty half as wide and one of the city's first quays. All the archipelago boats used to depart from here.
Stensjökyrkans klocka syns inifrån kyrko: You can see Stensjö Church's bell from inside the church. It was cast in 1674 from the metal of a 12th-century church bell that had cracked from ringing in 1588, and it first hung in the old church at Fässberg.
Stensjön har också kallats Gunnebosjön o: Stensjön has also been called Gunnebosjön and Mölndalssjön. The name, "Stone Lake", probably comes from its rather stony bottom in places, especially near the outlet.
Stensjön var perfekt för margarin: kallk: Stensjön was ideal for making margarine: cold springs in the gravel ridge gave clean water, and in winter ice was sawn from the lake for cooling. The factory had around forty production staff, plus extra seasonal workers for the ice harvest.
Stenskolan hade bassängbad, träslöjdsal: The stone-built school had a swimming pool, a woodwork room and a dining hall on its lower-ground floor. At the top were an art room, a music room and an open-air classroom where pupils with lung disease were taught. All in all there was room for around 470 pupils.
Stensö byggdes under miljonprogrammet, m: Stensö was built during the Million Programme, Sweden's big housing drive, with seven-storey point blocks and eight-storey slab blocks. In eastern Stensö small houses went up, some just 55 square metres, meant for pensioners and people living alone. Before that there were just a few 1920s villas out at the far end.
Stensö har fått sitt namn efter en halvö: Stensö is named after a peninsula that was once an island in Lake Ältasjön, and the Stensö swimming spot is at its tip. Through the area runs Ältavägen, built in 1934, which winds for just over eight kilometres through open countryside between Älta and Nackanäs. Not far away, in the Flaten nature reserve, people race radio-controlled model cars.
Stenugnsbageri i herrgården: A stone-oven bakery in the manor
Stenvalvsbron från 1822 blev så dyr att: The stone arch bridge of 1822 cost so much that a toll was charged to cross it. Even so, it stayed in service right up to the 1930s.
Stenåldersboplatser i dalen: Stone Age settlements in the valley
Stenåldersfolk vid kusten: Stone Age people on the coast
Stenåldersfolkets vattenkälla: The Stone Age settlers' water source
Stenåldersyxan från bussgaraget: The Stone Age axe from the bus depot
Sticklinge gårds huvudbyggnad blev 1926: In 1926 the main house at Sticklinge farm became the clubhouse of Lidingö Golf Club, whose course opened in 1927 as Sweden's first 18-hole course. The house burnt down in 1980, but Patron Haralds väg keeps the memory of its old owner, Harald Zetterberg, alive.
Sticklinge på nordvästra Lidingö är beka: Anyone who has run Lidingöloppet, the famous cross-country race, will know Sticklinge in north-western Lidingö, because the course runs right through it. South of the houses stretches the Sticklinge nature reserve: 108 hectares of forest, coast and grassland, protected since 2021. By Rödstuguviken bay stands Rödstugan, a house with roots in the 17th century that has been home to crofters, ferrymen and the families of farm labourers.
Sticklingebadet anlades på 1950-talet oc: Sticklingebadet was created in the 1950s and has a sandy beach about 80 metres long and a gently sloping lawn. There's a floating jetty, a beach volleyball court, an open-air dance floor and a barbecue area – but no showers.
Stieg Trenter föddes på Magelungsvägen 4: Crime writer Stieg Trenter was born at Magelungsvägen 453. His parents ran a grocery by Södertörns villastad station – today Farsta strand – where Stieg sometimes lent a hand. Since 1995 a sign on the square has carried a quote from his crime novel Tiga är silver.
Stieg Trenters torg är runt med en fontä: Stieg Trenters torg is a round square with a fountain in the middle. Since 1995 it has had a literary sign quoting from Trenter's 1955 crime novel Tiga är silver (Silence Is Silver).
Stigbergets äldsta kända namn är Galgebæ: Stigberget's oldest known name is Galgebærgith, Gallows Hill, recorded as early as 1545. Once the gallows had been moved away, a lookout tower went up here in 1827, which people jokingly called "the Toothpick on Söder".
Stinsen bytte ägare 2016. Den nya ägaren: The Stinsen shopping centre changed hands in 2016. That same year the new owner, Magnolia Bostad AB, applied to demolish it and build housing, and in 2017 a proposal for a new local plan was drawn up together with Sollentuna municipality.
Stjärnadressen i Gamla stan: A star address in the Old Town
Stjärnbildsgatan, en bit härifrån, fick: Stjärnbildsgatan, a short way from here, had an unusual makeover: its four-storey blocks were rebuilt so drastically that the top floors were removed altogether, leaving terraced houses around generous courtyards. Nearby is Interkulturella folkhögskolan, the Intercultural Folk High School. It started in 2007 as the first folk high school in the Nordic countries for Roma students and was opened by Crown Princess Victoria.
Stjärnhus efter brandstegen: Star-shaped blocks built to ladder height
Stjärnhusen byggdes på en före detta ind: The star-shaped Stjärnhusen were built on a former industrial site. The builder Olle Engkvist wanted to create an intimate, small-scale model town set into nature. The northern buildings have glorious views over Lake Mälaren.
Stjärnhusen fick åtta våningar eftersom: The star-shaped Stjärnhusen blocks got eight storeys because the fire brigade's ladders reached 22 metres, and a lift was only thought worthwhile if 40 flats shared it. The result was five flats per floor around a pentagonal stairwell.

The star-shaped blocks were given eight storeys because the fire brigade's ladders reached 22 metres, and a lift only paid for itself once a building had 40 flats. The result was five flats on each floor, arranged around a five-sided stairwell.
Stjärnhusen i Gröndal byggdes av Olle En: The Star Houses in Gröndal were built by Olle Engkvist to designs by Sven Backström and Leif Reinius, and the architectural historian Fredric Bedoire ranks them among the finest groups of buildings in Stockholm. The area is of national interest and a textbook example of folkhem architecture, from the early days of the Swedish welfare state. And after all that architecture, it's time for fika, the Swedish coffee break: Lundbergs konditori has been on the same corner, under the same name, since 1946.
Stjärnkrogens sista kapitel: The last chapter of a star restaurant
Stockholm Mejeri invigdes 1984 av kungen: Stockholm Mejeri was opened in 1984 by the King and Queen Silvia. With around 650 employees, it's Sweden's largest dairy by headcount. Every year it takes in some 235 million kilos of milk from farms within 250 kilometres.
Stockholm är byggt på vatten och omgivet: Stockholm is built on water and surrounded by forest. This route takes the boat out along the Saltsjön to Blockhusudden, continues through the Royal National City Park on Djurgården and ends at Källtorpssjön lake, deep in the Nacka nature reserve.
Stockholm är fullt av musik- och filmmin: Stockholm is packed with memories of music and film. This route runs from Kafé 44 and Cornelisparken on Södermalm, past the studios where ABBA recorded, to Filmstaden in Råsunda, where almost 400 Swedish feature films were shot.
Stockholmarnas tvätt för 20 öre: Stockholm's laundry at 20 öre a kilo
Stockholms frihamn öppnade som ett provi: Frihamnen, Stockholm's free port, opened in 1919 as a temporary solution, yet it kept growing right up until the 1970s. For much of that time, from 1921 to 1952, seaplanes landed at Lindarängen, where the port stands today. The Ford Building, designed by Uno Åhrén, went up between 1929 and 1931 as an assembly plant for Ford cars; these days it's the home of the stock exchange operator Nasdaq. The huge Magasin 6 warehouse had less luck – it was out of date almost as soon as container shipping took over.
Stockholms första södra tull hette Grind: Stockholm's first southern toll gate was called Grinds tull and stood at what is now Östgötagatan/Bondegatan. Around 1660 it moved to the narrow isthmus here. The toll station was abolished in 1857, and nothing of the toll houses survives today.
Stockholms sjukhem köpte gården 1903 och: Stockholms sjukhem bought the estate in 1903 and used it as a convalescent home. In the 1940s it cared for soldiers wounded in the Finnish Winter War, and from 1953 to 1968 for polio patients. Mathilda Sundelin was in charge right up until 1968.
Stockholms sjukhem köpte gården 1903 som: Stockholms sjukhem bought the farm in 1903 as a convalescent home. In the 1940s it cared for war invalids from the Finnish Winter War, and from 1953 to 1968 for polio patients. The matron, Mathilda Sundelin, bought the farm in 1922 and renamed it Solsunda vilohem, a rest home.
Stockholms stad byggde 1889 en sopstatio: In 1889 the City of Stockholm built a refuse station at Lövsta, and the rubbish came here by rail. All that manure attracted market gardeners, and greenhouses and hotbeds defined the garden suburb for most of the 20th century.
Stockholms stad köpte Skarpnäck 1922 och: The City of Stockholm bought Skarpnäck in 1922 and kept the field in reserve for a new civil airport. But in 1933 the city council decided to build at Riksby in Bromma instead. Bromma Airport opened in 1936.
Stockholms stad köpte egendomen Gubbänge: The City of Stockholm bought the Gubbängen estate from the farmer Albin Arvidsson in 1908, but building didn't really get going until the 1940s. The district grew up around two farms, Herrängen and Gubbängen, neither of which survives. The metro arrived on 1 October 1950, when the line from Slussen to Hökarängen opened.
Stockholms stad köpte marken 1885 och by: The City of Stockholm bought the land in 1885 and built the Lövsta refuse station by Lake Mälaren, with the rubbish arriving by train from Spånga. The workers needed homes, so Count Carl Trolle-Bonde of Hässelby Palace began leasing and selling plots.
Stockholms stad köpte marken 1930, men d: The City of Stockholm bought the land in 1930, but it lay empty until the mid-1950s. The first residents moved in during autumn 1956, to three-storey narrow blocks on Snösätrahöjden and Bjursätrahöjden, south of the metro.
Stockholms stad sålde slottet för 50 mil: The City of Stockholm sold the palace for SEK 50 million. The singer Tomas Ledin was among the buyers, and it was the new owners who switched to the spelling Hesselby in 2010.
Stockholms stads småstugebyrå lät bygga: Stockholm City's small-house bureau had 362 small houses of ten different types built in Bagarmossen, with residents building them themselves from standard plans. The town plan was led by Sven Markelius.
Stockholms stads småstugebyrå lät uppför: The City of Stockholm's small-house office had 362 small houses of ten different types put up in Bagarmossen – and they were built by their future owners themselves. The standard designs were drawn by the architect Edvin Engström.
Stockholms stadsmuseum bedömde målningen: The Stockholm City Museum judged the mural to be of cultural and historical value, and in 2015 it was decided that the wall would be protected and become the centrepiece of a new park. But in 2020 the decision came to demolish it, as it was in poor condition and at risk of collapse.
Stockholms största koloniområde ligger a: Stockholm's largest allotment area is right nearby, with no fewer than 554 plots, each with its own little cottage. It was laid out in three stages – in 1936, 1939 and 1941 – to replace several allotment areas in the southern suburbs that were cleared during the 1920s and 30s. Also in the neighbourhood is Pungpinan, an area of small cottages, where building began on Lugna Gatan as early as 1927.
Stockholms största stensträngsområde: Stockholm's largest field of stone walls
Stockholms tunnelbana är känd för sin ko: The Stockholm metro is famous for its art, but Johannelund – along with S:t Eriksplan and a handful of others – is one of the few stations with no artwork whatsoever.
Stockholms ånglokssällskap: Stockholms ånglokssällskap, the Stockholm steam locomotive society
Stockholms ånglokssällskap bevarar och r: Stockholms ånglokssällskap, the Stockholm Steam Locomotive Society, preserves and restores old railway vehicles. It started out in 1974 with an emergency reserve locomotive bought from SJ, the Swedish state railways. The society was first based at Tomteboda and then in the old slaughterhouse district, but when the Globe arena was about to be built it had to move, in 1988, to an industrial siding here in Västberga. Nearby Midsommarkransens skola was an elementary school from 1915 to 1962.
Stockholmsmässan hette Älvsjömässan fram: Stockholmsmässan, the Stockholm exhibition centre, was called Älvsjömässan until 1976. Today it's Sweden's largest venue for trade fairs and conferences, with around seventy fairs a year and just over a million visitors. In spring 2020 its halls were put to a very different use, when the Älvsjö field hospital was set up inside.
Stockholmsvägen är en av Lidingös äldsta: Stockholmsvägen is one of Lidingö's oldest roads – the municipality calls it Lidingö's historic lifeline. Along it stand Kopparhusen, the Copper Houses, three tower blocks from the 1950s and 1960s; the oldest has been marked by the city museum as being of very high cultural and historical value. Further on is Lidingö Arena, an office and retail building from the 1970s by the architect Bo Möller, so striking that it has become a local landmark.
Stockholmsåsen löper genom Sollentuna, o: The Stockholm esker runs through Sollentuna, and the road was laid along the dry ridge or its slopes. Older routes followed the ridge even more closely, passing the old farms of Kista and Tuna north of Edsviken.
Stockmos har haft sin fabrik i Stenhamra: Stockmos has had its factory in Stenhamra since 1932. In the 1940s there were 10,000 fruit trees here – the largest orchard in Sweden north of Skåne. Fruit trees are still common in the residential area later built on the land, and many street names recall the orchards.

Stockmos has had its factory in Stenhamra since 1932. In the 1940s there were 10,000 fruit trees here – Sweden's largest orchard north of Skåne. Many fruit trees still stand in the residential area built on the land, and several street names recall the orchards.
Stocksund är rikt på arkitektvillor. Vil: Stocksund is full of architect-designed villas. Villa Gärdsgården was built in 1904–05 to designs by Ragnar Östberg, for the artist Alf Wallander. Villa Tallom was built in 1904–06 by the architect Lars Israel Wahlman as a home for himself and his family, and it has been listed since 1979.
Stocksundet förbinder Lilla Värtan med E: The Stocksundet strait links Lilla Värtan with the bay of Edsviken and marks the border between Danderyd and Solna. Stocksund station used to sit closer to the harbour, with tracks running down to the water so goods could be loaded onto ships. The harbour also had the power station that supplied electricity to the Djursholm railway, and the Långängsbanan tramway started from the station.
Stora Delsjön ligger 69,5 meter över hav: Stora Delsjön lies 69.5 metres above sea level and covers 1.2 square kilometres. Its water passes through four streams before reaching the sea 14 kilometres away.
Stora Essingen är en 73 hektar stor ö i: Stora Essingen is a 73-hectare island in Lake Mälaren. Its highest point, Kungsklippan, is 41 metres above sea level, and on the second-highest stands Essinge church, designed by Cyrillus Johansson and consecrated in 1959. The local cinema Orkanen opened nearby in 1938. The two apartment buildings on Badstrandsvägen are called Byggindustrihuset, after AB Byggindustri, the construction company that built them.

Stora Essingen is an island of 73 hectares in Lake Mälaren, and its highest point, Kungsklippan, rises 41 metres above sea level. On the island's second-highest point stands Essinge Church, designed by Cyrillus Johansson and consecrated in 1959. Its free-standing bell tower, a 48-metre campanile, is a landmark of southern Stockholm.
Stora Essingens sommarvillor från 1700-t: The 18th-century summer villas on Stora Essingen became year-round homes in the early 20th century, and things really took off when the Essinge bridge opened in 1929. In 1966 came Essingeleden, Sweden's first six-lane motorway, along the island's eastern shore. On 14 October 2005 the floating crane Lodbrok crashed into the bridge, causing massive traffic jams.

The 18th-century summer villas on Stora Essingen became year-round homes in the early 1900s, and things really took off when the Stora Essingen bridge opened in December 1928. In 1966 Essingeleden, Sweden's first six-lane motorway, arrived along the island's eastern shore. On 14 October 2005 the floating crane Lodbrok crashed into the bridge, causing huge tailbacks.
Stora Fågelsången var en av flera små gå: Stora Fågelsången was one of several small farms carved out of the Hägersten estate in the late 1700s, which became manor-like summer retreats. The south wing is the oldest part, referred to as 'the new building' in 1756. The Stockholm City Museum has marked the farm as being of high heritage value.
Stora Förö är genom landhöjningen numera: Thanks to post-glacial land uplift – the land here is still slowly rising after the Ice Age – Stora Förö is now joined to Lilla Förö by a narrow isthmus. The island has a burial cairn and finds from the Stone Age. When the master carpenter Axel Hellqvist came out here on a boat trip in 1927, there wasn't a single tree, because the island had long been used for grazing sheep and cutting timber.
Stora Holm var från början tre skattegår: Stora Holm was originally three freehold farms that were merged into one. In 1748 four crofts are recorded as belonging to it: Torpet, Hagen, Boekullen and Grimman.
Stora Högmora låg på norra Kynäsberget o: Stora Högmora stood on the northern part of Kynäsberget, and the house survives, rebuilt, at Södervägen 9. Lilla Högmora lay down in the valley by Lake Magelungen, but that cottage burned down in the late 1970s.
Stora Kåsjön är Partille kommuns största: Stora Kåsjön is the largest lake in Partille municipality, just over a square kilometre in area and a full 32 metres deep. It sits high up, about 109 metres above sea level, and it's also the municipality's source of drinking water. Around it are more small lakes, such as Haketjärnen in the Maderna-Haketjärn Natura 2000 area.
Stora Mölnesjön ligger 97,2 meter över h: Stora Mölnesjön lies 97.2 metres above sea level, a little lower than Idtjärnet. Water from here flows through three watercourses and only reaches the sea 21 kilometres later.
Stora Mölnesjön lies 97.2 metres above sea level. Water from the lake flows through three streams and rivers, and travels 21 kilometres before it finally reaches the sea.
Stora Rödjan var ett kronohemman i Lundb: Stora Rödjan was a Crown farm in Lundby parish and served, among other things, as a colonel's residence. Work on the Ryahamnen oil harbour began here in the 1930s, followed by Skarvikshamnen in the 1950s.
Stora Saluhallen vid Kungstorget: Stora Saluhallen, the market hall on Kungstorget
Stora Sjötullen: Stora Sjötullen, the old customs house
Stora Sköndal var en bondgård redan unde: Stora Sköndal was already a farm in the Iron Age. Near the main building are two burial grounds probably used in the Vendel and Viking periods.
Stora Stampan byggdes på 1670-talet och: Stora Stampan was built in the 1670s and first stood on Observatoriegatan in Stockholm. When the blocks there were laid out in the 1880s there was no room for windmills, so in 1882 it was moved here. Its sister mill, Lilla Stampan, now stands as Kälvesta windmill in Solhem.

Stora Stampan was built in the 1670s and first stood on Observatoriegatan in Stockholm. When the area was to be developed with city blocks in the 1880s there was no room left for windmills, so in 1882 it was moved here to Kvarnbacken. It's probably one of the oldest surviving windmills in Greater Stockholm.

Stora Stampan was built in the 1670s and first stood on Observatoriegatan in Stockholm. When the area was redeveloped in the 1880s there was no room left for windmills, so in 1882 it was moved here to Kvarnbacken.
Stora Stampan maldes i till slutet av 19: Stora Stampan was still grinding until the late 1920s. Its sails were taken down during a renovation in 1971, and in winter 2019–2020 the mill was restored and given new ones.
Stora Stampan är en stubbkvarn, där hela: Stora Stampan is a post mill, so the whole mill house turns to face the wind. Holländskan, built in 1885, was an eight-sailed Dutch-style mill where only the cap turned. The name Stampan may suggest that flax and hemp were pounded here for rope and sailcloth, but there's no record of it.
Stora Stampan is a post mill, where the whole mill body turns to face the wind. Holländskan, built here in 1885, was a Dutch-style tower mill where only the cap could turn, and it had eight sails.
Stora Stampan är en stubbkvarn, vilket b: Stora Stampan is a post mill, which means the whole mill house can be turned to face the wind. Its name ('the Great Stamp') suggests it may have pounded flax and hemp for ropes and sails, but there's no record of that. In the winter of 2019–2020 it was given new sails.
Stora Torps trävilla brann i maj 1871. Ä: Stora Torp's wooden villa burned down in May 1871. The owner, Oscar Ekman, had been out to see some acrobats at Lorensberg and spotted the glow of the fire on his way home. In a letter to his wife he added that the acrobats had been very poor, by the way.
Stora Ursvik gränsar mot Kymlinge, Lilla: Stora Ursvik borders Kymlinge, Lilla Ursvik, Rissne and Rinkeby. Not far from here, on a hill by the Rissne interchange, stands the Stora Stampan windmill. Its companion, Holländskan, burned down in 1989, but Stora Stampan was restored over the winter of 2019–20 and now has new sails.
Stora Ursvik var en av flera stora medel: Stora Ursvik was one of several large medieval farms in the area and has a long military history – for many years the defence research agency FOA was based here. Homes only started to be built in 2006.
Stora delar av Hisingen har lerjord som: Much of Hisingen is covered in what's known as "Hisingslera", Hisingen clay. It isn't a particular type of clay; the name simply comes from the fact that it's found almost everywhere on the island. The soil is often very fertile, but can be tricky to build on.
Stora delar av Viksjö gränsar till Görvä: Much of Viksjö borders the Görväln nature reserve along Lake Mälaren, and here you'll find the Hummelmora green space with the Hummelmoraberget hill. As early as 1935 a regional plan proposed making both Görväln and Viksjö nature reserves, but the municipality only wanted to protect Gåsberget.

Much of Viksjö borders on Görväln nature reserve, which follows the shore of Lake Mälaren past Sandudden and the Görväln beach, among other spots. Viksjö is also home to the green space of Hummelmora and the Hummelmoraberget hill.

Much of Viksjö borders the Görväln nature reserve, which follows the shore of Lake Mälaren past spots such as Hummelmora hage and Görvälnsbadet beach. Viksjö also has the green area of Hummelmora, with Hummelmoraberget hill.
Stora delar av grannområdet Ekängen bygg: Much of neighbouring Ekängen was built in the 1940s as a neighbourhood of small family houses, and it's still a quiet residential area just north of Saltsjö-Duvnäs. A little further on you'll find Långsjön, a small forest lake that has been a nature reserve since 2005. There's a swimming spot and a 1.4-kilometre jogging trail all the way round – perfect if you fancy swapping the town centre for a lap of the lake.
Stora delar av ön har bördig lerjord som: Much of the island is covered in fertile clay known as 'Hisingslera'. It isn't a type of clay in its own right, just the name for the clay you find almost everywhere here. Farmers have always loved it, but builders have to survey the ground carefully.
Stora delar av ön har lerjord som kallas: Much of the island sits on clay known as "Hisingslera" – not a special kind of clay, but so called because it's found almost everywhere. It's very fertile but has caused problems for builders. In the Tuve landslide of 1977, rain-soaked clay began to slide and nine people lost their lives.
Stora hallen är 126,5 meter lång med 24: The Great Hall is 126.5 metres long with 24 metres up to the ceiling – the largest non-church interior in Sweden, apart from a few sports arenas. The building was actually meant to have four wings around a courtyard, but the money ran out.
Stora marker för liten peng: Plenty of land for little money
Storbageri i Peugeots gamla hus: A big bakery in Peugeot's old building
Storgatan gick länge rakt genom torget,: For many years Storgatan ran straight through the square, which in the 1900s was busy with cars and buses. Today the square is car-free and has a market every day. There's also a group of sculptures by Willy Gordon.
Storholmen i sjön Trehörningen var en gå: Storholmen in Lake Trehörningen was once a proper island. In the 1920s it was divided into plots, most of them sold to workers from Stockholm, and a footbridge was built to the mainland. Around twenty little summer cottages sprang up. Today it's mostly forest and shoreline open to all, and the lake is rich in fish and birdlife – the lesser spotted woodpecker among them – and even bats.
Storhögen på gravfältet är sex meter hög: Storhögen, the great mound on the burial ground, is six metres high and 46 metres across – the second-largest burial mound in Södermanland. When it was excavated in 1939, gold fragments of a sword hilt from around 650–700 were found. That sword is considered more magnificent than those from the boat graves at Vendel and Valsgärde.
Storkällans kapell och krematorium ritad: Storkällan's chapel and crematorium were designed by Wolfgang Huebner and opened in 1970. The building is made of brick, weathered steel and glass, and the crematorium itself is tucked away out of sight in the basement. Olle Nyman created the decoration in gold and silver.
Storskogstorget invigdes 1958 och formga: Storskogstorget square opened in 1958. The landscape architect N.H. Orénto designed it very much in the style of the day, with seating, greenery and two ponds. From here you can also get to Näckrosen metro station, the only one on the network with entrances in two different municipalities. A little further on is Filmstaden in Råsunda, the studios where almost 400 Swedish feature films were shot between 1920 and 1973 – a place especially linked with Ingmar Bergman.
Storstugan planerades som ett bågformat: Storstugan was planned as a curved 25-storey building with a restaurant at the top and a day nursery on the middle floors. When it was built in 1970, it ended up with 17 storeys and nothing but flats.
Storstugan var tänkt som ett bågformat h: Storstugan was meant to be a curved, 25-storey building with a restaurant at the top and a nursery halfway up. Those plans were dropped, and when it was finished in 1970 it had 17 storeys and was almost entirely flats.
Storängen grundades 1904 av Tjänstemänne: Storängen was founded in 1904 by the Salaried Employees' Home Ownership Association, and the Saltsjöbanan railway made the area attractive. Villas could be no taller than two storeys, house no more than two families and cover no more than a tenth of the plot.

Storängen was founded in 1904 by the Civil Servants' Home Ownership Association. Officials, university lecturers, company directors and artists moved here, drawn by the new Saltsjöbanan railway with its fast trains into Stockholm.
Storängen lockade en lång rad konstnärer: Storängen drew a whole host of artists, among them Georg and Hanna Pauli, Richard Bergh and Anton Genberg. Gottfrid Kallstenius's next-door neighbour was the publisher Wilhelm Widstrand, who moved in in 1906.
Storängen räknas som ett av Sveriges bäs: Storängen is considered one of Sweden's best-preserved early 20th-century villa suburbs, with large timber houses in the National Romantic style. Gustaf Hugo Sandberg designed the most houses, and since 1987 the area has been designated of national interest for cultural heritage.
Storängen var tidigare ett flackt jordbr: Storängen was once a flat field of farmland. It came into being in 1848, when Lake Trehörningen was lowered to create land for cultivation. The industrial area was built on marshland that had once been a bay of the lake.
Storängens industriområde, alldeles i nä: Building work on the Storängen industrial area, right nearby, began in the early 1950s, just under a kilometre south-east of Huddinge centrum. Now the area is about to change. Under a plan from 2009, it will eventually become a mixed neighbourhood, mostly homes plus businesses that sit comfortably alongside residents. It's also where you'll find Storängshallen, a hall for athletics and gymnastics.
Storängens villasamhälle grundades 1904: The Storängen garden suburb was founded in 1904 by the Civil Servants' Home Ownership Association. The new railway to Saltsjöbaden, with fast trains to Stockholm and a stop in Storängen, made the area an attractive place to live.
Storängshallen alldeles intill, invigd 2: Right next door is Storängshallen, opened in 2007, a hall mainly for athletics and gymnastics. The area has an amusing history. In 1902 the owner of Fullersta gård launched Huddinge villastad, a scheme for a brand-new garden suburb of villas. Only a handful of the old villas are left, and Huddinge centrum now stands right where the villa town was supposed to be.
Storängshallen är 94,5 meter lång och ha: Storängshallen is 94.5 metres long, with a vaulted roof that spans the entire hall without a single pillar and rises 14 metres high. Inside are a 200-metre track and a 60-metre sprint straight. Back in the 1970s, the old sports ground here was covered by an inflatable plastic dome instead.
Stranden är 1 200 meter lång med 18 000: The beach is 1,200 metres long, with 18,000 square metres of sand and room for up to 15,000 bathers. There are several bathing jetties and a diving tower.
Strandkyrkogården invigdes 1996 och rita: Strandkyrkogården cemetery opened in 1996 and was designed by Göran Bergquist, with Skogskyrkogården, the Woodland Cemetery, as its model. It has room for around 20,000 graves and a viewpoint over Lake Drevviken.
Strandkyrkogården invigdes 1996 och sakn: Strandkyrkogården opened in 1996 and has no chapel, since it's seen as an extension of Skogskyrkogården, the Woodland Cemetery. The architect, Göran Bergquist, drew his inspiration from there. The entrance on Gudöbroleden is adorned with granite blocks from Göinge.
Strandkyrkogården invigdes 1996 som komp: Strandkyrkogården opened in 1996 as an extension of Skogskyrkogården, the Woodland Cemetery, which is why no chapels were built. The architect, Göran Bergquist, took his inspiration from Skogskyrkogården itself. There's room for some 20,000 graves, plus a viewpoint over Drevviken lake.
Strandska huset var ett av de första hus: Strandska huset was one of the first houses in Kungälv with central heating. It's named after its owner, Nils Strand, a warehouse manager at Göteborgs Kexfabrik, the Gothenburg biscuit factory. Over the years the basement has housed both a steam bakery and an antiques shop.
Strandstädning har pågått i Öckerö sedan: Beach clean-ups have been going on in Öckerö since 1992. Around 80 per cent of the rubbish that washes up comes from countries other than Sweden, carried here by wind and currents.
Strandvägen anlades 1889 när Djursholms: Strandvägen was laid out in 1889, when the Djursholm garden suburb was founded. According to the prospectus, the outermost strip of shore was to belong to the whole community, and much of the road was built by filling in the lake edge with stone.
Strawberry Arena, som invigdes under nam: Strawberry Arena, which opened as Friends Arena, is Sweden's national stadium, home to the men's football team, and since 2013 it has hosted the final of Melodifestivalen, the contest that picks Sweden's Eurovision entry. For concerts it holds up to 65,000 people. Next door is a 25-storey hotel with round windows designed to look like footballs, and Mall of Scandinavia has an IMAX cinema with the biggest screen in Sweden, almost 22 metres wide.
Strax efter Akalla passerar stråket Akal: Just past Akalla, the trail passes Akalla village, one of the best-preserved 18th-century farming villages in the Stockholm area, with roots going back to the Bronze Age. At Hästa farm, one of the largest urban farms in the world, the land has been worked since the Viking Age.
Strax efter mitten av 1870-talet blev Ar: Soon after the mid-1870s, Arendal became a seaside resort. Wholesale merchants, shipowners, an eye doctor and a salt trader had summer retreats here, with villas such as Rosenborg, Tjällstorp and Fjordhem.
Strax före återinvigningen 1992 härjades: Shortly before the reopening in 1992, a major fire swept through several of the centre's buildings, delaying the opening.
Strax härifrån ligger Hammarkulletorget,: Just up the road is Hammarkulletorget, a square designed by White Architects and built in 1971. Beneath it lies the only completely underground tram stop in Sweden. It was modelled on the Stockholm metro – because in the 1970s there really were plans for a metro all the way out to Angered. That's why it's sometimes called Gothenburg's only metro station.
Strax intill inträffade Tuveraset, en av: It was right near here that the Tuve landslide struck – one of the worst natural disasters in modern Swedish history. At 4.09 pm on 30 November 1977, the ground in Tuve gave way in a massive landslide that claimed nine lives. It's also known as Raset i Tuve or Tuveskredet.
Strax intill ligger Arken kombiterminal: Right beside us is the Arken combi terminal in Skandia Harbour, where semi-trailers are switched between ships and trains. It replaced the old terminal at Gullbergs vass and Gothenburg Central Station, which had to move to make way for the Västlänken rail tunnel. Work started in January 2018, and the terminal was officially opened in February 2019.
Strax intill ligger Fässbergs kyrkogård,: Right next to it is Fässberg cemetery, with 4,800 graves and a chapel from 1936. A little further on is Fässbergs Bio, a 400-seat cinema run by the municipality in the converted Fässbergssalen assembly hall, which opened in January 2013. The upper secondary school that houses the hall was once one of Sweden's 20 schools with specialist elite programmes.
Strax intill ligger Hult Åsens naturvård: Right beside it is the Hult Åsen nature conservation area, a stretch of high ground with pine, birch and bare rock. Set aside in 1994, it covers ten hectares and is looked after by the City of Gothenburg. A little further away is Askims torg, the square at the heart of Askim, a district facing Askimsfjorden bay.
Strax intill ligger Kvibergsnäs landeri,: Right next door is Kvibergsnäs landeri, a country estate between Kviberg and Gamlestaden. Its present buildings date from the first half of the 19th century. Kvibergsnäs is something of a survivor: it's the only country estate in Gothenburg where both the house and the barns are still standing.
Strax intill ligger Lillhagsparkens sjuk: Right beside us is Lillhagsparken hospital, originally named Lillhagen hospital for the mentally ill. Gothenburgers usually just called it Lillhagen, Hagen or LS. There's no longer any care here – the forensic psychiatric unit moved to Rågården in 2013.
Strax intill ligger Mariakyrkan i Hammar: Right next to us is Mariakyrkan in Hammarkullen, formerly known as Tomaskyrkan, a church shared by the Uniting Church in Sweden and Angered parish. Close by there was also Hammarkullens Folkets Hus Bio, a 200-seat cinema. And a short walk away is Hammarkulletorget – the place to go for Gothenburg's only underground tram stop.

Right next door is St Mary's Church in Hammarkullen, formerly St Thomas's, shared by the Uniting Church in Sweden, Equmeniakyrkan, and Angered parish. The building has been abandoned because of mould and is to be replaced by a new one. Nearby was also Hammarkullens Folkets Hus Bio, a cinema seating 200. And a short walk away is Hammarkulletorget, where the tram stops at what is jokingly called Gothenburg's only underground station.
Strax intill ligger Motorbranschens tekn: Right next door is the Motor Industry Technical Upper Secondary School, where the focus is on vehicles and transport. A short way from here is Västra Frölunda Cemetery, with medieval roots; the old Västra Frölunda Church stood here until it was pulled down in the 1860s. Iron rings for tethering horses are still set into the cemetery wall – a kind of car park from days gone by.
Strax intill ligger Mörby verkstäder, in: Right next door are the Mörby workshops, designed by Sigge Cronstedt and opened in 1906. The great workshop hall has stepped gables and roof lanterns that let in daylight, and trains on the Roslagsbanan line are still serviced here. In 1944, 144 people worked here; by 2011 there were just 15.
Strax intill ligger Nylöse kyrka, som ti: Right next to it is Nylöse Church, which used to be called Gamlestadens kapell. A little further along Gamlestadsvägen is the Gothenburg Hospital Cemetery, which dates back to the late 1500s. Only the odd gravestone is left today, but the site is protected by law as a heritage site, and a Franciscan friary also once stood here.
Strax intill ligger Rudboda gård, ett ti: Close by is Rudboda gård, a former croft that gave its name to the whole district. On Elfviksvägen stands Villa Molin, designed by Ralph Erskine in 1947 for the garden architect Ulla Molin. Not far off is Kyrkviken, once called Koltorpsviken, the narrow inlet of the sea that splits Lidingö into a northern and a southern half.
Strax intill ligger Råda säteri, en herr: Right next door is Råda säteri, a manor on Lake Rådasjön with a main house, wings and old farm buildings, all listed since 1969. The lake is up to 23 metres deep and supplies Mölndal with its drinking water. The Mölndalsån river runs straight through it and changes its name further downstream to Gullbergsån, so the water here flows all the way into Gothenburg.
Strax intill ligger Solvalla, Sveriges n: Right next to us is Solvalla, Sweden's national harness racing stadium and the largest trotting track in the Nordic countries. Every year it hosts Elitloppet, one of the world's biggest trotting races, and the stands hold 35,000 spectators. The track opened on 31 July 1927, and twelve races were held in its first year.
Strax intill ligger Tuve kyrka, en av Gö: Right beside us is Tuve Church, one of the most popular churches for weddings in the Diocese of Gothenburg. Since 2010 it has been part of Tuve-Säve parish. The old parish of Tuve belonged to the province of Västergötland and the Östra Hising hundred, and became part of the City of Gothenburg in 1967. In 2000 the parish had just over 10,000 residents.
Strax intill låg Karlsrofältet, en idrot: Right beside us was Karlsrofältet, a sports ground for almost sixty years. The name goes back to the iron porter Carl Jonsson and appears as Carlsro as early as 1834. A little further on begins the Botanical Garden, which opened in 1923 in time for the Jubilee Exhibition but wasn't considered finished until 1948. Its emblem is a wood anemone, and it has two stars in the Michelin travel guide.
Strax intill reser sig Fässbergs kyrka p: Right nearby, Fässberg Church stands on its hill. From 1922 to 1976 it was called Mölndal Church, because in 1922 the old Fässberg parish became the town of Mölndal. The parish goes back to the Middle Ages, and Gunnebo House lies within it too. A stone's throw away is Fässbergs Bio, a 400-seat cinema in a converted assembly hall.
Strax intill rinner Tappström, sundet me: Right beside us is Tappström, the channel between the islands of Ekerön and Lovön. It's about one and a half kilometres long but only 3.2 metres deep. On the Ekerö side there's a guest harbour for visiting boats, and the bridge here carries Ekerövägen, county road 261, all the way towards Brommaplan. So this is where one island ends and the next begins.
Strax intill studsar basketbollarna i Go: Right next door, basketballs are bouncing in Gothia Arena – home of Högsbo Basket and the only club-owned sports hall in Gothenburg. On match days it holds a thousand people. This whole area was once part of the parish of Västra Frölunda, which had around 13,500 residents in 1944 and became part of the City of Gothenburg the following year.
Strax intill står Akalla värmeverk, ett: Right beside us is Akalla värmeverk, a district heating plant from the mid-1970s. It may not sound thrilling, but the Stockholm City Museum rates two of its buildings as especially valuable to the city's cultural heritage. A little further away, in Akalla centrum, is a church with an unusual story. Consecrated in 1976, it was first shared by the Church of Sweden and EFS, a Lutheran revival movement. In 2020 it was sold to the Catholic diocese and is now the home church of the Syriac Catholic community.
Strax intill står Gibraltar herrgård, fa: Right next to us is Gibraltar herrgård, the old Chalmers family manor that gave Gibraltargatan its name. The wooden main house, in the Empire style, was built in 1847, and since 2024 it has stood in a new spot on Orrspelsgatan, south of the Chalmers University campus. One of the old estate manager's houses served as the Chalmers students' union building from 1948 to 1952.
Strax intill står Nacka kyrka, byggd 189: Right next door is Nacka Church, built in 1891 in Gothic Revival style, which gained a new funeral chapel in 1908–1909. It belongs to the old parish of Nacka, which had just 1,708 inhabitants in 1887 and became the town of Nacka in 1949. Across Kyrkviken bay, the Nysätra headland juts out into the water. The Nackanäs Inn welcomed guests there until it burned down in 1960.
Strax norr om Fiskarhagen är det bara 28: Just north of Fiskarhagen, only 280 metres separate Aspen and Bornsjön. According to the antiquarian Olof Hermelin, a canal once linked the two lakes here, but it has long since dried up.
Just north of Fiskarhagen, only 280 metres separate the lakes Aspen and Bornsjön. According to the antiquarian Olof Hermelin, a canal – now dry – once linked the two.
Strax norr om kyrkan möter Tuve kyrkväg: Just north of the church, Tuve kyrkväg meets Holmvägen, the local road leading to Stora Holm's skid-training track, Stora Holm Manor and the Säve depot, among other places.
Strax norr om stationen finns en larmad: Just north of the station is an alarmed hall where metro trains are parked, with four tracks and room for six full-length trains. The station has only one way out, plus an emergency exit by the hall.
Strax norr om stationen grenade en hemli: Just north of the station, a secret branch line curved off to the west from 1941 until the late 1980s. Known as Krutbanan, the 'Gunpowder Line', it was three kilometres long and used for military purposes.
Strax norr om statyn står 13 stora almar: Just north of the statue stand 13 large elm trees that were going to be cut down for a new metro entrance. Thousands of Stockholmers protested, and in May 1971 the site was occupied for a week with hammocks and a tent camp. The elms are still standing.
Strax söder om Barkarby ligger Vålberga,: Just south of Barkarby lies Vålberga, a housing area built around 1963, made up mostly of long rows of terraced houses around a sports field. A little further away is Barkarby Villastad, with the neighbourhoods of Tingsbyn and Kyrkbyn – regarded as one of Järfälla's most valuable historic environments.
Strax söder om centrum, vid Stävholmsgrä: Just south of the centre, at Stävholmsgränd, lay a burial ground from the Bronze and Iron Ages. Excavations in 1966–1967 showed that people had lived here since the Stone Age. Its stone circle was unique in Stockholm, so the outer ring of stones was rebuilt when the rest made way for terraced houses.
Strax söder om kustsjukhuset byggdes 193: Just south of the coastal hospital, a house was built for the staff in 1936. Since 1999 it has been known as Pensionat Styrsö Skäret, a guesthouse.
Strax söder om kyrkans plats anlade Pete: Just south of where the church now stands, Peter Jonas Bergius laid out a botanic garden, Bergielund, in 1759. In 1885 it moved to Frescati, north of the inner city, and was renamed Bergianska trädgården, the Bergius Botanic Garden.
Strax söderut, i Kälvesta, ligger Stockh: Just to the south, in Kälvesta, is the largest grave field in the City of Stockholm, with some 145 ancient remains: mounds, round stone settings, three-pointed stone settings and three ship settings.
Strax utanför kusten ligger ön Trälen, o: Just off the coast lies the island of Trälen, which has had its moment as a TV star. In autumn 2006, TV4 aired a reality show called Trälen every weekday, in which wealthy inner-city Stockholmers and some less well-off suburbanites lived together on the island for 40 days. Half a million viewers tuned in for the first episode, but the numbers soon dropped off. The winner was Serhan Sören Erdal.
Strax väster om Danderyds kyrka, en bit: Just west of Danderyd Church, a little way from here, the runestone U 131 stands between the old Klockargården, the parish clerk's house, and the former parish hall. The Danderyd district is bordered by the Edsviken inlet to the south and west, and just over 11,000 people live here, most of them west of the E18.
Strax väster om Edsängens gravfält låg e: Just west of the Edsängen burial ground stood a hill fort, but it was removed in the early 1970s when the Tunberget water tower was built. In the Viking Age Edsviken and Norrviken were joined, with a connection to the Baltic Sea.
Strax väster om Järla gård finns ett vik: Just west of Järla farm is a Viking Age burial ground. When the graves were excavated in 1895, finds included a Thor's hammer ring, a needle case, tweezers, a pair of shears and beads.
Strax väster om gården ligger det välbev: Just west of the farm is Lugnet, a well-preserved croft – a red-painted double cottage with green shutters. Today it’s a summer café, and south of the farm some 15 apple trees survive from the old orchard.
Strax öster om Filipstadsbacken reser si: Just east of Filipstadsbacken rises Burmanstorpsberg, a 73-metre hill named after Burmanstorp. Around 1900, the land towards Lake Magelungen was meant to become Södertörns villastad, a garden suburb with almost 600 plots for well-to-do Stockholmers. But the plots were slow to sell, mostly because transport links were poor, and in 1912 the City of Stockholm bought out the whole company.
Strax öster om Holm ligger Stora Holms s: Just east of Holm lies the Stora Holm estate. In 1974 the playwright Ellen Bergman founded the Gothenburg Chamber Theatre here, in the house where she also lived, combining food and theatre in one evening. It closed in 1986.
Stridsledning i berget: A command centre in the rock
Stridsvagnshindren från andra världskrig: The anti-tank barriers from the Second World War were left standing at Kungsportsplatsen until 5 March 1952.
Strindbergs park och en bronsåldersgrav: Strindberg's park and a Bronze Age grave
Strindbergshus och filmrekvisita: A Strindberg house and film props
Strosa förbi Engelska radhusen i kvarter: Stroll past Engelska radhusen, the English terraces, in the Drivbänken block
Strosa i Ekerö centrum och leta upp den: Wander round Ekerö centrum and find the giant 'dot'
Strosa i Järla sjö bland gamla industrih: Wander around Järla sjö among old industrial buildings
Strålsjön är 7,4 meter djup. Vid sjöns s: Lake Strålsjön is 7.4 metres deep. At its south-eastern end there's a public bathing spot with a jetty, and the Sörmlandsleden trail passes by here too. Just offshore, white and yellow water lilies grow.
Strålsjön är en näringsfattig skogssjö s: Strålsjön is a nutrient-poor forest lake that's sensitive to acidification. Bog myrtle grows along the south-western shore, and just off the water's edge you'll find white and yellow water lilies and bulrushes.
Strålsjön är liten men hela 7,4 meter dj: Strålsjön is small but a full 7.4 metres deep, and it lies 34.8 metres above sea level. At its south-eastern end there's a bathing spot with a jetty, and the Sörmlandsleden trail passes by here too.
Ström till världens första elektriska tå: Power for the world's first electric train
Strömfåran vid Gunnebo bro fryser nästan: The channel at Gunnebo bridge hardly ever freezes over in winter. That's why hundreds of mallards and Canada geese spend the winter here – and since the 1930s, so have around a hundred whooper swans.
Strömmensberg ligger högt, och därför ha: Strömmensberg sits high up, so many of its streets are named after Sweden's tallest mountains: Sulitelmagatan, Sareks Trappgata, Ottfjällsgatan and Storhöjdsgatan. Kobergsgatan recalls Koberget, the area's former name. From up here there's a fine view over central Gothenburg.
Stucktaket i Stora salen gjordes 1704 av: The stucco ceiling in the Great Hall was made in 1704 by the Italian stuccoist Giuseppe Marchi, who had previously worked at Drottningholm Palace. It is closely related to the ceiling in the Stenbock Palace on Riddarholmen.
Studentbar i källaren: A student bar in the basement
Studenthuset Fyrtalet heter så för att m: The student residence Fyrtalet – 'the Foursome' – got its name because four identical buildings were planned, though only one was ever built. It was designed by the architect Léonie Geisendorf. On Furusundsgatan stands YK-huset, built in 1939 as a collective housing block for the Professional Women's Club, complete with a nursery, restaurant and gym. And Värtan's station building from 1882 has a blue rating – the highest level of protection the City Museum awards.
Studentområdet Kungshamra har ett kungli: The Kungshamra student village has a royal name for good reason: the land was a gift from King Gustaf VI Adolf. The buildings went up between 1965 and 1967, and today there are 1,383 student homes here. A short walk away, in a patch of woodland, is Invalidkyrkogården, the Invalids' Cemetery – a burial ground opened in 1824, where the last burial took place in 1905.
Studion användes också för jazz. I febru: The studio was used for jazz too. In February 1995 Herbie Hancock dropped by to play piano on drummer Peter Johannesson's album Sixtus.
Studion fick 2011 namnet Ingrid efter In: In 2011 the studio was named Ingrid, after Ingrid Bergman and the venue's past as a cinema. When the City Museum documented it in 2019, the red velvet cinema seats were still in place.
Studion som började på hjul: The studio that started on wheels
Stugan byggdes som en av de första svens: The cottage was one of the first Swedish buildings made from machine-sawn rather than hand-hewn timber. The roof trusses are decorated with proverbs from the Hávamál. It became both a piece of historical romanticism and an early example of industrialised building.
Stugan lever kvar i ett namn: The cottage lives on in a name
Stugan lär ha flyttats hit på 1880-talet: The cottage is said to have been moved here in the 1880s from the area around Kvillebäcken, where industrialisation was starting to change the countryside. This crofter's homestead is considered one of the best preserved around Gothenburg.
Stugan som blev skola: The cottage that became a school
Stugan som flyttades hit: The cottage that was moved here
Stugan som var skola: The cottage that was a school
Stureby började byggas 1921 och hette då: Building started in Stureby in 1921, when it was called Ersta Villastad, but after protests it was renamed in 1926 – and Stureby is a made-up name. Nearby is the Vivstavarvsvägen terrace, 36 terraced houses from the early 1950s designed by Erik F. Dahl, and the only housing in Stureby marked blue by the City Museum. And Sockenvägen, which links up the northern part of Brännkyrka parish, is no less than 5,450 metres long.
Stureplan var Sveriges dyraste plats för: Stureplan was the most expensive place in Sweden for illuminated advertising. In the 1950s a property owner with four or five signs could earn around 50,000 kronor a year. Brands lit up here included Marabou, Pommac, Osram and Lipton's tea.
Stureplan var en livlig bytespunkt med t: Stureplan was a busy interchange with a newsstand beneath Svampen, the Mushroom shelter. When Sweden switched to driving on the right on 3 September 1967, the trams disappeared and the square became a sterile island surrounded by traffic.
Stureplan är Östermalms livliga mötespla: Stureplan is Östermalm's buzzing meeting place. In the middle of the square stands Svampen, the Mushroom, a concrete rain shelter from the 1930s that has become the classic place to meet up.
Stuvsta gårds huvudbyggnad låg sydost om: Until the 1960s, the main house of Stuvsta farm stood south-east of Kvarnberget. Today only the tenant farmer's house survives, used by the Kvarnbergsgården youth centre. Two millstones are set into the path outside.
Stuvsta gårds kvarn, Kvarnberget: The Stuvsta gård windmill on Kvarnberget
Stuvsta gårds väderkvarn var en stolpkva: Stuvsta gård's windmill was a post mill, but no one knows how old it was or what it looked like – it was built without permission, and no drawings exist. The mill is said to have fallen into ruin during the 1800s.
Stuvsta gårds väderkvarn var en så kalla: Stuvsta farm's windmill was a post mill. It was built without permission, so no drawings exist. It fell into ruin during the 19th century, and nobody knows how old it was.
Stuvsta nämns första gången 1353 som Stu: Stuvsta is first mentioned in 1353 as Studzta. In the late Middle Ages the village consisted of four farmsteads: Mellangården, Västergården, Östergården and Oppgården. Until 1908 Stuvsta gård belonged to the Lagerbielke family.
Stuvsta och Snättringe var fram till 201: Until 2018, Stuvsta and Snättringe were a single municipal district of just over 16,000 people, before being split in two. Not far from here, Stuvsta gård's windmill once stood on Kvarnberget, Mill Hill, and several of its millstones survive. The municipality has placed one of them on Gymnasievägen, where Huddingegymnasiet, the sixth-form school, occupies a building listed among the municipality's most valuable.
Stuvsta sträcker sig hela vägen från Hag: Stuvsta stretches all the way from Hagsätra in the north down to Tomtberga and Hörningsnäs farm in the south, and east to Lake Trehörningen. Not far from here, the Stuvstaleden road runs through the Kungsklippan rock in the Stuvsta tunnel, opened in 1994. Its northern entrance is built into a block of flats that straddles the approach road.
Stuvstatunneln är 193 meter lång och går: The 193-metre Stuvsta tunnel has run through the Kungsklippan rock since 1994. Before that the road went right through Stuvsta, causing noise problems. A new bridge over the railway was built at the same time.
Stuvstatunneln är 193 meter lång. Den by: The Stuvsta tunnel is 193 metres long. It was built to take the noise of the old road away from Stuvsta, and a new bridge over the railway was put up at the same time.
Styrsö är en av de största öarna i södra: Styrsö is one of the largest islands in the southern archipelago. People live here all year round, and the island has sheltered swimming coves, meadows and old fishing villages.
Ställbart universum mäter 6 gånger 5 met: Adjustable Universe measures 6 by 5 metres and was unveiled on 10 September 1967. Three of its rings were stolen while it was in storage in 2009, and the sculpture wasn't complete again until November 2014.
Ställningen i Käppala började byggas 193: Work on the Käppala battery began in 1939. It had 75 mm anti-aircraft guns, among the most powerful around Stockholm, and was an important last outpost to the east. Today a Bofors gun, donated by the manufacturer, stands on the site.
Stäven som bröt isen: The bow that broke the ice
Stålbalkarna i Hangar A designades av Pa: The steel girders in Hangar A were designed by Paul Hedqvist, who reused truss girders from the old Traneberg bridge when it was demolished in 1934.
Stålbolag i glashuset: Steel companies in the glass house
Större delen av Skintebo ligger i en dal: Most of Skintebo lies in a hollow surrounded by hills. A narrow valley leads you down to the sea, half a kilometre to the west. The land that couldn't be farmed had already been built on with houses.
Större delen av Skärholmen byggdes 1964–: Most of Skärholmen was built between 1964 and 1975. The very first residents moved in on 1 September 1965, at Ekholmsvägen 79–91.
Större delen av den gamla tippen är seda: Since 1994 most of the old rubbish tip has been the Järva DiscGolfPark. The steep slope is used for paragliding and model aircraft, and in 2008 it was reshaped to suit the paragliders better.
Största hyresgästen i Lidingö Arena är e: The biggest tenant in Lidingö Arena is a 31-room hotel that moved in in 1996. An arcade runs along the street, and there's a car park underneath.
Subtopia, en kort promenad bort, hette t: A short walk away is Subtopia, formerly known as Kulturhuset Rotemannen. Today it's a production hub for the arts, with studios, workshops and rehearsal spaces, and it has been a long-standing supporter of the circus world. Further on is Fittja farm, whose inn was one of the largest coaching inns in Sweden in the 17th and 18th centuries. Since 1987 the farm has been home to the Multicultural Centre.
Subtopias hus byggdes i början av 1900-t: The Subtopia building was put up in the early 1900s by telephone magnate Lars Magnus Ericsson as an experimental cowshed for Alby farm. It was built of concrete and – naturally – had a telephone. Among other things, Ericsson tested how to get cows to give milk evenly all year round.
Sundbyberg är Sveriges till ytan minsta: Sundbyberg is the smallest municipality in Sweden by area, at just 8.79 square kilometres. On Esplanaden you'll find the library, Det Nya Museet – the New Museum – and a bust of the town's founder, Anders Petter Löfström. Right next door is the Bristol cinema, which opened on New Year's Eve 1939 and now doubles as an arts venue.
Sundbyberg är en av Stockholms äldsta fö: Sundbyberg is one of Stockholm's oldest suburbs. It became a market town, a köping, in 1888, and was granted town status in 1927. The railway station is older still: it opened in 1876 on the Stockholm–Västerås–Bergslagen railway. And 26 metres beneath your feet, deep in the rock, is the metro station, decorated with sculptures of building façades and the human senses.
Sundbybergs gamla stadshus vid torget ri: Sundbyberg's old town hall on the square was designed in 1932 by Nils Malmborg and Sven Ahlbom. Today it's part of Signalfabriken, but Ture Tideblad's municipal coat of arms still sits above the old main entrance.
Sundbybergs gård byggdes 1785. Marabou k: Sundbyberg farm was built in 1785. Marabou bought it in 1936 for 50,000 kronor and pulled it down, since according to the managing director the house was “in a miserable state”. The cocoa laboratory was built on the site in 1943.
Sundbybergs kommun köpte säteriet 1961 o: Sundbyberg municipality bought the manor in 1961 and let it as a residence, to the politicians Sven Andersson and Sven Aspling among others. In 2001 it was bought by Lennart Ehrenlood, who restored it and wrote a book about the estate. In 2017 the municipality bought it back for almost 20 million kronor.

Sundbyberg municipality bought the manor in 1961 and let it out as a home, to tenants including the government ministers Sven Andersson and Sven Aspling. In 2001 it was bought by Lennart Ehrenlood, who wrote a book about the estate. The municipality bought it back in 2017 for almost 20 million kronor.
Sundbybergs stadsmuseum berättar histori: Sundbyberg City Museum tells the story of Sweden's first suburb from the 1860s onwards. Its collection includes burnt bones from a Viking Age grave, excavated on the spot where the Sieverts cable works later stood. You can also see parts of the runestone U 78, which went missing in the 18th century. Two pieces were found in Ursvik, spent many years in the porch of Solna Church, and finally came to the museum in 1976.
Sundbybergs viktigaste landmärke, det nu: Sundbyberg's best-known landmark is its water tower, no longer in use. It was designed by Ivar Tengbom and completed in 1912 as a symbol of a growing, modern Sundbyberg. Around it lies Tornparken, the Tower Park, whose dance floor was a popular meeting place in the 1940s and 50s, and in the 1970s its community sing-alongs drew big crowds. The Bristol cinema on Sturegatan opened back on New Year's Eve 1939.
Sundbyfortet var en V-formad så kallad i: Sundby Fort was a V-shaped ‘infantry sausage’, completed in 1915. The name comes from the half-round concrete roof that snakes through the landscape. Mortar and concrete were hauled up to the rocky ledge in buckets.
Sundet Tappström är omkring en och en ha: The Tappström strait is about one and a half kilometres long and 3.2 metres deep. On the east side lies Fiskarfjärden and on the west Långtarmen.
Sundet antas ha fått sitt namn efter sto: The strait is thought to take its name from the logs, or stockar, laid across it in times of war to stop enemy ships. It's about 2,000 metres long and up to 15 metres deep.
Sundet binder ihop två fjärdar: Fiskarfj: The strait links two bays: Fiskarfjärden to the east and Långtarmen to the west. On the Ekerö side there's a guest harbour for leisure boats.
Sundet är en del av Mälaren. I sydväst a: The strait is part of Lake Mälaren. To the south-west it joins the Långtarmen bay, and to the north-east it opens out into Mörbyfjärden and Malmvikssjön.
Svalnäs byggdes snabbt ut under 1900-tal: Svalnäs grew rapidly during the first decade of the 1900s and took on an upper-middle-class character, with villas in the National Romantic and Art Nouveau styles. Elis Benckert designed the medieval-inspired Villa Lagercrantz at Svalnäsvägen 18, a listed building since 1979.
Svalnäs nämns första gången i ett pergam: Svalnäs is first mentioned in a parchment letter dated 28 December 1312, which records that Johannes Gaseborg acquired Svalnäs in an exchange with the abbess of St Clare's Convent in Stockholm.
Svandammen i Solhem är både park och bad: Svandammen, the Swan Pond, in Solhem is both a park and a swimming spot, and it's become a favourite hangout for teenagers and families alike. No wonder, really, since buses leave from there in almost every direction: to Brommaplan, Backlura, Vällingby, Hallonbergen, Solna centrum and Spånga station. A swim and a bus ride, all in one.
Svandammen är både park och badplats, oc: Svandammen, the Swan Pond, is both a park and a place to swim, and a favourite meeting spot for teenagers and families in Solhem. The name Spånga is really old: it was first written down as early as 1300, and means roughly 'spångar' – simple plank bridges over boggy ground. Spånga parish once took in both Hässelby Castle and Akalla.
Svanhuset hade en bassäng i mitten och t: The Swan House had a pool in the middle with wedge-shaped pens around it, and a hayloft under the roof. In winter it was heated by a tiled stove. That's how the park's swans lived right up until the 1960s.
Svartedalen byggdes mest under 1950- och: Svartedalen was mostly built in the 1950s and 60s, and between 1965 and 1967 the city's own housing company put up 358 flats here. A little way off is Jättesten, named after the boulders on the hill, and A C Lindblads gata, a street named after the newspaperman who became the first Gothenburger to sit in parliament for the Social Democrats.
Svartlöten gav namn åt Svartlösa härad o: Svartlöten gave its name to Svartlösa härad, an old administrative district or 'hundred', and later to Svartlösa district court, which was renamed Huddinge district court in 1977. From 1667 right up to 1916, however, the court sat at Fittja farm.
Svea artilleriregemente låg här fram til: The Svea Artillery Regiment was based here until 1963, which is why the streets are called Lavettvägen (Gun Carriage Road), Pjäsbacken (Gun Hill) and Kavallerivägen (Cavalry Road). Other names, such as Valkyriavägen and Odalvägen, allude to the area's many ancient remains.
Svea ritades av arkitekten Lennart Cleme: Svea was designed by the architect Lennart Clemens and had three auditoriums seating 90, 61 and 60. Back in its days as Klappan, the same cinema held 238 seats – more than it ever did afterwards.
Sveabron was meant to be a simple wooden bridge. But the company Skånska Cement offered to build an eight-by-eight-metre concrete arch bridge for just 1,800 kronor and got the job. The bridge opened in time for the General Art and Industrial Exhibition of 1897.
Sveavägen hade redan från start status s: From the very start, Sveavägen had the status of a station, with a passing loop and a stationmaster, and in 1901 a new station building was put up with living quarters for him. The delicatessen next door was already here before the railway closed.
Svedmyra låter oskyldigt, men namnet kom: Svedmyra sounds harmless enough, but the name comes from a croft called Svinmyran – ‘the pig bog’. Known since the 14th century, the croft belonged to Östberga farm. The district is ringed by woods and parkland, and the City of Stockholm classes the Svedmyra woods as a core area of high ecological value. In the metro station, the artist Torgny Larsson has created a 40-metre glass screen decorated with the leaves of broadleaf trees.
Svedmyra tunnelbanestation ligger trots: Despite its name, Svedmyra metro station isn't in Svedmyra at all, but just west of the boundary in Stureby. From around 2032 the station will belong to the blue line instead of the green.
Svedmyra tunnelbanestation ligger, trots: Svedmyra metro station, despite its name, isn't in Svedmyra but in Stureby.
