A stone's throw away is Svedmyrabadet from 1969, where the water is kept at a toasty 32 to 34 degrees for warm-water exercise. A little further off was the Enskede ski jump, which opened in 1924 and hosted jumping competitions right up until 1990.
Sven Markelius ritade 1931 en hangar för: In 1931 Sven Markelius designed a hangar for seaplanes. In winter it became Lindarängen's ice palace, Sweden's first indoor arena for ice hockey, curling and figure skating. Today the building is a state-listed monument and still stands in the container port.
Sven Markelius skissade 1958 på en stor: In 1958 Sven Markelius sketched a great ring of slab blocks on top of the rocky hill, but the plan gave too few homes and was rejected. Instead, Åke Östin designed the large parallel buildings that form big urban blocks.

In 1958 Sven Markelius sketched a great ring of apartment blocks on top of the rocky hill, but the plan didn't provide enough homes. Instead, Åke Östin designed the large parallel blocks. At the opening in 1973, Olof Palme called Hallonbergen 'the best housing environment in Sweden'.
Svensk Galopp sålde marken till bland an: Svensk Galopp, the Swedish racing body, sold the land to buyers including Skanska and JM. The sale funded the new Bro Park racecourse in Upplands-Bro. The first residents moved into Täby Park in spring 2020.
Svenska mästerskapen i friidrott har avg: The Swedish Athletics Championships have been held at Sollentunavallen five times: in 1969, 1971, 1995, 2006 and 2016. An athletics Grand Prix is also staged here every year.
Sveriges enda väg till havet: Sweden's only route to the sea
Sveriges första golfklubb bildades i Göt: Sweden's first golf club was founded in Gothenburg in 1891. Three years later, local man Viktor H. Setterberg laid out an 18-hole course of 1,692 metres on the Skalebackarna slopes in neighbouring Arendal. The course was turned into farmland during the First World War.
Sveriges första järnvägstunnel, 276 mete: Sweden’s first railway tunnel, 276 metres long, was blasted with gunpowder by prisoners from Långholmen prison. The rock was hoisted out with hand-operated cranes under the eye of armed guards. Work began on 16 July 1858.
Sveriges första klinik för cancerbehandl: Sweden's first cancer clinic, Radiumhemmet, was founded in 1910 in a flat on Kungsholmen, and since 1938 it has been part of the hospital here in Solna. A little further on stood Norrbacka inn, one of Stockholm's well-known roadside inns on the road to Uppsala, until it burned down in 1882. There were also plans for a lookout tower in Hagaparken, but work on it never even began.
Sveriges första privata elektronmusikstu: Sweden's first private electronic music studio, Andromeda, was set up in the late 1950s by the composer Ralph Lundsten at Kocktorp, by Lake Kocktorpssjön. The studio later moved to Tollare on Skurusundet strait, where it stayed until spring 2014.
Sveriges första socialdemokratiska stats: Sweden's first Social Democratic prime minister
Sveriges största rum utan kyrka: Sweden's largest room outside a church
Sveriges tidiga golfbana: One of Sweden's first golf courses
Sveriges volymmässigt största levande lö: A short walk from here grows Sweden's largest living deciduous tree by volume: the Ekebyhov Oak. It may be around 500 years old and was declared a natural monument in 1956. Beside it is Ekebyhov Palace, a Carolean-style manor house built in the late 17th century for Carl Gustav Wrangel. It may well be the largest surviving wooden palace in Sweden.
Svindersviken har fått namn efter hollän: Svindersviken is named after the Dutchman Johan van Swindern, who had a pitch works built here. It ran from 1671 to 1825.
Svindersviksbron kallas ibland Kvarnholm: Svindersviksbron is sometimes called Kvarnholmsbron. But the real Kvarnholmsbron is an older bridge, which opened back in 1924.
Svindersviksbron monterades ihop på Kvar: Svindersviksbron was assembled on the Kvarnholmen side and then pushed out across Svindersviken in April 2015. It has a 140-metre span, and the roadway hangs from stays attached to two steel arches leaning towards each other.
Svingel är ett gammalt dialektord för vä: ‘Svingel’ is an old dialect word for a bend in the road. This is where the road from Stampen swung round to reach a bridge over the dug canals – spelt ‘groopar’ in those days. The word is borrowed from Dutch or from the German ‘Zwingel’ or ‘Zwengel’.
Svingeln var från början namnet på en jo: Svingeln was originally the name of a farm property at the junction of Friggagatan and Stampgatan, listed in Örgryte's parish register for 1814–1815. Today trams 1, 3, 6 and 8 meet here, and the rebuild that began in 2017 increased the number of bus stops from two to five.
Svängbron och vattenledningen: The swing bridge and the water main
Swedbank var den första av de fyra storb: Swedbank was the first of Sweden’s four big banks to move its head office out of central Stockholm, relocating here from Brunkebergstorg. The building was designed by the Danish firm 3XN, who set out to express the bank’s values of openness, simplicity and care. SEB followed suit in 2017.
Sydost om vattentornet breder den 100 he: South-east of the water tower stretches the 100-hectare Fagersjöskogen forest. It's home to Stockholm's largest spruce, with a trunk more than three metres round at chest height.
Sydväst om slottet ligger en engelsk par: South-west of the palace lies an English-style park from around 1800, with stone-edged paths leading up to an arbour called Fåfängan ('the Folly'). There's also a little dog cemetery where the families' dogs Bisse, Boy and Mister are buried.
Syföreningen byggde kyrkan: The church that a sewing circle built
Symbolen som inte godkändes: The emblem that was turned down
Synskadades museum: Synskadades museum, the museum of visual impairment
Synskadades museum öppnade för allmänhet: The Museum of the Visually Impaired opened to the public in April 1997. It's run by the Swedish Association of the Visually Impaired, and its Open Store exhibition shares a building with the association's offices at Sandsborgsvägen 52.
Synvillan ritades av Rune Falk och Arman: Synvillan was designed by Rune Falk and Armand Björkman of White arkitekter. The largest studio measured 600 square metres, and the building housed a carpentry shop, a paint shop and a dining room for 85. Construction cost 30 million kronor, with another 20 million for the equipment.
Syrhåla, stadsdelen en bit härifrån, har: Syrhåla, the district just along from here, has a name that's hardly a selling point. It's recorded in 1550 as Siöralla and means a swampy spot or sour ground, after the low, damp land between the hills east and south-east of the old village. The district was created in 1957, when Arendal was split in two.
Systerkvarnen hamnade i Ursvik: The sister mill ended up in Ursvik
Systrarna Kabaca växte upp här: Where the Kabaca sisters grew up
Säby kyrka är en monteringsfärdig vandri: Säby kyrka is a flat-pack wooden church designed to be moved, consecrated in 1974 and designed by Rolf Bergh. It has a square plan, a pyramid roof and glazed windows in all four corners.
Säby kyrka, församlingskyrkan för hela S: Säby Church, the parish church for all of Salem municipality, is just a few steps away. A couple of hundred metres from here stood Charlottenlund, also called Lottalund, a little cottage for a farm labourer and his family. In the autumn of 1853 the labourer Lars Björkman moved in with his wife Christina Charlotta, and he put in his days of labour at Fågelsta farm. The family stayed until Björkman died in 1887.
Säby köptes in vid NK:s 25-årsjubileum 1: Säby was bought to mark the NK department store’s 25th anniversary in 1927. Staff at NK and the NK school could then spend their holidays here, and the estate became a meeting place with lots of activities.
Sägnen om den danska kanonen: The legend of the Danish cannon
Säteri utan huvudbyggnad: A manor without a main house
Säteriet ägs sedan 1969 av nuvarande Här: Since 1969 the manor has been owned by what is now Härryda Municipality, and in 1974 it was converted into an inn. The west wing burned down in the mid-1800s; the one standing today dates from 1887.
Säteritak efter branden: A manor roof after the fire
Sätra byggdes 1964–1968 och räknas ofta,: Sätra was built in 1964–1968 and is often – somewhat wrongly – counted as part of the Million Programme, Sweden's great mass-housing drive. Parliament decided on the programme in 1965, by which point Sätra and Bredäng were almost finished. The terraced houses in the Gillsätra block, designed by Åke Östin, are green-rated for their heritage value.
Sätra centrum invigdes 1965 och var Stoc: Sätra centrum opened in 1965 as Stockholm's first indoor shopping centre, inspired by enclosed malls in the USA. It was built straddling the metro, and its sign read not 'Sätra centrum' but 'Station Sätra'.
Sätra centrum invigdes den 16 maj 1965 o: Sätra centrum opened on 16 May 1965 as Stockholm's first indoor shopping centre, inspired by the glass-covered malls of the United States. The building straddled the metro, and its sign didn't say Sätra centrum but Station Sätra.
Sätra gård hör till Stockholms äldsta gå: Sätra gård is one of the oldest farms in Stockholm, known since the 1300s. It gave its name to the whole district, and its two surviving buildings probably date from the 1700s. On the district's highest point, Sätra berg, 71 metres above sea level, stands the water tower – a landmark since 1969 that you can see all the way from Ekerö.
Sätra gård köptes 1376 av Bo Jonsson Gri: Sätra farm was bought in 1376 by Bo Jonsson Grip. In the late 1800s it was left to three charitable foundations, which in 1961, after drawn-out negotiations, sold it to the City of Stockholm for 30 million kronor. In 1918 the estate had been valued at 86,000 kronor.
Sätra gård skänktes på 1800-talet till t: In the 19th century Sätra farm was donated to three charitable foundations. In 1918 the estate was valued at 86,000 kronor, but when the City of Stockholm finally bought it in 1961, after drawn-out negotiations, it paid 30 million.
Sätra kyrka användes vid inspelningen av: Sätra kyrka was used for filming the TV series Tre Kronor in the 1990s. It was the first church shared by EFS, the Evangelical Lutheran mission movement, and the Church of Sweden, and since 2012 it has been Catholic, named after the monk Maron.
Sätra radiolänktorn byggdes 1960 efter r: Sätra radio relay tower was built in 1960 to designs by Jan Wallinder. It stands on a 71-metre hill, so at just over 64 metres tall it reaches 135 metres above sea level. The white concrete tower has become a local landmark.
Sätra radiolänktorn byggdes 1961 åt Tele: Sätra radio relay tower was built in 1961 for Televerket, the state telecoms agency, and designed by the Gothenburg architect Jan Wallinder. Its facade was originally concrete grey. The familiar 'Stockholm white' only arrived in 1996, when Telia owned the tower.
Sätra radiolänktorn från 1960 står på en: Sätra's radio relay tower, from 1960, stands on a hill 71 metres high. At just over 64 metres tall, it reaches 135 metres above sea level and has become a well-known landmark. Along the shore of Lake Mälaren you'll find the Sätraskogen nature reserve and the Mälarhöjden bathing spot.
Sätra radiolänktorn, även kallat Sätra t: Sätra radio link tower, also known as Sätra telelänktorn, stands on Backvindeln, close to where Mälarhöjden meets Bredäng. Painted in the pale 'Stockholm white', it has become a familiar landmark, though it isn't open to the public. A little further on is Bredängshallen, a swimming pool and sports hall from the mid-1960s that the City Museum has marked in green for its heritage value.
Sätra varv startade 1878 och byggde blan: Sätra shipyard opened in 1878 and built barges, among other things, until 1935. Artists now have their studios in Varvsarbetarhuset, the house where the shipyard workers once lived.
Sätra shipyard opened in 1878 and built barges, among other vessels, until 1935. Today artists have their studios in the old shipyard workers' house.
Sätra vattentorn står på smala betongpel: Sätra water tower stands on slender concrete columns arranged in two rings – 16 on the outside and 10 inside – recalling a classical round temple. It's 40 metres tall, with 218 steps up to the reservoir.
Sätras högsta punkt är Sätra berg, 71 me: Sätra's highest point is Sätra berg, 71 metres above sea level, crowned by a water tower since 1969. The district is named after Sätra gård, one of Stockholm's oldest farms, known as far back as the 1300s. A little further on you'll find the Church of Saint Maroun, formerly Sätra church, and the Smistabron bridge for pedestrians and cyclists, which has spanned the motorway since 2008.
Säve anlades 1940 som militär flygflotti: Säve was founded in 1940 as a military air base, with underground hangars built to withstand an atomic bomb. Today the aviation museum Aeroseum occupies these Cold War rock hangars.
Säve flygplats anlades 1940 som militär: Säve airport was built in 1940 as a military air wing, with nuclear-proof underground hangars. Today those Cold War rock hangars house the Aeroseum aviation museum, which has staged the Göteborg Aero Show every late summer since 2008.
Säve har vuxit rejält. År 1913 bodde 1 5: Säve has grown a great deal. In 1913 Säve parish had 1,598 inhabitants; by 2000 there were almost 12,000. The parish belonged to Västra Hising hundred, an old district of Bohuslän, and became part of the City of Gothenburg in 1967. The parish church, Säve Church, is a short walk away, and since 2010 it has been part of Tuve-Säve parish.
Sävedalen betyder helt enkelt Säveåns da: Sävedalen simply means the valley of the Säveån river. It's an inner suburb of Gothenburg in Partille municipality. Right here, from 1985 to 2013, was Partille Bokhandel, a bookshop that sold mostly Swedish titles but also books in French – a little corner of Paris in the middle of Sävedalen.

Sävedalen simply means 'the valley of the Säveån river', and it's an inner suburb of Gothenburg in Partille municipality. From 1990, Partille Bokhandel, a bookshop, stood here on Göteborgsvägen. Most of its titles were Swedish, but it also stocked books in French – a little piece of Paris right in the middle of Sävedalen.
Säveån rinner ur sjön Säven mellan Borås: The Säveån river flows out of Lake Säven between Borås and Vårgårda and runs through Alingsås, Lerum and Partille before reaching Gothenburg. Along the way it passes several nature reserves, including Jonsereds strömmar and the Säveån valley.
Så lät det på runsvenska: How it sounded in runic Swedish
Så många lade kvistar här att rishögen i: So many people left twigs here that in the early 1900s the pile had to be carted away twice a year. It has quietly built itself up again beside the rebuilt road, and people still lay dry twigs on the spot.
Så renas vattnet i dammarna: How the ponds clean the water
Så sent som 1901 fanns bara spridda torp: As late as 1901 there were only scattered crofts where Sannaplan lies today. The square got its name in 1918. At its south-eastern corner is the entrance to Västra kyrkogården cemetery, with kiosks from the 1920s.
Så sent som 1913 bodde knappt 100 person: As late as 1913, fewer than 100 people lived in Herrängen. Most of the villas came in the 1940s and 50s, built by the owners themselves with materials and instructions supplied by the city.
Så sent som på 1940-talet bestod området: As late as the 1940s, the area around Blackeberg was mostly woods and rocky hills. Then, in the early 1950s, the district was built to a town plan drawn up under Sven Markelius. Bio Kaskad, the cinema on Blackebergsplan, opened in 1957, closed in the late 1990s and was brought back to life in 2018. And Råcksta träsk, the little pond nearby, was dredged in the early 1970s when it was starting to silt up.
Så såg husen ut förut: How the houses used to look
Sågaren som byggde stugorna: The sawmill man who built the cabins
Sågen som drevs av en lokomobil: A sawmill driven by a steam engine
Sågen är själva mittpunkten i Vendelsö,: Sågen is the very heart of Vendelsö, a residential area made up mostly of blocks of flats from the 1950s to the 1970s, with a grocery shop and a restaurant in the centre. Vendelsö lies on both sides of the Gudöbroleden road, between Lake Drevviken and Tyresta National Park to the east. Winding through it is the Vendelsån stream, which gathers water from three lakes on its way to Drevviken.
Sågverk och tegelbruk vid vattnet: Sawmill and brickworks by the water
Sångaren Peter Holm ägde Borgen en tid u: The singer Peter Holm owned Borgen for a while in the 1970s. For a few years the house belonged to Hare Krishna, who used it as a monastery.
Söder och öster om Visättra breder Flemi: South and east of Visättra stretches the Flemingsbergsskogen nature reserve. The Huddingeleden and Sörmlandsleden trails run through it, as does the historic parish road between Flemingsberg and Lissma.
Söder om Dalen ligger kvarteret Barnmors: South of Dalen lies the Barnmorskan block, where 22 terraced houses were built in 2008–2010. They have drawn attention for their striking black and white facades.
Söder om Elvesta gård har det lilla vatt: South of Elvesta farm a small stream has carved out a deep ravine. The farm track crosses it on a tall structure of stone arches.
Söder om Elvesta gård har ån grävt ut en: South of Elvesta farm the stream has carved out a deep ravine, which the farm track crosses on a tall stone arch. There was a mill here as early as the 1600s, and it kept working until the 1930s. The surviving mill building dates from the 1850s.
Söder om Lundby nya kyrka står Sannegård: South of Lundby nya kyrka, Lundby New Church, is Sannegårdsmonumentet, what remains of a burial ground from the transition between the Bronze and Iron Ages. Four standing stones are lined up in a row. The biggest, a triangular stone, is still in its original spot, while the other three were moved because of gravel digging. The church's own name, incidentally, has been used for two different church buildings.
Söder om Rågsved tar Rågsveds friområde: South of Rågsved begins the Rågsved open space, also called Kräppladalen: just over 100 hectares of wild country with some dramatic terrain – heights, cliffs and valleys in an ancient fissure-valley landscape. Part of it became a nature reserve in 2018. In the other direction is Högdalen skatepark, Stockholm's largest, built at the initiative of a local group called Stockholm Sub Surfers.
Söder om Stockholm finns Vargen i Huddin: South of Stockholm, in Huddinge, lies Vargen, an almost identical facility. The idea was that crisis management could move between the two and feel instantly at home. The main centres were given animal names, while smaller ones got plant names – like Pionen, the Peony, on Södermalm.
Söder om Stockholm, i Huddinge, finns Va: South of Stockholm, in Huddinge, is Vargen (the Wolf), an almost identical facility. The two were built to the same design so that crisis management teams could move between them and feel instantly at home. Main centres were given animal names, while smaller units were named after plants, such as Krokusen (the Crocus) and Pionen (the Peony).
Söder om den gamla bron står sedan 2016: Just south of the old bridge, Södra Marieholmsbron has stood since 2016. It's a lift-and-swing bridge: the opening section rises a few dozen centimetres, then swings round 90 degrees. It was built in Poland and lifted into place on 1 December 2015.
Söder om gården anlade Wijnbladh en stor: South of the house, Wijnbladh laid out a large garden with more than 400 fruit trees, and on a hillock an English-style park modelled on royal examples. The tall trees he planted in the late 1700s still stand in the park today.
Söder om höghusen ligger Akalla by, med: South of the tower blocks lies Akalla village, with buildings preserved from as far back as the 17th century. The farm is kept going with help from the youth organisation 4H. Järvafältet also has Hästa farm, the last working farm in the City of Stockholm.
Söder om höghuset finns en spegeldamm me: South of the tower block lies a reflecting pool with a fountain by landscape architect Erik Glemme, and in the basin stands Folke Truedsson's sculpture Horisontal from 1973. During the renovation that began in 2013, 1950s-style neon signs were put up above the shops.
Söder om trafikplatsen står de två tulls: South of the interchange, the two toll houses from 1733 still stand. Between them there was once a wooden toll gate shaped like a triumphal arch. When they were renovated in 2013, the original colours were uncovered: pink and white. Traffic passed between the houses right up until 1940.
Söderbystenen står kvar på sin ursprungl: The Söderby stone still stands where it was first raised, but its inscription faces away from today's road – because the ancient road ran on the other side. It reads: "Björn and Faste raised the stone in memory of Kättilbjörn, their father, Torgärd's husband."
Söderhöjden, en bit härifrån, byggdes 19: Söderhöjden, a short way from here, was built in 1967 as part of the Million Programme, Sweden's great housing drive, and it's where you'll find Jakobsberg's bowling alley. The square was renovated and reopened on 31 August 2013. In the middle stands a spherical artwork that glows in different colours depending on the season.
Söderledskyrkan i rött tegel invigdes 19: The red-brick Söderled Church opened in 1960 and is a listed building. Before it was built, the plot was used by travelling funfairs and circuses.
Söderledskyrkan ritades av Hans Borgströ: Söderled church was designed by Hans Borgström and Bengt Lindroos. The nave is 14 metres high, rising to 18 metres at the altar, and the church's three bells hang in full view in a crossbeam on the façade.
Söderlingsgatan i området föreslogs förs: Söderlingsgatan, here in the neighbourhood, was first going to be called Brantingsgatan, after Prime Minister Hjalmar Branting. The Hålekärr property, which the land belonged to, is mentioned as early as 1779.
Söderläget och bergsryggen i norr ger en: The south-facing slope and the ridge to the north give a noticeably higher average temperature, with an earlier spring and a longer summer. Over 400 species grow here, including two hawkweeds found nowhere else in the world and garden plants gone wild from the old summer villas.
Söderorts högsta punkt: The highest point in southern Stockholm
Södertelje Tändsticksfabrik grundades 18: Södertelje Tändsticksfabrik, a match factory, was founded in 1871 by Eric Holmberg. From 1907 he probably moved production in stages from Södertälje to Elisedal. His son Harald Holmberg became the factory's first managing director and stayed on until 1926.
Södertörn är den enda högskolan i Sverig: Södertörn is the only university in Sweden where you can study philosophy in the continental tradition. It has also been tasked by the government with training teachers in the Romani Chib language and Roma culture, in close cooperation with the Roma minority.
Södertörns villastad byggde sina första: In the early 1900s the Södertörn garden suburb company built its first villas here, north of the new Nynäs railway and close to Fagersjö station house. Many of them were demolished when modern Fagersjö was built in the 1960s.
To the south, Årstaviken bay sparkles.
Söderån var från början Orlångens naturl: Söderån was originally the natural outflow from Lake Orlången. Since the late 19th century most of the water has run through the man-made Orlångsån channel instead. Even so, Pumphusängen meadow still floods, especially in spring and after heavy rain.
Södra Djurgården hade då ingen bro till: Back then Södra Djurgården had no bridge to the mainland. Parents felt it was dangerous to send their children by ferry or across the ice to schools in Östermalm or Gamla stan, and in their application they highlighted the healthy location, with fresh air off the Saltsjön.
Södra Långevattnet är 13,5 meter djupt o: Södra Långevattnet is 13.5 metres deep and surrounded by rocky hills and wooded ridges. You'll need a fishing permit if you want to cast a line, and the fish are stocked.
Södra Långevattnet är en långsmal klarva: Södra Långevattnet is a long, narrow, clear-water lake surrounded by rocky hills and wooded ridges, and a popular spot for a swim. If you want to fish, you'll need a fishing licence.
Södra Långevattnet är upp till 13,5 mete: Södra Långevattnet is up to 13.5 metres deep and lies almost 95 metres above sea level. Its water flows north towards Stensjön and the Mölndalsån river, and the fish in the lake are stocked.
Södra länken nämns redan i 1960 års traf: The Södra länken road link already appears in the 1960 highway plan. The westernmost stretch was built quickly and opened in 1972 as Årstalänken, but then the project stalled during the economic crises of the 1970s. Construction proper didn't get going until 1998.
Södra station öppnade 1860 som Stockholm: Södra station opened in 1860 as Stockholm's first railway station, the terminus of the Western Main Line. For nine years it was the capital's most important station, until Stockholm Central opened in 1871.
Sörgården är Tenstas enda ursprungliga s: Sörgården is the only original area of small houses in Tensta. In 1974 architects Jon Höjer and Sture Ljungqvist won the Ytong Prize for the block, sharing it with Ralph Erskine for his Nya Bruket housing estate in Sandviken.
Sörgårdens småhus uppfördes med självbyg: The small houses at Sörgården were built by the residents themselves. Each has three bedrooms, which could become five with lightweight partitions. The living room sits at an angle and, together with a storeroom and a fence, encloses a private courtyard.
Sörman-skylten visade en elegant herre m: The Sörman sign showed an elegant gentleman with a cane in white neon, standing on the initials G and S in green. He gazed out over Sankt Eriksgatan, and a broad white arrow pointed down to the shop's name. The sign was ordered in 1937 and 1939.
Sörmlandsleden är markerad med orange ri: The Sörmlandsleden trail is marked with orange rings around trees and posts and orange dots on bare rock. Along the way there are shelters, huts and cold springs where you can top up your water. The trail is also part of the European long-distance path E6.
Sörmlandsleden är märkt med orange ringa: The Sörmlandsleden trail is marked with orange rings around trees and posts and orange dots on bare rock. Stage 1 starts at Björkhagen metro station and heads into the Nacka nature reserve. In all, the trail is around 1,000 kilometres long.
Sörred har ett namn som inte smickrar. D: Sörred's name isn't exactly flattering. It's recorded in 1388 as Surfua rudi, and the first part is thought to come from the nickname Surv, meaning a lazy, careless sort of man – a slacker or a good-for-nothing. The second part comes from the Old Swedish word ryd, a clearing. Still, the slacker's clearing ended up as a place of hard work: this is where construction of Volvo's Torslanda plant began in 1960–61.
Sörred hörde tidigare till Björlanda soc: Sörred used to belong to Björlanda parish and only became part of Gothenburg in 1967. Today, covering 886 hectares, it's one of the larger districts in Torslanda.
Sörreds namn har stavats på flera sätt g: Sörred has been spelled in all sorts of ways over the centuries. After Surfua rudi in 1388, it appears as Sorwerith in 1476, before being whittled down to today's shorter form.
T-Centralen är en av bara två stationer: T-Centralen is one of only two stations on the green line where the art was unveiled at the same time as the station opened. On the upper level you'll find Siri Derkert's Kvinnopelaren (the Women's Pillar) and the 145-metre ceramic frieze Klaravagnen, both from 1957.
TA, som gett hållplatsen namn, är kaross: TA, which gives the stop its name, is the body plant where production begins. T stands for Torslanda, and A, B and C follow the car on its way: body, paint shop and final assembly. TA delivered its first body back in 1961, for a Volvo Amazon.
Ta en fika eller middag på Trädgårn: Stop for fika – a coffee break – or dinner at Trädgårn
Ta en fika på något av kaféerna kring Ma: Stop for fika – a coffee break – at one of the cafés around Mariaplan (1 min). Here in Majorna you can read about both a song about tram 11 and the district's own hip hop.
Ta en paus i Trekantsparken vid sjön Tre: Take a break in Trekantsparken, by the little lake Trekanten
Ta en paus vid dammen: Take a break by the pond
Ta med kikaren! En bit bort ligger Svank: Bring your binoculars! A short way off is Svankälla wetland park, home to marsh harriers, little grebes and lesser spotted woodpeckers. A little further west is Ligårds mosse, a bog so hemmed in by marshland that it's hard to reach. Among the reeds and water lilies, crucian carp and grass carp weighing several kilos are said to lurk.
Tack vare en donation från Nordiska muse: Thanks to a donation from the Nordic Museum in 2003, the library holds around 14,000 old dissertations from the 17th, 18th and 19th centuries, from the universities of Uppsala, Lund, Turku and Greifswald, among others.
Tack vare sin äkta 50-talsmiljö har Kort: With its authentic 1950s interiors, Kortedala Museum has been used as a film location. The flat appears in the feature film Monica Z and in the TV series Upp till kamp and Vår tid är nu (The Restaurant), among others.
Taket i Säve kyrka är indelat i stora ru: The ceiling of Säve church is divided into large panels of biblical scenes, such as Jonah being spewed out by the whale. The first were painted in 1704 by the German Christian von Schönfeldt – his very first church commission. No other church in western Sweden has paintings like those in Säve.
Taket målades 1792 av Johan Liljedahl oc: The ceiling was painted in 1792 by Johan Liljedahl and shows the Holy Trinity, the Last Judgement and Hell. In the scene of Hell there's a creature that looks like a giant lion's mane jellyfish. The paintings have never been painted over.
Taket målades troligen under andra halva: The ceiling was probably painted in the second half of the 18th century, in rococo style, by an unknown artist. The gallery front has secular motifs: marbled urns and cartouches with roses.

The ceiling was probably painted in rococo style in the second half of the 18th century by an unknown artist. Instead of biblical scenes, the gallery front is decorated with urns and roses. The organ front from 1898 was designed by Ragnar Östberg.

The ceiling was probably painted in the rococo style in the second half of the 1700s, by an unknown artist. The organ front from 1898 was designed by Ragnar Östberg. The octagonal bell tower took its present form in 1832 and holds a bell from 1770.
Taket rullar på SKF-lager: A roof that rolls on SKF bearings
Taklagsfest i Blå hallen: Topping-out party in the Blue Hall
Takmålningarna från 1792 av Johan Liljed: The ceiling paintings by Johan Liljedahl, from 1792, depict the Trinity, the Last Judgement and hell. In the scene of hell there's a creature that looks like a giant stinging jellyfish. The paintings have never been painted over.
Takstolar från medeltiden: Roof trusses from the Middle Ages
Takterrass som ett fartygsdäck: A roof terrace like a ship's deck
Takterrass tio trappor upp: A roof terrace ten floors up
Takterrassen omges av ett långt relingsl: The roof terrace is edged by a long, rail-like balustrade that makes it look like a ship's deck – the children played explorers up there. The parents' bedroom could be divided with a sliding wall, which the press found remarkable.
Tallkrogen har fått sitt namn efter ett: Tallkrogen takes its name from an inn, Stora Tallkrogen. The district counts as one of Stockholm's garden suburbs, and one of its streets, Victor Balcks väg, is named after the father of Swedish sport. In fact there were three inns – Stora, Lilla and Gamla Tallkrogen, the Big, Little and Old – along the old country road to Dalarö.

Tallkrogen takes its name from an inn, Stora Tallkrogen. It's one of Stockholm's garden suburbs, and one of its streets, Victor Balcks väg, is named after the father of Swedish sport. The area also had a croft called Svedmyra, known in earlier times as Svinmyra, Pig Bog. It was pulled down in the 1930s but lent its name to the neighbouring district.
Tallskogen på höjderna har troligen slup: The pine forest on the hills has probably escaped modern forestry, so there are trees of all ages and plenty of dead wood. Look out for crested tits, black woodpeckers and goshawks. In 2012 a pond for amphibians was dug by the Ormkärrsbäcken stream.

The pine forest on the heights has probably escaped modern forestry, so the trees are of different ages and there's plenty of dead wood. Look out for crested tits, black woodpeckers and goshawks. By the stream there's a pond dug in 2012 for frogs, toads and newts.
Talludden kallas också Neptuns udde. I o: Talludden is also known as Neptune's Point. Here you'll find Käppalaställningen, a Second World War anti-aircraft battery with gun pits and weapon emplacements. It was restored and reopened in 1994 as a listed memorial to Stockholm's air defence, the only one of its kind in Sweden. A little further away is Käppalaverket, a sewage treatment plant from 1969 that's regarded as one of the most efficient in the world.
Tallumpaviljongen, med sina pyramidforma: The Tallum Pavilion, with its pyramid-shaped roofs, was designed by Gunnar Asplund in 1922. Its name comes from ‘Tallum’, the motto Asplund and Sigurd Lewerentz used when they entered the 1915 competition to design Skogskyrkogården, the Woodland Cemetery. The building was probably only meant to be temporary, but it stayed and served as a utility building until 1981. Skogskyrkogården has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1994.
Tandklinik i skolhuset: A dental clinic in the schoolhouse
Tanken var att båda föräldrarna skulle k: The idea was that both parents should be able to go out to work. The building had a restaurant, a day nursery, a supermarket, a photo lab, a petrol station and a chapel. The chapel is now a nursery, and in 1975 the road outside was named Olle Engkvists väg.
Tanken är att Järva begravningsplats ska: The idea is for Järva cemetery to become northern Stockholm's answer to Skogskyrkogården, the Woodland Cemetery. It's open to people of all faiths and none, and some sections have graves facing Mecca.
Tapeterna på sjukhusvinden: The wallpaper in the hospital attic
Tappström var en egen tätort fram till 1: Tappström was a separate town until 1975 and is now part of Ekerö. Commuter boat 89 to Stadshuskajen, the City Hall quay, is served by M/S Lux, among others.
Tappström är ett smalt sund mellan Ekerö: Tappström is a narrow strait between the islands of Ekerön and Lovön – about 1.5 kilometres long and only just over three metres deep. On its shore, Ralph Erskine designed Ekerö centrum, completed in 1991, with a 'dot' more than twenty metres high as its landmark. Erskine lived on Lovön himself and said he enjoyed coming here to do his shopping. From here, commuter boat 89 runs all the way into Stadshuskajen, the City Hall quay.
Tappsund var ett ångtegelbruk, där maski: Tappsund was a steam-powered brickworks, its machinery driven by a steam engine until it was electrified in the 1920s. At the centre of the works stood a ring kiln, with the drying sheds arranged in a square around it. The street name Tegelbruksvägen, Brickworks Road, recalls the old works.
Taverna och centraltvätt: A taverna and a central laundry
Teater Pero bildades 1983 av Peter Engkv: Teater Pero was founded in 1983 by Peter Engkvist and Roger Westberg. Its venue at Sveavägen 114 was one of Sweden's first cinema auditoriums. In 2018 the theatre received the City of Stockholm's honorary award.
Teater och mat på Stora Holm: Dinner and drama at Stora Holm
Teater och middag på Stora Holm: Theatre and dinner at Stora Holm
Teatern har fått namn efter matsalen, dä: The theatre is named after the dining room, where tables and cupboards could be lowered to the cellar to be laid and then hoisted up again. That way the royal family could dine without any servants present – 'in confidence', à confidence.
Teatern hörde tidigare till Göteborgs St: The theatre used to be part of Göteborgs Stadsteater, the City Theatre, but has been independent since 1996. Productions staged here include Momo, A Clockwork Orange, The Cherry Orchard and Himmel över Göteborg.
Teatern startades 2005 av skådespelarna: The theatre was founded in 2005 by actors Kristina Brändén Whitaker and Gary Whitaker. In 2010 the company won an award at the Edinburgh Fringe for Kristina's own play Expectations, and in 2015 they received the Årets Katharsis award for Constellations.
Teatern är spelplats för sex amatörteate: The theatre is home to six amateur dramatic societies, brought together under the umbrella of Mölndals Amatörteaterförening, founded in 1992. The current building opened in 1998.
Teaterälskare, spetsa öronen! Angereds t: Theatre lovers, listen up! Angereds teater, in the Blå Stället arts centre, stages brand-new plays for children, teenagers and adults, and runs its own drama school too. The arts centre is on Angereds torg, the square that was called Triörtorget until 1977. Closer to the stop is Gunnared cemetery.
Teckenspråk förbjöds och kom tillbaka: Sign language banned – and back again
Tegelbruket blev porslinsfabrik: The brickworks became a porcelain factory
Tegelbruket som gav gatan namn: The brickworks behind the street name
Tegelhuset vid Götaforsliden byggdes 185: The brick building by Götaforsliden was built in 1857 as a spinning mill, but the company went bankrupt straight away. It later housed a sulphite factory, a cotton mill and, from 1927 to 1971, a knitwear factory. Today it's offices.
Tegen räknas till Sveriges allra första: Tegen are counted among Sweden's very first terraced houses – but unlike the Canadahusen built around the same time for workers, they were designed for the well-off middle class. The plans didn't call them terraced houses at all, but “joined single-family houses”.
Teglet från Kristinedal användes till fa: Bricks from Kristinedal went into factories in Mölnlycke and Krokslätt. There was also a gravel pit here, worked out by the early 1930s – and today it's a football pitch.
Tegnér-sägnen som inte stämmer: The Tegnér legend that isn't true
Teknikintresserade Ericsson experimenter: Ever the technology enthusiast, Ericsson experimented with ventilation and electric ploughs. The ploughs were no success, but they gave the neighbours plenty to talk about. He also built the "Alby Stadium", which looked like a Roman aqueduct and carried manure.
Tekniska museet: Tekniska museet, the National Museum of Science and Technology
Tekniska museet invigdes 1936 med Deutsc: The National Museum of Science and Technology opened in 1936, modelled on the Deutsches Museum in Munich. From the outset, visitors could try out the machines for themselves. In 1938 the Mine exhibition opened, and it's still there today.
Telefonpionjären Lars Magnus Ericsson äg: The telephone pioneer Lars Magnus Ericsson owned Alby gård, the manor by Lake Albysjön a little way from here, from 1895 to 1913, and it was in his time that the house got its distinctive look. A later owner, Alfred Ekström, founded the laundry firm AB Fittja Familietvätt and pioneered new methods of industrial washing. Also in the neighbourhood is Fittja gård, where the Svartlösa district court used to sit.
Telefonplan domineras av LM Ericssons ga: Telefonplan is dominated by LM Ericsson's old factory and head office, built between 1938 and 1940 to designs by Ture Wennerholm. The architectural historian Fredric Bedoire has called it perhaps the most beautiful of all Stockholm's functionalist industrial complexes. Today it's home to, among others, Konstfack, the University of Arts, Crafts and Design, and the interactive light installation Colour by Numbers glows above Telefonplan.
Telegrafberget på Brevikshalvön är Tyres: Telegrafberget on the Brevik peninsula is Tyresö's highest point and became a nature reserve in 2021. In 2023 there were eight nature reserves in the municipality.
Teleskopgatan 2 byggdes 1980 om till kol: In 1980 Teleskopgatan 2 was converted into Stacken, a collective house, by Lars Ågren – the same architect who designed the buildings in the first place. In 2016–2017 it became a passive house, with an entirely new facade.
Teleskopgatan 2 var kontor åt Göteborgsh: Teleskopgatan 2 housed offices for the Göteborgshem housing company from 1975 to 1978. Lars Ågren, the architect who had designed the buildings, then converted it into Stacken, a co-housing block completed in 1980. In 2016–2017 it was turned into a passive house with a new facade.
Televerkets förvaltningsbyggnader: The old Televerket offices, once home to Sweden's telecoms authority
Televerkets förvaltningsbyggnader, en ko: A short walk away are the former offices of Televerket, the old Swedish telecoms authority, which served as Telia Company's headquarters until 2016. The complex was built in stages between 1962 and 1972 to designs by Bengt Hidemark and Gösta Danielson, and the buildings on Mårbackagatan won the prestigious Kasper Salin Prize for architecture. If you'd like to dig deeper into the area's past, Farsta hembygdsförening, the local history society, covers Farsta's story from prehistoric times to the present day.
Tellus visade film för första gången den: Tellus showed its first film on 22 November 1920, when the auditorium had 108 seats. In the 1930s two more cinemas opened in "Kransen", Saba and Svanen, but both closed in the 1960s.
Templet stod vid hållplatsen Brogrenen,: The temple stood at the Brogrenen stop, where the northern and southern Lidingö railway lines split. Before the bridge came in 1925, the two rival lines had their own ferry berths at Islinge and Herserud, with ferries across Lilla Värtan to Ropsten.
Tengbom arkitekter förvandlade kontorshu: Tengbom architects converted the office building into housing and placed 18 terraced houses on the roofs. The flats range from one room and a kitchen up to eight rooms and a kitchen. The building was nominated for Stockholm Building of the Year in 2012.
Tengbom arkitekter ville förena kontorsl: Tengbom architects wanted to combine the benefits of the open-plan office with private rooms. The result was the 'combi-office': private rooms along the facades around a large shared space, with glazed sliding doors for eye contact. A model of the building is in the Swedish Museum of Architecture.
Tengbom ritade villan i nedtonad nationa: Tengbom designed the villa in a toned-down National Romantic style, with a hipped, flared roof. The Brunius couple wanted a simple house that was cheap to run, with low ceilings to save on heating. Only the study at the very top was given a high ceiling.
Tengboms arkitekter använde kameran som: Tengbom architects built the Canon building around the idea of a camera. Facing busy Uppsalavägen, the facade is closed with square windows, while the side facing the square is glazed from the ground to the roofline. The brushed stainless-steel Canon signs are almost as tall as the building.
Tengdahl arbetade som murare och ritare: Tengdahl worked as a bricklayer and draughtsman before becoming a journalist at the newspaper Social-Demokraten. When Stockholm's Folkets hus, the labour movement's meeting hall, was to be built, someone with building know-how was needed, and from 1898 to 1901 he served as its agent and the main driving force behind the project.
Tengdahl satt i 13 år i arbetsutskottet: Tengdahl spent 13 years on the working committee for the building of Stockholm City Hall. It was he who took the initiative for the architect Ragnar Östberg to be granted an annual pension of 7,000 kronor in 1924.
Tennisbana där torpet stod: A tennis court where the croft stood
Tennishall med kyrktorn: A tennis hall with a church tower
Tennishallen kom till på initiativ av Gu: The tennis hall was built at the initiative of Gustaf V and paid for with backing from Marcus Wallenberg and the car dealer Ernst S. Nilson, among others. It cost three million kronor and opened on 22 October 1943, in the middle of the Second World War, with the royal family and Prime Minister Per Albin Hansson in attendance.
Tennispaviljongen är en nationalromantis: The tennis pavilion is a National Romantic wooden building with two aisles and a 'church tower' on the entrance side. It looks like a big turn-of-the-century villa, in the same spirit as the Stockholm Exhibition of 1897.
Tensta Träff, gymnasiet och Tenstahallen: Tensta Träff, the upper secondary school and Tenstahallen were completed in 1984 and stand out from the rest of the district. The architect Gösta Uddén blended modernism with traditional Asian architecture, using red brick, patterned concrete and glulam timber. All three buildings carry the blue heritage rating.
Tensta byggdes mellan 1966 och 1972 som: Tensta was built between 1966 and 1972 as part of the Million Programme, Sweden's great housing drive, but today it's the culture that draws people in. Tensta konsthall, a few minutes away, shows contemporary art, and Tenstakyrkan church has a thriving music scene rooted in gospel, where many different Christian traditions share one congregation.
Tensta gymnasium och Tekniska i Tensta: Tensta gymnasium and Tekniska i Tensta, upper secondary schools
Tensta konsthall grundades 1998, när Sto: Tensta konsthall was founded in 1998, the year Stockholm was European Capital of Culture. Internationally renowned artists such as Wolfgang Tillmans, Julian Opie and Shirin Neshat have exhibited here. Since 2014 the gallery has also awarded a writing prize to young writers from the suburbs.

Tensta konsthall, the art centre, was founded in 1998, the year Stockholm was European Capital of Culture. Internationally renowned artists such as Wolfgang Tillmans, Julian Opie, On Kawara and Shirin Neshat have exhibited here.
Tensta vattentorn tronar på Tenstas högs: Tensta water tower stands proudly on the highest point in Tensta and can be seen from far across the open land of Järvafältet. It was built in 1969 and the Stockholm City Museum has marked it in green as particularly valuable. Underneath the tower is the Tensta tunnel, where the E18 motorway runs through two separate 300-metre concrete tubes, built between 2010 and 2014.
Tenstakyrkan stod klar 1973. I dag delar: Tensta Church was finished in 1973. Today the Mission Covenant congregation shares the premises with a Syriac Catholic and an Orthodox congregation, and the Church of Sweden also holds some activities here.
Tenstakyrkan, alldeles intill, är en fri: Right next door is Tenstakyrkan, a free church known for its rich musical life with strong gospel roots. Close by is Tensta konsthall, a centre for contemporary art. And down in the metro, the artist Helga Henschen decorated the station on the theme A Rose for the Immigrants, using texts and poems among other things.
Tenstatunneln byggdes bland annat för at: One reason for building the Tensta tunnel was to let Tensta and Hjulsta merge with the Järvafältet open space, which the E18 motorway had cut off. The tunnel is built strong enough to carry future housing on top.
Terminalen ligger intill rorohamnen och: The terminal sits next to the ro-ro port and partly came into use in December 2018. Once fully built, it will be able to handle two trains of 560–730 metres and four trains of 420 metres at the same time.
Terminalen ritades av Gustaf Rosenberg,: The terminal was designed by Gustaf Rosenberg, who won the Tengbom Prize in 1984. The track hall has four railway lines and a roof of glulam arches, with daylight pouring in through eight roof lanterns. The total floor area is about 104,000 square metres.
Terminalen, platsen och gatan har fått n: The terminal, the square and the street are all named after Nils Ericson, the engineer who brought the Western Main Line to Gothenburg. The tram stop next door used to be called Nordstan.
Tessin och Årstafrun på krogen: Tessin and the Lady of Årsta at the inn
Tessinparken fick sitt namn 1931 efter a: Tessinparken was named in 1931 after the architects Nicodemus Tessin the Elder, his son Nicodemus Tessin the Younger and his grandson Carl Gustaf Tessin. Designed by Arvid Stille, the park continues symmetrically northwards from Karlaplan.
Testhuset i Bäst i test: The test house in Bäst i test
Textilföretaget Gamlestadens Fabriker ha: The textile company Gamlestadens Fabriker had lots of long shafts that kept bending out of true and wrecking the rigid ball bearings. The mechanical engineer Sven Wingquist solved the problem with a self-aligning ball bearing that could adjust to the angle.
The Cure och Lill-Babs i källaren: The Cure and Lill-Babs in the basement
The Jordo Cricket Ground har permanenta: The Jordo Cricket Ground has permanent goalposts and measures 135 by 100 metres – enough for Australian rules football, with 15 players on each side.
Thiel ville först bygga nära Prins Eugen: Thiel first wanted to build near Prince Eugen's Waldemarsudde, which was also designed by Boberg. After a royal protest he had to settle for a plot further out, on Blockhusudden.
Thiels första större köp var Bruno Lilje: Thiel's first major purchase was Bruno Liljefors's Morning Mood by the Sea, for 2,000 kronor. When his apartment on Strandvägen grew too cramped, he wrote to the architect Boberg: 'I want a home decorated with paintings on every wall.'
Thomas van der Noot kallades till diplom: Thomas van der Noot was called away on a diplomatic mission to the Netherlands and never moved into his palace. Instead, the house was let to Dutch envoys.
Thörnströms Kök låg i bottenvåningen på: Thörnströms Kök was on the ground floor of a block of flats and seated around 60 guests. The cooking was modern Scandinavian with a regional focus, and in 2007 the Michelin Guide named it a rising star.
Tibble kyrka började användas första adv: Tibble Church first came into use on Advent Sunday 1976, at a ceremony with Bishop Ingmar Ström. Even so, the formal consecration didn't take place until 1978. The organ was built in 1977 in Hillerød in Denmark.
Tibble kyrkas kyrkorum ligger på byggnad: The sanctuary of Tibble kyrka is on the building's fourth floor. Its only decoration is 950 square metres of glass mosaic by Mogens Jørgensen and Gudrun Steenberg. The same building houses a restaurant, a preschool and a youth centre.
Tideräkningsgatans västra del är en kilo: The western end of Tideräkningsgatan is a kilometre-long hill known as Burmabacken. Legend has it that the name comes from the Burma Road of the Second World War, but both the naming committee and the road builder deny it. The name was already in use when there was nothing here but a footpath.
Tidig vår i söderläge: An early spring on the south slope
Tidiga sommarnöjen vid Mälaren: Early summer retreats on Lake Mälaren
Tidigt fick biografen klarröda neonbokst: Early on, the cinema got bright red neon letters above the entrance: BROMMATEATERN. After it closed in 1971, the auditorium became a bingo hall and later a shop. Today only the name of the block, Biografen ('the Cinema'), recalls it.
Tidigt på 1960-talet infördes fjärrstyrn: In the early 1960s, remote control of the trains was introduced on the line. The control centre was in the Roslags Näsby station house until 1977, when it moved to Stockholms östra.
Tidningen Idun gjorde 1906 ett hemma hos: In 1906 the magazine Idun ran an at-home feature on Villa Bergh, with its blue walls and Blüthner grand piano. Richard Bergh said the house was so peaceful that he often sat lost in a book until half past one in the morning.
Tidskriften Gourmet har två gånger lyft: The magazine Gourmet has twice singled out the bakery for its fine food culture, calling it “Sweden's best gingerbread bakery”. It has also received an honorary award from the M Sandahl Foundation.
Till Angereds Centrum hör också Lärjeåns: Angered Centrum also includes Lärjeåns trädgårdar, a biodynamic market garden with a café beside the Lärjeån river.
Till Corso kom nya filmer en vecka före: New films reached Corso a week before the Enskede Kvarn cinema. So plenty of people from Gamla Enskede came here to see them earlier than at their local picture house.
Till Corso kom nya filmer en vecka tidig: New films reached the Corso a week before they got to Enskede Kvarn – so plenty of people from Gamla Enskede came here to see them ahead of their neighbours.
Till Elvesta gård hörde en kvarn som fin: Elvesta farm had a mill recorded as early as the 1600s. It kept working right up until the 1930s, and the mill building still standing beside the stream dates from the 1850s.
Till GP:s hundraårsjubileum 1959 fick sä: For the 100th anniversary of the newspaper GP in 1959, the typesetting room was given Gunnar Nylund's ceramic relief "Vår tid" (Our Time). The printing works later moved to Backa, and in 1988 the old presses in the GP building were dismantled by a Chinese company.
Till Gamla Tyresö räknas också den stora: Gamla Tyresö also takes in the large forest to the south, where Tyresta National Park lies. About half the national park is in Tyresö municipality.
Till Grönvik vid Mälaren tog man sig på: In the 1880s people reached Grönvik on Lake Mälaren by steamboat, and as late as 1939 the white steamers still made daily trips to the Mälaren islands. Grönvik's small boatyard and harbour from the 1880s are still there today.
Till Gustaf V:s 70-årsdag 1928 samlades: For Gustaf V's 70th birthday in 1928, more than five million kronor was raised and presented to him in a silver casket. The King decided the money should go to the fight against cancer, and the result was the Jubilee Clinics in Stockholm, Gothenburg and Lund.
Till Hökmossen hörde backstugan Mickelsb: Hökmossen once included the cottage of Mickelsberg, which gave Mickelsbergsvägen its name. Tradition has it that a man from Livonia called Mickel lived there, and that the cottage 'stood right up against a rock face'.
Till Hökmossen hörde förr backstugan Mic: Hökmossen once included the cottage of Mickelsberg, which gave Mickelsbergsvägen its name. A little further away is Hägerstensbadet, known locally as Personnebadet after Personnevägen – an outdoor pool that opened on 21 June 1961. The water is heated by solar panels, and swimming is free.
Till Nackanäs värdshus hörde en lummig t: Nackanäs inn had a leafy garden and an octagonal pavilion out in the strait, where the annual crayfish premiere – the start of the crayfish season – was held, among other events. Breakfast, dinner and late suppers were served, and guests could play on two skittle alleys.
Till Snörom hörde inga ägor, bara ett ka: Snörom came with no land of its own – just a kappland, an old measure of just over 150 square metres, where the residents grew potatoes. The 18th-century log cabin is now let out as a holiday cottage.
Till Spånga gymnasium hör ett djurhus me: Spånga upper secondary school has its own animal house with a barn, where students on the agriculture and natural resources programme learn to look after animals. The animal care unit was built up in the 1970s by Owe Sandström, a teacher who was also a fashion designer.
Till Sätra gård hörde en vattenkvarn vid: Sätra gård once had a watermill on the dammed Sätraån stream. The mill burned down in the late 1960s and only its foundation stones remain, but the miller's cottage still stands on a little hill at Sätragårdsvägen 183.
Till bygget gick drygt en miljon handsla: Just over a million handmade bricks and almost seven million machine-made ones went into the building, all in a specially produced dark red brick. The project has been called the last true masons' lodge in Sweden, in the old guild sense.
Till en annan värld: The sculpture Till en annan värld – “To Another World”
Till hemmet hörde ett litet lantbruk med: The home had a small farm with a horse, cows, pigs and hens, and the girls helped with the chores. They also went to elementary school and were taught housekeeping, weaving, sewing and gardening. The home closed in 1950.
Till höger ligger Gröna Lund, Sveriges ä: On the right is Gröna Lund, Sweden's oldest amusement park.
On your right is Kungliga slottet, Stockholm Palace.
Till höger ligger Skansen Lejonet, en fö: On your right is Skansen Lejonet, the Lion Fort, a 17th-century stronghold crowned with a gilded lion.
On the right is the Liseberg amusement park.
Till höger reser sig Avicii Arena, den s: Rising on your right is Avicii Arena, the big white dome formerly known as Globen, the Globe.
Till höger reser sig Nya Ullevi, arenan: On your right is Nya Ullevi, the stadium built for the 1958 football World Cup.
Till höger ser du Vasamuseets tak, med m: On your right you can see the roof of the Vasa Museum, with masts that show just how tall the ship Vasa is.
Till höger ser du den röd-vita skyskrapa: On your right is the red-and-white tower that Gothenburgers call Läppstiftet – the Lipstick.
Till höger syns Kaknästornet, ett av Sto: On the right you can see Kaknästornet, the Kaknäs Tower, one of the tallest towers in Stockholm.
Till höger syns Riddarholmskyrkan med si: On your right is Riddarholmen Church, with its slender cast-iron spire. Many of Sweden's kings are buried there.
Till höger syns Stadshuset med sitt torn: On your right is Stadshuset, Stockholm City Hall, with its tower topped by the three golden crowns.
Till höger syns Älvsborgsbron, invigd 19: On the right is Älvsborgsbron, the Älvsborg Bridge, opened in 1966.
Till höger, på andra sidan vattnet, ligg: Across the water on the right is the island of Långholmen.
Till höger, uppe på berget, ser du Masth: On your right, up on the hill, is Masthuggskyrkan, the Masthugget Church, from 1914.
Till höger, uppe på berget, syns Skansen: On your right, up on the hill, is Skansen Kronan, the Crown Fort, built in the 17th century.
Till höger, vid kanalen, ligger Feskekôr: On your right, by the canal, is Feskekôrka, the city's fish market hall from 1874. It looks just like a church – which is why Gothenburgers call it 'the fish church'.
Till orgeln som invigdes 1885 hade kunge: The King donated 4,000 kronor towards the organ consecrated in 1885, and came to the ceremony himself with Princes Karl and Eugen. Inside the church are also some thirty gravestones, most of them for people who worked at Drottningholm Palace.
Till palatset hörde en stor trädgård. På: The palace had a large garden. In the 18th century it held 81 fruit trees, 18 clipped spruces and masses of berry bushes, and an orangery followed in 1770. A small remnant survives as today's Jakob Mommas park.
Till råoljehamnen på Hjärtholmen har äve: Even ULCC-class vessels – the world's largest tankers, 333 metres long and 60 metres wide – have called at the crude oil harbour on Hjärtholmen. The oil is then stored in huge rock caverns next to the harbour.
Till vänster ligger Gröna Lund, Sveriges: On your left is Gröna Lund, Sweden's oldest amusement park.
On your left is the Royal Palace.
Till vänster ligger Skansen Lejonet, en: On your left is Skansen Lejonet, a 17th-century fortress with a gilded lion on top.
Till vänster ligger nöjesparken Liseberg: On your left is Liseberg amusement park.
Till vänster på berget ser du Masthuggsk: On the hill to your left is Masthuggskyrkan, the Masthugget church. To your right you can catch a glimpse of the harbour and the Göta älv river.
Till vänster reser sig Avicii Arena, den: On your left rises Avicii Arena, the big white dome once known as the Globe, Globen.
Till vänster reser sig Nya Ullevi, arena: On the left is Nya Ullevi, the stadium built for the 1958 football World Cup.
Till vänster ser du Vasamuseets tak, med: On your left you can see the roof of the Vasa Museum, with masts that show just how tall the ship Vasa was.
Till vänster ser du den röd-vita skyskra: On your left is the red-and-white skyscraper that Gothenburgers call Läppstiftet – 'the Lipstick'.
Till vänster syns Kaknästornet, ett av S: On your left is Kaknästornet, the Kaknäs Tower, one of the tallest towers in Stockholm.
Till vänster syns Riddarholmskyrkan med: On the left is Riddarholmskyrkan, the Riddarholmen Church, with its slender cast-iron spire. Many of Sweden's kings are buried there.
Till vänster syns Stadshuset med sitt to: On your left is Stockholm City Hall, its tower topped by three golden crowns.
Till vänster, uppe på berget, ser du Mas: On your left, up on the hill, is Masthuggskyrkan, the Masthugget church, built in 1914.
Till vänster, uppe på berget, syns Skans: Up on the hill to your left you can see Skansen Kronan, the Crown Fort, a 17th-century stronghold.
Till vänster, vid kanalen, ligger Feskek: On your left, by the canal, is Feskekôrka, the city's fish market hall from 1874. It looks just like a church, and Gothenburgers have called it 'the fish church' ever since.
On the left, by the canal, is Feskekôrka, the city's fish market hall, built in 1874. It looks just like a church, which is why Gothenburgers call it the “fish church”.
Tillbaka in mot centrum, förbi Ullevi No: Back towards the centre, past Ullevi Norra and Drottningtorget, named after one of the old city gates.
Tillbaka in mot centrum. Rundan slutar v: Back towards the centre. The tour ends at Kopparmärra, the bronze equestrian statue on Kungsportsplatsen.
Tillbaka in mot stan. Lyssna efter Kungs: Back towards the city. Listen out for Kungssten, where Älvsborgsbron was Sweden's longest suspension bridge when it opened in 1966.
Tillbaka mot centrum. Rundan slutar i Br: Back towards the city centre. The route ends at Brunnsparken.
Tillbaka ner till Järntorget för att byt: Back down to Järntorget to change trams.
Tillbaka till Brunnsparken, stadens hjär: Back to Brunnsparken, the hub of the city's public transport.
Tillbaka till Liljeholmen för vidare res: Back to Liljeholmen to continue towards the city centre.
Tillbaka till Ropsten. Gå ner till båtbr: Back to Ropsten. Walk down to the boat jetty.
Tillbaka uppströms ett stopp, med Lindho: Head back upstream one stop, with the old shipyard surroundings of Lindholmen in front of you.
Tillbaka via Haga södra och Odenplan til: Back via Haga södra and Odenplan to the Central Station.
Tillbaka via Haga, Odenplan och S:t Erik: Back via Haga, Odenplan and S:t Eriksplan to the Central Station.
Tillbaka via Rinkeby centrum, vars tunne: Back via Rinkeby centrum, whose metro station is decorated with Viking art, and Sundbybergs torg.
Back across the water to Hornstull.
Tillbaka över älven. Kliv av vid Lilla B: Back across the river. Hop off at Lilla Bommen for the Lipstick tower, the Gothenburg Opera House and the sailing ship Barken Viking from 1906.
Tillbyggnaden från 2017 är klädd i grå t: The 2017 extension is clad in grey titanium-zinc sheeting, and the gables are made of graphic concrete with freely drawn fantasy motifs by the artist Rebecka Bebben Andersson. The work is called Rökning förbjuden! – No Smoking! The building won Stockholm Building of the Year 2018.
Tillhåll för tjuvar och banditer: A haunt of thieves and bandits
Tillsammans med Rågsveds friområde bilda: Together with the Rågsved open space, Kynäsberget forms a green corridor linking Rågsved, Hagsätra, Högdalen and Fagersjö with Myrängen-Högmora and Stuvsta.
Tillsammans med Rågsveds naturreservat b: Together with the Rågsved nature reserve, Kynäsberget forms a green corridor linking Rågsved, Hagsätra, Högdalen and Fagersjö in Stockholm with Myrängen-Högmora and Stuvsta in Huddinge.
Timmer och tegel vid Mälaren: Timber and brick by Lake Mälaren
Timmerhus med fem kakelugnar: A timber house with five tiled stoves
Ting eller kult på berget: Court or cult on the hill
Tingen stannade inte kvar på ängen. Från: The assemblies didn't stay on the meadow. From 1667 right up until 1916, the Svartlösa district court sat at Fittja farm instead.
Tingsbyn har fått namn efter Sollentuna: Tingsbyn takes its name from the old assembly and court site of Sollentuna hundred at Barkarby torg. It was here, in the early 1800s, that Lars Molin – better known as Lasse-Maja – was convicted of stealing the church silver from Järfälla church. The coaching inn next door is now called Lasse-Maja Wärdshus.

Tingsbyn is named after the old district court site of Sollentuna hundred at Barkarby torg. It was here, in the early 19th century, that Lars Molin – better known as Lasse-Maja – was convicted of stealing the church silver from Järfälla Church.
Tingshuset hade en tingssal, en bostad f: The courthouse had a courtroom, a home for the caretaker and holding cells in the basement. It stopped being a courthouse after 1982, and the Swedish Radiation Protection Institute later moved in. Since 2010 it has housed the Hagströmer Library, a research library for the history of medicine.
Tingshuset invigdes 1907 och kostade 135: The courthouse opened in 1907 and cost 135,000 kronor. It's an imposing villa in Art Nouveau Baroque style with a black metal roof, originally rendered in white. In the 1940s it was criticised as a jarring interruption in the continuous parkland.
Tingsplatsen nedanför berget: The assembly site below the hill
Tingstadsleden beräknades först kosta 17: Tingstadsleden was first expected to cost 170 million kronor, but by the time it was finished in 1970 the bill had reached around 330 million. Among the casualties of the project was the Renström public baths, which had to be demolished.
Tingstadsvassen bär ett riktigt gammalt: Tingstadsvassen has a truly ancient name. Tingstad is recorded as early as 1388 and comes from a village where the ting, the local assembly, used to meet. The city was tight-fisted at first: in 1874 it turned down the chance to buy the reed beds for ten öre a square foot. Two years later it changed its mind – and paid 300,000 kronor. Today most of the district is taken up by the island of Ringön.
Tingstadsvassen var en av Göteborgs tre: Tingstadsvassen was one of Gothenburg's three great reed beds, known together as the ‘stadsvassarna’ – the city reed beds. Today the district covers 198 hectares where the Kvillebäcken stream flows out and the Hisingsbron bridge comes ashore.
Tio procent av biobiljetten: Ten per cent of the cinema ticket
Tio år på bruket för en tomt: Ten years at the works for a plot
Tippningen på Granholmstoppen pågick 196: Tipping on Granholmstoppen went on from 1965 to 1974, when the hill collapsed – it sat on unstable ground in the old Hästa marsh. It was meant to be taller, but the landslides gave it its spread-out shape. Today cows graze on the north-east slope.
Titta in i Childhoodhallen, känd från HC: Peek into Childhoodhallen, known from HCZ
Titta på Gröna Lund (2 min), Sveriges äl: Take a look at Gröna Lund (2 min), Sweden's oldest amusement park, dating from 1883. Then walk to the ferry pier at Allmänna gränd (2 min).
Titta på Sköndalsskolans fasad mot Perst: Take a look at Sköndal School's facade facing Perstorpsvägen. It's decorated with playful brick figures – a sailing boat, a witch, a julbock (Christmas goat) and a girl skipping – plus the short poem 'a b c - 1953'. On the main building is the relief Noah's Ark by the artist Allan Wallberg.
Titta på Trisshusen, tidiga radhus från: Look out for the Trisshusen, early terraced houses from 1909
Titta på bergväggarna vid perrongerna nä: Look at the rock walls by the platforms when it's dark. That's where the light sculpture "En hyllning till rörelse" (A Tribute to Movement) by the artist Raha Rastifard is projected. It was unveiled in 2017 and covers a full 60 by 12 metres.
Titta på gamla Lundbybadet på Herkulesga: See the old Lundbybadet baths on Herkulesgatan
Titta på perrongen. Där sitter en kvinna: Take a look at the platform. A bronze woman in a pointed hat is sitting there waiting – and she has been since 2001. The sculpture is called Väntan, 'Waiting', and it's by Britt Ignell. Perhaps she's waiting for someone to step off the tram. In the meantime, she's watched the multi-storey car park opposite get a new top floor of homes.
Titta på taket: alla små ventilskorstena: Look at the roof: all those little vent chimneys come from the chamber-pot cupboards in the cells. Each cupboard had its own vent running up through the roof. Although the prison got flushing toilets in 1927, the cupboards stayed in use right up until it closed.
Titta på taket: de många små ventilskors: Take a look at the roof: the many small vent chimneys come from the chamber-pot cupboards in the cells. Each cupboard had its own vent up through the roof, and the pots stayed in use right up until the prison closed.
Titta upp mot en fyra meter hög granitpe: Look up at the four-metre granite column outside Karolinska Institutet. Up on top, running, is a bronze sculpture by Eric Grate called The Entomological Abduction – a woman and a man carrying off a third figure who has no arms or legs. The woman being carried wears a hat or perhaps a crown, and the man carrying her has insect-like antennae sprouting from his jaw.
Titta upp på ÅF-huset, 65 meter högt: Look up at ÅF-huset, 65 metres tall
Titteridamm ligger i området Gunnared, ö: Titteridamm pond lies in the Gunnared area, east of Angeredsleden. Titteridammsvägen, Titteridammsstigen and Titteridammshöjden wind around it, and next door is a residential area of the same name.
Titteridamm, en bit härifrån, har fått s: Titteridamm, just up the road, owes its name to a legend. On Saturday evenings, so the story goes, the girls would go down to the pond to check their reflections in the shiny water and make themselves pretty for the dance. They 'tittade' – peeked – into the pond, and that's where the name comes from! Close by is Sankt Paulus av Korsets kyrka, the Church of St Paul of the Cross, a Catholic parish church.
Tivoli där kyrkan står: A funfair where the church stands
Tjugo år till första graven: Twenty years to the first burial
Tjärad timmervilla för en överdirektör: A tarred timber villa for a director-general
Tobak där höghusen står: Tobacco where the tower blocks stand
Tobak och öl i palatset: Tobacco and beer in the palace
Tofslärkan 6 såldes färdigbyggd till Hen: Tofslärkan 6 was sold, newly completed, to Henric Tamm, a bank director and Sweden's finance minister in 1920–1921. By 1926 two of his sons, both lieutenants, were living in the house too. The attic was originally a billiard room.
Togs i bruk före invigningen: In use before it was consecrated
Togs i bruk två år före invigningen: In use two years before its consecration
Tolered hade i 15 år ett eget bibliotek: For 15 years Tolered had its own library on Bjurslätts torg, opened in 1952. It was the first of Gothenburg's public libraries to have a gramophone, and the first to hold film screenings for both children and adults.
Tolered hette ursprungligen Toleröd och: Tolered was originally called Toleröd, and it's mostly detached and terraced houses. Not far from here is Torpet Klara, a day labourer's croft with five buildings. It was so well hidden at the end of a road through a modern villa area that for many years the post office had no address for it. It has been a listed building since 2006.
Tolv lopp första året: Twelve races in the first year
Tom parkering tack vare barn-tv: An empty car park, thanks to children's TV
Tompa Eken, som startade konserterna på: Tompa Eken, who started the concerts at Kafé 44, baked buns for every single gig until he retired in 2018. The café is run by volunteers and even has its own bookshop.
Tomtehuset byggdes 1890 åt publicisten o: Tomtehuset was built in 1890 for the newspaperman and member of parliament Sven Adolf Hedlund. It was designed by his nephew Hans Hedlund together with Yngve Rasmussen. The house has been a listed building since 1982.
Tomten kom från slottet: The plot came from the palace
Tomten ligger på det tidigare landeriet: The site was once part of the Carlberg estate, which served as the place of execution from 1702 to 1809 and was known as Galgbacken (Gallows Hill) or Röhssen's Hill. When the nursing home opened in 1927, it had 72 beds.
Tomten sluttar ner mot Magelungen, med d: The garden slopes down towards Lake Magelungen, with a pond, a pergola and cast steps leading down to the water. On the street side are wrought-iron gates decorated with oak leaves. Today the villa is a private home.
Tomter för tio öre kvadratmetern: Plots at ten öre a square metre
Tomtförsäljningen i Nora trädgårdsstad b: Plots in the Nora garden suburb went on sale in 1926, a few decades later than in the other districts. The roads wind with the hilly terrain, and the plots are smaller than in neighbouring Djursholm and Stocksund.
Tomtförsäljningen tog fart när SJ öppnad: Plot sales took off when SJ, Swedish State Railways, opened a station here in 1918. Commuters poured in, and by the early 1950s Stuvsta was the third-busiest railway station in the country by passenger numbers.
Tor Svae hade just byggt sagomiljöerna p: Tor Svae had just built the storybook scenes at Junibacken when he got the commission. He brought in George Johansson and Jens Ahlbom, creators of the children's character Mulle Meck, and together they built the park out of old scrap and plenty of imagination.
Torben Grut ritade Piplärkan 8 samtidigt: Torben Grut designed Piplärkan 8 while he was also working on Stockholm Olympic Stadium. The villa was built of hand-moulded Helsingborg brick, the same kind used for the stadium.
Torg efter amerikansk förebild: A square on the American model
Torget Hagaplan ligger delvis ovanpå mot: Hagaplan, a square that opened in 2023, sits partly on top of the motorway tunnels of Norra länken, the Northern Link. In the middle of its southern part stands the round office building Forskaren, 'the Researcher', and some sixty trees are planned here, among them giant sequoias and tulip trees. Since September 2023 the square has also been home to Inflyttarna, 'The Newcomers', an artwork by Johanna Karlin.
Torget anlades efter Mariabranden 1759,: The square was laid out after the Maria fire of 1759, which destroyed more than 300 properties, and was sometimes used for executions. When it was named after King Adolf Fredrik in 1768, it was on condition that no more executions would take place here. Gustav III later held one of his tournaments on the square.
Torget byggdes 1953 och ritades av arkit: The square was built in 1953 to designs by the architects Sven Brolid and Jan Wallinder. When it was refurbished in 2019–2020, three new buildings went up: two taller blocks of flats and a lower two-storey building with shops on the ground floor.
Torget byggdes 1953–1955 som ett så kall: The square was built in 1953–1955 as a 'C-square' – a social, cultural and commercial hub for around 9,000 people. The buildings around it were designed by Sven Brolid and Jan Wallinder.

The square was built in 1953–1955 as a "C-square" – a social, cultural and commercial centre for around 9,000 residents. It takes its name from Axel Dahlström, who sat on Gothenburg's city council from 1915.
Torget byggdes 1971 och är uppkallat eft: The square was built in 1971 and named after the author and Nobel laureate Selma Lagerlöf. It's about four kilometres north of central Gothenburg and serves as the local centre for northern Backa. It's home to two schools, Svenska Balettskolan – the Swedish Ballet School – and Skälltorpsskolan, and the square also once had Bäckebol's church hall, part of Backa parish.
Torget där sjön Fatburen låg: The square where Lake Fatburen lay
Torget en kort promenad härifrån hette t: The square a short walk from here used to be called Dragonplan, and its octagonal building has become Rissne's landmark. Beneath the square, in a rock cavern 25 to 40 metres down, is the metro station. Along its walls runs a lettered timeline of historical events from 3000 BC up to 1985, an artwork by Madeleine Dranger and Rolf H Reimers.
Torget fanns med redan på regleringskart: The square already appears on town-planning maps from the 1600s and was long known as Ladugårdslandz Torget. In 1797 it was described as large and desolate, “in many respects a dismal square”. Even in the mid-1800s its surroundings were mostly hovels and fences.
Torget fick namnet Mariaplan 1918, efter: The square was named Mariaplan in 1918 because it sits where Mariagatan ends. The first suggestion was Ladugårdstorg, after the Älvsborg royal farm. Why Mariagatan is called what it is, nobody knows.
Torget fick ny färg och form: A square with a new look
Torget fick sitt namn 1886 efter Landala: The square was named in 1886 after Landala chapel, and fish was being sold here as early as the 1880s. Landala was one of Gothenburg's first three working-class suburbs outside the Vallgraven moat. On Landala torg it's honoured by the sculpture Arbetarhustru, the Worker's Wife, inscribed: ‘With a firm hand, strong from work, soft with love, you held the home together.’ The school next door opened in 1892 as Landalaskolan.
Torget fick sitt namn 1924 efter den hög: The square was named in 1924 after the high ground it sits on, and the name then spread to the whole district, Höglandet – “the Highlands”. From 1926 to 1929, Höglandstorget was the end of the line for tram route 12. On the square is the Höglandsbiografen cinema, opened in 1936, and a small park a little way off is named after the artist Einar Forseth, who lived in a villa nearby from 1925 to 1981.
Torget fick sitt namn 1939, efter den le: The square was named in 1939 after the legendary sea captain Charles – or Carl – Chapman, who was active in Majorna in the 18th century.
Torget fick sitt namn 1946, troligen eft: The square was named in 1946, probably after the governor Nils Kagg. Here stands Våren, 'Spring', a bronze statue by Eric Grate of a naked woman on a granite plinth, put up in 1950 – there's an identical one in Alingsås. The old Torpavallen ground, where Qviding FIF used to play on gravel, is now a retail park.
Torget fick sitt namn 1949 efter läkaren: The square was named in 1949 after the physician Robert Fries, son of the botanist Elias Fries. It was built for the city's housing company under the name Guldhedscentrum, and by 1958 it had 265 flats.
Torget fick sitt namn i mitten av 1920-t: The square was named in the mid-1920s after the high ground it sits on, and it was the square that later gave the whole district of Höglandet its name. From 1926 to 1929 Höglandstorget was the terminus of tram line 12. On the square is the Höglandsbiografen cinema, opened in 1936, and a little way off is a small park named after the artist Einar Forseth, who lived in a villa nearby from 1925 to 1981.
Torget formgavs av arkitekterna Backströ: The square was designed by the architects Backström & Reinius. In the middle stands Per-Erik Willö's Farsta Fountain from 1960, the year the square opened. In the north-east corner there used to be a paddling pool, now covered over.
Torget har bytt stavning genom åren. År: The square's spelling has changed over the years. In 1641 it was Riddare Huss platzen, and in 1662 Riddarehus Torget.
Torget har en blandad service: restauran: The square offers a real mix: the Rancho restaurant, Baguettebaren, a tobacconist and even a pet shop, Göteborgs Zoologiska.
Torget har fått namn efter Drottningport: The square takes its name from Drottningporten, the Queen's Gate – one of the three gates into the fortified city. It was first built of wood in the 1640s and then in stone in 1669, with a sandstone portal from the old Älvsborg fortress. The gate was finally demolished in 1821.
Torget har fått namn efter en by i Ostpr: This square is named after a village in East Prussia, famous for a battle in the Seven Years' War.
