Ulvsunda är det tidigast belagda ortnamn: Ulvsunda is the earliest recorded place name in Stockholm, known since the 1300s. An 11th-century runestone told of the farmer Björn, who "built Ulvsundi". Ulvsund was originally the name of the narrow outlet from Lillsjön lake.
Ulvsundabrons stålstomme byggdes mest på: The steel frame of the Ulvsunda bridge was mostly built on land and then rolled out from the abutments, a technique known as incremental launching. The bridge rests on four concrete piers in the water.
Under 1600-talet härjade danskarna flera: The Danes raided the area several times in the 1600s, and in 1645 the Danish army burned the manor to the ground. It was rebuilt that very same year. The present main house dates from around 1800.
Under 1600-talets sillperiod blev Kalven: During the herring boom of the 1600s, Kalven became the hub of the parish's herring trade, and in 1762 the island got a customs station. In 1865 it became the parish's first seaside resort. Today Kalvsund is car-free.
Under 1700- och 1800-talen var herrgårde: In the 18th and 19th centuries the manor was a summer retreat for artists, writers and royalty. Jakob Olof Gripensvärd, who bought it in 1855, was a close friend of Charles XV, and the king often came over from nearby Ulriksdal.
Under 1700-talet ägdes Beckombergas gård: In the 18th century the farms of Beckomberga were owned by the Stierncrona family of Åkeshov. In 1862 they were bought by Anders Petter Löfström, who went on to found the town of Sundbyberg.
Under 1800-talet köpte brukspatronen Wil: In the 19th century the mill owner William Gibson bought the land, including the farms Kåhögs gård and Högens gård. That's why Kåhögs gård shares the brick architecture of the mill town of Jonsered. Employees could buy a cheap plot of land if they promised to work ten years at the mill.
Under 1800-talet växte tegelbruken på Mä: In the 1800s brickworks sprang up across the Mälaren islands to supply Stockholm with building materials. In 1863 the Mälaren region delivered 19 million bricks to the city; just over 20 years later it was 60 million. They were carried on barges towed back and forth.
Under 1800-talet ägdes Kumla av släkten: In the 19th century Kumla belonged to the Rosenblad family, who added a mansard storey to the main house. The frame is of interlocking logs, but rendered and painted yellow with white trim. The Kumla allé avenue leading up to the house is about 850 metres long.
Under 1800-talets andra hälft växte fler: In the second half of the 1800s several industries sprang up here, including a paint factory and a starch factory. From 1856 to 1877 the Sandvik glassworks made beer bottles, and the Scandinavian Wire Curtain Factory hung on until 1956.
Under 1800-talets senare hälft fanns en: In the second half of the 1800s there was a harbour basin with warehouses just south of Mölndalsbro. This is where the steam launches on the Mölndalsån river tied up, carrying passengers out from Gothenburg to Mölndal.
Under 1870-talets högkonjunktur hade var: During the boom of the 1870s the shipyard employed nearly 800 workers, and that's when most of the workers' housing on Slottsberget went up. The little wooden houses were built with no town plan at all – and it was they that swept away the last remains of the castle walls.
Under 1900-talet hittades fyra allegoris: In the 20th century, four allegorical paintings from the old church turned up in a barn in Askim. Today they adorn the gallery, depicting Chastity, Gentleness, Religion and Truth.
Under 1900-talet var Rudan ett småbruk m: In the 1900s Rudan was a smallholding with a laundry, and the parish records list 'washerwoman' and 'washerman' as occupations. Today the Ormen cultural society has its theatre barn in one of the outbuildings, and the drying barn is a rest hut for walkers.
Under 1930-talet lades grunden till dage: The 1930s laid the foundations of modern harness racing. In 1930 Solvalla held 36 race days with 225 races, and turnover topped five million kronor. The first Elitloppet race was run in 1952.
Under 1950-talet gick Ingo på Islandsfis: In the 1950s Ingo spent her summers fishing off Iceland, and in the 1960s she carried saltpetre and sacks of coffee to Karlstad. In her last years as a cargo ship she was called 'the last of her line'. In 1976 a Swedish company bought her so she wouldn't be sold abroad.
Under 1980-talet startade skolan ett ege: In the 1980s the school set up its own youth centre to tackle rising youth unemployment. Its aim was to help young people into work or education.
Under 2014–2015 byggdes Alviks torn, som: Alviks torn went up in 2014–2015 and has become Bromma's new landmark. It has 18 storeys and 151 flats, with views towards Kungsholmen and Lake Mälaren, among other things.
Under 2023 byggdes torget om till ett gr: In 2023 the square was transformed into a leafy garden square, with repainted facades, furniture made specially for the site and new lighting. It reopened on 23 April 2024. The first major makeover had come back in the late 1980s.
Under 2023 gjordes torget om till ett gr: In 2023 the square was transformed into a leafy garden square, inspired by Gothenburg's vision of a modern garden city. With freshly painted façades and furniture designed especially for the spot, it reopened on 23 April 2024.
Under 3000-talet f.Kr. stod vattnet tolv: In the 3000s BC the sea stood twelve metres higher than today, and Ramberget rose straight out of it as a steep cliff. Now Keillers park sits on top of the 87-metre hill, with one of the best views in Gothenburg.
Under FN:s miljökonferens 1972 blev fält: During the UN environment conference in 1972, the field became a festival ground for the world's youth, with a tent camp and gigs by bands such as Träd, Gräs och Stenar, Blå Tåget and Kebnekajse. Some called it a hippie camp; others claimed the CIA was behind it.
Under FN:s miljökonferens i Stockholm 19: During the 1972 UN environment conference in Stockholm, the field became a huge festival ground for the world's youth, known as Hog Farm. There was a tent camp and gigs by bands such as Träd, Gräs och Stenar, Blå Tåget and Fläsket brinner.
Under Farsta lydde många torp och gårdar: Many crofts and farms came under Farsta, among them Burmanstorp, Forsens gård, Starrmyran, Bergholm and Lugnet. Of these, only Hökarängen farm and Larsbodatorpet survive today.
Under Göta älv i närheten löper Tingstad: Beneath the Göta älv river nearby runs the Tingstad tunnel, an immersed-tube tunnel that carries the E6 between Hisingen and the rest of Gothenburg. It's actually two tubes with three lanes each, 455 metres long. It's also a link in the key motorway between Oslo and Copenhagen – so down under the riverbed here, traffic is speeding between two capital cities.
Under Hagalund går tåget i berget. Hagal: Beneath Hagalund, the trains run through solid rock. The Hagalund tunnels are four railway tunnels about 500 metres long. The first was built in 1911, when Solna station moved to its present site at the northern entrance, and more followed later in the 20th century. The tram stop sits below the residential area known as Blåkulla.
Under Hagsätra torg finns ett stort park: Beneath Hagsätra torg is a large car park. Until the early 1990s it also housed a petrol station with a repair workshop.
Under Hammarkullen ligger en hemlis: Sve: Hammarkullen hides a secret underground: Sweden's only fully underground tram stop, 25 metres below the surface. The platforms were built to take 120-metre trams, but because of ramps and unfinished sections of tunnel, only 70 metres are in use. Up above is Hammarkulletorget, the square built in 1971 and remodelled in 1997 with new colours and a new shape.
Under Hjulstaskolan sprängdes ett bergru: A rock cavern was blasted out for the metro beneath Hjulsta School, and on 31 August 1975 the blue line's trains began running here, about 14 kilometres from Kungsträdgården. Close by are the green Hjulsta allotments. Their association was founded in 1973, and today it's held up as a model of multicultural gardening.
Under Huvudsta centrum gömmer sig en trä: Beneath Huvudsta centrum lies a hidden garden – carved into the rock. The metro station sits in a cavern 25 metres underground and is decorated with Hanging Gardens, an artwork by Per Holmberg from 1985, the year the station opened. The entrance was designed by the architect Yorgo Turac.
Under OS 1912 spelades fotboll här: Finl: Football was played here during the 1912 Olympics: Finland beat Italy 3–2 and Russia 2–1. Today the site is parkland, but traces of the stone wall along the western curve survive, along with a sign about the Olympic matches.
Under OS i Stockholm 1912 hölls skyttet: During the 1912 Stockholm Olympics, the moving-target shooting was held at Råstasjön lake. Clay pigeons were fired out over the lake, and a 'running deer' target ran towards the edge of the forest. The Swede Alfred Swahn won the running deer and the American James Graham the clay pigeons.
Under OS-maratonet 1912 bjöd familjen Pe: During the 1912 Olympic marathon, the Petré family offered the Japanese runner Shiso Kanaguri cordial and buns here. He then caught the train back to Stockholm without telling anyone he had pulled out – and it became "the world's longest marathon". A plaque marks the spot where the Petré house stood.
Under Sickla Köpkvarter finns Atlas Copc: Beneath Sickla Köpkvarter lies Atlas Copco's old test mine, still in use today. It has three kilometres of tunnels on two levels, 20 and 40 metres underground. You can visit parts of it on a guided tour.
Under Södertäljevägen drogs kring sekels: Around 1900, the main water pipe from the Norsborg waterworks to Stockholm was laid beneath Södertäljevägen. The pipe runs under the strait and was completed in 1904, and the water keeper's house from 1902 is still standing.
Under Vita bergen finns Pionen, ett skyd: Beneath Vita bergen lies Pionen, a 1943 shelter for a command centre. The nuclear-proof bunker has been used for parties, among other things, and since 2007 it has been a data centre housing the largest server farm in central Stockholm.
Under andra halvan av 1800-talet tvättad: In the second half of the 19th century, crofting families on Södertörn washed Stockholmers’ dirty laundry to earn a bit of extra money. By the early 1900s there were hundreds of little laundries here, and the laundry era peaked during the Second World War.
Under andra världskriget användes Isolda: During the Second World War Isolda served as an accommodation ship, both in Mollösund on Orust and at Käringberget in Gothenburg. As competition from more modern vessels grew, she spent more and more of her time sailing the Baltic.
Under andra världskriget användes skolan: During the Second World War the school's premises were used as a military signals centre. In the 1950s and 1960s the building housed a Sunday school and a youth club, before it was pulled down in 1972.
Under andra världskriget blev fältet kri: During the Second World War the field became a military airfield. In 1943 it came out that the guards had let German military planes take off again after emergency landings, even though neutrality rules said they should have been detained. The affair made headlines in the press.
Under andra världskriget var Isolda loge: During the Second World War the Isolda served as an accommodation ship in Mollösund and at Käringberget in Gothenburg. She was later sold to Finland, and in 2002 she was listed as a historic vessel. The society behind her hopes to restore her and see her sail again as a training ship.
Under andra världskriget var gården förl: During the Second World War the farm housed families who had fled occupied Norway. In the 1950s the Luther Foundation provided a home here for refugees from the Baltic states. Before that, the house had been a guesthouse and even a detergent factory.
Under berget mellan Främlingsvägen och B: Under the hill between Främlingsvägen and Bäckvägen, Nässlan was built in 1943 – one of Stockholm's secret civil command centres, attached to Hägersten fire station. It closed in the 1990s. The southernmost of the new buildings stands directly above it.
Under bygget gav stålställningen vika, o: During construction the steel scaffolding gave way, and on 10 December 1964 a 30-metre bridge span crashed into the water. No one was hurt, but the work was held up by a couple of months.
Under bygget hette arenan först Änglagår: While it was being built, the arena was called first Änglagården and then Göteborgs Nya Arena. Its current name, after the sponsors, was only revealed on opening day, 10 July 2015. Construction cost 800 million kronor.
Under både mark och hav: Below ground and below sea level
Under de första fyra dagarna kom 50 000: In its first four days the new shopping centre drew 50,000 visitors. From the very start it had nearly 3,000 parking spaces, its own tram stop and two department stores, Domus and Tempo.
Under den gustavianska tiden var Carl Mi: In the Gustavian era, Carl Michael Bellman, Sweden’s great 18th-century songwriter, was among the guests, and he sang the praises of Clas på Hörnet in his Epistles: ‘Come open our temple! Raise the Wreath as our sign!’
Under den kalla vintern 2009–2010 tror m: It's believed the first wild boar crossed the ice of Lake Mälaren to the area north of Görväln during the cold winter of 2009–2010. Birds nesting in the reserve include nutcrackers, common rosefinches and tawny owls.
Under den svåra bostadsbristen efter för: During the severe housing shortage after the First World War, the whole of the Exercishuset drill hall was turned into emergency housing. Simple wooden partitions divided the floor into dozens of one-room flats, with no ceilings at all. Today the building is used for table tennis, dance and historical fencing, among other things.
Under en arkeologikurs vid Stockholms un: During an archaeology course at Stockholm University in spring 2020, two students spotted stone frames that once marked the walls of houses. The largest is about 25 metres long and is thought to be a longhouse. A nearby burial ground yielded finely made bronze objects, including a brooch from AD 475–550.
Under en period bodde familjen Feith på: For a time the Feith family lived at Forsen farm. They ran the well-known Feith's patisserie on Strandvägen and Hornsgatan in Stockholm. In 1792 the farm is recorded as one of several gardeners' homes.
Under en period på 2000-talet var Prinsv: For a time in the 2000s, the Prince’s Villa was the residence of South Africa’s ambassador. In autumn 2004 it welcomed Nobel laureate Archbishop Desmond Tutu, who was visiting to mark ten years since the end of apartheid.
Under en storm 1721 tände en gnista eld: During a storm in 1721, a spark set the wooden-shingle roof alight. The entire upper floor burned, chapel and precious library included. When the palace was rebuilt, the roof was given the shape it has today.
Under forntiden var berget en ö. På plat: In prehistoric times this hill was an island. On the plateau are the remains of a hillfort measuring about 800 by 350 metres, probably from the Migration Period, though only around 70 metres of its wall survive. In 1735 a Viking hoard, buried in the mid-1000s, was found at Finnboda.
Under förhistorisk tid fanns en vattenfö: In prehistoric times there was a waterway between Stora Värtan and Edsviken through what is now Danderyd. Post-glacial land uplift has turned the old strait at Nora into a valley between Noraberget and Klingstaberget, both around 40 metres above sea level.
Under förhistorisk tid gick ett sund mel: In prehistoric times a strait ran through Danderyd between Stora Värtan and Edsviken. Land rise turned it into a valley between Noraberget and Klingstaberget hills. A stream from Lake Ekebysjön once flowed past the church, but today it runs mostly underground in a culvert.
Under förhistorisk tid var Råstasjön en: In prehistoric times Råstasjön was part of Brunnsviken bay, but the rising land cut it off. The lake is named after Råsta farm, recorded as crown property in 1375.
Under förhistorisk tid var Råstasjön och: In prehistoric times Råstasjön and Lötsjön were part of a bay of Brunnsviken. In the Viking Age this was Fröfjärden, a stretch of water connected to Lake Mälaren.

In prehistoric times, Råstasjön and Lötsjön were part of a bay of what is now Brunnsviken. In the Viking Age this was Fröfjärden, a stretch of water connected to Lake Mälaren. An ancient route marked by two runestones also ran past Råsta.
Under fötterna här i trakten går Gnistän: Running beneath us here is the Gnistäng tunnel, built in 1978 as part of the Västerleden road. At 712 metres, it's one of the longer road tunnels in Sweden. To begin with, traffic in both directions shared a single tube, but as the queues grew the air became stale and exhaust fumes built up, despite an extensive system of fans. So in the summer of 1996, a concrete wall was put in to separate the two directions.
Under fötterna ligger Husby tunnelbanest: Beneath your feet is Husby metro station, blasted out of the bedrock and opened in 1977. The artist Birgit Broms painted its yellow walls with birch trunks and Vaxholm archipelago steamers, bringing a surprising touch of the archipelago to the middle of Järva. Above ground stands Husby Church from 1976, given a green listing by the City Museum for its high cultural and historical value.
Under gatorna klättrar blå rankor och bl: Down below the streets, blue vines and leaves creep across the cave-like walls of the blue line platforms. The artist Per Olof Ultvedt painted them in 1975, and if you look closely among the tendrils you'll see silhouettes of the workers who built the station. Ultvedt was best known for his mechanical sculptures, and in 1966 he helped create the famous installation Hon – en katedral, ‘She – a Cathedral’.
Under jord pågår ett stort bygge: Södra: Deep below us, a major construction project is under way: Södra Hagalund will be a new station on the green line's branch to Arenastaden, no less than 45 metres underground. It's expected to open in 2029. Up above, in Eric Grate's park, you can see the sculptor's bronzes, including Oberon and Sparvguden, the Sparrow God.
Under kalla kriget skulle bergrummet bli: During the Cold War, the rock cavern was to become a top-secret defence facility – the first to be proof against an atomic bomb. It was built to protect Swedish fighter jets from nuclear attack.
Under koret byggdes ursprungligen ett gr: A burial chapel was originally built beneath the chancel; today it serves as a smaller church. The upper hall still has its original painted ceiling and is used as a rehearsal room for the choirs.
Under korsningen Sveavägen–Odengatan lig: There's a bridge buried beneath the junction of Sveavägen and Odengatan. Sveabron was built in 1897, but when Sveavägen was raised in the 1910s, the bridge was simply left where it was and covered over. These blocks were once a cinema strip, too. Rialto opened on the corner of Odengatan in 1921, and since 1993 Teater Pero has staged children's theatre in its old premises. Röda Lyktan, the Red Lantern, showed films from 1917 to 1982.
Under kriget fanns ett femtiotal luftvär: During the war there were some fifty anti-aircraft batteries around Stockholm, along with searchlights and sound locators. They weren't manned all the time, but at critical moments – such as when Denmark and Norway were invaded in April 1940 – the units stood ready at their positions.
Under krigsåren fanns ett femtiotal luft: During the war years there were around fifty anti-aircraft batteries around the capital, plus sites with searchlights and listening devices. The heaviest had 75 mm guns, the smallest 8 mm machine guns.
Under köpcentrets passage över E20 ligge: Beneath the shopping centre's walkway over the E20 is a bus station, and the commuter train station is 200 metres to the north. In 2012 there were plans to develop the area around Kyrktorget, north of the E20, but they were dropped.
Under marken här i närheten gömmer sig E: Somewhere underground near here lies Elefanten, 'the Elephant' – a 3,300-square-metre command centre built to withstand a nuclear bomb, blasted into the rock in the 1970s. It stood empty for 19 years until the Swedish Armed Forces bought it in 2017 and put it back into service. Far older is the Edsängen burial ground, a short walk away, with about 125 Viking Age graves – one of the largest in Sollentuna.
Under medeltiden kallades Skeppsholmen W: In the Middle Ages Skeppsholmen was called Wangsö, from vång, meaning a field. The island was mostly bare rock, but its southern part had soil for crops and grazing. By the late 1500s it was known as Lustholmen.
Under medeltiden var Frösunda by, med fe: In the Middle Ages the five-farm village of Frösunda was the largest in Solna parish. In the 1640s the privy councillor Mattias Soop bought two of the farms. Later the commerce councillor Joachim Brandenburg gave the place the feel of a charming Gustavian manor.
Under många år blinkade en rörlig ljusre: For many years an animated neon sign flashed here, showing coins tumbling into Sparbanken's piggy bank. It was a much-loved feature of the Stockholm cityscape until it came down in the late 1980s, when the bank changed its name.
Under många år skördades hö på kyrkogård: For many years hay was cut on the cemetery's unused ground, and in 1866 it earned the city 500 riksdaler. The old main entrance was pulled down in 1927 to make way for the tramline.
Under namnet Ribo fick biografen teknik: As Ribo, the cinema was fitted out for 70 mm film and showed Around the World in 80 Days on Christmas Day 1959. After it closed, the space became a theatre, a TV studio and, from 1997 to 2015, home to the percussion ensemble Kroumata.
Under några år på 2010-talet drev Kista: For a few years in the 2010s, Kista folk high school ran Sweden's first training programme for imams. The school started in 2007 as a branch of Sjövik folk high school in Dalarna and became independent in 2010.
Under reklamtavlorna i Alby station finn: Beneath the advertising boards at Alby station are little figures sticking out their tongues and poking fun at the ads. They weren't in the sketches – Olle Ängkvist painted them while he waited during the work.
Under senmedeltiden fanns i Kallhäll ett: In the late Middle Ages there was a croft in Kallhäll owned by the archbishop, and before the Reformation the land belonged to the archbishop's castle at Stäket. The name first appears in 1539, spelled Kalhelle.
Under sent 1970-tal var Rågsved kärnan i: In the late 1970s Rågsved was the heart of the Swedish punk movement, centred on the Oasen music club. Posters from the very first gigs by Ebba Grön and KSMB still hang on the walls of today's Folkets Hus community centre.
Under shoppingstråken i Sickla Köpkvarte: Hidden beneath the shopping streets of Sickla Köpkvarter is something you wouldn't expect: a test mine where rock drills and mining machinery are put through their paces. It's owned today by Epiroc, which was spun off from Atlas Copco in 2018. The name Sickla means roughly 'a low spot where water seeps up' – a little marsh – and comes from the old Stora Sickla estate. The area was also home to Nobelberget, an old warehouse that became a venue for concerts and events.
Under sin exil från Nazityskland på 1940: In the 1940s, while in exile from Nazi Germany, Willy Brandt – later Chancellor of West Germany – lived at Finn Malmgrens väg 23. Since 1997 the park by the metro's eastern entrance has carried his name. The street itself honours the polar explorer Finn Malmgren, and on Finn Malmgrens plan stands the statue Avskedet på polarisen, 'Farewell on the Polar Ice'. Keep your eyes peeled at the station, too: it has the smallest artwork on the whole metro, a decoration set into the brickwork.
Under skolans första 50 år var svenskt t: For the school's first 50 years, Swedish Sign Language was a natural part of life both in and out of the classroom, and the manual alphabet was used to teach pupils to read and write. The linguist Kristina Svartholm has summed up the school's view of its pupils in two words: 'deaf people can!'
Under skolans första femtio år var svens: For the school's first fifty years, Swedish Sign Language was used as a matter of course, both in and out of the classroom. In 1862 the oral method was introduced: sign language was banned and deaf teachers were dismissed. Today Manillaskolan is bilingual, and since 2013 it has been on Kungsholmen.
Under spårvagnshållplatsen byggs Korsväg: Beneath the tram stop, Korsvägen station is being built as part of Västlänken, the new rail tunnel under the city. From here you can also catch buses to Borås, Kungälv and Landvetter Airport, among other places.
Under stadshuset finns Dalénsalen, uppka: Beneath the town hall are the Dalén Hall, named after the inventor Gustaf Dalén, and the Raoul Wallenberg Room. The diplomat Raoul Wallenberg was born in the summer villa Kappsta on Lidingö.
Under stenåldern hade Magelungen förbind: In the Stone Age, Magelungen lake was linked to Saltsjön, the Baltic inlet, via Drevviken. The connection was cut off in the Bronze Age, around 3,500 years ago. This is also where you'll find the City of Stockholm's largest wetland.
Under tidig medeltid byggdes Askims sock: Askim's parish church was built on this spot in the early Middle Ages. It burned down in 1876 and was replaced by today's Askim church further south. A memorial stone in the churchyard recalls the old church.

Askim's parish church was built here in the early Middle Ages. It burned down in 1876 and was replaced by today's Askim Church further south. A memorial stone in the churchyard recalls the old church, and next to it is Backa School, from 1865.
Under torget byggs tunnelbanestationen B: Beneath the square, the Barkarbystaden metro station is under construction, and all around it a whole new district is springing up on the grounds of the old Svea air wing and its closed-down airfield. A little further away is Kyrkbyn, the church village, once called Järfälla gård, which played a central part in Järfälla's early history.
Under vikingatiden bildade Farstaviken o: In the Viking Age, Farstaviken and Ösbyträsk formed a narrow strait between the Baggensfjärden and Torsbyfjärden bays. Post-glacial land rise cut the link, and Gustavsberg's centre now sits in the old strait's valley.
Under vikingatiden och tidig medeltid lå: In the Viking Age and early Middle Ages a large and influential village called Väsby stood here. When Kungsgatan was blasted through the Brunkeberg ridge, workers found skeletons, armour and coins belonging to buried villagers.
Under vikingatiden var Edsviken och Norr: In the Viking Age, Edsviken and Norrviken formed one continuous waterway with a connection to the Baltic. Just west of the burial ground was an ancient hillfort, but it was removed in the early 1970s when the Tunberget water tower was built.
Under Älvsborgsbron, en bit härifrån, li: Just along from here, under Älvsborgsbron, the Älvsborg Bridge, is one of the city's least glamorous but most essential facilities: Ryaverket. This plant treats the wastewater of nearly 800,000 people in the Gothenburg region, and it has been extended time and again since work began in 1968. Further off rises the Rya accumulator tank, a cylinder about 60 metres tall that smooths out peaks in demand for district heating. You can see it from the harbour entrance.
Under älven en bit härifrån ligger Marie: Under the river, not far from here, runs the Marieholm tunnel, which opened to traffic on 16 December 2020. It was built from prefabricated sections sunk into place, and like the Tingstad tunnel it isn't fixed to the bedrock – instead it floats in the clay. It was expected to cost 3.5 billion kronor. The Säveån river also flows through this area; counting its headwaters, it's 130 kilometres long.
Under åren 1762–1770 arrenderades värdsh: From 1762 to 1770 the inn was leased by James Carnegie. He then moved into Gothenburg and ran a coffee house on Köpmansgatan, next to the German Church. Jacob Wallenberg stayed here in 1769 while waiting to sail on the ship Finland.
Ungdomarna byggde om själva: The young people rebuilt it themselves
Ungdomscenter mot arbetslösheten: A youth centre to fight unemployment
Ungefär 300 meter väster om badplatsen J: About 300 metres west of the Jungfruviken bathing spot is a stone labyrinth 7.5 metres across. It originally had twelve rings, but only six circuits of stones survive. The site is known as Stora Möet, meaning 'the Great Meeting', or Tröggebergs slott, Tröggeberg Castle.
Ungefär där Karl IX:s staty står byggdes: Roughly where the statue of Karl IX stands, a reservoir holding 700 barrels of water was built and opened in 1797 to the sound of kettledrums and trumpets. Inside was a poem by the mayor, Daniel Pettersson. It later became an outpatient clinic and was demolished in 1899.
Ungefär där Karolinska sjukhuset ligger: Until the 1600s there was a farming village called Bolstomta roughly where Karolinska University Hospital now stands. Tomteboda came about through a deliberate twisting of that name.
Ungefär en kilometer sydost om kyrkan li: Roughly a kilometre south-east of the church there's a stone labyrinth, 7.5 metres across, laid out on a slab of bedrock. It originally had twelve rings, but only six circuits of stones remain. The spot is called Stora Möet.
Upp mot Majorna. Titta efter Masthuggsky: Up towards Majorna. Look out for Masthuggskyrkan, the 1914 church high on the hill.
Uppdraget att rita kyrkan gick först til: The commission to design the church first went to Backström and Reinius, but they turned it down and it passed to Peter Celsing. Planning took more than six years, and building didn't start until 1958. The church is blue-listed by the City Museum, its highest category.
Uppe i biljetthallens lanternin hänger s: Up in the ticket hall's lantern roof hangs the sculpture Min vän (My Friend) by the artist couple Eva and Peter Moritz. It's made of aluminium rods bolted and welded together, and was unveiled in 2006.
Uppe på Albyberget börjar en lång rulltr: At the top of Albyberget hill, a long escalator takes you down to Alby metro station, about 24 metres underground. Down there, the artist Olle Ängkvist has painted flowers in vivid colours on moss-green concrete walls. Alby is also home to Cirkus Cirkör, the circus company, based at the Subtopia cultural centre a little way from here.
Uppe på Almhöjden finns en kvadratisk pl: On top of Almhöjden, the Elm Hill, is a square enclosure, 20 by 20 metres, surrounded by a wall of dressed granite just over a metre high. The top of the wall is a planting trough, and the space is framed by twelve high-pruned umbrella elms.
Uppe på Hökeberget står Guldhedens norra: Up on Hökeberget stands Guldheden's northern water tower, which was converted in 2008 into 74 student flats. The roof is about 140 metres above sea level, and on the eleventh floor there's a shared roof terrace. On every floor, the flats are laid out like a fan. The KV art school, founded in 1969, was also based round here until it moved to Lindholmen in 2023.
Uppe på Kvarnberget finns fortfarande en: Up on Kvarnberget hill there's still a church ruin from Karl IX's Gothenburg. Nearby is Kaféhusets trädgård, where you can still make out the foundations and steps of Villa Dalhem, a three-storey house built by the merchant Svante Gustafsson in 1896.
Uppe på Kvarnberget snurrade en gång Stu: Up on Kvarnberget, the Mill Hill, the windmill of Stuvsta gård once turned – and that's how the whole Kvarnbergsplan area got its name. Several of the millstones survive, and the municipality has put one on display on Gymnasievägen. That's also where you'll find Huddingegymnasiet, an upper secondary school whose building is rated among the most valuable in the municipality.
Uppe på Kyrkåsberget, i villastaden Para: Up on Kyrkåsberget, in the villa suburb of Paradiset, stands Villa Porthälla – known to locals, as long as anyone can remember, as Borgen, the Castle. The company director Ernst Harbeck built it between 1914 and 1918 to look like a medieval German castle in stone and brick: five floors and 17 rooms. In autumn 1972 the police carried out a major raid on the villa. Today it's divided into flats.
Uppe på Lilla Klippan står i dag Sankta: Today St Birgitta's Chapel stands on top of Lilla Klippan. It was built in 1857 by David Carnegie the Younger.
Uppe på Störtfjällsberget invigdes Kvarn: Up on Störtfjällsberget hill, Kvarnbyvallen opened on a Sunday in midsummer 1934. It was Mölndal's first proper sports ground and home to FK Herkules, Sweden's oldest 'frisksport' club – part of a healthy-living sports movement. The ground closed in 2007 and is now housing. Not far from here, Biografen Möllan has been showing films since 1959, with 289 seats in the Folkets hus community hall.
Uppe på Vattentornsberget reser sig Jarl: Up on Vattentornsberget – Water Tower Hill – stands the Jarlaberg water tower. It's 47.5 metres tall, and its two tanks supply the whole of Sicklaön with water. The Nacka Forum shopping centre opened in 1989, replacing a set of temporary huts that had stood there for years. A little further on, in Storängen, is Villa Yngve Larsson, designed by Ragnar Östberg – the architect of Stockholm City Hall – and built in 1907 for Yngve Larsson, later a city commissioner, and his wife Elin, née Bonnier.
Uppe på berget i närheten ligger Skansen: Up on the hill nearby is Skansen Lejonet, a 17th-century fortress with a gilded lion on top. It was built to defend the city against attack from the east.
Uppe på berget står Larsbergs hus med te: Up on the hill are the Larsberg buildings, with their brick-red façades, green metal roofs and white balconies – classic 1960s. Just over 1,200 flats were completed here in 1969, all designed by the architect Bengt Gate. Down below is Malmstens, where students learn furniture design, cabinetmaking and upholstery. And the old hospital building in Högsätra was due to come down during 2025, to make way for the new Kärnan district.
Uppe på berget står ett långt hus som lä: Up on the hill is a long building that for many years stood all on its own. It was built in 1914 as housing for workers at AGA, and today it's a state-listed building. In 2001 it was renovated and the flats were sold off as owner-occupied apartments. Just along from it stands AGA's yellow optics tower.
Up on the hill you can see Sofia Church.
Uppe på ett hustak i Råcksta lyser en bi: Up on a rooftop in Råcksta, a bit of the 1950s still glows. The neon sign – RÅCKSTA in green with a swooping 'Centrum' in yellow – went up in that decade, when suburban shops lured customers with little neon signs reading BLOMMOR, FRISÖR and KONDITORI: flowers, hairdresser, pâtisserie. Most of that glowing heritage has gone, but this sign was restored in 2011 and shines as brightly as ever.
Uppe på höjden i området ligger Furulund: Up on the heights here is Furulund, where snow shovels get a lot more use than down in the valley. Furulund sits more than 100 metres higher than Gothenburg, and since the temperature hovers around freezing on many days, it gets more snow, and the snow sticks around longer. Below lies Kåhög, a small villa community on the Säveån river.
Uppe på Åsöberget finns, tillsammans med: Up on Åsöberget hill, together with Djurgårdsstaden, you'll find the largest unbroken area of wooden houses in Stockholm. It has been a cultural reserve since 1956. On Kvastmakarbacken stand Hedberg's malmgård – one of the old town estates – and wooden houses from the early 18th century. Down below was the bay of Tegelviken, filled in in 1910, and that's where Viking Line's ferries to Finland now dock.
Uppe till vänster ligger Skinnarviksberg: Up on the left is Skinnarviksberget, the highest natural point in central Stockholm. Climb to the top for a sweeping view over Riddarfjärden bay, the City Hall and Kungsholmen. The name comes from the 'skinnare', the craftsmen who once prepared hides and leather down by the cove here.
Uppfarten som blev park: The approach road that became a park
Uppför backen ligger Kungliga slottet, s: Up the hill is Stockholm Palace, completed in 1754 after the old Tre Kronor castle burned down in 1697. It has more than six hundred rooms, and the changing of the guard in the outer courtyard draws visitors every day.
Uppkallad efter vindarnas gud: Named after the god of the winds
Uppståndelsekapellet: Uppståndelsekapellet, the Chapel of the Resurrection
Uppvärmd uppfart mot snön: A heated driveway against the snow
Uppvärmd uppfart och hiss: A heated driveway and a lift
Ur askan efter simbadet: Rising from the ashes of the old baths
Ur den medeltida Utby församling bröts 1: In 1473 the parish of Götaholm, or Nylöse, was carved out of the medieval parish of Utby. After its church was destroyed in 1566, what remained was absorbed into Partille, and in 1928 the area was transferred to Gamlestaden.
Uroxe och vildsvin på menyn: Aurochs and wild boar on the menu
Urskog och en ny fluga: Primeval forest and a new fly
Ursvik är egentligen två stadsdelar, Lil: Ursvik is really two districts, Lilla Ursvik and Stora Ursvik. A short way from here stretches Rissne äng, Rissne Meadow, a city park linking Rissne, Hallonbergen and central Sundbyberg. Several red-listed beetles thrive here, and since 2024 work has been under way to turn the area into a nature reserve.
Ursvik är känt för sina skogar och motio: Ursvik is known for its woods and running trails. Every spring it hosts the Ursvik Ultra, a 75-kilometre endurance race that doubles as the Swedish trail-running championships.
Ut till världsarvet Drottningholm på Lov: Out to the World Heritage Site of Drottningholm on Lovön, with two buses. Stroll along Långa raden, a row of houses from the 1780s, and return the same way.
Utan buss till centrum i 22 år: No bus to the centre for 22 years
Utanför Gathenhielmska huset står sedan: Since 2003 the sculpture group ‘Ett segelfartyg sover i hamnen’ (‘A Sailing Ship Sleeps in the Harbour’) by Bianca Maria Barmen has stood outside the Gathenhielm House. The name Stigberget itself is old: it turns up as early as 1593, spelt Stegiebergz watz.
Utanför Hässelby trädgårds- och hembygds: Outside the Hässelby garden and local history museum stands a grey granite runestone, known as Uppland inscription 85. It was found at Riddersvik in the early 19th century and moved here in October 1988. Beside the museum is Hässelby villastad church. A short walk away is the Åkermyntan shopping centre from 1977, which features in a sketch by the comedy group Killinggänget: it's home to the character Fred Asp, famous for partying with his ferret, Göran.

Outside the Hässelby garden and local history museum stands a grey granite runestone, Upplands runic inscription 85. It was found at Riddersvik in the early 1800s and moved here in October 1988. Hässelby Villastad Church is the museum's neighbour. The museum itself occupies the garden suburb's old municipal hall from 1925, which also held a police station and post office – and there's still a police cell in the basement.
Utanför Lovö kyrka står inte en eller tv: Outside Lovö Church stand not one or two, but five runestones – the Viking Age and the parish church side by side on the same churchyard hill. Lovö parish also takes in Drottningholm Palace, and inside the church are around thirty gravestones, most of them for people who worked at the palace. Along Lovö kyrkallé, about 800 metres east of the church, is a woodland cemetery laid out in the 1830s.
Utanför Nya Ullevi står Ingo – the Champ: Outside Nya Ullevi stadium stands Ingo – the Champ, Peter Linde's bronze statue of Ingemar Johansson, world heavyweight boxing champion in 1959–1960. It's 2.4 metres tall and weighs 400 kilos. Inside the stadium, Ingo beat the American Eddie Machen in front of more than 53,000 spectators. Along Stampgatan runs Fattighusån, a canal dug as early as 1641 by Count Per Brahe.
Utanför Sturegallerian står en gaslykta: Outside Sturegallerian stands a gas lamp on an ornate cast-iron post with a bench. It was designed in 1885 by the sculptor Daniel Carlsson and decorated with St Erik and lion heads.
Utanför Västertorpshallen står Efter bad: Outside Västertorpshallen, the sports hall, is Efter badet, 'After the Bath', a limestone group by the sculptor Pye Engström. It's shaped like a sofa where you can sit on the laps of seven people – all of them political campaigners who were in the public eye in the early 1970s. In the same block, Isprinsessan, was Västertorp's upper secondary school, whose buildings were turned into flats in 2007.
Utanför badets entré står bronsskulpture: Outside the entrance to the baths stands Linnéa Jörpeland's bronze sculpture Här och nu, där och då (Here and Now, There and Then): a boy in swimming trunks holding a beach ball shaped like a globe. The globe stands for all the nationalities in the area, and the oak leaf he's looking at is a nod to Eggeby.
Utanför det gamla kommunalhuset vid stat: Outside the old municipal building by the station stands a statue of Jarlabanke, a Viking Age chieftain. According to a runestone in Täby kyrkby, he alone owned "all of Täby".
Utanför står Arne Jones skulptur Ställba: Outside stands Arne Jones's sculpture Ställbart universum ('Adjustable Universe'), six by five metres of copper alloy. While it was in storage during the 2009 renovation, three of its rings were stolen. It went back up anyway, and it wasn't complete again until November 2014.
Utanför torget står Arne Jones skulptur: Outside the square stands Arne Jones's sculpture Ställbart universum (Adjustable Universe), 6 by 5 metres. While it sat in storage during the 2009 renovation, three of its rings were stolen. It went back up regardless, and it wasn't until November 2014 that it was finally made whole again.
Utanför torget står Ställbart universum,: Outside the square stands ‘Ställbart universum’ (‘Adjustable Universe’), a six-by-five-metre sculpture in copper alloy by Arne Jones, unveiled in 1967. The central hall once had a glass artwork from Orrefors too, but it was taken down in the 1990s.
Utanför Önnered ligger Lilla Rösö, i fol: Just off Önnered is Lilla Rösö, which locals simply call 'Lilla öa', the Little Island. It has boathouses, ancient remains, places to swim and even an open-air dance floor. Eskils kanal, Eskil's Canal, runs along its northern side, and to the north-west lies its big sister, Stora Rösö. Önnered itself is a district of 516 hectares in the city's South-West area.
Utbudet i centrumet har krympt under 200: The range of shops in the centre has shrunk since 2000, and the post office became a restaurant in 2001. Since 2005 Vårberg flea market has had its sales floor on the level below the shops.
Utby kyrka ligger alldeles i närheten oc: Utby Church is close by and now belongs to Nylöse parish. But Utby's church history goes back further – and is more dramatic. The old parish of Utby lost its church when it was destroyed in 1566, and in 1571 the parish was absorbed into Partille. A little further away was Fjällbohemmet, a care home that operated in Utby from 1939 to 1983.
Utby kyrka ritades av Arvid Bjerke och i: Utby Church was designed by Arvid Bjerke and consecrated on Palm Sunday 1923. It's built of rough-hewn augen gneiss quarried on the spot. The top of the tower is clad in red-painted timber and crowned with a copper-covered cap and a weathercock.
Utbyggnaden av Viksjö var en av landets: The development of Viksjö was one of the biggest small-house projects in Sweden. At its fastest, a house was finished every day. Between 1970 and 1980 the population rose from just under 5,000 to almost 13,000.
Ute i Göteborgs södra skärgård, cirka 16: Out in Gothenburg's southern archipelago, about 16 kilometres south-west of the city centre, lies Donsö. The island covers less than two square kilometres, yet it has over 1,500 year-round residents. Since 2020 the settlement has officially been part of the town of Styrsö, and the island has its own church, Donsö Church, in Styrsö parish.
Ute i Lännerstasundet ligger Fisksätra h: Out in the Lännerstasundet strait lies Fisksätra holme, an islet with spots for swimming and barbecues, reached by a footbridge and cycle bridge. Since 1974 the community centre, Folkets hus, has hosted the International Festival, with music and dancing.
Ute i Mälaren ligger Björnholmen, en ö s: Out in Lake Mälaren lies Björnholmen, an island belonging to the royal estate of Drottningholm. Legend has it that the name, 'Bear Islet', comes from the day King Karl IX shot a bear there. In the 18th century the island had a lakeside tavern, and in the first half of the 19th century it was a favourite day out for well-to-do Stockholmers. Around 1859, the newspaper publisher and agitator Franz Sjöberg built Stora Villan, the Great Villa, in Italian style.
Ute i Rivö fjord ligger ön Hjärtholmen,: Out in the Rivö fjord lies the island of Hjärtholmen, where two families employed by Shell lived in the 1950s. There was no bridge, so the workers had to be ferried back and forth by boat. The island was later linked by a bridge, and in the late 1960s the Torshamnen oil harbour was built alongside. Today crude oil is stored in caverns deep in the island's rock, and from 1993 to 2018 five wind turbines turned here.
Ute på plattformen vid Rågsveds station: Out on the platform at Rågsved station is Björn Selder's bronze sculpture Fågel Grön, Bird Green. A short way off in Högdalen is the Cyklopen culture house, run entirely by volunteers from the Kulturkampanjen association. The first Cyklopen was finished in 2007, but in November 2008 it burned down in an arson attack thought to be the work of Nazis. The volunteers didn't give up – they built a new one.

Utställningen invigdes den 24 maj 1927 a: The exhibition was opened on 24 May 1927 by King Gustaf V, together with Prince Carl and Prince Eugen. It ran until 15 September and drew around 25,000 visitors. Its board included Gunnar Asplund, Sigurd Lewerentz and Sven Markelius.
Utställningen visar litografin från börj: The exhibition shows lithography as it was in the early 1800s, with printing presses and a large collection of lithographic stones. Most of the stones were used to print matchbox labels, and the designs are still on them.
Uttalet är viktigt här: Ramberget sägs m: Here's a pronunciation tip: Ramberget is said with a short 'a', and the first part of the name comes from ramn, an old word for raven. BK Häcken used to play at the old Rambergsvallen ground, and on the same spot today stands Nordic Wellness Arena, formerly Bravida Arena, opened in 2015. Next door is Lundbybadet, the swimming baths from 1973. Interestingly, the arena came as a kit, put together from prefabricated sections, and it has twins in Paderborn and Offenbach in Germany.
Uttrycket Kyss Karlsson myntades i Haga: The Swedish expression "Kyss Karlsson" was coined at Haga courthouse in 1913.
Utöver de svenska banden har också norsk: It's not just Swedish bands that have recorded at Studio Fredman – Norway's Dimmu Borgir and America's Panic! at the Disco have too. At The Gates, The Haunted and Arch Enemy have all passed through, and the studio has worked with labels such as Nuclear Blast and Century Media.

Vagnen rullar på gummihjul och dras av l: The car runs on rubber wheels and is pulled by cables. It's built for 35 people, but SL, the Stockholm transport authority, has cut its capacity to 17. Since its 2009 renovation it has worn the same colours as the C20 metro trains.
Vagnhallen Rantorget är Göteborgs spårvä: Vagnhallen Rantorget is the main depot for Gothenburg's trams, with a car park on the roof. Designed by Abako, it won the Kasper Salin Prize, Sweden's top architecture award, in 1985. It was renamed from Vagnhallen Gårda so it wouldn't be confused with the Gårdahallen sports hall.
Vagnhallens första etapp byggdes av PEAB: The first phase of the tram depot was built by PEAB and the second by Skanska. The expansion is needed partly for the planned tram line along Lindholmsallén. The track joins the network between the Frihamnen and Hjalmar Brantingsplatsen stops.
Vakten som tappade bron: The guardhouse that lost its bridge
Valand hade teakpanel, lampetter från Sv: Valand had teak panelling, wall lamps from Svenskt Tenn, leather-upholstered chairs and neon tubes by Ruben Morne. When the café closed in 2018, the regular Per Faxneld took the initiative to buy, dismantle and store the entire interior. Parts of it were then to furnish the newly renovated Bio Aspen cinema in Aspudden.
Valands 1950-talsmiljö har synts i långf: Valand's 1950s interior has appeared in the feature films Monica Z, Gentlemen and The Man on the Balcony, and in the TV series Ramona, Silvermannen and The Restaurant (Vår tid är nu). Parts of Gun-Britt Sundström's novel Maken are set at Valand, as a sign on the façade once pointed out.
Valands konsthögskola har fått sitt namn: The Valand Academy of art takes its name from this building, where the school was based from 1886 to 1925. Today the Valand building houses a party venue and nightclub, also called Valand.
Valborgsbrasa där kvarnen stod: A Walpurgis bonfire where the mill stood
Valborgsbrasan där kvarnen stod: A Walpurgis bonfire where the mill stood
Valborgsbål där kvarnen stod: A Walpurgis bonfire where the mill stood
Valla torg har fått namn efter Valla går: Valla torg is named after Valla gård, a farm mentioned as early as 1330; the last of its buildings were demolished in 1960. In the square, Bertil Johnson's Valla fountain bubbles away. Along the footpath towards Årsta centrum is a burial ground from the late Iron Age, with ten burial mounds and 35 stone settings, two of them in the shape of ships. Beside it stands Årsta Church, designed by Johan Celsing and consecrated in 2011.
Valla var en av flera gårdar runt det bö: Valla was one of several farms around the fertile fields now known as Årstafältet – once a bay of the Baltic Sea. The name Valla comes from the Old Swedish 'valder': a bank, a field, grassy ground.
Vallen som nästan blev bostäder: The sports ground that nearly became housing
Valvsal med liten kupol: A vaulted hall with a little dome
Van der Nootska palatset: Van der Nootska palatset, the Van der Noot Palace
Van der Nootska palatset byggdes 1671 ti: The Van der Noot Palace was built in 1671–72 for Baron Thomas van der Noot, at a time when Sweden was one of Europe's great powers, and it has survived several attempts to knock it down. A block away is Monteliushuset, the house where the National Antiquarian Oscar Montelius was born and where he died. Nearby, Spegelteatern, the Mirror Theatre, was based for 35 years, under the motto: 'We will hold a mirror up to the world – without smashing the mirror.'
Vanadisbadet i Vanadislunden var Stockho: Vanadisbadet, in Vanadislunden park, was Stockholm's first electrically heated outdoor pool. At the southern end of the park stands Stefan's church from 1904. And on Surbrunnsgatan was Konditori Valand, a café run for 60 years from 1954 by Stellan and Magdalena Åström. Magdalena had come to Stockholm as a refugee from Nazi Germany.
Vantörs kyrka i Högdalen har en förgylld: Vantör church in Högdalen has a gilded weathercock made by the sculptor Arne Jones in 1960. It was voted Church Cockerel of the Year in 1997 and has become Högdalen's emblem – hence the route's motto, "From cockerels in Högdalen to garden plots by Årstaviken".
Vantörs kyrka invigdes 1959. Dess förgyl: Vantör Church opened in 1959. Its gilded cockerel, designed by the sculptor Arne Jones, was voted Church Cockerel of the Year in 1997 and has become the symbol of Högdalen. One of the tower blocks in the centre is even called Tupphuset, 'the Cockerel House'.
Vapenhusets brädtak har målningar av äng: The wooden ceiling of the church porch is painted with angels and clouds by the painter David Schwenk in 1712. The west entrance has a sandstone portal from 1754, probably designed by Carl Hårleman.
Var stod slaget egentligen?: Where was the battle really fought?
Varde ljus i aluminium: Let there be light, in aluminium
Varför byta ett namn från medeltiden? Jo: Why change a name dating from the Middle Ages? Because in 1947 the villa areas here were renamed Trollbäcken so they wouldn't be confused with the town of Kumla in Närke.
Varhelyi hade tänkt bo i en av ateljévån: Varhelyi had planned to live in one of the studio flats at the top himself. But his wife was afraid of heights, so it never happened. The building was designed for living 'from cradle to grave', with a youth hostel, homes for the elderly and family flats.
Varje augusti tävlar skolans ettor och t: Every August the school's first- and second-years compete in a range of events in Hulesärken. The idea is to bring the new students together and do away with hazing.
Varje radhus fick ett stort allrum i sam: Each terraced house had a large living room on the same level as the kitchen, separated by glass panels so parents could keep an eye on the children at play. Skylights reinforced the idea. Next to the entrance was a small room intended for the housewife, a lodger or a domestic help.
Varje radhus har ett stort allrum vid kö: Each terraced house has a large family room next to the kitchen, divided off with glazed panels and intended for meals and children's play. The idea was new at the time, and skylights made the most of it. The houses were stepped up, down and sideways to fit the hilly terrain.
Varje radhus är bara 4,5 meter brett och: Each terraced house is only 4.5 metres wide and 9.5 metres deep, yet fits in three rooms and a kitchen, a cellar with a laundry room and a small toilet. The architect Victor Bodin drew his inspiration from English garden cities.
Varje station har en kort signatur. Före: Every station has a short code. Before it closed, Sävenäs was known as Säv, but since reopening in 2026 its code has been Gsv, for Göteborg Sävenäs.
Varje vår blir det blått på Björkö. Vid: Every spring, Björkö turns blue. At Bovik there's an area called Pjonken, famous for the masses of hepaticas – little blue anemones – that flower there. The island is in Gothenburg's northern archipelago, and the village has around 1,400 residents. A short way from here stands Björkö Church, which belongs to Öckerö parish.
Varje vår leker en stor mängd grodor i s: Every spring huge numbers of frogs spawn in the forest. Lesser and great spotted woodpeckers, jays and starlings have all nested here. A two-kilometre heritage trail takes you past ancient remains, and from the southern slope there's a wide view over Långbro.
Varje vår samlas tusentals människor vid: Each spring thousands of people turn up at Kåhög farm to watch the cows being let out to pasture. Salmon fishing on the Säveån river has a long tradition, and Kåhögs löd was one of the most popular spots. Jonsered even used to have its own Kåhög apple.
Varje år besöks pegmatitbrotten av ett s: Every year large numbers of students from the University of Gothenburg and Chalmers come to study the pegmatite quarries. The area was declared a natural monument as early as 1972.
Varje år firades midsommar i Tornparken,: Every year Midsummer was celebrated in Tornparken, organised by Sundbyberg's local heritage society. Today the park has a paddling pool, a playground and a football pitch, among other things.
Varje år går ett fackeltåg från Fräntorp: Every year a torchlit procession sets off from Fräntorps Folkets hus, the community hall, up to a clearing in the woods where children can meet Father Christmas. The rest of the year the hall is used for dancing, theatre, yoga and children's parties.
Varje år hålls en mindre julmarknad vid: Every year a small Christmas market is held at Långnäs farm, which sometimes hosts art exhibitions too.
Every year the owners of Långnäs farm hold a small Christmas market there. The farm sometimes opens for art exhibitions too.
Varje år kommer ett stort antal studente: Every year, large numbers of students from the University of Gothenburg and Chalmers come here to study the pegmatite. The area was declared a natural monument as early as 1972.
Varje år reds cirka 400 löpningar på Täb: Every year around 400 races were run at Täby Galopp racecourse, with some 43 million kronor paid out in prize money. The biggest races included Stockholms Stora Pris and Täby Vårsprint.

Around 400 races are run at Täby every year, and some 43 million kronor was paid out in prize money. The biggest included Stockholms Stora Pris, and in September the steeplechases HM Konungens Pris and HM Drottningens Pris – the King's and Queen's Prizes – were run.
Varsin ateljé på landet: A studio each in the country
Varuhusen fick egna fasader: vita elemen: Each department store got its own façade: white panels pierced with a circular pattern for Tempo, and white metal cassettes for Kvickly. The middle building has oiled teak panelling topped by stylised battlements crowned with globe lights. The square was laid out like an Italian piazza.
Varuhuset vid Kungens kurva blev en förs: The store at Kungens kurva became a testing ground for new ideas. This was where the play corner with a ball pit at the entrance and an in-house restaurant serving traditional Småland cooking were first tried out – and where self-service with pick-it-yourself warehouse shelving really took off.
Varvet kom till för att båtarna som bygg: The shipyard was founded because the vessels being built at Hornstull had grown too big to pass through Nils Ericson's lock out to the Saltsjön bay. By 1900 Finnboda had become one of Sweden's largest shipyards, second only to Götaverken.
Varvet som blev park: The shipyard that became a park
Varvsarbetarnas pärlband: The shipyard workers' string of pearls
Varvsgatan hette fram till 1885 Pipbruks: Until 1885 Varvsgatan was called Pipbruksgränd, Pipe Works Lane, after a pipe works by Långholmssundet strait where clay pipes were made from white Dutch clay in the 18th century. The memory lives on in Pipmakartrappan, the Pipe Maker's Steps. The big buildings in the Plankan and Drakenberg blocks show that the Million Programme, Sweden's huge housing drive, reached the inner city too.
Varvsjätten Götaverken höll till här änd: The shipbuilding giant Götaverken was based here until 1991, and its old shipyard halls now have a new life as sports halls. Kanalhuset, by the water, was designed for the camera maker Hasselblad, who only stayed a short time. Today it's where Swedish television, SVT, and Swedish Radio broadcast from. And Lundbybadet, the bathhouse from 1915, became a karate club after the last bath attendant, Ante Melander, went home for good in 1973.
Varvsägaren Gustav Groth i Sjötorp byggd: The shipyard owner Gustav Groth in Sjötorp built Ingo on his own account to keep his yard workers busy during the depression of the early 1920s. She cost 27,000 kronor and was named after his brother-in-law, Ingo Busck.
Vass ena sidan, kaj andra: Reeds on one side, a quay on the other
Vassen hörde först till Backa socken. Ge: Vassen originally belonged to Backa parish. A royal letter in 1881 decreed that it be transferred to the City of Gothenburg, which happened on 1 January 1883. Dredging and drainage work followed from 1885 to 1898.
Vatten och avlopp i husen ansågs mycket: Running water and drains were considered a real luxury. Storängen got electricity as early as 1910, and an advertising brochure boasted that all the roads were ‘well lit by electric light’.
Vatten som rinner ur väggen: Water that flows from the wall
Vatten som trycker på: Water with a push of its own
Vattenborgen behövdes eftersom trycket i: The water tower was needed because the pressure in the pipes dropped so much on hot summer days that kitchens and fire hydrants sometimes ran dry. Construction began in 1892. The Vattenborgen block east of Stadshagsplan is a reminder of it.
Vattenborgen på berget: The water castle on the hill
The water level in the Lärjeån river varies enormously. In dry summers stretches of it shrink to a stream, while during the snowmelt it can burst its banks.
Vattenståndet i Lärjeån varierar kraftig: The water level in Lärjeån varies greatly. In dry summers parts of the river shrink to little more than a stream, while it can flood when the snow melts. In 1969 it was decided to blast a tunnel through the rock of Vättlefjäll to carry away high water.

The water level in Lärjeån varies enormously. In dry summers, stretches of the river shrink to a stream, while the spring thaw can make it burst its banks. In 1969 it was decided to blast a tunnel through the rock of Vättlefjäll down to the Göta älv river, to help Lärjeån cope with high water.
Vattenståndet varierar enormt. Torra som: The water level varies enormously. In dry summers stretches of the river shrink to a stream, yet it can burst its banks when the snow melts. In 1969 it was decided to blast a tunnel through the rock of Vättlefjäll down to the Göta älv river to help it cope with high water.
Vattenståndet varierar kraftigt. Torra s: The water level varies dramatically. In dry summers parts of the river dwindle to little more than a stream, yet it can flood when the snow melts. In 1969 it was decided to blast a tunnel through Vättlefjäll to carry away the high water.

Vattentornet byggdes 1962–1963 på Tallbe: The water tower was built in 1962–1963 on the summit of Tallberghöjden. It's 28 metres tall, holds 3,000 cubic metres of water and stands on 14 concrete pillars. When it was drained in 2015, the council had to reassure people that it wasn't a leak.
Vattentornet har en tidig betongkonstruk: The water tower has an early concrete structure but is entirely clad in Helsingborg brick laid in a strongly patterned bond, in the National Romantic style of the 1910s. It's 27 metres tall, with five storeys and a terrace at the top.
Vattentornet och branden: The water tower and the fire
Vattentornet på höjden: The water tower on the hill
Vattentornet ritades av Ivar Tengbom och: The water tower was designed by Ivar Tengbom and Ernst Torulf in a restrained National Romantic style and was built in just eight months. Inside the tower was a flat for the engineer, with two rooms and a kitchen. It was taken out of service as early as the late 1930s.
Vattentornet ritades av Vattenbyggnadsby: The water tower was designed by Vattenbyggnadsbyrån, which did Sätra water tower at the same time. With its massive concrete, sturdy columns and rhythmic pilaster strips it looks like a scaled-up ancient round temple, and the concrete still bears the imprint of the boards used for the moulds.
Vattentornet som liknar en svamp: A water tower like a mushroom
Vattentornet stod klart 1936 och rymde 3: The water tower was finished in 1936 and held 300 cubic metres of water. Casting the entire outer shell in just eight days was considered quite a feat.
Vattentornet stod klart 1987 och är 20 m: The water tower was finished in 1987 and is 20 metres wide. The artist Åke Pallarp painted its facade with abstract patterns and letters that together spell out the word NACKA. The water level in the upper tank is 103 metres above sea level.
Vattentornets yttre reservoar vilar på 2: The water tower's outer reservoir rests on a ring of 20 concrete pillars. In 2010 someone proposed fitting around 70 flats between the pillars, but Norrvatten said no – the tower is a protected facility.
Vattenverket ritades av Paul Hedqvist i: The waterworks was designed by Paul Hedqvist in a crisp functionalist style. The semicircular tower on the west facade ends in a viewing platform with a light steel railing that brings to mind a ship's bridge.
Vattnet från Fnyskbäcken passerar först: Water from the Fnyskbäcken stream first passes through an oil separator and a pond where particles carrying phosphorus and heavy metals sink to the bottom. It then flows across a grassy area that deals with the nitrogen, and finally into a bio-pond. Measurements show that the treatment works well.
Vattnet från Örtjärnen rinner via Finneb: Water from Örtjärnen flows out via Finnebäcken, passes through two streams and reaches the sea 24 kilometres away. The lake lies 72 metres above sea level and belongs to the catchment of the Kungsbackaån river.
Vattnet når Välen via Stora ån, som avva: Water reaches Välen via Stora ån, the stream that drains the entire Fässberg valley. The bay lies at the innermost end of the northern part of Askimsviken.
Vattnet når havet långt bort: A long way to the sea
Vattnet pumpas hit från Görvälns vattenv: The water is pumped here from the Görväln waterworks by Lake Mälaren. The overflow drains into Edsviken. Building it cost 8.9 million kronor.
Vattnets väg till havet: The water's road to the sea
Vattängen betyder ”den våta ängen” och k: Vattängen means "the wet meadow", after a stream that once ran through the area. The farm appears on the earliest known map of Lidingö, from November 1661.
Vaxljusfabriken i Sjövillan: The wax candle factory in Sjövillan
Verandans pelare har visat sig vara iden: The veranda's pillars turn out to be identical to those that once stood in the Hall of State at Stockholm Palace, which were shipped out to Drottningholm in 1788. When today's bridge was built in the early 1970s, the whole house was moved a little to the south-east.
Verket byggdes 1958–1969 och byggdes ut: The plant was built in 1958–1969 and extended between 1994 and 2000. On 26 April 2000 it was reopened by King Carl XVI Gustaf. In 2007 it treated wastewater for the equivalent of about 520,000 people.
Verket byggdes på 1970-talets mitt som e: The plant was built in the mid-1970s as a counterpart to the Hässelby plant, supplying district heating to the new districts of Husby, Akalla and Kista. It was originally jointly owned by Stockholm and Sollentuna municipalities.
Verket planerades i slutet av 1970-talet: The plant was planned in the late 1970s under the working name Mårtensdalsverket and was intended as an oil-fired reserve plant. In 1983 the city council decided it should be fitted with heat pumps instead.
Verket stängdes 1974, bland annat efters: The plant closed in 1974, partly because low oil prices made it unprofitable. The heavy water was sold to Canada, and since 1980 the fire service has used the site as a training ground. Vattenfall dismantled the plant in 2020–2025.
Verket är delvis insprängt i berget i et: The plant is partly blasted into the rock in an outdoor recreation area and was designed by the architect Sture Frölén. Since nobody was sure how long the reactor vessel would last, the facility was built so the vessel could be replaced, with room to store up to three vessels in the reactor pit.
Verkets två skorstenar är båda 135 meter: The plant's two chimneys are both 135 metres tall. The older one is brick and was originally only 80 metres; in 1966 a second one was built in concrete, and the old one was extended at the same time.
Verksamheten fick sitt nuvarande namn 19: The hospital got its current name in 1999. Ground was broken in 2015 for a new 31,000-square-metre wing, and the first patients moved in in 2021.
Verksamheten har skiftat genom åren. I h: The building has had many uses over the years. Its eastern end once housed a herring smokehouse and a foundry, and from the 1880s the smithy was a workplace for prisoners from Nya Varvet – until the prison there closed in 1907.
Verkstad i vardagsrummet: A workshop in the living room
Verkstaden lades ner 1929, och en av de: The engineering works closed in 1929; one of its last deliveries was the icebreaker Västervik that December. The site was then cleared for housing, and street names such as Slipgatan, Lindvallsplan and Verkstadsgatan recall the old industry.
Verkstadens första fartyg levererades 18: The yard delivered its first vessel in 1847: a small iron steamer called Kare, ordered by the navy. It was meant to serve as a tug in Stockholm and a pleasure boat for the royal family, but ended its days as a tug on the Ångermanälven river.
Vesslan var en gåva av Magna Sunnerdahl,: Vesslan, the Weasel, was a gift from Magna Sunnerdahl, a keen patron of art and culture. On the back of the plinth it says "Gåfva af M.S. - 1911" (Gift from M.S.). The sculpture was cast in bronze at the Herman Bergman art foundry.
Veteran-VM i gamla badet: Masters world championships at the old baths
Veteranbrandbilar i bunkern: Vintage fire engines in the bunker
Veteranvagnarna åker bara uppför: The vintage trams only go uphill
Vi befinner oss på Hisingen, till ytan S: We're on Hisingen, Sweden's fifth-largest island by area – after Gotland, Öland, Södertörn and Orust – and the second most populous. It's bounded by the Göta älv river, the Nordre älv river and the Kattegat. About three quarters of the island belongs to the province of Bohuslän, while the rest, the parishes of Lundby and Tuve, belongs to Västergötland. Nearby is the little village of Holm in Tuve parish.
Vi har just korsat Göta älv på Hisingsbr: We've just crossed the Göta älv river on Hisingsbron, a lift bridge that opened in 2021, replacing the old Götaälvbron. Frihamnen was once a free port, where goods could be stored without paying customs duty. Now a whole new district is taking shape here.
Vi kör över Västerbron, med en av Stockh: We're crossing Västerbron, the Western Bridge, with one of the best views in Stockholm – out over Riddarfjärden bay, City Hall and Gamla stan, the Old Town.
Vi kör över Västerbron. Titta åt vänster: We're now crossing Västerbron, the Western Bridge. Look to your left: there's City Hall, Riddarholmen and Gamla stan, the Old Town. Down below on the right is the island of Långholmen.
Vi närmar oss Kålltorp, ett lugnt villa-: We're coming into Kålltorp, a quiet residential area of villas in eastern Gothenburg. From here it's not far to the Delsjö area, a large nature reserve of lakes and forest.
Vi närmar oss Södra station. Den stora h: We're coming up to Södra station. The huge semicircular building curving around Fatbursparken is known as Bofills båge – Bofill's Arch – after the Spanish architect Ricardo Bofill, and it was completed in 1992. Where the park is today there used to be a lake, Fatburssjön, which was filled in during the 1800s when the railway arrived.
Vi närmar oss ändhållplatsen här i Sofia: We're nearly at the final stop, here in Sofia, the easternmost part of Södermalm. From here you can stroll down towards the water, or take your time wandering back through Vita bergen and SoFo. Thank you for riding with us, and we hope to see you on the next tour!
Vi är i Biskopsgården. Lägg märke till g: We're in Biskopsgården. Look at the street names: Vårväderstorget, Mildvädersgatan, Önskevädersgatan and Friskväderstorget – Spring Weather Square, Mild Weather Street, Perfect Weather Street and Fresh Weather Square. Round here, the streets are named after the weather.
Vi är i Hammarby sjöstad, en stadsdel so: We're in Hammarby sjöstad, a district built from the 1990s onwards on old industrial land. The big functionalist building is the old Luma factory, where light bulbs used to be made.
Vi är i Marieberg på Kungsholmen. Det hö: We're now in Marieberg on Kungsholmen. The tall tower nearby is DN-skrapan, the DN Tower, which the newspaper Dagens Nyheter moved into in the 1960s. Right next to it is Rålambshovsparken, one of the city's favourite parks on a summer's day.
Vi är i Marieberg. Det höga tornet i när: We're in Marieberg. The tall tower nearby is DN-skrapan, the DN skyscraper, which the newspaper Dagens Nyheter moved into in the 1960s. Right beside it is Rålambshovsparken, one of the city's favourite summer parks. Keep your eyes open – in a moment we'll be heading up onto Västerbron, the Western Bridge.

We're now in Marieberg. The tall tower nearby is DN-skrapan, the skyscraper the newspaper Dagens Nyheter moved into in the 1960s, and right next to it is the Rålambshovsparken park. Now keep watching, because in a moment we'll be heading up onto Västerbron, the Western Bridge.
Vi är i SoFo, området söder om Folkungag: We're in SoFo, short for 'south of Folkungagatan'. It's full of little shops, cafés and bars, and at its heart is Nytorget, one of Södermalm's best-loved parks.
Vi är i Vasastaden, med pampiga stenhus: We're in Vasastaden, with its grand stone buildings from the late 1800s. Several University of Gothenburg buildings are here too, and Vasaparken, with the university's main building, is right next door.
Vi är på Kungsportsavenyn, som göteborga: We're on Kungsportsavenyn, known to every Gothenburger simply as Avenyn, 'the Avenue'. It's the city's grand boulevard, running up to Götaplatsen, where Carl Milles' statue of Poseidon has stood since 1931. Along the way you'll pass restaurants, pavement terraces and theatres.
Vi är vid Eriksdal, på Södermalms södra: We're at Eriksdal, on the southern edge of Södermalm. Below us is Årstaviken bay, where rowers and kayakers train for much of the year. This is also where you'll find Eriksdalsbadet, one of Stockholm's biggest swimming centres, with an outdoor pool in summer.

We're at Eriksdal, on the southern edge of Södermalm. Down below is the bay of Årstaviken, where rowers and kayakers train for much of the year. It's also where you'll find Eriksdalsbadet, one of the biggest swimming centres in Stockholm.
Vi är vid Lisebergs norra sida. Nöjespar: We're on the north side of Liseberg. The amusement park opened in 1923 as part of the city's anniversary exhibition, and today it's one of the most visited in the Nordic region. At Christmas it becomes a Christmas market with millions of twinkling lights.
Vi är vid Vita bergen. På toppen står So: We're at Vita bergen, the White Hills. At the top stands Sofia church, consecrated in 1906 and named after Queen Sofia. Around the hill are little red wooden cottages from the 18th and 19th centuries – a glimpse of what Södermalm looked like before the stone city arrived.

We're at Vita bergen, the White Mountains. At the top stands Sofia Church, consecrated in 1906 and named after Queen Sofia. Around the hill are little red wooden houses from the 18th and 19th centuries, a glimpse of what Söder – Södermalm – looked like before the stone city was built. In summer there's theatre in the park.
Via Asperö, där fåren betar på grannön R: Via Asperö, where sheep graze on neighbouring Rivö.
Via Fridhemsplan och Alviksplan till Bro: Via Fridhemsplan and Alviksplan to Brommaplan.
Via Hornstull och Fridhemsplan till Oden: Via Hornstull and Fridhemsplan to Odenplan.
Via Spånga station, vars namn finns i sk: Via Spånga station, whose name appears in writing as early as 1300, and Svandammen, the Swan Pond.
Via Säveån till havet: Down the Säveån to the sea
Via Zinkensdamm till Södra station, nära: Via Zinkensdamm to Södra station, near Medborgarplatsen.
Viblestenarna har troligen stått som bro: The Vible stones probably once stood as bridge stones by a stream. Since then U 92 has been moved several times and has even done service as a gatepost.
Victoria Tower, ett par minuter bort, är: Victoria Tower, a couple of minutes away, has been the tallest hotel in Northern Europe since 2011. At 117.6 metres, it just pips the 117-metre Oslo Plaza. The building is named after Crown Princess Victoria. A little further on, just over the border in Sollentuna, is Helenelund commuter rail station, 10.9 kilometres from Stockholm Central.
Vid 40-årsjubileet 2008 döptes centrumet: For its 40th anniversary in 2008, the shopping centre was renamed SKHLM – The Capital of Shopping, a play on the abbreviation Sthlm. The name never caught on with locals, and most people kept calling it Skärholmen centrum.
Vid Albysjön ligger Fittja moské, som sk: By Albysjön lake stands the Fittja mosque, which made history on 26 April 2013 as the first mosque in Sweden to broadcast the call to prayer. Right next to it is Hagaviken, where the Ekerö ferries cross and the Spendrups brewery has its plant. Arching over it all is Vårbybron, a bridge opened in 1996 and nominated for the Beautiful Roads award.
Vid Albysjön, ett par hundra meter bort,: A couple of hundred metres away, by Albysjön lake, is the Fittja mosque. It made history on 26 April 2013 as the first mosque in Sweden where the call to prayer could be heard. Right beside it lies Fittjaviken, a bay of Lake Mälaren up to 16 metres deep, with the boundary between Huddinge and Botkyrka running right down the middle of the water. Across the bay, the Vårbybron bridge from 1996 carries the motorway; it was shortlisted for the Beautiful Roads award.
Vid Albysjöns strand, ett par hundra met: A couple of hundred metres away, on the shore of Albysjön lake, is Hagalunds tvätterimuseum. When it opened in 1994 it was Sweden's first museum devoted to laundry. It was the idea of Olle Magnusson, an artist from Huddinge, and it's housed in a laundry family's drying barn from 1906. A bridge carries the red metro line over Albysjön, and above the area rises Masmoberget hill, 94 metres above sea level.
Vid Alviksplan låg Bromma-Teatern, en bi: Alviksplan was once home to Bromma-Teatern, a cinema that held its first show on 27 September 1921. The idea was to put on plays as well as films. The cinema closed in 1971, and the building is now a paint shop. Just south of the square is Alviks rättarbostad, the old farm foreman's house – a double cottage from the early 1800s and all that's left of Alvik farm.
Vid Aspnäs fanns en vägkrog säkert från: A roadside inn stood at Aspnäs on the old Enköping road from at least 1792. In 1836 the parish meeting demanded it be closed, and a wholesale merchant complained of the "mischief committed there". The inn seems to have shut around 1843.
Vid Baggensstäket, i sundets östra del,: At Baggensstäket, in the eastern part of the strait, the Russian advance was halted in the summer of 1719 as their forces made their way through Lännerstasundet to burn Stockholm. Today the strait is probably the busiest shipping lane in the archipelago.
Vid Barkarby torg låg gästgiveriet, en v: The coaching inn at Barkarby torg was an important stop for travellers on the road between Stockholm and Enköping. It survives today as Lasse-Maja Wärdshus, next to the preserved old courthouse.
Vid Bovik ligger området Pjonken, som ha: Near Bovik lies Pjonken, an area known for the carpet of blue hepaticas that flowers there every spring.
Vid Brunnbyvägen står en skålgropssten m: On Brunnbyvägen stands a stone covered in more than 250 cup marks – small, round hollows carved in prehistoric times – found during excavations on Årstafältet in 1958 or 1959. Its neighbour is Årsta partihallar, the wholesale market, where Trädgårdshallen, with its distinctive folded roof, was the first building finished, in 1962. Today the hall is Sweden's largest wholesale market for ornamental plants.
Vid Brunnsparken står Gustav II Adolf, k: At Brunnsparken stands Gustav II Adolf, the king who founded Gothenburg in 1621. The city was built by Dutch engineers – hence the canals.
Vid Brunnsvikens nordvästra strand ligge: On the north-west shore of Brunnsviken bay is Bergshamra village, a villa area of historic value and a protected cultural reserve. The house called Övre Karlsro, from around 1865, was home to the furniture designer Carl Malmsten and his family, which is why it's also known as Carl Malmsten's House. Bergshamra gård itself was called Bergshammar until 1865, and its main building was demolished in 1929.
Vid Danderyds kyrka, en bit bort, står r: At Danderyd Church, a little way off, stands runestone U 127, one of the Jarlabanke stones from his famous runestone causeway in Täby kyrkby.
