The grand villa has a large south-facing veranda of the kind made for sipping Swedish punsch. The wooden cladding was originally painted red but is now yellow.
Villa Wållgren byggdes åt ingenjören Ern: Villa Wållgren was built for the engineer Ernst Wållgren. After his death in 1926, the opera singer and actor Emile Stiebel moved in and stayed until 1941. The architect, Ivar Callmander, lived just a few houses away.
Villa av vrakvirke: A villa built from a wreck
Villan Hildedal har putsad fasad och bru: Villa Hildedal has a rendered façade and a tiled mansard roof in a manor-house style. Since 1987 it has been part of the city's conservation programme.
Villan blev en träffpunkt för utländska: The villa became a meeting place for foreign architects. Alvar Aalto stayed here, and in 1933 Markelius brought his great role model Le Corbusier. The newspaper DN was less impressed, complaining in 1931 that the house had 'too much objectivity and too little romance'.
Villan byggd av saltpråmar: A villa built from salt barges
Villan byggdes 1912 åt sillhandlaren Bör: The villa was built in 1912 for the herring merchant Börjesson, and its timber is said to have been salvaged from the wrecked ship Svolder. In 1927 it was bought by Ernst Bremer, the smuggling king, whose fleet numbered up to 16 vessels at its peak.
Villan byggdes strax söder om Elektraver: The villa was built just south of the Elektraverken factory, designed by Ivar Tengbom in 1917. The plot, over 40,000 square metres, also became home to Olle Engkvist's offices, workshops and machinery.
Villan fick en oplanerad akustisk effekt: The villa had an unplanned acoustic quirk. The Myrdals' son Jan has described how, at a certain wall downstairs, he could hear every whisper from his parents' study, as if they were standing right behind his ear.
Villan har fått namn efter Jean François: The villa is named after Jean François Beylon, reader, friend and adviser to Gustav III and Louisa Ulrika. Princess Christina lived here with her family from 1974 to 2006.
Villan har fått sitt namn efter de orang: The villa takes its name from the orange wooden balls that decorate the upper veranda. They may be meant to look like lit ornamental lanterns, but most people think they look like oranges.
Villan med det lustiga tornet: The villa with the quirky tower
Villan namngavs av Törners hustru Josefi: Törner's wife Josefina named the villa after herself. When Törner began making fireworks in his laboratory next door in 1893, the villa became the family's permanent home. The workshop and three gunpowder sheds still stand by Stockbysjön lake.
Villan på ekbacken: The villa on the oak hill
Villan på Åhmanssonska gården byggdes i: The villa at Åhmanssonska gården was built in yellow brick for the merchant Carl Albin Borgström, with both a shop and a home. It was one of the grander buildings in Majorna, with a garden stretching all the way to today's Djurgårdsskolan. In the 1870s it was bought by the master ropemaker Charles Åhmansson.
Villan ritades av Johan August Westerber: The villa was designed by Johan August Westerberg. Gustaf Werner, who owned the estate until his death in 1948, added a large greenhouse and housing for the workers, and rebuilt the stables and the cowshed.
Villan ritades av arkitektbyrån Kellgren: The villa was designed by the architects Kellgren & Hammarling in a traditional style with a mansard roof. It had seven rooms, a kitchen, a hall and a bathroom for the children's home, plus a caretaker's flat with two rooms and a kitchen.
Villan som blev regemente: The villa that became a regiment
Villan som fick byggarens namn: Named by its builder after himself
Villan som omringades av cisterner: The villa surrounded by oil tanks
Villan står på Blockhusuddens högsta höj: The villa stands on the highest point of Blockhusudden, Eolskulle, named after Aeolus, god of the winds. Boberg drew inspiration from the Orient and the Vienna Secession building, with white facades, green and yellow tiles and gilded globes on the corners.
Villan var byggd för att bo i året runt,: The villa was built for year-round living, but Jacob and Sophie Setterwall only stayed here in summer. They spent their winters in a flat at Sturegatan 18 in Stockholm. After Sophie's death in 1923 the villa was sold for 135,000 kronor.
Villan var ett montagebygge med prefabri: The villa was assembled from prefabricated timber panels, a method Markelius called the ‘system house’. It became a symbol of Swedish post-war architecture, and the Architectural Review dubbed the style ‘The New Empiricism’.
Villan var från början en liten enplanss: The villa started out as a small single-storey cottage. A rebuild in 1908–1909 made it more than three times larger, in an Art Nouveau-inspired manor style with patterned timber cladding, large bay windows and a hipped mansard roof. The municipality rates it as "irreplaceable".
Villan är en borglik byggnad med tinnar: The villa is a castle-like neo-baroque building with battlements and towers, warm ochre facades and pale grey stone detailing. The grounds cover 27,550 square metres. Mittag-Leffler was one of the first to buy a plot when the villa town was founded in 1889.
Villans murar av gulrött holländskt tege: The villa's walls of yellowish-red Dutch brick rest on a high sandstone plinth, with details in grey and yellow. The house has a tower, a lantern, bay windows and a veranda with a balcony. Inside are oak panelling, silk wallpaper in the drawing room and fireplaces of Italian marble.
Villans vardagsrum var 11 gånger 11 mete: The villa's living room measured 11 by 11 metres with a 4.5-metre ceiling. To the south a sloping wall of glass ran from floor to ceiling, and inside it lay a winter garden with a pool and exotic plants.
Villaområdet Edsviken i Helenelund har f: The villa area of Edsviken in Helenelund is named after Edsviken, the inlet of the Baltic that borders it to the north-east. Not far away, by Kummelby church, stands the Kummelby stone, a runestone from the late 11th century. The church stands where the old Kummelby farm used to be.
Villaområdet Flysta gömmer en försvunnen: Somewhere in the residential area of Flysta lies a lost Viking Age runestone, known to experts as Uppland Runic Inscription 70. People have searched for it several times without success, and it's probably gone for good. In the neighbouring district of Beckomberga, the Round Houses, Runda husen, were built in 1953–54 on the corner of Bällstavägen and Spångavägen, mainly as staff housing for the nurses at Beckomberga Hospital.
Villaområdet Nysätra ligger på en udde m: Nysätra is a neighbourhood of villas on a headland between three lakes: Kyrkviken, Järlasjön and Sicklasjön. Out at the very tip, on Nackanäs, stood Nackanäs värdshus, a country inn that welcomed guests from 1859 until it burned down in 1960. Its predecessor, Nacka värdshus, stood on the far side of the water for a full 300 years. A little way off is Setterwallska villan, a grand villa built in 1896 by a successful shipowner.
Villaområdet Råstahem kallades ursprungl: The villa area of Råstahem was originally named Ulriksdals järnvägshem, the Ulriksdal railway homes, by SJ, the Swedish State Railways – and plots were sold only to people who worked for the railways. Most of the houses went up between the late 1920s and the mid-1930s. The railway is still close at hand: Hagalund yard is the largest marshalling yard for passenger trains in Sweden.
Villaområdet Sjövalla i östra Mölndal bö: The Sjövalla villa area in eastern Mölndal began to take shape as early as the 1920s and 30s. A little further on is Kristinedal, completed in 1964, beside Lake Stensjön and close to Gunnebo House and Lake Rådasjön. Its houses were designed by an architect at Småhusbyrån, a small-house design office in Malmö, and built by Skånska Cementgjuteriet in the ideal style of the day: brick façades and long, low floor plans.
Villaområdet Skälby i södra Järfälla har: Skälby, a villa area in southern Järfälla, takes its name from nearby Skälby gård, a former noble estate. The Barkarby-Skälby district has neighbourhoods with almost space-age names, such as Neptuni, Orgona and Aniara in Skälby. Here you'll also find Kyrkbyn, with the old Gästgivargården coaching inn, which in recent years has been known as Wärdshuset Lasse-Maja.
Villaområdet heter Edsviken efter viken: This residential area is called Edsviken, after the inlet of the Baltic it borders. Edsviken itself is about 7.7 kilometres long but narrow, about 20 metres at its deepest, and reaches all the way from Stocksund to Edsberg. Along its shores stand several grand buildings: Ulriksdal Palace, Edsberg Palace, Rådan and Bergendal Manor.
Villasamhälle tack vare tåget: A villa suburb thanks to the train
Villasamhället Storängen grundades 1904: The villa community of Storängen was founded in 1904 by a home-ownership association for office workers, and that same year Villa Lodén, the very first villa, was built for one of the founders. Artists such as Richard Bergh and the couple Georg and Hanna Pauli lived here. Villa Jacobsen housed Nacka's council offices from 1916 to 1961, and when Villa Bellander burned in 1918, Ragnar Östberg gave it a completely new look.
Villastad längs Roslagsbanan: A garden suburb along the Roslagsbanan
Villastad vid Saltsjöbanan: A garden suburb on the Saltsjöbanan line
Villastaden började 1901 när Birger Sven: The garden suburb began in 1901 when Birger Svenonius bought land and divided it into some 200 plots, though only about 25 were built on in the first few years. Many of the villas were given pyramid roofs, which still define the area. In Tingsbyn the plots were larger and the villas grander than in Kyrkbyn.

The villa suburb began in 1901, when Birger Svenonius divided off around 200 plots – but only about 25 were built on in the first few years. Many villas were given pyramid roofs, which still define the area today.
Villastaden började 1906 när direktör Er: The villa suburb began in 1906, when the company director Ernst Kihlberg divided up the land of Enebyberg farm along the Roslagsbanan railway. In 1921 there were only around 80 villas, but the 1923 town plan covered some 550 plots, and by the 1940s every one had been built on.
Villastaden började anläggas 1901 när un: Work on the garden suburb began in 1901, when around 200 plots were divided up, though only about 25 were built on in the first few years. Many of the villas share a uniform style with pyramid roofs that still defines the area. Marked heritage trails lead past the old houses.
Villastaden låg mellan sjöarna Drevviken: The garden suburb lay between the lakes Drevviken and Magelungen, and the developer sold both lakeside plots and plots with good garden soil. The residents' association looked after the bathing spot on Magelungen – today's Farsta strandbad beach.
Villastaden som aldrig blev: The garden suburb that never was
Villastaden som inte blev av: The garden suburb that never happened
Villastaden startade 1906, när direktör: The garden suburb began in 1906, when the businessman Ernst Kihlberg started dividing up the farm's land near the Roslagsbanan railway. By 1921 there were only around 80 villas, but the town plan of 1923 covered some 550 plots.
Villastaden vid Nynäsbanan: The garden suburb by the Nynäs line
Villastaden växte snabbt och 1930 fanns: The garden suburb grew fast: by 1930 there were around 250 villas and 1,000 residents, with a dedicated bus to Jarlaplan. Nora torg gained shops, a post office, a bank and a fire station and became the hub of all Danderyd – until shopping moved to Mörby Centrum in the 1960s.
Villastadens allra första byggnad är Ske: The very first building in the garden suburb is Skeppargården, from 1906, at Stockholmsvägen 61. It was built for the suburb's manager, Erik Andersson, known as "the skipper".
Villastadens hjärta växte fram kring Res: The heart of this garden suburb grew up around Restauranten, a restaurant and function hall that was the centre of Djursholm's social life for 66 years, from 1890 to 1956. Its founder, Wilhelm Strandberg, was only 25 and had learned his trade at the famous Berns salonger in Stockholm. Not far away is Prinsvillan, the Prince's Villa, rebuilt in 1908–09 for Prince Erik, Duke of Västmanland – who probably never moved in.
Villaägarna räddade källan: The villa owners saved the spring
Villorna här hör till Enebyberg, ett sam: The villas here are part of Enebyberg, a community mostly built in the first half of the 20th century. A little further on is Enebyberg station on the Roslagsbanan line, with a waiting room on the eastern platform. It's a quiet stop – on an ordinary winter weekday, around 200 people are estimated to get on here.
Villorna här står på marker som förr hör: The villas here stand on land that once belonged to Nora gård, a farm that began to be divided into villa plots in 1926. A little further away is the lake Nora träsk and Norahällen, a rock carving cut into a smooth slab of rock. In 1927 it was fenced off with iron railings. By 1973 they had been removed, and that same year the carving was given a sign and its lines were painted in.
Villorna längs Skårsgatan byggdes 1938–1: The villas along Skårsgatan were built in 1938–1945 to a town plan by Uno Åhrén, and most were designed by Börje Eliasson. They have two storeys, pale rendered façades and almost flat roofs.
Villorna runt omkring hör till Enebyberg: The villas all around belong to Enebyberg, a villa community in Danderyd with about 5,000 residents and many houses from the first half of the 20th century. A little further on, on Eneby torg square, is Eneby church, which is shared by two congregations: the Church of Sweden's Danderyd parish and the Uniting Church in Sweden's Eneby congregation.
Vilohem i över hundra år: A convalescent home for over a century
Vin & Sprits bergrum bestod av fem tunnl: Vin & Sprit's rock caverns consisted of five tunnels, each 150 metres long and 20 metres high. Tankers brought wine here from the Mediterranean, and wine and spirits were bottled here from 1959 to 1997.
Vindarnas tempel: Vindarnas tempel, the Temple of the Winds
Vingarna fick till slut rymd: The wings finally got their space
Vinnaren hette Öarna: The winning entry was called 'The Islands'
Vinnarförslaget hette Well: The winning design was called Well
Vinsta har tre delar: radhus och villor: Vinsta has three parts: terraced houses and villas to the north, the business park to the south-east and the hill of Johannelundstoppen to the south-west. The business park used to be called Johannelund industrial estate and sits next to Johannelund metro station.
Vintern 1984 stod ett helt hus tomt på T: In the winter of 1984 an entire building on Teleskopgatan stood empty. Gothenburg's TV studios used it to film Carin Mannheimer's television series Tryggare kan ingen vara ...
Vintern 1984 stod ett helt hus tomt. Göt: In the winter of 1984 an entire building stood empty, and Gothenburg's TV studio seized the chance to film Carin Mannheimer's series Tryggare kan ingen vara … there.
Vintern 2009 var så kall att dammen näst: The winter of 2009 was so cold that the pond almost froze solid and nearly all the fish died. Only the crucian carp came through unscathed. Since then roach and carp have started to recover, and a newcomer, the tench, has turned up.
Vintern 2009 var så kall att sjön nästan: The winter of 2009 was so cold that the lake almost froze to the bottom and nearly all the fish died. Only the crucian carp came through unscathed. Since then roach and carp have started to return, and a newcomer has appeared: the tench.
Vintern då dammen nästan frös: The winter the pond nearly froze solid
Vintertid sågades is ur Hålsjön och såld: In winter, ice was sawn out of Hålsjön lake and sold. This grew into an ice factory that kept going right up until 1979, and it gave its name to both the bus stop and the Isfabriken area.
Visste du att Coca-Cola-flaskan har rött: Did you know the Coca-Cola bottle has its roots in Surte? Its designer, Alexander Samuelson, came from Surte glassworks. Right beside us, in the works' old premises, is Glasbruksmuseet, the Glassworks Museum. The building went up in 1852 as a mill and became a glassworks ten years later. It's the oldest building in Surte and has also served as a power station, a telephone exchange and a laundry.
Visste du att Göteborg först grundades h: Did you know that Gothenburg was first founded here on Hisingen? In Färjestaden, known locally as Färjenäs, King Karl IX founded a town in the early 1600s with the help of the Dutch. It quickly grew to around a hundred houses, several churches and a town hall – but in 1611 the Danes burned it to the ground. Today the lost town is known as Karl IX's Gothenburg.
Visste du att Hisingen till största dele: Did you know that most of Hisingen actually belongs to the province of Bohuslän? About three quarters of the island does, taking in the parishes of Torslanda, Björlanda, Säve, Backa and Rödbo. The remaining quarter, with Lundby and Tuve, belongs to Västergötland. So here on Hisingen you can switch provinces without ever leaving the island.
Visste du att Nordöstra Göteborg är den: Did you know that Nordöstra Göteborg, north-east Gothenburg, is the largest urban area in Sweden that isn't the main town of its municipality? It's also the third most densely populated, after Fisksätra and Norra Riksten in Greater Stockholm. This urban area only came into being in 2015, when Statistics Sweden started interpreting the definition of an urban area in a new way. A little further on is Hjällbo Centre with its food hall.
Visste du att Sveriges äldsta ännu aktiv: Did you know that Sweden's oldest field hockey club still in action is based round here? Partille Sport Club was founded in 1975 and has won a whole string of Swedish championships in both field hockey and indoor hockey. In 2019 the men's team even won the European club cup. A little way off is Stora Kåsjön, Partille's largest lake and the source of the municipality's drinking water.
Visätra, som det stavades förr, var ett: Visätra, as it was once spelt, was a croft belonging to Flemingsberg farm, at the far end of a valley that was once an arm of Lake Orlången. It's mentioned as early as 1653. After 1836 it became a poorhouse, and it was demolished when Visättra Ängar was built.
Visättra hette tidigare Östra Flemingsbe: Visättra, which used to be called Östra Flemingsberg, is a residential area in Huddinge, with the Visättra sports centre a little further off. Flemingsberg station is something of a railway junction, with lines heading off in three directions. Commuter trains run towards Södertälje centrum, long-distance and regional trains towards Södertälje syd, and both long-distance and commuter trains towards Huddinge.
Visättra sportcenter räknas som ett av d: Visättra sports centre is one of the largest in Greater Stockholm. It has an artificially frozen ice hockey rink, a bandy pitch, tennis, mini golf and disc golf, and two dog clubs are based here as well.
Vit fabrik med fönsterband: A white factory with ribbon windows
Vita bergen och Sofia kyrka: Vita bergen, the White Mountains, and Sofia Church
Vita skolan med friluftsklassrum: The White School with an open-air classroom
Vita skolan på kullen: The White School on the hill
Vita stenen vid busshållplatsen: The white stone by the bus stop
Vitabergsklubben hade som mest drygt 100: At its peak the Vitaberg Club had just over 100 members, among them Stig Claesson (Slas) and Svante Foerster. The club put on plays and held reading evenings and discussion nights. Its members' magazine, Utropstecknet (The Exclamation Mark), ran to 29 issues between 1946 and 1951, and some members are said to have been models for characters in Per Anders Fogelström's novels.
Vitsands fyra slanka skivhus från 1962–1: Vitsand's four slender slab blocks from 1962–1966 used to be painted grey. Now each has its own colour: red, green, yellow and blue, from south to north.
Vivstavarvsvägens radhus har spritputsad: The terraced houses on Vivstavarvsvägen have roughcast facades in strong, lively colours that are still in their original state. Every house was given an open fireplace, and the chimneys give the area its character.
Volvo Duett på gatan: A Volvo Duett in the street
Volvohallen har kupolform men en kvadrat: Volvohallen is dome-shaped but square in plan. It was built next to what was then Volvo Cars’ head office.
Volvohallen är en kupolformad utställnin: Volvohallen is a domed exhibition hall built on a square plan, which Volvo Cars put up in 1975 next to what was then its head office. A little way off is Torslandaverken, Volvo Cars' plant, which was the largest single-storey factory in the Nordic countries when it opened. Building work started in Sörred in 1960–61.
Volvos grundare i första kullen: Volvo's founder in the first year
Volvos vd Assar Gabrielsson oroade sig f: Volvo's managing director Assar Gabrielsson worried that the farmers would raise their prices if they knew Volvo was the buyer. He confided in the county governor, then had a firm of agents buy up the farms without revealing who was behind it.

Volvo's chief executive Assar Gabrielsson feared the farmers would raise their prices if they knew Volvo was buying. So the land in Sörredsdalen was bought through an estate agency that kept the buyer's name secret. In all, the land cost 8.25 million kronor.
Vridande moment är 35 meter hög och väge: Vridande moment (Turning Moment) is 35 metres tall and weighs 40 tonnes. It's made of Corten steel, which weathers to an even rust-red, and stands like an exclamation mark on the multi-storey car park.
Vråkärr och Höga är två grannbyar i Tors: Vråkärr and Höga are two neighbouring villages in Torsby parish, Kungälv municipality. Not far off is Glose, by the shallows of the Ryskärsfjorden inlet, with grazed shore meadows full of plants and birds. They've even caught the attention of Swedish Radio, which broadcast its nature programme Naturmorgon live from there.
Väderkvarn på sin gamla plats: A windmill on its original spot
Vädertemat fortsätter längs spårvägen. L: The weather theme carries on along the tramline, as lines 5 and 6 roll on from Väderilsgatan (Squall Street) towards Varmfrontsgatan (Warm Front Street).
Vägarna runt omkring heter sådant som St: The surrounding roads have names like Stormästarvägen (Grand Master Road), Banérförarvägen (Standard-Bearer Road) and Korsfararvägen (Crusader Road). When the foundation turned 50 in 1961, King Gustav VI Adolf came to visit and signed his name on a rock slab in front of the G building.
Vägarna var så dåliga att villaägarna i: The roads were so bad that in 1911 the homeowners of Långsjö decided to lay a wooden boardwalk along Långsjövägen to Älvsjö station. When two people met, whoever was heading home had to step aside, so that the one going into town arrived with clean shoes.
Vägen anlades på initiativ av Pehr Pette: The road was built on the initiative of Pehr Pettersson, known as Patron Pehr, who became owner of Fullersta farm in 1848. He had made a fortune from brännvin, Swedish schnapps. He gave land to the State Railways on condition that they built a station outside his farm – today's Huddinge station.
Vägen från Gloseby ner till fjorden sköt: The road from Gloseby down to the fjord is maintained by a local residents' association that has worked to boost the wild flowers along its verges. In 2025 the Swedish Society for Nature Conservation featured it in its campaign 'The World's Longest Flower Meadow'.
Vägen från Gloseby till fjorden sköts av: The road from Gloseby to the fjord is looked after by a local road association, which has made a special effort to encourage wild flowers along the verges. In 2025 this earned a mention from the Swedish Society for Nature Conservation in its campaign "The World's Longest Flower Meadow".
Vägen följer vikingatidens sjöväg mellan: The road follows the Viking Age waterway between Edsviken and Norrviken towards Sigtuna. You'll find a health centre, a pizzeria, a couple of tobacconists and a pâtisserie for anyone in need of a fika, the Swedish coffee break, with a restaurant close by too. Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 7 mot Komet: Welcome aboard tram 7 towards Komettorget! The journey takes about 66 minutes. Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 7 mot Opalt: Welcome aboard tram 7 towards Opaltorget! The journey takes about 66 minutes. Rymdtorget, Kometgatan, Kosmosgatan, Universumsgatan and Meteorgatan – Space Square, Comet Street, Cosmos Street, Universe Street and Meteor Street. Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 7 mot T-Cen: Welcome aboard tram 7 towards T-Centralen! The journey takes about 13 minutes. Waldemarsudde was the home of the artist Prince Eugen, son of King Oscar II and one of the leading landscape painters of his day. Today his waterside villa and garden are an art museum.
Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 7 mot Walde: Welcome aboard tram 7 towards Waldemarsudde! The journey takes about 12 minutes. Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 8 mot Anger: Welcome aboard tram 8 towards Angered Centrum! The journey takes about 64 minutes. Frölunda Torg opened in 1966 as one of Sweden's first big suburban shopping centres. All around it is Västra Frölunda, and a few kilometres to the west the sea and the archipelago begin.
Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 8 mot Frölu: Welcome aboard tram 8 towards Frölunda Torg! The journey takes about 63 minutes. Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 9 mot Anger: Welcome aboard tram 9 towards Angered Centrum! The journey takes about 57 minutes. Kungssten sits close to the mouth of the Göta älv river. Välkommen ombord på spårvagn 9 mot Kungs: Welcome aboard tram 9 towards Kungssten! The journey takes about 56 minutes. Välkommen ombord! Du kliver på vid Drott: Welcome aboard! You're boarding at Drottningtorget, right in front of the Central Station, on a tram that belongs to the largest tram network in the Nordic countries. Gothenburg got horse-drawn trams in 1879 and electric ones in 1902, and while many other Swedish cities got rid of their trams, Gothenburg held on to its own. The Central Station opened in 1858 and is one of the oldest station buildings in Sweden still in use. So sit back and relax – we're heading along the river, through the old working-class neighbourhoods and out to the sea.
Välkommen till Majorna. Titta på husen:: Welcome to Majorna. Take a look at the houses: a stone ground floor with two wooden storeys on top. That's a landshövdingehus, a type of building found almost nowhere but Gothenburg. It was a clever way round an old rule that wooden houses could be no more than two storeys high – the stone floor simply didn't count.
Välkommen till Mölndal. Längs forsen i M: Welcome to Mölndal. Along the rapids in Kvarnbyn, Mölndal's old mill village, water power has driven mills and factories for several hundred years. Today Kvarnbyn is a heritage area with a museum and cafés.
Vällingby Centrum blev en internationell: When Vällingby Centrum was completed in 1954, it became an international model for the modern town centre. The metro depot next door was originally called Spångahallen – a slightly odd name that dates from the time when Vällingby belonged to Spånga municipality, before it merged with the City of Stockholm. Right next door, too, is Jan-Pers stuga, Jan-Per's cottage.
Vällingby brandstation på Krossgatan rit: Vällingby fire station on Krossgatan was designed by the architect Mårten J. Larsson. The firefighters started work there in December 1964, but the official opening didn't come until 22 January 1965.
Vällingby byggdes som en ABC-stad med ar: Vällingby was built as an 'ABC town', combining workplaces (arbete), homes (bostad) and a town centre (centrum). When the centre opened in 1954, the thinking was that residents would have practically no need to travel into central Stockholm. It was designed for 26,000 people – and within ten years the population had doubled.
Vällingby planerades som ABC-staden, med: Vällingby was planned as an 'ABC town' – A for work, B for housing and C for a town centre, all in one place – and it even had its own cinema. Fontänen opened in 1956, named after the fountains on the square. That same year, the Trappan community centre opened, built in terraces stepping down between an upper and a lower square. Both were designed by the architects Backström & Reinius.
Vällsjön ligger några hundra meter bort,: A few hundred metres away is Lake Vällsjön, a small lake only four and a half metres deep. It marks Pixbo's south-eastern edge, and the Vällbäcken stream links it with Lake Rådasjön. Pixbo itself is built on and around the height of Björnåsen – so expect hills.
Väntan sitter på en sockel av granit och: Väntan (Waiting), roughly life-size, sits on a granite plinth. The sculpture was placed here by Charles Felix Lindberg's donation fund.
Värden som öppnade kaffehus: The innkeeper who opened a coffee house
Värdshus i överläkarens hus: An inn in the chief physician's house
Värdshuset byggdes i furu- och grantimme: The old inn was built of pine and spruce logs, clad in red-painted boards and fitted with wooden gutters. Inside, the rooms had paper wallpaper and five kakelugnar, the tall tiled stoves typical of Swedish homes. Today four families live here.
Värdshuset låg där vägen mot Roslagen ko: The inn stood where the road to Roslagen crossed the stream. In the early 1800s it was leased by Benjamin Grafström, who was also the cellar master at Hagalund inn. It was pulled down when the Roslagsbanan railway was built in the 1880s.
Värdshuset med sjöpaviljong: The inn with a lakeside pavilion
Värdshuset Övre Haga fick två uthuslängo: The Övre Haga inn had two rows of outbuildings. The innkeeper lived in the western one, while the eastern one held a henhouse, a cowshed, a carriage shed and stabling for 22 horses. The western row burned down in 1956, and only the foundations remain.
Värdshuset är byggt i rödmålat liggtimme: The inn is a two-storey building of red-painted horizontal logs. Its walls were hung with painted paper wallpaper pasted directly onto the timber. In the 1980s the house was restored to its original appearance.
Världens dans på liten scen: World dance on a tiny stage
Världens första konstfrusna skrinnarbana: The world’s first artificial-ice speed skating track
Världens första kurdiska bibliotek finns: The world's first Kurdish library is just a stone's throw from here. Kurdiska biblioteket opened in 1997 and spent its first ten years on Skeppsholmen, then, after a brief stop in Duvbo, moved into the Alvik community centre in 2011. Its shelves hold around 13,000 books in almost 30 languages, most of them in Kurdish. Next door is St Ansgar's Church.
Världens största tankers lägger till: Where the world's biggest tankers dock
Världscuphoppning varje år: World Cup show jumping every year
Världskulturmuseet: Världskulturmuseet, the Museum of World Culture
Världslitteraturhuset: Världslitteraturhuset, the House of World Literature
Världspremiär för röntgenbehandling: A world first in X-ray treatment

Värme, kyla och el ur avlopp: Heat, cooling and power from sewage
Värmeverket har en tydlig industrikarakt: The heating plant has a strongly industrial look, with façades of corrugated sheet metal in bold colours meant to break up the large volumes. Its tall concrete chimney, painted yellow and blue, has become a familiar landmark in Akalla.
Värtahamnen anlades 1879 till 1886 som h: Värtahamnen harbour was built between 1879 and 1886 for coal and other bulk goods. Today it's where ferries leave for Finland, Åland, Estonia and Latvia. The old Kommunalhuset building was home to Värtan fire station from 1905 to 1934. A little further on, outside the entrance to the Värtaverket power plant, stands Kungseken, the King's Oak, around 600 years old. It was probably named after Oscar II, who used to make springtime outings to the tree.
Värtans stationshus i rött tegel påminne: Värtan's red-brick station building, with its tall turret-like roofs, looks rather like a small French wine château. "Värtan station is like a château on the Loire," the columnist Jolo wrote in Dagens Nyheter in 1968. It was designed by Adolf Wilhelm Edelsvärd.
Väsjön intill skidbacken är bara 2,35 me: Lake Väsjön, next to the ski slope, is only 2.35 metres deep. Test fishing has turned up perch, pike, roach, rudd and tench. There are two swimming spots, and the water eventually drains into Lake Mälaren.
Västan hade 400 platser i en salong helt: The Västan cinema had 400 seats in an auditorium entirely below ground, behind the row of buildings. The walls were dark red brick, the curtain yellow and the seats blue, with a copper-clad canopy over the entrance. The last film was shown on 2 May 1971.
Västberga begravningsplats, mellan Solbe: Västberga cemetery, between Solberga, Västberga and Liseberg, carries the City Museum's blue rating for exceptionally high cultural and historical value. Its neighbour, Liseberg, is at 38 hectares the smallest district in all of Söderort, Stockholm's southern suburbs. A little further on is Årsta partihallar, a wholesale market where around 200 companies trade in fruit, vegetables, fish and flowers.
Västberga gård, med anor från 1300-talet: Västberga gård goes back to the 14th century, became a noble estate in the 17th century and has given its name to the whole district. The City of Stockholm has owned the manor since 1935. Not far from here runs Älvsjöbågen, the Älvsjö Arch, a 1,396-metre railway bridge that's part of the Citybanan rail link. It's Sweden's fourth-longest railway bridge and was built using a technique rarely seen in Sweden.
Västberga nämns första gången 1330, när: Västberga is first mentioned in 1330, when the nuns of St Clare's Convent sold land to Elof Håkansson, the bailiff of Stockholm. By 1535 the village had three homesteads.
Väster om Kristinedal står Tornvillan, b: West of Kristinedal stands Tornvillan, the Tower Villa, built in 1898 by the estate's owner as a home for the manager of the brickworks. The estate itself was sold in 1960 and demolished when the housing area was built.
Väster om badplatsen Jungfruviken ligger: West of the Jungfruviken bathing spot, the Tryggeberg labyrinth – 7.5 metres across – lies on a slab of bare rock. It once had 12 rings, of which six stone circuits survive. The spot is called Stora Möet, meaning 'the Great Meeting'.
Väster om hamnen reser sig det cirka 35: West of the harbour rises Sörhallsberget, about 35 metres high. It's named after the 18th-century Sörhallen estate, with its herring warehouses, salting houses, train-oil boilery and loading jetties. A huge fire reduced it all to ashes on 15 June 1897.
Väster om slottet anlades en barockträdg: West of the palace, a baroque garden was laid out with hedges, ponds and avenues. It stretched all the way down to what was then Kyrksjön lake – roughly where the Stockholmsmässan exhibition centre stands today.
Väster om slussen har kanalens norra sid: West of the lock, the canal’s north bank has a reed-fringed waterside walk with wooden decking and plenty of seating, while the south bank has a crisp urban quay with most of the canal’s 124 moorings. East of the lock there are natural shores.
Västerortskyrkan i Vällingby centrum rit: Västerortskyrkan in Vällingby centre was designed by Carl Nyrén and Bertil Engstrand and built in 1956. From the outside it looks closed and plain, with rendered walls, but step inside and you're in the world of New Brutalism: dramatically leaning walls of raw concrete, with light filtering down from the roof. The church is also built together with an eleven-storey block of flats.
Västertorps tunnelbanestation är den näs: Västertorp is the second-highest station on the whole metro network, at 42.8 metres above sea level. The district is also home to Stockholm's largest sculpture park, with 21 outdoor works. And on Västertorpsplan was the neighbourhood cinema Västan, which showed films from 1954 to 1971.
Västertorpshallen med idrottshall och ba: Västertorpshallen, with its sports hall and swimming pool, was built next to the school in 1966–1967 and designed by the same architect, Curt Laudon. In 2007 the school premises were turned into flats to designs by WAK Architects.
Västorgeln från 1861 har flera ovanligt: The west organ, from 1861, has several unusually well-preserved stops. Since 1992 the north gallery has also had an organ in the North German baroque style, built by John Brombaugh in the USA.
Västra Balltorp ligger alldeles intill e: Västra Balltorp sits right next to a golf course – and the golf club even had a hand in developing the area. Its neighbour, Östra Balltorp, has had trouble making up its mind: sometimes it's counted as a town of its own, sometimes as part of Gothenburg, depending on the year Statistics Sweden did its count.
Västra Hisingen hörde till Norge ända ti: Western Hisingen belonged to Norway right up until the Treaty of Roskilde in 1658, while the eastern part, including Tuve, became Swedish back in the 13th century. And in 1927 the very first Volvo car rolled out of the factory on the island.
Västra Hisingen är industrins och hamnar: Western Hisingen is the land of heavy industry and docks. Not far from here is the Preemraff oil refinery, which gets most of its crude oil from the North Sea. In neighbouring Arendal, the Arendal shipyard was in business from 1963 to 1989; today the site is home to Volvo Buses' headquarters, among others. Arendal is so thoroughly industrial that in 2012 only 90 people actually lived there.
Västra Hisings härad, med bland annat To: The western district of Hisingen, including Torslanda and Säve, belonged to Norway right up to the Treaty of Roskilde in 1658. The eastern part, with Lundby and Tuve, had already become Swedish in the 13th century.
Västra dammen anlades för fåglarna och s: The western pond was made for the birds and was meant to be free of fish, as little grebes are easily disturbed by them. Even so, crucian carp and common carp swim here – though they're hard to get at, thanks to the dense vegetation and soggy moss around the pond.
Västra dammen är tänkt att vara fisktom,: The western pond is meant to be free of fish, as little grebes are easily disturbed by them. Crucian carp and carp live there all the same. With its dense vegetation and damp moss, the pond is a tricky place to fish.
Västra gatan och Östra gatan har till st: Västra gatan and Östra gatan have kept much of their old small-town character. Several houses on Västra gatan are listed buildings, among them the Thorild, Strand and Zetterlöf houses.
Vättersparken är ungefär 350 gånger 60 m: Vättersparken measures roughly 350 by 60 metres and lies about 50 metres above sea level. At its southern end is a football pitch.
Väveriet Krokslätts fabriker anlades på: The Krokslätt weaving mills were founded in the 1870s. By 1915 the spinning mill was the largest in Sweden, with around 1,000 workers. After merging with Mölnlycke, the company was Sweden's biggest textile firm in 1949, employing 4,600 people. Production closed down in 1973–1974.
Vågmästaren och brukspatronen Johan Oliv: Johan Oliveholm, weighmaster and ironworks owner, bought the estate in 1759 and turned it into a well-run property. In 1774 he also bought part of Skälltorps Östergård, where the private Friedländer cemetery was later laid out.
Vålberga har fått namn efter en gård som: Vålberga is named after a farm mentioned as early as the 15th century. Its 19th-century main house stood roughly where the playground is today and was demolished around 1965–66.
Vålberga är uppkallat efter en gård vars: Vålberga is named after a farm mentioned as far back as the 1400s. The main house stood roughly where the playground is today and was demolished around 1965–66.
Vålberga, en bit härifrån, är ett bostad: Vålberga, not far from here, is a housing area built around 1963, made up mostly of rows of terraced houses. It's in Barkarby-Skälby, Järfälla's southernmost district. Nearby is the manor of Skälby gård, surrounded by four ancient burial grounds. And the old parish of Barkarby was merged into a newly formed Järfälla parish in 2010.
Vårberg centrum invigdes i september 196: Vårberg centre opened in September 1968, just under a year after the metro station in the same complex, and it has been praised for its international modernist architecture. The City Museum calls it an early and well-preserved example of an indoor square. Nearby is the Kummelholmen art gallery, whose name simply comes from the building's land registry designation.
Vårberg sträcker sig hela vägen ner till: Vårberg stretches all the way down to Lake Mälaren in the north-west, and 65 hectares of the district are actually water. The homes in the Bergholmen block on Rönnholmsgränd date from the late 1960s and have a green listing from the City Museum. So does Vårbergsskolan, built between 1968 and 1972 as a lower secondary school, which today houses an adult education college and an independent school.

Vårberg stretches all the way down to Lake Mälaren in the north-west, and 65 hectares of the district is water. The flats in the Bergholmen block on Rönnholmsgränd were built in the late 1960s and have been given the City Museum's green listing for buildings of special value. So has Vårberg School, built between 1968 and 1972 as a secondary school; since 2005 it has housed adult education, and since 2020 part of Slättgård School too.
Vårbergs sjukhem ritades av Ervin Pütsep: Vårberg nursing home was designed by Ervin Pütsep, one of Sweden's leading hospital architects, and opened in 1969 with 300 beds. The low wing had a swimming pool and atrium courtyards, and the entrances have art by Siri Derkert, among others. The City Museum describes the architecture as "uncompromisingly modernist".
Vårbergs tunnelbanestation invigdes den: Vårberg metro station opened on 2 December 1967, and just under a year later Vårberg Centre opened in the same complex. The centre has been praised for its international modernist design and is an early example of an indoor square. Nearby are the Vårberg nursing home from the late 1960s – for many years the only major employer in Vårberg – and the Kummelholmen art gallery.
Vårbergs tunnelbanestation öppnade den 2: Vårberg metro station opened on 2 December 1967, with an open-air platform 12.6 kilometres from Slussen. Less than a year later, in September 1968, Vårberg centrum opened in the same complex. It's an indoor square that the City Museum has given a green listing for its importance in the history of town planning and its international modernist architecture.
Vårbergstoppen består av 2,2 miljoner ku: Vårbergstoppen is made up of 2.2 million cubic metres of blasted rock and excavated earth, mostly from building the metro. The idea came from the city's head gardener, Holger Blom, who wanted to give the hill an artistic shape.
Vårby grindstuga kallades också Svenstor: Vårby gatehouse cottage was also known as Svenstorp. The cottage itself is gone, but it gave its name to the nearby Grindstu school.
Vårby är belagt redan 1381 som \"Warby\": Vårby is recorded as early as 1381 as ‘Warby’. The site is thought to have been strategically important for protecting trade at Helgö and Birka, and the name is interpreted as ‘Vardh by’ – the watchmen’s village.
Vårby, belagt 1381, anses ha fått sitt n: Vårby, recorded in 1381, is thought to be named after its role: "Vardh by", the village of the watchmen. From here, people kept a lookout for enemy ships.
Vårbybrons pelare formgavs av Jonas Björ: The piers of Vårbybron were designed by Jonas Björkman to give the bridge a sense of lightness. Around 50,000 vehicles cross every day, and dirty run-off is caught in hanging gutters and channelled into a treatment basin beneath the bridge before it's released.
Vårbyfjärden ligger i Östra Mälaren mell: Vårbyfjärden is a bay of eastern Lake Mälaren between Södertörn and Ekerön. At its southern end it connects with Lake Albysjön via Hagaviken and Fittjaviken. The Jungfruholmarna islets lie some six nautical miles into Mälaren from Stockholm.
Vårbys första skola låg i Sadelmakartorp: Vårby's first school was in Sadelmakartorpet, the saddler's croft, after it stopped being worked as a croft in 1860. There, the unqualified schoolmistress Charlotta Falk taught some 30 children for five hours a day.
Vårbyskatten hittades i april 1871 av 14: The Vårby hoard was found in April 1871 by 14-year-old Otto Ludvig Jonsson, who was out gathering brushwood in Wårby forest. He was given a reward of 250 kronor. The jewellery dates from the 10th century and is now on display at the Swedish History Museum.
Vård för krigsinvalider och polioskadade: Care for war invalids and polio patients
Vårdkasen i kommunvapnet: The beacon in the coat of arms
Våren 1849 byggde ett par vita storkar b: In spring 1849 a pair of white storks built a nest in an oak in Rya Forest, but a hunter shot one of them and the other flew off. Today the lesser spotted woodpecker is among the birds breeding here, and in 2020 a total of 26 species were reported as confirmed breeders in the forest.
Våren 2007 flyttade radion och tv:n till: In spring 2007 Swedish radio and TV moved into Hasselblad's old premises at Lindholmen – promptly dubbed 'Kanalhuset' (the Channel House) by Gothenburg wits. From 2014 more than 500 homes, including terraced houses and rental flats, were built on the old site.
Vårfrukyrkan: Vårfrukyrkan, the Church of Our Lady
Vårfrukyrkan i Fruängen fick vänta länge: Vårfrukyrkan, the Church of Our Lady in Fruängen, had a long wait for its church. The red-brick church centre opened in 1963, but without the sanctuary shown on the plans. Building didn't start until 2004, in cast concrete, and on the first Sunday of Advent 2005 the church was finally consecrated and given the name Vårfrukyrkan.
Vårväderstorget har blivit Sveriges förs: Vårväderstorget has become the first square in a disadvantaged area of Sweden to be certified under the BoTryggt2030 safety standard. This means it meets demanding requirements for safety and security.
Vårväderstorget ritades av arkitekten He: Vårväderstorget was designed by the architect Helge Zimdal and completed in 1958, in an Italian style with terraces and arches. The name means Spring Weather Square, one of many names in Biskopsgården on the theme of weather. The square has its own tram stop, and it's home to Göteborgs folkhögskola, a folk high school, and Biskopsgården library, one of the busiest in the city.
Waldemarsudde var konstnären prins Eugen: Waldemarsudde was the home of Prince Eugen, the artist prince. A son of King Oscar II, he was one of the leading landscape painters of his day. Today his villa and garden by the water are an art museum.
Wallander fick idén till sopnedkast på e: Wallander got the idea for rubbish chutes on a trip to the USA in 1920. The health board said no. He replied that the board could ban people from using rubbish chutes, but not from building them. So they were built – and later approved.
Wallanders hustru Gerda var landskapsmål: Wallander's wife Gerda was a landscape painter and had a hand in the interiors. The villa's name, Gärds-går'n, was probably a play on her name. The house had central heating from the very start.
Wallenberg-mausoleet är byggt som ett li: The Wallenberg mausoleum, from 1912, takes the form of a small, circular Classical temple with a dome. An avenue of thujas leads up to the top of the hill, which is itself a glacial meltwater deposit from the Ice Age.
Wallenbergkullen är en isälvsavlagring f: Wallenbergkullen hill is a glacial meltwater deposit from the Ice Age, and the trees planted on it make it look even taller. On eastern Lindö there are ancient remains such as stone settings and burial sites.
Wendelsbergs folkhögskola: Wendelsbergs folkhögskola, the Wendelsberg folk high school
Wendelsbergs kamratförbund startade 1913: Wendelsberg's alumni association was founded in 1913 by former pupils and staff. Every spring it publishes a yearbook about life at the school past and present, and each year it holds a reunion where all former pupils are welcome.
Wesslau byggde tidigt arbetarbostäder oc: Wesslau was quick to build housing for its workers, along with a free school for their children. The company offered free medical care and medicine and set up a pension fund. After 1956 production moved elsewhere, and the Gothenburg operation closed.
Wesslau var en av de första i Sverige so: Wesslau was one of the first in Sweden to weave linen on mechanical looms. With the factory sitting right on the Mölndalsån river, coal for the machines could be brought in by barge from Gothenburg.
Westra Piren rankades länge som en av de: For years Westra Piren ranked among the best restaurants in Sweden's food guides. But competition for business dinners grew ever fiercer, and in the winter of 2000 the starred restaurant went bankrupt.
William Chalmers testamenterade pengar t: William Chalmers left money in his will for an industrial school for poor children who had learned to read and write. It opened on 5 November 1829 as Chalmerska Slöjdeskolan, in the great hall of the Freemasons' Society.
Wisdome Stockholm, invigt 2023, är en do: Wisdome Stockholm, opened in 2023, is a dome theatre where films are projected in 360 degrees. The roof is an undulating grid of timber beams in five layers, spanning 48 metres without a single pillar. The building won the Kasper Salin Prize, Sweden's top architecture award.
Wisingska villan var 300 kvadratmeter i: The Wising villa was a two-storey, 300-square-metre house in the Swiss chalet style with lavish fretwork. It stood at the edge of a fault scarp, and a fieldstone retaining wall about five metres high created a level area around it. The root cellar survives.
World Trade Center byggdes 1986–89 och ä: The World Trade Center was built in 1986–89 and is joined to the Cityterminalen bus terminal, with an entrance from Kungsbron too. It contains around 45,000 square metres of office space.
Ytterby har gamla anor, bygden har varit: Ytterby has a long history: people have lived here since the Iron Age, and the area is full of ancient remains. A short way from here are the ruins of Ytterby's old church, built in the Romanesque style in the 1100s on what was then Norwegian soil. Legend credits Saint Olaf with building it, and the stone church may have been preceded by an even older wooden one from the 1000s.
Yttringe betyder den yttre ängen. Namnet: Yttringe means "the outer meadow". The name appears as Ytra ængia in a deed of sale from 1381. Västra Yttringe farm by Gråviken is now used by the Iranian embassy.
Zorn och Liljefors på slottet: Zorn and Liljefors at the palace
Zorn och Liljefors på väggarna: Zorn and Liljefors on the walls
Ägaren som namngav kvarteret: The owner who named the block
Äggelundastenen, en runsten som ursprung: The Äggelunda Stone, a runestone that once stood at Äggelunda gård in Veddesta, was moved to the Fruns backe burial ground in 2014, when building work began around Barkarby commuter station. Another Veddesta runestone has had less luck: Olof Celsius the Elder mentioned it in 1728, and it has been missing ever since.
Äggelundastenen, runstenen U 84, stod ur: The Äggelunda stone, runestone U 84, originally stood at Äggelunda farm in Veddesta. In 2014, when the area around Barkarby commuter station was about to be developed, the stone was moved to Fruns backe, a burial ground south-west of Veddesta gård. Not far from there are two more Viking Age runestones, known as the runestones on Häradsvägen.
Äldreboendet Danvikshem har en historia: The Danvikshem care home traces its history back to Danvik's Hospital, which was founded in 1551 and didn't close until 1915. Close by stood the Danvik asylum, a mental hospital from 1788 to 1861, and along Kvarnholmsvägen lies an abandoned cemetery, Danvikens begravningsplats. Happier memories belong to Gomanhuset, the Goman Building, where Kooperativa Förbundet, the Swedish Cooperative Union, had its laboratory for cooked meats and sausages.
Äldst i samlingen är en hästomnibus, en: The oldest piece in the collection is a horse-drawn omnibus known as a 'Wurst', probably built in the 1840s. It's very likely the oldest surviving local public transport vehicle in Sweden. The museum has some 60 trams, buses and trains.
Älta kyrka från 1994 är byggd som en utb: Älta Church, from 1994, is built as an extension at the back of a five-storey apartment block. The walls of the church interior are a rusty brownish orange, and behind the altar a stained-glass window shows leafy branches with a red apple.
Älta kyrka invigdes 1994 och är byggd so: Älta church was consecrated in 1994 and is built as an extension at the back of a five-storey block of flats. You can spot the church interior from outside because it rises a little higher than the rest of the building. The walls are rendered white, and one façade bears a cross with a wreath of flowers.
Älta köpcentrum i Stensö invigdes 1968 o: Älta shopping centre in Stensö opened in 1968 and was one of the first indoor malls in the Stockholm area. Its eleven-storey centre building became sheltered housing for pensioners, and in eastern Stensö small houses of just 55 square metres were built for pensioners and single people.
Opened in 1968, Älta's shopping centre in Stensö was one of the first indoor malls in the Stockholm area. Its eleven-storey centre building was turned into sheltered housing for pensioners.

Älta's shopping centre in Stensö opened in 1968 and was one of the first indoor malls in the Stockholm area. The eleven-storey centre building became sheltered housing for pensioners. In eastern Stensö, small houses of just 55 square metres were built with pensioners and single people in mind.
Älta shopping centre in Stensö opened in 1968 and was one of the first indoor shopping centres in the Stockholm area. The eleven-storey centre building became sheltered housing for pensioners.
Älta mosse är Nackas största högmosse oc: Älta mosse is Nacka's largest raised bog and one of the bigger peat bogs in the Stockholm area. Typical bog plants still grow here, such as cranberry, bog myrtle, marsh Labrador tea and cloudberry.
Älta mosse är Nackas största högmosse, c: Älta mosse is Nacka's largest raised bog, about a kilometre long. Typical bog plants grow here, such as cranberry, bog myrtle, Labrador tea and cloudberry.
Älta mosse är ungefär en kilometer lång: Älta mosse is about a kilometre long and 700 metres wide, making it the largest raised bog in Nacka. Typical bog plants grow here among sparse birch woodland: cranberry, bog myrtle, marsh Labrador tea and cloudberry.
Älta är en av Nackas fyra kommundelar, o: Älta is one of Nacka's four districts, and nearby is Stensö, home to around 2,600 people. It's named after the peninsula that was once an island in Lake Ältasjön, and at its tip you'll find the Stensö swimming spot. A couple of minutes away, beside Ältavägen, is Älta Church.
Ältasjön används för bad, vattenskidåkni: Ältasjön is used for swimming, waterskiing, birdwatching and fishing. In the lake lies the island of Tallholmen, and a lakeside path links up with the Sörmlandsleden trail.
Ältavägen är 8,1 kilometer lång och fick: Ältavägen is 8.1 kilometres long, and its route was set in 1934. It runs mainly through open countryside between Älta and Nackanäs. In the Flaten nature reserve there's an unexpected attraction: a racetrack for radio-controlled model cars, at Ältavägen 301 in the Flaten district.
Ältaån är bara cirka 2 km lång, och fram: Ältaån is only about 2 km long, and until the early 1900s Söderbysjön lake reached all the way to Brotorp. In the 1960s and 1970s a major road, Skarpnäcksleden, was planned along the river, but it was never built and the area became a nature reserve instead.
Älvestaån rinner från sjön Aspen till Tu: The Älvestaån stream flows from Lake Aspen to Lake Tullingesjön, dropping 17 metres in only about 2.5 kilometres. Part of it runs through a culvert beneath Hågelby manor and the Hågelbyleden road. In Hågelby's park the stream has been reshaped into a canal, becoming part of the park's design. The name comes from Elvesta farm by Lake Tullingesjön, also spelled Älvesta.
Älvestaån var en gång en slingrande bäck: Älvestaån was once a meandering stream. In the 19th century the fields were drained and the stream became a wide, straight ditch. But about 300 metres east of Hågelbyleden it still follows its original winding course.
Älvestaån var från början en meandrande: Älvestaån started out as a meandering stream. In the 19th century the fields at Hågelby were drained and the stream was straightened into the wide, straight ditch you see today. Even so, about 300 metres east of Hågelbyleden its original winding course survives.
Älvkvarnstenen har ungefär 120 inhuggna: The Älvkvarnstenen boulder has around 120 cup marks carved into it, each 3–6 centimetres wide. Folk belief held that elves ground grain in them – hence the name, 'elf mill stone'. Stones like this had their heyday in the Bronze Age.
Älvsborgs kyrka hette tidigare Hagens ka: Älvsborg church was once known as Hagen's chapel, and it has belonged to Älvsborg parish since 1967. A little further on rises Stora Billingen, a 40-metre hill by Nya Varvet. Military facilities were blasted into the rock beneath it, but in the 2000s, once every appeal had been turned down, the housing cooperative HSB was given the go-ahead to build 50 small houses on the site.
Älvsjö gård har mycket gamla anor, med k: Älvsjö gård has deep roots, with owners known by name from the mid-15th century. One family held the farm for almost two hundred years, right up until 1968. For a long time hardly anyone lived in the area: around 1900 the population was mainly people working on the farm or at the station.
Älvsjö skrevs 1461 Elffuesio. Förleden k: In 1461 Älvsjö was written Elffuesio. The first part may be the man's name Ælve, though that's uncertain. The 'sjö' (lake) in the name is the long-gone Lake Brännkyrkasjön, which lay east of Älvsjö farm.

In 1461 Älvsjö was written Elffuesio. The first part may be the man's name Ælve, though that's uncertain. The second part refers to Brännkyrkasjön, a lake that lay east of Älvsjö farm and has since disappeared.
Älvsjöbadet ritades av Helge Zimdal och: Älvsjöbadet was designed by Helge Zimdal and Nils Ahrbom in austere functionalist style and opened on 22 June 1938. The entrance building survives and shows off their light touch. For the youngest, there's a small nine-sided paddling pool with a slide.
Älvsjöbågens brobana göts i 38 etapper m: The deck of the Älvsjöbågen bridge was cast in 38 stages using a 70-metre mould that rolled forward on a formwork carriage above live traffic. The method is used mostly in Asia and elsewhere in Europe, and specialists from Asia trained the crew.
Älvsjövägen har en imponerande trafikmän: Älvsjövägen carries a remarkable amount of traffic. At 22,000 vehicles a day, that's as much as all the daily cross-border traffic between Norway and Sweden on the E6 and E18 put together. For something calmer, head to Solbergaskogen, a short way off – a wood classed as a key habitat in 2009, with ancient remains such as the Solberga burial ground.
Ända fram till 1992 var Åbydalen en exkl: Right up until 1992 Åbydalen was an exclave – a detached piece of Fässberg parish and Mölndal municipality. Several hundred years ago the farmers of Åby were given the land as compensation after a man from the village was killed in Råda.
Ända fram till sommaren 1968, då Redberg: Right up until summer 1968, when Redbergsplatsen was rebuilt, there was a turning loop for the trams here. The pavilion in Redbergslid’s People’s Park had already been pulled down in 1936.
Ända in på 1950-talet talade man om Fröl: Right up to the 1950s people spoke of Frölanns parish, and its residents were called frölänningar. Well into the 19th century they also went by the nickname “koljenackar”.
Well into the 1950s people still spoke of Frölanns parish, and its residents were known as ‘frölänningar’. Until late in the 19th century they also had another nickname: ‘koljenackar’.
Ändelsen -sta i Kälvesta betyder plats,: The ending ‘-sta’ in Kälvesta means place, and the first part of the name was originally a man’s name. The old village of Kälvesta dates back to the Middle Ages.
The ending -sta in Kälvesta means "place", and the first part was originally a man's name. The old village of Kälvesta in Spånga parish dates back to the Middle Ages.
Ändhållplatsen ligger vid Östra sjukhuse: The last stop is at Östra sjukhuset hospital. From here it's only a short way to the Delsjö area, a large nature reserve of lakes, forest and swimming spots, where plenty of Gothenburgers spend their weekends.

The last stop is at Östra sjukhuset, the hospital. From here it's only a short way to the Delsjö area, a large nature reserve with lakes, forest and places to swim, where lots of Gothenburgers spend their weekends. Thank you for riding with us!
Ändstationen som inte skulle vara det: The terminus that wasn't meant to be
Ängarna en kort promenad härifrån är sed: Since 2026, the meadows a short walk from here have been protected as the Rissne ängar nature reserve – about 21 hectares where Rissne, Hallonbergen and Duvbo meet. Open meadows are ringed by wooded slopes of pine, and several red-listed beetles thrive here. A little further on is Duvbo Church, perched on a steep rocky slope among the villas.
Ängbystenen är ristad ganska sent. Det s: The Ängby stone was carved fairly late. You can tell from the dragons in the decoration, which are treated as plain ribbons and sometimes have neither head nor tail. The carver also used the same rune for i and e and mixed up a and n.
Ängeln finns i St. Louis och London: The angel is also in St Louis and London
Ängeln på taket är en kopia: The angel on the roof is a copy
Ängen Svartlöten, alldeles i närheten, ä: The meadow right next to us, Svartlöten, is a protected ancient site. It gave its name to Svarta Löt, a medieval assembly place mentioned in several documents from the 1400s. The meeting place itself is thought to have been at the Eriksberg croft near Kumla gård – partly where the E4/E20 motorway runs today. The Botkyrka suburb around us grew up in the late 1960s and early 1970s as part of the Million Programme, Sweden's huge housing drive. Alby centrum opened in 1972, and on the square just outside you can buy fresh fruit and vegetables.
Ängen är traktens klassiska plats för va: The meadow is the local spot for celebrating Valborg, Walpurgis Night, with a bonfire and fireworks. In winter there's a sledging hill, and during the Second World War potatoes were grown here.
Änkans hämnd i Erikskrönikan: The widow's revenge in Erik's Chronicle
Ärvinge byggdes i början av 1990-talet m: Ärvinge was built in the early 1990s with low, narrow blocks and dual-aspect flats, modelled on the suburbs of the 1940s and 50s. The office buildings sit closest to the main roads, shielding the homes from traffic noise.
Ärvinge är ett informellt område i södra: Ärvinge is an unofficial neighbourhood in southern Kista, and it's not far from here to Kista Galleria. As well as 180 shops and restaurants, the mall has a bowling alley, a multiplex cinema and a go-kart track covering a full 4,000 square metres. Students live in its two towers too – so for some, the shopping is right under their beds.
Ät eller handla i Kville saluhall: Eat or shop at Kville saluhall food hall
Ät eller handla i Kville saluhall (1 min: Eat or shop at Kville market hall (1 min) and see Carl Milles' statue Susanna on Kvilletorget (4 min).
Äta gott, dansa och förlusta sig: Eat well, dance and make merry
Även Tygförvaltningen för Östra Militäro: The ordnance administration for the Eastern Military District was also based in Ursvik. It had its own railway, nicknamed Krutbanan – the Gunpowder Line.
Även fartyg av ULCC-klass, världens stör: Even ULCC-class ships – the world's biggest tankers, measuring 333 by 60 metres – have docked at Hjärtholmen. The refinery can process about 6 million tonnes of crude oil a year.
Även om stenen är borta finns inskriften: The stone itself is gone, but its inscription has been recorded. In modern English it reads: 'Djärv … this in memory of Est, his son. Torbjörn carved.' So Torbjörn was the one who carved the stone.
ÅF-huset byggdes av Skanska, som sålde d: The ÅF building was built by Skanska, which sold it in 2015 for 495 million kronor. Two slightly lower buildings went up next door in 2016 and 2018, also for AFRY.
Åbydalen var fram till 1992 en exklav i: Until 1992 Åbydalen was an exclave of Fässberg parish. Several hundred years ago the farmers of Åby were given the land as compensation after a man from the village was killed in Råda.
Åbyfältets trav- och galoppbana öppnade: The Åbyfältet trotting and racecourse opened on 28 June 1936 with a grandstand for just over 1,000 people and stabling for 52 horses. More than 12,000 spectators came to the first meeting. Until 1976 it hosted both trotting and flat racing.

The trotting and galloping track at Åbyfältet opened on 28 June 1936, with a grandstand for just over 1,000 people and stabling for 52 horses. More than 12,000 visitors came to the first race day. Until 1976, both trotting and flat races were run here.

The Åbyfältet trotting and galloping track opened on 28 June 1936, with a grandstand for just over 1,000 people and stabling for 52 horses. More than 12,000 spectators came to the opening day. Flat racing was held here too until 1976.

The trotting and galloping track at Åbyfältet opened on 28 June 1936, and more than 12,000 visitors turned up for the first race day. Back then there was room for 52 horses in two stables. Until 1976, Åby hosted both trotting and flat racing.

The Åbyfältet trotting and flat-racing track opened on 28 June 1936, and more than 12,000 people turned up for the première. There were stables for 52 horses, and both trotting and galloping races were held here until 1976.
Åbytravet har två open stretch-spår. Det: Åby has two 'open stretch' lanes, which means horses behind the leader can use two inside lanes on the home straight, making for more open finishes. Its big races include Åby Stora Pris and the King Gustaf V Cup.
Åbytravet har två open stretch-spår. Eki: Åby's trotting track has two open-stretch lanes. Horses running behind the leader can use two inside lanes in the home straight, which makes overtaking easier and gives more open finishes.
Åbytravet har två så kallade open stretc: Åbytravet has two 'open stretch' lanes: horses behind the leader can use two inside lanes on the home straight, which makes for more open and exciting finishes.

Åbytravet, the trotting track, has two ‘open stretch’ lanes. Horses running behind the leader can use two inside lanes on the home straight, which makes for more open finishes. The track draws around 100,000 visitors a year over some sixty race days.

Åby racecourse has two 'open stretch' lanes: horses and sulkies behind the leader can use two inside lanes in the home straight, which makes for more open finishes. Around 100,000 visitors come each year to some 60 race days.
Åbyvägen har fått sitt namn efter byn Åb: Åbyvägen takes its name from the village of Åby, which lay between Brunnby and Ersta gård and is thought to have existed from as early as the Viking Age until the early 1500s. The road has also gone by the name Fabian Wredes väg. Ersta, too, is a farm that has long since vanished; it stood on the south-western edge of Årstafältet. On the same open field you'll find the Årstafältet allotments, which in 2018 counted as Stockholm's newest allotment garden.
Ågesta gårds stora stenbyggnad från 1600: Right next to us is the big 17th-century stone house of Ågesta farm, which got its present look around 1800. The City of Stockholm has owned the farm since 1945. Below it lies Lake Ågestasjön, and its name is a bit of a puzzle. 'Åg' is an old word for bulrushes and reeds, but the local heritage society believes the name actually comes from 'Åkes sta', Åke's place. The lake is part of the Orlången nature reserve.
Ågesta stängdes 1974 eftersom låga oljep: Ågesta closed in 1974 because low oil prices made it uneconomic to run. After it shut, the heavy water was sold to Canada and the fuel moved to CLAB, the interim storage facility for spent nuclear fuel. In 2020 Vattenfall began dismantling the plant, a job completed in summer 2025.
Ågestabadet var ett gammalt, lite använt: Ågestabadet was an old, little-used children's bathing spot, tucked away from any houses, when it was chosen as a nudist beach. It opened in June 1989. On the furthest knoll of the point is a grove with maze-like paths.
Ågestasjön är en grund och näringsrik sl: Ågestasjön is a shallow, nutrient-rich lowland lake teeming with life. The lake and its surrounding wetlands have been a bird sanctuary since 1976.
Ågestaverket: Ågestaverket, the old nuclear power plant
Ågestaverket kallades också R3 eller Ada: The Ågesta plant was also known as R3, or Adam. It was one of two reactor projects decided on in 1958; the other, at Marviken outside Norrköping, was named Eve.
Ågestaverket var i drift 1963–1974 och g: The Ågesta plant ran from 1963 to 1974 and mainly supplied district heating to Farsta, with only a little electricity. Its turbine was second-hand, from the steam power station at Värtan. The plant is partly built into the bedrock.
Åhlinska skolan var den tredje i Sverige: Åhlinska skolan was the third school in Sweden to offer girls higher education. From 1894 pupils could sit the studentexamen, the national school-leaving exam, at the school, and by the 1930s it had over 700 pupils. From 1908 it was at Dalagatan 16–18.
Åkarlarnas by: The village of the river men
Åkermyntans centrum nämns i en av Killin: Åkermyntan's centre gets a mention in one of the comedy group Killinggänget's sketches: it's where the character Fred Asp, famous for partying with his ferret Göran, lives nearby.
Åkermyntans centrum är ett litet köpcent: Åkermyntans centrum is a small shopping centre that opened in November 1977 – and it has earned itself a place in Swedish comedy history. In one of the sketches by the comedy group Killinggänget, the character Fred Asp, famous for partying with his ferret Göran, lives near Åkermyntan. A short way off is the Hässelby garden and local history museum, and outside it stands a grey granite runestone that was found at Riddersvik in the early 1800s.
Åkeshovs reningsverk togs i bruk 1934 oc: Åkeshov sewage works opened in 1934 and is Stockholm's oldest treatment plant still in operation. But it's due to close, with the sewage diverted through a new tunnel to Henriksdal.
Åkeshovs slott var en gång centrum för e: Åkeshov Castle was once the heart of a large estate, on which districts such as Nockeby, Nockebyhov and Åkeslund were later built. Baroness Agneta Wrede lived here for more than fifty years, from 1747 to 1800, and a room in the castle is named after her. In the castle park is an elegant Rococo orangery designed by Carl Hårleman in 1749, and beside it an arboretum planted in 1998, when Stockholm was European Capital of Culture.
Åkeshovshallen invigdes 1959 och öppnade: Åkeshovshallen swimming baths opened in 1959 and reopened in 2018 after more than two years of renovation. The water in the big pools is kept at 27 degrees, and in the children's area at a cosy 29. Not far from here are the Linnéa allotments, also called Kortenslund after the old boatswain's croft that once stood on the site. And a little further on you can catch a glimpse of Åkeshov's orangery, built in 1749.
Ålderdomshemmet Gammelbyn stod klart 193: The Gammelbyn old people's home was completed in 1930. Instead of one big barrack-like building, it was split into ten two-storey houses set among greenery – fresh thinking in Swedish elderly care.
Ålfiske eller en man vid namn Ale?: Eel fishing or a man called Ale?
Ålkistan kallas trakten där Brunnsviken: Ålkistan is the name of the area where Brunnsviken bay meets Saltsjön, the arm of the Baltic, and the canal here was blasted out of the rock in 1863–64. On Roslagsvägen, on the north side, there used to be an inn, Ålkistans värdshus, which opened in the early 1700s and was pulled down in the 1880s. The housing estate of Sfären, also known as Himlabacken – “Heaven Hill” – was built between 1989 and 1991.
Ålsten hette fram till mitten av 1500-ta: Until the mid-16th century Ålsten was called Åsunda. How to interpret the new name is uncertain: it may refer to a big rock where people fished for eel ('ål'), but another theory links it to the Old Swedish name Ale.
Ån i den gamla fjorden: A river in an ancient fjord
Ån slutar i Mälaren: The stream that ends in Lake Mälaren
Ån som blev en väg: The stream that became a road
Ån som nästan fylldes igen: The stream that was almost filled in
Ångbåtarna mellan Arboga och Stockholm s: The steamboats between Arboga and Stockholm had no restaurant on board, so passengers went ashore here to eat – and that, according to the ethnologist Sigurd Erixon, is how the tavern got its name, 'Arboga Kitchen'.
Ångloksnördar, se hit! En kort promenad: Calling all steam train fans! A short walk away is Bergslagernas Järnvägssällskap, a volunteer society set up in 1972 to look after locomotives, mainly from the old Bergslagen Railways. They have around a hundred vehicles, including restored steam, electric and diesel locomotives that still run. The Rex cinema was nearby too, showing films from 1959 to 1973.
Ånglokssällskapets klassiska turer gick: The steam locomotive society's classic excursions ran on the Slakthus line, and the last trip took place around St Lucia's Day in 1993. Since then the local outings have used the Liljeholmen–Västberga freight line and the Saltsjöbanan railway. Longer trips have gone to Strängnäs, Nora and around Lake Mälaren.
Ångslup till värdshuset: By steam launch to the inn
Ångslupen som tystnade 1913: The steam launch that fell silent in 1913
Ångsåg och kolmilor: A steam sawmill and charcoal stacks
År 1354 skrevs namnet Siaffuar, en genit: In 1354 the name was written Siaffuar, a genitive form of the word for lake, so Säve would mean something like 'the lake parish' – perhaps after a marshy area near the church. Another theory links it to an old word for calm and still, as in the modern Swedish 'sävlig', meaning unhurried.
År 1370 bytte kung Albrekt mark med Nils: In 1370 King Albert swapped land with Nils Kettilsson, Gustav Vasa's great-great-great-grandfather. That led to a ferry crossing between Lövsta and Svartsjölandet that lasted around 400 years, and the farmers of Lövsta were obliged to row travellers across.
År 1381 skrevs namnet ruuddobodha. Ett \: In 1381 the name was written ruuddobodha. In the Middle Ages a "rudde" was cleared land, so the name roughly means the hut by the new clearing. Rudboda farm also has a red house from the 1850s – Lidingö's only surviving statare dwelling, home to farm labourers paid largely in kind.
År 1388 skrevs namnet Thorlandum. Det ko: In 1388 the name was written Thorlandum. It comes from the church village and combines the name of the god Thor with the word land.
År 1415 skrevs namnet Awngaryd. Det komm: In 1415 the name was written Awngaryd. It may come from the man's name Agund plus ryd, meaning a clearing. Another theory is that it means 'those who live by the aven' – the pool of water.
År 1467 sålde Tyska orden Vendelsö till: In 1467 the Teutonic Order sold Vendelsö to Erik Axelsson Tott, together with everything else the order owned in Sweden. The estate became a manor before 1610.
År 1527 köpte Stockholms borgmästare And: In 1527 Anders Simonsson, mayor of Stockholm, bought the Ersta farm and was granted tax exemption 'at pleasure' – for as long as the Crown saw fit. In 1563 it was sold to another mayor, Mats Persson Skulte, who received the same privilege.
År 1528 lät Gustav Vasa riva kyrkan. I s: In 1528 Gustav Vasa had the church torn down. In his letter he wrote that it stood so close to the town that it wasn't needed, and that the enemy could use it in the event of war. Its stones were used to build the church in Nya Lödöse instead.
År 1541 bestod Törnby av två frälsegårda: In 1541 Törnby was made up of two tax-exempt noble farms and one freehold farm. In 1544 Karin Axelsdotter (Tott) sold the noble farms to King Gustav Vasa.
År 1547 förlänade Gustav Vasa Vårby och: In 1547 Gustav Vasa granted Vårby and Smista as a fief to the scribe Clemet Hansson. His son Måns Clemetsson, later ennobled as Oliveblad, made Vårby gård the main seat of the whole estate.
År 1562 ägdes Viksjö av Nils Eriksson Ry: In 1562 Viksjö was owned by Nils Eriksson Ryning, one of the richest men in the country. He owned some 340 farms in almost every province, most of them in Småland.
År 1562 ägdes gården av riksrådet Gabrie: In 1562 the estate was owned by the councillor of the realm Gabriel Kristiernsson-Oxenstierna, uncle of the Lord High Chancellor Axel Oxenstierna. A later owner, Arnold Grothusen, was forced to flee the country, and Duke Karl then seized the estate for the Crown.
År 1568 inkvarterade Erik XIV skotska le: In 1568 King Erik XIV quartered Scottish mercenaries in the vicarage to fight off a Danish attack on Stockholm. The Swedes won the clash in the fields by the church, but the Danes burned down the vicarage before they fled.
År 1571 skänkte Johan III gården till An: In 1571 King Johan III gave the farm to Antonius de Palma, an Italian nobleman at the Polish court. For almost 150 years after that it belonged to the Görväln estate.
År 1571 skänkte Johan III gården till de: In 1571 King Johan III gave the farm to the Italian nobleman Antonius de Palma, who served at the Polish court. By the end of the 1500s the farm had 12 cows, 12 sheep and two pigs, among other livestock.
År 1571 skänkte Johan III gården, som då: In 1571 Johan III gave the farm, then called Gerfelle, to Antonius de Palma, an Italian nobleman at the Polish court. For almost 150 years after that it belonged to the Görväln estate. By the end of the 16th century the farm had, among other things, 12 cows, 12 sheep and 2 pigs.
År 1599 konfiskerade staten godset i tro: In 1599 the state confiscated the estate during the struggles over the throne. But in 1603 Kristina Sture got part of it back, as she could prove that her husband Gustav Axelsson Banér had given her Djursholm as a morning gift – the traditional gift from husband to bride.
År 1601 blev Gustav Vasas svägerska, gre: In 1601 Countess Ebba Lilliehöök, sister-in-law of King Gustav Vasa, became the owner of Lärjeholm. The burghers of Nya Lödöse complained that she seized their land and livestock by force. She died on the estate in 1609.

In 1601, Countess Ebba Lilliehöök, Gustav Vasa's sister-in-law, became the owner of Lärjeholm. The burghers of Nya Lödöse complained that 'Fru Iba' was seizing the town's land by force and trying to take their cattle. She died on the estate in 1609.
År 1608 skänkte Karl IX Kummelby gård ti: In 1608 King Karl IX gave Kummelby farm to his castle steward, Erik Jöransson Tegel, who was later stripped of it by the courts. In 1641 the farm was bought by Gabriel Oxenstierna, and for the next 200 years it belonged to the Edsberg estate.
År 1645, under Hannibalsfejdens slutsked: In 1645, in the closing stages of the war known as the Hannibal Controversy, Hannibal Sehested tried to attack Gothenburg. Norwegian troops threw a makeshift bridge across the Göta älv river, and the Fredrikshamn redoubt was built on Hisingen to protect the bridgehead. The redoubt is just nearby – a reminder that this riverbank was once a battlefield.
