År 1653 såg riksrådet Svante Svantesson: In 1653 the privy councillor Svante Svantesson Banér made Danderyd a parish of its own. He donated land at Sätra and had a rectory built with a main house and wings, where the first vicar moved in in 1656. In the 1700s the property fell into decline, starting with the plague of 1710–1711.
År 1660 beslöts att den omoderna borgen: In 1660 it was decided that the outdated castle should be blown up. In 1661 its name passed to the new fortress on Kyrkogårdsholmen, Nya Elfsborg. The ruin was then used as a quarry, and today the remains are protected by a roof structure.
År 1679 drogs gårdens säterifrihet in, e: In 1679 the estate lost its tax-exempt manor status because its buildings had fallen into disrepair and the land was let out. The privileges were restored a few years later, but the criticism continued, and in 1704 most of the buildings were described as no better than ordinary farmhouses.

In 1679 the farm lost its säteri status – the tax exemption granted to manors – because the buildings were run-down and the land was leased out. The privileges were restored, but the criticism kept coming: in 1704 most of the buildings were described as ordinary farmhouses.
År 1684 arrenderades Henriksborg ut till: In 1684 Henriksborg was leased to the Dutchman Abraham Vichenhaan, who built a saltworks. The idea was to extract salt from the waters of the Saltsjön, the brackish bay here – but it didn't work very well.
År 1691 byggde handelsmannen Jacob Gavel: In 1691 the merchant Jacob Gavelius built a cloth mill here. By the 1780s the textile factory was Stockholm's largest workplace, with 640 workers. It closed in 1826.
År 1703 målade göteborgskonstnären Erik: In 1703 the Gothenburg artist Erik Eriksson Grijs painted the church ceiling with black-and-white ornaments, angels shown only from the waist up, apostles and the fall of the Antichrist. The paintings were lost when the church was demolished and its timber sold.
År 1721 tände en gnista under en storm e: In 1721, during a storm, a spark set the shingle roof alight. The whole upper floor, chapel and library included, was destroyed, and when it was rebuilt the roof was given the shape it has today.

In 1721, during a storm, a spark set the shingle roof alight. The entire upper floor, with the chapel and the precious library, burnt down. When it was rebuilt the roof was given a new shape – the one you see today.
År 1722 fick Ingela Gathenhielm ett priv: In 1722 King Fredrik I granted Ingela Gathenhielm a charter to build a ropewalk, as compensation for having to give up the Old Shipyard. The ropeworks covered about 46,000 square metres, and ropes and hawsers were made here right up until 1879, when Bangatan was to be built.
År 1723 fick slottet sitt nuvarande yttr: In 1723 the palace got its present exterior, with a säteri roof – a distinctive broken hipped roof – replacing the old hipped one. Above the entrance is a sandstone portal bearing the arms of Gabriel Stierncrona and his wife and the year 1723, the same year he died, and beneath it a wrought-iron rococo grille with gilded leaves.
År 1734 grundades Sveriges första frikyr: In 1734 Sweden's first free church, Filadelfiska Societén (the Philadelphian Society), was founded and based in the palace. Its members lived there too.
År 1735 fick bröderna Smith tillstånd at: In 1735 the Smith brothers were given permission to build a steelworks to an English design at Follbrinken. It was built in great secrecy, since the technology was an English state matter. As early as 1631 there was a blast furnace here for ore from Utö.
År 1740 brann kyrkans torn och tak. Peng: In 1740 the church's tower and roof caught fire. There wasn't enough money to rebuild the tall spire, so to this day the tower has a low pyramid roof. Erik Dahlbergh's picture from 1661 shows the original pointed spire.
År 1741 fick konstnären Johan Ross den ä: In 1741 the artist Johan Ross the Elder was commissioned to paint the church's barrel-vaulted wooden ceiling. The painting shows the Last Judgement, with Christ in the middle of the church. Today these Rococo ceiling paintings are what the church is best known for.
År 1747 fick torparen lämna Isbergatorpe: In 1747 the crofter had to leave Isbergatorpet when alderman Gustaf Johan Ruth took it over on a perpetual lease. He renamed the place Herrängen and built a new main house on the meadow of that name. The farm then became a summer retreat for well-off Stockholmers.
År 1758 startade rådman Daniel Enerot et: In 1758 the alderman Daniel Enerot opened a brewery on the Eastern Harbour next to Kungsporten, the King's Gate – roughly level with today's Kopparmärra equestrian statue. After his death his widow ran it for a while, and the brewery kept going until 1816.
År 1765 skänkte Riddarhuset en del av si: In 1765 the House of Nobility gave part of its plot to the city so that the square could be enlarged and given a statue of Gustav Vasa. When the square was remodelled in 1914–1916, the statue was moved to where it stands now.
År 1769 köpte bryggaren Anders Berg Väst: In 1769 the brewer Anders Berg bought Västergården in Eneby. According to tradition he coined the name Enebyberg from Eneby and his own surname, but that's never been confirmed. Others believe berg – hill – refers to a hillock that was blasted away.
År 1769 köpte bryggaren Anders Berg en g: In 1769 the brewer Anders Berg bought a farm in the village of Eneby. Tradition says Enebyberg farm got its name when he combined Eneby with his surname, but that's never been confirmed. Others believe ‘berg’ refers to a hill that has since been blasted away.

In 1769 the brewer Anders Berg bought a farm in Eneby village. Tradition has it that he combined Eneby with his surname to make Enebyberg, though that's never been confirmed. Another theory is that "berg" refers to a hillock next to the farm that was later blasted away.
År 1769 köpte skotten Thomas Lewis områd: In 1769 the Scotsman Thomas Lewis bought the area and set up a foundry for cooking pots. He applied for permission to cast iron the English way, using the then brand-new reverberatory furnace. The following year the place where his house stood was called Berg och Sund.
År 1770 köptes palatset av tobaksfabrikö: In 1770 the palace was bought by the tobacco manufacturer Johan Christian Nentwig, who spun tobacco on the premises. Around 1800 it belonged to the brewer Johan Gustaf Wertmüller, and the building became known as the Wertmüller house.
År 1770 planterades en lindallé längs ån: In 1770 an avenue of lindens was planted along the river, using saplings from Holland. Some of them are still standing and are Gothenburg's oldest planted trees. Anyone who damaged one risked a fine of ten daler in silver coin.
År 1774 anlade grosshandlaren J.G. Claus: In 1774 the wholesale merchant J.G. Claussen set up a wax bleachery at Jacobsdal, producing white wax for candles. The area is known as Polska udden and also had a cotton printing works. Industry here came to an end around 1815.
År 1775 kom Carl Michael Bellman till kr: In 1775 Carl Michael Bellman came to the inn – his brother-in-law owned nearby Hägersten farm. The visit is described in song no. 65, where the croft appears among shady aspens, maples and alders.
År 1776 bad Aaron Isaac, grundaren av Ju: In 1776 Aaron Isaac, founder of the Jewish community in Stockholm, asked for a burial ground. It was named Aronsberg after him, and he is buried there himself. The cemetery was used from 1782 to 1888 and has 300 graves.
År 1782 gav Gustav III Drottningholmsmal: In 1782 Gustav III granted Drottningholmsmalmen town privileges to tempt traders and craftsmen to settle. A grid plan was drawn up in 1783 but never completed – today only Långa raden, Dragonvägen, Malmbacken and Kvarnbacken follow it.
År 1785 köptes Slagsta av friherre Johan: In 1785 Slagsta was bought by Baron Johan Liljencrantz, who also owned Fittja gård, Norsborg manor and Sturehov Castle. The City of Stockholm bought the estate in 1908, and since 1978 it has belonged to Botkyrka municipality.
År 1789 köpte församlingen en orgel av P: In 1789 the parish bought an organ by Pehr Schiörlin from the English church, where it had probably never been installed. When a new organ was built around 1870 it was sold to Jonsered Church, where it remains to this day.
År 1795 besöktes Råda av den engelska fö: In 1795 the English writer Mary Wollstonecraft paid a visit to Råda. For part of the 19th century the manor was owned by Baroness Martina von Schwerin.
År 1801 tillkom genom kungligt beslut na: In 1801, by royal decree, the museum received the natural history collections that had belonged to Queen Lovisa Ulrika and been kept at Drottningholm Palace. As early as 1784 it had been decided that the museum should open to the public at certain times.
År 1810 ägdes granntorpet Månskär av Jac: In 1810 the neighbouring croft of Månskär was owned by Jacob Rubensson, ‘Cattun Fabrikeur’ – a maker of calico. The croft fell into disrepair over many years and was finally destroyed by fire in 1984.
År 1812 ägdes gården av bryggaråldermann: In 1812 the estate belonged to Gustaf Lychou, alderman of the brewers’ guild, who had the house renovated when he was awarded the Order of Vasa in 1832. Around 1890 the wholesale merchant Oscar Arvidson pulled down several old outbuildings and built, among other things, a large villa, a bathhouse and a skittle alley. They have all since been demolished.
År 1816 satte ordenssällskapet Neptunior: In 1816 the Neptune Order, a fraternal society, set a three-pronged ‘Neptune's fork’ into the bare rock on Svanholmen. No trace of it remains.
År 1832 flyttade fabrikör Fredrik Modin: In 1832 the manufacturer Fredrik Modin moved his wax candle production from Södermalm to Hustegaholm and built the house now known as Sjövillan. In the first year his six employees made 31,000 candles. Once stearin candles caught on, Modin was quickly outcompeted.
År 1833 köpte skotten William Gibson och: In 1833 the Scotsmen William Gibson and Alexander Keiller bought Jonsered to start a textile business. The site on the Säveån river provided water power, and for many years the goods were shipped out by barge along the river.
År 1834 byggde apotekaren på Kronan, Han: In 1834 Hans Jacob Cavallin, the apothecary at Kronan pharmacy, built a stone well house here. The spring drew crowds until 1858 – the poet Esaias Tegnér came to take the waters in 1837. After that, one wing served as a hot bathhouse until 1879.
År 1838 anlades en privat väg från Kålle: In 1838 a private road was built from Kållered to Lindome, paid for by fees collected at a tollgate here in Flabäck. A coaching inn went up in 1844–1845 but was demolished in 1967–1968 to make way for the E6 motorway.
År 1838 köptes Orhem av Ebba Gustava af: In 1838 Orhem was bought by Ebba Gustava af Wirsén, wife of the composer Hildebrand Hildebrandsson. When her husband was away she wrote letters to friends signed 'Frun i skogen' – 'the Lady in the Forest'. The letters were later published in several books.
År 1840 inredde Johan Otto Wedberg en ko: In 1840 Johan Otto Wedberg fitted out a complete theatre in the north wing of Lidingsberg. It’s still intact, with its stage sets and a separate make-up room. Family and friends performed plays by writers such as August Blanche and Eugène Scribe.
År 1840 lät Johan Otto Wedberg inreda en: In 1840 Johan Otto Wedberg had a complete theatre fitted out in the estate's north wing. It survives with its original interior, its scenery and its own make-up room. Plays by August Blanche and Eugène Scribe, among others, were staged here, often with relatives and friends as amateur actors.

In 1840 Johan Otto Wedberg had a complete theatre fitted out in the farm's north wing. It survives with its original interior, scenery and its own make-up room. Plays by August Blanche and others were staged here, often with relatives and friends as the cast.
År 1845 skrev Pehr Adam Wallmark att man: In 1845 Pehr Adam Wallmark wrote that you could satisfy your appetite cheaply at the inn, as long as you weren’t too much of a gourmet. Conscripts from Marieberg liked to pop over for a bite to eat or a cup of coffee, and by 1852 there was a skittle alley.
År 1847 åtalades värdshusvärden Karl Pet: In 1847 the innkeeper Karl Petter Lindbom was prosecuted for running an unlicensed tavern in a house next door. His defence was that good order required not mixing very different classes of people in the same room. The charge was dismissed.
År 1848 sänktes sjön rejält. Tidigare st: In 1848 the lake was lowered considerably. Before then it reached right up to where the station area is now, and the vanished Kyrksjön lake by Huddinge Church was part of Trehörningen.
År 1850 byggdes ett lusthus på en hög kl: In 1850 a summerhouse was built on a high rocky ledge near the water. It became a well-known landmark for boats on Lilla Värtan, and in 1869 the estate also got its own steamboat jetty.
In 1850 a summerhouse was built on a high rocky ledge near the water, and it became a well-known landmark for shipping on Lilla Värtan. In 1869 the estate also got its own steamboat jetty.

In 1850 a summerhouse was built on a high rocky ledge near the water, and it became a well-known landmark for shipping on Lilla Värtan. The buildings have changed little since the steamboat jetty arrived in 1869.
År 1855 drog Solna församling in värdshu: In 1855 Solna parish revoked the inn's right to serve spirits, and it became a temperance inn. The white Swiss-style wooden villa arrived in 1868, and in 1987 it gained an octagonal glass pavilion with a crystal chandelier.
År 1857 köptes huset av Jacques Lamm, so: In 1857 the building was bought by Jacques Lamm, owner of the Ludwigsberg engineering works, and his workers moved in. In 1904 the whole lot was bought by the Münchenbryggeriet brewery, and brewery workers lived here instead. Running water and drains weren't put into the kitchens until 1918.
År 1859 såldes Bergfana till Statens jär: In 1859 Bergfana was sold to Swedish State Railways. Two years later Frans Joseph Björklund moved in as the first track master, in a lodge given the number 120. He looked after the line from Långmossen to Dånängen.
År 1860 blev Sadelmakartorp Vårbys först: In 1860 Sadelmakartorp, the saddler’s croft, became Vårby’s first school. The teacher, Charlotta Falk, taught up to 30 children for five hours a day. Today only old house foundations, a road embankment and some fruit trees bear witness to the croft.

In 1860 Sadelmakartorp became Vårby's first school. The schoolmistress, Charlotta Falk, taught up to 30 children five hours a day. All that's left on the site today are old house foundations, a road embankment and fruit trees.
År 1861 köpte snusfabrikören Knut Ljungl: In 1861 the snuff manufacturer Knut Ljunglöf, known as “the Snuff King”, bought up large tracts of land here. By the early 1900s his factory was the biggest snuff producer in Europe. Between 1890 and 1893 he built Ljunglöfska slottet, his castle on Lake Mälaren.
År 1862 infördes den så kallade talmetod: In 1862 the so-called oral method was introduced. Teaching was no longer allowed in sign language, and deaf teachers were dismissed. In 1879 the department for the blind moved to Tomteboda.
År 1862 köpte grosshandlaren och träpatr: In 1862 the merchant and timber baron James Robertson Dickson bought the estate. He spent hundreds of thousands of kronor tearing down the old house, building the grand villa and laying out an English-style park – all for use as a summer home.
År 1862 köpte träpatronen James Robertso: In 1862 the timber magnate James Robertson Dickson bought the Billdal estate and spent hundreds of thousands of kronor on it. He built the large villa and laid out an English-style park. Today the park is an outdoor recreation area, with the Krogabäcken stream winding through it.
År 1864 anlade Lars Montén en stearinlju: In 1864 Lars Montén set up a stearin candle factory on the shore at Alvik, which later made soap as well. The White House by the water started out as a lactic acid factory and is now the heart of the office district.
År 1864 köpte grosshandlaren Lars Montén: In 1864 the merchant Lars Montén bought the Alvik and Äppelviken farms and set up a candle factory on the shore of Lake Mälaren. Later it made soap as well. In 1920 the factory merged with Barnängens Tekniska Fabrik.
År 1865 flyttade Alfred Nobel sin nitrog: In 1865 Alfred Nobel moved his nitroglycerine factory to Vinterviken after his earlier works on Söder Mälarstrand had blown up. Dynamite was made here right up into the 1920s. Among what survives is the old sulphuric acid factory from the 1890s.
År 1866 bad Örgryte socken att Landala s: In 1866 Örgryte parish asked for Landala to be handed over to Gothenburg, as the area was considered 'a haunt of thieves and bandits'. As late as 1889 the houses were described as 'of wood and very wretched'. In the end the city bought Landala for 115,000 kronor.
År 1866 köptes Långbro gård av Alfred Sö: In 1866 Långbro farm was bought by Alfred Söderlund, known as 'the Långbro King'. Between 1898 and 1918 he divided up and sold around 500 plots, laying the foundations for the villa suburbs of Linboda and Långbrodal. The rest was bought by Ericsson in 1918 and by the City of Stockholm in 1947.
År 1867 beskrivs Lindvreten som en liten: In 1867 Lindvreten is described as a small log cottage, about 6 by 4 metres, with a porch and a single room with a fireplace and bread oven. The last crofter was Jonas Bäcklin, born in 1785, and his wife Greta.
År 1868 startade en bläckfabrik i Tottie: In 1868 an ink factory opened in the Tottie family's country house, and it later became Barnängens Tekniska Fabrik. Part of the house was moved to the Skansen open-air museum in 1935.
År 1870 blev Nya Varvet fängelse under F: In 1870 Nya Varvet became a prison run by the national prison board. After the union with Norway was dissolved in 1905, the area regained its military importance, and in 1985 it was sold into civilian hands.
År 1872 fick krogen stänga eftersom gäst: In 1872 the inn had to close because it had too few guests. The building then became a primary school for southern Sollentuna and, after 1893, housing for statare – farmworkers paid largely in kind. Not until Walpurgis Eve 1983, 111 years after it closed, did Christer Lingström reopen an inn here.
År 1873 kostade det ett öre att gå över: In 1873 it cost one öre to walk across the bridge and nine öre for carts and sledges. A skipper who wanted the drawbridge opened had to pay 19 öre. In 1909, a motor car cost nine öre.
År 1877 drogs den första telefonförbinde: In 1877 Gothenburg's first telephone line was put up, between the city and Jonsered. Back in 1856, the first stretch of the Western Main Line railway had opened, also between Gothenburg and Jonsered.
År 1878 tog Elsa Borg, kallad Vita berge: In 1878 Elsa Borg, known as the Queen of the White Hills, took over the farm and turned it into a refuge for young women, who knitted, sewed, did laundry and tended the garden. The gardener's house became a home for eleven children. In the park just north of the farm stands a 1972 statue of her by Astri Bergman-Taube, holding two small children in her arms.
År 1879 köptes gården av slaktaren Johan: In 1879 the farm was bought by the butcher Johan August Johansson, and from 1894 it also had a laundry. In 1906 it was sold to AB Södertörns villastad, but just six years later the City of Stockholm bought the land.
År 1879 öppnade här det första museet, A: The first museum, the Artillery Museum, opened here in 1879. It was renamed the Army Museum in 1932 and reopened under that name in Stora Tyghuset, the great arsenal, in 1943. In the middle of the courtyard stands Theodor Lundberg's Poltava monument from 1904.
År 1884 köptes Breviks gård av Jean Boli: In 1884 Brevik farm was bought by Jean Bolinder, one of the brothers behind the Bolinders engineering works. The streets Västra Allén, Stora Allén and Östra Allén are named after the farm's old tree-lined avenues.
År 1885 bodde 54 vuxna och 80 barn i hus: In 1885, 54 adults and 80 children lived in the building's 28 flats. Machine fitter Johan Berg shared a one-room flat of just over 20 square metres with his wife, eight children and two lodgers. Today there are twelve flats, each with two rooms and a kitchen.
År 1885 flyttade Frans Krig, Brommas sis: In 1885 Frans Krig, Bromma's last soldier under the old allotment system, moved into the dragoon's croft. He started a rubbish collection service in Bromma that his son Sixten later took over, and the croft was extended with a piggery for 200 pigs.

In 1885 Frans Krig, Bromma's last allotted soldier – one of the farm-supported soldiers of Sweden's old army system – moved into the croft. He started a rubbish collection service in Bromma, and the croft was extended with a piggery for 200 pigs. Since 2012 the house has been home to an estate agent.
År 1885 invigdes en av Stockholms tidiga: In 1885 one of Stockholm's early water reservoirs, known as Vattenborgen, "the Water Castle", opened on top of Stadshagsberget. It was pulled down in 1934 to make way for new housing, and the little Stadshagsplan park was laid out at the same time.
År 1888 blev Spånga grenstation för en b: In 1888 Spånga became a junction for a branch line to Lövsta and the garden suburb of Hässelby villastad. In the early days both long-distance and local trains stopped here.
År 1890 beslöt Djursholms AB att reparer: In 1890 Djursholms AB decided to repair the castle for 30,000 kronor. The bill came to 70,000, and Henrik Palme had to leave the company in 1891. He later defended himself by saying the castle had become a worthy centrepiece for the villa town.
År 1890 byggdes en stor skolbyggnad efte: In 1890 a large school building was put up to designs by Axel Kumlien, and girls aged 5 to 18 were cared for here until 1946. Then the band of the Svea Life Guards moved in, with rehearsal rooms and quarters for young musicians.
År 1890 utredde stadsfullmäktige om Fatt: In 1890 the city council looked into filling in Fattighusån, as the water had stagnated and begun to stink. The question came up again in 1906 and 1911, but in 1926 the harbour board demanded that the idea be dropped – and so it was.
År 1892 tvångsintogs en lantbrukare från: In 1892 a farmer from Halland was committed to the Tufvan asylum against his will, with no medical certificate – his relatives had tricked him into going. The scandal led to a doctor appointed by the National Board of Health taking charge, and to stricter rules on admission papers.
År 1893 föreslogs en lanterna med rött s: In 1893 someone proposed putting a red lantern at the end of the pier. It would warn pedestrians on the bridge, and also help the steamboat captains who complained they couldn't find their way in at night.
År 1894 fick Pixbo en liten station på j: In 1894 Pixbo got a small station on the Gothenburg–Borås railway, where trains stopped until 1978. In the early 1900s well-to-do Gothenburgers built large villas overlooking Rådasjön lake, some in Art Nouveau and some in Old Norse style.
År 1894 köpte trävarufirman Olsson & Ros: In 1894 the timber firm Olsson & Rosenlund bought the estate and set up industries. Lake Mälaren provided a natural harbour for the logs, and the clay for the brickworks was dug in what is now the Örnsberg industrial area. The villas in Mälarhöjden were built with the firm's own timber and bricks.
År 1895 blev företaget AB Gerh. Arehns M: In 1895 the company became AB Gerh. Arehns Mekaniska Verkstad and moved into new factory buildings in the Dykaren block, designed by Gustaf Lindgren. Its machines were partly based on patents held by the technical director, Frans Lundgren.
År 1895 började Djursholmsbanan som värl: In 1895 the Djursholm railway became the world's first electric passenger train in regular service, with its power coming from here. The power station stood strategically at Stocksund harbour, where coal could easily be unloaded, roughly halfway between the line's two termini.
År 1895 började man föda upp grisar på h: In 1895 an attempt was made at Lövsta to raise pigs on household waste. It was abandoned when the pigs died from the unhealthy diet. Instead, work began on a plant for burning the rubbish.
År 1895 tog Saltsjöbanans bolag över köp: In 1895 the Saltsjöbanan railway company took over the purchase of Järla manor. The idea was to attract industry whose freight would make the railway pay. De Laval's large machine hall from 1911 still stands.
År 1897 köptes bostället av Solna försam: In 1897 the residence was bought by Solna parish. Between 1937 and 1967 it housed Solna's local history museum, with the curator living upstairs. The museum then moved to Charlottenburg farm, where it still is today.
År 1897 köptes villan av före detta skom: In 1897 the villa was bought by Johan Fredrik Källgren, a retired master shoemaker from Stockholm. It stayed in the Källgren family right up until the 1970s. Today it's lived in all year round.
År 1898 köpte snusfabrikanten Knut Ljung: In 1898 the snuff manufacturer Knut Ljunglöf, known as 'the Snuff King', bought Beckomberga farm. He tore down most of the old buildings and put up modern stables, a fodder barn and a five-flat cottage for the farm labourers. The yellow villa from 1856 became the farm foreman's home.
År 1899 lyckades Thor Stenbeck med värld: In 1899 Thor Stenbeck carried out the world's first successful treatment of skin cancer with X-rays. His assistant was a young medical student, Gösta Forssell, who went on to build up the Radiumhemmet cancer clinic.
År 1900 kallade Stockholms Dagblad skola: In 1900 the newspaper Stockholms Dagblad called the school the largest in the world. The paper couldn't find a school as big anywhere in Europe – though there might possibly be something similar in Chicago. Plans of the building were sent to the Paris World's Fair that same year.
År 1900 var piren 151 meter lång. När Gö: In 1900 the pier was 151 metres long. In 1973, when the Götaverken shipyard needed more room to manoeuvre around its floating dock and the shipping channel had to be moved, Stenpiren was shortened by 42 metres. Today the quay is 215 metres long.
År 1901 bodde 17 statarfamiljer på Ulvsu: In 1901 seventeen statare families – farm labourers paid mostly in kind – lived at Ulvsunda farm, in four houses in what was then a very rural setting. The stable held 22 horses. Most of the farm buildings were demolished in 1938.
År 1901 köptes Marieborg av industrimann: In 1901 Marieborg was bought by the industrialist Ernst Gäbel, who built the present villa in 1902 – one of many in the Södertörn garden suburb. It was remodelled in 1927 to designs by Hakon Ahlberg. Today the house holds the Magelungarna preschool and an artists' studio association.
År 1901 stod en helt ny skolbyggnad klar: In 1901 a brand-new school building was completed at Aspnäs, with a classroom for 64 primary pupils and 36 infants, a teacher's flat and a woodwork room. There was even a dental clinic with a surgery and a small waiting room. The old school was sold the same year for 1,000 kronor.
År 1902 exploderade luftballongen Svensk: In 1902 the hot-air balloon Svenske exploded over Trolldalen and plunged 1,500 metres with two passengers on board. Against all odds, nobody was hurt.
År 1903 avstyckades en tomt från Långbro: In 1903 a plot was split off from Långbro manor for a rope works. The area was first known as Blackens hage, after a horse called Blacken that had died in a paddock nearby. Only the dwelling house survives, on today's Blackensvägen.
År 1904 blev den nybyggda Trekantsreserv: In 1904 the newly built Trekant reservoir became the end point of the new main water pipeline from Norsborg to Stockholm. It's still the city's main source of drinking water from the south.
År 1904 invigde kung Oscar II det västra: In 1904 King Oscar II opened the western waterworks in Norsborg. The water came from Bornsjön lake, which the city had bought around the turn of the century. The cast-iron main was more than a metre in diameter, and a few years later a second, 700-millimetre pipe was laid beside it.
År 1904 köpte Stockholm Enskede gårds 60: In 1904 Stockholm bought the 600 hectares of Enskede farm for two million kronor – the city's first and largest land acquisition beyond the old toll gates. On this land came Stockholm's first garden suburb, the Southern Cemetery and the city slaughterhouse.
År 1905 invigdes Johannesdals folkskola: In 1905 Johannesdal primary school opened on land donated by the wholesale merchant Nils Sandberg. The schoolhouse still stands and is now part of Mälarhöjden school.
År 1905 köpte staten gårdarna på Järvafä: In 1905 the state bought the farms on Järvafältet to create a military training ground. Eggeby became a billeting farm, and the tenant was paid per bed – there were twelve. The area was closed to the public until 1962.
År 1906 började direktör Ernst Kihlberg: In 1906 the businessman Ernst Kihlberg began dividing up the farm's land into plots for a garden suburb along the Roslagsbanan railway. The company built a sawmill by the farm so it could sell building materials right on site. By the 1940s, every plot had been built on.
År 1906 köpte finansmannen Allan Abenius: In 1906 the financier Allan Abenius bought the estate and divided the land into plots for villas of 28–30 rooms. A steamer, the S/S Brevik, was acquired for commuters in 1909, and Ferdinand Boberg designed an Art Nouveau waiting room and bathhouse on the jetty.
År 1907 började bygget av Gula Villan på: In 1907 work began on Gula Villan (the Yellow Villa) at Welanders väg 4, designed by Dorph & Höög. It was the first building in Sweden built and fitted out purely as a day nursery, and it's still used as a preschool.
År 1907–1908 höjdes tornet drygt tio met: In 1907–1908 the tower was raised by just over ten metres, and the weather vane bears the year 1908. After 1960 it was no longer needed and was earmarked for demolition, but protests saved it. Since 1974 it has housed the local heritage society and the association archives.
År 1910 köpte auditören Clas Östberg 30: In 1910 the military judge Clas Östberg bought 30 hectares between the station and Edsviken and divided the land into 61 villa plots. Around twenty had been sold by the end of the first year. The shopping centre arrived in 1975 and has become one of the largest in Greater Stockholm.
År 1910 styckades gården i lotter som bl: In 1910 the farm was divided into lots, eventually some 500 plots, sold to workers and junior clerks. Vidja became a classic summer-cottage area, but today most people here live year-round. Icelandic horses are kept at the old Vidja croft.
År 1910 var gatan bara 223 meter lång. G: In 1910 the street was just 223 metres long. The pavements were almost entirely gravel and the roadway macadam – only 43 square metres were laid with stone, asphalt or concrete.
År 1910 vägrade Djurgårdens fotbollslag: In 1910 the Djurgården football team refused to share a pitch with AIK. The city then offered them a site just beyond Tranebergsbro bridge, and the sports ground was opened in September 1911 by Crown Prince Gustaf Adolf.
År 1911 hade bara 110 tomter sålts, för: By 1911 only 110 plots had been sold, at 10 to 18 öre per square metre. The following year the City of Stockholm bought the whole company and 645 hectares of land for one million kronor.
År 1913 blev Göteborgsfabriken en del av: In 1913 the Gothenburg factory became part of Ivar Kreuger's AB Förenade Svenska Tändsticksfabriker, and in 1917 of Svenska Tändsticks AB, the Swedish Match Company. That was when it was renamed Göteborgs Tändsticksfabrik.
År 1914 drogs spårvagnslinje 13 ut till: In 1914 tram line 13 was extended to Ulvsunda across the pontoon bridge at Tranebergssund. The terminus was at Lillsjöplan, where a tram depot was built.
År 1914 lät grosshandlaren C. Leffler by: In 1914 the wholesale merchant C. Leffler built a large stone villa in the National Romantic style on land belonging to Bräcke farm, designed by Ernst Krüger. In 1927 the villa was donated to the Bräcke deaconry, and today it's known as Bräcke diakonigård.
År 1915 var Sveriges holme till salu, oc: In 1915 the islet of Sveriges holme was up for sale, and there were fears it would end up covered in villas or oil tanks. The lawyer Harald W Lettström bought the island and later donated it to the state.
År 1916 annonserades 28 av Rya skogs eka: In 1916, 28 of the oaks in Rya forest were advertised for sale. The Gothenburg branch of the Swedish Society for Nature Conservation wrote to the King in Council, and the answer was that only dead and wind-felled trees could be cut down. It was the forest's first real protection.
År 1916 annonserades 28 av skogens ekar: In 1916, 28 of the forest's oaks were advertised for sale. The Gothenburg branch of the Swedish Society for Nature Conservation wrote to the King in Council, and the reply was that only dead and wind-felled trees could be cut. It was the first real protection Rya Forest ever had.
År 1916 såldes godset till ett bolag som: In 1916 the estate was sold to a company that divided the land up for housing and industry. In 1920 the people working here included six carters, eleven labourers and eleven rock blasters. Of the estate's cottages, only Hökmossen still stands in its original place.
År 1917 bodde Gustav Valfrid Lindberg i: In 1917 Gustav Valfrid Lindberg lived in the Parken croft. He worked under the forester at Skarpnäck farm, and in 1924 he married the daughter of the fisherman-crofter at neighbouring Brotorp, which still stands today.
År 1917 fick fabriken ett eget spår till: In 1917 the factory got its own track to Mölndal's upper station. At first the wagons were pulled by horses, but a locomotive was soon bought. The railway embankment and the brick-red office building still survive, and in 1965 Volvo bought the site for an experimental workshop.
År 1918 byggde bröderna Fredrik och Birg: In 1918 the brothers Fredrik and Birger Ljungström built a workshop at Gåshaga for steam-turbine locomotives. There was no railway line to the factory, so the engines were shipped on large barges to Stockholm's rail network. It was here, too, that they developed an air preheater now used all over the world.
År 1918 patenterade SKF det sfäriska rul: In 1918 SKF patented the spherical roller bearing, which can take far greater loads than a ball bearing. That made it ideal for railway carriages, which until then had only been able to use plain bearings.
År 1919 öppnade Göteborgs första yrkessk: In 1919 Gothenburg's first vocational school opened here, and during the Second World War the Swedish Air Force trained aircraft mechanics on the site. It later became a nursery. Since a conversion that began in 2015, the villa has held four flats, with two new residential buildings in the grounds.
År 1921 köptes Villa Sandrew av Herman R: In 1921 Villa Sandrew was bought by Herman Rasch, who had made a fortune in Russia. An art collector, film producer and competitive rider, he fitted out the top floor as a gallery with works by Rembrandt, Velázquez and Goya – plus an early home cinema.
År 1922 tog fortifikationsförvaltningen: In 1922 the military fortifications administration took over, and the house became the regimental commander's residence. In 1985 SAS bought the property, renovated it and used it for hosting guests while its head office at Frösundavik was being built.
År 1923 beslutades att ålderdomshemmet G: In 1923 it was decided to build the Gammelbyn old people's home to mark 400 years since Gustav Vasa marched into Stockholm in 1523. It was finished in 1930, just as a stop for the Örby line tram opened next door.
År 1924 anlades Torslanda Havsbadskoloni: In 1924 Torslanda's seaside allotment colony was laid out on Skeppstadsholmen, with 123 plots of about 1,000 square metres each. It was the first seaside colony in Scandinavia, and the idea came from the local politician Herman Lindholm.
År 1925 bebyggdes de första 34 tomterna,: In 1925 the first 34 plots were built on, in the blocks called Putsaren, Eldaren and Föraren – the engine cleaner, the stoker and the driver. The eightieth and final plot wasn’t built on until 1957. Schultzvägen is named after Herbert Schultz, the Swedish State Railways district manager who drove the project forward.
År 1925 köpte uppfinnaren Fredrik Ljungs: In 1925 the inventor Fredrik Ljungström bought the villa, which was then renamed Ljungströmshof. During his time an inventor's workshop of his own was built in the grounds.
År 1925 köptes villan av uppfinnaren Fre: In 1925 the villa was bought by the inventor Fredrik Ljungström and renamed Ljungströmshof. He built his own inventor's workshop further down the grounds and had both the dining room and the gentlemen's study extended.
År 1926 fick Farstanäsbron en filmroll:: In 1926 the Farstanäs bridge landed a film role, playing the bridge defended by the soldier Sven Dufva in Fänrik Ståls sägner, The Tales of Ensign Stål. The bridge over Lake Magelungen was originally built by the armed forces, which is why it's also known as Militärbron, the Military Bridge. Today's 200-metre footbridge and cycle bridge dates from 1998. Not far away, at Farsta gård, stands Farstastenen, the Farsta Stone – the only surviving runestone in all of Söderort, Stockholm's southern suburbs.
År 1927 bad kolonisterna staden att få b: In 1927 the allotment holders asked the city for permission to build bigger huts, from 14 to 17 square metres, because people had started using them as summer homes. Today 26 plots remain.
År 1927 rullade den första Volvobilen ut: In 1927 the very first Volvo car rolled out of the factory on Hisingen. The island was also home to some of the world's biggest shipyards – Götaverken, Arendal, Eriksberg and Lindholmen – until the shipyard crisis of the 1970s.

In 1927 the very first Volvo car rolled out of the factory on Hisingen. The island was also home to some of the world's biggest shipyards, such as Götaverken and Eriksberg, until the shipyard crisis of the 1970s.
År 1927 var hällen inhägnad med ett järn: In 1927 the rock was surrounded by an iron railing, which had gone by 1973. That same year the carving got a sign and was painted in, and it was repainted in 1987.
År 1928 byggdes ett bussgarage här, och: A bus garage was built here in 1928, and it was the main depot for buses in the northern suburbs until well into the 1970s. The land was sold in 2000, and between 2004 and 2006, 18 villas in a modern functionalist style went up where the garage had been.
År 1928 byggdes ett bussgarage här, som: A bus garage was built here in 1928, and until the 1970s it was the main depot for buses serving the northern suburbs. Today the site along Gamla Norrtäljevägen is home to 18 villas in modern functionalist style, built in 2004–2006.
År 1928 köpte staden området med stöd av: In 1928 the city bought the land with help from Charles Felix Lindberg’s donation fund. On 21 June that year the park was named S.A. Hedlunds park.
År 1928 satte Coldinuorden upp ett gjutj: In 1928 the Coldinu Order put up a cast-iron cross on Korseberget as a memorial to seafarers. The tradition of raising crosses in the archipelago goes back to the voyages of Henry the Navigator in the 15th century. At the centre of the cross is a five-pointed star with an eye.

In 1928 the Coldinu Order, a seafarers' society, raised a cast-iron cross on Korseberget as a memorial for the welfare of sailors. The tradition of crosses in the archipelago goes back to the voyages of discovery of Henry the Navigator. At the centre of the cross is a five-pointed star with an eye.
År 1928 startade ABA försök med postflyg: In 1928 the airline ABA began trial airmail flights to London and Amsterdam. The plane had a postbox where members of the public could drop their letters, and the flight to London took 19 hours.
År 1930 hade villastaden redan cirka 250: By 1930 the villa town already had around 250 villas and its own bus to Jarlaplan. Around Nora torg there was a post office, bank, fire station and bicycle repair shop – the centre of all Danderyd right up to the 1960s.
År 1931 höll Jussi Björling sin första k: In 1931 Jussi Björling gave his first concert at Liseberg. Two years later the French singer Mistinguett arrived with an entourage of 50, six tonnes of luggage and more than 700 costumes.
År 1931 tippades 80 000 ton sopor i en v: In 1931, 80,000 tonnes of rubbish were dumped in a bay of Lövstafjärden. The bay has since been completely filled in, and the old tip is now a grassy hill with an entirely new shoreline.
År 1932 fick snickarmästaren Axel Hellqv: In 1932 the master carpenter Axel Hellqvist persuaded his boat club, Motorbåtsföreningen Delfin, to buy the island. By 1934 the frames of 80 little summer cottages were already up.
År 1932 renoverades huset efter ritninga: In 1932 the building was renovated to designs by Ivar Tengbom, and that same year a café and patisserie opened, serving outdoors in summer. Three generations of the same family ran it until 1990.
År 1932 räddades kvarnen från rivning nä: In 1932 the mill was saved from demolition when it was given to the local heritage society. The sails have been taken down, but the machinery still works. Below it stands the miller's log cabin from the mid-1800s.
År 1933 hittade man fridlyst murgröna hä: In 1933 protected ivy was found here – a relic of the Bronze Age, when the climate was warmer. Later attempts to find it again on the scree slope have so far come to nothing.
År 1936 avled fyra patienter på Maria sj: In 1936 four patients at Maria Hospital died after receiving the wrong treatment. The hospital went on to lend its name to a law, Lex Maria, which governs the reporting of such incidents.
År 1936 invigdes Lisebergsbadet, med und: Lisebergsbadet opened in 1936, with underwater lighting and artificial waves – it was considered the most modern pool in Europe. It was drained in 1956 and demolished in 1962.
År 1937 byggdes laboratorier i Ursvik fö: In 1937 laboratories were built in Ursvik for the Defence Chemical Institute, which later became FOA, the National Defence Research Institute. The work done here was of great importance to the Swedish nuclear weapons programme. FOA's old premises now house the Nobla school.
År 1938 antogs en byggnadsplan av arkite: In 1938 a development plan by the architect Gunnar Wetterling was adopted for the villa community that then grew up here. When Spånga rural municipality was dissolved in 1949, Lilla Ursvik ended up in Sundbyberg.
År 1940 bestämdes att Skarpnäcksfältet s: In 1940 it was decided that the Skarpnäck field would be a reserve airfield for fighter planes, but it was never used. The Stockholm Gliding Club moved in instead. From the mid-1980s Skarpnäcksstaden was built: a miniature town of red-brick buildings with 3,400 flats.
År 1943 flyttade Sjökrigsskolan från Ske: In 1943 the Royal Swedish Naval Academy moved from Skeppsholmen to Näsby slott, and 25 buildings went up around the palace. The academy stayed until 1987, and since 1989 the palace has been a conference hotel.
År 1945 fanns 123 fiskebåtar på Hönö. Un: In 1945 there were 123 fishing boats on Hönö. During the Second World War eight boats were lost, 27 fishermen died at sea and 53 ended up as prisoners of war in Germany.
År 1946 byggdes Nya Lundenskolan i gult: In 1946 the new Lundenskolan was built in yellow brick just outside the stone wall of the old schoolyard, and at the end of 2018 the school gained a sports hall for around 500 spectators, which the pupils helped to plan.
År 1947 bytte villaområdena i Hanviken o: In 1947 the villa areas of Hanviken and Kumla were renamed Trollbäcken, so they wouldn't be confused with the town of Kumla in Närke. The name Kumla probably comes from kummel, a prehistoric cairn used as a sea mark or boundary marker.
År 1948 beräknades bygget kosta 690 000: In 1948 the building was expected to cost 690,000 kronor. But because the tower is so visible, the site demanded a great deal of its appearance, and new plans were drawn up. By 1951 the estimate had climbed to 1,290,000 kronor.
År 1949 kostade en fyrarummare på 104 kv: In 1949 a 104-square-metre house with four rooms cost 54,000 kronor, with a 12,000 deposit. In March 2020 one of the terraced houses, at Åkervägen 31, sold for 9 million kronor.
År 1949 reste arkitekten Bengt Gate och: In 1949 the architect Bengt Gate and the association's chairman travelled to London to draw inspiration from the new community centres. The civic centre was to be a multi-activity house open to all, but money was tight and it didn't open until September 1957.
År 1951 byggdes tre experimenthus vid Ar: In 1951 three experimental houses went up on Arvid Lindmansgatan. Known as the Trestadshusen – the Three Cities Houses – they were the Gothenburg House, the Stockholm House and the Malmö House.
År 1952 visades nya Gröndal i ett SF-rep: In 1952 the new Gröndal featured in an SF newsreel titled 'New Gröndal – the ugly duckling that became a swan'. At the very top of Galjonshuset, the eleven-storey Figurehead House, the artist Otte Sköld had his studio.
År 1953 fanns omkring 1 100 fastigheter: In 1953 Askim municipality had around 1,100 properties, and roughly 40 per cent of them were summer homes. By the time Askim merged with Gothenburg in 1974, it had just over 14,000 residents.
År 1953 köptes Lugnet av tre bröder Olss: In 1953 Lugnet was bought by the three Olsson brothers, who ran a building firm and were known as the 'Tre Knas' – the Three Nutters. They managed to block the extension of Lingvägen and upper Russinvägen. By the time they sold up in 1962, the land had become so expensive that the city had to build taller and denser than before in Hökarängen.

In 1953 Lugnet was bought by three Olsson brothers who ran a building firm and were known as “Tre Knas” – roughly “the Three Nutters”. They managed to stop the extension of Lingvägen across their land. When the city finally bought it in 1962, the land was so expensive that it had to be built up higher and more densely.
År 1954 målade Kristian Lundstedt ett ta: In 1954 Kristian Lundstedt painted a ceiling that moves from light above the gallery to darkness over the nave and back to light above the chancel. The darkness is shown through realistic scenes from the Second World War.
År 1955 gick Arehns ihop med AB Siefvert: In 1955 Arehns merged with AB Siefvert & Fornander to form Arenco AB. In 1969 the subsidiary Arenco Electronics was sold to Philips.
År 1960 hade Tappström 343 invånare och: In 1960 Tappström had 343 residents and Träkvista 582. Since 1975 they have officially counted as one built-up area, and today Ekerö is home to more than 10,000 people.
År 1960 hade Träkvista 582 invånare och: In 1960 Träkvista had 582 inhabitants and Tappström 343. Since 1975 they've been counted as one built-up area, and today it's home to more than 10,000 people. Near Träkvista, by Ekerövägen, lies the burial mound known as Fantans hög.
År 1961 samlades tyska och brittiska omk: In 1961, German and British servicemen who died in both world wars were brought together here in two separate burial grounds, set aside in perpetuity. There are also sections dedicated to Swedish seamen, Latvians and Muslims, among others.
År 1963 fick Årstaskolan en vinkelställd: In 1963 Årstaskolan gained an L-shaped extension along Hjälmarsvägen for six-year-olds and the lower primary years. It too was designed by Stig Åkermark. Today buses 160 and 164 run along the street.
År 1963 framförde Hasse och Tage en visa: In 1963 the comedy duo Hasse and Tage performed a song about Rågsved in their revue Konstgjorda Pompe, to the tune of Tiptoe Through the Tulips, sung by Sonya Hedenbratt. Back in 1959, Pär Rådström had written a short story about nine-year-old Kent, who thinks Rågsved is better than town.
År 1963 framfördes Hasse och Tages visa: In 1963, the comedy duo Hasse and Tage's song about Rågsved was performed in the revue Konstgjorda Pompe, to the tune of 'Tiptoe Through the Tulips', sung by Sonya Hedenbratt. Spotify founder Daniel Ek grew up here.
År 1964 låg gården övergiven och förfall: By 1964 the farm was abandoned and falling apart. The librarian Kerstin Elfstrand rallied local associations, and in 1967 nineteen of them formed the Jakobsberg Farm Association. The cultural and community centre opened on 16 May 1973 and today is run by around 25 associations.
År 1969 beslöts att spränga en bergtunne: In 1969 it was decided to blast a tunnel through the rock from the brickworks in Angered, under Vättlefjäll and down to the Göta älv river. It was meant to help the Lärjeån river cope with floodwater whenever heavy rain fell on the new Angered district.
År 1969 utreddes ett kärnkraftvärmeverk: In 1969 a nuclear heating plant inside the rock south of Värtahamnen was investigated. The idea was that surplus heat could warm outdoor pools and extend the season at Kampementsbadet. But by the time the report was finished in 1974, the political winds had shifted, and the plant was never built.
År 1970 blev Grand Sveriges första biogr: In 1970 the Grand became Sweden’s first cinema complex with more than one screen. It was rebuilt with three auditoriums and renamed Grand 1–2–3.
År 1970 byggde Olof Hammarberg från Göte: In 1970 Olof Hammarberg from Gothenburg built two mechanical organs for the chapel. They were exactly alike and each stood in its own room.
År 1970 byggde Olof Hammarberg två ident: In 1970 Olof Hammarberg built two identical mechanical organs for the chapel, one for each of its halls. The pews have steel frames and are upholstered in chrome-tanned leather.
År 1970 flyttade musikteatergruppen Nati: In 1970 the music theatre group Nationalteatern moved into Backa youth centre on Selma Lagerlöfs torg. So it was here in northern Backa that the group had its base.
År 1972 beskrevs Bergfana som ett rödfär: In 1972 Bergfana was described as a single-storey wooden house painted red, with red corner boards and white window frames. Both the croft and the railway lineman's cottage were demolished in the 1970s.
År 1973 tog Västerorts kulturkommitté öv: In 1973 the cultural committee for Västerort, Stockholm's western suburbs, took over the running of Prisma, which is why it survived when many suburban cinemas shut down. After a renovation in 2003 the auditorium had 316 seats, and in 2005 the film 165 Hässelby had its world premiere here. Today the space is used for drama and music teaching.
År 1974 inreddes huvudbyggnaden till gäs: In 1974 the main building was turned into a country inn, and the ground floor was altered slightly. The west wing was destroyed by fire in the mid-1800s; today's wing dates from 1887.
År 1974 startade dramatikern Ellen Bergm: In 1974 the playwright Ellen Bergman founded Göteborgs kammarteater, a chamber theatre, at the Stora Holm manor where she also lived. She served up food and theatre as one experience, right up until 1986.
År 1974 visade kommunen en skiss med hög: In 1974 the council unveiled a sketch for tower blocks housing around 500 people here. The plans met with protests, and in 1986 the council bought the land to stop it being built on. Ten years later the area became a nature reserve.
År 1975 fick man bygga tak över entréern: In 1975 canopies had to be built over the entrances to protect people from glass panels coming loose from the walls. Ralph Erskine designed them, and in 1984 he added the library, which softened the building's huge scale.
År 1975 fördes byn Kyrkhamn, Riddersvik: In 1975 the village of Kyrkhamn, Riddersvik and most of Lövsta were transferred from Järfälla to the City of Stockholm.
År 1980 bråkade Mölndals kommun med Förs: In 1980 Mölndal council locked horns with the Swedish Armed Forces over noise from the Sisjön firing range. Despite the military's objections, a town plan for 1,040 flats was approved in 1982.
År 1980 bröt en strid ut mellan Mölndal: In 1980 a dispute broke out between Mölndal and the Swedish Armed Forces over noise from the Sisjön firing range. Despite the military's protests, a town plan with 1,040 flats was approved in 1982.
År 1983 spelades filmen Raskenstam in vi: In 1983 the film Raskenstam was shot at the Groen malmgård, a historic suburban manor. Gunnar Hellström both directed and starred, and the cast included Lena Nyman and Agnetha Fältskog.
År 1983 tog Helige Savas församling över: In 1983 the St Sava congregation took over a church in Enskede that had belonged to the Swedenborgians. Restoration revealed serious mould and damp, so it was demolished, and in 1991 a new church was built on the same site.
År 1986 beslutades att bygga bostäder på: In 1986 the decision was taken to build homes on the farmland at Eklanda. The area grew from Eklanda Hage and Eklanda Skog in the north-west towards Eklanda Vall and Eklanda Äng in the south, and it borders the Änggårdsbergen nature reserve.

In 1986 the decision was taken to build homes on the farmland. The area then grew from the north-west, with Eklanda Hage and Eklanda Skog, towards the south and south-east with Eklanda Vall and Eklanda Äng.
År 1990 fick stationen en stor busstermi: In 1990 the station got a large bus terminal for the Haninge and Tyresö buses, built on a deck over the tracks. The station building also houses the control centre for the green metro line. Don't miss Lennart Jonasson's artwork Reaktion 1968 on the square.
År 1990 hade Ö-varvet 17 anställda. Någr: In 1990 the Ö-varvet shipyard had 17 employees. A few years later, in 1997–1998, a branch yard was set up on the neighbouring island of Hönö. Today the yard is part of the marine group Ö-Borgen.
År 1992 beslöt Stockholms stad att lägga: In 1992 the City of Stockholm decided to close the school and turn the building into a school museum. In protest, a foundation was set up, and in 1993 it reopened the school as an independent school. The building was originally grey but has long been yellow.
År 1993 byggdes stationen om till platse: In 1993 the station was rebuilt as the point where the double track from Roslags Näsby becomes single track, and it was moved about 50 metres east. The double track was extended to Viggbyholm in 2010. On a normal winter weekday, around 1,500 people board here.
År 1993 gjordes bockkranen om till utsik: In 1993 the gantry crane was turned into a viewing attraction, and in the summer months you could bungee jump from it. At 84 metres above sea level, it was the highest bungee jump in Sweden.
År 1994 föreslogs att Böskolan skulle lä: In 1994 there were plans to close Böskolan. The parents responded by forming a cooperative, and today Böskolan is an independent school with a preschool and every year group right up to lower secondary.
År 1995 hölls Sveriges första Alphakurs: In 1995 Sweden's first Alpha course was held at Kummelby church, and Alpha Sweden had its office here until 2009. In the 1960s and 70s the church musician Anders Lindström introduced Anglican choral music here and released records.
År 1998 fick Sörmanmannen hedersomnämnan: In 1998 the Sörman man received an honourable mention in the Sign of the Year awards, for having enriched the city at night for 60 years as “an Oscar among signs”. When the shop closed in December 2021, the sign was taken down.
År 1999 startade en arkivdepå i före det: In 1999 an archive depot opened in former mine premises in Grängesberg. It closed in 2015, and the material was moved back to Stockholm.
År 1999 sålde föreningen byggnaden och d: In 1999 the association sold the building, which was then used as offices, among other things. On 14 December 2013 it reopened as Allaktivitetshuset, an activity centre where various local groups run events across 2,700 square metres.
År 2000 smyckades biljetthallen och gång: In 2000 the ticket hall and ramp were decorated with Christian Partos's clinker mosaic Teleportations. Since 2015 the entrance has been set right in the middle of a new building.
År 2001 byggdes Skandinaviens största ci: In 2001 Scandinavia's largest circus hall was built here, home to the contemporary circus company Cirkus Cirkör. The hangar, converted from a timber warehouse, opened in 2010 as the first circus stage in Stockholm County since Cirkus on Djurgården in 1892.
År 2001 hittades en medeltida stockbåt a: In 2001 a medieval oak dugout canoe was found near the lake. It was about four metres long and 60 centimetres wide, and the oak was probably felled around 1202.
År 2001 hittades en medeltida stockbåt i: In 2001 a medieval oak dugout canoe was found during ditch-digging near the lake. It had been about four metres long and 60 centimetres wide, and the oak was probably felled around 1202.
År 2001 öppnade Ryanair sin första linje: In 2001 Ryanair opened its first route from Säve, to London, and services grew to around fifteen destinations. The last scheduled flight left for Bromma on 18 January 2015.
År 2002 upptäckte arkeologen Nils Ringst: In 2002 the archaeologist Nils Ringstedt discovered a plateau house above Östergården – a house foundation with stone-lined edges. No more than about twenty of these are known in Sweden, and they are usually dated to between the 400s and 700s.
År 2004 flyttade djursjukhuset till nuva: In 2004 the animal hospital moved into its current building on Månskärsvägen. Today it's one of the largest of its kind in Sweden, treating around 26,000 patients a year, with a 24-hour ward and even a hydrotherapy pool for physiotherapy.
År 2005 avgjordes tornets framtid i en f: In 2005 the tower's future was settled in a local referendum: it would become a café. During the 2009 renovation the handsome wooden staircase was cleaned and the windows repainted in their original colour with linseed-oil paint. Today the tower houses a restaurant and exhibitions.
År 2005 fick Solparken en stensatt bäck: In 2005 Solparken was given a stone-lined stream flowing down into a pond. It slows down and cleans stormwater from Råsundavägen before it runs on towards Råstasjön lake. The park's tall spruces have grown higher than the buildings around them.
År 2005 fick gamla Åbybadet ett äventyrs: In 2005 the old Åbybadet pool gained a water park with three slides – the longest 78 metres – and a jungle lagoon. In the first half of 2006 it welcomed 275,000 visitors. The new swimming baths on the same site cost 500 million kronor.
År 2005 föreslog lokalpolitiker att idro: In 2005 local politicians proposed building homes on the sports ground by Edsviken. Residents protested and the plans were dropped. Instead the area got an indoor athletics hall, delayed by difficult ground conditions and not opened until November 2016.
År 2006 byggdes en glashytta i anslutnin: In 2006 a glassworks designed by the architect Christer Håkansson was built alongside the museum. The museum itself opened on 23 May 1992, after a museum board had been set up in 1985.
År 2007 flyttade SVT och SR hit från Syn: In 2007 Swedish public television and radio, SVT and SR, moved here from Synvillan in Torp. Kanalhuset is 12,000 square metres smaller and has two studios instead of three. Digital technology simply takes up less space and needs fewer people.
År 2007 vann Farsta gymnasium Arlas Guld: In 2007 Farsta gymnasium won Arla's Golden Cow award as Sweden's best school for food enjoyment. The school also had a health studio where pupils and staff got their own training programmes.
In 2007 Farsta gymnasium won Arla's Golden Cow competition as Sweden's best school for enjoying good food. The school also had a health studio with its own health educator.
År 2008 bjöd Stockholms stad in arkitekt: In 2008 the City of Stockholm invited architects from around the world to compete with ideas for building on the abandoned motorway and the Årsta field. The winner was Arkipelag, a proposal from a French team. The plan is a new district of 4,000 homes for 10,000 residents, due to be completed around 2035.
År 2008 fanns planer på att riva badet o: In 2008 there were plans to tear down the pool and build a whole new complex with indoor pools, a waterfall, sports halls and a sliding roof. It never happened. Instead the pool was refurbished for around 53 million kronor, the water slides were removed, and it reopened on 15 June 2014.
År 2008 nominerades Västerortskyrkan av: In 2008 the magazine Betong nominated Västerortskyrkan as one of 21 candidates for Sweden's Seven Wonders in Concrete. The congregation now belongs to the Uniting Church in Sweden, Equmeniakyrkan.
År 2008 ställdes en rekonstruktion av de: In 2008 a reconstruction of the lost runestone was put up by the footbridge over the railway next to Överjärva farm.
År 2008 utsågs biblioteket i Fässbergsgy: In 2008 the library at Fässbergsgymnasiet, with over 20,000 titles, was named School Library of the Year. The jury praised the way teachers and librarians worked together. The school itself closed in 2015.
År 2008 öppnade Media Markt, senare Powe: In 2008 Media Markt, later Power, opened its second Gothenburg store here, in Coop Bygg's former premises. The area was originally developed by KF Fastigheter and has changed hands several times since.
År 2009 flyttade Ericsson lagerhantering: In 2009 Ericsson moved its warehousing to Borås. The huge space was divided up, and today some twenty companies are based in the building. The old office wing has become a serviced office centre.
År 2009 sålde Stockholms stad Hässelby s: In 2009 the City of Stockholm sold Hässelby Palace for 50 million kronor. The buyers were Torbjörn Blomqvist and the singer Tomas Ledin. They took over in 2010 and began using the old spelling of the name: Hesselby slott.
År 2009 sålde staden slottet för 50 milj: In 2009 the city sold the palace for 50 million kronor. The new owners, Torbjörn Blomqvist and the singer Tomas Ledin, took over in 2010 and revived the old spelling, Hesselby slott.
År 2009–2011 byggdes raffinaderiet om fö: In 2009–2011 the refinery was converted to make diesel from vegetable oils. Tall oil from paper mills is refined in Piteå and shipped here for the final stage, before being blended with ordinary diesel.
År 2010 fick kapellet ett rum för minnes: In 2010 the chapel gained a room for memorial gatherings beneath one of its projecting roofs – a glazed veranda with space for 45 people. The walls of the ceremony hall are decorated with paintings by Pär Andersson.
År 2010 var gamla Åbybadet en av arenorn: In 2010 the old Åbybadet pool was one of the venues for the World Masters Swimming Championships, with 6,500 competitors aged 25 to 96 from 74 countries. The first pool opened in 1977, and in 2005 it gained a water park with three slides.
År 2010 var Åbybadet en av arenorna för: In 2010 Åbybadet was one of the venues for the World Masters Swimming Championships, with 6,500 competitors aged from 25 to 96 from 74 countries.

In 2010, Åbybadet was one of the venues for the World Masters Swimming Championships. Some 6,500 swimmers aged between 25 and 96, from 74 countries, competed in the same events as at any ordinary championship.
In 2010 the Åbybadet pool was one of the venues for the World Masters Swimming Championships, with 6,500 competitors aged 25 to 96 from 74 countries.
År 2012 vann Råckstaskylten tävlingen Ly: In 2012 the Råcksta sign won the 'Brilliant Sign' competition, voted for by 370 people. The other nominees included the DN sign at Marieberg, the NK clock on Hamngatan and the Drick Ramlösa sign at Tegelbacken. The jury said it shines 'both cocky and understated'.

In 2012 the Råcksta sign won the Lysande skylt (Brilliant Sign) competition, voted for by 370 people. The other nominees included the DN sign, the NK clock and the Drick Ramlösa sign at Tegelbacken. The jury felt it shone both cockily and quietly at the same time.
År 2018 invigdes en solcellsanläggning m: In 2018 a solar installation with 1,588 panels was opened on one of the farm's paddocks. It's expected to generate 400,000 kWh a year, making the whole farm self-sufficient in electricity.
År 2023 röstades Kvastekulla kapell fram: In 2023 Kvastekulla Chapel was voted Sweden's most beautiful brutalist building.
År 2025 startade två elever skolsatirtid: In 2025 two pupils launched the school satire paper Östra Löken. Since then it has staged a half-satirical political debate called ‘Den rostade Löken’ (The Roasted Onion) and made a spoof version of the school website.
År 2035 planeras en tunnelbanestation hä: A metro station is planned here for 2035 on the new line between Fridhemsplan and Älvsjö. The agreement for the line was signed in March 2017.
Åren 1376–1381 köpte Bo Jonsson Grip de: Between 1376 and 1381 the nobleman Bo Jonsson Grip bought up most of the farms on Lidingö, and Långnäs appears in the deeds of sale. The present farmhouse was built in the late 18th century.
Between 1376 and 1381, Bo Jonsson Grip bought most of the farms on Lidingö. Långnäs gård is listed in the deeds of sale.
Åren 1736–1785 fanns ett glasbruk i Lill: From 1736 to 1785 there was a glassworks at Lilla Björknäs, which gave its name to Glasbrukssjön, 'Glassworks Lake'. Rörstrand bought the land in 1906 to build a porcelain factory, but the factory ended up in Lidköping instead.
Åren 1861–1862 köptes godset Skarpnäck m: In 1861–1862 the Skarpnäck estate and all its cottages were bought by the German brewer Friedrich Neumüller, who had founded Neumüllers Bryggeri on Södermalm. In 1886 Listudden became a summer retreat for his daughter Pauline, who was married to the artist Johan Åkerlund.
Åren 1927–1935 var Tengdahl ordförande f: From 1927 to 1935 Tengdahl chaired Stockholm City Council. His epitaph became "His paths were absolutely straight", and the city bought his grave at Bromma churchyard for its chairman.
Åren 1928–1972 fanns den kända progressi: From 1928 to 1972, the well-known progressive boarding school Viggbyholmsskolan occupied a large area in and around Viggbyholm farm. By then the garden suburb had already grown up around the Roslagsbanan station.
Åren 1933–35 breddades bron och fick spå: In 1933–35 the bridge was widened and tram tracks were laid. Today's bridge, with its slip roads, was built in the early 1970s when the traffic along Gamlestadsvägen was reorganised.
Åren 1935–1978 gick badbussar hit för ba: From 1935 to 1978 special buses brought children here to swim from the parts of Stockholm south of Slussen. On an ordinary summer's day in the 1950s, 2,000 children came. They had swimming lessons and were given buns and milk for lunch.
Åren 1937–1938 byggdes ett butiks- och b: In 1937–1938 a building with shops and flats went up, complete with a post office and the Grand cinema, and the Frändberg building became known as Centrumhuset. Mölndals torg, also called Albert's Square, was inaugurated in 1984 when the statue of Albert was unveiled.
Åren 1939–1950 arbetade Olof Traungs son: From 1939 to 1950, Olof Traung's son, the naval architect Jan-Olof Traung, worked at the yard. Under his leadership it expanded, building sailing boats, minesweepers, workboats and fishing boats – including Star boats and Folkboats.
Åren 1950–1957 var Slottsskogsvallen hem: From 1950 to 1957 Slottsskogsvallen stadium was home to the speedway team Kaparna. At the 1956 Swedish Championships 14,770 people crammed in to watch Ove Fundin win – and plenty of them asked for their money back because they couldn't see.
Åren 1975–2009 drev Svenska Turistföreni: From 1975 to 2009 the Swedish Tourist Association ran the farm as a tourist lodge and hostel, with up to 23,500 overnight stays a year at its peak. After an extension in 1984 there were 34 rooms, two saunas, floodlit jogging trails and even a dance floor.
Åren 1986–1990, när Ullevi byggdes om ef: Between 1986 and 1990, while Ullevi stadium was being rebuilt after damage done during a Springsteen concert, the big concerts moved to Eriksberg. U2 and David Bowie played here in 1987, Michael Jackson in 1988, and the Rolling Stones and Madonna in 1990.
Åren 1992–1997 låg den isklassade räddni: From 1992 to 1997 the ice-class rescue cruiser Hjalmar A:son Tech was stationed in Hovås. She was around 18 metres long and could make 13 knots, and was eventually sold to Tønsberg in Norway to serve as a harbour boat.
Åren 2009–2011 byggdes raffinaderiet om: In 2009–2011 the refinery was converted into a biorefinery. Tall oil from the sulphate pulp mills is turned into crude tall diesel in Piteå, then shipped here for the final stage before being blended with fossil diesel and sold at petrol stations.
Åren 2011–2013 hölls popmusikfestivaler: From 2011 to 2013, pop music festivals were held on Knarrholmen. Just east of the island lies Lilla Knarrholmen.
Åren 2013–2014 spelades TV4:s programser: In 2013–2014 the TV4 series Mia på Grötö was filmed here, with Mia Skäringer and celebrity guests.
Åren 2013–2016 byggdes Värtahamnen om fö: In 2013–2016 Värtahamnen port was rebuilt to make room for the new Norra Djurgårdsstaden district. A new pier on a piled concrete deck was built further out, and parts of the harbour basin were filled in. The pier has a new passenger terminal.
Åren 2017–2025 fanns också den enklare s: From 2017 to 2025 the same building also housed Rinos bodega, a more casual sister restaurant. Both Aloë and Rinos closed in February 2025.
Åren 2021–2022 totalrenoverades Tureberg: In 2021–2022 Turebergshuset was completely renovated, and its ground floor extended towards Turebergs torg. After the rebuild, the library moved in in 2023.
Årets Folkpark två gånger: Folk Park of the Year, twice
Årets kyrktupp blev emblem: Church Weathercock of the Year became an emblem
Årsta centrum: Årsta centrum, the local town centre
Årsta centrum var det första förortscent: Årsta centrum was the first suburban centre built in Sweden. Inspired by English community centres, it was completed in 1953, though the Forum cinema on the square had already opened in 1951. Just south of Årsta Church, designed by Johan Celsing and consecrated in 2011, is a late Iron Age burial ground with ten burial mounds and 35 stone settings, two of them shaped like ships.
Årstabergsparken är 16 hektar med branta: Årstabergsparken covers 16 hectares, with steep slopes and a plateau 40 metres above sea level. From an eleven-metre lookout tower you can see out over Södermalm and Liljeholmen. The park's theme is the forest.
Årstadal har tillsammans med Sundbyberg: Årstadal, along with Sundbyberg, has been called Stockholm's first suburb. Close by, the Nyboda tunnels cut through the rock, and the oldest of them became Sweden's very first railway tunnel when the Western Main Line reached the city in 1860. Up on the hill above Liljeholmskajen is Årstabergsparken, a park that opened in 2018 and was even shortlisted for Stockholm's Building of the Year.
Årstafruns park fick sitt namn 2010 efte: Årstafruns park was named in 2010 after Årstafrun, 'the Lady of Årsta' – Märta Helena Reenstierna, the diarist who ran the manor of Årsta gård. Right next to it are the EPA houses, among the first deck-access blocks of flats in Sweden and now protected under the Cultural Environment Act. A little further on is Snigelparken, the Snail Park, where children play in a sandpit shaped like a giant concrete snail.
Årstahusen är tre punkthus på 16 våninga: Årstahusen are three 16-storey point blocks, about 52 metres tall, designed by Varg Arkitekter. On the railway side the facades are closed and clad in glazed clinker tiles, with a sharp vertical fold. On the courtyard side the buildings open up with balconies.
Årstalänken bjuder på en ovanlig syn: de: Årstalänken offers an unusual sight. The eastern part of this stretch of motorway has been closed since 2004 – a 'ruin motorway', where new homes are now being planned. On an ordinary winter weekday, around 8,300 passengers board at Årstaberg commuter station, and the Tvärbanan light rail has called here since 2000. On Årstaskogs väg rise the Årstahusen, three residential tower blocks built between 2017 and 2020.
Årstalänken öppnade 1972 som början på e: Årstalänken opened in 1972 as the start of a planned southern ring road, Södra länken – but the rest wasn't finished until 2004. For more than three decades, drivers had to carry on along smaller roads, while the motorway languished with only minimal upkeep of its lights and signs.
Årstaskolan byggdes 1946 efter ritningar: Årsta school was built in 1946 to designs by Stig Åkermark, and today it has just over 900 pupils, from the reception class up to year nine. Many of Årsta's streets are named after lakes – Hjälmarsvägen, for instance, was named after Lake Hjälmaren in 1941. Södra länken also runs nearby; at 3.8 kilometres, its longest tunnel is the longest road tunnel in Sweden.
Årstidstorget kallas av många kort och g: Lots of people just call Årstidstorget, the Seasons Square, 'Norra' or 'Norra centrum', and it's the little hub of northern Kortedala. There's a health centre, a pizzeria, a couple of tobacconists and a konditori, a café-bakery, for anyone in need of a fika, and there's a pub nearby too. Local clubs and societies also have their premises on the square. It's served by tram line six and sits by the line's terminus.
Årstidstorget kallas också Norra centrum: Årstidstorget is also known as Norra centrum, or simply Norra. There are premises for local organisations here too, such as Lugna gatan, and Utmarksskolan school with its sports hall, Utmarkshallen, is a couple of hundred metres away.
Årtalet står på porten: The date is on the doorway
Åsnor och getter i parken: Donkeys and goats in the park
Åsögatan 213 är Stockholms högsta husnum: Åsögatan 213 is the highest street number in central Stockholm. The building went up in 1959 using older timber, replacing an almost identical one that had to be pulled down because it was infested with house longhorn beetles.
Åt Järfällahållet breder Viksjö ut sig,: Out towards Järfälla stretches Viksjö, a district of about 11 square kilometres, mostly family houses from the 1960s, 70s and 80s, with plenty of open countryside. On the Stockholm side is Backlura, where every street is named after a flower or plant. And here's a curiosity: the Hässelby district administration existed for just two years, 1997 and 1998.
Åttkantig kyrka med blått glas: An octagonal church with blue glass
Åva gymnasium: Åva gymnasium, the Åva sixth-form school
Åva gymnasium invigdes 1972 där Roslagsb: Åva upper secondary school opened in 1972, right where the Roslagsbanan railway divides. Its school magazine, Cumulus, has won the Lilla journalistpriset award twice and been named the best school magazine in Sweden. In 2018 the school was given an industrial robot from AGA's research labs, and the students brought it back to life themselves. A little way off stands Tibble Church, sometimes called the cathedral of Roslagen.
Ö-varvet bygger och reparerar fartyg men: Ö-varvet builds and repairs ships, but it also makes trawls and fishing winches. A branch yard opened on Hönö in 1997–1998, and in 2015 the ferry M/S Härön was built here.
Ö-varvet en bit bort är en riktig familj: The Ö-varvet shipyard nearby is a real family saga. Ernst Backman founded it in 1916 to repair fishing boats, his sons Gösta and Hugo took over in 1945, and two more generations of Backmans have run it since. Today the yard can handle ships of up to 900 tonnes. Nearby is Öckerö old church, also known as Mariakyrkan.
Ö-varvet grundades 1916 av Ernst Backman: Ö-varvet, the shipyard here, was founded in 1916 by Ernst Backman as a repair yard for fishing boats, and it has been handed down through several generations of the Backman family ever since. Today the yard builds and repairs vessels of up to 900 tonnes, and it also makes trawl nets and fishing winches. The sea shapes life at Öckerö seglande gymnasieskola, a little way off, too – a sailing-focused upper secondary school where around 300 students follow courses with a maritime element.
Ö-varvet kan serva fartyg upp till 900 t: The Ö-varvet shipyard can service vessels of up to 900 tonnes. Among the boats it has built or rebuilt are the cable ferry Malin and M/S Härön from 2015.
Ö-varvet på Öckerö grundades 1916 av Ern: Ö-varvet, the shipyard on Öckerö, was founded by Ernst Backman in 1916 to repair fishing boats and has been handed down through several generations of the Backman family. In 1997–1998 it opened a second yard here on Hönö. Today it builds ships and makes trawls and fishing winches.
Öarnas broar och vägar var byggda för hä: The islands' bridges and roads were built for horse-drawn traffic. When heavy motor vehicles began appearing just before the First World War, all cars had to be banned beyond Drottningholm.
Öckerö har inte bara en sockenkyrka utan: Öckerö has not one parish church but two, close together: Öckerö Old Church, also known as Mariakyrkan, St Mary's, and Öckerö New Church, which these days usually goes simply by Öckerö Church. The parish covers the whole municipality, and the old parish takes in places like Hönö, Fotö, Hälsö, Björkö, Kalvsund, Källö-Knippla and Rörö.

Öckerö has not one parish church but two, close together: Öckerö Old Church, also known as St Mary's, and Öckerö New Church, these days usually just called Öckerö Church. The parish covers the whole municipality. The old stone church dates from the 1450s, and the new one was consecrated in 1906 up on the rocky hill of Sörgårds vale.
Öckerö kommun är unik på sitt sätt: tio: Öckerö Municipality is one of a kind: ten inhabited islands and no fixed link at all to the mainland, so everything relies on the ferries. The only other example in Sweden is Gotland. The islands have a rich variety of plants and plenty of birdlife, though the municipality also struggles with marine litter washing ashore. The main town is called – no surprise – Öckerö.
Öckerö är en av de centrala öarna i Göte: Öckerö is one of the central islands of Gothenburg's northern archipelago and gives its name to the whole municipality. It measures barely four square kilometres, yet it had 3,570 year-round residents in 2020 and is home to the municipal offices. The houses have grown so close together that since 2018 it has been counted as one urban area with its neighbour Hönö, under the name Hönö-Öckerö.
Ögonläkaren Ernst Saléns villa Rosenborg: Villa Rosenborg, home of the eye doctor Ernst Salén, appears in Berndt Lindholm's painting Arendal 1879. Back then its little tower had a flat roof; the pointed one came later. The stone gateposts still bear the villa's name and the year 1884.

Villa Rosenborg, home of the eye doctor Ernst Salén, was a converted farmhouse. In Berndt Lindholm's painting Arendal 1879 its little tower has a flat roof, later replaced by a pointed one. The stone gateposts bear the name Rosenborg and the year 1884.

Villa Rosenborg, home of the eye doctor Ernst Salén, was a converted farmhouse. In Berndt Lindholm's oil painting Arendal 1879, its little tower still has a flat roof, later replaced by a pointed one. The stone gateposts are carved with the name Rosenborg and the year 1884.
Öjersjö ligger högt, cirka 110 till 120: Öjersjö sits high up, around 110 to 120 metres above sea level, so the winters here can be a little snowier than down in the lower parts of the municipality. The village lies on Stora Kåsjön, the largest lake in Partille – 32 metres deep, and the source of the municipality's drinking water. All around, nature takes over, with the Knipeflågsbergen nature reserve running right up to the Delsjö area.
